Post-migration_025: the authoritative write is the `UPDATE chat_messages SET model_id = ...` (L184-187) issued BEFORE the vec0 attempt — the `message_embeddings` BLOB side table no longer exists.

CAVEAT (behavioural change vs the old dual-write design): a swallowed vec0 failure is NOT re-discovered by the CRON backfill. `getMessagesWithoutEmbeddings()` predicates solely on `chat_messages.model_id` (NULL or != current model_id); once model_id is set, a row with a missing vec0 entry is never re-surfaced — the message is silently unsearchable until the embedding model changes (model-drift cleanup nulls model_id) or EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED is toggled. Note the asymmetry: `UserMemoriesRepository.saveMemoryEmbedding` orders the vec0 write BEFORE setting provenance, so a failed vec0 write leaves `model_id = NULL` and the regen cron retries it — the message-side repo does not have this protection.

title: Design doc review found `_filterByMaxMessages` called but never defined
content: In the initial write-up of `docs/design/vector-search-native.md`, the `_filterByMaxMessages()` helper was referenced in the `_nativeVectorSearch()` method (as Option A post-filter) but was never defined anywhere in the document. This was fixed by switching to Option B (pre-filter by date), which eliminated the helper entirely.

title: vec0 tables are dimension-aware: separate table per embedding dimension
content:
vec0 message-embedding tables use dimension-aware naming: `vec_message_embeddings_{N}` where N is the embedding dimension (e.g. `vec_message_embeddings_384`, `vec_message_embeddings_1024`). This solves the vec0 constraint that embedding dimensions are baked into the table schema at creation time and cannot vary within one table. `vec_user_memories_{N}` follows the same convention.

- The table name is constructed by the REPOSITORY caller, not by vectorSearch(): `_nativeVectorSearch` builds `f"vec_message_embeddings_{dimension}"` from `dimension = len(queryEmbedding)` (chat_search.py L765) and `_upsertVecMessageEmbedding` from `len(embedding)` (chat_embeddings.py L262). `vectorSearch()` receives the finished `table` name — it has no `dimension` parameter.
- Multiple dimension sizes coexist in separate vec0 tables simultaneously.
- Table creation is lazy: `createVectorTable()` on first write, guarded by a `listTables()` existence check.
- Post-migration_025: there is no physical BLOB side table anymore — vec0 carries the vectors, and provenance lives in `chat_messages.model_id` (integer FK into the `models` lookup table; the vec0 partition keys are `chat_id` + `model_id`).
- Design rationale: docs/design/vector-search-native.md §4.7 (Dimension Handling, L710) and §5.2.

title: vec0 tables created dynamically at runtime, not via migration
content:
vec0 virtual tables are NOT created by any migration — they are created lazily at runtime via `BaseSQLProvider.createVectorTable()` on the first write of a given embedding dimension (called from `ChatEmbeddingsRepository._upsertVecMessageEmbedding`, internal/database/repositories/chat_embeddings.py L268-284, guarded by a `listTables(tableName)` existence check; `UserMemoriesRepository._upsertVecMemoryEmbedding` mirrors this for `vec_user_memories_{N}`). Post-migration_025 facts:

- vec0 (plus `chat_messages.model_id`) is the SOLE embedding store — the physical `message_embeddings` BLOB side table was DROPPED by migration_025. There is no dual-write anymore: `saveMessageEmbedding()` UPDATEs `chat_messages.model_id` and INSERTs into the dimension-specific vec0 table.
- migration_025 touches vec0 directly: its `up()` DROPS both vec0 families (`_dropVec0Families`, listTables + `_<digits>` regex) because vec0 DDL is not ALTER-able and the partition key changed from `model TEXT` to `model_id INTEGER`. Its `down()` deliberately does not recreate them — they rebuild lazily at runtime.
- The CRON backfill job (`ChatSearchHandler._dtCronJob`) calls `embedAndSaveMessage()` → `getMessagesWithoutEmbeddings()` discovers rows via the `chat_messages.model_id` predicate (NULL or != current model_id) — there is no INSERT...SELECT...JOIN migration backfill.
- Runtime model-drift cleanup: `ChatEmbeddingsRepository.deleteObsoleteModelEmbeddings()` (triggered by `_dtCronJob` on embedding-model change) lists `vec_message_embeddings_%` tables, filters shadow tables via `^vec_message_embeddings_\d+$`, and DELETEs stale-`model_id` rows — it does not DROP tables.
- Historical: an early design sketched a `migration_019_vec0_embeddings.py` with backfill; it was never implemented (migration_019 is the webhook_updates table).

title: BaseSQLProvider new methods: listTables() and createVectorTable()
content:
Two vector-search methods on `BaseSQLProvider` (internal/database/providers/base.py):

1. **`listTables(likePattern: str = "%") -> list[str]`** (line 558) — concrete default body raises `NotImplementedError` (NOT `@abstractmethod`). ONLY `SQLite3Provider` overrides it: `SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name LIKE :pattern`. SQLinkProvider, MySQLProvider, and PostgreSQLProvider inherit the raising default (the SHOW TABLES / pg_tables implementations sketched in the design doc were never implemented).

2. **`createVectorTable(tableName: str, columns: list[VectorColumnDef]) -> None`** (line 578) — same concrete-default-raise pattern; only SQLite3Provider implements it, mapping `VectorColumnType` (TEXT/INTEGER/FLOAT/BLOB/VECTOR) to vec0 DDL (`FLOAT[{dim}] distance_metric={metric}`, `PARTITION KEY` suffix). `VectorColumnDef` TypedDict supports `isPartitionKey`, `vectorDimension`, `distanceMetric`.

This mirrors `vectorSearch`/`isVectorSearchSupported`: concrete defaults so providers without vector support need no overrides (isVectorSearchSupported returns False by default; the other three raise).

title: Gotcha: readonly SQLite3Provider blocks DDL — cannot CREATE TABLE on readonly provider
content:
`SQLite3Provider` sets `PRAGMA query_only = ON` when `readOnly=True` (internal/database/providers/sqlite3.py:116-117). This pragma blocks ALL writes including DDL statements like `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE`. 

This means any code path that calls `createVectorTable()` (or any DDL) on a provider obtained with `readonly=True` will fail at the SQLite level with "attempt to write a readonly database" error. The `getProvider()` method at internal/database/manager.py validates readonly at the manager level, but it's the SQLite3 PRAGMA that enforces it at the connection level — and it's strict: no INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, or DDL is allowed.

In the vector search design (docs/design/vector-search-native.md), `_nativeVectorSearch()` gets a `readonly=True` provider (search path) but tries to call `createVectorTable()` for lazy table creation — this will always fail. Table creation must only happen on `readonly=False` providers (write path, e.g., `saveMessageEmbedding()`). The search path should never create tables; if the table doesn't exist during search, the search should either return empty results (with numpy fallback) or raise a catchable exception.

title: Convention: use NotRequired[], not total=False, for mixed required/optional TypedDicts in this project
content:
The project convention for TypedDicts with both required and optional fields is to keep `total=True` (the default) and mark optional fields with `NotRequired[]` from `typing`. This pattern is used in 71+ locations across the codebase (internal/services/cache/types.py, lib/aurumentation/types.py, lib/geocode_maps/models.py, internal/database/models.py, etc.).

Using `total=False` makes ALL fields optional — including essential ones like `name` and `columnType` in `VectorColumnDef`. This triggers pyright `reportTypedDictNotRequiredAccess` errors when bracket-accessing what should be required fields (e.g., `col["name"]`). The project pattern avoids this.

The correct pattern for `VectorColumnDef`:
```python
class VectorColumnDef(TypedDict):
    name: str
    columnType: VectorColumnType
    isPartitionKey: NotRequired[bool]
    isPrimaryKey: NotRequired[bool]
    vectorDimension: NotRequired[int]
    distanceMetric: NotRequired[str]
```

This makes `name` and `columnType` required (bracket access is safe) while keeping the rest optional (use `.get()` for bracket access or `NotRequired`.

title: Documentation drift: ParametrizedQuery.__init__ docstring says FETCH_ALL default but code is NO_FETCH
content: In `internal/database/providers/base.py`, `ParametrizedQuery.__init__` (line 92) has `fetchType: FetchType = FetchType.NO_FETCH` as the actual default, but the docstring at line 98 says the default is `FetchType.FETCH_ALL`. Per the project rule that code is truth, the code-default (`NO_FETCH`) is correct and the docstring is stale. This affects any code or understanding that relies on the documented default. Should be fixed to match the actual default.

title: Inconsistent typing style in base.py — mixed Optional[] and PEP 604 X|Y
content: In `internal/database/providers/base.py`, the file uses both old-style `from typing import Dict, List, Optional` (pre-3.9) AND PEP 604 union syntax (`X | Y`, Python 3.10+). For example: `query: str | ParametrizedQuery` (line 225) uses `|`, but `params: Optional[QueryParams]` (line 226) on the same method uses `Optional[]`. The file also imports `Dict`, `List`, `Optional` from `typing` (line 13) and uses PEP 695 `type` syntax for aliases (lines 70-77). This mixed style is inconsistent with the rest of the codebase, which (per AGENTS.md) prefers modern typing. No `__all__` is defined in this file.

title: Backfill round-robin scheduling: one chat per cron tick via _backfillIndex
content:
The `ChatSearchHandler._dtCronJob()` backfill processes exactly ONE chat per CRON_JOB tick (~60s), not all enabled chats at once. It uses a round-robin cursor `self._backfillIndex` (int, init 0) to rotate through the sorted list of chats with `EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED = true` (chat_search.py:371-374):

```
chatList = sorted(self._trackedChats)
chatId = chatList[self._backfillIndex % len(chatList)]
self._backfillIndex += 1
self._backfillIndex %= len(chatList)
```

This spread is deliberate — it avoids hammering the embedding API with large batches across all chats simultaneously. Each tick also calls `asyncio.sleep(BACKFILL_INTER_MESSAGE_DELAY_SECS = 0.1)` (defined in internal/bot/constants.py:252) between individual message embeddings within a batch.

The batch size is configurable via `[search-history.embeddings].reindex-batch-size` (default **100**, set in configs/00-defaults/search-history.toml:10). The CRON call to `getMessagesWithoutEmbeddings` passes both `modelName` and `dimensions` keyword args (chat_search.py:428-432) for model-change and dimension-mismatch detection.

title: SQLite3Provider: PRAGMAs in connect() — only 3, all conditional, no performance tuning
content:
`SQLite3Provider.connect()` (internal/database/providers/sqlite3.py, connect() starts at line 162) configures exactly three PRAGMAs, all conditional:

1. `PRAGMA query_only = ON` — only if `self.readOnly` is True (line 188).
2. `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL` — only if `self.useWal` is True (line 190).
3. `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` — only if `self.enableForeignKeys` is True (default True) (line 192).

The only non-PRAGMA connection setup is `connection.row_factory = aiosqlite.Row` (line 186, unconditional).

**sqlite-vec extension loading happens eagerly in connect()** (lines 194-220): after PRAGMAs, if `_SQLITE_VEC_AVAILABLE` is True, the helper `_loadSqliteVecExtension()` is called. On success, `self._vectorSearchAvailable = True` (line 211); on failure, `False` (line 214). Loading uses `enable_load_extension(True)` → `load_extension(sqlite_vec.loadable_path())` → `enable_load_extension(False)`. There is a secondary lazy fallback in `vectorSearch()` (lines 522-523) but the primary path is eager.

**Notably absent PRAGMAs** (not set anywhere in connect()): synchronous (defaults FULL), cache_size (defaults -2000/2MB), busy_timeout (defaults 0), temp_store (defaults FILE), mmap_size (defaults 0), page_size (defaults 4096). If `useWal` is False, no fallback journal_mode PRAGMA is set.

The `aiosqlite.connect()` call (line ~178) uses `dbPath` and `timeout=self.timeout`.

Pattern for adding conditional PRAGMAs: `await connection.execute("PRAGMA name = value")` guarded by a config-derived boolean, same as the existing three. Note: the previously-documented claim 'no extension loading in connect()' is now FALSE — sqlite-vec IS loaded eagerly.

title: Model change detection for embeddings: DB query-level, not application-level
content:
When the user switches the `EMBEDDING_MODEL` chat setting, the backfill re-embeds old messages automatically — detection happens at the DATABASE QUERY level, not in application code. Post-migration_025, `db.chatEmbeddings.getMessagesWithoutEmbeddings(chatId, *, limit=100, modelName=None, dimensions=None, dataSource=None)` (chat_embeddings.py:450) resolves `(modelName, dimensions)` to an integer `model_id` via the injected resolver and returns `chat_messages` rows (joined with chat_users) where `model_id IS NULL OR model_id != :currentModelId`. When `modelName` is None, only `model_id IS NULL` rows are returned.

So rows embedded under the old model show up as pending on the next cron tick and get re-embedded under the new model — no separate comparison logic in the handler (the handler passes `modelName=modelName, dimensions=currentDims`, chat_search.py ~line 491). This is distinct from vec0 stale-row cleanup, handled by `deleteObsoleteModelEmbeddings` gated by the in-memory `_embeddingModelTracker`.

title: Semantic search is rate-limited at the LLM budget level, not separately
content:
Both the `/search` slash command and the `search_messages` LLM tool gate embedding generation through `llmService.rateLimit(chatId, chatSettings)`. This means semantic searches consume from the user's per-chat LLM budget, just like regular LLM requests. There is no separate rate limiter for embeddings.

Applied at:
- `ChatSearchHandler.searchCommand` (line ~940)
- `ChatSearchHandler._llmToolSearchMessages` (line ~460)

The rate limit check happens before the embedding API call, so abuse of `/search` can be controlled via the same budget controls as regular bot usage.

title: Vector search methods are concrete NotImplementedError defaults, not abstract
content: The 4 vector search methods on BaseSQLProvider (`vectorSearch`, `listTables`, `createVectorTable`, `isVectorSearchSupported`) are CONCRETE methods with default implementations, not abstract methods. This is a deliberate design choice: providers that don't support native vector search (e.g. a plain SQLite3 provider without sqlite-vec) don't need to implement these methods at all. Three of the methods raise `NotImplementedError` by default; `isVectorSearchSupported` returns `False` by default. Providers with vector support override the subset they support.

title: queryVector parameter is pre-serialized bytes, not raw floats
content: The `vectorSearch()` method on BaseSQLProvider accepts `queryVector: bytes` — the query vector must be pre-serialised to the provider's expected binary format (e.g. `array.array("f", floats).tobytes()` for sqlite-vec float32). This design avoids an extra copy/conversion inside the provider. Callers must know the expected binary format and serialise before calling. This is documented in the method's docstring.

title: _MinimalProvider pattern for testing abstract class concrete defaults
content:
When testing concrete (non-abstract) default methods on a class with abstract methods (like testing vector search defaults on BaseSQLProvider), the pattern is to create a minimal concrete subclass in the test file that implements all abstract methods with type-annotated stubs. This avoids needing a real database provider. Example from `tests/database/providers/test_vector_search.py`:

```python
class _MinimalProvider(BaseSQLProvider):
    async def connect(self) -> None: pass
    async def disconnect(self) -> None: pass
    async def _execute(self, query: ParametrizedQuery) -> QueryResult: pass
    async def batchExecute(self, queries: Sequence[ParametrizedQuery]) -> Sequence[QueryResult]: return []
    async def upsert(self, table: str, values: Dict[str, Any], conflictColumns: List[str], updateExpressions: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> bool: return True
    async def isReadOnly(self) -> bool: return False
    def applyPagination(self, query: str, limit: Optional[int], offset: int = 0) -> str: return query
    def getTextType(self, maxLength: Optional[int] = None) -> str: return "TEXT"
    def getCaseInsensitiveComparison(self, column: str, param: str) -> str: return f"LOWER({column}) = LOWER({param})"
    def getLikeComparison(self, column: str, param: str) -> str: return f"LOWER({column}) LIKE LOWER({param})"
```

Key differences from earlier snippets: (1) all methods now have full type annotations per project conventions, (2) `batchExecute` returns `[]` not `pass` (which would implicitly return None), (3) `upsert` returns `True` not `pass`. This pattern is defined inline in `test_vector_search.py` (line 16-135).

title: Correction: git checkout + freeze is not enough when venv has leaked packages
content:
When the task is to regenerate `requirements.txt` with only a new package added, the naive approach of:

1. `git checkout requirements.txt` (restore to clean state)
2. `pip install <new-package>`
3. `make freeze-requirements`

**does NOT work** if the venv contains leaked packages from prior manual installs or ext_module development. Those leaked packages remain in the venv and get captured into `requirements.txt` by `pip freeze`.

The correct approach is to FIRST clean the venv (either recreate it or uninstall leaked packages), THEN install the new package, THEN freeze.

**Wrong approach** (what the user initially proposed):
```
git checkout requirements.txt         # restores file, but venv still dirty
pip install sqlite-vec==0.1.9
make freeze-requirements              # re-captures all leaked packages!
```

**Correct approach** (what was actually done):
```
# Option A: recreate venv and install from scratch
rm -rf venv && make install && pip install sqlite-vec==0.1.9 && make freeze-requirements

# Option B: just uninstall leaks (faster)
pip uninstall <leaked-packages>
pip install sqlite-vec==0.1.9
make freeze-requirements
```

Root cause of the mistake: assuming `git checkout` + re-freeze is sufficient when the contamination is in the venv, not in the file.

title: Convention: test stubs overriding abstract methods need full type hints + structured docstrings
content:
When writing test stub classes that override abstract methods from `BaseSQLProvider` (or any abstract base), every override method must have:

1. Full type hints matching the abstract signature exactly (including `Sequence[ParametrizedQuery]`, `dict[str, Any]`, `Optional[...]`, `QueryResult`, etc.)
2. Structured docstrings with `Args:` and `Returns:` sections, even for trivial stubs. Use "No-op stub." or similar for the summary line.

This was applied to `_MinimalProvider` in `tests/database/providers/test_vector_search.py` during a code review fix. The abstract signatures from `BaseSQLProvider` should be imported from `internal.database.providers.base` (absolute import path, even in tests).

Necessary import pattern:
```python
from collections.abc import Sequence
from typing import Any, Optional
from internal.database.providers.base import (
    BaseSQLProvider, ParametrizedQuery, QueryResult, ...
)
```

title: Gotcha: `make format` (black) may reformat pre-existing dirty files, causing git stash conflicts
content:
When the working tree has pre-existing uncommitted changes (e.g., `.opencode/memory.jsonl`, `main.py`, `requirements*.txt`), running `make format` triggers black which may reformat those files (e.g., trailing-whitespace cleanup on comments). This creates a conflict with `git stash` operations: if you stash your changes before running quality gates, the stash captures the pre-dirty state, but black modifies the working tree, causing stash pop failures.

Workaround: Before running `make format lint`, ensure the working tree is clean of unrelated changes. Or after `make format`, restore unrelated files with `git checkout <file>` before popping the stash.

In this session, `main.py` had a pre-existing trailing-whitespace edit that black reformatted, causing a `git stash pop` conflict when trying to recover the base.py changes from the stash.

title: sqlite-vec has zero Python transitive dependencies
content: Confirmed during requirements.txt freeze review: sqlite-vec==0.1.9 was added to requirements.txt and the freeze diff showed only that single line (+sqlite-vec==0.1.9) with zero additional packages. This confirms sqlite-vec has no Python package dependencies (it's a native C extension that bundles its own shared library). The freeze-requirements contamination fix was verified by code review — the diff against the pre-change state was clean, with none of the 12 unrelated packages (brotli, cssselect2, fonttools, lxml, onnxruntime, pydyf, pyphen, tinycss2, tinyhtml5, weasyprint, webencodings, zopfli) from the prior dirty-freeze appearing.

title: sqlite-vec==0.1.9 is the actually installed version (design doc had 0.1.10)
content:
The actually-used sqlite-vec version is 0.1.9 (the design doc's 0.1.10 was never adopted). Current state (verified 2026-08):

- `requirements.direct.txt` line 16: `sqlite-vec==0.1.9` (under `# Runtime`).
- `requirements.txt` (frozen): sqlite-vec is ABSENT — a known open issue (a fresh `make install` from the frozen file will NOT install sqlite-vec; native vector search silently degrades to unavailable, semantic search returns []). Regenerating via `make freeze-requirements` is needed, or install manually.
- `tests/dependencies/test_sqlite_vec.py` pins behavior to 0.1.9 via `SELECT vec_version()` and asserts the pinned version at runtime.
- numpy==2.5.2 IS in the frozen requirements (still used outside chat search).

title: Test naming: default NotImplementedError tests should not say "unsupported"
content:
The test `test_vectorSearchUnsupportedMetric` was renamed to `test_vectorSearchDefaultRaisesRegardlessOfMetric` because the old name was misleading. The default `BaseSQLProvider.vectorSearch()` raises `NotImplementedError` for ANY metric (including valid ones like COSINE, L2, DOT_PRODUCT), not just for "unsupported" metrics. The behavior being tested is that the default implementation always raises regardless of input, not that a particular metric is unsupported. 

When naming tests for default/abstract method implementations that unconditionally raise, prefer the pattern `test_<methodName>DefaultRaisesRegardlessOf<param>` over `test_<methodName>Unsupported<param>`, because the latter implies conditional behavior based on input.

Location: `tests/database/providers/test_vector_search.py::test_vectorSearchDefaultRaisesRegardlessOfMetric`

title: @patch context manager exits at sync fixture return, breaking async test body calls
content:
When a sync `@pytest.fixture` uses `with patch(...)` around provider construction then returns the provider, the patch context manager exits before the test body runs. If an async test method then calls a method (e.g. `connect()`) that reads the patched module-level flag, it sees the REAL (unpatched) value — not the intended test condition.

**The fix**: Use `monkeypatch.setattr` in the fixture. Example:

```python
@pytest.fixture
def providerWithoutVec(self, tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        "internal.database.providers.sqlite3._SQLITE_VEC_AVAILABLE",
        False,
    )
    provider = SQLite3Provider(dbPath=str(tmp_path / "test.db"))
    return provider
```

`monkeypatch` auto-reverts at test teardown (after the test function completes, including async), so the patch stays active through `connect()` calls in the test body.

The original failing fixture used:
```python
with patch("internal.database.providers.sqlite3._SQLITE_VEC_AVAILABLE", False):
    provider = SQLite3Provider(...)
    return provider  # BUG: patch exits here, connect() in test sees real value
```

This is a general pattern: sync fixtures that need to mock a module-level state for async test methods should use `monkeypatch`, not `with patch(...)`.

title: sqlite-vec extension loaded eagerly at connect time in SQLite3Provider (deviates from design doc)
content:
sqlite-vec is loaded EAGERLY inside `SQLite3Provider.connect()` (sqlite3.py ~lines 194-220), right after PRAGMA setup — this deviates from the design doc's lazy-loading strategy. Current shape:

- Extension source resolution: `sqlite_vec.loadable_path()` when the pip package is importable (`_SQLITE_VEC_AVAILABLE`); else `self._vectorExtensionPath` (config `vectorExtensionPath`, Alpine/source-built fallback); else skip.
- `_loadSqliteVecExtension(connection, extensionSource)` is called with the LOCAL `connection` variable — `self._connection` is still None at that point (assigned only at line ~222).
- Success: `logger.info("sqlite-vec %s loaded from %s", ...)` + `_vectorSearchAvailable = True`. Failure: `logger.warning(...)` + False (silent degradation, no crash).

`isVectorSearchSupported()` is no longer a plain flag read — it auto-connects when `self._connection is None` (and disconnects again when `keepConnection` is False) so capability detection works on fresh providers. `vectorSearch()` has a secondary lazy auto-connect (`if not self._vectorSearchAvailable and _SQLITE_VEC_AVAILABLE: await self.connect()`), but the primary path is eager.

title: Test file imports must be at module top, even when brief specifies inline imports
content:
Confirmed: The project AGENTS.md rule "All imports at top of file" applies strictly — even to test files, even when a detailed implementation brief specifies inline imports inside test methods.

The brief for `test_sqlite3_vector_search.py` had `import array` and `from internal.database.providers.base import VectorColumnType, VectorDistanceMetric` inside individual test methods. During implementation these were hoisted to module-level, matching the project convention.

This also avoids `redundant-import` pyright/lint warnings when the same import appears in multiple methods.

title: Vec0 model-change cleanup in ChatSearchHandler._dtCronJob
content:
`_dtCronJob` in `ChatSearchHandler` (internal/bot/common/handlers/chat_search.py, cleanup block ~lines 457-481) delegates model-change cleanup to `ChatEmbeddingsRepository.deleteObsoleteModelEmbeddings()`:

1. Resolves `modelName` from `chatSettings[ChatSettingsKey.EMBEDDING_MODEL]`; bails if model missing or `not model.supportsEmbedding`.
2. `currentDims = await model.getDimensions()` (async, on AbstractModel).
3. Builds `modelKey` as a STRING — `f"{modelName}:{currentDims}"` when dims is not None, else bare `modelName` (the tracker is `Dict[int, str]`; it is NOT a tuple key).
4. If `_embeddingModelTracker.get(chatId) != modelKey`, calls `await self.db.chatEmbeddings.deleteObsoleteModelEmbeddings(chatId=chatId, currentModel=modelName, currentDimensions=currentDims)`.
5. Only on True return updates `_embeddingModelTracker[chatId] = modelKey` — a failed cleanup is retried on the next tick.

The repository handles all provider access (`readonly=False`), `listTables("vec_message_embeddings_%")` with shadow-table regex filtering and NotImplementedError catching, and both the `chat_messages.model_id` clear and vec0 mirror deletes. Tests: tests/bot/common/handlers/test_chat_search_cleanup.py (uses `# type: ignore[method-assign]` mock pattern; `_makeDatabase()` in test_chat_search.py pre-wires `db.chatEmbeddings.deleteObsoleteModelEmbeddings` as an AsyncMock).

title: Obtaining a writable SQL provider from Database via db.manager.getProvider
content:
When code needs direct database provider access (not through a repository), it can obtain a writable or readonly provider via `Database.manager.getProvider()`. The `Database` class has a public `manager` attribute (declared in `__slots__` at database.py:108, typed as `DatabaseManager`) that exposes:

```python
async def getProvider(
    self,
    *,
    chatId: Optional[int] = None,
    dataSource: Optional[str] = None,
    readonly: bool = False,  # NOTE: default is False (writable), NOT True
) -> BaseSQLProvider
```

Pattern for a writable provider:
```python
provider = await self.db.manager.getProvider(chatId=chatId, readonly=False)
```

Pattern for a readonly provider:
```python
provider = await self.db.manager.getProvider(chatId=chatId, readonly=True)
```

The method is at manager.py:103. This is the same entry point the repositories use internally. The `dataSource` parameter is optional — if omitted, the manager resolves the appropriate data source from the chat's routing configuration.

Used in `ChatSearchHandler._dtCronJob` cleanup block and in repositories (e.g. `chat_embeddings.py`, `chat_search.py`) to get providers for database operations.

title: listTables raises NotImplementedError on SQLinkProvider — must catch when used
content:
`BaseSQLProvider.listTables(likePattern: str = "%") -> list[str]` (internal/database/providers/base.py:558) is a CONCRETE method with a body that raises `NotImplementedError` — it is NOT decorated `@abstractmethod`. Only `SQLite3Provider` overrides it (`SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name LIKE :pattern`). SQLinkProvider, MySQLProvider, and PostgreSQLProvider all inherit the raising default.

Same for `createVectorTable` (base.py:578): concrete default raise, SQLite-only override.

Any code calling `listTables` must handle `NotImplementedError`. The canonical catch pattern now lives in `ChatEmbeddingsRepository.deleteObsoleteModelEmbeddings` (chat_embeddings.py ~line 432): `except NotImplementedError: logger.debug(...)` around the vec0 table walk. Note that `isVectorSearchSupported() == True` does NOT guarantee `listTables` is implemented — they are independent methods.

title: vec0 DELETE WHERE on metadata columns may fail — fallback to rowid-based DELETE
content:
In the dual-write helper `_upsertVecMessageEmbedding()` (`internal/database/repositories/chat_embeddings.py`), the initial attempt uses:

```python
await sqlProvider.execute(
    f"DELETE FROM {tableName} "
    f"WHERE chat_id = :chatId AND message_id = :messageId AND model = :model",
    {...},
)
```

Some vec0 backends may reject DELETE with WHERE predicates on metadata columns (non-rowid columns). The implementation wraps this in a try/except and falls back to a two-step approach:
1. `SELECT rowid FROM {tableName} WHERE chat_id = :chatId AND message_id = :messageId AND model = :model`
2. `DELETE FROM {tableName} WHERE rowid = :rowid`

This fallback ensures the dual-write works even on vec0 implementations that only support rowid-based deletes.

title: saveMessageEmbedding date parameter threaded through embedding_utils from EnsuredMessage.date
content:
The `_upsertVecMessageEmbedding()` helper needs the message date (ISO-8601 string) for the vec0 table. `saveMessageEmbedding()` in `chat_embeddings.py` originally had no `date` parameter. The change:

1. Added `date: Optional[str] = None` keyword-only parameter to `saveMessageEmbedding()`.
2. In `embedding_utils.py`'s `embedAndSaveMessage()`, `EnsuredMessage.date` is a `datetime.datetime` — must convert via `.isoformat()` when passing: `date=ensuredMessage.date.isoformat() if ensuredMessage.date is not None else None`.
3. Inside `saveMessageEmbedding()`, if `date` is None, falls back to `now.isoformat()` (where `now` is the existing local variable).

This is necessary because `chat_messages.date` is stored as ISO-8601 TEXT in SQLite (via `convertToSQLite()`), and the vec0 `date` column is also TEXT.

title: _loadSqliteVecExtension fix: outer try/except for enable_load_extension failure
content:
The `_loadSqliteVecExtension()` fix required more than just an inner try/finally. The actual implementation uses nested try blocks:

- **Outer try/except**: catches the case where `enable_load_extension(True)` itself fails (e.g., macOS Apple Python where the extension-loading API isn't compiled in). Returns `None` immediately.
- **Inner try/finally**: wraps `load_extension()` + `vec_version()` call, ensuring `enable_load_extension(False)` runs even if loading fails.

This two-layer pattern is necessary because `enable_load_extension()` itself can raise, and the finally block must only run if the enable succeeded. The outer try/except prevents the AttributeError from leaking on systems without extension-loading support.

title: saveMessageEmbedding date=None falls back to datetime.now() — weakens vec0 recency contract
content:
In `internal/database/repositories/chat_embeddings.py`, `saveMessageEmbedding()` accepts `date: Optional[str] = None` (chat_embeddings.py:79). When `date` is omitted, it substitutes `now.isoformat()` where `now = libUtils.now()` (line 113):

```python
actualDate = date if date is not None else now.isoformat()
```

**Problem**: The vec0 table's `date` column is meant to hold the actual message timestamp (from `chat_messages.date`) to support correct `maxMessages` recency pre-filtering. Substituting "now" for missing dates means any future direct caller that forgets to pass `date` will write a wrong timestamp — old messages will incorrectly appear as "now" in native search, skewing recency filtering.

**Current callers (both pass date correctly)**:
1. `ChatSearchHandler.embedAndSaveMessage` at `internal/bot/common/handlers/chat_search.py:500` — passes `date=ensuredMessage.date.isoformat() if ensuredMessage.date is not None else None`.
2. `MessagePreprocessorHandler` at `internal/bot/common/handlers/message_preprocessor.py:210` — passes `date=ensuredMessage.date.isoformat() if ensuredMessage.date is not None else None`.

NOTE: the originally-cited caller `embedAndSaveMessage` in `internal/bot/common/embedding_utils.py` no longer exists — that file was DELETED; the function was inlined into ChatSearchHandler. The method contract remains unsafe for future callers.

**Suggested fixes**: (1) make `date` required (non-optional) for vector-enabled writes; (2) resolve date from chat_messages when absent; (3) skip the vec0 write with a logged warning when date is absent and vector search is supported.

title: Final fix: vectorSearch() auto-connects internally to preserve keepConnection=False lifecycle
content:
The definitive fix for the vector search lifecycle bug (isVectorSearchSupported() returning False on unconnected providers) was implemented in `SQLite3Provider.vectorSearch()` in `internal/database/providers/sqlite3.py`.

**Previous intermediate fix** (Option B, now superseded): A manual `await sqlProvider.connect()` was added in `_semanticSearch()` before the `isVectorSearchSupported()` check. This broke the `keepConnection=False` lifecycle — the SQLite3Provider cursor tracking sees `wasConnected=True` when connect() was called externally, so `cursor()` skips auto-disconnect, effectively pinning the provider open permanently.

**Final fix**: `vectorSearch()` now auto-connects internally before the capability check:
```python
if not self._vectorSearchAvailable and _SQLITE_VEC_AVAILABLE:
    await self.connect()
```
The sqlite-vec extension is loaded inside `connect()`, so `_vectorSearchAvailable` stays `False` until a connection is established. The auto-connect fires once to detect capability and populate the flag; subsequent calls skip it since `_vectorSearchAvailable` is now `True`. The manual `connect()` was removed from `_semanticSearch()` — both the native path (through `vectorSearch()`) and the numpy path (through `executeFetchAll` → `cursor()` → `connect()`) self-connect. The `keepConnection=False` contract is restored: connections open and close per operation as intended.

**Files changed**: `internal/database/providers/sqlite3.py` and `internal/database/repositories/chat_search.py`.

**Regression test added**: `test_vectorSearchAutoConnectsWhenUnconnected` in `tests/database/providers/test_sqlite3_vector_search.py` — verifies that calling `vectorSearch()` on a fresh unconnected provider succeeds (results returned + `_vectorSearchAvailable` flips to True) without the caller calling `connect()`. Without the fix this raises `NotImplementedError`.

title: Correction: test mock monkey-patching uses `# type: ignore[method-assign]` not `cast(Any, ...)`
content:
The "No Any type" hard rule in AGENTS.md applies to test code too. The previously recorded convention (memory 678cd785) recommending `cast(Any, handler)` for mock monkey-patching in tests is superseded.

The correct pattern is direct attribute assignment with a per-line pyright suppression:

```python
# Instead of:
handler = cast(Any, ChatSearchHandler(...))
handler.getChatSettings = AsyncMock(return_value=cs)

# Use:
handler = ChatSearchHandler(...)
handler.getChatSettings = AsyncMock(return_value=cs)  # type: ignore[method-assign]
```

This preserves concrete typing while silencing only the single line. The `[method-assign]` error code is preferred over a bare `# type: ignore` because it's more specific.

Files updated to this pattern: `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_chat_search_cleanup.py`. Removed `from typing import Any` and `cast(...)` imports entirely.

See also AGENTS.md §Hard rules: "No `Any` type. Never use `Any` except when a method genuinely accepts any type."

title: vec0 native search applies post-filters after top-K — diverges from numpy pre-filter semantics
content:
`_nativeVectorSearch()` (internal/database/repositories/chat_search.py) fetches top-K nearest neighbours via `vectorSearch(k=topK, filterClause=...)` with only the partition-key filter `(chat_id, model_id)` and the optional maxMessages compound date filter pushed down; the remaining filters (`userFilter`, `categoryFilter`, `maxAgeDays`, `rootMessageId`, `threadId`, `substring`) are applied AFTER ranking via `_filterMessageIds()` (line ~790-814).

Consequence (still true post-migration_025): a filtered query can return fewer than `limit` results — or miss valid hits entirely — when matching rows fall outside the unfiltered top-K, because post-filters can only remove candidates. `maxAgeDays` is still a post-filter, NOT pushed into the vec0 filterClause (the vec0 `date` TEXT column would allow it).

Note: the original Gate-2 framing ("diverges from numpy pre-filter semantics") is obsolete — migration_025 removed the numpy cosine fallback; vec0 is the sole semantic path and returns [] when unavailable. Post-filter behavior is covered by tests (`test_nativeSearchWithPostFilters`, `test_semanticNativeNeedsPostFilterGuardThreadAndSubstring` in tests/database/repositories/).

title: vectorSearch() readonly search path: missing vec0 table raises → numpy fallback, never attempts DDL
content:
`_semanticSearch()` obtains its provider with `readonly=True` (SQLite `PRAGMA query_only = ON` blocks all writes including DDL). Table creation (`createVectorTable()`) happens ONLY in the write path (`saveMessageEmbedding` → `_upsertVecMessageEmbedding`) on a `readonly=False` provider — the search path never issues DDL.

Post-migration_025 (Decision D8): there is NO numpy fallback anymore. If vec0 is unsupported, `vectorSearch()` raises, or the result is empty (table missing/pre-backfill), `_semanticSearch` catches the exception (warning log, exc_info) and returns `[]`. Callers must treat an empty list as "no semantic results", not as an error. This is documented in docs/database-schema.md (vec_message_embeddings_N section).

title: sqlite-vec extension loading: avoid sqlite_vec.load(), use aiosqlite enable/load_extension/disable instead
content: The sqlite-vec extension is loaded via raw aiosqlite calls: `await db.enable_load_extension(True)` → `await db.load_extension(sqlite_vec.loadable_path())` → `await db.enable_load_extension(False)`, wrapped in try/finally. The `sqlite_vec.load(conn)` helper is deliberately NOT used because it accesses `connection._conn` (the raw sqlite3 connection under aiosqlite's async wrapper), which is fragile and bypasses aiosqlite's async safety. Extension availability is verified via `SELECT vec_version()`. The design doc originally proposed `connection.run(_load)` but aiosqlite has no `run()` method (confirmed against aiosqlite 0.22.1 source).

title: vec0 dual-write rowid fallback: if metadata-column DELETE fails, SELECT rowid → DELETE by rowid
content:
The vec0 dual-write in `ChatEmbeddingsRepository._upsertVecMessageEmbedding()` uses DELETE-then-INSERT because vec0 has no unique constraint on metadata columns. Post-migration_025 the metadata columns are `(chat_id, message_id, model_id)` (INTEGER model_id partition key replaced the legacy `model TEXT`).

The fallback trigger is an EXCEPTION from the metadata DELETE (try/except Exception), not a non-unique match: on failure it runs `SELECT rowid FROM {table} WHERE chat_id = :chatId AND message_id = :messageId AND model_id = :modelId`, and if a row is found, `DELETE FROM {table} WHERE rowid = :rowid`. The code comment explains some sqlite-vec builds may restrict WHERE predicates — under the pinned sqlite-vec 0.1.9 the fallback branch is believed dead code (see the tests/dependencies/test_sqlite_vec.py pins), but it is kept as a defensive workaround. Lazy table creation via `listTables(tableName)` + `createVectorTable(...)` happens on the same write path (writable provider only).

title: Compound filter for maxMessages: date + message_id to fix timestamp-ties precision
content:
The native vec0 path (`_nativeVectorSearch()` in internal/database/repositories/chat_search.py, ~line 747-763) computes a cutoff row when `maxMessages` is set and pushes a compound filter into the vec0 MATCH query:

```
(date > :minDate OR (date = :minDate AND message_id >= :minMessageId))
```

Post-migration_025 shape: the cutoff query is a SINGLE-TABLE query on `chat_messages` filtered by `model_id` (the legacy `message_embeddings JOIN chat_messages` was dropped with that table):
```sql
SELECT message_id, date FROM chat_messages
WHERE chat_id = :chatId AND model_id = :modelId
ORDER BY date DESC, message_id DESC
``` + `applyPagination(limit=1, offset=maxMessages-1)`.

Both cutoff columns (`date`, `message_id`) are returned and passed as `minDate`/`minMessageId` filter params. The compound predicate exactly mirrors the cutoff-row selection semantics (`ORDER BY date DESC, message_id DESC`), so messages sharing the cutoff timestamp do not leak into or out of the candidate pool. Note: the original rationale (keeping native and numpy paths consistent) is historical — the numpy cosine fallback was removed entirely in migration_025; vec0 is the sole vector store.

Test: `test_nativeSearchWithMaxMessages` in tests/database/repositories/test_chat_search_native.py:407.

title: AbstractModel embedding API surface: exact inventory of members + cross-provider dimension resolution
content:
Comprehensive inventory of embedding-related members on `AbstractModel` (lib/ai/abstract.py):

**Existing members (always available on every AbstractModel instance):**
1. `supportsEmbedding: bool` — `@property` at abstract.py:455, reads `self._config.get("support_embeddings", False)`. Always available.
2. `_generateEmbeddings(text: str) -> list[float]` — `@abstractmethod`. Must be implemented by every concrete subclass. `YcAIModel` (yc_sdk_provider.py:617) implements it as a stub that raises `NotImplementedError` at line 636 — YC SDK provider does not support embeddings.
3. `generateEmbeddings(text, *, attempts=3, consumerId=None) -> list[float]` — public async method at abstract.py:492. Always available. Raises `NotImplementedError` if `supportsEmbedding` is False, `ValueError` on empty/bad input, `RuntimeError` on retry exhaustion.
4. `getDimensions(forceDetect=False) -> int` — async method at abstract.py:578. The canonical way to query embedding dimensions.

**NOT on AbstractModel:** `embeddingDimensions` is NOT defined anywhere in the codebase. It does NOT exist on `FastembedModel` — an earlier version of this memory incorrectly claimed it was a `@property` at fastembed_provider.py:449. The property was never implemented; it appears only in docstrings (fastembed_provider.py:336, :440) and test mock helpers. The actual dimension is stored privately as `self._dimensions: Optional[int]` on AbstractModel (abstract.py:123) with no public accessor — use `getDimensions()` instead.

**Internal-only dimension config:** `BasicOpenAIModel._generateEmbeddings` reads `embedding_dimensions` from `self._config` and passes it as OpenAI's `dimensions` kwarg. This configured value is NOT exposed as a public property.

**Cross-provider dimension resolution:** `len(await model.generateEmbeddings(text))` or `await model.getDimensions()` are the reliable ways to get embedding dimensions from an arbitrary model object returned by `LLMManager.getModel()`.

title: YcAIModel._generateEmbeddings is a NotImplementedError stub — no embedding support
content: `YcAIModel` (lib/ai/providers/yc_sdk_provider.py) implements `_generateEmbeddings` as a stub that raises `NotImplementedError`. This means the Yandex Cloud SDK provider does not support embeddings at all — any code path that attempts to generate embeddings using a model from the `yc-sdk` provider will hit a `NotImplementedError`. This is intentional behavior, not a missing implementation.

title: Cleanup logic consolidated: deleteObsoleteModelEmbeddings() moved to ChatEmbeddingsRepository
content:
Model-change embedding cleanup lives in `ChatEmbeddingsRepository.deleteObsoleteModelEmbeddings(chatId, currentModel, currentDimensions) -> bool` (internal/database/repositories/chat_embeddings.py:331). Post-migration_025 mechanism:

1. Resolves the canonical integer `model_id` for `(currentModel, currentDimensions)` via the injected `_modelIdResolver` (bound `EmbeddingModelsRepository.getOrCreateModelId`).
2. Authoritative cleanup: `UPDATE chat_messages SET model_id = NULL WHERE chat_id = :chatId AND model_id IS NOT NULL AND model_id != :currentModelId` — there is NO `message_embeddings` BLOB table anymore (dropped by migration_025); provenance is `chat_messages.model_id` referencing the `models` lookup table.
3. Vec0 mirror (best-effort): gated on `isVectorSearchSupported()`; lists `vec_message_embeddings_%` tables (regex-filtered to exclude sqlite-vec shadow tables), deletes non-matching `model_id` rows in the same-dimension table and clears all rows for the chat in other-dimension tables. `listTables` `NotImplementedError` is caught (debug log, skip).

Stateless and idempotent (zero rows on the common path). Outer `except Exception` swallows failures at warning level with exc_info=True and returns False so the handler's `_embeddingModelTracker` is NOT updated (cleanup retried next tick). The handler (`ChatSearchHandler._dtCronJob`) is a thin caller; tests live in tests/bot/common/handlers/test_chat_search_cleanup.py.

title: Reversal: in-memory model tracking reinstated for cleanup gating in _dtCronJob
content:
The model-change cleanup strategy in `ChatSearchHandler._dtCronJob()` uses in-memory tracking, delegating cleanup to `ChatEmbeddingsRepository.deleteObsoleteModelEmbeddings()`.

`_embeddingModelTracker: Dict[int, str]` (chat_search.py:176) tracks chatId -> modelKey. Cleanup only fires when modelKey differs from stored value (line 405). Delegates to `db.chatEmbeddings.deleteObsoleteModelEmbeddings(chatId=chatId, currentModel=modelName, currentDimensions=currentDims)` (lines 413-417) — NOTE: the call passes `currentDimensions=currentDims`, not just `(chatId, currentModel)` as previously documented.

modelKey construction (lines 402-404): `modelName` alone when `currentDims is None`; `f"{modelName}:{currentDims}"` when the model exposes dimensions.

Key distinction from earlier approaches: this version doesn't rely on tracking for correctness (the repo method is idempotent and safe to call) — the tracker is purely an optimization to avoid redundant work on every CRON tick. If restarted, the tracker is empty and cleanup fires once (idempotent), which is correct.

title: Pyright workaround: use getattr instead of hasattr for optional model attributes not on AbstractModel
content:
When pyright rejects `hasattr(model, "someAttr")` + subsequent attribute access because pyright doesn't narrow types based on `hasattr`, use `getattr(model, "someAttr", None)` instead. This produces identical runtime behavior (None when the attribute is absent) and pyright is satisfied because `getattr` with a default is dynamically typed.

**Verified fact**: `embeddingDimensions` is NOT defined on `FastembedModel`, `AbstractModel`, or any other class — `grep -rn "def embeddingDimensions"` across the codebase returns ZERO results (re-verified 2026-08). The name survives only in comments/docstrings.

The handler code no longer uses `getattr(model, "embeddingDimensions", None)` — `ChatSearchHandler._dtCronJob` now obtains dimensions via `currentDims = await model.getDimensions()` (async method on `AbstractModel`, `lib/ai/abstract.py:589`), and builds `modelKey = f"{modelName}:{currentDims}"` (or bare `modelName` when dims is None).

The `getattr(..., None)` pattern remains the correct pyright workaround for any handler code that needs to conditionally access subclass-specific properties on `AbstractModel` instances.

title: Mock auto-creates attributes: must explicitly set embeddingDimensions=None for default test model mock
content:
When using `Mock()` for a model that should NOT expose `embeddingDimensions`, the Mock auto-creates `mockModel.embeddingDimensions` as a child Mock object on first access. This means `getattr(mockModel, "embeddingDimensions", None)` returns a Mock (truthy, not None), which breaks gating logic that checks `if dims is not None:`.

Fix: explicitly set `mockModel.embeddingDimensions = None` in the default test model mock. This makes `getattr` return None, correctly simulating both "attribute doesn't exist on base class" and "model hasn't probed dims yet" cases.

Another option: use `Mock(spec=AbstractModel)` which raises AttributeError for unknown attributes. However, this requires the base class to declare all accessed attributes (like `supportsEmbedding`).

Rule of thumb: when a mock should simulate "attribute does not exist", explicitly set it to `None` rather than relying on Mock's auto-creation or del.

title: Handler tests should not test repo-level concerns after delegation
content:
When a handler delegates database work to a repository method, handler tests should only test the handler-level contract (gating, argument passing), not repo-level concerns. Specifically:

1. The shared `_makeDatabase()` helper should pre-wire the new repo method as `AsyncMock()` so all tests work by default.
2. Tests that verified repo-level internals (e.g., `isVectorSearchSupported()`, `listTables()` behavior, provider fetch failures) through the handler should be removed from handler tests — those belong in the repository's own test suite.
3. Handler tests should verify: correct arguments passed to the repo method, correct gating logic (tracker prevents redundant calls), and that the method is not called on early-return paths (model missing, model doesn't support embedding).

This pattern was applied in the ChatSearchHandler refactor: old inline vec0 cleanup used provider directly, and its tests checked `provider.execute` calls with specific SQL. After delegating to `ChatEmbeddingsRepository.deleteObsoleteModelEmbeddings()`, those 4 repo-level tests were removed from the handler test file, and the remaining tests check the `db.chatEmbeddings.deleteObsoleteModelEmbeddings` mock instead.

title: Full config-to-SQLite3Provider wiring chain through all layers
content:
The complete chain from TOML config to SQLite3Provider instantiation passes through 4 intermediate layers with no transformation:

1. **ConfigManager.getDatabaseConfig()** (internal/config/manager.py:310-324) — returns `self.get("database", {})` raw, no key filtering or transformation.

2. **Database.__init__(config)** (internal/database/database.py:194) — passes the entire `[database]` section dict to `DatabaseManager(config)`.

3. **DatabaseManager.__init__(config)** (internal/database/manager.py:60-89) — stores the config. The `DatabaseManagerConfig` TypedDict expects `default: str`, `chatMapping: Dict[int, str]`, `providers: Dict[str, SQLProviderConfig]`.

4. **DatabaseManager.getProvider(providerName)** (manager.py:170-176) — passes `self.config["providers"][providerName]` to `getSqlProvider()`.

5. **getSqlProvider(config: SQLProviderConfig)** (providers/__init__.py:90-138) — extracts `parameters: dict = config.get("parameters", {})` and calls `SQLite3Provider(**parameters)`.

Key behavioral property: **the `parameters` dict is splatted directly into the constructor with NO filtering**. Any key under `[database.providers.N.parameters]` in TOML becomes a keyword argument. If the constructor doesn't accept it, Python raises TypeError. No transformation, renaming, or validation happens between TOML and the constructor.

This means adding a new SQLite3Provider parameter requires exactly 3 changes with no pipeline modifications:
(a) TOML defaults in `configs/00-defaults/00-config.toml` under `[database.providers.default.parameters]`
(b) Constructor signature + __slots__ entry in `internal/database/providers/sqlite3.py`
(c) Instance attribute initialization in `__init__` body

No changes needed to `getSqlProvider`, `DatabaseManager`, `ConfigManager`, or the TOML parsing pipeline.

title: SQLProviderConfig.parameters is a bare unparameterized dict
content:
In `internal/database/providers/__init__.py:86`, the `SQLProviderConfig` TypedDict defines `parameters: dict` — a bare `dict` with no key/value type parameterization (not `dict[str, Any]` or a specific TypedDict like `SQLite3ProviderParameters`).

Consequence: pyright will NOT catch typos or type mismatches in TOML parameter keys for SQLite3Provider (or any provider). A key like `dbPathe` (typo for `dbPath`) passes type checking silently and only fails at runtime with `TypeError: unexpected keyword argument` when `getSqlProvider()` calls `SQLite3Provider(**parameters)`.

If strict type safety is desired, a new provider-specific TypedDict (e.g., `SQLite3ProviderParameters`) could be created and assigned to `parameters` — but this would complicate `getSqlProvider()` since the type would vary per provider. For now the system is deliberately open to accommodate all providers with the same config type.

title: sqlite-vec extension loading: self._connection is None at connect() call site
content:
In `SQLite3Provider.connect()` the `async def connect()` method has this structure:
1. Opens a new `aiosqlite.Connection` (stored in local `connection`).
2. Calls `_loadSqliteVecExtension(...)` with that local connection.
3. Sets `self._connection = connection`.

`self._connection` is still `None` during step 2. Any reference to `self._connection` at that point (e.g., passing it to `_loadSqliteVecExtension`) will pass `None` instead of a live connection, which pyright catches as `Argument of type "None" cannot be assigned to parameter "connection" of type "Connection"`. Always use the local `connection` variable for the extension-loading call.

Root cause: the agent followed instructions literally that said to use `self._connection`, but the original code used the local `connection` variable because `self._connection` hadn't been assigned yet. The fix is to use the local `connection`, which is the correct, existing pattern.

title: sqlite-vec extension loading: custom path fallback for Alpine/source-built extensions
content:
`SQLite3Provider` now supports two sources for the vec0 extension, resolved in priority order in `connect()`:

1. **pip package path** (`_SQLITE_VEC_AVAILABLE` is True): use `sqlite_vec.loadable_path()` — version-matched, reliable, the default.
2. **Custom filesystem path** (`self._vectorExtensionPath` is not None): fallback when the pip package is unavailable (e.g. Alpine Linux has no musl wheel, extension built from source) — accessed via the `vectorExtensionPath` kwarg on `SQLite3Provider.__init__`.

The previous logic was a simple `if _SQLITE_VEC_AVAILABLE:` guard. The new logic decouples package availability from extension loading: the extension can be loaded even when the Python package isn't importable, as long as the compiled `.so` exists at a known path.

`_loadSqliteVecExtension()` itself was also refactored: it now accepts an `extensionPath` parameter, falling back to `sqlite_vec.loadable_path()` when None. The `connect()` method determines which path to pass.

Relevant config key: `[database.providers.<name>.parameters].vectorExtensionPath`.

title: vectorExtensionPath config parameter under [database.providers.*.parameters]
content:
The `vectorExtensionPath` config parameter lives under `[database.providers.<name>.parameters]` in the TOML config, not under a separate `[database.vectorSearch]` section. It's an `Optional[str]` constructor parameter of `SQLite3Provider`.

Purpose: custom filesystem path to a prebuilt sqlite-vec shared library (`.so`/`.dylib`). When the `sqlite_vec` pip package is unavailable (e.g. Alpine Linux with no musl wheel) but the extension was built from source, the provider loads vec0 from this path instead of the pip-package bundled library.

Loading priority (code at `sqlite3.py` lines 198-221):
1. If `_SQLITE_VEC_AVAILABLE` (pip package installed): use `sqlite_vec.loadable_path()` (the package's bundled .so)
2. Else if `self._vectorExtensionPath is not None`: use the custom config path
3. Otherwise: skip loading, `_vectorSearchAvailable` stays `False`, numpy fallback takes over

When the config key is commented out or omitted, auto-detection via `sqlite_vec.loadable_path()` (Python package) is the first-priority path.

The example in `configs/00-defaults/00-config.toml` (lines 46-51):
```
# Custom path to the sqlite-vec extension (.so/.dylib). Use this when the
# sqlite-vec pip package is unavailable (e.g. Alpine Linux with no musl
# wheel) but the extension was built from source. When set, the provider
# loads vec0 from this path instead of the pip-package bundled library.
# Leave commented (or omit) to auto-detect via the sqlite-vec Python package.
# vectorExtensionPath = "/usr/local/lib/vec0.so"
```

title: vectorExtensionPath config example in 00-config.toml for Alpine/musl environments
content: Added a commented-out `vectorExtensionPath` example to `configs/00-defaults/00-config.toml` (lines 46-51) under `[database.providers.default.parameters]`, between `keepConnection` and the proxy comment block. This documents the custom path to the sqlite-vec shared library for environments where the pip package's prebuilt wheel is unavailable (e.g. Alpine Linux without a musl-compatible wheel). The config key `database.providers.default.parameters.vectorExtensionPath` is referenced by the sqlite-vec extension loading logic in `internal/database/providers/sqlite3.py` to locate the .so/.dylib at runtime.

title: embedAndSaveMessage reverted to EnsuredMessage contract — attachment data needed in embeddings
content:
`embedAndSaveMessage` accepts `(ensuredMessage: EnsuredMessage)` as its sole data parameter (not individual fields). Rationale: the user plans to incorporate content from attachments (available via EnsuredMessage's media resolution) into embedding text. The `EnsuredMessage` contract carries attachment metadata needed for future embedding quality improvements.

**Current location**: `embedAndSaveMessage` is a method on `ChatSearchHandler` in `internal/bot/common/handlers/chat_search.py:461`. The method reads `ensuredMessage.date.isoformat()` for the vec0 `date` column (line 500).

NOTE: This method was originally in a separate `internal/bot/common/embedding_utils.py` module, but that module was subsequently DELETED and its functionality merged into `ChatSearchHandler`. The test file comment at `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_chat_search.py:973` confirms: 're-homed from deleted embedding_utils module'.

The theoretical race condition where a downstream handler mutates `ensuredMessage.messageText` before the background task reads it is accepted as low risk.

title: Rate-limit gate moved inside keywords block — filter-only /search no longer consumes LLM budget
content: In `ChatSearchHandler.search_command()`, the `self.llmService.rateLimit(...)` call was moved from its position before the `if keywords:` block to inside it. Filter-only searches (e.g., `/search user: @alice days: 7` with no keyword text) don't hit the embedding API or LLM, yet previously consumed the chat's LLM rate-limit budget. Now the rate limit only gates semantic searches (which actually use the embedding model).

title: Small nitpick fixes applied: _backfillIndex bounded, lambda→_embedSync, _dtCronJob docstring renumbered
content:
Three small fixes applied during code-review cleanup of the chat-search branch:

1. **`_backfillIndex` bounded** — After `self._backfillIndex += 1`, added `self._backfillIndex %= len(enabledChats)` to keep it bounded. Python ints are arbitrary precision so no overflow risk, but cleaner.

2. **Lambda → `_embedSync` helper** — In `LocalEmbeddingsProvider._generateText()`, replaced `lambda: list(embedding.embed([text]))` with a module-level helper function `_embedSync(embedding, text)` called via `asyncio.to_thread(_embedSync, embedding, text)`. More explicit, avoids closure-variable capture fragility.

3. **`_dtCronJob` docstring renumbered** — After the `_searchEnabled` kill-switch step was removed, the numbered list in the docstring skipped from step 1 to step 3. Renumbered steps 3→2, 4→3, 5→4, 6→5.

title: Parallel subagent edits on same file require explicit reconciliation
content:
When dispatching parallel `software-developer` tasks that both modify the same file (in this case, `internal/bot/common/handlers/chat_search.py` was edited by both Group A and Group B subagents), conflicts arise. Key conflicts from this session:
- Group A removed a `_searchEnabled` kill-switch check (correct — dead code); Group B re-added it as a "bonus fix" (incorrect — misunderstood the architecture).
- The second subagent's changes can overwrite the first subagent's if both read the original and write independently.

Mitigation: avoid parallel dispatch to the same file. If unavoidable, add a dedicated reconciliation step after both batches complete to verify all changes are applied and resolve conflicts. The reconciliation should verify each intended change by reading the file state and checking for contradictions.

title: Test pattern: LLM tool gating tests in ChatSearchHandler — mock getChatSettings + assert error dict
content:
When testing LLM tool gating in ChatSearchHandler (ALLOW_TOOLS_COMMANDS, EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED), the established pattern is:

## Pattern

1. **Mock `getChatSettings`** on the handler to return a dict where the relevant gate evaluates to `False`.
2. **Set up `extraData`** with a mock `EnsuredMessage` containing `recipient.id`.
3. **Call the tool handler directly** (e.g., `await handler._llmToolSearchMessages(extraData=extraData, query="test")`).
4. **Assert error dict** — the tool returns `{"done": False, "error": "..."}` (Russian error message, never raises).

## Example implementation

```python
class TestSearchMessagesLLMTool:
    async def test_tools_disabled(self, handler: ChatSearchHandler) -> None:
        """ALLOW_TOOLS_COMMANDS disabled → error dict, no DB calls."""
        extraData = {"ensuredMessage": _makeMessage(recipientId=-100123)}
        mockSettings = _makeChatSettings(allowTools=False)
        with patch.object(handler, "getChatSettings", AsyncMock(return_value=mockSettings)):
            result = await handler._llmToolSearchMessages(extraData=extraData, query="poem")
        assert result["done"] is False
        assert "отключены" in result.get("error", "")

    async def test_embeddings_disabled(self, handler: ChatSearchHandler) -> None:
        """EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED disabled → error dict before embedding."""
        extraData = {"ensuredMessage": _makeMessage(recipientId=-100123)}
        mockSettings = _makeChatSettings(allowTools=True, embeddingsEnabled=False)
        with patch.object(handler, "getChatSettings", AsyncMock(return_value=mockSettings)):
            result = await handler._llmToolSearchMessages(extraData=extraData, query="poem")
        assert result["done"] is False
        assert "поиска" in result.get("error", "") or "отключен" in result.get("error", "")
```

## Helper

```python
def _makeChatSettings(allowTools: bool = True, embeddingsEnabled: bool = True) -> ChatSettingsDict:
    return {
        ChatSettingsKey.ALLOW_TOOLS_COMMANDS: ChatSettingsValue(allowTools, "test"),
        ChatSettingsKey.EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED: ChatSettingsValue(embeddingsEnabled, "test"),
        # ... other required keys ...
    }
```

The helper fixture is defined in the test file and reused across test classes for `search_messages`, `list_users`, and `get_thread` tools.

## Coverage requirements

Test these gates for every LLM tool:
- Missing `extraData` / `ensuredMessage` context → error dict
- `ALLOW_TOOLS_COMMANDS` disabled → error dict with `"отключен"` or similar
- Feature-specific gate disabled (e.g., `EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED` for `search_messages`) → error dict
- `getChatSettings` raises → error dict
- Repository raises → error dict
- Happy path → `{"done": True, ...}`

title: Health-check-type presence IS the restart signal — no separate `restart-on-failure` flag needed
content: Design decision (2026-06-26, still in effect Aug 2026): the `restart-on-failure` boolean was removed as redundant — if `health-check-type = "url" | "command"` is configured, health monitoring runs and a failed check triggers restart (`ProxyLifecycle.onCronTick` → `restart()`); `health-check-type = "none"` means no checks and no restart. `max-restarts` was likewise eliminated — retries are unlimited, bounded naturally by the cron interval (no backoff needed since checks run every few minutes). Confirmed: no `restartOnFailure`/`maxRestarts` keys exist anywhere in `internal/services/proxy/`. Config shape: `health-check-type` + `health-check-interval` (minutes, default 5). Design doc now lives at `docs/archive/plans/proxy-lifecycle-design.md` (moved from docs/plans/); durable summary in `docs/llm/memories/proxy-lifecycle.md`.

title: _formatMessageDict reverted — tests fixed to match production camelCase output, production untouched
content:
The `_formatMessageDict` method was initially "fixed" to produce snake_case keys matching its docstring, but the user **reverted that fix**. The production code remains as-is: `_formatMessageDict` delegates to `EnsuredMessage.formatForLLM(..., format=LLMMessageFormat.JSON, ...)` which returns camelCase keys (`messageId`, `text`, `login`, `name`, `replyId`, `date`), drops keys with falsy values (so `replyId` is absent when None, not present-with-value-None), and does NOT produce `thread_id`.

The tests in `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_chat_search.py` were fixed to match the actual production output instead. Key changes:
- `message_id` → `messageId` (int, not string)
- `message_text` → `text`
- `username` → `login`
- `full_name` → `name`
- `reply_id` → `replyId` (absent when None, not present-with-None)
- `thread_id` assertion removed (production doesn't produce it)

The `_llmToolSearchMessages` `formatted.append(retMsg)` fix (missing append was the real bug causing empty search results) was **kept** — only `_formatMessageDict` was reverted.

title: ProxyLifecycle commands all optional — empty command lists are no-ops
content:
All three lifecycle commands (`start-command`, `stop-command`, `restart-command`) in `ProxyLifecycleConfigDict` are optional (the TypedDict is `total=False`). When a command list is empty or missing, the corresponding method becomes a no-op:

- `start()`: empty `startCommand` → sets `_started = True` and returns immediately (no subprocess launched)
- `stop()`: empty `stopCommand` → returns immediately (no kill attempt)
- `restart()`: empty `restartCommand` → falls back to calling `stop()` then `start()` sequentially

This means you can configure a lifecycle with just `start-command` (let the OS clean up on exit), just `stop-command` (kill an externally-managed proxy), or both. A lifecycle with neither is pointless but handled without crashing — `_started` flips to True but no process runs, and health checks/restarts become meaningless.

title: Global proxy lifecycle NOT duplicated to per-service — resolveProxy creates no lifecycle for inherited configs
content:
When a service doesn't have its own `[service.proxy.lifecycle]` section, `ProxyService.resolveProxy()` returns early WITHOUT creating a new `ProxyLifecycle` instance. The service inherits the global proxy (and its lifecycle data) via `getCombined()`, but only as data on the `ProxyConfig` object — NOT as a managed process.

The effect: only `ProxyLifecycle("global", ...)` exists in `ProxyService._activeLifecycles`. All services that use the global proxy share this single lifecycle instance. There is NO per-service lifecycle duplication — one SSH tunnel, one health check schedule, one stop-on-shutdown.
