title: collectOrphanContainers date-parsing fail-open: unparseable createdAt leads to removal, not skip
content:
In `GarbageCollector.collectOrphanContainers()` at `lib/sandbox/gc.py:194-199`, the container `createdAt` string is parsed with `datetime.fromisoformat(createdAt.replace("Z", "+00:00")).timestamp()`. If this parsing fails (ValueError from malformed date, OSError from system issues), the exception handler uses bare `pass` — meaning the container **falls through to the kill/remove operations** rather than being skipped.

```python
try:
    createdTs = datetime.fromisoformat(createdAt.replace("Z", "+00:00")).timestamp()
    if createdTs > cutoff:
        continue  # Too young
except (ValueError, OSError):
    pass
```

This is a **fail-open** design: unparseable timestamps are treated as "old enough to remove." This is the opposite of the fail-safe pattern in `collectOrphanWorkspaces()` (line 118-119) where `OSError` during `stat()` causes `continue` (skip the orphan).

The `createdAt.replace("Z", "+00:00")` normalization is necessary because Python's `datetime.fromisoformat()` didn't support the trailing `Z` UTC designator until Python 3.11. Since the project targets Python 3.12+, this is technically unneeded but remains as a defensive pattern.

Implications: A Docker container with a corrupted or missing `createdAt` label will be unconditionally killed and removed by the GC on the next cycle, regardless of age.

title: reproduce_llm_dialog.py: strips randomContext from all messages unlike production break-on-found
content:
The debug script `scripts/reproduce_llm_dialog.py` (lines 390-393) strips `randomContext` from ALL fetched messages' metadata before building the context deque:

```python
if eMsg.metadata.get("randomContext", None) is not None:
    eMsg.metadata.pop("randomContext", None)
```

This is the INVERSE of production behavior in `internal/bot/common/handlers/llm_messages.py` (lines 924-927), which breaks out of the message-collection loop when it encounters a message that already has `randomContext` set:

```python
if eMsg.metadata.get("randomContext", None) is not None:
    break
```

(The equivalent break exists in the script but is deliberately commented out at lines 406-408, marked "Not needed to ensure proper recondensing".)

Consequence: the reproduce script forces re-triggering of the condensing logic on every run (no message carries a pre-existing randomContext), while production short-circuits and stops adding older messages once it finds an already-condensed boundary. The script's output therefore always covers the full fetched message range rather than stopping at the first already-condensed boundary.

title: PythonRuntime.runCommand() full shell command structure with conditional stdin and timeout wrapper
content:
The `PythonRuntime.runCommand()` method (lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/runtime.py, lines 69-85) constructs a shell command with this full structure:

```python
stdinPart = f"< /workspace/.run/{runId}/stdin" if hasStdin else ""

cmd = [
    "timeout",
    "-s", "TERM",
    "-k", str(limits.timeoutGraceSeconds),
    str(limits.timeoutSeconds),
    "sh", "-c",
    (
        f"cd /workspace/.run/{runId}/work && "
        f"python -u /workspace/.run/{runId}/{self.getScriptName()} "
        f"{stdinPart} "
        f"> /workspace/.run/{runId}/stdout.log "
        f"2> /workspace/.run/{runId}/stderr.log"
    ),
]
```

Key details:
- The entire shell command is wrapped in coreutils `timeout -s TERM -k <grace> <seconds> sh -c "..."` — the timeout fires SIGTERM after `timeoutSeconds`, then SIGKILL after `timeoutGraceSeconds`.
- The script name is resolved via `self.getScriptName()` (which returns `"main.py"` but is a method, allowing subclasses to override).
- The stdin redirect (`< /workspace/.run/{runId}/stdin`) is CONDITIONAL — only present when `hasStdin=True`. When False, `stdinPart` is an empty string (with trailing space that becomes harmless).
- stdout and stderr are redirected to files in runDir (not work/), consistent with the design that runDir holds infrastructure files while work/ holds user-created files.
- The `cd /workspace/.run/{runId}/work &&` sets the working directory to work/ but the script itself is executed from the absolute path in runDir/, so script execution is unaffected by the cd.

title: reproduce_llm_dialog.py: never calls condenseContext(), outputs raw pre-condensing message list
content:
The debug script `scripts/reproduce_llm_dialog.py` (lines 411-423) does NOT call `LLMService.condenseContext()` — a grep for `condenseContext` across the file returns zero results.

Instead, when the message count exceeds `MAX_RANDOM_CONTEXT_MESSAGES`, it prepends `condensingSystemPrompt` (as a system role message) and `condensingPrompt` (as a user role message) directly to the `contextMessages` deque:

```python
if len(contextMessages) > constants.MAX_RANDOM_CONTEXT_MESSAGES:
    contextMessages.appendleft(ModelMessage(role="system", content=condensingSystemPrompt))
    contextMessages.append(ModelMessage(role="user", content=condensingPrompt))
```

This means the script outputs the raw pre-condensing message list (what you would send TO a condensing LLM), NOT the actual condensed context. This differs fundamentally from production in `internal/bot/common/handlers/llm_messages.py` (random-context branch, now lines 929-956), which:
1. Calls `self.llmService.condenseContext(...)` with force=True, keepFirstN=0, keepLastN=0, condensingModel (lines 937-946)
2. Persists the merged summary as `ensuredMessage.metadata["randomContext"]` (line 951)
3. Writes the updated metadata back to the database (lines 952-956)

For A/B testing actual condensing behavior, use `scripts/check_condensing.py`, which does call condenseContext(force=True).

title: Sandbox runCode(): no chmod on workDir, created before container runs
content:
Supplementary detail for the existing memory `RunResult.workDir: path format and directory creation in runCode()` (c299744c).

In `SandboxManager.runCode()` (lib/sandbox/manager.py):

1. **No `os.chmod()` on work/ directory:** The only `os.chmod()` call in `runCode()` is on the session workspace directory (`workspacePath`, line 564). The `work/` subdirectory (created at lines 569-570 via `mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)`) receives default OS permissions only — no explicit chmod call is made on it. This is intentional: the work directory is an internal artifact storage area that doesn't need explicit permission hardening like the workspace root.

2. **work/ created before container runs:** The `work/` subdirectory is created at lines 569-570, which is before the container execution at lines 626-651 (`self._backend.runOneshot(...)`). This means when the container starts, the host-side work directory already exists on disk and is ready for the container to write into (via bind mount to `/workspace/.run/{runId}/work`).

Line references (as of June 2026):
- `workDirPath = runDir / "work"` — line 569
- `workDirPath.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` — line 570
- `os.chmod(workspacePath, ...)` — line 564 (the only chmod, not on workDir)
- Container execution (`runOneshot`) — lines 626-651

title: Response format convention: Markdown for human commands, JSON for LLM tools
content:
Confirmed design pattern in internal/bot/common/handlers/sandbox.py: the sandbox handler formats responses differently depending on the entry point:
- `/run` (human-facing slash command): file list rendered as Markdown list with backtick-wrapped paths: `  - \`path\` (X.X KB)` (lines 795-800).
- `run_python` (LLM tool): file list returned as JSON dict with `"files"` key containing array of `{"path": str, "sizeBytes": int, "isDirectory": bool}` objects (lines 335-344).

This is a general convention for the bot: human commands produce formatted Markdown, LLM tools produce structured JSON.

title: SandboxManager.listFiles() method signature and behavior
content:
`SandboxManager.listFiles()` at lib/sandbox/manager.py lines 766-820:

Signature: `async def listFiles(self, sessionId: str, *, path: str = "/", recursive: bool = False) -> list[FileInfo]`

- `sessionId: str` — positional, required.
- `path: str` — keyword-only, defaults to "/" (workspace relative). Internally resolved via `resolveWorkspacePath()` for security.
- `recursive: bool` — keyword-only, defaults to False.

Returns `list[FileInfo]` where `FileInfo` has fields: `path: str`, `sizeBytes: int`, `modifiedAt: datetime`, `isDirectory: bool`.

Used by the handler after `runCode()` to enumerate files created during execution, always called with `path=result.workDir, recursive=True`.

title: Divination systems are class-based with ClassVar attributes, no constructors
content:
TarotSystem and RunesSystem in lib/divination/ are purely class-based designs with no __init__ or __new__ methods. All public methods are @classmethod. Key behavior is hardcoded via ClassVar attributes defined at class body level, not constructor parameters:

- TarotSystem: supportsReversed=True, systemId="tarot", deckId="rws", deck=TAROT_RWS_DECK
- RunesSystem: supportsReversed=False, systemId="runes", deckId="elder_futhark", deck=RUNES_ELDER_FUTHARK_DECK

The ClassVar declarations live on the abstract base class BaseDivinationSystem (lib/divination/base.py:164-167):
  systemId: ClassVar[str]
  deckId: ClassVar[str]
  supportsReversed: ClassVar[bool]
  deck: ClassVar[Tuple[Symbol, ...]]

supportsReversed is consumed in base.py:220 (passed to drawSymbols()) and drawing.py:54 (controls 50% reversal probability). It is NOT a config toggle, NOT a constructor parameter, NOT overridable per-reading — it's statically determined by which system class is used. This follows the project convention documented in AGENTS.md: "Prefer class-based designs over free-function collections."

title: DivinationHandler LLM tool JSON response shape
content:
The `_handleReading` method in `internal/bot/common/handlers/divination.py` (lines 813-838) returns a JSON-encoded dict on the LLM tool path (`if isLLMCall:`) with these exact keys:

```json
{
  "done": true,
  "layout": {
    "id": layout.id,
    "en": layout.nameEn,           // bare English name
    "ru": layout.nameRu,           // bare Russian name from layout object
    "positions": layout.positions
  },
  "draws": [
    {
      "nameEn": d.symbol.name,
      "nameRu": divinationLocalization.tr(divinationLocalization.SYMBOL_NAMES, d.symbol.name, "ru"),  // localized via symbol names table
      "glyph": d.symbol.glyph,
      "reversed": d.reversed,
      "position": d.position,
      "meaning": d.symbol.meaningUpright if not d.reversed else d.symbol.meaningReversed
    }
  ],
  "interpretation": interpretationText,
  "image_sent": imageBytes is not None
}
```

Key facts:
- `"summary"` key is **absent** — not in the response.
- `"imageGenerated"` key is **absent** — the image-sent status uses `"image_sent"` (snake_case).
- `nameRu` uses `divinationLocalization.tr()` for localization, NOT bare English. It looks up symbol names via the `SYMBOL_NAMES` localization table with locale `"ru"`.
- `"en"` and `"ru"` in the layout dict are bare strings from `layout.nameEn` / `layout.nameRu` (not localized via the tr system).
- Error responses use `{"done": false, "errorMessage": "..."}` (lines 634, 702, 491).

title: Image send in _handleReading: empty caption, per-path messageCategory, typingManager commented out
content:
In `internal/bot/common/handlers/divination.py`, the image send code is at lines 756-766. When `imageBytes is not None`:

1. **No text caption**: The `sendMessage` call has no `messageText=` argument — photo is sent with empty/no caption on both paths.
2. **messageCategory differs by path**: Uses ternary: `MessageCategory.BOT if isLLMCall else MessageCategory.BOT_COMMAND_REPLY` (line 763). LLM tool path → `BOT`, slash-command path → `BOT_COMMAND_REPLY`.
3. **typingManager is commented out**: There's a commented-out `# typingManager=typingManager` line (line 765), meaning the photo message does NOT pass typingManager.
4. **addMessagePrefix** is set to the `FALLBACK_HAPPENED_PREFIX` chat setting value if `imageFallback` is True, else empty string.
5. **mediaPrompt** (for DB logging) is passed as `imagePromptForDb`.

The text interpretation reply is sent as a separate `sendMessage` call (lines 772-784) only on the slash-command path (`if not isLLMCall:`), with `typingManager=` passed explicitly.

title: Text reply on slash-command path uses systemCls.renderReplyTemplate
content:
In `internal/bot/common/handlers/divination.py`, lines 772-784, the slash-command text reply (inside `if not isLLMCall:`) calls:

```python
systemCls.renderReplyTemplate(
    chatSettings[ChatSettingsKey.DIVINATION_REPLY_TEMPLATE].toStr(),
    layoutName=layout.nameRu,
    drawnSymbolsBlock=systemCls.renderDrawnSymbolsBlock(reading, lang="ru"),
    interpretation=interpretationText,
)
```

Key facts:
- `systemCls` is `TarotSystem` or `RunesSystem` — the method is dispatched statically (class method, not instance method).
- The template is fetched from chat settings (`DIVINATION_REPLY_TEMPLATE` key), not hardcoded.
- Template variables: `layoutName` (Russian name), `drawnSymbolsBlock` (rendered via `systemCls.renderDrawnSymbolsBlock`), `interpretation` (full text).
- On the LLM tool path, no separate text message is sent — interpretation text is returned in the JSON response.

title: Divination drawsJson: DB persistence shape vs LLM response shape differ
content:
In `internal/bot/common/handlers/divination.py`, the `drawsJson` used for database persistence (lines 795-804) has a DIFFERENT shape from the draws returned in the LLM JSON response.

**DB persistence shape (5 fields):**
```python
{
    "symbolId": d.symbol.id,
    "symbolName": d.symbol.name,
    "reversed": d.reversed,
    "position": d.position,
    "positionIndex": d.positionIndex,
}
```

**LLM JSON response shape (6 fields, lines 822-834):**
```python
{
    "nameEn": d.symbol.name,      // note: same as symbolName
    "nameRu": ...,                 // localized via divinationLocalization.tr()
    "glyph": d.symbol.glyph,
    "reversed": d.reversed,
    "position": d.position,
    "meaning": ...                 // upright/reversed meaning
}
```

Notable differences:
- DB shape has `symbolId` (internal ID) and `positionIndex` — absent from LLM response.
- LLM response has `nameRu` (localized), `glyph`, `meaning` — absent from DB shape.
- `symbolName` in DB ↔ `nameEn` in LLM response (same value, different key name).
- `reversed` and `position` are present in both.

title: TypingManager save/restore pattern during image generation in _handleReading
content:
In `internal/bot/common/handlers/divination.py`, lines 720-770, the handler saves and restores the `typingManager.action` around image generation:

**Save (lines 720-733):**
```python
originalAction: Optional[TypingAction] = None

if wantImage:
    imagePrompt: str = systemCls.buildImagePrompt(...)
    if typingManager is not None:
        originalAction = typingManager.action       # save
        typingManager.action = TypingAction.UPLOAD_PHOTO
        typingManager.addTimeout(300)               # bump timeout to keep indicator alive
        await typingManager.sendTypingAction()
```

**Restore (lines 768-770):**
```python
if typingManager is not None:
    typingManager.action = originalAction if originalAction is not None else TypingAction.TYPING
    await typingManager.sendTypingAction()
```

Key facts:
- The variable is named **`originalAction`** (type `Optional[TypingAction]`), NOT `originalMaxTimeout`.
- Timeout is bumped via `typingManager.addTimeout(300)` (line 732), not stored/restored in a variable.
- On restore, falls back to `TypingAction.TYPING` if `originalAction` is None (e.g., if `wantImage` was False so save never happened).

title: _handleReadingFromArgs and _runReadingForTool wrapper signatures and call flow
content:
Two wrappers around `_handleReading` exist in `internal/bot/common/handlers/divination.py`:

**`_handleReadingFromArgs` (lines 516-571):**
- Signature: `async def _handleReadingFromArgs(self, systemId: str, ensuredMessage: EnsuredMessage, args: str, typingManager: Optional[TypingManager], *, invokedVia: str) -> None`
- Called by `taroCommand` (line 313) and `runesCommand` (line 351), both with `invokedVia="command"`.
- Parses args via `_parseArgs` (line 551), validates layout name existence, delegates to `_handleReading` with `isLLMCall=False` and `generateImage=None`.
- Returns `None` — error messages are sent directly via `sendMessage` with `MessageCategory.BOT_ERROR` (lines 546, 557).

**`_runReadingForTool` (lines 428-491):**
- Signature: `async def _runReadingForTool(self, *, systemId: str, extraData: Dict[str, Any], question: str, layout: Optional[str], generateImage: bool, defaultLayoutId: str) -> str`
- Called by `_llmToolDoTarotReading` (line 387) and `_llmToolDoRunesReading` (line 419).
- Extracts `ensuredMessage` and `typingManager` from `extraData` dict (lines 463-471) — the LLM framework passes these as extra context to tool handlers.
- Resolves layout name with fallback to `defaultLayoutId` (line 477).
- Delegates to `_handleReading` with `isLLMCall=True`, `generateImage=generateImage`.
- Always returns `str` (JSON-encoded). If `_handleReading` returns `None` unexpectedly, returns `{"done": False, "errorMessage": "Unknown error"}` (line 491).

title: _generateImageViaImagesApi URL download: timeout, Content-Type sniffing, error handling
content:
In `_generateImageViaImagesApi()` at `lib/ai/providers/basic_openai_provider.py` (~lines 894-925 as of 2026-08-20), when the Images API returns a URL (not b64_json), the code downloads the image via httpx:

- **URL validation** (~line 896): Only `https` scheme URLs are accepted; anything else returns `ModelRunResult(status=ERROR, error=ValueError(f"Unsupported image URL scheme: ..."))` with tokens passed through.
- **Proxy + timeout** (~lines 908-909): Resolves `ProxyConfig.fromServiceConfig(self.provider.config).toKwargs()` and constructs `httpx.AsyncClient(**proxyKwargs, timeout=30.0)` — timeout hardcoded, not configurable.
- **Content-Type sniffing** (~lines 913-915): Reads the `content-type` header; if it starts with `"image/"`, strips parameters (`image/png; charset=utf-8` → `image/png`) and overrides the output_format-derived MIME. If it doesn't start with `"image/"`, the MIME from the mimeTypes dict (based on the `output_format` customParam, defaulting to `image/png`) is kept:
  ```python
  contentType = str(fetchResponse.headers.get("content-type", ""))
  if contentType.startswith("image/"):
      mediaMimeType = contentType.split(";")[0].strip()
  ```
- **Error handling** (~lines 916-925): Catches `httpx.HTTPError` and returns `ModelRunResult(status=ERROR, error=e)` with tokens passed through. Other exception types propagate uncaught.

The downloaded bytes are returned as plain `mediaData` bytes plus `mediaMimeType` on the `ModelRunResult` — there is NO `MediaResource`/`MediaSourceType.URL_DOWNLOAD` wrapper in this codebase (an earlier version of this memory claimed one; verified false by grep on 2026-08-20).

Line numbers drift as the file grows — grep for `imageUrl.scheme` to relocate.

title: _generateImageViaChatsApi empty images list returns ERROR with misleading log message
content:
In `_generateImageViaChatsApi()` at `lib/ai/providers/basic_openai_provider.py`, when `retMessage.images` is an empty list `[]`:

1. The `hasattr(outcome.retMessage, "images")` check passes (attribute exists but is empty).
2. The `len(images) > 1` check does not trigger (0 is not > 1).
3. The `for i, image in enumerate(images)` loop iterates zero times.
4. Execution falls through to the fallback path (around line 688) which logs: `"No images field in model response"` — this message is misleading because the field exists, it's just empty.
5. Returns `ModelRunResult(status=ModelResultStatus.ERROR, ...)` with the outcome text and tokens.

The same fallthrough also handles the case where `hasattr` is False entirely (no images field at all). The misleading log message means debugging empty-image responses takes extra effort. If you need to distinguish these cases, add an explicit check for an empty list vs. missing attribute before the fallthrough.

title: _MESSAGE_ID_FILTER_BATCH_SIZE updated from 500 to 1024 with 32766-based dynamic cap
content:
The `_MESSAGE_ID_FILTER_BATCH_SIZE` constant in `ChatSearchRepository` (`internal/database/repositories/chat_search.py`, line 48) was changed from 500 to 1024. The dynamic per-batch calculation (line 552) was updated correspondingly from `990 - baseParamCount` to `32766 - baseParamCount`. The docstring rationale shifted from "stay under older SQLite 999 limit" to "modern SQLite (3.32+, shipped with Python 3.12) has SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER=32766; 1024 is a safe default batch size." The `perBatchCount` dynamic reduction still applies: `min(_MESSAGE_ID_FILTER_BATCH_SIZE, 32766 - baseParamCount)`.

This change affects these existing memories which are now stale:

title: VectorSearchResult with rowKey dict supports composite primary keys
content:
The `VectorSearchResult` TypedDict was redesigned from single-rowId to composite-rowKey to support composite primary keys:

```python
class VectorSearchResult(TypedDict):
    rowKey: dict[str, Any]  # {col_name: value} for ALL requested return columns (values are strings at runtime, but typed as Any)
    distance: float
```

The `vectorSearch()` method signature uses `returnColumns: list[str]` (not a singular `returnColumn: str`). For a composite key like `(chat_id, message_id)`, the returned `rowKey` will have both columns: `{"chat_id": "42", "message_id": "abc"}`. For single-column keys, it has one entry.

The SQL becomes: `SELECT {', '.join(returnColumns)}, distance_fn(...) AS distance FROM ...`

The provider constructs `rowKey` as `{col: str(row[col]) for col in returnColumns}`.

Caller code uses `vr["rowKey"]["message_id"]` instead of the old `vr["rowId"]`.

Note: the TypedDict annotation is `dict[str, Any]` (not `dict[str, str]`), though at runtime values are always strings. This was a deliberate typing choice to avoid overly narrow constraints on the TypedDict definition.

title: generateText() passes prompt positionally to AbstractModel.generateText
content: At internal/services/llm/service.py lines 764-769, LLMService.generateText() calls llmModel.generateText() passing `prompt` (its own first parameter, typed Sequence[ModelMessage]) as a positional argument (not keyword). `tools`, `fallbackModels`, and `consumerId` are passed as keyword arguments. This means the first positional parameter of AbstractModel.generateText must accept the same Sequence[ModelMessage] type. The asymmetric naming — LLMService.generateText calls its param `prompt` while generateTextViaLLM calls its equivalent `messages` — persists through to the AbstractModel boundary unchanged.

title: update-project-docs skill lacks reciprocal cross-reference to read-project-docs
content:
The tandem-update requirement between `.agents/skills/read-project-docs/SKILL.md` and `.agents/skills/update-project-docs/SKILL.md` is asymmetric.

- `read-project-docs` (line 100) explicitly directs: "If the change is structural, load the `update-project-docs` skill afterward."
- `update-project-docs` does NOT contain any reciprocal directive saying "when you update documentation structure, also update `read-project-docs`."

The only mention of `read-project-docs` in `update-project-docs` is a workflow guard (line 25): "You haven't made the change yet — use `read-project-docs` first."

This means an agent using only `update-project-docs` instructions would not be reminded to keep `read-project-docs` in sync when doc structure changes (e.g., adding a new directory like `docs/llm/memories/`). The tandem-update rule (documented in memory 26ba0b22) relies on implicit convention plus the read→update cross-reference, but the reverse direction is missing from the skill file itself.

title: Glob tool may not match hidden directories — use read() for .dot-directories
content:
The glob tool (glob()) may return empty results when the pattern targets hidden directories (names starting with `.`). Verified on 2026-06-29: `glob(pattern=".agents/skills/**/*")` returned no matches even though `.agents/skills/read-project-docs/SKILL.md` and `.agents/skills/update-project-docs/SKILL.md` both exist and are readable via `read()` on the directory path.

Workaround: When searching for files under hidden directories (`.agents/`, `.github/`, `.vscode/`, `.opencode/`, etc.), use `read(directoryPath)` to list directory contents instead of relying on `glob("path/**/*")`. The `read()` tool reliably returns entries including those in hidden directories.

title: Verified: SandboxManager singleton guards in correct order (line-by-line)
content:
Line-by-line verification of the SandboxManager singleton (`lib/sandbox/manager.py`) confirmed all five guards are in the correct order and the singleton is robust against misordering and reentrancy:

1. **`getInstance()` checks `_configInstance` before `cls()`**: Line 135 (`if cls._configInstance is None:`) guards lines 137-138 (`if cls._instance is None: return cls()`). Missing config raises RuntimeError before any instance creation.

2. **`__new__` sets `cls._instance` before `__init__` runs**: Line 115 (`cls._instance = super().__new__(cls)`) assigns to the class variable, and Python's object model guarantees `__new__` returns before `__init__` is called on the returned object.

3. **`__init__` sets `self.initialized = True` before checking `_configInstance`**: Line 155 sets the guard first; line 156-158 reads/checks `_configInstance` second. The `hasattr(self, "initialized")` early return on line 153 prevents double-initialization.

4. **`injectConfig()` refuses if `cls._instance is not None`**: Line 219 checks `cls._instance is not None` and raises RuntimeError on line 220. `cls._configInstance` is only assigned on line 221 after the guard passes. Normalization (fromDict) happens before the guard on line 218.

5. **Two-phase init pattern is correct**: Full trace of all paths (normal: injectConfig → getInstance, error: getInstance before injectConfig, error: injectConfig after instantiation, idempotent: multiple getInstance calls, defensive: direct `SandboxManager()` call bypassing getInstance) all terminate correctly without leaving a broken singleton in place. The `__init__` re-check of `_configInstance` (lines 156-158) is a defense-in-depth measure for direct constructor calls.

title: ModelRunResult.__str__ renderer branch: unconditional {rendered} (no !r conditional)
content:
In `lib/ai/models.py`, `ModelRunResult.__str__` has two rendering paths:

**Renderer branch (line 1040-1045):** Fields with a custom renderer in `_STR_RENDERERS` use `f"{name}={rendered}"` unconditionally — no `!r` and no isinstance check on the rendered value. The renderer is expected to return a pre-formatted string.

```python
renderer = self._STR_RENDERERS.get(name)
if renderer is not None:
    rendered = renderer(value)
    if rendered is _OMIT:
        continue
    # Strings are emitted as-is (already formatted by the renderer).
    parts.append(f"{name}={rendered}")
```

**Default branch (line 1047-1056):** Fields WITHOUT a custom renderer use `f"{name}={value!r}"` — repr is always applied.

This means renderer-produced values appear UNQUOTED in the output (e.g., `error=ValueError: oops`) while default-rule strings appear QUOTED (e.g., `resultText='hello'`). This is the opposite behavior from what a reader might expect.

Formerly the code had a conditional `f"{name}={rendered!r}" if not isinstance(rendered, str) else f"{name}={rendered}"` pattern, but this was simplified to the unconditional form above. The current code makes all rendered values display without repr, regardless of their type.

title: Docs-only session pattern: implementation and docs update decoupled into separate sessions
content:
The divination feature demonstrated a clean decoupling pattern: feature implementation and documentation updates were executed as separate sessions. The implementation session built all code, tests, configs, and migrations; a separate docs-only session handled documentation updates across multiple files under `docs/` (including `docs/llm/` files and schema docs).

Key characteristics of the docs-only session:
1. User provides a comprehensive feature summary (new files, modified files, database schema, config keys, slash commands, LLM tools, predefined layouts, ChatSettingsKey entries)
2. Agent loads the `update-project-docs` skill for authoritative workflow guidance
3. Agent cross-references the skill's matrix with the user's explicit file list (brief wins on conflict)
4. Agent reads each target doc to understand its structure before editing
5. Agent reads the actual migration file and config files to ensure accuracy, not relying solely on the user's summary
6. Agent verifies no code/test/config files were touched (pure Markdown-only)
7. Agent produces a structured report: list of modified files, git diff-stat, deviations from skill guidance, things noticed but not fixed, and confirmation of scope constraints

Scale (re-verified 2026-08-20): divination is referenced across ~21 non-archive doc files (database-schema.md / database-schema-llm.md / database-README.md, developer-guide.md, product-page.md, sql-portability-guide.md, documentation-review-process.md, and the docs/llm/ set including docs/llm/memories/) plus archived material under `docs/archive/`. Note: `golden-data-testing-system-v2.md` has since been moved from `docs/design/` to `docs/archive/design/` and no longer counts toward the non-archive total — re-grep before citing an exact count, it drifts as docs are added/archived.

The feature is fully gated behind a config flag (`[divination] enabled = false` in `configs/00-defaults/divination.toml`).

This decoupling pattern works well when the feature is fully gated behind a config flag and hasn't shipped to production — the docs update can be safely deferred without blocking deployment.

title: Gotcha: CacheRepository getCacheEntry vs setCacheEntry have asymmetric parameter order — cacheType moves position
content:
The `CacheRepository` in `internal/database/repositories/cache.py` has a non-obvious parameter order asymmetry between its get and set methods:

- `getCacheEntry(key: str, cacheType: CacheType, ttl: Optional[int] = None, *, dataSource: Optional[str] = None)` — cacheType is the **2nd** positional parameter (line 181).
- `setCacheEntry(key: str, data: str, cacheType: CacheType, *, dataSource: Optional[str] = None)` — cacheType is the **3rd** positional parameter, with `data` inserted between `key` and `cacheType` (line 243).

This is the only repository where the same semantic parameter (`cacheType`) changes position between read and write methods. Calling `setCacheEntry(key, cacheType, data)` by mistake would silently type-error or produce wrong behavior. Always use keyword arguments for `cacheType` when calling these methods to avoid positional confusion, or verify parameter order carefully.

Additionally:
- `getCacheStorage(*, dataSource: Optional[str] = None)` — takes NO key parameter, only keyword-only dataSource, returns ALL cache storage entries ordered by `updated_at DESC` (line 68).
- `setCacheStorage(namespace: str, key: str, value: str, *, dataSource: Optional[str] = None)` — operates on individual namespace/key storage entries (line 97).

title: Telegram vs Max adapter proxy resolution: explicit getCombined() vs lazy delegation via ProxyService
content:
Verified 2026-08-20. The two bot adapters resolve proxy configuration differently at the application level:

**Telegram** (`internal/bot/telegram/application.py:355`):
- Calls `ProxyService.getInstance().resolveProxy(botConfig, "telegram-bot").getCombined()` EXPLICITLY before the `match proxyConfig.type` block (line 369). The comment at lines 350-354 documents the rationale: the resolved (combined) type is needed for the switch, and the internal `getCombined()` calls inside `getProxyURL()`/`toKwargs()` are no-ops on an already-combined config.
- HTTP case → `.proxy(url).get_updates_proxy(url)`; SOCKS5 case (lines 378-387) → two separate `HTTPXRequest` instances (main + get_updates), each via `proxyConfig.toKwargs()` (returns `{proxy: "socks5://..."}` — httpx2 native URL, no transport object).

**Max** (`internal/bot/max/application.py:311`):
- Calls `ProxyService.getInstance().resolveProxy(botConfig, "max-bot")` WITHOUT `.getCombined()`, logs `getProxyURL(maskPassword=True)`, and passes the unresolved `ProxyConfig` directly to `libMax.MaxBotClient(self.botToken, proxyConfig=proxyConfig, caBundlePath=..., basePollingUrl=..., localReceiverToken=...)` (lines 346-352).
- `MaxBotClient._getHttpClient()` (`lib/max_bot/client.py:214`) calls `self._proxyConfig.toKwargs()` with NO arguments (line 227) — the old `toKwargs(verify=self._sslContext)` signature was removed in the httpx2 migration (ADR-021 D2) — and applies `verify=self._sslContext` uniformly at the `httpx2.AsyncClient` level (lines 237-238) for both HTTP and SOCKS5 proxies. `toKwargs()` calls `getCombined()` lazily (lib/proxy/__init__.py:442) at client-construction time.
- No `match` block on proxy type exists at the Max adapter level — `MaxBotClient` handles proxy transparently.

Net: the Max adapter's proxy resolution is fully delegated to the client library (lazy), while the Telegram adapter resolves eagerly at the application layer. When modifying proxy wiring, both paths must be kept in sync.

title: Telegram bot proxy: explicit getCombined() before match block rationale via ProxyService
content:
In `internal/bot/telegram/application.py` (proxy setup at line 347, match at line 361), `ProxyService.getInstance().resolveProxy(botConfig, "telegram-bot").getCombined()` is called explicitly before the `match` block, even though `getProxyURL()` and `toKwargs()` call `getCombined()` internally. The comment at lines 343-346 documents the rationale: `getCombined()` is needed for the `match proxyConfig.type` switch to work on the resolved (combined) proxy type. The subsequent internal `getCombined()` calls inside `getProxyURL()` / `toKwargs()` become no-ops when passed an already-combined config, so there's no redundant work.

This is a deliberate micro-design choice: resolve early so the type switch has the final value, rather than resolving inside each method call and duplicating the logic.

title: Handler proxy wiring via ProxyService.resolveProxy() — not ProxyConfig.fromServiceConfig()
content:
All bot handlers/services wire proxy via `ProxyService.getInstance().resolveProxy(serviceConfig, serviceLabel)` — NOT `ProxyConfig.fromServiceConfig()` directly. `resolveProxy()` (internal/services/proxy/service.py:141) wraps `ProxyConfig.fromServiceConfig()` (line 162) and additionally registers per-service `ProxyLifecycle`s, deduplicated by serviceLabel.

Pattern used everywhere:

```python
proxyConfig = ProxyService.getInstance().resolveProxy(serviceConfig, "service-label")
maskedUrl = proxyConfig.getProxyURL(maskPassword=True)
if maskedUrl:
    logger.info(f"Proxy enabled for ServiceName: {maskedUrl}")
client = SomeHTTPClient(..., proxyConfig=proxyConfig)
```

Verified call sites (2026-08-20):
- `internal/bot/common/handlers/weather.py:81` — label `"openweathermap"`
- `internal/bot/common/handlers/weather.py:113` — label `"geocode-maps"`
- `internal/bot/common/handlers/yandex_search.py:114` — label `"yandex-search"`
- `internal/services/stt/service.py:206` — label `"stt"` (STTService injects the resolved ProxyConfig into the provider; lib/stt never resolves proxy itself)
- `internal/bot/telegram/application.py:355` and `internal/bot/max/application.py:311` — labels `"telegram-bot"` / `"max-bot"`

`YandexSearchHandler._downloadUrl()` (yandex_search.py:566) still calls `self._proxyConfig.toKwargs()` inline and spreads it into `httpx.AsyncClient(..., http2=True)` — but the old SOCKS5 HTTP/2 disable (checking `"transport" not in proxyKwargs`, later the D3 `ProxyType.SOCKS5` check) was REMOVED 2026-08-13: httpcore2 negotiates HTTP/2 over the SOCKS5 tunnel via TLS ALPN natively (see the _downloadUrl docstring). The handler still stores `self._proxyConfig` (a `ProxyConfig`) for this. The OLDER free-function pattern `resolveProxyConfig()` + `buildHttpxClientKwargs()` remains fully dead (zero production .py references — re-verified 2026-08-20).

title: Correction: BaseSQLProvider.listTables() is NOT abstract — it's a concrete method raising NotImplementedError
content:
Correction to memory 30846bdd which claimed `BaseSQLProvider.listTables()` "is an abstract method". The actual code shows it is NOT decorated with `@abstractmethod`. It is a concrete method with a body that raises `NotImplementedError(f"{type(self).__name__} does not support table listing")`. This is the same pattern used by `createVectorTable()` and `vectorSearch()` in BaseSQLProvider: optional-override methods that subclasses may implement without compile-time enforcement.

The actual signature at line 558: `async def listTables(self, likePattern: str = "%") -> list[str]:`
SQLite3Provider implements it (line 558). Neither SQLinkProvider nor any other provider implements it.

title: Mixed Optional[] and PEP 604 style in base.py — no enforced convention
content:
`internal/database/providers/base.py` has mixed type annotation styles:

- **PEP 604 (`X | Y`)**: type aliases (e.g. `type QueryParams = Dict[str, Any] | Sequence[Any]`), `execute()` parameter `query: str | ParametrizedQuery`
- **`Optional[X]` (old-style)**: most method signatures — `execute()` params `params: Optional[QueryParams]`, `ParametrizedQuery.__init__` params `params: Optional[QueryParams]`, `vectorSearch()` params `filterParams: Optional[dict[str, str | int | float | None]]` (note: PEP 604 inside Optional), `applyPagination()` and `getTextType()` use `Optional[int]`

The `execute()` method (line 301-306) is the single clearest example of mixed style in one signature: `query: str | ParametrizedQuery` (PEP 604) alongside `params: Optional[QueryParams]` (old-style). The `__aexit__` method (line 260-265) similarly uses `Optional[type[BaseException]]` and `Optional[BaseException]`.

There is no enforced project convention for which style to use in this file. Type aliases consistently use PEP 604; function/method signatures consistently use `Optional[]`.

title: NotRequired is the dominant convention in internal/database, total=False persists in lib
content:
The project convention for TypedDict optional fields is `NotRequired[]` (from `typing`), not `total=False`. However, adoption is uneven across the codebase:

**internal/database/** — uses `NotRequired` exclusively:
- `internal/database/providers/base.py`: VectorColumnDef uses `NotRequired[bool]`, `NotRequired[int]`, `NotRequired[VectorDistanceMetric]`
- `internal/database/models.py`: uses `NotRequired[float]`
- Zero uses of `total=False`

**lib/** — uses BOTH patterns:
- `lib/rate_limiter/types.py` — imports and uses `NotRequired`
- `lib/yandex_search/models.py` — imports and uses `NotRequired` extensively (20+ fields)
- `lib/geocode_maps/models.py` — imports `NotRequired` BUT also uses `total=False, closed=False` on some TypedDicts
- `lib/aurumentation/types.py` — imports `NotRequired` BUT has `ScenarioInitKwargs` with `total=False`
- `lib/proxy/__init__.py` — exclusively uses `total=False` on 3 TypedDicts

When adding new TypedDicts, prefer `NotRequired` (matching the database layer convention). Existing `total=False` usages in `lib/` are legacy and should be migrated if touched.

title: VectorDistanceMetric StrEnum defined in base.py with COSINE and L2 members
content:
`VectorDistanceMetric` is a `StrEnum` defined in `internal/database/providers/base.py` at lines 135-146:

```python

    COSINE = "cosine"  # Range [0, 2]

```

title: Design doc _loadSqliteVecExtension code is stale vs implementation
content:
`docs/design/vector-search-native.md` §4.1 (lines 401–428) contains a `_loadSqliteVecExtension` code sketch that differs from the actual implementation in `internal/database/providers/sqlite3.py` (lines 39–76) in three ways:

1. **No `extensionPath` parameter** — the design doc hardcodes `sqlite_vec.loadable_path()`, but the real function takes `(connection, extensionPath)` so callers can supply an explicit path.
2. **No nested try/finally for security** — the design doc has a single `try/except` block with `enable_load_extension(False)` inside the try. If `load_extension()` raises, the finally never runs and extension loading stays enabled. The real code has an outer `try/except Exception` + inner `try/finally` that unconditionally calls `enable_load_extension(False)` in the finally block.
3. **No None guard for vec_version** — the design doc assumes `row` is never None. The real code has `if row is None: return None`.

The code is correct and strictly more robust than the design doc shows — the documentation needs to be updated to match.

title: Correction: memory 50192c63 "listRemoteModels fetches only one page" is WRONG — async for fetches ALL pages
content:
Memory 50192c63 claims `BasicOpenAIProvider.listRemoteModels()` "fetches only a single page of results" because it calls `async for model in await self._client.models.list()`. This is factually incorrect.

The OpenAI SDK's `models.list()` returns an `AsyncPage`/`SyncPage` object that implements full async iteration. The `async for` loop consumes the ENTIRE async iterator, which the SDK handles by transparently fetching all pages internally. The method does NOT stop at one page — it fetches the complete model catalogue.

Verified at `lib/ai/providers/basic_openai_provider.py:1076-1096`:
```python
async def listRemoteModels(self) -> Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]]:
    result: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}
    async for model in await self._client.models.list():
        result[model.id] = model.model_dump()
    return result
```

The `async for` iteration pattern is the standard way to consume paginated OpenAI SDK list methods across all pages. This memory should be corrected or deleted.

title: Correction: BaseSQLProvider has 21 methods (11 concrete + 10 abstract), not 16
content:
Code verification shows `BaseSQLProvider` (internal/database/providers/base.py) defines **21 methods total** (11 concrete + 10 abstract), NOT 16 (6 concrete + 10 abstract) as previously recorded in memory 5c4baa65.

**10 abstract methods** (confirmed: all have `@abstractmethod` decorator):
1. `connect()` — open connection(s)
2. `disconnect()` — close connection(s)
3. `_execute(query: ParametrizedQuery)` — internal execution
4. `batchExecute(queries: Sequence[ParametrizedQuery])` — batch execution
5. `upsert(table, values, conflictColumns, updateExpressions=None)` — provider-specific upsert
6. `isReadOnly()` — check read-only status
7. `applyPagination(query, limit, offset=0)` — append LIMIT/OFFSET
8. `getTextType(maxLength=None)` — portable TEXT column type name
9. `getCaseInsensitiveComparison(column, param)` — case-insensitive equality
10. `getLikeComparison(column, param)` — case-insensitive LIKE

**11 concrete methods** (business + dunder):
1. `__init__()` — constructor
2. `__repr__()` — string representation
3. `__aenter__()` — calls `connect()`
4. `__aexit__()` — calls `disconnect()`; fixed to use proper `exc_info=(exc_type, exc, tb)` pattern
5. `execute(query, params, fetchType)` — wraps string in `ParametrizedQuery`, delegates to `_execute`
6. `executeFetchOne(query, params)` — shorthand for `FETCH_ONE`
7. `executeFetchAll(query, params)` — shorthand for `FETCH_ALL`
8. `isVectorSearchSupported()` — concrete NotImplementedError default
9. `vectorSearch(queryVector, tableName, limit)` — concrete NotImplementedError default
10. `listTables(likePattern="%")` — concrete NotImplementedError default
11. `createVectorTable(tableName, vectorLength)` — concrete NotImplementedError default

**5 methods missing from previous memory**: `__aexit__`, `isVectorSearchSupported`, `vectorSearch`, `listTables`, `createVectorTable`. The 4 vector-related methods are deliberately concrete NotImplementedError defaults (not abstract), allowing providers to opt in.

title: startDelayedScheduler synchronous prologue semantics with loop.create_task
content:
The `startDelayedScheduler` method in `internal/services/queue_service/service.py` (lines 259-311) has a synchronous prologue (lines 286-292) before the first `await` at line 293. This prologue does:

1. Guard check (`self.db is not None` raise) — line 286-287
2. Assigns `self.db = db` — line 289
3. Registers `_doExitHandler` — line 291
4. Registers `_cronJobHandler` — line 292

CRITICAL timing nuance with `loop.create_task()`: `create_task` does NOT execute any coroutine body during the call. It only wraps the coroutine in an `asyncio.Task` and schedules it on the event loop. The synchronous prologue runs on the FIRST event loop iteration that drives the task, in one contiguous chunk before any `await` yields control. So handler registration does NOT happen during the `create_task` call itself, but it IS the first thing that executes when the event loop gets around to the task.

This means: if code calls `loop.create_task(startDelayedScheduler(database))` and then immediately (in the next line) registers additional handlers, those additional handlers may or may not be registered before the scheduler's own DO_EXIT and CRON_JOB handlers, depending on whether the event loop has a chance to run the task between the two lines. In the current `GromozekBot.__init__`, the task is created and then more handlers are registered by `ProxyService.getInstance().initialize()` — the actual handler registration by `startDelayedScheduler` hasn't happened yet when `initialize()` runs, because the task hasn't been scheduled for execution yet.

title: _doExitHandler is first in DO_EXIT handler list, registered synchronously in startDelayedScheduler prologue
content:
In `internal/services/queue_service/service.py`, `_doExitHandler` is registered at line 291 as:
```python
self.registerDelayedTaskHandler(DelayedTaskFunction.DO_EXIT, self._doExitHandler)
```
This is the FIRST registration for `DelayedTaskFunction.DO_EXIT` because `registerDelayedTaskHandler` creates a new list if the function key doesn't exist (line 255) or appends if it does (line 253). Since `startDelayedScheduler` initializes `self.tasksHandlers` and immediately registers `_doExitHandler` before any other code can register DO_EXIT handlers, `_doExitHandler` is guaranteed to be first in the DO_EXIT handler list.

Handlers are executed in insertion order (list iteration at line 378): `for handler in self.tasksHandlers[delayedTask.function]:`. So `_doExitHandler` runs before any externally-registered DO_EXIT handlers (e.g., from `ChatSearchHandler._dtOnExit`).

This matters for shutdown sequencing — the built-in handler (which waits for background tasks to drain) runs first, then external cleanup handlers run.

title: Initial CRON_JOB tick at time.time() fires before restored pending tasks in startDelayedScheduler
content:
In `startDelayedScheduler` (`internal/services/queue_service/service.py`), the CRON_JOB initial scheduling at `time.time()` (immediate) happens at lines 293-298, which is BEFORE the loop that loads pending tasks from the database (lines 300-308). This means the first CRON_JOB tick fires during initialization (before any restored tasks are processed), then on every subsequent 60-second reschedule.

The sequence within `startDelayedScheduler`:
1. [sync] Register `_doExitHandler` — line 291
2. [sync] Register `_cronJobHandler` — line 292
3. [await] Schedule initial CRON_JOB at `time.time()` — lines 293-298
4. [await] Load and re-schedule pending tasks from DB — lines 300-308
5. [await] Start the delayed queue processing loop — line 310

This ordering means the initial CRON_JOB tick (triggering all registered CRON_JOB handlers: `_cronJobHandler`, plus any external ones like `HandlersManager._dtCronJob` or `ChatSearchHandler._dtCronJob`) fires BEFORE restored pending tasks from a previous session get re-enqueued. This could affect timing if a restored task and the initial CRON_JOB tick both target the same resource.

title: Current canonical LLM tool signatures in ChatSearchHandler (3 tools)
content:
ChatSearchHandler (internal/bot/common/handlers/chat_search.py) registers exactly 4 LLM tools (registerTool calls ~lines 240, 303, 324, 348):

1. **search_messages** (handler `_llmToolSearchMessages`, ~line 578) — 7 parameters:
   - `query` (STRING, optional) — search query text (empty = filter-only mode)
   - `limit` (NUMBER, optional, default 5) — clamped to [1, 100] via hardcoded 100, not `self._maxResults`
   - `max_age_days` (NUMBER, optional)
   - `user_name` (STRING, optional)
   - `thread_message_id` (STRING, optional)
   - `current_thread_only` (BOOLEAN, optional, default true) — restrict to the thread/topic the current message belongs to; an explicit `thread_message_id` overrides it
   - `substring` (STRING, optional) — case-insensitive exact substring match; without a query performs a pure text search with no semantic ranking and no embeddings required
2. **list_users** (handler `_llmToolListUsers`, ~line 772) — `limit` (NUMBER, optional, default 20, clamped [1, 200]), `min_messages` (NUMBER, optional)
3. **get_thread** (handler `_llmToolGetThread`, ~line 859) — `message_id` (STRING, required)
4. **get_messages_by_ids** (handler `_llmToolGetMessagesByIds`, ~line 925) — `message_ids` (ARRAY of STRING, **required=True**) — de-duped, clamped to MAX_GET_MESSAGES_BATCH. Pure DB lookup, NOT gated on EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED or ALLOW_TOOLS_COMMANDS. Intended for reading the original messages underlying a condensed summary (summaries carry coveredMessageIds).

Also registers one delayed task handler: `self.queueService.registerDelayedTaskHandler(DelayedTaskFunction.CRON_JOB, self._dtCronJob)` (~line 237).

title: _llmToolSearchMessages limit clamping uses hardcoded 100, not self._maxResults
content:
In `ChatSearchHandler._llmToolSearchMessages()` (chat_search.py:488-489), the `limit` parameter is validated with:

```python
effectiveLimit = int(limit) if limit is not None else 5
limit = max(1, min(effectiveLimit, 100))
```

The upper bound is a hardcoded `100`, not `self._maxResults` (which is the user-configurable `/search` limit, default 10). This means the LLM tool always allows up to 100 results regardless of the user's `/search` preference. The tool description at registration also says "max 100" — the hardcoded value and the tool description are consistent with each other.

This differs from the `/search` user command which uses `self._maxResults` (default 10) as its upper bound. The asymmetry is intentional: LLM tools have their own, higher limit than the user-facing command.

title: ProxyConfig.getCombined() both-enabled path shares lifecycle dict reference (aliasing asymmetry vs service-disabled path)
content:
**`ProxyConfig.getCombined()` both-enabled path shares the global lifecycle dict by reference, while the service-disabled path creates a shallow copy — causing aliasing asymmetry.**

Located in `lib/proxy/__init__.py`, lines 367–408.

The three paths behave differently regarding lifecycle dict ownership:

1. **Kill-switch (global proxy disabled, lines 393–395):** Returns `ProxyConfig(proxyType=ProxyType.NONE)`. Lifecycle is `None`. No aliasing concern.

2. **Service-disabled (`self.enabled` is False, lines 397–399):** Returns `globalProxyConfig.copy()`. The `copy()` method (lines 276–290) uses `cast(ProxyLifecycleConfigDict, dict(self.lifecycle))` — this creates a **new shallow copy** of the lifecycle dict. The returned ProxyConfig does NOT share the mutable lifecycle dict reference with the global config.

3. **Both enabled (lines 401–408):** Assigns `lifecycle=self.lifecycle if self.lifecycle is not None else globalProxyConfig.lifecycle` (line 407) — this passes the **same dict reference** directly, with no `dict()` copy. The returned ProxyConfig shares the global lifecycle dict reference.

**Impact:** If any caller mutates the lifecycle dict on the returned ProxyConfig from path 3 (e.g., `proxyConfig.lifecycle["healthCheckInterval"] = 10`), the mutation also affects the global `ProxyHelper` singleton's `globalProxyConfig.lifecycle` dict. Callers using path 2 (service-disabled) are safe because `copy()` shallow-copies the dict.

**Fix:** The both-enabled path should also shallow-copy the lifecycle dict when falling back to global, e.g.: `lifecycle=dict(self.lifecycle) if self.lifecycle is not None else dict(globalProxyConfig.lifecycle) if globalProxyConfig.lifecycle is not None else None`, or apply `self.lifecycle or dict(globalProxyConfig.lifecycle)` (wrapped with the appropriate None guards).

title: Test convention: _makePendingMessage provides full ChatMessageDict to prevent fromDBChatMessage KeyError
content:
In `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_chat_search.py`, backfill/embedding tests use a `_makePendingMessage` helper (line 1101) that returns a fully populated dict matching `ChatMessageDict` shape. This is required because `EnsuredMessage.fromDBChatMessage` accesses every column from the `chat_messages` table, and a sparse dict causes `KeyError`.

The helper provides all 17 fields with sensible defaults:
- Identifiers: `chat_id`, `message_id`, `user_id`, `reply_id`, `root_message_id`, `thread_id` (default 0)
- Content: `message_text`, `message_type`, `quote_text`, `media_id`, `media_group_id`
- Metadata: `date`, `created_at`, `metadata` (default `""`), `markup` (default `""`)
- User info: `full_name` (default "Alice"), `username` (default "alice")

Notable defaults that prevent gotchas:
- `"markup": ""` — prevents KeyError: 'markup'
- `"metadata": ""` — prevents KeyError: 'metadata' (this is stored as TEXT, not a dict — see memory 52af291b)
- `"thread_id": 0` — matches DEFAULT_THREAD_ID convention
- `"reply_id": None, "root_message_id": None` — nullable fields as None

Use this pattern in any test that constructs `EnsuredMessage.fromDBChatMessage` from synthetic data rather than a real DB row.

title: CORRECTION: Memory 81f3f890 is INCORRECT — ProxyService IS wired in main.py
content: Memory 81f3f890 (id 53) states "Proxy lifecycle NOT wired in main.py — wired at proxy config resolution through ProxyService." This is factually incorrect as of current code. title: Gotcha: grep for "zero-vector" misses "near-zero norm" warning at chat_search.py:407

title: Repository naming deviations catalog: set*, unset*, list*, ensure*, cleanup*, update* for upserts
content:
Verified against source files on 2026-07-14. The project convention is `add*` for inserts, `update*` for updates, `get*` for queries, `delete*/clear*` for removals. Six areas deviate from this pattern:

**ChatSettingsRepository** (`internal/database/repositories/chat_settings.py`): uses `setChatSetting` (line 43) / `unsetChatSetting` (line 83) instead of `add*`/`delete*`. Has `clearChatSettings` (line 115) and `getChatSetting`/`getChatSettings` (lines 142, 171). NOTE: `listChatsBySetting` does NOT exist — it was deleted (2026-07-10) as part of the `_trackedChats` rewrite that replaced DB-scan chat discovery with an in-memory set.

**ChatUsersRepository** (`chat_users.py`): `updateChatUser` (line 48) is an upsert named `update*` instead of `add*`. All other methods follow `get*`.

**ChatInfoRepository** (`chat_info.py`): `updateChatInfo` (line 42) is an upsert named `update*` instead of `add*`. All other methods follow `get*`.

**CacheRepository** (`cache.py`): uses `setCacheStorage`/`unsetCacheStorage`/`setCacheEntry` instead of `add*`/`delete*`. Uses `clearCache`/`clearOldCacheEntries` for removals.

**DelayedTasksRepository** (`delayed_tasks.py`): `cleanupOldCompletedDelayedTasks` (line 271) uses `cleanup*` instead of `delete*`/`clear*`.

**MediaAttachmentsRepository** (`media_attachments.py`): `ensureMediaInGroup` (line 68) uses `ensure*` prefix.

Implication: when writing code against an unfamiliar repository, verify the actual method names rather than assuming `add*`/`get*`/`delete*` conventions.

title: FastembedModel docstring at line 324 has dead reference to non-existent embeddingDimensions property
content:
In `lib/ai/providers/fastembed_provider.py` line 324, the class docstring for `FastembedModel` includes a usage example:

```python
>>> model.embeddingDimensions
384
```

This references `embeddingDimensions` as if it's a public property, but `embeddingDimensions` does NOT exist on `FastembedModel` (or anywhere in the codebase — confirmed via `grep -rn "def embeddingDimensions"` returning zero results). The property is not defined on `AbstractModel` (the parent class), nor on `FastembedModel` itself.

The code uses `_dimensions` (private attribute, set by `AbstractModel.__init__` from `self._config.get("dimensions", ...)` or probed lazily) and `getDimensions()` (a public method on `AbstractModel`). If a doctest runner encounters this example, it will raise `AttributeError: 'FastembedModel' object has no attribute 'embeddingDimensions'`.

To fix: either define `embeddingDimensions` as a property that delegates to `getDimensions()`, or update the docstring to use `getDimensions()` or `model._dimensions` (if private access is acceptable for a docstring example).

title: Pyright suppression syntax for proxy type errors in telegram application.py
content:
In `internal/bot/telegram/application.py` lines 374 and 376, proxy-related type errors from passing `proxyConfig.toKwargs()` (returns `Dict[str, Any]`) to `HTTPXRequest(httpx_kwargs=...)` (expects `Optional[Dict[str, Any]]`) are suppressed with:

```python
mainRequest = HTTPXRequest(httpx_kwargs=proxyConfig.toKwargs())  # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]
getUpdatesRequest = HTTPXRequest(
    httpx_kwargs=proxyConfig.toKwargs()  # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]
)
```

The suppression uses the **pyright-specific** name `reportArgumentType`. The equivalent mypy suppression would be `# type: ignore[arg-type]` — using that syntax in this codebase would have no effect because the project uses pyright (typeCheckingMode="basic"), not mypy. Always use `# pyright: ignore[...]` with pyright's diagnostic name.

title: Method name discrepancy: _semanticSearchNative/_semanticSearchFallback → actual names are _semanticSearch/_nativeVectorSearch

- `_nativeVectorSearch()` (line 638) — the native vector search implementation using sqlProvider.vectorSearch()

The numpy fallback is inlined inside `_semanticSearch()` (lines 365-433), not in a separate `_semanticSearchFallback` method. Existing memories (3d111e65, 203e05fc) do reference the correct names but never document the naming discrepancy as a correction to the original inaccurate memory.

title: searchChatMessages lives in ChatSearchRepository, not ChatMessagesRepository — full signature with defaults
content:
`searchChatMessages` lives in `ChatSearchRepository` at `internal/database/repositories/chat_search.py` (~line 130; NOT in ChatMessagesRepository).

**Current signature (verified 2026-08):**
```python
async def searchChatMessages(
    self,
    chatId: int,
    queryEmbedding: Optional[List[float]] = None,
    *,
    limit: Optional[int] = 10,
    topK: int = 100,
    userFilter: Optional[int] = None,
    categoryFilter: Optional[Sequence[MessageCategory]] = None,
    maxAgeDays: Optional[int] = None,
    rootMessageId: Optional[MessageId] = None,
    modelName: Optional[str] = None,
    maxMessages: Optional[int] = None,
    dataSource: Optional[str] = None,
    threadId: Optional[int] = None,      # NEW since the memory was written
    substring: Optional[str] = None,     # NEW since the memory was written
) -> List[ChatMessageDict]:
```

**Key behavior (post-migration_025 — CHANGED from the old numpy description):**
- Semantic mode (queryEmbedding provided): cosine ranking delegates to the provider's NATIVE vec0 virtual table via `_semanticSearch` → `_nativeVectorSearch` (~line 622). `modelName` is resolved to `model_id` internally via the injected resolver. numpy is fully retired (Decision D8); there is NO in-process fallback — when vec0 is unavailable, raises, or yields no matches, an empty list is returned.
- Filter-only mode (queryEmbedding None): SQL filters against chat_messages JOIN chat_users, ordered by date desc, score=0.0; `threadId` (0 = main) and case-insensitive `substring` (bound via getLikeComparison) filters available.
- `limit: Optional[int] = 10` — None means no LIMIT clause (caller post-filters); `topK` = candidates considered before final trim.

title: Correction: summarization.py line 274 already logs batchRequest (bugfix in memory 7331776b is stale)
content:

```python
# Line 220 — outer scope, full message list
reqMessages: List[ModelMessage] = [systemMessage, *parsedMessages]

# Line 253 — inner batch loop, current batch
batchRequest: List[ModelMessage] = [systemMessage, *parsedMessages[startPos:startPos + currentBatchLen]]

logger.debug(f"LLM Request messages: {batchRequest}")
```

The logger variable was already corrected from `reqMessages` to `batchRequest` in the codebase. The memory describing the stale-variable bug is itself stale — the fix has been applied. No further action needed.

title: fromDBChatMessage expects full ChatMessageDict with direct dict access — partial dicts raise KeyError
content:
`EnsuredMessage.fromDBChatMessage(cls, data: ChatMessageDict, db: Database, forceGetAllMedia: bool = False)` expects a complete `ChatMessageDict` (from `internal.database.models`) with all fields populated. It uses direct bracket access (`data["key"]`) on 15+ keys — NOT `.get()` with defaults — so passing a partial dict will raise `KeyError`.

Keys accessed directly:
- `data["markup"]`, `data["metadata"]` (JSON-serialized strings)
- `data["user_id"]`, `data["full_name"]`, `data["username"]`
- `data["chat_id"]`, `data["message_id"]`, `data["date"]`, `data["message_text"]`, `data["message_type"]`
- `data["media_group_id"]`, `data["reply_id"]`, `data["quote_text"]`, `data["thread_id"]`, `data["media_id"]`

This means: when constructing test data for tests that call `fromDBChatMessage` or when writing scripts that reconstruct an `EnsuredMessage` from DB data, the dict must include all expected keys. Missing any will crash at runtime before any fallback/default logic is reached.

Location: `internal/bot/models/ensured_message.py`, lines 819-899.

title: Correction: Memory 6e7d191e is wrong — _dimensionsProbed lazy probe was never implemented in FastembedModel
content:
**Discovery date:** 2026-06-29 verification session

**What memory 6e7d191e claims:**
Memory 6e7d191e ("Fix: FastembedModel.detectDimensions now lazy via _dimensionsProbed flag + asyncio.to_thread") states that a fix was applied to `FastembedModel` in `lib/ai/providers/fastembed_provider.py` that:
- Added `self._dimensionsProbed` flag
- Added `asyncio.to_thread` for lazy dimension probing
- Removed synchronous `self._provider.detectDimensions()` from `__init__`

**What the actual code shows (verified June 29, 2026):**
None of this was implemented. The current code at `lib/ai/providers/fastembed_provider.py`:

1. **`_dimensionsProbed` is docstring-only** — appears only in the class `Attributes:` docstring at line 309. It is never initialized (`self._dimensionsProbed = False`) or referenced in any method body (lines 353-403 `__init__`, lines 405-436 `_generateEmbeddings`).

2. **No `detectDimensions` method** on `FastembedModel`. Grep confirms zero matches for `def detectDimensions` in `fastembed_provider.py`.

3. **`__init__` does not call `self._provider.detectDimensions()`** — it only stores `self._provider` (line 397) and builds `self._fastembedKwargs` (lines 401-403).

4. **`_generateEmbeddings` has no dimension-probe logic** — it calls `self._provider.embedOne(...)` which lazily creates the `TextEmbedding` via `_getOrCreateEmbedding` (line 229-254) using `asyncio.to_thread`. But this is model construction laziness, not dimension probing laziness.

5. **Actual lazy dimension probing** (if `embedding_dimensions` was absent from config) happens in `AbstractModel.getDimensions()` at `lib/ai/abstract.py:578`, which uses `self._dimensions is None` as the guard (no `_dimensionsProbed` flag, no `asyncio.to_thread`).

**Impact:**
- Anyone relying on memory 6e7d191e would incorrectly believe a lazy dimension probe exists with a `_dimensionsProbed` guard
- The class docstring (lines 299-309) is misleading — it describes behavior that doesn't exist
- Running `model._dimensionsProbed` at runtime would raise `AttributeError`

title: CORRECTION: Caption limit constant removed — photo and text sent as separate messages
content:
The existing memory "Caption limit constant per platform: Telegram 1024, Max Messenger limit unknown" (bd080766, created 2026-06-10) is stale. It states that "1024 characters [is] hard-coded in the divination handler" — this is no longer true.

The CAPTION_LIMIT = 1024 constant was removed during refactoring. The current divination handler (internal/bot/common/handlers/divination.py, lines 755-784) sidesteps the caption limit entirely by sending the photo and the text as separate messages:

1. **Photo** (line 759): `await self.sendMessage(ensuredMessage, photoData=imageBytes, ...)` — sends the image with NO `messageText` parameter, meaning no caption at all. The `mediaPrompt` argument (line 762) is used for internal DB storage, not as a caption.

2. **Text** (line 774, slash-command path only): `await self.sendMessage(ensuredMessage, messageText=..., ...)` — sends the reading text as a separate follow-up message.

This two-message approach avoids the per-platform caption limit issue entirely (Telegram: 1024 chars for regular users, 2048 for channels; Max: unknown). No per-provider constant is needed since no captions are used.

title: lib/ai/providers/__init__.py exports only 3 provider classes — not 5
content:
Current `lib/ai/providers/__init__.py` exports exactly three names: `YcAIProvider`, `YcOpenaiProvider`, `OpenrouterProvider`. Notably absent from exports:

- `BasicOpenAIProvider` / `BasicOpenAIModel` — internal base classes, not re-exported
- `CustomOpenAIProvider` — used by `LLMManager` (registered under config key `"custom-openai"`) but not re-exported
- `FastembedProvider` / `FastembedModel` — used by `LLMManager` (registered under config key `"fastembed"`) but not re-exported

This is a more restrictive export set than previously documented (memory b8dae5fa claimed `BasicOpenAIProvider` and `BasicOpenAIModel` were also exported — the `__init__.py` was trimmed at some point). The pattern is: only the "top-level" providers consumers would reference directly are exported. Base classes and provider-specific implementations are accessible only via their full module path (`lib.ai.providers.basic_openai_provider.BasicOpenAIProvider`) or via `LLMManager`.

title: Event loop lifecycle: single loop created in main(), shared across GromozekBot and platform adapters, closed in finally
content:
main.py manages the complete event loop lifecycle in `main()` (lines 320-327):
1. `loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()` — creates a fresh loop
2. `asyncio.set_event_loop(loop)` — sets it as the current loop
3. Loop is passed to `GromozekBot.__init__(configManager, loop)` and stored as `self._loop`
4. Loop is passed to `GromozekBot.run(loop)` which delegates to `self.botApp.run(loop)`
5. Both TelegramBotApplication (line 327) and MaxBotApplication (line 136) accept the loop parameter
6. Telegram adapter uses `application.run_polling(close_loop=False)` (line 404) to avoid closing the shared loop
7. `_shutdown()` runs on the shared loop via `loop.run_until_complete(self._shutdown())` (line 172)
8. `finally: loop.close()` (line 327) — loop is closed in the finally block of main()

Key invariant: NO component other than main.py owns the loop lifecycle. Platform adapters explicitly refuse to close it (close_loop=False). Shutdown runs on the same loop.

title: Scheduler lifecycle centralized to GromozekBot, removed from platform adapters
content:
The scheduler task (`_schedulerTask`) and its lifecycle management were removed from both platform-specific application classes and centralized in GromozekBot (main.py):

- GromozekBot.__init__ (main.py line 66-69): `self._schedulerTask = loop.create_task(QueueService.getInstance().startDelayedScheduler(self.database), name="delayed-scheduler")` — started in __init__
- GromozekBot._shutdown() (main.py lines 130-135): scheduler cancellation + QueueService drain — stopped in _shutdown()

Changes in TelegramBotApplication (internal/bot/telegram/application.py):
- `_schedulerTask` attribute: REMOVED
- `postInit` (line 237-308): NO scheduler task creation — only handler init + command setup
- `postStop` (line 311-325): NO scheduler await — only handler shutdown

Changes in MaxBotApplication (internal/bot/max/application.py):
- `_schedulerTask` attribute: REMOVED
- `postInit` (line 80-99): NO scheduler task creation — only handler init
- `postStop` (line 101-134): NO scheduler await — only task tracking set cleanup + handler shutdown + rate limiter destroy

This means platform adapters are now pure bot-communication layers with no scheduler awareness. The scheduler lives as part of the application bootstrap in main.py only.

title: Gotcha: Telegram uses resolveProxy(...).getCombined(), Max uses raw resolveProxy(...) without .getCombined()
content:
There is a call-style asymmetry in how the two platform adapters call ProxyService.resolveProxy (verified 2026-08-21):

- Telegram (internal/bot/telegram/application.py:355): `proxyConfig = ProxyService.getInstance().resolveProxy(botConfig, "telegram-bot").getCombined()` — chains `.getCombined()` explicitly (comment at 351-354 explains getProxyURL/toKwargs call getCombined() internally anyway, so the second call is a no-op) and then switches on `proxyConfig.type` for HTTP (.proxy() builder) vs SOCKS5 (two separate HTTPXRequest instances with toKwargs()).

- Max (internal/bot/max/application.py:311): `proxyConfig = ProxyService.getInstance().resolveProxy(botConfig, "max-bot")` — passes the raw ProxyConfig object to MaxBotClient, which calls toKwargs() internally (client.py:227).

IMPORTANT correction to the earlier version of this memory: `.getCombined()` returns a **ProxyConfig**, NOT a dict — both platforms ultimately work with ProxyConfig objects, and `getProxyURL()`/`toKwargs()` call `self.getCombined()` internally (lib/proxy/__init__.py:411, 442), so Max's raw config gets combined lazily at use time. The asymmetry is stylistic (pre-combined for the match block vs lazy combination), not a type difference.

title: PythonRuntime.validatePackageSpec docstring claims shell-metachar check but only does PEP 508 validation
content: In `lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/runtime.py` lines 164-179, `PythonRuntime.validatePackageSpec()` has a docstring (lines 165-174) claiming it "Rejects specs containing shell metacharacters or starting with '-'." However, the implementation (lines 176-179) only calls `Requirement(spec)` (PEP 508 validation), which does NOT check for shell metacharacters (;, |, &, $, backticks) or leading `-`. The actual shell metacharacter and leading-dash checks are implemented in `SandboxManager._validatePackageSpec()` (`lib/sandbox/manager.py` lines 1241-1264). This is a docstring vs. code mismatch: either the docstring is wrong (the Python runtime relies on the manager-level guard) or the implementation is incomplete.

title: ContainerSpec violates input-classes-should-be-frozen convention in sandbox types.py
content: In `lib/sandbox/types.py`, the module docstring (lines 3-5) states: "Input classes are frozen (immutable); output classes are mutable." The input classes `NetworkPolicy` (line 40) and `ResourceLimits` (line 51) correctly use `@dataclass(slots=True, frozen=True)`. However, `ContainerSpec` (line 481, `@dataclass(slots=True)`) is logically an input class — it specifies container creation parameters — but is NOT frozen, violating the module's own convention. All output classes (`ShutdownResult`, `RunInfo`, `RunResult`, `FileInfo`, `FileContent`, `PackageInfo`, `HealthcheckResult`, `GcResult`, `SessionInfo`, `ContainerOutcome`, `ManagedContainerInfo`) correctly use `@dataclass(slots=True)` without `frozen=True`.

title: _generateImageViaImagesApi does not reject non-image Content-Type on URL download
content:
In `BasicOpenAIModel._generateImageViaImagesApi()` at `lib/ai/providers/basic_openai_provider.py` (~line 835), when a URL-returned image is downloaded via `httpx.AsyncClient`, the Content-Type header is checked only to *update* the mediaMimeType (if it starts with `"image/"`). There is **no `else` branch** — non-image Content-Types (e.g., `text/html`, `application/octet-stream`) are silently accepted, and the raw bytes are stored in `mediaData` and returned to the caller as-if they were valid image data. The code trusts whatever the upstream server returns without enforcement.

Additionally, there is no hostname validation for internal/private IPs after the HTTPS scheme check passes — the URL is fetched from any HTTPS host, which is a potential SSRF vector. (The scheme check for `https` does exist at line 817.)

Status as of June 2026: unfixed.

title: Correction: internal/bot/common/workers/ directory does NOT exist (not just missing __init__.py)
content: Correction to memory ID 05e8568e: `configs/00-defaults/bot-defaults.toml` is **415 lines** as of 2026-07-14 (verified via wc -l). An earlier correction claimed 315 lines (2026-06-29), but the file has since grown by ~100 lines as new default settings were added (bot tier defaults, memory/embedding settings, divination, etc.).
