title: deleted_at filter asymmetry FIXED — saveMemoryEmbedding now filters, deleteMemoryEmbedding must NOT
content:
The `deleted_at IS NULL` asymmetry between the two embedding-layer methods in `internal/database/repositories/user_memories.py` is load-bearing — a blanket 'add deleted_at IS NULL to all queries' pass would BREAK the soft-delete cleanup path.

**FILTERS deleted_at (correct):** `saveMemoryEmbedding`'s internal SELECT (~line 1128-1139) fetches `permanent` from `user_memories WHERE chat_id/user_id/memory_id AND deleted_at IS NULL`. A soft-deleted row falls through to `memoryRow is None` → returns False — a soft-deleted memory must never be re-embedded into vec0 (which has no deleted_at column). Only the regen-cron gatekeeper (already filtered) and `addMemory` (fresh live rows) reach here today; the guard is defense-in-depth.

**Does NOT filter deleted_at (MUST NOT — invariant):** `deleteMemoryEmbedding`'s provenance-nulling UPDATE (~line 1353-1371) sets `user_memories.model_id = NULL` with NO deleted_at filter. It runs from `deleteMemory` (soft-delete path, vecOnly=False) AFTER the row was just soft-deleted (deleted_at now set); the UPDATE must match the just-soft-deleted row to null the single `model_id` provenance column (post-migration_025 shape — the old embedding_model/embedding_dimensions pair is gone). Adding `deleted_at IS NULL` here would skip the provenance reset → `getMemoriesWithoutEmbeddings` would never re-surface control stays correct.

All other live reads (getPermanentMemories, getLatestMemories, getMemory, getDistinctTags, both search paths, getMemoriesWithoutEmbeddings, deleteObsoleteMemoryEmbeddings staleWhere) filter `deleted_at IS NULL`; `getMemoriesByIds` deliberately does not (historical reconstruction).

title: LRUCache.get requires default arg; use `in` for membership probe; union valueType needs pyright ignore
content:
Gotchas about the `LRUCache` class in `internal/services/cache/service.py` (complements memory 88282a3a which documents `LRUCache.set`'s `ensureTypes=False` default). Confirmed 2026-07-09.

**1. `LRUCache.get(self, key, default)` — `default` is REQUIRED (no None fallback).**
Unlike `dict.get(key, default=None)`, the LRUCache `get` signature is `def get(self, key: K, default: V) -> V:` — `default` has no default value. You CANNOT call `cache.get(key)`. For a cache typed `LRUCache[str, Optional[SingleMemoryDict]]` (V = Optional[...]), pass `None` explicitly: `cache.get(mid, None)`. The `.get()` call moves the key to the end (LRU touch) on hit.

**2. Use `key not in cache` for membership probing, NOT `.get()`.**
To partition hits vs misses WITHOUT perturbing LRU order, use `mid not in self.memoriesById`. LRUCache subclasses `OrderedDict` and does NOT override `__contains__`, so `key in cache` uses OrderedDict's membership test (no LRU touch). Calling `.get(key, None)` just to check presence would inappropriately mark the key recently-used.

**3. Union types in `LRUCache(keyType=..., valueType=...)` need `# pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]`.**
When constructing an LRUCache whose `valueType` is a union (e.g. `valueType=Optional[SingleMemoryDict]`) or `keyType` is a union (e.g. `keyType=int | str`), pyright flags `reportArgumentType` because the param expects `Type[V]` and a union isn't a plain `Type`. The existing CHATS entry already has `# pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]` on its `keyType=int | str`; mirror that pattern for any new union keyType/valueType.

title: reportTypedDictNotRequiredAccess=false pragma + local-binding for Optional narrowing in test files
content:
Convention for test files that access `NotRequired` TypedDict keys (confirmed 2026-07-09). Two reusable pyright workarounds for the Gromozeka codebase, where TypedDicts with `NotRequired` fields are common (e.g. `SingleMemoryDict.id`, which is `NotRequired` because `convertDBMemoryToSingleMemoryDict` only adds it when `keepId=True`).

**1. File-level pragma for NotRequired access:**
Add `# pyright: reportTypedDictNotRequiredAccess=false` at the top of the test file (after the module docstring, before imports). This mirrors `tests/database/repositories/test_user_memories.py` (line 22). Use it when a test legitimately accesses a `NotRequired` key after ensuring (by construction) the key is present — e.g. asserting `entry["id"] == ...` on an entry built with `keepId=True`. The pragma disables the check for the whole file, so only apply it to files focused on the TypedDict in question, not general-purpose test files. Applied in `tests/services/cache/test_cache_service.py` for the `TestMemoriesByIdCache` class.

**2. Optional narrowing via local binding (no pragma needed for this one):**
When subscripting a value typed `Optional[TypedDict]` from a dict (e.g. `resolved = getMemoriesByIds(...); resolved[idA]["content"]`), pyright errors "Object of type None is not subscriptable" because it re-evaluates `resolved[idA]` each access and can't narrow across the expression. Fix: bind to a local FIRST, then narrow:
```python
entryA = resolved[idA]
assert entryA is not None
assert entryA["content"] == "alpha"
```
This narrows `entryA` to the TypedDict. Subscripting inside a comprehension (`{resolved[mid]["content"] for mid in ids}`) CANNOT be narrowed this way — restructure to iterate bound locals or filter None explicitly.

title: Spy pattern: patch.object(Repo, method, new=AsyncMock(wraps=original)) for call-count assertions against real DB
content:
Testing convention for asserting that a repo method was called N times while STILL hitting the real database (confirmed 2026-08-20 in `tests/services/cache/test_cache_service.py::TestMemoriesByIdCache`, lines 888-891 and 954). Complements memory 814d7aa8 (reset CacheService + injectDatabase for real-DB round-trips) and contrasts with the BROKEN `patch.object(..., return_value=AsyncMock(...))` pattern (memory 518dd36a).

**The pattern:**
```python
original = testDatabase.userMemories.getMemoriesByIds
with patch.object(UserMemoriesRepository, "getMemoriesByIds", new=AsyncMock(wraps=original)) as spy:
    resolved = await cacheService.getMemoriesByIds([idA, idB])
    spy.assert_called_once_with([idA, idB], chatId=None, dataSource=None)
    # ... cache warm-up ...
    assert spy.call_count == 1  # warm hit does not query DB again
```

**Why `new=AsyncMock(wraps=original)` (not `return_value=`):**
- `wraps=original` makes the AsyncMock DELEGATE to the real (unbound) method, so the actual SQLite query still runs and returns real rows. You get genuine integration behavior PLUS a `.call_count` / `.call_args` spy.
- `return_value=AsyncMock(...)` is broken for this use case: `patch.object` with `return_value=` creates a MagicMock that is not directly awaitable.
- Patching the CLASS (not the instance) is required because the cache service holds a reference to the repo via `self.database.userMemories`; patching the bound instance method after construction doesn't always intercept. Class-level patch with `new=` replaces the attribute lookup the instance resolves.

**Note:** `UserMemoriesRepository` defines `__slots__ = ("_modelIdResolver",)` (internal/database/repositories/user_memories.py:172) — a non-empty slots tuple, but still NO instance `__dict__`, so instance-level attribute patching remains impossible and the class-level patch is the correct layer. Same pattern applies to other slotted repos, e.g. `ChatUsersRepository` (`__slots__ = ()`, chat_users.py:34) in tests/bot/common/handlers/test_user_info_cache_regression.py:222-226 (dual spies on updateChatUser + getChatUser).

**Test scaffolding:** class/module-scoped autouse fixture resetting `CacheService._instance = None` around each test, then `cache = CacheService.getInstance()` + `await cache.injectDatabase(testDatabase)`.

title: Negative caching soundness verified — both addMemory call sites generate fresh uuid.uuid4().hex
content:
Verified the soundness of negative caching (storing `None` for not-found memory IDs) in `CacheService.getMemoriesByIds`. The reasoning: `addMemory` takes a caller-supplied `memoryId` param, and BOTH production call sites generate a fresh UUID immediately before insert:

1. `internal/bot/common/handlers/user_memories.py:532` — `memoryId = uuid.uuid4().hex` then `await db.userMemories.addMemory(..., memoryId=memoryId, ...)`
2. `internal/bot/common/handlers/user_memories.py:2648` — same pattern (manual memory-add wizard)

Since UUIDs are 128-bit random and always freshly generated, a previously-queried-and-not-found UUID can NEVER be reused as a memory ID for a new memory. Therefore a cached `None` is permanently correct for that ID. Combined with:
- Soft-delete preserves content (`getMemoriesByIds` repo method has NO `deleted_at` filter — returns soft-deleted rows for historical reconstruction; all other read methods filter `deleted_at IS NULL`).
- No `updateMemory` — content never changes in place.
- `MEMORY_ONLY` persistence clears the cache on process restart.

This confirms the 'no invalidation method' design decision is sound. No invalidation is needed for the MEMORIES namespace.

title: keepId invariant asymmetry: permanent loader keepId=True, by-id cache keepId=False
content:
Non-obvious design constraint in the memory-compaction cache layer (`internal/services/cache/service.py`), confirmed 2026-07-09 during Phase 3a implementation:

- **`getChatUserPermanentMemories`** uses `convertDBMemoryToSingleMemoryDict(m, keepId=True)` — each entry carries its `id` field. This is the WRITE path's source: `injectMemories` extracts `permanentIds` from the `id` field to persist compact IDs.
- **`getMemoriesByIds`** (the by-id resolution cache, Phase 2) uses `convertDBMemoryToSingleMemoryDict(row)` WITHOUT `keepId` (i.e., `keepId=False`). Resolved entries are looked up by dict key (`mid -> SingleMemoryDict`), so the internal `id` field is stripped. This prevents uuid leakage into `formatForLLM` (honors the `SingleMemoryDict.id` invariant: "absent on injected/in-memory snapshots").

Do NOT change `getMemoriesByIds` to `keepId=True` — that would leak uuids into the LLM context. Do NOT change `getChatUserPermanentMemories` back to `keepId=False` — that would break the compact-ID extraction in `injectMemories`.

title: Walrus operator + is not None narrows Optional in list comprehensions (avoids cast)
content:
Reusable pyright pattern confirmed in `internal/bot/models/ensured_message.py` `EnsuredMessage.formatForLLM` (the JSON branch, ~lines 1147-1156):

When filtering `Optional[T]` values out of a dict in a list comprehension, the walrus operator `:=` combined with an `is not None` predicate narrows the bound variable to the non-Optional type. This is cleaner than `cast()`:

```python
# cache.getMemoriesByIds returns Dict[str, Optional[SingleMemoryDict]]
permanentEntries: List[SingleMemoryDict] = [
    entry for mid in permanentIds if (entry := resolved.get(mid)) is not None
]
```

Pyright narrows `entry` to `SingleMemoryDict` (not `Optional`) inside the comprehension body. Without the walrus, `resolved.get(mid)` returns `Optional[SingleMemoryDict]` and a plain `if resolved.get(mid)` filter does NOT narrow the element type — pyright keeps it as `SingleMemoryDict | None`, requiring `cast(SingleMemoryDict, resolved[mid])` instead.

Note: this pattern lives in `formatForLLM` (memory resolution happens lazily at LLM-render time via `cache.getMemoriesByIds`), NOT in a method called `resolveMemories` (that method does not exist). Earlier form of this memory misnamed the method.

This is a cleaner alternative to the `cast()` pattern for cases where the value comes from a dict `.get()` with a None filter.

title: formatForLLM JSON branch drops falsy values via `if v` — userMemories=None omits the key
content:
`EnsuredMessage.formatForLLM` JSON branch (internal/bot/models/ensured_message.py:1174-1189) builds the output dict then filters it with `if v` — ALL falsy values are dropped before serialization, not just userMemories. The `userMemories` value is a LOCAL dict built at render time (ADR-018; there is no per-message field): it is empty — and therefore the key is OMITTED — whenever cache=None (non-chat/TEXT path), metadata carries no memory IDs, all IDs are filtered out by excludeMemoryIds, or nothing resolves from cache/DB (stale references, negative-cached None). Legacy content-form metadata rows (no permanentIds/shortTermIds keys) also render WITHOUT the key. (Pre-ADR-018 the empty case emitted an `{"permanent": [], "shortTerm": []}` dict — that legacy noise behaviour is gone.)

When writing tests that assert on formatForLLM JSON output, use json.loads(output) and check `assert "userMemories" not in parsed` for the omitted case rather than `assert parsed["userMemories"] is None`. Documented in the formatForLLM docstring (:1083-1088) and ADR-018's 'Stale-ID behavioral delta' consequence (docs/llm/architecture.md:693).

title: pyright: ast.AST base type doesn't declare lineno — return it from helpers, don't access on bare AST
content:
Pyright gotcha for AST-based tests/code in this repo (pyright typeCheckingMode=basic, no-Any rule).

When iterating `ast` nodes (e.g. via `ast.walk` or a custom scope-aware walk that yields `ast.AST`), accessing `node.lineno` triggers a pyright error: `Cannot access attribute "lineno" for class "AST" — Attribute "lineno" is unknown`. This is because the base `ast.AST` type does not declare `lineno` (only concrete statement/expression subclasses like `ast.Call`, `ast.Assign` do).

**Wrong:** collect nodes into a `List[ast.AST]` and access `.lineno` at the call site — pyright can't narrow through the helper's isinstance check.

**Right:** have the classifier helper return the lineno alongside its classification. E.g. a helper `_nameAttrCall(node: ast.AST) -> Optional[Tuple[str, str, int]]` that returns `(name, attr, lineno)` after internally narrowing with `isinstance(node, ast.Call)`. The caller never touches `.lineno` on a bare `ast.AST`.

Encountered 2026-07-09 while building `tests/test_memory_resolution_coverage.py`.

**Related AST technique (correctness, not types):** `ast.walk` does BFS and descends into nested `FunctionDef`/`AsyncFunctionDef`/`Lambda`/`ClassDef` bodies, causing double-counting when you iterate per-function. For per-function analysis, use a scope-aware walk that yields a node but does NOT descend into nested scope nodes:

```python
def walkScopeBody(func: ast.AST):
    stack = list(ast.iter_child_nodes(func))
    while stack:
        node = stack.pop()
        yield node
        if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.Lambda, ast.ClassDef)):
            continue  # yielded but not descended
        stack.extend(ast.iter_child_nodes(node))
```

For source-order comparison of events (assignments vs. resolve calls vs. render calls), collect all matches into lists with their linenos, then sort by lineno — do not rely on `ast.walk`'s traversal order.

title: migration_021 deleted_at corrected TEXT→TIMESTAMP per Gate-2 review (SQLite affinity-neutral)
content:
migration_021's `deleted_at` column was CORRECTED from `TEXT` to `TIMESTAMP` on 2026-07-09 per a Gate-2 whole-work review fix. The locked decision (plan §1.3 #1, §2.1/§2.3 "Portable TIMESTAMP type") was always TIMESTAMP — the migration SQL had drifted to `TEXT`, creating an internal self-contradiction (module docstring said TIMESTAMP, SQL said TEXT).

After fix: `ALTER TABLE user_memories ADD COLUMN deleted_at TIMESTAMP NULL` (line ~68). The `up()` docstring was also aligned from `deleted_at TEXT` → `deleted_at TIMESTAMP`. The `down()` (no-op-logs) was left untouched.

This aligns with sibling columns `created_at`/`updated_at` in migration_020 (both `TIMESTAMP NOT NULL`).

**SQLite affinity insight (still valid):** TIMESTAMP has no native storage class in SQLite; it is stored as TEXT affinity (ISO-8601 strings). The TEXT→TIMESTAMP keyword change is affinity-neutral — no behavioral change, tests stayed green at 3079 passed, 11 skipped. But TIMESTAMP is the correct keyword per the project's SQL portability rules (AGENTS.md lists TIMESTAMP as a portable type; PostgreSQL/MySQL have native TIMESTAMP).

**vec0 EXCEPTION (unchanged):** vec0 virtual tables REQUIRE `TEXT` for date columns because vec0's column-type parser rejects `TIMESTAMP` (see separate memory cd64051e). This only applies to vec0 virtual tables, not app-level tables.

**Docs convention (unchanged):** All app-level timestamp columns remain documented as `TIMESTAMP` in `docs/database-schema*.md`. The docs and migration SQL now AGREE (both TIMESTAMP) — previously they diverged.

**Supersedes deleted memory 342b1ca5**, which incorrectly interpreted the TEXT/TIMESTAMP divergence as an intentional convention and advised against fixing the migration. That advice was wrong — the locked decision was TIMESTAMP and the migration was a drift bug.

title: getMemoriesByIds now accepts chatId/dataSource for data-source routing
content:
As of 2026-07-10, `getMemoriesByIds` at both the repo and cache layers accepts `chatId` and `dataSource` params for data-source routing. This supersedes the previous design where no scoping was passed (UUIDs are still globally unique per DB, but routing now determines WHICH DB is queried on cache miss).

**Repo layer** (`UserMemoriesRepository.getMemoriesByIds`, internal/database/repositories/user_memories.py):
- Signature: `async def getMemoriesByIds(self, memoryIds: List[str], chatId: Optional[int] = None, dataSource: Optional[str] = None) -> List[UserMemoryDict]`
- Provider call: `await self.manager.getProvider(chatId=chatId, dataSource=dataSource, readonly=True)`
- Default None → falls back to `self.default` provider (same as before).

**Cache layer** (`CacheService.getMemoriesByIds`, internal/services/cache/service.py):
- Signature: `async def getMemoriesByIds(self, memoryIds: List[str], chatId: Optional[int] = None, dataSource: Optional[str] = None) -> Dict[str, Optional[SingleMemoryDict]]`
- Forwards to repo: `await self.database.userMemories.getMemoriesByIds(missingIds, chatId=chatId, dataSource=dataSource)`
- Cache key stays `mid` (the UUID) — a hit returns correct content regardless of routing. Routing only affects which DB is queried on miss.

**Read-path caller** (`EnsuredMessage.resolveMemories`, ensured_message.py):
- Calls `cache.getMemoriesByIds(allIds, chatId=self.recipient.id)` — passes the message's chatId (self.recipient.id is the chatId for EnsuredMessage).

**Also fixed:** 4 stale docstrings in cache/service.py that referenced `memoriesById`/`MEMORIES_BY_ID` (the old namespace name) → corrected to `memories`/`MEMORIES` (CacheNamespace.MEMORIES).

title: One-off DB maintenance script structural pattern (confirmed across 2 scripts)
content:
Confirmed convention for one-off database maintenance scripts in `scripts/` (established by `scripts/clear_memory_refinement.py`, replicated by `scripts/clear_old_format_memories.py`). When writing a new maintenance script that mutates JSON metadata columns, follow this structural pattern:

1. **Manual transaction control**: `sqlite3.connect(path, isolation_level=None)` then explicit `BEGIN` / `COMMIT` / `ROLLBACK`. Do NOT use the default isolation level or `with conn:` context manager — manual control lets the dry-run path short-circuit before opening a transaction.

2. **Dry-run short-circuit**: `if dryRun or not pendingUpdates: <report and return>` placed BEFORE `BEGIN`. Dry-run must never open a write transaction. The `--dry-run` flag uses `dest="dryRun"` (not the argparse default `dry_run`) to maintain the repo's camelCase convention — argparse auto-converts `--dry-run` to `dry_run` (snake_case) by default, which violates the camelCase rule.

3. **`conn.close()` in `finally`**: always close the connection in a finally block, not just on success.

4. **TOCTOU warning in module docstring**: the script does SELECT-then-UPDATE (fetchall all rows, process in Python, batch UPDATE). Between SELECT and UPDATE the bot could modify a row and the UPDATE would clobber it. The module docstring MUST warn to stop the bot first. This is inherent to the design and accepted for one-off use.

5. **Serializer**: mirror production `jsonDumps` shape — `json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",",":"), sort_keys=True)`. Omit `default=str` (safe because input is fresh `json.loads` output; see memory 407216e6 for full rationale).

6. **PK-targeted WHERE**: UPDATE must target the table's full primary key. For `chat_messages` that's `WHERE chat_id = ? AND message_id = ?` (chat_id INTEGER, message_id TEXT). For `chat_users` that's `WHERE chat_id = ? AND user_id = ?`.

7. **Idempotency**: a second run must be a no-op (0 updates). After removing a key, the row no longer has it, so the classifier skips it on re-run.

8. **Edge-case safety**: malformed JSON, non-dict metadata, non-dict `memories` value, empty metadata — all must be safely skipped (SKIP_MALFORMED / SKIP_NO_KEY), never crash, never modify.

9. **No committed tests required**: one-off maintenance scripts don't need regression tests or doc updates (see memory 7dc32611). The script should be stdlib-only (no project imports).

10. **Action enum + counters**: use a `StrEnum` for classification actions (UPDATE, SKIP_NO_KEY, SKIP_MALFORMED, SKIP_NEW_FORMAT, etc.) with per-action counters for the summary report.

title: StrEnum test-data gotcha: use VALUE not NAME — MessageType("TEXT") fails, MessageType("text") works
content:
Gotcha discovered 2026-07-10 during Phase A gate-fixing of the memory-compaction refactor.

When constructing test data dicts that include StrEnum-typed fields (e.g., `ChatMessageDict["message_type"]`), you must use the enum's **VALUE** (the lowercase string), not its **NAME** (the uppercase identifier).

**Concrete example:** `MessageType` is a `StrEnum` with `TEXT = "text"`. The `_chatMessageDict` test helper in `tests/bot/models/test_ensured_message.py` set `"message_type": "TEXT"` (the name). When `fromDBChatMessage` calls `MessageType(data["message_type"])`, this does `MessageType("TEXT")` which looks up by VALUE — and `"TEXT"` is NOT a value (`"text"` is). Result: `ValueError: 'TEXT' is not a valid MessageType`.

**Fix:** Use the lowercase string value `"text"` (or `MessageType.TEXT.value`, or just `MessageType.TEXT` since StrEnum members ARE str instances).

**General rule:** `StrEnum("X")` constructor looks up by VALUE, not by NAME. This applies to all StrEnums in the codebase (MessageType, MemoryType, ProxyType, etc.). When round-tripping enum values through DB → JSON → dict → enum constructor, the stored value must be the enum's `.value`, not its `.name`.

title: Testing maintenance scripts: tmp_path not :memory:, capsys for counters
content:
Gotcha for testing maintenance scripts in `scripts/` that call `sqlite3.connect(str(dbPath))` internally (e.g. `clear_old_format_memories.py:processDatabase`, `clear_memory_refinement.py:processDatabase`):

1. **`:memory:` does NOT work.** Each `sqlite3.connect(":memory:")` call creates a fresh, empty, per-connection database. Since `processDatabase` opens its own connection, any table you pre-populate via a separate setup connection will be invisible. Must use `tmp_path` to create a file-based SQLite DB so all connections share the same data.

2. **`processDatabase` returns only an exit code (0).** Row counters (scanned, skipped, updated, new-format) are printed to stdout with right-padded 16-char labels, e.g. `f"{'Rows updated:':<16}{count}"`. In dry-run mode the label changes to `'Rows to update:'`. To verify counter values in tests, capture stdout via `capsys` fixture and parse lines by label prefix.

Example test pattern (from `tests/scripts/test_clear_old_format_memories.py`, 18 tests):
```python
def _parseCounter(stdout: str, label: str) -> int:
    for line in stdout.splitlines():
        if line.startswith(label):
            return int(line[len(label):].strip())
    raise AssertionError(...)

def testUpdate(capsys, tmp_path):
    dbPath = tmp_path / "test.db"
    # create table + insert old-format row...
    rc = processDatabase(dbPath, dryRun=False, verbose=False)
    assert rc == 0
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    assert _parseCounter(captured.out, "Rows updated:") == 1
```

The `chat_messages`-like test table should use `PRIMARY KEY (chat_id, message_id)` with `metadata TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ""`.

title: Sibling maintenance scripts align SELECT column order with PK definition
content:
Convention confirmed 2026-07-10: sibling maintenance scripts in `scripts/` that walk a table and rewrite rows should SELECT columns in primary-key definition order, keeping the scripts parallel.

Applied to `scripts/clear_old_format_memories.py`: the SELECT was reordered from `SELECT message_id, chat_id, metadata` to `SELECT chat_id, message_id, metadata` to match the `PRIMARY KEY (chat_id, message_id)` definition and the sibling `scripts/clear_memory_refinement.py` (which does `SELECT chat_id, user_id, metadata` matching `PRIMARY KEY (chat_id, user_id)`).

When reordering, three things must change together:
1. The SELECT statement column list.
2. The `for` loop unpacking order (`for chatId, messageId, metadata in rows:`).
3. The `rows` type annotation (e.g. `list[tuple[int, str, str]]` for `(chatId: int, messageId: str, metadata: str)`).

The `pendingUpdates` list and its `WHERE chat_id = ? AND message_id = ?` clause are unaffected — they're already in PK order.

title: sqlToCustomType union member probing logs ERROR on happy path
content:
Systemic gotcha in `sqlToCustomType` (`internal/database/utils.py`): when a field is typed `Union[TypedDictA, TypedDictB]`, the two-loop Union iteration (lines 132-141) probes each member. For a TypedDict member that doesn't match the data (missing required keys), the recursive `sqlToCustomType` call enters the TypedDict branch (lines 288-293), `sqlToTypedDict` raises `KeyError`, which is caught at line 291 and logged at **ERROR level** (`logger.error(f"Failed to convert {data} to {expectedType}: {e}")`). The function returns `(False, None)`, the Union loop tries the next member, which may succeed. The ERROR is therefore logged on the HAPPY PATH — the data loads correctly via the second member.

**Root cause:** The KeyError catch at utils.py:291-293 doesn't distinguish "probing a union member" (expected failure) from "genuine validation failure" (real error). It logs all failures at ERROR.

**Current state (verified 2026-07-14):** No field in the codebase currently uses a Union of two TypedDicts, so this issue is DORMANT. The original trigger — `MetadataDict.memories: UserMemoriesDict | CompactMemoryIdsDict` in `internal/bot/models/message_metadata.py` — was simplified to a single TypedDict (`memories: CompactMemoryIdsDict`, line 257). The Union was removed entirely, not just reordered. The remaining `randomContext: Union[str, CondensingDict]` only triggers the spurious ERROR on genuinely invalid data (a dict missing the required `text` key), not on the happy path.

**Deeper fix (still NOT applied):** Demote union-member probe failures to DEBUG in `sqlToCustomType`. Any future `Union[TypedDictA, TypedDictB]` field will hit the spurious ERROR if the common-case member isn't first in the union.

title: Pyright: NotRequired TypedDict key access in list comprehensions — use walrus + .get()
content:
Complements memory c3b784cd (which covers `.get(key, default)` for sort lambdas with NotRequired keys).

When filtering AND extracting a `NotRequired` key from TypedDict entries in a list comprehension, pyright's `reportTypedDictNotRequiredAccess` (even in `typeCheckingMode = "basic"`) flags `m["key"]` access even when guarded by `if m.get("key")`. The `.get()` truthy guard does NOT narrow `__getitem__` access for TypedDicts.

**Fails pyright:**
```python
"permanentIds": [m["id"] for m in permanent if m.get("id")]
```

**Passes pyright (walrus pattern):**
```python
"permanentIds": [mid for m in permanent if (mid := m.get("id"))]
```

The walrus captures the `.get()` return value, and the `if` truthiness check narrows it. This mirrors the `resolveMemories` pattern already used in `internal/bot/models/ensured_message.py` (e.g., `[entry for mid in permanentIds if (entry := resolved.get(mid)) is not None]`).

This applies wherever you need to both filter on and collect a NotRequired TypedDict key. Use walrus + `.get()` — never bracket access guarded by `.get()`.

title: Decision #7 superseded: compact-only format — old content-format read-path dropped
content:
Locked decision #7 ("read path detects format and handles both compact + old content formats") is SUPERSEDED as of the 2026-07-10 refactor. `loadMemoriesMetadata` (the format-detection + old-format fallback method) was fully deleted. Only the **compact format** (`{"permanentIds": [...], "shortTermIds": [...]}`) is now supported.

**Consequence:** old-format messages (`{"permanent": [...], "shortTerm": [...]}` in `metadata["memories"]`) now render SILENTLY without memories. There is no backward-compat read path.

**Mitigation:** a one-time cleanup script (`scripts/clear_old_format_memories.py`, mirrors `scripts/clear_memory_refinement.py` — raw sqlite3, `--dry-run`, TOCTOU warning) removes old-format `memories` from `chat_messages.metadata`, leaving compact-format entries untouched. Regression tests at `tests/scripts/test_clear_old_format_memories.py`.

This is documented as a "Superseded" note in `docs/llm/memories/user-memories.md` (read-path resolution section) and in ADR-017's follow-up note in `docs/llm/architecture.md`.

title: sqlToCustomType union member ORDER affects logger.error output — put common shape first
content:
`sqlToCustomType` (`internal/database/utils.py:89-316`) handles TypedDict unions by trying members in **declaration order** via two loops (lines 132-137 `_checkType`-gated, 138-141 ungated retry). When a TypedDict conversion FAILS (missing required key → KeyError), it is caught at line ~291 and `logger.error(...)` emitted at ~292 before returning (False, None); the union then tries the next member.

**Consequence:** union member ORDER directly affects production logging — if the common shape is NOT first, every load of a common-shape row logs a spurious ERROR; if it IS first, only rare/legacy shapes hit the error-log path.

**Historical example (now resolved):** during the 2026-07-10 memory-compaction refactor, `MetadataDict.memories` was `CompactMemoryIdsDict | UserMemoriesDict` (compact first) to avoid error spam. That union has since been REMOVED — `MetadataDict.memories` is now plain `CompactMemoryIdsDict` (internal/bot/models/message_metadata.py:263), so this specific example no longer applies; the ordering gotcha remains valid for any future TypedDict unions.

title: Embedding-reuse refactor: injectMemories receives pre-computed embedding instead of generating its own
content:
**Current architecture (was originally a refactor on branch user-memory-v2, now merged):** `MessagePreprocessorHandler.injectMemories` uses the SAME embedding as the message (one `generateEmbedding` call feeds both the `message_embeddings` write AND the memory-search query), instead of generating a separate embedding inside `injectMemories`.

**Deleted:** `internal/bot/common/embedding_utils.py` is gone (the shared free function `embedAndSaveMessage(ensuredMessage, modelName, db)` no longer exists).

**Moved:** `embedAndSaveMessage` is now a METHOD on `ChatSearchHandler` in `internal/bot/common/handlers/chat_search.py`. It resolves settings/model internally via `self.llmService.generateEmbedding(...)` — no `modelName`/`db` params. The backfill loop (`_dtCronJob`) calls `self.embedAndSaveMessage(...)`.

**Signature:** `MessagePreprocessorHandler.injectMemories(self, ensuredMessage: EnsuredMessage, embeddingModel: Optional[str], queryEmbedding: Optional[List[float]] = None) -> None`. The `getChatSettings` + `MEMORY_INJECTION_ENABLED` gate moved up into `newMessageHandler`.

**Key consequence:** when an embedding is computed for chat-search message-embedding purposes, that same vector is threaded into `injectMemories` for the memory semantic-retrieval query — one `generateEmbedding` call serves both. If chat-search is off but memory injection (relevant mode) is on, a separate embedding is generated for the memory path only. Embeddings are passed as raw `List[float]`, not pre-serialised bytes.

title: Gotcha: mock generateEmbedding boundary not getLLMManager chain — singleton leaks across tests
content:
**Gotcha: ChatSearchHandler embedAndSaveMessage test passes in isolation but fails in-suite — singleton-state leakage exposed by the embedding-reuse refactor.**

Test: `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_chat_search.py::TestDtCronJob::test_cron_per_message_error_does_not_abort_batch`. Signal: `assert mockModel.generateEmbeddings.await_count == 2` → got `0`.

**Root cause:** The refactor moved `embedAndSaveMessage` from a self-contained free function (which resolved the model via `getLLMManager().getModel(name)` and called `model.generateEmbeddings(text)` DIRECTLY) to a `ChatSearchHandler` method that routes through `self.llmService.generateEmbedding(...)`. That singleton method internally does three steps: (1) `resolveModel(...)` (routes through `chatSettings[EMBEDDING_MODEL].toModel()` → the singleton's `getLLMManager`), (2) `rateLimit(chatId, chatSettings)` (a NEW step the old direct path never had), (3) `model.generateEmbeddings(text)`.

The test mocks at the OLD boundary (`handler.llmService.getLLMManager = Mock(...)` → `getModel` → `mockModel.generateEmbeddings`), which it mutates ON the `LLMService.getInstance()` singleton. That mutation leaks across tests. A sibling test (`test_cron_embeds_pending_messages`, same mock pattern, runs FIRST in definition order) leaves the shared singleton — particularly its `rateLimiterManager` state, which the new `generateEmbedding` exercises but the old path did not — in a state where `generateEmbedding`'s `try/except` swallows an exception and returns `None` BEFORE reaching `generateEmbeddings`. Hence `await_count == 0`.

**Proof it's test-side:** the test PASSES in isolation (`pytest tests/bot/common/handlers/test_chat_search.py::TestDtCronJob::test_cron_per_message_error_does_not_abort_batch` alone), FAILS in-suite. The refactor behavior is correct.

**Fix direction (TEST-UPDATE):** Mock the new boundary directly — `handler.llmService.generateEmbedding = AsyncMock(...)` returning a `(modelName, vector)` tuple (or `None`/raising for the error-isolation case) — instead of mocking the low-level `getLLMManager().getModel().generateEmbeddings` chain. This both matches the refactored call path and removes the dependency on mutable singleton state.

**Reusable convention:** When production code routes through `LLMService.generateEmbedding` (or any LLMService singleton method), tests must mock AT that boundary, not at the lower `model.generateEmbeddings` level. The `LLMService` singleton holds mutable state (`getLLMManager`, `rateLimiterManager`, `resolveModel`/`toModel` chain) that leaks across tests. The old pattern of mocking `getLLMManager().getModel().generateEmbeddings` only works when the code calls that chain directly.

title: generateEmbedding never-raises contract replaces old multi-layer error handling
content:
Embedding-path error isolation (corrected 2026-08-21 — an earlier version of this memory claimed `embedAndSaveMessage` had NO try/except and that the empty-text gate was removed entirely; BOTH claims are false of current code):

- **`LLMService.generateEmbedding`** (`internal/services/llm/service.py:1463-1503`) owns the never-raises contract: wraps `resolveModel` + `rateLimit` (skipped when `chatId is None`) + `model.generateEmbeddings` in a broad `try/except Exception` → `logger.exception` + `return None`. Returns `Optional[Tuple[str, List[float]]]`; callers treat `None` as 'skip the row'.
- **`ChatSearchHandler.embedAndSaveMessage`** (chat_search.py:524-572) ADDITIONALLY has its own try/except boundary returning `False` — the `_dtCronJob` loop comment (:503-506) explicitly relies on this helper-level boundary ('has its own try/except boundary and never raises'). So error isolation is NOT exclusively in generateEmbedding.
- **The empty-text gate EXISTS, on FORMATTED text**: both `MessagePreprocessorHandler.newMessageHandler` (message_preprocessor.py:220) and `embedAndSaveMessage` (chat_search.py:551) embed only `if messageText.strip():` where messageText is the `formatForLLM(TEXT, useSingleMedia=False)` output. Empty formatted text is NOT embedded (garbage-vector guard); media-only messages with a media description ARE embedded (user-confirmed intent — see memory 8d1874b9). The old RAW-text gate (`ensuredMessage.messageText.strip()`) is what was removed.
- `saveMessageEmbedding` repo method swallows exceptions internally (unchanged).

title: Module-level _llmManager cache in chat_settings.py not reset between tests — toModel() uses stale reference
content:
**Root-cause detail behind the singleton-leak gotcha (complements memory 84b64a50).**

`internal/bot/models/chat_settings.py` has a module-level `_llmManager: Optional["LLMManager"] = None` global (line 19) and a `getLLMManager()` function (line 22) that caches the LLMManager on first call: `_llmManager = LLMService.getInstance().getLLMManager()`. This exists to avoid a circular import (documented in memory 65122ef1).

**The problem:** The autouse `resetLlmServiceSingleton` fixture in `tests/conftest.py` (line 337) resets `LLMService._instance = None` before each test. But it does NOT reset the module-level `_llmManager` global in `chat_settings.py`. So after the first test that triggers `getLLMManager()`, the module global holds a reference to the OLD (now-destroyed) singleton's LLMManager.

**Why mocking `handler.llmService.getLLMManager` doesn't work for the `toModel()` path:** `ChatSettingsValue.toModel()` (chat_settings.py:586) calls the MODULE-LEVEL `getLLMManager()` function, NOT `handler.llmService.getLLMManager()`. So setting `cast(Any, h).llmService.getLLMManager = Mock(return_value=mockManager)` on the instance has ZERO effect on `toModel()` — the module global returns whatever was cached first. This is a silent disconnect: the instance mock works for code that calls `self.llmService.getLLMManager()` directly (like the CRON gate at chat_search.py:354), but NOT for code that goes through `toModel()` → `resolveModel()` → `generateEmbedding()`.

**Actionable fix:** When testing code that routes through `LLMService.generateEmbedding` (which calls `resolveModel` → `toModel`), mock `generateEmbedding` directly (`handler.llmService.generateEmbedding = AsyncMock(...)`) rather than trying to control the model-resolution chain. This bypasses both the module-level cache AND the singleton's mutable `rateLimiterManager` state.

title: generateEmbedding chatId type hint was stale (int → Optional[int])
content:
`LLMService.generateEmbedding` in `internal/services/llm/service.py` was declared with `chatId: int` but the body already branched on `if chatId is not None:` (skipping `rateLimit` when None) and the docstring explicitly documented "pass None to skip rate limiting (e.g. for a background regen tick)". The type hint was simply stale/wrong. Corrected to `chatId: Optional[int]` on 2026-07-10.

This was surfaced when the backfill path (`ChatSearchHandler.embedAndSaveMessage`) needed to pass `chatId=None` to avoid consuming per-chat hot-path rate budget — pyright flagged the `None` against `int`. Four other methods in `service.py` already used `chatId: Optional[int]`, so this aligned with convention.

Lesson: when a method's body and docstring handle `None` but the type hint says otherwise, the hint is the bug, not the callers.

title: embedAndSaveMessage now on ChatSearchHandler: backfill-only, never-crash, chatId=None
content:
`embedAndSaveMessage` lives on `ChatSearchHandler` (`internal/bot/common/handlers/chat_search.py:524`), moved from the deleted `internal/bot/common/embedding_utils.py` module. Contracts (verified 2026-08-21):

1. **Backfill-only**: the sole production caller is the `_dtCronJob` cron loop (:511); all other callers are tests.
2. **Never-crash**: body wrapped in `try/except Exception` → `logger.exception(...)` + `return False` (:543-572). The caller's comment (:503-506) explicitly relies on this boundary — a single bad row never aborts the batch.
3. **chatId=None**: passes `chatId=None` to `generateEmbedding` (:554) so background backfill does NOT consume the per-chat hot-path rate budget.
4. It applies its own formatted-text guard (`if messageText.strip():` on `formatForLLM(TEXT)` output, :551) before embedding.

Note (updated): the memory-regen cron is in **user_memories.py** (renamed from user_data.py) — `_runMemoryEmbeddingRegen` (~:914) still passes the real chatId and DOES consume rate budget (pre-existing asymmetry), while `_runSingleRefinement` passes `chatId=None` (:1301). `saveMessageEmbedding` in the repo also swallows exceptions internally, so the never-crash wrapper is belt-and-suspenders for the format/embed steps.

title: Multiple concurrent opencode sessions on same repo cause silent file clobbering
content:
On 2026-07-10, three live `opencode` processes were running concurrently on the same repo (confirmed via `ps aux | grep opencode` showing PIDs for 3 separate sessions). One session was actively rewriting `message_preprocessor.py`'s `newMessageHandler` #5 region with a different implementation than another session, causing repeated clobbering of edits.

Symptoms: edits would apply successfully, but re-reading the file moments later showed a completely different version (different structure, different variable names, added annotations like `Tuple`). The `git status` showed `MM` (modified in both index and working tree).

How to detect: if a file's content changes between your edit and a subsequent read without your intervention, run `ps aux | grep opencode` to check for multiple sessions. If found, the conflict is a coordination failure that the user must resolve (close other sessions or assign non-overlapping files).

This differs from the "parallel subagent" pattern (where a single session dispatches multiple subagents) — here it was independent top-level sessions each with their own editing loop.

title: injectMemories signature: queryEmbedding param selects latest vs semantic retrieval
content:
`MessagePreprocessorHandler.injectMemories` signature as of 2026-07-10:

```python
async def injectMemories(
    self,
    ensuredMessage: EnsuredMessage,
    embeddingModel: Optional[str],
    queryEmbedding: Optional[List[float]] = None,
) -> None:
```

Behavior:
- `queryEmbedding=None` (or omitted) → `getLatestMemories` (time-based, cap `EPHEMERAL_RETRIEVAL_LIMIT=5`, ephemeral-only).
- `queryEmbedding=<floats>` (non-None) + `embeddingModel=<str>` → `searchMemories(queryEmbedding=..., embeddingModel=..., permanent=False)` (vec0 semantic-ranked).

The param was renamed from `embeddings` (bare `Optional[list]`, AGENTS.md violation) to `queryEmbedding` (`Optional[List[float]]`) to match `searchMemories(queryEmbedding=...)`. It's a single float vector, matching `generateEmbedding`'s `Optional[Tuple[str, List[float]]]` return (the `[1]` element).

Call sites in `newMessageHandler` pass it positionally or as keyword (`queryEmbedding=embeddings[1]`). The embedding generation itself happens in `newMessageHandler`, NOT inside `injectMemories` — the refactor moved it out so the embedding can be reused for both chat-search and memory injection.

title: Empty-text embedding guard is on FORMATTED text — media-only messages ARE embedded (author's confirmed intent)
content:
**User-confirmed design decision (2026-07-10).** The empty-text guard in `MessagePreprocessorHandler.newMessageHandler` (`internal/bot/common/handlers/message_preprocessor.py`, ~lines 192-208) operates on the **formatted** `formatForLLM(TEXT, useSingleMedia=False)` output, NOT on the raw `ensuredMessage.messageText`:

```python
if chatSearchEnabled or chatMemoriesEmbeddingsEnabled:
    messageText = await ensuredMessage.formatForLLM(self.db, format=LLMMessageFormat.TEXT, useSingleMedia=False)
    if messageText.strip():
        embeddings = await self.llmService.generateEmbedding(...)
```

**This is correct and intentional.** The author WANTS media-only messages (empty raw text but non-empty media description) to be embedded. `formatForLLM(TEXT)` prepends a `<media-description>...</media-description>` block for messages with media content, so a media-only message produces non-empty formatted text → embedding IS generated. The media description provides the content for the embedding vector.

Behavioral rules:
- Empty/whitespace raw text + NO media → formatted text is empty → NOT embedded. Falls through to `injectMemories(queryEmbedding=None)` → `getLatestMemories`.
- Empty raw text + media → formatted text is `<media-description>[...]</media-description>\n\n` (non-empty) → IS embedded.

**Do NOT change this to a raw-text guard.** Two prior sessions (2026-07-10) incorrectly flagged the formatted guard as a "bug" or "defect" claiming media-only messages should not be embedded. Those analyses were WRONG and their memory entries were deleted. The formatted guard stays.

**Regression test pin:** `testMediaOnlyMessageTriggersEmbedding` in `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_message_preprocessor.py` — a media-only message (empty raw text + mediaContent) asserts `generateEmbedding` IS called. This test FAILS if the guard is changed to raw text and PASSES under the formatted guard.

title: Mock(spec=EnsuredMessage).formatForLLM returns truthy MagicMock — use real EnsuredMessage for embedding path tests
content:
**Gotcha in `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_message_preprocessor.py`.** When a test uses `_makeEnsuredMessage()` (which returns `Mock(spec=EnsuredMessage)`), the spec-introspected `formatForLLM` method is configured as an `AsyncMock`. When awaited, it returns `AsyncMock.return_value` = a `MagicMock` instance, which is **truthy**. So `messageText.strip()` returns a truthy Mock → the guard `if messageText.strip():` always passes → `generateEmbedding` is always called.

This caused `testNoDispatchEmptyText` to FAIL (asserted `generateEmbedding.assert_not_called()` but it WAS called 1 time). It also produced `RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'AsyncMockMixin._execute_mock_call' was never awaited` in `testDispatchAllGatesPass` and `testEmbeddingFailureReturnsNext`.

**Fix:** Tests that exercise the embedding path (where `formatForLLM`'s return value matters for the guard) must use a REAL `EnsuredMessage`, not a `Mock(spec=EnsuredMessage)`. A real `EnsuredMessage` runs its actual TEXT-formatting logic so `formatForLLM` returns a real string.

Helper `_realEnsuredMessageForEmbedding(*, messageText="", mediaContent=None)` builds a real `EnsuredMessage` for this purpose. Callers must wrap the handler call in `patch.object(EnsuredMessage, "updateMediaContent", AsyncMock(return_value=None))` because:
1. `formatForLLM` calls `self.updateMediaContent(db)` which polls the DB for media descriptions.
2. `EnsuredMessage` uses `__slots__`, so `updateMediaContent` cannot be patched at the instance level — it MUST be patched at the CLASS level via `patch.object(EnsuredMessage, ...)`.
3. The helper also calls `msg.setBaseMessage(Mock())` so `newMessageHandler`'s `getBaseMessage()` call doesn't raise `ValueError("Message is not set")`.

title: Testing pattern: building media-only EnsuredMessage for embedding regression tests
content:
**How to populate media content on a real `EnsuredMessage` for embedding tests** (tests/bot/common/handlers/test_message_preprocessor.py).

To make `formatForLLM(format=LLMMessageFormat.TEXT, useSingleMedia=False)` return a non-empty `<media-description>` block for a media-only message:

1. Set `msg.mediaContent = "description string"` — the TEXT branch checks `if self.mediaContent:` (the **attribute**) to decide whether to prepend the block.
2. Append a `MediaContent(id="media-1", content="description string", processingInfo=None)` to `msg.mediaList` — with `useSingleMedia=False`, the local `mediaContent` variable is reassigned to `[v.content for v in self.mediaList if v.content]`, and this list is what gets stringified into the `<media-description>{mediaContent}</media-description>` block.
3. Set `msg.mediaId = "media-1"` (any non-None value).
4. Set `msg.messageText = ""` (empty raw text — the key condition that distinguishes formatted from raw guard).
5. Wrap handler call in `patch.object(EnsuredMessage, "updateMediaContent", AsyncMock(return_value=None))` to prevent DB polling.

Import `MediaContent` from `internal.bot.models.ensured_message` (NOT re-exported from `internal.bot.models.__init__`).

The resulting `formatForLLM(TEXT)` output is `"<media-description>['description string']</media-description>\n\n"` — non-empty, so the formatted-text guard allows embedding.

**Regression test verification:** `testMediaOnlyMessageTriggersEmbedding` was verified to FAIL when the guard is temporarily changed to raw `ensuredMessage.messageText.strip()` and PASS under the formatted guard (AGENTS.md fails-before/passes-after requirement).

title: getUserIdByUserName is a misnomer — returns List[int] of chat_ids, not user_ids
content:
**Gotcha (2026-07-10):** `ChatUsersRepository.getUserIdByUserName` (internal/database/repositories/chat_users.py:362) is a misnomer. Despite the name, it does NOT return user IDs. Its signature:

```python
async def getUserIdByUserName(self, username: str, *, dataSource: Optional[str] = None) -> List[int]:
```

It performs a case-insensitive username lookup in the `chat_info` table (NOT `chat_users`) and returns a list of **chat_ids** associated with that username across data sources. It is a CROSS-CHAT lookup, not a per-chat lookup.

**Do NOT use this for per-chat user resolution.** It is only used in `HandlersManager` (manager.py:672) for resolving bot-owners by username. For resolving a username to a userId WITHIN a specific chat, use `getChatUserByUsername(chatId, username)` instead (chat_users.py:164), which returns `Optional[ChatUserDict]` from which you extract `["user_id"]`.

title: search_memories tool has optional `user` param for cross-user search
content:
As of 2026-07-10, the `search_memories` LLM tool (registered in `UserDataHandler.__init__`, gated on `self._memoryRefineEnabled`) has an optional `user` parameter that allows the LLM to search a DIFFERENT user's memories instead of the caller's own.

**Tool description (rewritten):** `"Search memories. By default searches the calling user's own memories; pass ``user`` to search a different user's memories. Pass ``query`` for semantic search, or omit it to list memories matching a filter (by type/tags)."`

The old description said "Only the caller's own memories are ever returned — never another user's." — that is now FALSE and was replaced.

**Handler behavior in `_llmToolSearchMemories`** (signature: `..., user: Optional[str] = None, ...`):
- `user=None` (omitted) → searches sender's own memories (preserved behavior).
- `user` provided → resolved via `self._resolveUserId(chatId=chatId, userIdentifier=user)`. If unresolved → returns `{"done": False, "error": f"User not found: {user}"}` immediately (does NOT call `searchMemories`).
- Numeric `user` (e.g. `"12345"`) → treated as user_id, no DB lookup.

**Asymmetric error behavior between tools (intentional design decision):**
- `search_memories`: errors on unresolvable user (`{"done": False, ...}`).
- `search_messages`: keeps the silent fallback (unresolved → `userFilter=None` → all users). Do NOT change message-search's fallback behavior.

This was a deliberate choice: message-search's all-users fallback is the established precedent; memory-search was given stricter behavior because searching the wrong user's memories (or all users') is more surprising than broadening a message search.

title: str.isdigit() admits Unicode superscripts int() can't parse — use str.isdecimal() as int() guard
content:
**Bug fix (2026-07-10):** `str.isdigit()` returns `True` for Unicode "other digit" characters (e.g. `"²"` U+00B2 superscript two, `"³"`, `"¹"`) that `int()` CANNOT parse → `int(clean)` raises `ValueError`. This broke the "never raises" contract of `BaseBotHandler._resolveUserId` (internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py), which is called by the unguarded message-search LLM tool path.

**Fix:** Change `clean.isdigit()` to `clean.isdecimal()`. `str.isdecimal()` is the precise predicate for the character set `int()` accepts in base 10. Superscripts like `"²"` are NOT decimal digits (`"²".isdecimal()` → `False`), so they fall through to the login path instead of hitting `int()`.

Sanity check: `'²'.isdecimal()` → `False`, `'²'.isdigit()` → `True`.

**General rule:** Anywhere you validate "is this string safe to pass to `int()` in base 10," use `str.isdecimal()`, not `str.isdigit()`. The three methods differ: `isdecimal()` ⊂ `isdigit()` ⊂ `isnumeric()`. Only `isdecimal()` corresponds exactly to what `int()` accepts.

Regression test: `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_base.py::TestResolveUserId::test_unicodeSuperscript_returnsNone` (pass `userIdentifier="²"`, assert result is None, no exception).

title: flake8 F841 flags unused 'except ... as e' binding when e is not referenced
content:
**Correction (2026-07-10):** The agent assumed pyflakes would NOT flag unused exception bindings (`except Exception as e:` where `e` is never referenced in the body). This assumption was WRONG — the project's flake8/pyflakes version DOES report F841 "local variable 'e' is assigned to but never used" for unused exception bindings.

**Trigger:** When refactoring an except block from `logger.exception(e)` (which references `e` as the msg arg — an anti-pattern but satisfies F841) to `logger.exception("msg %s %d", arg1, arg2)` (the correct %-style pattern), the `e` binding becomes unused and F841 fires.

**Fix:** Drop the `as e` binding entirely when the exception variable is not needed:
```python
except Exception:
    logger.exception("resolveUserId: failed to look up user %r in chat %d", clean, chatId)
```
`logger.exception()` captures the active exception context automatically via `sys.exc_info()`, so no explicit binding is needed for the traceback.

**Lesson:** Always run `make lint` after changing except blocks — never assume F841 won't fire. If you're switching from `logger.exception(e)` to `logger.exception(msg, *args)`, remove `as e` in the same edit.

title: _resolveUserId on BaseBotHandler — corrected: numeric path uses isdecimal()
content:
`_resolveUserId` lives on `BaseBotHandler` (`internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py:460`) and is inherited by all handlers. Signature:
```python
async def _resolveUserId(self, *, chatId: int, userIdentifier: Optional[str]) -> Optional[int]
```

**Resolution order:**
1. Falsy/None → return None.
2. `clean = userIdentifier.lstrip("@").strip()` → if empty return None.
3. **Numeric path:** if `clean.isdecimal()` → return `int(clean)` directly (NO DB lookup). IMPORTANT: it's `isdecimal()`, NOT `isdigit()` — `isdigit()` admits Unicode superscripts like `²` that `int()` can't parse.
4. **Login path:** re-prepend `@` (`clean = f"@{clean}"`), then `self.db.chatUsers.getChatUserByUsername(chatId=chatId, username=clean)`. Returns `user_id` as int, or None on not-found/exception.

**Call sites (as of 2026-07-14):**
- `ChatSearchHandler._llmToolSearchMessages` (chat_search.py): `userIdentifier=user_name` — keeps silent all-users fallback.
- `ChatSearchHandler.searchCommand` (chat_search.py): `userIdentifier=parsed["user"]`.
- `UserMemoriesHandler._llmToolSearchMemories` (user_memories.py:697): `userIdentifier=user` — ERRORS on unresolvable. Note: the handler was renamed from UserDataHandler to UserMemoriesHandler and the file from user_data.py to user_memories.py.

title: Cross-user memory search is chat-scoped by compound key — numeric user_id can't leak cross-chat memories
content:
Security property: the `search_memories` cross-user feature allows the LLM to search ANY user's memories by passing a numeric `user` ID. The numeric path in `_resolveUserId` (internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py:506-507) returns `int(clean)` directly without a DB lookup — so it accepts ANY positive integer as a user_id.

**This does NOT create a cross-chat leak** because `searchMemories` is always called with BOTH `chatId` and `userId`:
```python
results = await self.db.userMemories.searchMemories(chatId, userId, ...)
```
Memories are stored per `(chatId, userId)` compound key (verified at internal/database/repositories/user_memories.py:616 — the method signature requires both `chatId: int` and `userId: int`). A numeric user_id that doesn't exist in the current chat simply returns zero results — it cannot access memories from a different chat.

**Contrast with login path:** the login path (`getChatUserByUsername`) IS scoped to the chat — it only finds users in `chat_users` for that specific `chatId`. So login resolution is chat-scoped by definition, while numeric resolution is globally accepted but chat-scoped at the query level.

The `_llmToolSearchMemories` handler lives in `internal/bot/common/handlers/user_memories.py:647` (note: formerly user_data.py, renamed in the UserMemoriesHandler refactor).

title: Module rename gotcha: mock.patch target strings break at runtime, not at import/lint time
content:
When a Python module is renamed (e.g. `user_data.py` → `user_memories.py`), string-based `mock.patch` targets that reference the old dotted module path will break at RUNTIME — not at import time, not at lint/typecheck time. This happened in the `UserDataHandler` → `UserMemoriesHandler` rename (July 2026).

Specific failure: `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_user_memories_memory_regen.py:664` had:
```python
mock.patch("internal.bot.common.handlers.user_data.asyncio.sleep", ...)
```
After the production module was renamed to `user_memories`, this patch target caused:
```
AttributeError: module 'internal.bot.common.handlers' has no attribute 'user_data'
```
raised from `pkgutil.py` (getattr-based module walking inside the patch resolver).

These string targets are invisible to ALL static checks:
- NOT caught by `import main` circular-import check (they're strings, not imports)
- NOT caught by `grep UserDataHandler` (the patch target references the module path, not the class name)
- NOT caught by `make format lint` / `pyright` / `flake8`

**Checklist for any future module rename in this project:**
1. `grep -rn "old_module_name" tests/ --include="*.py"` — catch string-based `mock.patch` targets, `importlib.import_module()` calls, `getattr(module, ...)` patterns
2. Also check for hardcoded production file path strings in test assertions (see separate memory about `test_memory_resolution_coverage.py`)
3. Clear stale `__pycache__/*.pyc` files from pre-rename filenames — they survive `git mv` and will create false-positive `grep` matches (use `--include="*.py"` to filter them out)

title: When renaming a module, bare filename references also need updating (not just full paths)
content:
During bulk doc renames (e.g., a class/file rename), THREE forms of reference must be updated — the third is easy to miss:

1. **Full path references** — `path/to/old_name.py` → `path/to/new_name.py` (including relative markdown link targets like `../../internal/...`).
2. **Class name references** — `OldClass` → `NewClass`.
3. **Bare filename references** — these slip past path-grep:
   - Markdown link LABELS: `` [`old_name.py`](...) `` → `` [`new_name.py`](...) ``
   - Directory tree entries: `` ├── old_name.py  # handler comment ``
   - Brace expansion paths: `` `path/{a,b,old_name}.py` ``
   - Inline code references: `` (`old_name.py` `_method`) ``

A safe replacement strategy: target the `path/old_name.py` substring and the class name. Then manually fix bare filenames by checking context. (A FOURTH category — human-readable description prose that uses the old concept name without the code identifier — is covered by memory 1c5706b9.)

**HISTORICAL / OBSOLETE scope guard (do NOT act on):** The original memory listed items that must NOT be renamed during the 2026-07-10 `UserDataHandler → UserMemoriesHandler` rename: the `user_data` SQL TABLE, `class UserDataRepository` in `internal/database/repositories/user_data.py`, and cache methods `setChatUserData`/`getChatUserData`. **All three have since been DELETED** by the v1 user_data retirement — `migration_022_drop_user_data.py` dropped the table, the repository file no longer exists, and the cache bridge methods have zero repo-wide matches. title: Gotcha: grep self-sabotage — don't reintroduce the pattern in your fix note
content:
When the acceptance criteria for a cleanup task is grep-based (e.g., "grep -rn UserDataRepository docs/ returns zero in live docs"), the explanatory note you add during the fix can ACCIDENTALLY REINTRODUCE the exact pattern being removed.

**Observed (2026-07-10):** When removing `UserDataRepository` from `docs/suggestions/refactoring.md`, the agent wrote a parenthetical note: "(the legacy `UserDataRepository` was later removed...)" — which itself contains the grep target string `UserDataRepository` and would have failed the acceptance criteria.

**Fix:** Rephrased to "(the legacy user-data repository was later removed...)" — lowercase, no camelCase — avoiding the exact pattern.

**Lesson:** When adding explanatory notes during a grep-driven cleanup, use natural-language rephrasing (lowercase, different casing, descriptive name) rather than the exact identifier being removed. Run the grep check AFTER all edits, including the notes you added.

title: Dropping a table requires updating expected-tables lists in schema tests
content:

title: Drop-table migration convention: down() must recreate the FINAL accumulated table shape, not migration_001's original
content:
Convention established by `migration_022_drop_user_data.py` — the FIRST migration in this codebase whose `up()` drops an existing table. This sets the pattern for future table-retirement migrations.

**The pattern:**
- `up()`: `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS <table>` via `provider.batchExecute([ParametrizedQuery("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS ...")])` — matches the shape used in migration_020's down() and migration_001's down().
- `down()`: `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS <table>` with the table's FINAL accumulated schema shape — i.e., the state the table was in JUST BEFORE this migration ran, after all prior migrations have been applied.

**THE TRAP (non-obvious):** The `down()` DDL must reflect the POST-all-prior-migrations shape, NOT the original shape from migration_001. If you naively copy the CREATE TABLE from migration_001, you'll reintroduce `DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` on timestamp columns that migration_013 explicitly removed. You MUST cross-check the `down()` DDL against BOTH the original migration (e.g. migration_001) AND any intervening schema-modifying migrations (e.g. migration_013 which recreated all tables to strip timestamp defaults).

**Concrete verification:** migration_022's down() recreates `user_data` with `created_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL` / `updated_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL` (no DEFAULT) — matching migration_013's `user_data_new` shape, NOT migration_001's which had `DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`.

**Other rules that apply (from AGENTS.md SQL portability):**
- No `AUTOINCREMENT`, no `DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`
- Portable types only: TEXT, INTEGER, REAL, TIMESTAMP, BOOLEAN
- Composite natural PK (e.g. `PRIMARY KEY (user_id, chat_id, key)`)
- No indexes to recreate unless prior migrations created them on the table (user_data never had any)

Structural reversibility only — data is unrecoverable after drop. This is acceptable for retiring dead tables.

Populated in newMessageHandler when per-chat settings are on: chat_search.py:964 adds on EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED; user_memories.py:1574 adds on MEMORY_ENABLED && EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED. Both crons iterate sorted(self._trackedChats) with round-robin index.

ChatSettingsRepository.listChatsBySetting was DELETED (~67 lines removed from internal/database/repositories/chat_settings.py). The only surviving mentions are in test docstrings describing the old code.

Self-eviction: uses self._trackedChats.discard(chatId) (chat_search.py:383, user_memories.py:847) — NOT .remove(). The .discard() fix was applied per code review (avoids KeyError on overlapping cron ticks). The branch (user-memory-v2) is merge-ready per the pre-merge review.

title: Bugfix: set.remove() → set.discard() on _trackedChats (KeyError risk)
content:
During the regen-discovery rewrite review-fixes session (2026-07-10, branch `user-memory-v2`), a KeyError bug was found and fixed in BOTH crons that evict chats from the in-memory `_trackedChats: MutableSet[int]`:

**Sites (2):**
1. `ChatSearchHandler._dtCronJob` (`internal/bot/common/handlers/chat_search.py`) — after the per-chat gate fails (`REGENERATE_EMBEDDINGS` or `EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED` now false)
2. `UserMemoriesHandler._runMemoryEmbeddingRegen` (`internal/bot/common/handlers/user_memories.py`) — after the per-chat gate fails

**Root cause:** The eviction used `self._trackedChats.remove(chatId)`, which raises `KeyError` if the element is not present. A chat could be evicted from `_trackedChats` between ticks (e.g. another code path, or a race) before the cron's per-chat gate re-checks and tries to evict it again. `set.discard()` is the correct method — it's a no-op if the element is absent.

**Fix:** Changed `.remove(chatId)` → `.discard(chatId)` at both sites. This was the ONLY behavioral change in the 13-edit doc-fix changeset; the other 11 edits were purely docstrings/comments.

Note: Memory `492649e3` (the architecture description of this rewrite) documents the eviction as `.remove()` — that is now stale; it's `.discard()`.

title: _d_tCronJob rewrite: in-memory _trackedChats replaces listChatsBySetting DB-scan
content:
`ChatSearchHandler._dtCronJob` discovers which chats to process via an in-memory set `self._trackedChats: MutableSet[int]` (initialized `set()` in `__init__`, chat_search.py:228). The old DB scan via `ChatSettingsRepository.listChatsBySetting` was DELETED (method no longer exists anywhere in internal/).

Current flow (updated 2026-08-21, post-2026-07-11 consolidation):
1. Gate 1: `if not self._trackedChats: return` (:427).
2. Round-robin pick: `chatList = sorted(self._trackedChats); chatId = chatList[self._backfillIndex % len(chatList)]` (:434).
3. Gate 2: per-chat settings check on `EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED` ONLY (:445) — the `REGENERATE_EMBEDDINGS` part of the original rewrite was REMOVED by the consolidation (backfill is always-on for embeddings-enabled chats). On fail: `self._trackedChats.discard(chatId)` (:446) and return.
4. Gate 3: resolve embedding model — bail if missing or no vec0 support.
5. Cleanup: `deleteObsoleteModelEmbeddings`.
6. `getMessagesWithoutEmbeddings` batch fetch → `embedAndSaveMessage` loop.

Population: `newMessageHandler` adds chat IDs on arrival, gated on `EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED` (:1065-66) — symmetric with cron eviction (see memory c2a88dea for the cross-handler symmetry invariant).

title: Doc-sync convention: deleted identifiers must have ZERO literal matches in live docs
content:
When a method/identifier is deleted from the codebase and docs are synced, the acceptance criterion is ZERO literal string matches of the identifier in live (non-archive/plans/superseded) docs — not merely removing references that imply the identifier still exists.

Discovered 2026-07-10 during the `listChatsBySetting` deletion doc-sync: the documenting agent initially wrote removal-context mentions like "the previous `listChatsBySetting(MEMORY_EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED)` discovery ... was removed" in 8 places across 6 doc files. These are legitimate documentation (they explain the migration), but the strict `rg -n "listChatsBySetting" docs/` acceptance criterion required zero matches. All 8 had to be reworded to describe the deletion without using the literal token (e.g., "the deleted `ChatSettingsRepository` DB-scan discovery method" or "the old DB-scan discovery (now removed)").

Practical guidance: when documenting a deletion, describe the mechanism without naming the deleted identifier. Use phrases like "the old DB-scan discovery method (now removed)" rather than backtick-quoting the exact deleted name.

Note: frozen docs (`docs/archive/`, `docs/plans/`, superseded banner files) are exempt — they retain historical references unchanged per the established archive policy.

title: Gate 2 review: regen-discovery rewrite integration-clean (no behavioral bugs)
content:

- **`.discard()` eviction is idempotent** — no KeyError path even on double-eviction.
- **Refinement cannot run with embeddings off** — `_runMemoryRefinement` gate re-checks both `MEMORY_REFINEMENT_ENABLED` AND `MEMORY_EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED` per candidate and drops survivors from `_accounting` + `_lastRefinedTS`. `_runSingleRefinement` is only reachable after the gate.
- **Both `newMessageHandler` overrides return `HandlerResultStatus.NEXT`** — don't break the handler chain. `ChatSearchHandler` is registered `PARALLEL`, `LLMMessageHandler` still last/`SEQUENTIAL`.
- **6 new regression tests are meaningful** — they exercise real add/skip/evict paths via `newMessageHandler`, not seed-and-assert-mocks.
- **`ChatSettingsValue` import removal is safe** — no remaining runtime use in either handler (only a docstring reference in user_memories.py:799).
- **`getMessagesWithoutEmbeddings` `dimensions` kwarg** is keyword-only with `None` default — all existing positional callers unaffected.
- **`getChatSettings` always returns all keys** (merged with defaults) — so `chatSettings[key]` subscript won't KeyError even on empty cache.

The `_runRefinement` → `_runSingleRefinement` rename (done IN this changeset) was NOT propagated to docs. `rg "_runRefinement\b"` returns ~20 live-doc references + 1 production docstring. title: Schema docs convention: inline numeric defaults, not constant names
content:
When documenting method signatures in schema docs (`docs/database-schema.md`, `docs/database-schema-llm.md`, `docs/llm/database.md`), use inline numeric values for defaults (e.g., `limit=50`) rather than the Python constant name (e.g., `limit=BACKFILL_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE`).

This matches the convention of every adjacent method signature in those files — they all use raw numbers like `limit=10`, `limit=5`, `limit=20`, `limit=100`. Using the constant name would break visual consistency and make the doc less scannable.

If a default is a named constant, look up its value and inline it. Example: `BACKFILL_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE = 50` → write `limit=50` in the doc signature.

- `getMessagesWithoutEmbeddings(self, chatId, *, limit=100, modelName=None, dimensions=None, dataSource=None) -> List[ChatMessageDict]` — in `chat_embeddings.py:466`
