Add an integration regression test where the model explains or documents the exact syntax and assert the handler is not called.

title: Inline healing needs disabled-tool allowlist coverage
content: The inline healing matcher validates the tool name against the global `toolsHandlers` registry, while actual execution later applies the `filteredToolNames`/`useTools` allowlist. Existing integration coverage enabled all tools, and the disabled-tool test covered only native `TOOL_CALLS`; therefore the new inline route lacked a regression test proving that a registered-but-disabled inline tool is not executed and that the model receives the expected “not available” tool result. Add an end-to-end inline-form test with the tool excluded by `useTools`, asserting the handler is never awaited and the next model turn receives the rejection result.

title: Tool healing must reject trailing JSON remainder
content: Code review of `internal/services/llm/service.py` found that the fenced/inline healing path uses `_tryParseJson()`/`raw_decode()`, which parses only the first JSON value and returns `endPos`. If `_tryApplyToolCallMatch()` does not require `toolArgsStr[endPos:].strip()` to be empty, inputs such as `{"a": 1}\n{"b": 2}` or valid JSON followed by prose can be converted into an executable tool call using only the first object. The matcher should require full argument-string consumption and regression-test multiple objects, trailing prose, and no-mutation on rejection.

title: Healing matcher needs explicit malformed-input coverage
content: For the inline-code tool-name plus fenced-JSON healing route in `tests/services/llm/test_tool_call_healing.py`, successful coverage should include both unlabeled and `json`-labeled Markdown fences; negative coverage should include unknown tools, malformed JSON, and trailing content/multiple JSON objects. These cases exercise the regex language-tag branch and the raw-decoder boundary, rather than only proving the happy path with an unlabeled fence.

title: Durable healing docs must list new matcher
content: When adding a new LLM tool-call healing matcher, update both `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md` and `docs/llm/memories/llm-tool-call-healing.md`; stale text claiming the orchestrator has five matchers and omitting `_matchTextForInlineCodeToolNameAndJson` makes the documented recovery cascade inaccurate. Keep durable implementation notes synchronized with the actual matcher count and names.

title: Yandex SpeechKit STT API — integration reference
content:
Comprehensive technical reference for integrating Yandex SpeechKit STT (via AI Studio / Yandex Cloud). Gathered 2026-07 from official docs at aistudio.yandex.ru/docs/en/speechkit (mirrors cloud.yandex.ru/en/docs/speechkit).

## API modalities
- v1 SYNC (REST): POST https://stt.api.cloud.yandex.net/speech/v1/stt:recognize — <=30s, <=1MB, mono.
- v2 ASYNC (REST): POST https://transcribe.api.cloud.yandex.net/speech/stt/v2/longRunningRecognize — Object Storage URI only; result embedded inline when done. Returns per-word confidence scores.
- v3 ASYNC (REST + gRPC) [PREFERRED for transcription]:
  - submit: POST https://stt.api.cloud.yandex.net/stt/v3/recognizeFileAsync
  - poll:   GET  https://operation.api.cloud.yandex.net/operations/{id}
  - result: GET  https://stt.api.cloud.yandex.net/stt/v3/getRecognition?operation_id={id}  (concatenated JSON stream of events)
  - delete: DELETE .../stt/v3/deleteRecognition?operation_id={id}
  - gRPC host: stt.api.cloud.yandex.net:443, AsyncRecognizerStub.RecognizeFile / .GetRecognition
  - Protobuf: github.com/yandex-cloud/cloudapi/tree/master/yandex/cloud/ai/stt/v3
- v2/v3 STREAMING (gRPC): RecognizerStub.RecognizeStreaming — <=5min session, <=10MB, mono.

NO VIDEO SUPPORT anywhere — only audio. Must demux first (ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -ac 1 -ar 16000 -c:a pcm_s16le out.wav).

## Formats (only 3)
- LPCM raw (LINEAR16_PCM, 16-bit signed LE): 8/16/48 kHz for STT.
- OggOpus (OGG+OPUS): no restrictions.
- MP3: no restrictions EXCEPT not supported in v1 sync or v2 streaming.
- Containers in v3: WAV, OGG_OPUS, MP3 via container_audio.container_audio_type.
- Channels: sync/streaming=1; async<=2.

## Timestamps (CRITICAL — both word + utterance level available)
v3 getRecognition returns concatenated JSON objects, each a result.{final|finalRefinement|eouUpdate|...}:
- final.alternatives[].words[]{text, startTimeMs, endTimeMs} — WORD-level, ms from start (as strings).
- final.alternatives[]{text, startTimeMs, endTimeMs} — PHRASE-level.
- eouUpdate.timeMs — end-of-utterance boundary = "replica" delimiter.
- finalRefinement.normalizedText — same timestamps, normalised (punctuation/caps/numbers).
- v3 confidence field is always 0 (placeholder). v2 returns real confidence 0-1.
v2 longRunningRecognize returns response.chunks[].alternatives[].words[]{startTime:"0.160s",endTime,word,confidence} (Go duration strings).

## Speaker labeling (v3 only)
- speakerLabeling.speakerLabeling=SPEAKER_LABELING_ENABLED.
- Constraints: FULL_DATA mode, MONO, MAX 2 SPEAKERS. channel_tag 0/1 per phrase.
- For >2 speakers need external diarisation.

## Auth
- IAM token: Authorization: Bearer <token> — expires ~12h, refresh needed.
- API key: Authorization: Api-Key <key> — SERVICE ACCOUNT only, long-lived. PREFERRED for daemons.
- Folder ID: required for user accounts (v1/v2 in body folderId=; v3 in x-folder-id header). NOT required for service accounts (inferred).
- ASYNC REQUIRES service account — user/federated accounts cannot do async.
- Roles on SA: ai.speechkit-stt.user + storage.uploader (+ KMS roles if bucket encrypted).

## Languages
- ru-RU default + best. 16 total: en-US, de-DE, es-ES, fr-FR, it-IT, pt-PT, pt-BR, kk-KZ, uz-UZ, nl-NL, pl-PL, sv-SE, fi-FI, tr-TR, he-IL.
- auto-detection (v3 only): language_restriction with restriction_type=WHITELIST, language_code=['auto'] or list. Returns per-phrase language_code + probability.
- Model tags: general (stable), general:rc, general:deprecated (2-week overlap after general bump — pin in prod). Async also: deferred-general (cheaper, low-priority queue).

## Limits
- Sync: 30s / 1MB / 1ch.
- Streaming: 5min / 10MB / 1ch.
- Async: 4h / 1GB (Object Storage URI) or 60MB (inline base64 in v3) / 2ch.
- Results retained 3 days then deleted.
- Quotas: streaming 40 rps; sync 20 rps; async 500 req/hour; status poll v2=2500/hour, v3=5/sec; 10000 billable hours/day.

## Pricing (USD ex-VAT)
- Sync/streaming: $0.0013327867 per 15s mono.
- Async standard: $0.0012418035 per 15s of 2-CHANNEL audio (channels rounded UP to even; min 15s per 2ch; per-second after 16s).
- Async deferred: $0.0003122955 per 15s 2ch.
- Empty request = 1 unit (billed). 5xx internal errors NOT billed.
- ~Cost: 1h mono ru-RU async standard ≈ $0.596/hour of audio; deferred ≈ $0.15/hour.

## Python SDK
- PREFERRED: yandex-cloud-ml-sdk (official, multimodal). pip install yandex-cloud-ml-sdk. Python>=3.9. Latest 0.19.x (Jan 2026). Repo github.com/yandex-cloud/yandex-cloud-ml-sdk. Init: YCloudML(folder_id=..., auth=...); auto-reads YC_API_KEY env var.
- LEGACY: yandex-speechkit-lib-python (TikhonP) — community, v2 only, avoid.
- SDK STT method names evolve between minors — verify against pinned version's examples/ + py.typed stubs. readthedocs index currently 404s. Underlying wire contract is v3 gRPC regardless.
- Raw gRPC fallback: clone cloudapi repo, grpcio-tools protoc to generate stt_pb2/stt_service_pb2 stubs.

## Gotchas
- Inline base64 in v3 capped at 60MB — larger files MUST go via Object Storage URI.
- Single global endpoint, no regions.
- Results expire 3 days — persist immediately.
- IAM token ~12h expiry — use API key for long-running services.
- v3 status poll quota is 5/sec (friendlier than v2's 2500/hour).
- Recognition is ~10x realtime (1 min audio -> ~10s).
- general tag silently moves on updates — pin to general:rc or general:deprecated for reproducibility; watch release-notes-stt.
- v3 confidence always 0 — use v2 if confidence scoring needed.
- Speaker labeling: mono, <=2 speakers, FULL_DATA.
- Errors via google.rpc.Status in operation.error when done:true. Retry 5xx (not billed). 4xx may be billed.
- MP3 unsupported in v1 sync and v2 streaming.

## Source URLs (all under aistudio.yandex.ru/docs/en/speechkit, mirror cloud.yandex.ru/en/docs/speechkit)
- /en/speechkit/stt/ (modality matrix)
- /en/speechkit/formats (audio formats)
- /en/speechkit/stt/models (languages, model tags)
- /en/speechkit/stt/transcribation (async concepts, modes)
- /en/speechkit/stt/speaker-labeling
- /en/speechkit/concepts/auth (auth + folder id rules)
- /en/speechkit/concepts/limits (quotas + technical limits)
- /en/speechkit/pricing (billing rules + prices)
- /en/speechkit/stt-v3/api-ref/ (v3 REST service URL)
- /en/speechkit/stt-v3/api-ref/AsyncRecognizer/recognizeFile (full request schema: content vs uri, RecognitionModelOptions, SpeakerLabelingOptions, SummarizationOptions)
- /en/speechkit/quickstart/stt-quickstart-v2 (curl flow + response examples for both v2 and v3)
- /en/speechkit/stt/api/transcribation-api-v3 (gRPC Python example)
- /en/speechkit/stt/api/streaming-examples-v3 (v3 streaming gRPC example)
- /en/speechkit/stt/api/request-examples (v1 sync example)
- github.com/yandex-cloud/cloudapi (protobuf interface definitions)
- pypi.org/project/yandex-cloud-ml-sdk

title: SpeechKit SDK correction: project uses yandex-ai-studio-sdk, NOT yandex-cloud-ml-sdk
content:
Cross-references and corrects the SDK recommendation (§9) in research memory `17b7097b` (Yandex SpeechKit STT API — integration reference). The research was accurate at the REST/gRPC API level (endpoints, formats, timestamps, auth, limits, pricing — all package-independent and stand). ONLY the SDK-recommendation section is corrected here.

## The discrepancy
The research recommends `yandex-cloud-ml-sdk` (import `yandex_cloud_ml_sdk`, class `YCloudML(folder_id=..., auth=...)`, PyPI "official, current"). This is a REAL but DIFFERENT and OLDER package. **This project does NOT use it and must not add it.**

This project pins and actively uses **`yandex-ai-studio-sdk==0.22.0`** (import `yandex_ai_studio_sdk`, class `AsyncAIStudio(folder_id=..., auth=APIKeyAuth(...))`):
- `requirements.direct.txt:18` → `yandex-ai-studio-sdk==0.22.0`
- `requirements.txt:94` → same pin
- Actively imported in `lib/ai/providers/yc_sdk_provider.py` (lines 53-68) for completions, image generation, function-calling/tools. Uses `AsyncAIStudio`, `AsyncGPTModel`, `AsyncImageGenerationModel`, `AsyncFunctionCall`, `APIKeyAuth`/`IAMTokenAuth`/`YandexCloudCLIAuth` from `yandex_ai_studio_sdk.auth`.

These two packages are NOT the same SDK renamed — they are separate distributions with incompatible APIs (`YCloudML` vs `AsyncAIStudio`). Introducing `yandex-cloud-ml-sdk` would duplicate the Yandex SDK dependency.

## The installed SDK already has full SpeechKit STT support
The `yandex-ai-studio-sdk` ships a `_speechkit/` module exposing both TTS and STT. The STT API surface (audited 2026-07-18 against the installed wheel at `venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/yandex_ai_studio_sdk/_speechkit/`, fully documented in `docs/other/yc-ai-sdk/speech.md`):

```python
from yandex_ai_studio_sdk import AsyncAIStudio
from yandex_ai_studio_sdk.auth import APIKeyAuth
from yandex_ai_studio_sdk._speechkit.enums import AudioFormat

sdk = AsyncAIStudio(folder_id="b1g...", auth=APIKeyAuth("..."))
stt = sdk.speechkit.stt(                      # or .speech_to_text(...)
    audio_format=AudioFormat.WAV,             # WAV | MP3 | OGG_OPUS | PCM16(sample_rate_hertz=16000, channels=1)
    language_codes="auto",                    # NOTE underscore codes: ru_RU, en_US, not ru-RU
    speaker_labeling=True,                    # bool, not an enum
)
result = await stt.run(audio_bytes, timeout=60)        # real-time, returns SpeechToTextResult (Sequence over ChannelResult)
async for event in stt.run_stream(audio_bytes): ...    # async GENERATOR (never await — see memories c4ddc735, ba9253ac)
operation = await stt.run_deferred(audio_bytes_or_s3url)  # long audio; await operation for DeferredSpeechToTextResult
await stt.attach_deferred(operation_id="...")
stream = stt.create_bistream(timeout=600)              # bidirectional streaming
# factory-level (NOT model-level): sdk.speechkit.stt.get_recognition_result(operation_id="...")
```

Key SDK facts for the architecture proposal:
- **Execution methods on the model**: `run`, `run_stream`, `run_deferred`, `attach_deferred`, `create_bistream`. `get_recognition_result` is on the speechkit FACTORY (`sdk.speechkit.stt`), NOT the model instance — calling it on a model raises AttributeError.
- **`SpeechToTextConfig` fields** (audio_format REQUIRED): model, language_codes, text_normalization, eou_classifier, recognition_classifiers, speech_analysis, speaker_labeling (bool), llm_post_process.
- **`SpeechToTextResult`** is a `Sequence` over `ChannelResult`; each `ChannelResult.utterances` is a tuple of `Utterance`. For single-channel audio, `result.text` returns joined text. Iterate `for channel in result: for utt in channel.utterances:`.
- **`Utterance`**: `.final_text`, `.final_refinement_text` (None if no refinement events), `.text` (refinement or final). Also `.events`, `.finals`, `.final_refinements`, `.timespan`, `.speaker_analysis`, `.classifiers`.
- **`SpeechToTextStreamingEvent`**: `event_type` (str-enum: partial/final/final_refinement/eou_update/...), fields `partial`/`final` are `Alternatives | None` (NOT bool). Convenience props: `.partial_text`, `.final_text`, `.final_refinement_text`, `.text`.
- **`run_stream` is an async generator in ALL domains** — never `await` it (TypeError). General rule per memory `ba9253ac`.
- **Language codes use UNDERSCORES** in the SDK (`ru_RU`, `en_US`, `auto`) — the REST API uses hyphens (`ru-RU`). Easy to get wrong.

## Current wiring status
SpeechKit (TTS + STT) is **entirely UNWIRED in production** — grep for `speechkit|text_to_speech|speech_to_text|\btts\b|\bstt\b` across `lib/ai/providers/yc_sdk_provider.py` returns ZERO matches. `docs/other/yc-ai-sdk/gap-analysis.md` lists both TTS and STT as "Not used / Low priority". So the SDK package is installed but the SpeechKit domain is not yet exercised by any production code path — the architecture proposal would be the first integration.

## Net guidance for the proposal
1. Use the EXISTING `yandex-ai-studio-sdk==0.22.0` and its `sdk.speechkit.stt(...)` API. Do NOT add `yandex-cloud-ml-sdk`.
2. The REST/gRPC-level reference in memory `17b7097b` (endpoints, formats, timestamps, auth, limits, pricing) remains valid and authoritative — that's the wire contract the SDK implements under the hood.
3. For long-audio transcription specifically, `stt.run_deferred(s3_url_or_bytes)` is the SDK entry point (wraps v3 async `recognizeFileAsync`). For per-word timestamps and replica boundaries, the SDK surfaces them via `Utterance.timespan` / `SpeechToTextStreamingEvent.eou_update_ms` and the `final`/`final_refinement` `Alternatives` (which carry the word-level `startTimeMs`/`endTimeMs` from the underlying v3 API).
4. Auth reuses the project's existing `APIKeyAuth`/`IAMTokenAuth` pattern already in `yc_sdk_provider.py` — same credential model as completions.

title: STT feature — design decisions locked-in
content:
Video/voice/audio transcription feature for Gromozeka. Locked-in design decisions from planning session (m0001-m0007):

SCOPE: Video + voice + audio (VIDEO, VIDEO_NOTE, VOICE, AUDIO). Unified pipeline, one chat setting, one provider.

TRIGGER: Chat-setting auto, mirroring PARSE_ATTACHMENTS image-parsing path. New TRANSCRIBE_MEDIA chat setting (BOOL, page=FRIEND, default=false). Runs in _processMediaV2 message preprocessor.

PROVIDER: Yandex SpeechKit v3 async (recognizeFileAsync). Word-level timestamps available (startTimeMs/endTimeMs per word), utterance/replica boundaries via eouUpdate.timeMs.

AUDIO EXTRACTION: PyAV (Python wheel bundling ffmpeg libs, no system install). CPU-bound decode via asyncio.to_thread. Optional-dep guard pattern (_AV_AVAILABLE flag).

DELIVERY: Transcript stored as media_attachments.description column (REUSED — zero schema migration). Auto-injects into LLM message via existing updateMediaContent → formatForLLM path as <media-description>…</media-description>. Format: [HH:MM:SS] utterance per line.

ABSTRACTION: Build lib/stt/ provider registry now (mirrors lib/ai/ shape). AbstractSTTProvider + STTManager + YandexSpeechKitProvider. Reversible — can swap providers later.

HTTP: Raw httpx for Yandex SpeechKit provider (NOT yandex-cloud-ml-sdk). Research flagged SDK STT method surface as underdocumented. Mirrors lib/yandex_search/ pattern (Api-Key header, ProxyConfig.fromServiceConfig, never-raise contract). SDK can be added as alternative provider later.

DEFERRED: Object Storage (>60MB files), speaker diarization, auto-language detection, word confidence scores. v1 is inline-only (≤60MB), ru-RU only, single-speaker.

KEY FILES TO MIRROR:
- lib/yandex_search/client.py (raw httpx + never-raise pattern)
- lib/ai/ + internal/services/llm/ (layering template)
- internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py:1316-1367 (_parseImage — template for _transcribeMedia)
- internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py:1726-1930 (_processMediaV2 — three edits needed: gate at 1834, existing-attachment branch at 1809, fallthrough at 1892)
- internal/bot/models/ensured_message.py:973-998 (updateMediaContent — reads description into mediaContent)
- internal/bot/models/ensured_message.py:1179-1185 (formatForLLM — wraps as <media-description>)

NEW CHAT SETTING (4 sites per add-chat-setting skill):
1. ChatSettingsKey.TRANSCRIBE_MEDIA = "transcribe-media" in internal/bot/models/chat_settings.py
2. _chatSettingsInfo entry: type=BOOL, page=ChatSettingsPage.FRIEND
3. configs/00-defaults/bot-defaults.toml: transcribe-media = false
4. Consumer: _processMediaV2

NEW CONFIG: [stt] section in configs/00-defaults/stt.toml + ConfigManager.getSTTConfig(). Keys: enabled, provider, use-proxy, api-key (${YC_API_KEY}), folder-id (${YC_FOLDER_ID}), language (ru-RU), request-timeout (300), ratelimiter-queue (stt), max-duration-sec (3600), max-file-size-mb (100), poll-interval-sec (3).

IMPLEMENTATION: 13 steps in plan. Each ends with `make format lint && make test`. Step 5 (Yandex provider) must verify exact v3 field names against live API first — research flagged this as ambiguous.

OPEN RISKS: MAX_MEDIA_AWAIT_SECS may be too short for long videos; PyAV wheel ~30MB; concurrent-storm protection (consider asyncio.Semaphore in STTService); word confidence always 0 in v3.

Full plan in conversation m0007. Awaiting user decision on: save as planning doc / adjust scope / start dispatching Step 1 + Step 5 research.

title: STT plan — canonical doc location
content:
The canonical STT feature plan now lives at `docs/design/media-transcription-stt-v1.md` (moved out of docs/plans/; docs/plans/ currently holds only python-sandboxing-v1.md, llm-empty-truncated-final-handling-v1.md, embedding-model-lookup-refactor-v1.md). Companion docs: docs/design/lib-stt-v1.md (library design), docs/design/stt-v1.1.md (object-storage routing + stats gates).

Implementation is COMPLETE: lib/stt (models/exceptions/audio/abstract/providers incl. yandex_object_storage.py) and internal/services/stt/ (STTService + formatter). Status 'awaiting user go-ahead' is long obsolete.

title: PyAV in-memory STT conversion requires dual flushing
content: For the planned media-to-SpeechKit pipeline, current PyAV supports `av.open(io.BytesIO(...))` for in-memory demuxing and bundled wheels generally avoid a system FFmpeg runtime dependency on supported platforms; source builds still need FFmpeg development libraries. A viable conversion is `AudioResampler(format="s16", layout="mono", rate=16000)`, an output stream `add_stream("pcm_s16le", rate=16000)`, set output layout to `mono`, encode/mux, close the output container, then read `BytesIO.getvalue()`. `AudioResampler.resample()` returns a list of frames. Critical gotcha: flush both stages—call `resampler.resample(None)` after input decoding, then drain encoder packets with `outputStream.encode(None)`—or delayed samples may be truncated. Prefer named layouts (`mono`/`stereo`) rather than numeric channel counts. Wheel behavior is platform/release dependent, so do not claim absolute host determinism.

title: SpeechKit v3 result retrieval is separate streaming response
content: SpeechKit v3 async result retrieval (verified against code and committed goldens): poll `GET https://operation.api.cloud.yandex.net/operations/{id}` reports operation state only; after done=true fetch `GET https://stt.api.cloud.yandex.net/stt/v3/getRecognition?operation_id=...`. The body is a stream of consecutive JSON objects (NDJSON-like; each wrapped as `result.final` / `result.finalRefinement.normalizedText`) — NOT a single JSON document and NOT `operation.response` or a flat alternatives array. The provider buffers the whole body (`response.content`) and hands bytes to parseRecognitionEvents. Timestamp fields (`startTimeMs`/`endTimeMs`, `finalIndex`, `responseWallTimeMs`) arrive as protobuf-JSON STRINGS (e.g. "280") per the recorded goldens — the parser's _coerceInt accepts integers and decimal strings. Final and normalized text are merged by refinement replacement (never emitted as separate messages).

title: SpeechKit v3 uses protobuf JSON recognition_model schema
content: The v3 async REST submit contract is camelCase `POST https://stt.api.cloud.yandex.net/stt/v3/recognizeFileAsync`, not the v2-style `:recognize_file_async` path. The JSON body is based on `RecognizeFileRequest`: inline audio is `content` (protobuf bytes represented as base64) or `uri`, with recognition options under `recognition_model` such as `model`, `audio_format.container_audio.container_audio_type`, and `language_restriction` (`WHITELIST`/`BLACKLIST` plus language codes). Do not send v2-like top-level `folderId`, `audioFormat`, `recognizeSpec`, `languageCode`, or `autoLanguage`. Include `x-folder-id` consistently according to the v3 examples, alongside `Authorization: Api-Key ...` or `Bearer ...`.

title: STT duplicate delivery requires atomic claim
content: The existing _processMediaV2 flow checks for a media_attachments row and later inserts it; addMediaAttachment() can return False on duplicate but callers do not use that result. For a first-seen duplicate file_unique_id delivered concurrently, both handlers can schedule transcription and incur duplicate SpeechKit billing. A PENDING shortcut only helps after one insert commits. STT integration must add an atomic insert-or-return-existing/status-claim operation, or a keyed lock plus a database claim, and regression-test concurrent first delivery and duplicate-while-PENDING behavior.

title: Media attachment updates do not verify row existence
content: The current media attachment repository's updateMediaAttachment() executes the UPDATE but does not check the affected-row count, so it can report success even when fileUniqueId matches no row. Any STT/media state machine that relies on update success must either make the repository return failure for zero matches or explicitly verify the row/claim before treating a transition as persisted; otherwise missing or concurrently changed records can be silently misclassified.

title: Max attachment downloads are currently unbounded
content: lib/max_bot/client.py's downloadAttachmentPayload() performs an HTTP GET and returns the full response.content without a byte cap or streaming enforcement. Adding media/STT limits only after this call cannot protect memory or bandwidth; the platform adapter (and corresponding Telegram download path) must enforce the maximum before or while buffering the payload, with regression tests for oversized responses.

title: Max STT dispatch omits voice and video notes
content: STT-eligible media routing is platform-asymmetric in internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py. Telegram dispatches VIDEO, VIDEO_NOTE, AUDIO, and VOICE through processTelegramMedia -> _processMediaV2. processMaxMedia handles only IMAGE, STICKER, VIDEO, AUDIO, and FILE attachments (Max VIDEO at ~lines 1762-1776, AUDIO at ~1777-1791) — there is no VOICE or VIDEO_NOTE dispatch for Max, so Max STT-eligible input is limited to VIDEO and AUDIO. The shared _processMediaV2 needProcessSTT gate (base.py:1933-1944) covers VIDEO/VIDEO_NOTE/VOICE/AUDIO, but Max never feeds the latter two through it. This asymmetry survived the shipped v1.1 STT implementation as the intentional scope; extending Max routing for VOICE/VIDEO_NOTE would require explicit work in processMaxMedia.

title: TEXT media injection misses Max multi-attachments
content: `EnsuredMessage` has asymmetric media-description injection: JSON formatting falls back to `mediaList`, but TEXT formatting emits the `<media-description>` block only when `self.mediaContent` is set (`internal/bot/models/ensured_message.py:1110-1114, 1158-1185`). Max preprocessing deliberately calls `addMediaProcessingInfo(..., setMediaId=False)` for each attachment (`internal/bot/common/handlers/message_preprocessor.py:168-170`), so multi-attachment Max messages can have descriptions in the list while `mediaContent` remains unset and TEXT output omits them. Any STT result injection must populate the field/path consumed by both output formats or add a regression test for Max multi-media TEXT rendering.

title: Media await path is not uniformly bounded
content: `MediaProcessingInfo.awaitResult()` directly awaits its task (`internal/bot/models/media.py:39-51`). The database polling/timeout logic is in `EnsuredMessage.updateMediaContent()` (`internal/bot/models/ensured_message.py:984-998, 1025-1061`) and occurs after the task await. Therefore an STT worker must not be attached to the existing `MediaProcessingInfo.task` if the plan relies on the DB timeout to bound work; use a separately managed background task or enforce cancellation/timeout before the direct await contract is reached.

title: STT lifecycle must register workers with QueueService
content: Load-bearing shutdown contract, still current: QueueService drains ONLY tasks registered through addBackgroundTask() (internal/services/queue_service/service.py:161-188 tracks them in the backgroundTasks set); its DO_EXIT handler (service.py:203-231) waits until that set is empty. The STT transcription task honors this: BaseBotHandler._processMediaV2 creates `sttTask = asyncio.create_task(self._transcribeMedia(mediaId, chatId, data))` and registers it via `queueService.addBackgroundTask(sttTask)` (internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py:2039-2043, mirroring the image parseTask pattern at :2033-2036). STTService.transcribeMedia's internal asyncio.Semaphore does NOT make a task drainable — QueueService registration is what keeps in-flight transcriptions alive through shutdown. Implemented lifecycle in main.py: startup creates the scheduler task BEFORE ProxyService.initialize (main.py:74-86, so the queue-drain DO_EXIT handler registers before proxy stop) and calls STTService.getInstance().initialize(...) AFTER RateLimiterManager.loadConfig and BEFORE the bot application (main.py:114-121). Shutdown order in _shutdown() (main.py:157-199): scheduler drain (Steps 2.1-2.2) → RateLimiterManager.destroy (2.3) → LLM manager close (2.4) → STTService.aclose (2.5) → database close (2.6). Note STT closes AFTER rate-limiter destruction — safe because transcription tasks finish draining at Step 2.1/2.2 while limiters still exist. Authoritative reference: ADR-020 in docs/llm/architecture.md and docs/llm/services.md §7.

title: STT tests need local singleton cleanup and new media-state coverage
content: Singleton cleanup rule (verified 2026-08-20): tests/conftest.py autouse fixtures reset only LLMService, ProxyService, and ProxyHelper. QueueService, StorageService, CacheService, RateLimiterManager, and STTService retain singleton state across tests — any test module touching them must provide its own reset fixture setting `Service._instance = None` before and after each test. Precedents: tests/services/queue_service/test_queue_service.py:25-37 (queueService fixture), tests/services/storage/test_integration.py:17-22 (autouse resetStorageServiceSingleton), tests/services/stt/test_transcribe.py (autouse resetSttServiceSingleton), and TestProcessMediaV2STT._resetSingletons in tests/bot/common/handlers/test_base.py (resets STT/Storage/Queue/Cache around every test in the class).

title: S3 backend is synchronous and has no transport timeouts
content: `S3StorageBackend` uses synchronous boto3 calls, including `put_object()` (`internal/services/storage/backends/s3.py:113-135`), despite being invoked from async media code. Its constructor/client setup (`internal/services/storage/backends/s3.py:57-91`) currently has no connect/read timeout or retry configuration, and `configs/00-defaults/storage.toml:8-28` has no such keys. Media/STT storage work must either move these calls off the event loop and add explicit transport settings, with tests updating both `tests/services/storage/test_s3_backend.py` (exact boto3 kwargs) and `tests/services/storage/test_service.py` (config-to-constructor forwarding).

title: Split STT formatter and provider event parser
content: The implementation plan's file tree omitted a formatter despite requiring deterministic bounded transcript formatting, and placing Yandex SpeechKit event parsing directly in the provider would make the high-risk wire parser hard to isolate. Keep a dedicated lib/stt/formatter.py and preferably lib/stt/providers/yandex_events.py so formatting and event-envelope parsing can be unit-tested independently and adjusted after live-wire validation without expanding the HTTP provider's responsibilities.

title: Separate STT code-complete from release-ready
content: The STT plan contradicted itself by calling §13.3 manual smoke tests release gates while §16 said implementation is complete only after those gates. Use two milestones: code-complete means automated tests/format/lint/full test pass with STT still default-off (P0–P16); release-ready means live SpeechKit wire/model, Max media, latency/RSS, graceful native-decoder shutdown, and Alpine/clean-install gates pass, with any corrections merged and docs/changelog synchronized. Manual runtime gates block release/enabling STT, not completion of the safely default-off code.

title: Dependency pin constants need field docs
content: Every `PINNED_VERSION` constant in `tests/dependencies/` carries a `#:` field-documentation comment immediately above it (the repo's field-doc rule applied to module-level typed constants in dependency contract tests). The comment explains the constant is the exact pinned distribution version the assertions were observed against and that a bump changing behaviour must be consciously re-verified before updating it. Verified at test_dateutil.py:32-35, test_tomli.py:22-25, test_python_magic.py:31-34, test_html_to_markdown.py:45-48, test_httpx2.py:11-13. CORRECTION of the original memory (2026-07-27): `tests/dependencies/test_pyav.py` does NOT exist in the repo and no PyAV version-pin test exists anywhere — `av==18.1.0` is a direct runtime dependency (requirements.direct.txt:5) whose behaviour tests live in `tests/lib/stt/test_audio.py` with no version assertion.

title: STT package needs export and import-boundary tests
content: Review found no dedicated tests for the complete `lib.stt` public API or its independence from bot/runtime modules. Tests should assert the exact expected `lib.stt.__all__` and use a fresh subprocess to import `lib.stt`, then verify no forbidden `internal.bot`, `internal.database`, or singleton-service modules were loaded. Importing within the normal pytest process is insufficient because unrelated tests may already pollute `sys.modules`.

title: Validate TranscriptionResult terminal-state invariants
content: `TranscriptionResult` should reject contradictory combinations at construction rather than merely typing them: FINAL requires valid nonempty transcript/segments as defined by the contract, NO_SPEECH must not carry recognized segments, and ERROR requires an `errorCode` (and corresponding error-state shape). Add tests for every invalid combination. This keeps provider-neutral STT results trustworthy at downstream boundaries.

title: Frozen STT containers must reject mutable collection inputs
content: A frozen dataclass only prevents field reassignment; it does not make list-valued `words` or `segments` immutable. Provider-neutral STT models must normalize accepted collections to tuples in `__post_init__` (or reject lists) so nested data cannot be mutated after construction. Test list inputs and attempted nested mutation, not only top-level field reassignment.

title: Reject unsupported TranscriptionResult statuses
content: `lib/stt/models.py` `TranscriptionResult` currently performs NO construction-time validation at all — there is no `__post_init__` in the dataclass (or anywhere in lib/stt). Callers can construct it with a raw string or unknown `status` and nothing rejects it. Because `STTResultStatus` is a StrEnum, a raw string like `"error"` compares equal to `STTResultStatus.ERROR`, so equality-based checks silently pass while identity checks (`is`) fail — validation must use `isinstance(status, STTResultStatus)` and reject non-members (e.g. with `ValueError`), with regression coverage for raw/unknown statuses. This is narrower than (and complements) the terminal-state invariant validation recommendation: first ensure the status itself is an allowed enum value.

title: STT Gate1 review caught incomplete coverage
content: The first Gate 1 implementation of the STT models/formatter appeared complete and passed its initial targeted tests, but follow-up review found two omissions: `TranscriptionResult.__post_init__` had no final rejection path for raw/unknown status values, and entity-boundary tests exercised only head truncation despite claiming both sides. The corrected implementation explicitly validates/normalizes status and adds separate tail cases for `&`, `<`, and `>`. For similar bounded-formatting/model work, inspect untyped constructor inputs and verify each claimed boundary direction independently rather than relying on broad happy-path tests.

title: PyAV optional imports need deferred annotations
content: In `lib/stt/audio.py`, PyAV types used in annotations (including `AudioFrame` and `OutputContainer`) must not be evaluated at module import time. If PyAV is optional/absent, undefined annotation names can raise `NameError` before `extractAudio()` reaches its intended `STTConfigurationError`. Use deferred annotations or quoted type names, and keep a regression test that imports the module with PyAV unavailable.

title: Skip PyAV streams without decoders
content: PyAV 18 can expose an audio stream whose `codec_context` is `None` when no decoder is available. Calling decode on that stream raises raw `AttributeError` and can prevent trying a later decodable audio stream. Audio extraction should detect and skip such candidates, then continue stream selection; test unsupported-first/valid-later media.

title: Flush tests must assert emitted tail audio
content: A PyAV extractor flush test that only verifies `resample(None)`/`encode(None)` calls is insufficient: fixtures with no delayed output can pass even when returned tail frames or packets are dropped. Inject delayed resampler/encoder output and assert it reaches the WAV and sample accounting. This complements the existing dual-flush requirement for resampler and encoder pipelines.

title: P2 bounded STT audio extractor API
content: lib.stt.audio public API (current, post-v1.1): `async def extractAudio(data: bytes, supportedInputFormats: Sequence[AudioFormatSpec]) -> ExtractedAudio`. It is async — all blocking PyAV work runs in asyncio.to_thread internally (await it directly; do not wrap again). It does NOT normalize to mono-16kHz-s16 WAV anymore: it probes the source, then negotiates one of three paths against the provider's supportedInputFormats — pass-through (container + channels/rate already in spec → source bytes returned verbatim), transcode (encode to the provider's first compressed target — OGG_OPUS for Yandex — clamping channels to the spec's [min,max] and rate to range via AudioResampler; Opus output is always 48 kHz native), or reject (EncoderError when no compressed target exists). Duration is measured from the actual sample count on every path. Typed exceptions map 1:1 to STTErrorCode: NoAudioTrackError, AudioDecodeError (open/decode failures), EncoderError (encoder/muxer/finalize failures + channel-count guard) — containers are closed on all exit paths via finally. PyAV is now a HARD import at module top (no try/except ImportError fallback in audio.py).

title: Preserve primary STT extraction errors during cleanup
content: PyAV extractor cleanup must close output and input containers independently. If `outputContainer.close()` raises and cleanup immediately aborts, `inputContainer.close()` leaks; if cleanup exceptions are allowed to escape normally, they can replace the meaningful decode/limit/mux error. Preserve the active primary exception, still attempt every resource close, and only surface/map a close failure when no earlier exception exists.

title: Separate PyAV input and output failures
content: Do not classify every `FFmpegError` from the P2 extractor as an undecodable candidate stream. Decode errors from an input candidate may justify skipping it and trying the next audio stream, but encoder, resampler, muxer, or output-finalization failures are deterministic pipeline failures and must map to an appropriate stable STT error instead of misleading `NO_AUDIO`. Scope candidate-retry handling to input decode operations only.

title: Yandex parser must reject malformed finalIndex
content: Code review of the isolated `lib/stt/providers/yandex_events.py` found that invalid `audioCursors.finalIndex` values can be interpreted as absent, allowing an event with malformed index data to produce `FINAL`. The parser must distinguish missing from present-but-invalid, read the documented `audioCursors.finalIndex` field, and return a stable `PROTOCOL_ERROR` for malformed indexes rather than silently falling back to completion. Regression coverage should include malformed values and the valid official index `0`.

title: Validate SpeechKit int64 timestamp syntax
content: Yandex SpeechKit event parsing must validate timestamp strings before calling `int()`: require ASCII decimal digits and constrain the value to the protobuf `int64` range `0..2**63-1`. Non-ASCII digit characters may be accepted by Python numeric conversion despite not being valid wire syntax, oversized values violate the protocol, and extremely long input can raise rather than yielding the parser's stable protocol-error result. Add regression tests for non-ASCII digits, overflow, and very long values.

title: Use strict JSON framing in SpeechKit parser
content: For raw concatenated Yandex recognition JSON, strict protocol parsing should accept only JSON whitespace (`space`, tab, CR, LF) between objects and reject non-standard JSON constants such as bare `NaN` and `Infinity`. Python's default `str.lstrip()` and `json.JSONDecoder` are more permissive than the wire format, so configure explicit whitespace handling and `parse_constant` rejection, mapping violations to `PROTOCOL_ERROR`. Tests should cover same-chunk concatenation, invalid UTF-8, and actual mid-codepoint UTF-8 fragmentation; splitting only between complete Cyrillic text does not exercise incremental UTF-8 decoding.

title: Map JSON recursion failures deterministically
content: Malformed, deeply nested Yandex event JSON can raise Python `RecursionError` from `json.JSONDecoder`; this currently escapes instead of becoming the parser's deterministic `PROTOCOL_ERROR` terminal result. Catch recursion-depth failures at the JSON parsing boundary and add a regression test for deeply nested malformed input.

title: SpeechKit provider must reject all non-2xx responses
content: Code review found that the raw HTTP Yandex SpeechKit provider used `Response.is_error`, which excludes 3xx responses. Because redirects are not followed, a 3xx `getRecognition` response could be sent to the event parser; an empty redirect body could become a valid `NO_SPEECH` result and then trigger cleanup, discarding the actual recognition operation. Submit, poll, and fetch paths should require `response.is_success` before parsing, map every non-2xx status to `PROVIDER_ERROR` (while preserving retry handling for 429/5xx), and test a 302 fetch with no parser invocation and no DELETE cleanup.

title: Handle incomplete SpeechKit operation errors immediately
content: The Yandex SpeechKit polling implementation only inspected the operation `error` field inside the `done` branch. An operation shaped like `{"done": false, "error": {...}}` therefore kept polling until timeout instead of terminating as `PROVIDER_ERROR`, wasting poll quota. Poll responses must detect an operation error before scheduling another poll, then process successful terminal responses; add regression coverage for error-bearing incomplete operations.

title: Coordinate SpeechKit polling rate across concurrent calls
content: The raw Yandex SpeechKit provider applies poll delays independently inside each `transcribe()` call. Its shared HTTP client does not coordinate admission, so concurrent transcriptions can issue immediate operation polls in parallel (e.g. six calls exceed the documented aggregate five polls/second vendor limit), causing avoidable 429s and consuming retry/operation budgets. Poll throttling must be provider-instance/shared, include initial polls and retries, and remain deadline-aware; add a concurrent multi-transcription test asserting the aggregate dispatch limit.

title: Honor both Retry-After formats in SpeechKit retries
content: Current Retry-After handling in YandexSpeechKitProvider._retryAfterSeconds (lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py): ONLY the delta-seconds form is parsed — `max(0.0, float(header))`. An absent, empty, or unparseable header (including the HTTP-date form, explicitly documented as unsupported in v1) returns None and falls back to exponential backoff (`retryBackoffSeconds * 2**min(attempt,100)`, capped at `_maxPollIntervalSeconds`). A honoured Retry-After value is returned unclamped by _retryDelay but is bounded in practice by the operation budget (asyncio.timeout around submit+poll+fetch). Discarding HTTP-date values is the documented, deliberate v1 behavior — not a contract violation; revisit only if Yandex is observed emitting HTTP-date Retry-After in practice.

title: Validate SpeechKit numeric configuration as finite
content: SpeechKit provider configuration validation must reject non-finite TOML numeric values such as `nan` and `inf`, not merely check positivity. Otherwise timeout values can produce immediate or unbounded deadline behavior. Integer byte limits also need actual integer validation rather than accepting arbitrary numeric values. Treat these as configuration errors and cover the edge cases.

title: Map deep SpeechKit JSON failures to protocol errors
content: The raw SpeechKit submit/poll envelope parsing should convert `RecursionError` from deeply nested JSON into the stable `PROTOCOL_ERROR` result instead of allowing it to escape the provider boundary. This matches the parser's defensive behavior and prevents malformed or adversarial response nesting from crashing the transcription lifecycle.

title: Keep SpeechKit submission non-retryable and fetch idempotent
content: The Yandex SpeechKit lifecycle separates ambiguous operations: do not retry `createRecognition` after an ambiguous transport failure, because resubmission can create duplicate recognition operations. Result fetching is safe to retry; each fetch attempt must instantiate a fresh event parser so partial events from a failed streamed response cannot contaminate the next attempt or duplicate transcript state.

title: SpeechKit P5 needs explicit retry regression tests
content: A read-only review of the P5 Yandex SpeechKit provider found no confirmed production-code defect, but regression coverage is incomplete for a load-bearing lifecycle invariant: POST submission must never retry, while only bounded safe GET operations may retry. Existing tests cover a poll GET 503 retry and a POST transport exception, but do not cover the separately implemented streamed `getRecognition` result-fetch retry path or a POST that receives a transient HTTP status. Add mocked-transport tests asserting result-fetch 503/transport failure retries exactly as bounded and then succeeds, with one submit and one cleanup; and asserting submit 429/5xx performs exactly one POST and returns `PROVIDER_ERROR`. This is specifically required by the P5 plan's retry contract.

title: Cover SpeechKit auth headers on every lifecycle request
content: The Yandex SpeechKit P5 contract requires `Authorization` and `x-folder-id` on every lifecycle HTTP request, not just submission. A review found the happy-path test asserts these headers only for submit, while polling/deletion use the shared `_request()` and streamed result fetching constructs its request separately. Add assertions over every captured request, including poll, result fetch, and cleanup, to prevent a future endpoint-specific header regression.

title: Complete SpeechKit polling retry/auth matrix
content: Gate 1 review found that Yandex SpeechKit polling tests covered only HTTP 503. The retry/status contract still needs explicit coverage for transport failures and 429 responses (including retry behavior/`Retry-After` handling), plus terminal 401/403 responses proving authentication errors are not retried and suppress downstream processing. Tests should assert attempt counts, result/status mapping, response cleanup, and no unnecessary subsequent request.

title: Always clean up SpeechKit recognitions
content: Gate-1 review found a residual lifecycle leak in `lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py`: once `createRecognition` returns an operation ID, terminal result-fetch failures and task cancellation can bypass remote recognition deletion. Since callers do not receive the operation ID for later cleanup, deletion should be scheduled from a `finally`-style path after operation creation, as bounded best-effort cleanup that preserves the original exception and does not swallow `CancelledError`. Add regression coverage for terminal fetch failure and cancellation, asserting deletion is attempted without extending beyond the active cleanup deadline.

title: Assert SpeechKit deletion and deadline behavior
content: A test named for cleanup after result-fetch HTTP errors is insufficient if it only asserts the raised error: it must record and assert exactly one DELETE for each non-retryable fetch status (such as 400/404). Likewise, a loose outer elapsed-time bound does not prove response close stays within the operation lifetime; use a controlled clock or assert the actual deadline with a narrow tolerance. These assertions prevent cleanup regressions from passing silently.

title: Review must reconcile delegated findings
content: In the Yandex SpeechKit scoped review, a delegated analysis explicitly found a Low-severity test-coverage gap: tests exercised only one cancellation of one waiter and did not cover repeated cancellation while shielded cleanup was pending or concurrent `aclose()` callers sharing `_closeTask`. The final review incorrectly said 'No findings' and claimed the guarantees were verified. Review workflow rule: reconcile all subagent/task findings before the final verdict; if a specific actionable gap remains, report it even when production behavior and quality gates pass. Also distinguish production correctness from adequacy of regression coverage.

title: STT config credentials are substituted eagerly
content: ConfigManager performs environment-variable substitution across the entire loaded configuration before STT validation; it does not lazily substitute credentials only when STT is enabled. Therefore comments/default-config claims must describe credentials as validated conditionally, not substituted conditionally, unless the loader is redesigned. This matters for accurate security/lifecycle expectations around default-off STT.

title: STT limiter declarations for later wiring
content: The default configuration (configs/00-defaults/00-config.toml:82-94,108-109) declares separate STT rate limiters and maps the service's queue names to them: stt-chat (SlidingWindow, 3 requests / 60 s — applied per chat, keyed str(chatId)) and stt-global (SlidingWindow, 10 requests / 60 s); [ratelimiter.queues] maps stt-chat = 'stt-chat' and stt-global = 'stt-global'. STTService.transcribeMedia applies the per-chat limiter then the global limiter before the concurrency semaphore ([stt] max-concurrency = 2; service.py:298-305). The declarations ship while STT is default-off so the service wiring consumes a stable contract; defaults contain only ${...} environment placeholders for credentials. NOTE: the rates were lowered from the 2026-07 plan's 20/hour and 450/hour to 3/min and 10/min.

title: MySQL media transitions need named-parameter conversion
content: P7 review found that `MySQLProvider.executeUpdate()` was forwarding the repository's portable `:named` SQL placeholders directly to aiomysql, which expects `%s`/`%(name)s` binding. This breaks `transitionMediaAttachment()` conditional UPDATEs before a matched-row count can be returned; verification SELECTs using named parameters are affected too. MySQL placeholder conversion must be centralized and applied consistently in both update and read execution paths.

title: PostgreSQL TIMESTAMP binding must normalize aware datetimes
content:
DURABLE CROSS-DRIVER GOTCHA (applies whenever the PostgreSQL provider becomes selectable): asyncpg requires OFFSET-NAIVE datetimes for `TIMESTAMP` (without time zone) columns, while the repo's write path produces UTC-AWARE datetimes (dbUtils.getCurrentTimestamp(); FORCE_SQL_TIMEZONE makes READS tz-aware UTC). The postgresql provider currently has NO datetime normalization in _execute/batchExecute (verified 2026-08-21) — naive pass-through. So any datetime-writing query will fail at bind time once PG is enabled, unless normalization to UTC-naive is added across ALL PostgreSQL execution methods (not just one).

Context: originally flagged in the P7 review against `transitionMediaAttachment()` — that method (and the whole conditional media-transition machinery) has since been REMOVED from media_attachments.py, but repositories still write aware datetimes (e.g. created_at/updated_at via getCurrentTimestamp in every repo), so the latent binding mismatch remains real for the PG provider.

title: SQL placeholder conversion must be token-aware
content: Dynamic conditional media transitions can generate parameter names such as `expectedStatus1` and `expectedStatus10`. Naive sequential string replacement can replace the shorter name inside the longer one and corrupt SQL. Provider placeholder conversion must tokenize named parameters or otherwise enforce boundary-aware matching; do not rely on replacement order or arbitrary parameter-name lengths.

title: Isolate optional database-driver stubs in tests
content: When testing optional MySQL/PostgreSQL/SQLink provider bindings without real driver dependencies, do not install fake `aiomysql`, `pymysql`, or `asyncpg` modules permanently at test-module import time. Mutating `sys.modules` globally can make later tests receive stubs instead of installed packages and create order-dependent behavior. Use a fixture or context manager that saves prior `sys.modules` entries, installs stubs only for the test scope, and restores both the module entries and any imported provider modules during teardown.

title: Provider command-tag tests must match SQL operation
content: In PostgreSQL provider `executeUpdate` contract tests, a mocked `DELETE 0` command tag paired with an `UPDATE` SQL statement only tests tag parsing, not DELETE execution/binding. Keep operation fidelity by parameterizing or separately testing matching UPDATE and DELETE SQL with their expected driver calls, so the test proves both command-tag parsing and the correct statement path.

title: Import SQLink before optional-driver stubs
content: In provider binding tests, importing `internal.database.providers.sqlink` only after installing fake optional-driver modules does not prove SQLink can be imported without those drivers; the test may pass because stubs satisfy imports. Import/cache SQLink while the real optional-driver environment is absent, then install stubs only for MySQL/PostgreSQL binding tests. This keeps the no-optional-driver contract meaningful.

title: Restore provider package attributes in import-isolation tests
content: Removing `internal.database.providers.mysql` and `.postgresql` from `sys.modules` is insufficient cleanup: Python can leave `mysql`/`postgresql` attributes on the parent `internal.database.providers` package. Later imports may reuse those stale stub-backed module objects, creating order-dependent tests. Isolation fixtures must snapshot and restore or delete both the `sys.modules` entries and corresponding parent-package attributes.

title: STT source buffer must be released before provider call
content: Current STT pipeline pins the source byte buffer through provider transcription. `AbstractSTTProvider.stt()` (lib/stt/abstract.py:181-215) keeps its `data` parameter live in its frame while `self.transcribe(audioData, ...)` runs the whole provider HTTP lifecycle, and `STTService.transcribeMedia` (internal/services/stt/service.py:266-326) likewise holds `data` across the semaphore-acquired provider call (`self._provider.stt(data)` at line 311). Peak memory on the transcode path is source bytes + re-encoded audio + base64 request body (+33%) simultaneously on the inline Yandex path (`_buildSubmitBody`, lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py); on the pass-through path `ExtractedAudio.data` IS the source bytes by design (lib/stt/audio.py:254-260), so no savings are possible there. To cut the avoidable peak on the transcode path, drop the source reference once extraction has produced the `ExtractedAudio` (e.g. `del data` in `stt()` before delegating to `transcribe`). Note lib/stt/audio.py deliberately does NOT bound decoded PCM (module docstring, lines 25-30) — source-size bounding stays the caller's job (maxSourceBytes gate in STTService.transcribeMedia, default 1 GiB).

title: STT service shutdown race lacks deterministic regression tests
content: Current tests deterministically verify that blocked queue tracking does not delay readiness/admission (`tests/services/stt/test_service.py:469-532`), but do not invoke `STTService.aclose()`. The only service-level close test (`test_service.py:201-222`) uses the deferred path with no registry coordinator or tracking task. Registry-only tests (`985-1053`) do not cover the service-level tracking snapshot race or cancellation of `STTService.aclose()`. Shutdown coverage should use explicit scheduling gates/events to reproduce dispatch-vs-close and cancellation races, not sleeps.

title: STT lifecycle integration needs a main import regression test
content: There are no existing tests that directly instantiate or exercise GromozekBot or main(); current startup-related tests cover the standalone Max webhook receiver and unrelated scripts. P9 explicitly calls for a startup regression/import-cycle check, so add a test that imports main (and ideally constructs the lifecycle with fakes) after STT composition is wired. Keep lib/stt provider-neutral with no internal.* imports; compose ConfigManager, ProxyService, STTService, and concrete providers only at main.py. Avoid package re-exports or service imports that pull bot applications/handlers into internal/services/stt.

title: P9 startup must roll back partial resources
content: The P9 startup path in main.py acquires long-lived resources (including the STT provider's persistent HTTP client) before constructing the platform bot application. If a later constructor raises, the normal _shutdown() path is never entered, so already-created provider clients and other services can leak. Startup should be transactional: wrap post-acquisition initialization in rollback cleanup, or move acquisition into a lifecycle/factory that guarantees closing all partially initialized resources on failure.

title: Unified cleanup required for post-scheduler startup failures
content: A lifecycle review found that GromozekBot startup creates the delayed scheduler and then performs ProxyService initialization, LLMManager setup, rate-limiter loading, and STT initialization before the bot application is fully constructed. If any of these later steps raises, the existing cleanup guard only handles application-construction failures, so _shutdown() is skipped. This can leave the scheduler task pending, proxy subprocesses running, LLM HTTP clients/rate limiters open, and STT resources unclosed. Startup must put all post-scheduler initialization under one guarded cleanup path, initialize cleanup fields safely before use, and await _shutdown() on every initialization failure.

title: Fail fast when delayed scheduler dies during startup
content: Still present at HEAD (re-verified 2026-08-20): GromozekBot.__init__ creates the delayed-scheduler task via `loop.create_task(QueueService.getInstance().startDelayedScheduler(...))` (main.py:74-77) but never inspects whether that task completed with an exception. If startDelayedScheduler fails during startup — e.g. getPendingDelayedTasks() raises on a DB error at internal/services/queue_service/service.py:309 — the bot continues as if startup succeeded with no functioning scheduler: no CRON_JOB ticks (no proxy health checks, no deferred lifecycle starts) and no DO_EXIT processing on shutdown (proxies and queued exit work never drain; _shutdown() just logs the failed task). History: a startup fail-fast check (`_schedulerTask.done()` + `result()` after the first event-loop turn, plus an initial `asyncio.sleep(0)` yield) was added in commit ba868907 (2026-07-31) and removed in 60ef1ce2 'Simplify STTService' (2026-08-02). If re-added, propagate the failure into the unified startup cleanup path before the bot starts polling.

title: Cancelled scheduler can make shutdown busy-spin
content: main.py shutdown/scheduler-cancellation note (verified 2026-08-21): current _shutdown() (main.py:157-199) has NO _shutdownTask, NO shield, and NO retry loop — the shielded-retry busy-spin mechanism described earlier does not exist in the tree. The surviving sharp edge: Step 2.2 awaits the scheduler task (`await self._schedulerTask`, main.py:172) inside `try/except Exception`. If the scheduler task is already cancelled, awaiting it raises CancelledError, which `except Exception` does NOT catch — it escapes _shutdown(), skipping rate-limiter/LLM/STT/database cleanup (steps 2.3-2.6), and propagates out of `loop.run_until_complete(self._shutdown())` in run()'s finally. Also note RateLimiterManager.destroy() (line 177) is the one cleanup step with no try/except wrapper at all. If shutdown robustness is revisited: handle scheduler-task cancellation explicitly (distinguish an already-cancelled scheduler task from caller cancellation) and ensure each step's failure cannot skip later resources.

title: Make lifecycle tests prove dependency wiring
content: Startup/shutdown lifecycle tests must validate behavior, not merely that constructors or methods were called. For the shipped stateless STT wiring (ADR-020): assert STTService.initialize constructs the provider from STT_PROVIDERS_MAP (key 'yandex-speechkit') with the proxy resolved through ProxyService.resolveProxy(sttConfig, 'stt') injected as proxyConfig= (internal/services/stt/service.py:206-227), and that STTService.aclose() closes the provider — main.py _shutdown closes it at Step 2.5, AFTER the LLM manager (Step 2.4) and BEFORE the database (Step 2.6). For shutdown-ordering tests generally: use a genuinely blocked queue/scheduler drain and assert the downstream close is not called until the drain completes; setting a task field to None only proves call order and can miss the race. Note: the old STTManager(providerName=..., providers={...}) class no longer exists — STTService constructs providers directly.

title: Scheduler BaseException must not abort cleanup
content: Still present at HEAD (re-verified 2026-08-20): GromozekBot._shutdown() in main.py guards `await self._schedulerTask` with `except Exception` (main.py:165-174). KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit and CancelledError are BaseException subclasses and are NOT caught — if the delayed-scheduler task terminates with one, the exception propagates out of _shutdown() and rate-limiter destroy, LLM manager close, STT close, and database closeAll() (main.py:176-199) are all skipped. History: a BaseException-isolation fix was added in commit ba868907 (2026-07-31) and deliberately removed in 60ef1ce2 'Simplify STTService' (2026-08-02), so the exposure returned at HEAD. Any future shutdown re-hardening must isolate non-cancellation BaseExceptions from the scheduler await while still running the remaining cleanup steps, with regression tests covering a scheduler task raising BaseException (no such tests exist at HEAD).

title: Platform adapter must not destroy shared limiter early
content: In the real Max lifecycle, `MaxBotApplication` was destroying the shared `RateLimiterManager` from its own shutdown before `GromozekBot` had drained and closed STT work. Pending STT admission or worker operations can then fail during graceful shutdown. Shared-resource ownership belongs in the central main lifecycle: let the bot application stop transport/handlers, drain QueueService and close STT, then destroy rate limiters, followed by LLM/database cleanup. Test the full Max path rather than only calling `GromozekBot._shutdown()` directly.

title: Shutdown waiters must not cancel shared cleanup
content: GromozekBot shutdown is a shared, idempotent lifecycle operation rather than independent cleanup per caller. Concurrent shutdown callers must await one cleanup execution; if one caller is cancelled while a resource close is blocked, cancellation must affect only that waiter, not the underlying cleanup. The cleanup operation must continue to completion and subsequent callers must observe the same completion, with every initialized resource closed exactly once. Tests should explicitly cancel one waiting shutdown caller and assert completion plus per-resource call counts.

title: Scheduler failure can leak initialized proxies
content: Latent gap still present at HEAD (re-verified 2026-08-20): proxy child processes are stopped ONLY via the DO_EXIT delayed-task dispatch inside QueueService's scheduler loop — ProxyService registers `_dtOnExit` at internal/services/proxy/service.py:109 and it is dispatched at internal/services/queue_service/service.py:382-409. The scheduler loop swallows all regular Exceptions (service.py:416-418), so it dies only on BaseException (CancelledError/KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit) or loop closure. If the scheduler task dies after ProxyService.initialize() started a proxy, GromozekBot._shutdown() (main.py:157-199) has no direct proxy-close fallback: the DO_EXIT sentinel is never consumed and the proxy subprocess can outlive the bot. History: a direct `_dtOnExit` fallback (synthetic DelayedTask, `_closeProxyServiceAfterSchedulerFailure`) was added in commit ba868907 (2026-07-31) and deliberately removed in 60ef1ce2 'Simplify STTService' (2026-08-02) as over-engineered; it survives only on the stale add-audio-transcribation branch. If shutdown is ever re-hardened, prefer a simple idempotent ProxyService close invoked from _shutdown()'s scheduler-failure path over re-adding the synthetic-DelayedTask fallback machinery.

title: Shutdown cancellation can leave later resources open
content: `main.py` shutdown currently suppresses cancellation/cleanup exceptions after sequentially calling `RateLimiterManager.destroy()`, `LLMManager.aclose()`, and `DatabaseManager.closeAll()`. These managers are not individually cancellation-safe: if cancellation interrupts one close operation, cleanup of later registered limiters, providers, or database connections may never run, while the outer shutdown proceeds as if shared resources were closed. Resource teardown must be shielded from cancellation (or each manager must complete its full cleanup before re-raising cancellation), while preserving eventual cancellation semantics. Regression coverage should interrupt each close phase and verify all resources are still closed.

title: Scoped read-only review preference
content: For code-review requests, the user may require a strict read-only review limited to explicitly named files and their changes versus HEAD. Related production code may be read only as context, but findings must not mention other worktree changes. Report only verified actionable issues with exact changed-file line numbers; omit unrelated style suggestions and state briefly when the scoped diff is clean.

title: Proxy cancellation regression covers partial cleanup
content: The P9 proxy lifecycle regression suite now exercises the important partial-handler interleaving with two child lifecycles: cancellation occurs after the first lifecycle has been claimed/stopped, then main.py's direct fallback runs and must stop only the still-registered second lifecycle. This validates both halves of the claim-before-await contract—no duplicate stop for the already-claimed child and no leak for unclaimed children—rather than testing only an all-or-nothing cancellation case.

title: Proxy onExit failures must not abort remaining lifecycle drain
content: ProxyService._dtOnExit (internal/services/proxy/service.py:211-226) is a simple sequential drain: iterates list(self._activeLifecycles.items()), awaits each lifecycle.onExit() inside try/except Exception, then calls self._activeLifecycles.clear(). Latent hazard still present: asyncio.CancelledError is a BaseException (Python 3.8+), so it is caught by NEITHER ProxyLifecycle.onExit()'s 'except Exception' around stop() (lifecycle.py:288-297) NOR _dtOnExit's 'except Exception'. If the scheduler task is cancelled mid-stop, CancelledError propagates out of the drain — remaining lifecycles are never stopped and clear() never runs (they stay in the registry). Any other BaseException from a lifecycle likewise escapes the loop. main.py has NO direct DO_EXIT fallback that re-drains lifecycles: GromozekBot._shutdown() (main.py:157-174) only calls QueueService.beginShutdown() then awaits the scheduler task, so an aborted drain is never retried. Historical note for anyone re-attempting shutdown hardening: a 'P9' redesign (popitem() claiming of lifecycles, per-lifecycle child tasks, shielding, main.py direct fallback) was reviewed across sessions on 2026-07-28 but never merged — the current code has no claiming logic and no child tasks, and only the happy-path test_dtOnExitDelegates exists in tests/services/proxy/test_service.py.

title: Bound EnsuredMessage media polling by deadline
content: A read-only review of the media/STT diff found that `EnsuredMessage.updateMediaContent()` can exceed `MAX_MEDIA_AWAIT_SECS` by up to one full `MEDIA_AWAIT_DELAY`: the loop checks elapsed time, then sleeps the fixed delay before the next check. A wall-clock adjustment can also make elapsed time move backward. The correct fix is to use a monotonic deadline and sleep only `min(MEDIA_AWAIT_DELAY, max(0, deadline - monotonic_now))`, stopping when the budget is exhausted. This preserves the plan's strict 'at most' timeout contract.

title: downloadAttachment compatibility and cancellation contract
content:
TheBot.downloadAttachment(mediaId, fileId) error/cancellation contract (verified 2026-08-20; the maxBytes parameter this memory referenced was reverted 2026-08-03):

- Telegram branch (bot.py:1205-1208): get_file(fileId) + download_as_bytearray() with NO try/except — operational failures (NetworkError etc.) RAISE and propagate to the caller; they are NOT converted to None. Callers in base.py rely on None only for the Max path.
- Max branch (bot.py:1203-1204): delegates to maxBot.downloadAttachmentPayload(fileId), which catches Exception → logs → returns None (lib/max_bot/client.py:1715-1718).
- asyncio.CancelledError propagates on both platforms: the Telegram branch has no handler at all, and the Max branch's `except Exception` does not catch it (CancelledError is BaseException on Python ≥3.8).
- Platform mismatch (neither branch matches botProvider) raises ValueError.

Guardrail still binding: there is no explicit cancellation regression test for this path — future changes must avoid broad `except BaseException` catches that would swallow cancellation, and must not wrap the Telegram branch in failure→None translation without checking call-site assumptions (handlers in media.py/dev_commands.py and base.py treat None as 'no media', while a raising Telegram path currently surfaces errors through normal exception handling up to _processMediaV2's callers).

labels.supersedes_reason: Telegram failure→None claim invalidated by revert

title: Media await treats terminal states as safe results
content: P14 established that EnsuredMessage media rendering must explicitly handle database attachments in terminal NEW and FAILED states instead of treating every non-DONE row as still pending or raising. The await path polls only PENDING work; once an attachment is NEW/FAILED it returns the row safely so formatting can proceed without an exception or unbounded wait. Regression coverage belongs in tests/bot/models/test_ensured_message.py alongside the bounded polling tests.

title: Render STT descriptions through computed media content
content: The media render contract now computes the complete multi-attachment mediaContent before serializing both JSON and TEXT LLM messages. This is required for Max media groups: Max preprocessing supplies multiple attachments, and relying on the single-message field causes TEXT output to omit the <media-description> block even when JSON appears correct. STT descriptions must remain quoted/untrusted XML-safe in both serializers; tests cover Max multiattachment JSON/TEXT output and transcript characters that require XML escaping.

title: Compressed Max downloads bypass byte cap
content: Durable HTTPX gotcha for any future bounded streaming download (lesson from the bounded Max downloader that existed 2026-07-27..2026-08-03 and was fully reverted on 2026-08-03): `response.aiter_bytes()` transparently decompresses gzip/deflate/etc. before yielding chunks, so a small compressed attachment can expand and be allocated far beyond a cap that only counts yielded/retained bytes — per-chunk caps bound RETAINED memory, not ALLOCATED memory (the transport has already allocated and yielded each chunk before the app checks it). Correct pattern: stream with `aiter_raw()` rather than `aiter_bytes()`, send `Accept-Encoding: identity`, reject any non-identity `Content-Encoding` before body iteration, use a small fixed chunk size (64 KiB), check the accumulated size before retaining each chunk, and avoid chunk-list + `b"".join()` shapes that transiently double peak memory. Current state (re-verified 2026-08-20): `MaxBotClient.downloadAttachmentPayload` (lib/max_bot/client.py:1673) is a plain `client.get` returning `ret.content` — unbounded by accepted design (docs/design/media-transcription-stt-v1.md sections 8.3 and 12.4) — so this gotcha is dormant until bounded downloading is reintroduced. The lesson is NOT recorded anywhere in project docs, only in memory.

title: Cancellation tests must release blocked workers
content: A cancellation regression test for synchronous attachment storage can deadlock the suite if it waits indefinitely for the worker's start/release events and only unblocks the worker after the cancellation assertion. Use bounded `Event.wait()`/async waits and release the blocked worker in `finally`, so a failure cannot leave an executor thread holding the attachment-storage lock or hang subsequent tests.

title: Avoid wall-clock heartbeat assertions
content: For tests proving synchronous work is off the event loop, a strict elapsed-time heartbeat threshold (the P12 test used 50 ms) is load-dependent and can fail spuriously on CI. Coordinate with events: keep storage blocked, assert an async heartbeat/event completes while it is blocked, and use only generous bounded timeouts for failure detection. Also assert the exact expected SHA-512-derived storage key rather than merely checking prefix/suffix, and add thread-identity/concurrent same-key coverage when testing off-loop content-addressed storage.

title: Telegram local-mode paths need bounded file reads
content: PTB local-mode gotcha (python-telegram-bot==22.8, pinned in requirements.direct.txt): when the bot runs against a local Bot API server (`localMode = true`, wired at internal/bot/telegram/application.py:363), `File.file_path` can be a local filesystem path instead of an https URL. PTB's own download helpers handle this (telegram/_files/file.py checks `is_local_file(self.file_path)` and reads via `Path(...)`), so the current `TheBot.downloadAttachment` (internal/bot/common/bot.py:1188, uses `fileInfo.download_as_bytearray()`) is unaffected in local mode. The bug bit only the bounded-download implementation (reverted 2026-08-03) that passed `file_path` straight to an HTTPX client. Any future custom/bounded Telegram downloader that bypasses PTB must detect filesystem paths and read them with a capped reader off the event loop, with regression coverage for both URL and local-path file_path values. Re-verified against source 2026-08-20.

title: Drain to_thread reads after cancellation
content: When a bounded local file read is offloaded with `asyncio.to_thread`, cancelling the awaiting coroutine does not stop the running synchronous read. If the caller releases an STT/admission semaphore immediately on cancellation, the worker thread may continue holding the capped allocation and a new job can start, violating concurrency and memory limits. Keep an explicit executor task, shield it from cancellation, and drain/await it before re-raising `CancelledError` (or otherwise ensure the worker has finished before releasing the admission slot). Add a cancellation regression test covering the ordering.

title: P16 acceptance audit residual gaps
content: A read-only audit of the implemented media-transcription STT feature against docs/plans/media-transcription-stt-v1.md §13.2/§16 found that library, provider, service-concurrency, and basic handler-dispatch tests are present, but several acceptance items remain weakly covered: no focused end-to-end assertion that EnsuredMessage.formatForLLM injects transcripts correctly in both JSON and TEXT; no dedicated Max multi-attachment per-item rendering regression; no complete handler-level exercise of the DB state matrix (DONE without description, NEW/FAILED retry, stale PENDING reclaim, concurrent first insert, and all download/storage terminal failures); and no direct assertion that transcript content cannot become a role=system message. Native PyAV cancellation remains inherently unverified by coroutine tests because to_thread codec work cannot be interrupted; graceful drain is tested, while hard native hangs, live SpeechKit wire behavior/latency, resource usage, Alpine PyAV compatibility, and supervisor hard-kill behavior remain manual release gates.

title: Do not overclaim P16 verification
content: The implementation agent's final report claimed P16 automated acceptance was complete after `make format lint` and `make test` (`3707 passed, 11 skipped`), but review identified unclosed gaps: no true concurrent absent-row insert race, no real handler-to-service four-type integration, shutdown test did not prove provider-before-manager-close ordering, and role assertions did not prove transcript injection. Passing tests and green quality gates do not justify claiming acceptance when the test design omits required scenarios.

title: lib/stt extraction spec at docs/plans/lib-stt-v1.md
content: The lib/stt spec lives at docs/design/lib-stt-v1.md (NOT docs/plans/ — that path no longer resolves; docs/plans/ now contains only 3 unrelated files). Status is now 'IMPLEMENTED (simplified shape)' — the implemented lib/stt differs from the v1 spec in places, and v1.1 changes (Object Storage routing gate-3, stats recording gate-4, operation-budget reconciliation 180s→2400s in §7.4/§10) are governed by the companion doc docs/design/stt-v1.1.md (status IMPLEMENTED), which lib-stt-v1.md cross-references throughout. Contracts that held through implementation: dependency firewall (lib/stt imports no internal.bot/internal.database/singleton-service; proxy injected as an already-resolved ProxyConfig; media loading owned by the service layer), the raise contract (providers' stt()/transcribe never raise for expected failures — they return TranscriptionResult incl. ERROR; audio.extractAudio is the only runtime raise-point, typed exceptions mapping 1:1 to STTErrorCode), and formatter purity (internal/services/stt/formatter.py formatTranscript imports only stdlib + lib.stt.models, must not raise). Caps are read by the caller (STTService reads [stt] max-source-bytes / max-concurrency / ratelimiter queues), never by lib/stt modules.

title: Proxy injection seam: resolve in service, inject into lib client constructor
content:
Two distinct proxy-wiring patterns exist for lib-level HTTP clients, and the choice matters because of per-service proxy lifecycle registration:

PATTERN A — "resolve inside lib" (used by AI providers): the lib calls `ProxyConfig.fromServiceConfig(providerConfig).toKwargs()` itself and spreads the result into a per-request or persistent `httpx.AsyncClient`. Example: `lib/ai/providers/basic_openai_provider.py` (~line 908, and the `_proxyHttpClient` field). See memory 10a28aa1.

PATTERN B — "service resolves, lib receives injected" (REQUIRED for lib/stt; the cleaner pattern for any lib client owned by a singleton internal service): the internal service calls `ProxyService.resolveProxy(serviceConfig, serviceLabel)` which returns a resolved `ProxyConfig` AND registers the per-service proxy lifecycle, then passes that ProxyConfig into the lib client's constructor. The lib stores it (e.g. `self._proxyConfig`) and spreads `self._proxyConfig.toKwargs()` into `httpx.AsyncClient` at request time. It NEVER calls `fromServiceConfig()` itself. Clean existing examples: `lib/yandex_search/client.py` (stores `self._proxyConfig`, line ~182; spreads `toKwargs()` line ~363), `lib/openweathermap/client.py` (line ~473), and `lib/max_bot/client.py._getHttpClient()` (memory 182ba59e).

WHY IT MATTERS: `ProxyConfig.fromServiceConfig()` bypasses per-service proxy lifecycle registration. The lifecycle registration happens inside `ProxyService.resolveProxy()` (`internal/services/proxy/service.py`, the `resolveProxy(serviceConfig, serviceLabel)` method — see memory 24c90899). So a lib that calls `fromServiceConfig()` directly gets a proxy that is not registered for health-check/CRON/shutdown lifecycle management by ProxyService.

RULE OF THUMB: if the lib client is instantiated by and owned by a singleton internal service (like STTService owning YandexSpeechKitProvider), use Pattern B — the service resolves via `ProxyService.resolveProxy(...)` and injects the resolved ProxyConfig into the lib constructor. The lib/stt dependency firewall explicitly forbids `fromServiceConfig()` inside lib/stt (parent plan §9.2, now pinned in lib-stt-v1.md §1 contract 1).
