title: STT template-method refactor: AbstractSTTProvider concrete transcribe wraps abstract _transcribe
content:
As part of the STT v1.1 simplification refactor (commit 561dd04), `AbstractSTTProvider` (lib/stt/abstract.py) became a template-method base:

- CONCRETE `__init__(proxyConfig, statsStorage, **extraKwargs)` with `__slots__`.
- CONCRETE `transcribe(self, audio, *, consumerId=None)` that wraps the NEW abstract `_transcribe(self, audio) -> TranscriptionResult` with: timing, best-effort `_recordStats`, `except Exception` → PROVIDER_ERROR, and `CancelledError` propagation (never swallowed).
- `_recordStats` was hoisted OUT of `YandexSpeechKitProvider` into the base class. `YandexSpeechKitProvider.transcribe` became `_transcribe` and no longer owns stats timing/recording.
- `consumerId` stays on `stt`/`transcribe` for stats purposes; it is REMOVED from `_transcribe`.

Implication for future STT providers: concrete providers only implement `_transcribe` (raw transcription); stats recording and timing come free from the base. The base class imports `CancelledError` (from asyncio or the underlying lib) and must propagate it while mapping other exceptions to `PROVIDER_ERROR`.

title: maxInlineBytes: only positive check remains, no 60MB upper-bound validation (supersedes earlier validation memories)
content:
STT v1.1 simplification removed the `maxInlineBytes <= 60_000_000` upper-bound validation from `YandexSpeechKitProvider.__init__` (lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py). Only the `maxInlineBytes <= 0 → ValueError("maxInlineBytes must be positive")` check remains (line ~270-271). This SUPERSEDES the earlier v1.1 design memories (266c46c3 split error messages, 1a0c865e validation ordering including maxInlineBytes upper bound, and 2e69a246 boto3-absent ValueError) — those described the pre-simplification design.

Current truth: an operator can set `max-inline-bytes` higher than the 60 MB vendor inline ceiling (default is 40 MiB = 41943040). Risk documented as residual: setting it ≥ 60 MB can cause opaque runtime SpeechKit rejection after base64 expansion. Docs (docs/design/stt-v1.1.md §6.3, docs/llm/configuration.md) now state this explicitly; the doc task specified "the 60 MB vendor inline ceiling is still the design's max-inline-bytes default rationale, but NOT enforced at startup".

title: Bugfix: return-in-finally swallowed CancelledError in AbstractSTTProvider.transcribe
content:
Root cause (A1 fix-pass, STT v1.1, lib/stt/abstract.py): the original `transcribe` did `finally: await self._recordStats(...); return ret`. A `return` inside a `finally` block OVERRIDES any in-flight BaseException — including asyncio.CancelledError — silently converting task cancellation into a normal return. That violated the never-raise/cancellation contract.

Correct fix shape (verified in review):
- `try: ret = await self._transcribe(audio=audio)` / `except Exception:` (NEVER `BaseException`) — bind `ret` to an ERROR `TranscriptionResult(status=ERROR, segments=(), errorCode=PROVIDER_ERROR)` in the except branch, with a descriptive `logger.exception("...")` message (not bare `logger.exception(exc)`).
- Call `await self._recordStats(...)` and `return ret` AFTER the try/except, NOT in a `finally`.
- `segments=()` — empty tuple, not `[]`.

Result: CancelledError propagates past `_recordStats` and `return` (record = 0 on cancellation); `ret` is bound on every reachable `_recordStats` call (success → from `_transcribe`, Exception → bound in except). Stats record-exactly-once per call on success and ERROR paths. This same "no return/await-that-raises inside finally when BaseException must propagate" rule applies anywhere CancelledError must survive cleanup.

title: Bugfix: bare `super` + `locals()` spread bug in YandexSpeechKitProvider.__init__
content:
Root cause (A1 fix-pass, STT v1.1, lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py): the provider `__init__` used `kwargs = locals()` then `super.__init__(**kwargs)`. Two bugs: (1) `super` without parentheses (calls the class object, not the bound super proxy); (2) `locals()` spreads `self` and every parameter into the base `__init__`.

Correct fix (verified in review): make `proxyConfig` and `statsStorage` explicit named subclass params (defaults None) and call `super().__init__(proxyConfig=proxyConfig, statsStorage=statsStorage, **extraKwargs)`. Base `AbstractSTTProvider.__init__` accepts `proxyConfig`, `statsStorage`, `**extraKwargs` and stores `self.proxyConfig`, `self.statsStorage`, `self._extraLabels`. Reusable rule: never pass `locals()` to `super().__init__`; name the params you own and forward the rest via `**extraKwargs`.

title: STT v1.1 verified template-method invariants + stats-enabled filter removal accepted
content:
lib/stt template-method invariants (verified still true 2026-08-21): `_transcribe(self, audio)` is the abstract hook and MAY raise; base `transcribe` owns timing, exception mapping, and stats recording; never-raise boundary lives in the base; zero `internal.*` imports in lib/stt.

**Decision (still valid):** `"stats-enabled"` must NOT be restored to the `[stt]`→provider kwarg filter in internal/services/stt/service.py — stats gating is owned by main.py via `[stats].enabled`.

**Filter shape UPDATE (2026-08-21):** the filter tuple grew from 4 to 8 entries — it now also strips the service-consumed caps before passing config to the provider:
`("enabled", "use-proxy", "proxy-config", "provider", "max-source-bytes", "chat-ratelimiter-queue", "global-ratelimiter-queue", "max-concurrency")` (service.py lines 216-225). max-concurrency/max-source-bytes/ratelimiter queues are consumed by STTService itself (semaphore, byte cap, RateLimiterManager queues).

title: Test fakes of AbstractSTTProvider must call super().__init__()
content:
In tests/services/stt/test_transcribe.py, `FakeProvider(AbstractSTTProvider)` had an `__init__` that did NOT call `super().__init__()`, leaving `proxyConfig`, `statsStorage`, and `_extraLabels` unset. Harmless only by luck — `FakeProvider` overrides `stt` directly, so it never hits the base `transcribe`/`_recordStats` path that reads `self.statsStorage`. The A1 fix-pass added `super().__init__()` at the start of `FakeProvider.__init__`, matching the `_StubProvider` pattern already in tests/lib/stt/test_abstract.py.

Rule for any test fake/subclass of `AbstractSTTProvider`: always call `super().__init__()` first — the base `__init__(*, proxyConfig=None, statsStorage=None, **extraKwargs)` is all keyword-defaulted (no-arg call is valid) and sets `proxyConfig`, `statsStorage` (defaulting to `NullStatsStorage()`), and `_extraLabels`. A fake that omits the super call silently drops stats plumbing and will crash the moment a test exercises the base `transcribe` path.

title: STT template-method refactor: concrete transcribe wraps abstract _transcribe
content: 2026-08-07 user manual refactor (commit 561dd04) of lib/stt, applied on branch add-audio-transcribation-v2. `AbstractSTTProvider` (lib/stt/abstract.py) is now a template-method base: it has a CONCRETE `__init__(proxyConfig, statsStorage, **extraKwargs)` + `__slots__ = ("proxyConfig", "statsStorage", "_extraLabels")` (line 58), a CONCRETE `transcribe(self, audio, *, consumerId=None)` that wraps the ABSTRACT `_transcribe(self, audio) -> TranscriptionResult` with timing + best-effort `_recordStats` + `except Exception` → PROVIDER_ERROR (CancelledError propagates). `_recordStats` lives on the base and is called from the concrete `transcribe` (not from `_transcribe`). `YandexSpeechKitProvider.transcribe` → renamed `_transcribe` (no longer owns stats/timing). `consumerId` stays on `stt`/`transcribe` (for per-consumer stats rollup), REMOVED from `_transcribe`. `self._extraLabels` is a base-class dict spread into stats labels at abstract.py:241 (`**self._extraLabels`); the Yandex provider seeds it with `self._extraLabels["model"] = model` (yandex_speechkit.py:343). STTService (internal/services/stt/service.py) is a stateless singleton: `initialize(configManager, statsStorage=None)`; `async transcribeMedia(data, *, chatId) -> STTOutcome` pipeline = disabled → source-too-large → rate-limiters → semaphore → `provider.stt(data, consumerId=str(chatId))` → mapOutcome; never-raises (CancelledError propagates). `STTOutcome.success: bool` (not a status). Stats in `_recordStats` use keys generation_stt/request_count/audio_duration_ms/elapsed_time/is_error + status_{STATUS} (lowercase StrEnum value). Post-refactor `make test` = 3726/11, lint 0/0/0.

title: STT stats model label NOT dropped — emitted via provider _extraLabels
content: Correction (verified against code 2026-08-07): the user's simplification #2 summary said the `model` stats label was DROPPED, but code shows otherwise — `YandexSpeechKitProvider.__init__` sets `self._extraLabels["model"] = model` (lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py:343) and `AbstractSTTProvider._recordStats` spreads `**self._extraLabels` into the stats labels (lib/stt/abstract.py:241). So the `model` label IS still recorded for the Yandex provider. The model label was only removed from the base `_recordStats`'s explicit key list; the provider re-adds it via the `_extraLabels` extension mechanism (that's what `_extraLabels` exists for). Per AGENTS.md (code is the source of truth), docs were corrected to say "present via _extraLabels", NOT dropped. If the user truly intends to drop the model label, that is a pending CODE fix (remove the `_extraLabels["model"]` assignment), not a doc fix. Prior memory 58aa15e5 claiming "model label is DROPPED" is WRONG and was superseded.

title: STT stats data source key is [stats].stt-stats-data-source, NOT llm-stats-data-source
content:
STT stats use their OWN config key `[stats].stt-stats-data-source` (configs/00-defaults/stats.toml:5, default "default") — do not confuse it with `llm-stats-data-source`. The LLM/STT/message/tool/command paths each read their own key.

Current wiring (verified): main.py:118-121 builds `sttStatsStorage = StatsAggregationService.getInstance().createStatsStorage("stt_request", statsConfig.get("stt-stats-data-source", database.manager.default))` and passes it to `STTService.getInstance().initialize(configManager, statsStorage=sttStatsStorage)`. The FACTORY (not main.py directly) handles the enabled gate: when global `[stats].enabled = false` (default), createStatsStorage returns an UNREGISTERED NullStatsStorage and the registry stays empty; when enabled, it constructs and registers a DatabaseStatsStorage. `eventType="stt_request"` keeps STT rows separable from llm_request/message/llm_tool_call/command without a new table/migration. (Older memories claiming STT reuses llm-stats-data-source were wrong and are superseded.)

title: STT stats gating simplified: [stt].stats-enabled removed, global [stats].enabled only
content: Simplification 1 (2026-08-07): STT statistics are gated on the GLOBAL `[stats].enabled` flag only (checked in main.py). The independent `[stt].stats-enabled` key was REMOVED from `configs/00-defaults/stt.toml` AND from `STTService.initialize`'s filtered-keys tuple. Rationale: one global stats flag — `eventType="stt_request"` still separates rows in queries. This REVERSES the earlier v1.1 design (memory bcd35de8, which documented the independent flag, is superseded/outdated). Do not re-add a per-consumer stats flag for STT.

title: STT max-inline-bytes has no upper-bound validation; residual 60MB vendor ceiling risk
content: Simplification 4 (2026-08-07): `YandexSpeechKitProvider.__init__` NO LONGER validates an upper bound on `maxInlineBytes` — only the `> 0` positive check remains. The 60 MB vendor inline ceiling is still the rationale for the `max-inline-bytes` DEFAULT (41943040 = 40 MiB in configs/00-defaults/stt.toml) but is NOT enforced at startup. Residual risk: setting `max-inline-bytes` ≥ 60 MB risks opaque runtime SpeechKit rejection after base64 expansion. Also: `operation-budget-seconds` default in stt.toml is 2400 while the provider's Python default param is `180.0` (config wins at runtime). boto3 is a pinned dependency with a HARD unconditional import in lib/stt/providers/yandex_object_storage.py (the try/except ImportError + _BOTO3_AVAILABLE guard + construction-time ValueError were all removed — simplification 3). Object Storage validation remains all-or-nothing: if `object-storage-bucket` is set, both `object-storage-key-id` and `object-storage-key-secret` are required and no `${...}` placeholders allowed; keys are commented out in defaults (OS disabled by default). Routing: extracted payload ≥ inline threshold AND OS enabled → upload outside the operation budget, SpeechKit via `uri` field, object deleted in `finally`; ≥ threshold AND OS disabled → provider surfaces SOURCE_TOO_LARGE.

title: STT gate-numbering collision: v1.1 feature gates vs release-test gates disambiguated

title: STT handler integration: folded into _processMediaV2, not a separate handler
content: STT transcription is folded into `BaseBotHandler._processMediaV2` (internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py) — there is NO separate STTHandler. On the media branch, `needProcessSTT` triggers `sttTask = asyncio.create_task(self._transcribeMedia(ret.id, chatId, data=mediaData))`, registered via `queueService.addBackgroundTask(sttTask)` and `ret.task = sttTask` (mirrors the image-parsing background-task pattern). `_transcribeMedia` is a background task around STTService.transcribeMedia. title: Exact STT stats schema emitted by _recordStats (labels + counters, verified 2026-08-08)
content:
Verified against code 2026-08-08 (read-only verification, resolving prior conflicting agent reports). `AbstractSTTProvider._recordStats` (lib/stt/abstract.py:210-257) emits this EXACT schema for a FINAL result on `YandexSpeechKitProvider`:

labels dict (line 237-242):
- `provider` = `type(self).__name__` — DYNAMIC class name, e.g. "YandexSpeechKitProvider"; NOT a literal string.
- `generationType` = `"stt"` — literal.
- `status` = `result.status` — StrEnum VALUE (lowercase), e.g. "final".
- `**self._extraLabels` — spread at line 241; for Yandex provider this contributes `model` = provider's `model` param (default "general", yandex_speechkit.py:173/343).
- `errorCode` — added ONLY conditionally at line 243-244 when `result.errorCode` is truthy; NOT present on FINAL results.

stats counters dict (lines 247-254):
- `generation_stt: 1`
- `request_count: 1`
- `audio_duration_ms: audio.durationMs`
- `elapsed_time: elapsedSeconds`
- `is_error: 1 if result.status is STTResultStatus.ERROR else 0`
- `f"status_{result.status}": 1`

KEY GOTCHA: the `status_` stat key uses the StrEnum VALUE (lowercase), NOT `.name` — `STTResultStatus.FINAL = "final"`, `NO_SPEECH = "no-speech"`, `ERROR = "error"` (lib/stt/models.py:32-42). So the emitted key is `status_final` (never `status_FINAL`). The `status` label similarly carries the lowercase value.

Extension mechanism (how `_extraLabels` gets populated): `AbstractSTTProvider.__init__` (abstract.py:60-73) accepts `**extraKwargs` catch-all which is NEVER consumed to fill `_extraLabels`; it initializes `self._extraLabels: Dict[str, str] = {}` at line 72. Default `statsStorage` = `NullStatsStorage()` (no-op) when None (line 70). `YandexSpeechKitProvider.__init__` (yandex_speechkit.py:254-259) forwards kwargs built from `locals().copy()` (pops self/extraKwargs) to super(), then at line 343 sets `self._extraLabels["model"] = model`. So `_extraLabels` is only populated by concrete providers, not the base class.

title: Archival move convention: docs/design → docs/archive/design (2026-08-08)
content:
Convention for archiving implemented/superseded design docs (established 2026-08-08 when stt-next-steps.md was archived; re-verified 2026-08-20). Complements the earlier docs/plans → docs/design move convention.

**Archive structure:** `docs/archive/` has typed subdirs: `analysis/`, `design/`, `examples/`, `llm-sessions/`, `plans/`, `reports/`, `review/`. NOTE: only `design/` and `plans/` have a README.md index with "Recently Archived (date)" sections — analysis/, examples/, llm-sessions/, reports/, review/ have NO README (and analysis/ + examples/ are also missing from the top-level README's directory tree, a known open gap). Match the type: design/roadmap docs go to `docs/archive/design/`, implementation plans go to `docs/archive/plans/`.

**Procedure:**
1. Use `git mv` (never cp+rm) so history is preserved.
2. Add a one-line `> **ARCHIVED (YYYY-MM-DD):**` blockquote banner right after the title (matching the file's own existing `> **UPDATE (...))` blockquote style), stating why archived + linking the live authoritative docs with correct relative paths.
3. Add an entry to the archive subdir's README "Recently Archived (YYYY-MM-DD)" section + bump that README's "Last updated" footer date.
4. No CHANGELOG entry needed for pure doc relocation (exempt per docs/llm/changelog.md).

**Link-depth adjustments when moving docs/design/X.md → docs/archive/design/X.md (depth +1):**
- Repo-root relative links `../../` → `../../../` (targets: internal/, lib/, tests/, configs/, CHANGELOG.md, README.md, main.py, .agents/) — VERIFIED correct (stt-next-steps.md uses `../../../internal/...`).
- `../llm/` → `../../llm/` (2 levels up to docs/).
- Sibling links to docs that REMAIN in docs/design/: `](X.md)` → `](../../design/X.md)` — **TWO levels up, not one.** The originally recorded rule `](../design/X.md)` is WRONG: from docs/archive/design/, `../design/` resolves back into docs/archive/design/ itself. The 2026-08-08 archival applied the wrong rule: docs/archive/design/stt-next-steps.md's ARCHIVED banner links (`../design/stt-v1.1.md`, `../design/media-transcription-stt-v1.md`, `../design/lib-stt-v1.md`) are BROKEN and need fixing to `../../design/...` (compare docs/archive/design/README.md which uses the correct `../../design/` form). - Inbound refs: files in docs/design/ linking the moved doc change `./X.md` → `../archive/design/X.md`.
- Also bump the design count in the TOP-LEVEL docs/archive/README.md directory tree ("N archived docs + 1 README") — it was missed in the 2026-08-08 move (says 23, actual is 24).

title: AbstractSTTProvider full post-refactor surface: 3 abstract + 2 concrete members
content:
After the v1.1 template-method refactor (commit 561dd04), the complete `AbstractSTTProvider` surface in lib/stt/abstract.py is FIVE members — this is the canonical contract any new STT provider must satisfy (reconciled into docs/design/lib-stt-v1.md §8 on 2026-08-08):

CONCRETE on the base (never-raise):
- `stt(self, data, *, consumerId=None)` — high-level entry; wraps extractAudio + transcribe; STTExtractionError→its errorCode, Exception→PROVIDER_ERROR.
- `transcribe(self, audio, *, consumerId=None)` — template-method wrapper: time.monotonic() timing + best-effort `_recordStats` + `except Exception`→TranscriptionResult(ERROR, PROVIDER_ERROR); CancelledError propagates.

ABSTRACT (provider overrides these — the provider NEVER overrides `transcribe`/`stt`):
- `_transcribe(self, audio) -> TranscriptionResult` — the raw transcription override; returns TranscriptionResult, never raises for expected failures; does NOT take consumerId and does NOT record stats.
- `supportedInputFormats()`
- `aclose()`

A recurring doc-drift pattern: older docs claimed `stt`/`transcribe`/`aclose` were all abstract. The correct post-refactor claim is `stt` + `transcribe` concrete, `_transcribe` + `supportedInputFormats` + `aclose` abstract.

title: STT v1.1 `uri` Object-Storage body shape is a SIBLING to inline content in _buildSubmitBody
content:
YandexSpeechKitProvider._buildSubmitBody (lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py) emits the Object-Storage routing request body as: the `uri` field is a SIBLING to the inline `content` (base64) field — one or the other is present, and the `recognition_model` block is byte-for-byte identical in both branches. Routing threshold: `len(audio.data) >= max-inline-bytes` → use Object Storage (`uri`), else inline base64. The Object-Storage URI scheme is `https://storage.yandexcloud.net/{bucket}/{key}` (from lib/stt/providers/yandex_object_storage.py).

Error surfacing: `YandexObjectStorage.upload()` failures surface as `STTErrorCode.OBJECT_STORAGE_ERROR` (provider-owned); extracted ≥ inline threshold AND Object Storage disabled → `SOURCE_TOO_LARGE` (ownership extended in v1.1 to also be provider-surfaced, previously service-only). consumerId threading: `str(chatId)` → STTService.transcribeMedia → provider.stt(data, consumerId=…) → base transcribe → _recordStats.

title: tests/lib/stt/ test architecture patterns (close-tracking proxy, MockTransport lifecycle)
content:
The stt-lib-tests batch (8 files under tests/lib/stt/, ~5961 LOC, all 190 tests pass) established reusable test patterns for the lib/stt/ library:
- test_audio.py uses a close-tracking proxy `_TrackedContainer` wrapping real `av.open` results (via monkeypatching `audioMod.av.open`, NOT mocking PyAV) to verify every container opened during probe/passthrough/transcode gets closed on success AND every exception path. Asserts exact open counts (`len(opened) == 2` passthrough, `== 3` transcode) — tightly coupled to implementation call counts. PyAV source synthesis helpers build real WAV/FLAC/Opus bytes in-test (no binary blobs). Note: `audio.py` calls `av.open()` then explicit `.close()` (no context manager), so dunder methods don't need forwarding on the proxy.
- test_yandex_speechkit.py drives the full submit→poll→getRecognition→delete lifecycle via `httpx.MockTransport` (no real network, "golden-HTTP" style). Helpers `_provider`/`_providerWithOs` construct the real provider, `await aclose()`, then swap in a MockTransport client / mock object storage.
- test_abstract.py regression-tests the never-raise contract of `AbstractSTTProvider.stt` by monkeypatching `audio.extractAudio` (module attribute on `lib.stt.audio`, reached via `from . import audio` in abstract.py) with raising async stubs, plus a `_RaisingTranscribeProvider`.
- test_yandex_events.py covers the protobuf-JSON event parser: int64-as-int coercion, non-finite timestamps (`"inf"`, `"1e400"`, `"nan"`) → PROTOCOL_ERROR, top-alternative-only selection, `DEFAULT_MAX_RESULT_BYTES == 5_242_880`.
Fixture/shape notes: no `@pytest.mark.asyncio` decorators (asyncio_mode=auto); no `python`/`python3` invocation strings in docstrings; camelCase test names verified clean.

title: ReplayTransport per-signature advancing cursor (STT polling lifecycle fix)
content:
lib/aurumentation/transports.py `ReplayTransport` now uses a per-signature ADVANCING CURSOR instead of first-match-wins. The old behavior had `call_index` as dead code — two recordings sharing a request signature made the second unreachable, so replaying STT's polling lifecycle (submit → poll done:false → poll done:true → getRecognition → delete) would return done:false forever.

Mechanism: on each `handle_async_request`, compute `matchingIndices` = indices of all recordings matching the incoming request signature (method/URL/params/body; headers excluded), use `matchKey = tuple(matchingIndices)` as a dict key into `_matchCursors`, return `recordings[matchingIndices[cursor]]`, increment cursor. Raises `ValueError` when cursor >= len(matchingIndices) (more requests than recordings for that signature).

Design properties:
- Single-match signatures are unaffected → backward-compatible with all 5 existing golden suites (openweathermap, yandex_search, geocode_maps, ai, divination), each of which records each signature at most once AND issues it exactly once. Verified: 26/26 golden tests pass across all suites.
- Two DIFFERENT request signatures matching the SAME recording set (possible only with wildcard `***MASKED***` matching) would share a matchKey → false exhaustion raise. Not possible with exact matching.
- Not concurrency-safe: read-increment-write of the cursor is not atomic; two coroutines issuing the same signature concurrently could double-serve index 0 and skip a recording. Assumes sequential request issuance per signature (STT polling loop is sequential, so fine today).
- O(n) scan over all recordings per request to rebuild matchingIndices; trivial for current 5-recording fixtures.

Body-match nuance that makes this work: the submit POST body must be byte-identical between record and replay; the recorded fixture body is compact JSON (`{"content":"...` no spaces), so httpx serializes the re-built `_buildSubmitBody` dict deterministically (insertion order + same pinned httpx version). Base64 cannot contain the literal `***MASKED***` substring (alphabet is A-Za-z0-9+/=, no `*`), so the exact-match path is always taken for the submit body.

title: Golden test suites sanction Dict[str, Any] for JSON scenario/fixture dicts
content: Confirmed convention: golden test suites (divination, STT, openweathermap, etc.) use `Dict[str, Any]` (also `List[Dict[str, Any]]`) for scenario/fixture dicts loaded from JSON — e.g. `_loadScenarios() -> List[Dict[str, Any]]`, `parsedBody: Dict[str, Any] = json.loads(bodyStr)`, `initKwargs: Dict[str, Any]`. This is the sanctioned exception to the AGENTS.md "No Any" rule: JSON-loaded scenario/fixture containers are "generic containers" and `Any` is acceptable there. Established precedent is `tests/lib/divination/golden/test_golden.py` (uses it extensively); the STT golden suite follows the same pattern. Pyright passes with this. Note this coexists with the other convention that `dict[str, object]` is the canonical Any-free replacement for heterogeneous config dicts — the golden suites predate/coexist with that preference, so match the surrounding file's style when editing them.

title: collectGoldenData double-resolves secrets; golden collect.py works via fallback path
content: Non-obvious quirk in the aurumentation collector contract: `collectGoldenData(secrets=...)` in lib/aurumentation/collector.py expects `secrets` to be a list of ENV-VAR NAMES — it calls `os.getenv(name)` on each and appends the resolved value (falling back to appending the literal if the env var doesn't exist). But every golden `collect.py` (STT, divination, openweathermap, etc.) pre-resolves names to literal VALUES via its own `collectSecrets()` helper before passing them in. So the framework re-attempts `os.getenv(literalSecretValue)` → returns None → falls back to appending the literal. It works only by accident through the fallback path. Fragile if a secret value ever happens to collide with an env-var name. This is the established (sanctioned) pattern across all golden suites — mirror it rather than "fixing" one collector, and never pass raw names directly expecting values to be masked (masking happens inside the recorder via the resolved values).

title: lib.stt.abstract imports audio → AbstractSTTProvider transitively requires PyAV
content:
Code review observation (stt-lib batch): `lib/stt/abstract.py` does `from . import audio` at module top level (used only by the convenience `stt()` template method, which calls `audio.extractAudio`). Because `lib/stt/audio.py` does a hard unconditional `import av`, importing `lib.stt.abstract` — i.e. subclassing `AbstractSTTProvider` — pulls PyAV into the process.

This is distinct from (and complements) the existing memory "Keep STT service import PyAV-free when disabled" (which is about the internal/services startup graph staying provider/PyAV-neutral). At the lib layer, the abstract base class is NOT PyAV-free; a hypothetical provider-only consumer that never needs audio extraction still drags in av. Per the simplify refactor PyAV is now a hard dependency, so this is accepted behavior, but it is a leaky abstraction worth knowing: the abstract interface cannot be imported without PyAV installed, and `lib.stt.__init__` re-exports both anyway. Import-inside-method would fix it but violates the AGENTS.md no-imports-inside-methods rule, so the current design is the convention-compliant one.

title: lib/stt batch: asyncio.CancelledError correctly propagates — verified across all files
content:
Code review verification (stt-lib batch, HEAD c88dafb): every `except Exception` clause in lib/stt correctly lets `asyncio.CancelledError` propagate (it is a BaseException, not Exception). Specifically verified in:

- `abstract.py` transcribe() (line ~126), stt() (~195), _recordStats() (~258)
- `yandex_speechkit.py` _transcribe() (~442), _bestEffortDelete() (~703), _bestEffortDeleteObject() (~742)
- `audio.py` container cleanup in finally blocks (inContainer/outContainer both closed on every path including non-FFmpegError exceptions)

This is the load-bearing never-raise boundary discipline from docs/design/lib-stt-v1.md §4/§5 — confirmed clean with 0 violations. Notable subtlety in `yandex_speechkit.py._transcribe`: `result: TranscriptionResult` is declared annotation-only and assigned in every except branch; on the success path it is assigned right after the try/finally (in the `if not operationFailed` block) before any use, and CancelledError in the try means the finally's best-effort deletes run but the method never reaches the `result` use — so no unbound-variable risk, though the annotation-only declaration is fragile if code is inserted between finally and the parse block.

title: STT provider _recordStats double-logs errors (logger.error + logger.exception)
content:
Minor code-quality finding in lib/stt/abstract.py `_recordStats` (and the pattern is discouraged for new code):

```python
except Exception:
    logger.error("Failed to record STT stats")
    logger.exception("STT stats recording failure")
```

`logger.exception` already logs at ERROR level WITH the traceback; the preceding `logger.error` produces a second, traceback-less ERROR entry for the same failure. Redundant. Use only `logger.exception(...)` (one call).

Same review also flagged other small nits in the stt-lib batch: unused module `logger` in lib/stt/providers/yandex_object_storage.py (defined at line 38 via `logging.getLogger` but never referenced — `import logging` + logger can be dropped); `_iterJsonObjects` in yandex_events.py returns `List[object]` though elements are always dicts (callers narrow via `_resolveEnvelope`); `sum([frame.samples for ...])` in audio.py builds an intermediate list (use a generator expression); `is` is used for StrEnum comparisons (works — members are singletons — but `==` is more conventional).

title: STT parent design doc (media-transcription-stt-v1.md) has stale stateful-design sections — trust lib-stt-v1.md for current shape
content:
A docs review (2026-08-08, stt-docs batch) found that `docs/design/media-transcription-stt-v1.md` (the parent v1 plan with D1–D8 decisions) was only PARTIALLY updated for the 2026-08-02 stateless STT simplification and v1.1. It got "Design pivot/simplification" callout notes in §6.2, §8.3, §12.4 but several implementation sections still describe the REMOVED stateful design and features that no longer exist in code:

- §5.1: describes STTService with "keyed in-flight task registry" and "DB status transitions" — the stateless STTService owns neither.
- §5.2: references `dispatchTranscription(request, chatGateEnabled)` — this method does not exist; actual entry is `transcribeMedia(data, *, chatId)` (chatId keyword-only).
- §6.3: in-process dedup `dict[str, STTInFlight]` with asyncio.Future status-ready signaling — removed.
- §8.1: product-limit table rows for `max-audio-bytes` (20 MiB decoded buffer), decoded-duration 600s stop-at-cap, 48,000-char transcript cap, 20s admission wait — ALL four caps/config keys were deleted (`max-audio-bytes`, `max-transcript-chars`, `admission-timeout`, `max-duration-seconds` are not in stt.toml); admission is unbounded, decoded PCM is unbounded, formatter does no truncation.
- §8.2: `STTMediaRequest.declaredSize` rejection and 20-second admission budget — STTMediaRequest was removed; service takes raw bytes.
- §8.4: `DurationExceededError` inside extractAudio — deleted (exception taxonomy has only NoAudioTrackError/AudioDecodeError/EncoderError).
- §6.2 state-table outcome rows: "Formatted, escaped, bounded transcript" and `[No speech detected]` sentinel — thin formatter does no escaping/bounding and returns "" for NO_SPEECH (no sentinel).
- §6.2 terminal-write: "update-plus-reread verified, at most three attempts with backoff" — the old CAS retry; current handler uses plain updateMediaAttachment (no retry loop).

AUDIENCE GUIDANCE: for the current STT design consult `docs/design/lib-stt-v1.md` (declared single source for lib/stt internals), `docs/design/stt-v1.1.md`, `docs/llm/services.md`, and `architecture.md` ADR-020. Do not cite the stale parent-doc sections above as authoritative; they were flagged for callout-note fixes but had not been corrected as of this review.

title: STT release-gate numbering: stt-v1.1 "gate-3"/"gate-4" are shorthand for parent §13.3 gates, not new gates
content: STT release-gate naming across the three design docs can confuse: `docs/design/media-transcription-stt-v1.md` §13.3 defines the manual release gates gate-1..gate-9 (gate-1 live-wire getRecognition framing ✅ PASS 2026-08-02; gate-2 model confirmation general vs deferred-general; gate-3 inline-limit semantics; gate-4 10-min end-to-end latency; ... through gate-9). `docs/design/stt-v1.1.md` §3/§4/§5 use "gate-3" and "gate-4" in section headings as SHORTHAND for the parent §13.3 gates, not as v1.1-specific new gate numbers: Enhancement 1 (gate-3) = Object-Storage routing for clips over the inline threshold; Enhancement 2 (gate-4) = statistics recording in lib/stt. v1.1 §8 "Release-gate scope" clarifies this mapping explicitly. lib-stt-v1.md §10 cross-refs parent gate-1/gate-4/gate-5 and they resolve correctly.

title: Status confirmed 2026-08-08: lib/stt Phase 3 audio.py bugs all fixed; toYandexSpeechKit converter HAS unit tests
content:
Status verifications made during the stt-lib-core code review (2026-08-08), correcting/updating earlier assumptions:

1. All 5 previously-flagged lib/stt/audio.py Phase 3 bugs (earlier memory 9d6641e1) are FIXED in current code:
   - `_probe` inner try now catches `av.error.FFmpegError` → raises AudioDecodeError (no untyped leak).
   - Muxer finalization (`outContainer.close()`) is wrapped in try/except capturing FFmpegError → re-raised as EncoderError.
   - `_layoutForChannels` raises EncoderError for channels > 2 (no invalid layout names).
   - `_mapContainerType` takes formatName + codecName and checks `codecName.lower() == "opus"` for OGG mapping.

2. `STTAudioContainerType.toYandexSpeechKit()` IS unit-tested in tests/lib/stt/test_models.py (line ~93 asserts the wire-label mapping; a bogus-value test with `# type: ignore[arg-type]` at line ~108 verifies the ValueError path). Earlier memory claiming "no dedicated unit test for the converter exists yet" is STALE — tests were added after that note.

3. Full lint pipeline green on the batch: flake8, isort --check-only, `import main` circular-import check, pyright all pass (0 errors, 0 warnings). 35 tests pass in tests/lib/stt/test_audio.py + test_abstract.py.

Reference: the abstract.py top-level `from . import audio` means subclassing AbstractSTTProvider unconditionally pulls in PyAV — documented as accepted trade-off (a3f2e348) given the no-imports-inside-methods rule.

title: YandexSpeechKitProvider _pollDelay/_retryDelay float overflow for attempt >= 1024
content: Latent edge in lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py (~lines 758 and 778): `_pollDelay` and `_retryDelay` compute `pollIntervalSeconds * (2**attempt)` (float * int). Python converts the huge int to float for the multiply; for `attempt >= 1024` (i.e. config `maxPolls` or `maxRetries` > 1024) `float(2**1024)` overflows and raises OverflowError. Unrealistic config, and it is caught by the defense-in-depth `except Exception` in `_transcribe` → mapped to PROVIDER_ERROR (never-raise contract holds), but it's a genuine latent bug. Cleaner shape: cap `attempt` before the multiply or apply `min(...)` to the multiplier. Flagged in code review at HEAD c88dafb.

title: Yandex event parser strictness asymmetry: _applyRefinement lenient on text, _extractWords strict on words
content:
In lib/stt/providers/yandex_events.py, the never-raise streaming parser is asymmetric in validation strictness:
- `_extractFinal`: a non-string `text` raises ValueError → poisons the whole stream → PROTOCOL_ERROR.
- `_applyRefinement`: a non-string `normalizedText` FALLS BACK to `raw.text` (lenient, deliberate — avoids poisoning the stream from a refinement).
- `_extractWords` (called from BOTH paths): a non-list `words` raises ValueError.

Net effect: a malformed refinement `text` is tolerated, but a malformed refinement `words` is fatal. Each choice is individually documented, but the asymmetry is surprising and easy to regress. Flagged in code review at HEAD c88dafb — recommend an inline comment in `_applyRefinement` noting the deliberate asymmetry, or making the two paths consistent.

title: _coerceInt accepts Python underscored numeric strings (e.g. "1_000" -> 1000)
content: Parser quirk in lib/stt/providers/yandex_events.py `_coerceInt` (~line 444): because `int("1_000")` is valid Python (underscores allowed in int literals since 3.6), a string like `"1_000"` from a protobuf-JSON field silently coerces to 1000 instead of being rejected as malformed. Unlikely from real Yandex SpeechKit responses, and it doesn't break the never-raise contract, but it's a minor surprise for a parser whose whole purpose is robust validation of adversarial/malformed input. Noted as a nitpick in code review at HEAD c88dafb. Related existing memories on _coerceInt: string-encoded timestamps (0db67e9d) and int64 range validation (9e5c1d73).

title: YandexSpeechKitProvider cleanup (delete operation/object) runs in finally OUTSIDE the asyncio.timeout budget
content:
Design detail of `YandexSpeechKitProvider._transcribe` (lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py ~424-454), verified in code review at HEAD c88dafb: the cleanup awaits — `_bestEffortDelete(operationId)` and `_bestEffortDeleteObject(objectUri)` — run in the `finally` block, which sits OUTSIDE the `async with asyncio.timeout(self._operationBudgetSeconds)` context. Consequences:
1. Cleanup is NOT bounded by the operation budget — it is bounded only by transport timeouts (httpx `requestTimeoutSeconds` and boto3 `read_timeout=30`).
2. Both deletes wrap in `except Exception` (never raise, log warning) — so the finally never raises; `asyncio.CancelledError` still propagates correctly through them.
3. Inline (non-Object-Storage) path: `objectUri` stays None, no delete attempted. Early-return paths (e.g. upload failure → OBJECT_STORAGE_ERROR at ~line 417, or SOURCE_TOO_LARGE) happen BEFORE the try block, so their `finally` never runs — a `put_object` that partially succeeded then raised can orphan an object (rare edge, documented as acceptable).
4. On the operation-failure path `operationId` may be None (submit raised), so delete is skipped; if submit succeeded, cleanup runs.

This unbudgeted-cleanup behavior is intentional and was confirmed correct; do not "fix" it by moving cleanup inside the timeout.

title: Any-type split: lib/stt avoids Any but service and tests use Dict[str, Any] / Optional[Any]
content: Current `Any` usage split in the STT feature (verified 2026-08-21): `lib/stt/` itself avoids `Any`. `internal/services/stt/service.py:184-187` uses `Dict[str, Any]` for sttConfig — acceptable and explicitly commented as mirroring `ConfigManager.getSttConfig() -> Dict[str, Any]` ("generic container" exception). Golden test suites sanction `Dict[str, Any]` / `List[Dict[str, Any]]` for JSON-loaded scenario/fixture dicts (tests/lib/stt/golden/test_golden.py throughout — established precedent from tests/lib/divination/golden). The previously-flagged `Optional[Any]` for eventTime in tests/lib/stt/providers/test_yandex_speechkit.py was FIXED to `Optional[datetime]` (line ~1750).

title: STT service-owned config keys now excluded from provider kwargs (leak fixed)
content: FIXED (2026-08-08): STTService.initialize in internal/services/stt/service.py (~line 209-213) previously forwarded ALL `[stt]` TOML keys to the provider constructor via **extraKwargs, silently leaking service-owned keys. The provider-kwargs exclusion set now includes: ("enabled", "use-proxy", "proxy-config", "provider", "max-source-bytes", "chat-ratelimiter-queue", "global-ratelimiter-queue", "max-concurrency"). No functional change (YandexSpeechKitProvider accepted **extraKwargs and silently dropped them; the service consumed those four values itself for the semaphore/maxSourceBytes/limiter queues), but the exclusion is now explicit at the source. Covered by test test_enabledValidForwardsAllProviderKwargs.

title: STTService._mapOutcome ERROR path: None errorCode falls back to PROVIDER_ERROR
content: FIXED (2026-08-08): `STTService._mapOutcome` (internal/services/stt/service.py, ~line 332-333) ERROR mapping now uses `errorCode=result.errorCode or STTErrorCode.PROVIDER_ERROR`. `TranscriptionResult.errorCode` is `Optional[STTErrorCode]` (lib/stt/models.py), so a None error code previously produced an STTOutcome carrying a None code. The fallback guarantees a concrete STTErrorCode on the FAILED outcome. Note PROVIDER_ERROR is already the established service-layer catch-all fallback (see related gotcha about it losing diagnostic precision).

title: git stash as verification tool collides with concurrent sessions — selective checkout recovery
content:
Incident (2026-08-08, branch add-audio-transcribation-v2): while verifying that pyright errors in `lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py` were pre-existing, the agent ran `git stash push -- tests/` to isolate its own test changes, then `git stash pop` after the pyright run. The pop was REFUSED: a concurrent opencode session was live in the same repo and had modified `tests/lib/stt/golden/test_golden.py` during the stash window, so the stash's copy of that file conflicted with the newer working-tree version. The failed pop left the working tree's copies of the three intended files reverted to HEAD while the stash retained them.

Recovery that worked: `git checkout stash@{0} -- <only my three files>` (restores exactly the files you need from the stash, leaving concurrent-session files untouched), then `git stash drop stash@{0}`. Verify afterwards with grep/diff that the intended edits are present and the diff is limited to the permitted files.

Lessons: (1) `git stash push/pop` is a dangerous way to answer "are these errors pre-existing?" when other sessions actively edit the same dirty tree — use `git diff` against HEAD instead. (2) A failed `git stash pop` silently reverts the stashed paths to HEAD in the working tree while keeping the stash; the working tree can then look like your work vanished. (3) When recovering from a stash that contains files you don't own (concurrent session's files), restore selectively with `git checkout <stash> -- <paths>` rather than popping the whole stash.

title: STT transcribeMedia admission gates: STT_DISABLED checked before SOURCE_TOO_LARGE (now test-locked)
content:
In `STTService.transcribeMedia` (internal/services/stt/service.py, ~lines 289-292) the two admission early-returns are ordered: `if not self._enabled: return STT_DISABLED` is checked FIRST, and only then `if len(data) > self._maxSourceBytes: return SOURCE_TOO_LARGE`. Because of this ordering, a disabled service returns STT_DISABLED even for oversized data.

This was untested until 2026-08-08, when `TestAdmissionEarlyReturns` was added to tests/services/stt/test_transcribe.py (per R10):
- `test_sourceTooLargeReturnsEarly`: 2048 bytes of b"\x00" vs `maxSourceBytes=1024` → errorCode STTErrorCode.SOURCE_TOO_LARGE, provider never called (assert provider.sttCallCount == 0).
- `test_disabledReturnsEarly`: builds service via `_buildService(provider=...)` (which sets `_enabled=True`) then flips `svc._enabled = False` in the test → errorCode STTErrorCode.STT_DISABLED, provider never called. Uses SMALL data (64 bytes) so the size check cannot trip — keeps the disabled path isolated.

Test-infra notes: `_buildService` helper in that file accepts `provider` and `maxSourceBytes` kwargs; `FakeProvider` exposes `sttCallCount`. Both early returns assert the provider is not invoked. The module docstring of test_transcribe.py now lists "admission early returns (STT_DISABLED, SOURCE_TOO_LARGE)" as a covered area.

title: Parallel edit-tool calls to the SAME file clobber each other silently
content:
In this environment, issuing multiple `edit` tool calls against the SAME file in a single parallel tool block is unsafe: only the LAST edit survives, the rest are silently lost even though every call reports "Edit applied successfully." Confirmed 2026-08-08 on tests/lib/stt/golden/test_golden.py — 5 of 6 parallel edits vanished (module docstring, _recoverAudioBytesFromFixture docstring, skip message lost; later ones in the same block survived).

Rule: apply edits to the same file SEQUENTIALLY (one edit call per turn, wait for completion). Edits to DIFFERENT files can still be parallelized safely. Always re-verify with grep after batched same-file edits.

title: STT golden fixtures: clips are committed synthetic samples; orphaned sample_ru.mp3 removed
content:
Resolved the earlier "orphaned sample_ru.mp3" flag (2026-08-08): tests/lib/stt/golden/input/ audio clips (sample_en.ogg, sample_ru.ogg) ARE committed TTS-generated synthetic samples, NOT gitignored (verified: `git check-ignore` matches nothing; all clips tracked in git). Old README/docstrings claiming they were `.gitignore`'d/never committed were corrected across test_golden.py, collect.py, scenario_runner.py, README.md. The orphaned tests/lib/stt/golden/input/sample_ru.mp3 (committed but unreferenced — scenarios.json only uses sample_ru.ogg + sample_en.ogg) was removed via `git rm`.

Design that makes replay self-contained: the `data/*.json` golden fixtures embed the audio bytes as base64 in the recorded `recognizeFileAsync` POST body's `content` field (not secret-masked, since base64 can't contain the API-key substring); replay recovers the exact submitted bytes from the fixture and never reads the clip on disk — so clips are only needed for RECORDING (via collect.py).

title: R1 fix implemented: _chooseTranscodeTarget returns AudioFormatSpec; spec validation placed AFTER containers open
content:
lib/stt/audio.py transcode path (current, verified):
- `_chooseTranscodeTarget(formats) -> Optional[AudioFormatSpec]` (audio.py:537) returns the FULL AudioFormatSpec (the first compressed entry), not just the container — so the transcode path honors the provider's declared channel/sample-rate limits.
- `_transcode(sourceBytes, probe, target: AudioFormatSpec)` CLAMPS the source to the spec rather than rejecting out-of-range sources: `outChannels` is clamped into `[max(target.minChannels,1), target.maxChannels]` (audio.py:305-307, downmix when too many / upmix when too few) and the output rate is clamped into `[minSampleRate, maxSampleRate]` for non-Opus targets (Opus always uses the native 48 kHz) — implemented via `av.AudioResampler`, instantiated only when a conversion is actually needed (zero-overhead passthrough for in-spec sources).
- EncoderError is raised only for failures the codec physically cannot satisfy: `_layoutForChannels` raises for channels not positive or > 2 (opus/mp3 physical limit, audio.py:580-586), plus encode/muxer/flush failures and 'no compressed transcode target available'.
- Muxer finalization (`outContainer.close()`) is wrapped: FFmpegError → EncoderError, with the container reference cleared so `finally` does not double-close.

NOTE: this supersedes the earlier R1 design where out-of-spec source channels/rates raised EncoderError — the implemented behavior deliberately downmixes/resamples instead (tests: testMultiChannelSourceDownmixesToMaxChannelsThroughTranscode, testRateClampsHighToMaxSampleRateThroughTranscode, testRateClampsLowToMinSampleRateThroughTranscode, testYandexForceMonoDownmixesSupportedStereoSources in tests/lib/stt/test_audio.py; the old testMultiChannelSourceRaisesEncoderErrorAndClosesContainers is gone).

The `user_memories` table (migration_020) still has NO stored score column — a memory's score exists only as a query-time cosine-similarity value. `SingleMemoryDict.score` (internal/bot/models/message_metadata.py:33-41, NotRequired[float]) is "Cosine similarity (0.0–1.0) when this entry came back from a semantic searchMemories query; absent on non-search reads" (getLatestMemories returns score 0.0).

title: Read tool returns stale pre-edit snapshots after successful edits — verify with grep, not read
content:
New tool-reliability variant observed 2026-08-08: the `read` tool can return a STALE pre-edit snapshot of a file even AFTER edits to it have been applied successfully. Happened twice in one session on lib/stt/audio.py and lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py — read showed the OLD `_transcode` signature / OLD unindented docstring (line 749) content, while `grep`/`git`/`black`/`ast.parse` against the actual disk showed the NEW content. This produced a phantom "black cannot parse yandex_speechkit.py:749:4" failure that vanished on re-run and a phantom "read shows old content" scare.

Fix/verification pattern: when `read` output contradicts grep or tool outputs, trust grep + re-running the failing tool, not the read snapshot. Also: a black failure on a file you did NOT touch should be re-checked by re-running black on just that file before assuming a real problem. Related prior variants: edit-tool silent loss (b16a7a81), parallel same-file edit clobbering (3318ad03), read truncation hiding misses (be7e993e).

title: Concurrent session editing yandex_speechkit.py / yandex_events.py / object_storage.py + their tests on add-audio-transcribation-v2
content:
Confirmed concurrent-process hazard on branch add-audio-transcribation-v2 (2026-08-08). While editing lib/stt core files, a second process was concurrently modifying the working tree: `lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py`, `lib/stt/providers/yandex_events.py`, `lib/stt/providers/yandex_object_storage.py`, and `tests/lib/stt/providers/test_yandex_speechkit.py`. Transient flake8 errors appeared (F401 `datetime` unused at test_yandex_speechkit.py:35, F821 `Any` undefined at ~1566) during one `make lint` run, then resolved on their own in a later run (HEAD version of the test file is clean). git status also showed `lib/aurumentation/transports.py`, `internal/services/stt/service.py`, `internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py`, and docs modified — likely a companion session.

Practical implications: (1) when `make lint` fails on files you didn't touch, check `git stash push -- <file>` / `git diff` to determine if it's a concurrent editor's uncommitted change before "fixing" it; (2) the test file edits may be merged at any time, so re-run quality gates just before final verification; (3) a file with working-tree-only modifications can pass ast.parse yet still break the repo's toolchain if a concurrent writer is mid-write — re-run rather than chase. Relates to prior memory d9fd48cd (multiple concurrent opencode sessions clobber files).

title: Muxer close double-close fix: outContainer = None moved into finally (R4)
content:
R4 fix in lib/stt/audio.py `_transcode` muxer-finalize block (2026-08-08): previously `outContainer = None` was set only after `outContainer.close()` succeeded or raised an `av.error.FFmpegError`. If `close()` raised a NON-FFmpegError, the reference stayed set and the outer `finally` would double-close a half-finalized container. Fix: moved `outContainer = None` into a `finally` clause of the inner close-try, so the reference is cleared unconditionally (success, FFmpegError, or any unexpected exception):

```python
muxerFinalizeError: Optional[av.error.FFmpegError] = None
try:
    outContainer.close()
except av.error.FFmpegError as exc:
    muxerFinalizeError = exc
finally:
    outContainer = None   # unconditional — outer finally never double-closes
if muxerFinalizeError is not None:
    raise EncoderError(...) from muxerFinalizeError
```

Pattern to reuse anywhere a container/resource is closed with error capture: clear the reference in `finally`, not after the try. Related prior note 1be60c3c (generic output finalization failures need STT mapping) — that gap remains open (a non-FFmpegError from close() still propagates raw to the caller, it just no longer double-closes).

title: STT design docs reconciled with stateless simplification (2026-08-08) — canonical current shape

Canonical current STT shape as verified 2026-08-20 (post 2026-08-02 stateless simplification + 2026-08-09 attribution/force-mono rounds + v1.1). Do NOT re-flag the reconciled items below as stale:

- STTService is stateless (internal/services/stt/service.py): no in-flight registry, no DB interaction, no dispatchTranscription(). Entry point `transcribeMedia(data, *, chatId)` (raw bytes + chatId kwarg); never-raise pipeline STT_DISABLED → SOURCE_TOO_LARGE (`len(data) > maxSourceBytes`, post-download) → rate limiters → semaphore (NO timeout) → provider → _mapOutcome. The handler owns the media-row lifecycle; dedup is by per-file_unique_id DB row.
- Removed config keys: max-audio-bytes, max-duration-seconds, max-transcript-chars, admission-timeout. Renamed to *-seconds: request-timeout-seconds, operation-budget-seconds, poll-interval-seconds, max-poll-interval-seconds. NO_SPEECH returns "" (no sentinel), no truncation, no XML escaping. Mono finals request Yandex speaker labeling; labels are opaque and recording-local.

title: Transient black/flake8 failures during concurrent WIP edits on add-audio-transcribation-v2
content:
During the docs-only fix session (2026-08-08, branch add-audio-transcribation-v2, which carries ~14+ files of uncommitted STT WIP), `make format` and `make lint` each failed transiently on files NOT touched by the session and NOT part of the permitted edit set:

1. `make format` → black "Cannot parse for target version Python 3.12: 749:4" on `lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py`. Direct `./venv/bin/black --check --target-version py312 <file>` passed immediately after, and the next `make format` run succeeded ("532 files left unchanged"). Non-reproducible.
2. `make lint` → flake8 F401 ('datetime.datetime' unused) at tests/lib/stt/providers/test_yandex_speechkit.py:35 and F821 (undefined 'Any') at :1566. These later resolved by themselves mid-session.

Root cause: a concurrent opencode session was actively editing the same dirty working tree (`.opencode/memory.jsonl` kept growing; modified-file set grew from 18 to 30 files during the session — new files appeared like docs/design/media-transcription-stt-v1.md, tests/services/stt/*). Verification at clean HEAD (git stash whole tree, run `make lint`, pop stash) passed 100%, proving the failures were not caused by the docs edits.

Lessons for this environment: (1) when `make format`/`make lint` fails on a file you didn't touch, first re-run — transient failures from mid-write concurrent edits are common here and vanish on retry; (2) verify reproducibility by running the tool directly on the single file; (3) if the failure persists, prove it pre-exists via a clean-HEAD lint run rather than assuming your change caused it; (4) do NOT "fix" files outside your permitted edit scope even when lint is red — the concurrent session will resolve its own WIP.

title: YandexObjectStorage __slots__ breaks test monkeypatching methods — use patch.object at class level
content:
N5 applied (2026-08-08): `YandexObjectStorage` (lib/stt/providers/yandex_object_storage.py) now declares `__slots__ = ("_client", "_bucket", "_prefix", "_endpointUrl", "_regionName")`.

Gotcha: this immediately broke the pre-existing test `testAcloseClosesObjectStorageHelper` (tests/lib/stt/providers/test_yandex_speechkit.py), which monkeypatched `provider._objectStorage.aclose = mockAclose`. With `__slots__` and no `__dict__`, assigning an instance attribute to shadow a method raises `AttributeError: 'YandexObjectStorage' object attribute 'aclose' is read-only`.

You CANNOT fix it by adding `aclose` to `__slots__`: the method definition in the class body conflicts with the slot name, raising `ValueError: 'aclose' in __slots__ conflicts with class variable` at class-creation time.

Resolution: keep `__slots__` exactly as specified and change the test to `with patch.object(YandexObjectStorage, "aclose", mockAclose):` — class-level patch.object works because classes have `__dict__`; the provider's `await self._objectStorage.aclose()` still hits the patched method. Behavior-preserving.

Adjacent facts:
- Monkeypatching instance attributes WORKS when the name is in the slots tuple: `os._client = mockS3Client` in tests/lib/stt/providers/test_yandex_object_storage.py:63 still functions because `_client` is a declared slot.
- `_endpointUrl` and `_regionName` are in the slots tuple but are NOT set as instance attributes in `__init__` (they're module-level constants); listing them is a harmless reservation per the explicit N5 spec.

General rule for this repo: with `__slots__` classes, tests must patch methods via `patch.object(Class, "method", ...)`, not via instance-attribute assignment.

title: YandexSpeechKitProvider language param is single str only; _language stays Sequence[str] for submit body

title: YandexSpeechKitProvider __init__: explicit proxyConfig/statsStorage replace locals().copy() passthrough
content:
I3/N4 applied (2026-08-08): `YandexSpeechKitProvider.__init__` (lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py) now declares `proxyConfig: Optional[ProxyConfig] = None` and `statsStorage: Optional[StatsStorage] = None` as explicit keyword params (before `**extraKwargs`), with imports `from lib.proxy import ProxyConfig, ProxyKwargs` and `from lib.stats import StatsStorage` (same import path abstract.py uses).

The old `kwargs = locals().copy()` → pop `self`/`extraKwargs` → `kwargs.update(extraKwargs)` → `super().__init__(**kwargs)` dance is fully replaced by the single call `super().__init__(proxyConfig=proxyConfig, statsStorage=statsStorage)`.

Net behavior unchanged: `AbstractSTTProvider.__init__` only accepts `proxyConfig`, `statsStorage`, and `**extraKwargs`, so the remaining `**extraKwargs` were always silently swallowed anyway. This completes the earlier locals()/bare-super bugfix (see memory 2461ae0d).

title: FIXED: SpeechKit _pollDelay/_retryDelay exponent capped with min(attempt, 100)
content:
N7 fix applied (2026-08-08): the latent `2 ** attempt` float overflow in `YandexSpeechKitProvider._pollDelay` / `_retryDelay` (lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py, previously ~lines 758/778) is now fixed. Both methods compute the delay as `pollIntervalSeconds * (2 ** min(attempt, 100))` / `retryBackoffSeconds * (2 ** min(attempt, 100))` (still capped at `maxPollIntervalSeconds`), and their docstrings note the cap.

Root cause recap (see also memory da108c09): `float * int` forces `int(2**attempt)` → float conversion; for attempt >= 1024 the int is too large and Python raises `OverflowError: int too large to convert to float`. With the cap, `2**100` ≈ 1.27e30 stays safely within float range. Cap is unreachable in practice (maxPolls/maxRetries defaults ≤ 100) but protects against pathological config values.

title: Concurrent session ROTATED/DROPPED stash refs entirely — orphaned-stash recovery via git fsck + git stash apply
content:
Incident (2026-08-08, branch add-audio-transcribation-v2, repo gromozeka): escalated version of the concurrent-session stash collision (complements memory 9730cdb0). The agent ran `git stash && pytest ...; git stash pop` to verify pyright/pytest errors were pre-existing. This time the failure was WORSE than a refused pop:

- A concurrent opencode session (same branch, actively editing the STT WIP) was mutating the repo between the agent's bash calls: the working tree went from dirty (21 files) → clean at HEAD → dirty again (32 files, including NEW files not in the original stash: TODO.md, docs/design/*, tests/lib/stt/test_audio.py).
- The agent's stash (holding ALL its work, 25 files incl. transports.py edits) was dropped/rotated out of `refs/stash` — `git stash list`/reflog no longer showed it, replaced by older stash entries (db-refactoring, weather-add-ratelimiter, master). The stash ref is NOT safe storage under concurrent sessions.
- Recovery that worked: `git fsck --unreachable --no-reflogs` to list orphaned commits, filter for stash commits via message pattern "WIP on add-audio-transcribation-v2: c88dafb" (= current HEAD message), then identify the right one by `git diff <candidate> -- lib/aurumentation/transports.py` / grep for known edit markers (logger.debug, asyncio.Lock, byte-exact) — `5ac2f74f` matched the intended 25-file state. Restore via `git stash apply <hash>`; if the tree is dirty again, that fails too — fall back to file-level backup (cp to /tmp) and verify `git diff <stash> -- <file>` is empty (= identical).
- Investigative confusion to avoid: `git stash show -p` (tracked only) vs `git stash show --include-untracked --stat` (untracked included) show DIFFERENT file sets for the same stash entry; plain `-p` can miss files. Also `/tmp` patch dumps from earlier stashes (older branches) pollute comparisons.

LESSON (reinforces 9730cdb0, now escalated): do NOT use `git stash` at all in this repo while parallel sessions may be live — even a successful stash+pop sequence can lose work when another actor rotates refs/stash or resets the tree. Answer "is this error pre-existing?" with read-only `git diff HEAD` / pyright on specific files, and keep a file-level /tmp backup of any edited file. If work is lost, the object DB is the safety net (`git fsck --unreachable --no-reflogs` + apply), but refs/stash itself cannot be trusted.

title: lib/aurumentation transport confirmed characteristics: O(n) matching, non-concurrency-safe cursors, byte-exact body
content:
Confirmed operational characteristics of `lib/aurumentation/transports.py` (verified 2026-08-08 during the R15/R16/R17 review pass; the notes are now also in docstrings). Complements memory 3a1df062 (matching by method/URL/params/body, headers ignored):

1. **`handle_async_request` matching is O(n)** — a linear scan over ALL recordings plus a tuple allocation per request (recordings from multiple signatures interleaved). Acceptable at current fixture sizes; if fixture counts grow large, precompute a `Dict[signature, Tuple[int, ...]]` of match indices in `__init__`.

2. **`_matchCursors` read-increment-write is NOT concurrency-safe.** The transport assumes sequential request issuance per signature (the advancing cursor assumes one in-flight request per matchKey). For concurrent consumers, a per-matchKey `asyncio.Lock` is required. Golden scenario runners that issue requests sequentially are fine.

3. **Body match is byte-exact against httpx's JSON serialization** — fragile across httpx versions; if httpx's JSON encoding changes, recorded fixtures must be regenerated.

Also (from the N16 dead-code fix): `_urlsMatch` masks API keys in URLs via the literal placeholder `***MASKED***` — it `re.escape`s the recorded URL then replaces the escaped `\*\*\*MASKED\*\*\*\*` with `[^&]*`. A second identical `.replace()` pass was dead code (URL-encoding `***MASKED***` would produce `%2A%2A...`, never the literal, so the old "Also handle URL-encoded masked key" comment was wrong).

title: Pyright rejects list[dict[str, object]] at nested-subscript test sites — use a record TypedDict instead of "no Any" dict[str, object]
content:
In tests/lib/stt/providers/test_yandex_speechkit.py (I5 review fix, 2026-08-08), replacing `List[Dict[str, Any]]` with the reviewer-suggested `list[dict[str, object]]` FAILS `make lint`: pyright (basic mode, and it DOES scan tests/ — pyproject excludes only venv/ext/etc.) reports `"__getitem__" method not defined on type "object"` (reportIndexIssue) at every nested subscript, e.g. `record["stats"]["generation_stt"]` and `record["labels"]["status"]`, plus `Operator "not in" not supported` for `"errorCode" not in record["labels"]`. In this project `object`-typed values cannot be further subscripted.

Correct resolution that honors the "No Any" hard rule, lowercase dict/list convention, AND passes pyright: a module-level `TypedDict` describing the record shape, e.g.:

```python
class _StatsRecord(TypedDict):
    """One recorded stats event as captured by _RecordingStatsStorage."""
    stats: dict[str, float | int]
    consumerId: Optional[str]
    labels: dict[str, str]
```

with `self.records: list[_StatsRecord] = []`. Two traps when doing this:
1. The dict literal passed to `records.append({...})` must be bound with an explicit annotation first (`record: _StatsRecord = {...}; self.records.append(record)`) — passing the literal inline makes pyright infer a union-typed dict that is not assignable to the TypedDict.
2. `labels` must be NON-Optional in the record type (the fake should store `dict(labels) if labels else {}` instead of `None`) or every `record["labels"][...]` site gets `Object of type "None" is not subscriptable`.

Also need `from typing import TypedDict` added. General rule: for "records" collections that tests must deeply index, prefer a TypedDict over `dict[str, object]` — the object value type cannot be nested-subscripted under this repo's pyright config.

title: STT channelTag and cancellation test gaps
content: STT cancellation-propagation contract is still untested (2026-08-20 audit). The public never-raise boundaries catch Exception, not BaseException, so asyncio.CancelledError must propagate unchanged from: AbstractSTTProvider.transcribe() and .stt() (lib/stt/abstract.py — the wrappers map exceptions to ERROR results but must let CancelledError through, per their docstrings) and STTService.transcribeMedia (internal/services/stt/service.py, 'NEVER raises (except asyncio.CancelledError)').
