title: STT channelTag is per-segment response metadata
content:
Attribution metadata propagates only along the Yandex recognition-response path and is now a generalized attribution concept (not just channels):
- lib/stt/providers/yandex_events.py reads the canonical envelope-level `channelTag`, normalizes it (`_normalizeTag`), and maps it onto per-segment attribution; `final.channelTag` in the raw response is never read (documented in the module docstring).
- Segments carry `attributionTag: Optional[str]`; the result carries `attributionType: STTAttributionType` (CHANNEL default, SPEAKER for Yandex speaker labels on final mono submissions).
- It is not sent in the SpeechKit submit body and does not affect audio extraction/Object Storage/stats.
- The integration formatter (internal/services/stt/formatter.py) renders `[Speaker#<tag>]` for SPEAKER mode and `[Ch#<tag>]` for CHANNEL mode only when the result spans MORE than one distinct non-empty tag; the formatted description is stored on media_attachments.description for LLM delivery via the JSON mediaDescription field.

title: STT channelTag belongs only on segments
content:
The lib/stt model correction went one step beyond removing the inert result-level `TranscriptionResult.channelTag`: channel tagging was GENERALIZED into an attribution concept. Current shape (lib/stt/models.py):
- `TranscriptionSegment.attributionTag: Optional[str] = None` — the sole public per-segment attribution representation (renamed from channelTag).
- `TranscriptionResult.attributionType: STTAttributionType` (default `STTAttributionType.CHANNEL`) — declares the ROLE of every segment's attributionTag; SPEAKER mode is used for Yandex speaker-labeled final mono submissions (README: "Final Yandex mono submissions automatically request opaque, recording-local speaker labels").
- There is NO channelTag field anywhere in lib/stt/models.py.

The formatter (internal/services/stt/formatter.py) renders `[Speaker#<tag>] [start..end] text` when attributionType is SPEAKER and the tag is non-empty, and `[Ch#<tag>] [start..end] text` in CHANNEL mode ONLY when the result has more than one distinct non-empty attribution tag (single-channel results omit the prefix).

title: Yandex channelTag parsing contract finalized
content: Current Yandex channelTag contract (docs/design/lib-stt-v1.md §7.3, lines 770-772; lib/stt/providers/yandex_events.py): the parser reads ONLY the canonical envelope-level `channelTag`. Missing/null/empty → None (unattributed); every other JSON value → `str(value)` (e.g. 123 → "123", [] → "[]") stored as `segment.attributionTag`. The deprecated `final.channelTag` is ignored entirely, including malformed values — there is no fallback to it in any mode. Attribution is independent of `audioCursors` cursor state and is preserved through `_RawFinal` and `_applyRefinement` into TranscriptionSegment; result-level `attributionType` is CHANNEL by default, SPEAKER when speakerLabelingRequested. Regression tests pin precedence (testCanonicalChannelTagWinsOverDeprecatedFinalTag), deprecated-ignoring for valid and malformed values, stringification (testCanonicalJsonTagValuesStringify), refinement preservation, sorting, and speaker-mode defaults.

title: Use presence flag for explicit null fixtures
content: When testing wire-format fallback fields such as Yandex SpeechKit's deprecated `final.channelTag`, a helper parameter defaulting to `None` cannot distinguish an omitted field from an explicitly serialized JSON null. The local `_finalEvent` test helper therefore needs a separate presence flag (e.g. `includeChannelTag`) so tests can exercise explicit-null behavior and keep omission cases distinct. This makes fallback tests meaningful against the real parser rather than accidentally testing only the missing-field path.

title: STT metadata assertions must match scope
content: For Yandex SpeechKit STT tests, assert per-segment channelTag coverage deliberately: a valid-tag provider test that checks only segments[0] can miss extra segments with missing or incorrect tags, so compare the complete tag tuple when the expected segment count is part of the contract. In golden replay tests whose purpose is metadata propagation rather than segment-count validation, a hard-coded tuple such as ("0",) unnecessarily couples the test to one-segment fixtures; prefer asserting all emitted segments have the expected tag, or maintain fixture-specific expected tag tuples when counts are intentional.

title: Golden STT tests must require FINAL speech
content: In the Yandex SpeechKit golden replay review, the channelTag assertion was initially guarded by `result.status is FINAL`; otherwise a `NO_SPEECH` result with zero segments could bypass the tag check, allowing a regression that drops the committed final recognition envelopes to pass. For known speech fixtures, assert `FINAL`, require non-empty segments, then assert every emitted segment has the expected channelTag. Keep the test documentation aligned with this terminal-state invariant.

title: Framing status is verified, not provisional
content: The earlier memory wording that treated SpeechKit v3 getRecognition framing as “provisional” is stale. Gate-1 is now VERIFIED/PASS based on committed live SpeechKit/aurumentation golden fixtures. Parser and parser-test documentation must describe the wrapped streaming-JSON wire format as verified; support for a bare envelope remains defensive backward compatibility only and must not be presented as a release blocker. This documentation-only correction does not require changing parser behavior, fixtures, or assertions.

title: Docstring-only review caught executable diff
content: In the Yandex SpeechKit Gate-1 review, the requested change was strictly docstrings/comments in `lib/stt/providers/yandex_events.py` and `tests/lib/stt/providers/test_yandex_events.py`. Despite lint and tests passing, the working-tree diff contained executable parser changes (`_buildResult` and `_extractChannelTag`, affecting channel-tag precedence/normalization/error behavior) plus new test helper/assertion logic (`_finalEvent` and assertions around lines 247–426). The correct review action was to fail the gate and require reverting all code/test-logic changes while retaining only the approved wording: live recorded `getRecognition` fixtures verify wrapped streaming-JSON framing; bare-envelope parsing is defensive compatibility. Passing tests (66 parser, 70 parser+golden) does not establish compliance with a docstring-only scope; exact diff inspection is required.

title: Async speaker labeling support requires validation
content: The authoritative SpeechKit v3 schema exposes `SpeakerLabelingOptions` as a top-level `speakerLabeling` option on `RecognizeFileRequest`, with `speakerLabeling: SPEAKER_LABELING_ENABLED`; recognition results associate speaker identity through the envelope-level `channelTag` (not `speakerId` or per-word speaker fields), while phrase/word timing remains under `final.alternatives[].{startTimeMs,endTimeMs,words[]}`. However, public documentation is internally incomplete for the async path: the speaker-labeling guide demonstrates `FULL_DATA` and mono, whereas the async `RecognizeFile` reference says `recognitionModel.audioProcessingType` is ignored. Do not claim that async `general:rc` labeling is fully supported for every model/container without a real sanitized request/result validation; treat the documented field placement and output shape as high confidence, but async feature availability/model-container compatibility as unresolved.

title: Force-mono must alter Yandex negotiation
content: For a Yandex STT `forceMono` option to guarantee speaker-labeling eligibility, it cannot merely make already-required transcodes mono. Current audio negotiation passes through supported stereo OGG_OPUS/MP3/WAV unchanged, so those submissions remain stereo. The bounded approach is to have the Yandex provider advertise `maxChannels=1` when forceMono is enabled; stereo sources then miss the pass-through match and enter the existing PyAV transcode/resampler path, while mono sources remain pass-through. Keep the option default-off for backward compatibility and test stereo supported containers plus mono pass-through.

title: STT audio tests use a reduced Yandex format fixture
content: `tests/lib/stt/test_audio.py` defines its own `_YANDEX_FORMATS` negotiation fixture rather than importing the provider's actual `_SUPPORTED_INPUT_FORMATS`. Its OGG_OPUS spec caps channels at 2, whereas the real Yandex provider accepts 1–8 channels. Audio negotiation tests therefore validate the generic extraction contract, not necessarily provider production limits; force-mono tests should cover both the fixture behavior and provider-level format selection to avoid mistaking the test cap for the production cap.

title: STT speaker attribution model and formatting contract
content:
IMPLEMENTED speaker-attribution contract (supersedes the original dual-field design; verified 2026-08-21):

**Model (lib/stt/models.py):** unified `TranscriptionSegment.attributionTag: Optional[str]` (line 212) — NOT separate speakerTag/channelTag fields. Result-level `TranscriptionResult.attributionType: STTAttributionType` (line 230): CHANNEL by default, SPEAKER when labeling was requested. Keyword-only `speakerLabelingRequested: bool = False` threads from the provider into `parseRecognitionEvents` (yandex_events.py:77).

**Parser (lib/stt/providers/yandex_events.py):** canonical envelope-level `result.channelTag` populates `attributionTag` (or None for missing/null/empty); deprecated `final.channelTag` is NEVER read; malformed non-string tags are protocol errors; refinement preserves attribution; result-level attributionType is SPEAKER iff speakerLabelingRequested (lines 293-294, 626, 641).

**Formatter (internal/services/stt/formatter.py):** prefix is `[Speaker#<tag>]` when attributionType is SPEAKER, `[Ch#<tag>]` in CHANNEL mode — but in BOTH modes the prefix renders ONLY when the result spans MORE THAN ONE distinct non-empty tag (line 71: `if attributionTag and attributionsCount > 1`). This differs from the original design where speaker tags were always rendered — single-speaker transcripts render plain `[start..end] text`.

title: Test speaker-mode fallback boundary explicitly
content: In the Yandex event parser the deprecated `final.channelTag` is NEVER read in any mode — ordinary or speaker-labeling. Only the canonical envelope-level `channelTag` supplies attribution; missing/null/empty canonical values leave the segment unattributed even when a valid deprecated tag is present (there is no fallback path at all, in either mode). The requested combined boundary test now exists, along with neighbours: testSpeakerLabelingNullOrEmptyCanonicalTagDoesNotUseDeprecatedFinalTag (canonical null/empty + valid deprecated + speaker mode → unattributed), testSpeakerLabelingDoesNotUseDeprecatedFinalChannelTag, testDeprecatedFinalChannelTagIsIgnored, testDeprecatedFinalChannelTagDoesNotCreateOrdinaryAttribution, and testDeprecatedFinalTagNeverAffectsCanonicalAttribution (malformed deprecated values are ignored, not validated).

title: Yandex forceMono API contract
content: The Yandex SpeechKit provider's forceMono enhancement is intentionally narrow: constructor accepts forceMono: bool = False and rejects non-bool values; default supportedInputFormats remains byte-for-byte equivalent in descriptor values, order, container type, and sample-rate bounds. When enabled, returned descriptors preserve the same sequence/container/rate constraints but set minChannels=maxChannels=1. Forced descriptors must be fresh objects rather than mutating or aliasing shared constant format specs. The option must not alter request wire format, provider config, or unrelated audio-processing behavior. A focused review of the provider/tests changes found no actionable violations; the focused suite passed (77 tests) and flake8/isort/import-main/pyright were clean.

title: Force-mono integration coverage uses real provider descriptors
content: The configuration/extraction integration phase validated the end-to-end contract without changing production Python: `configs/00-defaults/stt.toml` exposes `[stt].force-mono = false`; STT lifecycle tests assert generic forwarding produces boolean `forceMono=False` by default and `True` when overridden; audio tests negotiate against `YandexSpeechKitProvider.supportedInputFormats()` and use real PyAV fixtures. They cover forced-mono downmixing for supported stereo OGG_OPUS, MP3, and WAV to one channel, mono OGG_OPUS byte pass-through, and default-mode stereo pass-through. This complements provider descriptor unit tests by proving service wiring plus actual extractor behavior, with no API credentials or network calls.

title: Verify downmix bytes, not metadata
content: For PyAV STT downmix integration tests, asserting only `ExtractedAudio.channels == 1` is insufficient because the extractor could return stereo payload bytes with an incorrect metadata label and the test would still pass. Reopen `result.data` with PyAV and inspect the encoded audio stream's actual channel count for each supported format (e.g. OGG_OPUS, MP3, WAV). This catches mislabeled output and proves the provider-facing bytes were truly downmixed.

title: PyAV channel layout is tuple-like
content: When verifying encoded audio with PyAV, `audio_stream.layout.channels` is a tuple/sequence of channel descriptors, not an integer channel count. A direct assertion such as `layout.channels == 1` is wrong and fails even for valid mono output. Assert `len(audio_stream.layout.channels) == 1` (while preserving the existing metadata assertions).

title: Yandex mono speaker-labeling provider flow
content: YandexSpeechKitProvider now derives `speakerLabelingRequested = (audio.channels == 1)` exactly once inside `_transcribe`, from the final `ExtractedAudio` after any audio preparation—not source metadata and not the `forceMono` option directly. The same boolean controls both submission and parsing: when true, `_buildSubmitBody` adds the exact top-level protobuf-JSON object `"speakerLabeling": {"speakerLabeling": "SPEAKER_LABELING_ENABLED"}` to both inline-content and Object Storage URI requests; when false, the field is omitted. The boolean is passed to `parseRecognitionEvents(..., speakerLabelingRequested=...)`, ensuring `speakerTag` cannot be produced unless labeling was actually requested. Existing snake_case request keys and all timeout/never-raise/template-method semantics remain unchanged.

title: Speaker-labeling golden replay migration blocker
content: Adding Yandex mono speaker-labeling changes exact HTTP submit bodies, so pre-existing replay golden fixtures that captured mono submissions without the new top-level `speakerLabeling` object fail exact-body matching. This is an expected fixture-version mismatch, not a provider-flow failure. In the bounded provider implementation phase, do not hand-edit or fabricate recordings; report the affected fixtures precisely and handle regeneration/validation in a separate golden-data phase. The observed affected files were `tests/lib/stt/golden/data/yandex_basic_transcription_ru.json` and `tests/lib/stt/golden/data/yandex_english_transcription_en.json`.

title: STT speaker formatting propagation boundary
content: The formatter phase for speaker attribution is intentionally bounded to `internal/services/stt/formatter.py` plus formatter/service tests. Provider, parser, config, audio, and model behavior remain unchanged; the existing `STTService` pipeline already invokes `formatTranscript` when constructing `STTOutcome.description`, so speaker attribution propagates without a service production-code change. Regression coverage should assert the final service description, not add a second formatting call in handlers or callers.

title: Golden replay asserts speaker tags separately
content: The Yandex STT golden replayer (tests/lib/stt/golden/test_golden.py, testReplayTranscription) asserts: FINAL status, non-empty segments, the exact recorded attribution-tag set {"0", "1"} (EXPECTED_ATTRIBUTION_TAGS, compared via {segment.attributionTag for segment in result.segments}), and result.attributionType is STTAttributionType.SPEAKER. There is NO per-segment channelTag is None assertion — TranscriptionSegment (lib/stt/models.py) carries only the unified attributionTag field, and the parser never reads deprecated final.channelTag. The committed fixtures in tests/lib/stt/golden/data/ are mono recordings submitted with speaker labeling enabled (recorded submit bodies contain speakerLabeling: {speakerLabeling: SPEAKER_LABELING_ENABLED}), so canonical envelope tags map to speaker attribution. Transcript-text assertions remain intentionally out of scope (README 'Assertion philosophy').

title: Speaker refinements require speaker-scoped keys
content: Whole-work review of the Yandex speaker-attributed STT integration found a correctness bug: in speaker-labeling mode, Yandex streams may reuse `finalIndex` independently for each speaker. Storing final refinements by bare integer and applying them by global index lets one speaker's refinement overwrite another speaker's text/attribution, as the live goldens can conceal. Correlate final and refinement events by `(canonicalTag, finalIndex)` in speaker mode; preserve existing bare-index behavior for ordinary mode, and add an interleaved two-speaker regression with shared indices.

title: Changelog must match channel-tag rendering rule
content: CHANGELOG.md ([Unreleased] Added, lines 15-16) states that speaker-attributed segments "always" render as `[Speaker#<tag>] [start..end] text` and that `[Ch#<tag>]` appears only when a transcript has more than one distinct non-empty channel tag. The code has moved past this wording: internal/services/stt/formatter.py gates BOTH prefixes on `attributionsCount > 1`, so a transcript with a single distinct speaker tag renders NO prefix at all (locked by tests/services/stt/test_formatter.py::testSpeakerTagRendersForSingleSpeaker and testAttributionTypeDeterminesGenericTagFormatting, which assert empty prefixes for both roles with a sole tag). The same 'speaker always tagged' prose persists in the formatter module/function docstrings, docs/design/media-transcription-stt-v1.md §10 (~lines 574-577), and arguably README.md:20. Any changelog/doc pass must state the multi-distinct-tag rule for BOTH roles — or the speaker-suppression gate in code must be revisited as a deliberate decision.

title: Block bare refinement fallback for attributed finals
content: Yandex getRecognition refinement matching has a subtle boundary: retain the legacy bare-finalIndex fallback only when correlation metadata is missing. If a final already has a complete canonical (channelTag, finalIndex) identity, a failed exact lookup must leave it unchanged rather than falling back to the global bare-index map. Otherwise a refinement tagged for speaker B at index 0 can replace speaker A's raw final at index 0 when A has no refinement. Regression must use two fully attributed speakers sharing finalIndex=0 and only one tagged refinement; B is refined while A remains raw.

title: Speaker attribution requires complete correlation identity
content: In the Yandex event parser's speaker-labeling mode, the speaker-scoped refinement key `(canonicalTag, finalIndex)` is built only when BOTH a canonical envelope tag and a valid `audioCursors.finalIndex` are present (yandex_events.py _buildResult, lines 232-234); a missing or null cursor falls back to the legacy bare-index refinement matching. However, `segment.attributionTag` is populated from the canonical tag regardless of cursor state — cursor absence limits only refinement-correlation precision, never wire attribution (supersession of the earlier keep-speakerTag=None rule; see memory 4fcbdfb4). Tests: testSpeakerLabelingWithoutUsableCursorRetainsAttributionAndBareRefinement, testSpeakerRefinementsWithSharedFinalIndicesRemainCorrelated.

title: Yandex speaker fixture needs finalIndex
content: In Yandex speaker-labeling mode (lib/stt/providers/yandex_events.py), a final's attributionTag comes from the canonical envelope channelTag alone — audioCursors.finalIndex is NOT required for attribution. The (canonicalTag, finalIndex) composite key is used only to correlate a final with its speaker-tagged finalRefinement; when the cursor is missing or null, the parser falls back to bare stream-order index association (pinned by testSpeakerLabelingWithoutUsableCursorRetainsAttributionAndBareRefinement in tests/lib/stt/providers/test_yandex_events.py). Fixture-authoring gotcha that remains true: a speaker-tagged refinement is stored ONLY in the composite map, so it can never be applied to a final lacking the envelope tag or audioCursors.finalIndex (testTaggedSpeakerRefinementDoesNotCrossApplyToUntaggedCursorlessFinal) — emit audioCursors.finalIndex on tagged finals when a fixture expects normalized text. Segments expose a unified attributionTag field (no speakerTag field exists); its role is declared by TranscriptionResult.attributionType (STTAttributionType.SPEAKER/CHANNEL). Deprecated final.channelTag is never read by the parser.

title: Reject non-object audioCursors
content: In lib/stt/providers/yandex_events.py, `_getEnvelopeFinalIndex` distinguishes absent/null audioCursors from malformed present metadata. Absent or null `audioCursors` (or a null `finalIndex`) returns None, selecting the legacy bare-finalIndex refinement matching — but the canonical envelope `channelTag` still populates `segment.attributionTag` (attribution is independent of cursor state; see memory 4fcbdfb4). A present non-dict `audioCursors` value raises ValueError → the parser's atomic PROTOCOL_ERROR (pinned by testMalformedCursorContainerYieldsProtocolError, both ordinary and speaker modes). A present non-null `finalIndex` must pass `_coerceFinalIndex` (exact non-negative protobuf integer or canonical decimal string only).

title: Reject null refinement finalIndex
content: A read-only review of the current Yandex STT event parser found a refinement-specific null-handling bug: `finalRefinement.finalIndex: null` reaches `_coerceInt()` and becomes `0`, allowing the refinement to overwrite/refine the first final segment. Null must be treated as unusable before integer coercion and produce `PROTOCOL_ERROR`, consistent with the parser's missing-required-index policy. Add a regression test proving null never targets index 0.

title: Force-mono tests should assert selected container
content: For STT force-mono audio negotiation, a regression test that only checks the output is mono is insufficient: the implementation must also select the required compressed re-encode target (currently OGG_OPUS for supported Yandex input). Parametrized stereo WAV/MP3 cases should assert both mono channel count and `result.container is STTAudioContainerType.OGG_OPUS`, preventing an implementation from passing by re-encoding to an arbitrary mono container.

title: Default config tests must load shipped TOML
content: STT lifecycle tests using a helper such as `_validSttConfig()` verify forwarding behavior but do not protect the shipped default. To guarantee `configs/00-defaults/stt.toml` keeps `force-mono = false`, add a config-level test that loads/parses the actual defaults file and asserts the value. This distinguishes runtime fixture defaults from operator-facing configuration defaults.

title: Yandex null refinement fix verified
content: The targeted fix for Yandex SpeechKit `finalRefinement.finalIndex: null` rejects the refinement as malformed before `_coerceInt()` rather than converting null to 0. The parser returns its existing atomic `ERROR / PROTOCOL_ERROR` result, so the event cannot enter ordinary or speaker-scoped refinement maps and cannot overwrite index-0 text. A parametrized regression test covered both ordinary and speaker-labeling modes; before the fix it incorrectly returned `FINAL` with the refinement text replacing the index-0 final. Focused parser tests (87 passed), final format/lint (including pyright, 0 errors), and full suite (3799 passed, 11 skipped) passed.

title: Do not invent negative-index validation requirements
content: During the final Yandex STT parser review, an initial concern claimed `audioCursors.finalIndex = -1` must be rejected. Cross-checking the actual documented contract showed it requires a complete valid composite key but does not define a non-negative range; `_coerceInt` intentionally accepts coercible integers and no regression test establishes negative values as invalid. Review findings must be grounded in the repository's explicit contract, not assumed domain rules; retain the concern only if the contract is first clarified and tested.

title: STT fixture reviews must be privacy-safe and structural
content: For STT golden-fixture reconnaissance and reviews, do not print or expose raw identifiers, audio, transcripts, or complete fixture payloads. Report only paths, helper/test symbols, and masking/pattern strategy. The preferred STT test style is structural: keep credential `${VAR}` placeholders in scenario `init_kwargs`; verify masked header/URL/body tokens (typically `***MASKED***`) and request/response JSON keys/types with regex/type assertions; avoid exact raw IDs, transcript text, audio, or full-body snapshots. Generic IDs are not automatically protected by SecretMasker, so anonymize or assert them structurally when needed.

title: Golden fixture privacy must cover init metadata
content: Privacy assertions in tests/lib/stt/golden/test_golden.py must inspect fixture metadata.init_kwargs as well as recorded HTTP traffic. The collector can preserve constructor metadata without SecretMasker, so literal API credentials or cloud-folder identifiers in init_kwargs could be committed while request/response checks pass. Require credential-bearing metadata values to use the established ${ENV_VAR} placeholder or MASKED_VALUE (and similarly validate cloud-principal fields). Never include raw fixture values in review output.

title: Validate client and server request identifiers
content: Golden-fixture privacy checks must scan both request and response headers case-insensitively. Checking only response headers misses client-generated identifiers such as x-client-request-id; request/operation/session identifiers can leak even when server x-request-id and x-server-trace-id are masked. Allow only absent/non-identifying values or MASKED_VALUE, and preserve replay behavior while sanitizing fixtures.

title: Privacy checks must not expose fixture secrets
content: In STT golden-fixture privacy regression tests, ordinary bare `assert` expressions can be unsafe: pytest assertion rewriting may include compared credential/identifier values in failure introspection and traceback output. Privacy checks must use explicit conditionals and `pytest.fail()` with value-free diagnostics (and avoid embedding raw fixture content in messages), so a failing sanitizer test cannot leak the very secrets it protects. Structural checks should still cover every committed STT fixture while preserving replay behavior.

title: Normalize credential headers before privacy validation
content: STT golden-fixture privacy validation must treat HTTP header names case-insensitively and validate every occurrence. A case-sensitive check can be bypassed by retaining a masked canonical credential header while adding an unmasked differently-cased duplicate. Normalize header names, reject duplicate credential-header occurrences or inspect all values, and keep diagnostics limited to the fixture filename and a safe structural category.

title: Privacy helper parse errors must be safe failures
content: In tests/lib/stt/golden/test_golden.py privacy helpers such as _assertMaskedResponseIdentifiers and _assertFixturePrivacy should convert malformed JSON, malformed URLs, and non-scalar header structures into explicit pytest.fail(..., pytrace=False) failures. Do not let parser/type exceptions escape with tracebacks, and do not interpolate exception text, values, operands, header names, raw identifiers, or subtrees into failure messages; use only the fixture filename plus a safe structural category.

title: Negative coverage for fixture privacy validators
content: Privacy-validator tests are not sufficiently covered by only valid committed fixtures. Add adversarial negative cases for each failure category (credential/header leaks, identifier leaks, malformed JSON/URL/header structures, and case-variant duplicates), asserting that failures are explicit, traceback-free, and non-disclosing. This protects against future weakening of _assertMaskedResponseIdentifiers and _assertFixturePrivacy while preserving the valid-fixture replay checks.

title: Keep privacy-failure frames data-free
content: For STT golden-fixture privacy helpers in tests/lib/stt/golden/test_golden.py, pytest.fail(message, pytrace=False) alone does not make failures secret-safe: the raised exception still has a traceback whose frames can expose fixture-bearing locals (content, fixtureContent, requestUrl, headerValue, nestedValue), and exceptions raised inside an except block can retain sensitive parser data through __context__ (for example JSONDecodeError.doc). Perform parsing/traversal in non-raising validators that return sanitized error codes or flags, then invoke pytest.fail with fixed, data-free text only after returning to a wrapper with no sensitive locals. Regression tests should inspect traceback-frame locals and exception cause/context, not just rendered output.

title: Bound malformed fixture validation failures
content: Privacy validation of committed STT fixtures must normalize exceptional malformed-input paths, not only expected valid fixtures. Invalid UTF-8 can raise UnicodeDecodeError and deeply nested JSON/response objects can raise RecursionError; either can retain fixture data in exception state or leak it through ordinary pytest diagnostics. Convert decode/depth failures into sanitized validation results, preferably with iterative or explicitly bounded traversal, and test malformed JSON/NDJSON, malformed URLs, unmasked fields, and excessive nesting as negative cases while preserving positive coverage.

title: Fail closed on malformed golden-fixture URLs
content: STT golden-fixture privacy validation must not treat `urlsplit()` parsing as URL validation. `urlsplit()` accepts malformed or non-absolute inputs, so privacy checks can be bypassed before path/query identifiers are inspected. Validate URL structure first and fail closed: require HTTPS, the explicitly allowed host, and the expected endpoint shape; only then inspect and mask sensitive path/query identifiers. This was a remaining important blocker in review of `tests/lib/stt/golden/test_golden.py` around line 256.

title: URL validator must reject parser-normalized variants
content: In STT golden-fixture privacy tests, structural validation must inspect the raw URL before relying on urlsplit() results. Python's urlsplit() strips leading whitespace/control characters and does not preserve whether a trailing empty query or fragment delimiter ('?' or '#') was present, so inputs like ' https://...' or '...#' can be accepted as the same safe URL. Reject raw normalization/empty-delimiter discrepancies before extracting identifiers or masking; include synthetic cases for these malformed variants. Keep rejection diagnostics explicit and value-free.

title: STT golden URL allowlist shapes
content: The privacy validator in tests/lib/stt/golden/test_golden.py uses an explicit structural allowlist derived from the recorded SpeechKit traffic: HTTPS STT submit at /stt/v3/recognizeFileAsync; HTTPS operation polling at /operations/<opaque operation segment>; and HTTPS recognition result/deletion at /stt/v3/getRecognition or /stt/v3/deleteRecognition with exactly one operation_id query parameter. URL shape, scheme, host, netloc, path, query cardinality, and fragment/normalization checks must complete before masking or identifier inspection, so a newly introduced route cannot silently bypass privacy validation.

title: Reject empty query fields in STT URL allowlist
content: The STT golden-fixture URL privacy validator must reject empty query components before calling urllib.parse.parse_qs. parse_qs silently drops blank fields, so URLs with leading/trailing/repeated '&' can otherwise be normalized into an apparently valid query shape. Enforce raw query-field structure and add synthetic regressions for empty separators; keep failures explicit, value-free, and non-traceback.

title: Reject all Unicode control characters in STT URLs
content: The STT golden-fixture URL privacy validator's control-character check must cover more than ASCII C0 controls. DEL (U+007F) and C1 controls (U+0080–U+009F), along with other non-printable/control characters as applicable, must be rejected before URL parsing or operation-id masking. Otherwise malformed or hidden data can reach identifier validation. Add synthetic regressions and preserve value-free pytest.fail diagnostics.

title: Reject printable boundary whitespace before urlsplit
content: The STT golden-fixture URL privacy hardening initially checked Unicode non-printable/control characters but still accepted leading ASCII space: space is printable, while Python's urlsplit() strips leading whitespace before structural validation. The synthetic regression caught this (focused pytest had 1 failure, 2 passes). Validate the raw URL before parsing and reject boundary whitespace (for example, require url == url.strip()) so parser normalization cannot turn a malformed fixture URL into an apparently valid one. Keep the review/report value-free.

title: STT golden sanitizer must reject unknown identifier fields
content: Static review of the mono/speaker-attribution STT diff found that tests/lib/stt/golden/test_golden.py's privacy sanitizer was allowlist-based: it recognized only three request-ID headers and four response field names. Its recursive response checks and header/parameter checks therefore allowed unmasked cloud-, request-, session-, or operation-ID values when emitted under equivalent but unlisted JSON/header/query names. The required design is fail-closed: normalize identifier names and reject every unmasked occurrence across fixture metadata, request headers/params/body, response headers, and response JSON; add synthetic negative tests for each identifier class and keep failure diagnostics value-free (for example via pytest.fail(..., pytrace=False)).

title: Reject malformed finalRefinement envelopes
content: A read-only review of `lib/stt/providers/yandex_events.py` found that present non-object `finalRefinement` values, and present non-object `normalizedText`, were silently ignored around lines 248-270. This lets an otherwise malformed event stream return a successful transcript, contradicting the parser's documented atomic malformed-input contract (malformed event shapes should poison the complete stream). Validate present fields structurally and raise `ValueError`, allowing the public parser to return `PROTOCOL_ERROR`; add regression coverage for malformed object shapes. This is distinct from the existing deliberate leniency for a non-string normalizedText value inside a valid refinement object.

title: Reject fractional or negative Yandex cursor indices
content: The Yandex STT event parser must validate every present `audioCursors.finalIndex` and `finalRefinement.finalIndex` as an exact non-negative protobuf integer before inserting or matching refinement keys. Do not rely on coercion: fractional and negative values are malformed identities and must produce the parser's atomic `PROTOCOL_ERROR`; only absent/null cursor metadata may use the legacy unattributed fallback. This prevents invalid speaker/refinement identities from cross-applying text.

title: Validate refinement index independently of text
content: In the Yandex SpeechKit event parser, `finalRefinement.finalIndex` validation must happen whenever the `finalRefinement` object is present, before branching on `normalizedText`. The current conditional path validates the index only when `normalizedText` is a dict, so a refinement with absent/null/wrong-typed `normalizedText` can silently bypass malformed or null index validation and yield a successful raw FINAL result. For example, after a valid final, `{"result":{"finalRefinement":{"finalIndex":null}}}` or `{"finalIndex":" 0"}` must terminate atomically with `ERROR / PROTOCOL_ERROR`, not be ignored. Add regression coverage for malformed index plus missing/non-object normalizedText.

title: Canonical Yandex cursor index forms
content: The hardened Yandex SpeechKit event parser accepts cursor indices only as exact non-negative protobuf integer representations: JSON integer values or canonical decimal strings such as "0" and "123". Canonical strings must not contain whitespace, signs/prefixes, or leading-zero variants; booleans, fractional numbers, negatives, null when the field is present, and incompatible types are rejected. Validation applies to both final `audioCursors.finalIndex` and refinement `finalRefinement.finalIndex`, before ordinary or speaker-scoped map insertion/matching, while valid zero remains supported.

title: Yandex STT index wire contract is strict and atomic
content: The authoritative `docs/design/lib-stt-v1.md` parser contract now specifies that present `audioCursors.finalIndex` and `finalRefinement.finalIndex` accept only a non-negative JSON integer (excluding booleans) or a canonical decimal string: `0` or an unpadded positive decimal (`[1-9][0-9]*`). Fractional, negative, whitespace-containing, prefixed, zero-padded, null, and otherwise incompatible values are malformed. A malformed non-null cursor container or index must atomically make the event parse as `ERROR/PROTOCOL_ERROR`; it must not fall back to an unattributed result or partially apply refinement. An absent or explicitly null cursor remains the compatibility fallback: refinement may use legacy unattributed matching, while valid index zero remains supported.

title: Gate-2 scope excludes pre-existing parser leniency
content: During the final whole-work review of the STT force-mono/speaker-attribution integration, an initial finding claimed that non-dict finalRefinement/normalizedText payloads and non-string selected refinement text must now produce atomic PROTOCOL_ERROR. That finding was withdrawn: this lenient refinement-content handling predates the integration, is intentionally documented and pinned by existing tests for compatibility, and is outside the changed contract. The feature-specific strictness added in scope is for cursor/refinement indices (including malformed, null, noncanonical, or invalid finalIndex), which must raise ValueError and be atomically mapped to PROTOCOL_ERROR. For future reviews, compare suspected issues against the actual base/diff and existing compatibility contract before reporting them as new blockers; do not expand the requested scope based on a pre-existing behavior.

title: Merge STT attribution into tagged result model
content: STT attribution design (implemented in commit a697e047, 2026-08-10 'Add ability to speaker-recognition via Yandex Speech Kit' — originally a research recommendation, now live): one per-segment `attributionTag: Optional[str] = None` plus one result-level `STTAttributionType` StrEnum (CHANNEL default; SPEAKER for mono diarization) in `lib/stt/models.py`. The result-level discriminator is required because a tag value alone cannot distinguish a speaker from an ordinary channel. In `lib/stt/providers/yandex_events.py`: canonical envelope `channelTag` is normalized by `_normalizeTag` (line 543) — missing/null/empty -> None, every other JSON value (including 0, false, arrays, objects) -> `str(value)` — and stored as `attributionTag`; deprecated `final.channelTag` is never read. Speaker refinements correlate by `(normalized canonical tag, validated finalIndex)` and apply only when both are present/valid (speakerRefinementKey built at lines 232-234; speakerRefinements keyed at line 264); ordinary refinements use the bare stream position; strict cursor/index validation (`_coerceFinalIndex` rejects bool/negative/fractional) yields atomic PROTOCOL_ERROR. `YandexSpeechKitProvider` supplies `speakerLabelingRequested` (= `audio.channels == 1`, yandex_speechkit.py line 427). DEVIATION from the original plan: the formatter was implemented with the >1-distinct-tags prefix gate applying to BOTH speaker and channel roles (a sole speaker tag is suppressed), not speaker-always-renders — see the corrected formatter-contract memory.

title: Yandex attribution tag independent of cursor
content: Gate-1 parser fix: in speaker mode, a valid canonical envelope channelTag (normalized as None for missing/null/empty, otherwise str(value), with no final.channelTag access) must populate the segment's attributionTag even when audioCursors.finalIndex is absent or null. Cursor absence is a safe fallback for refinement correlation; it must not suppress wire attribution. A malformed non-null cursor remains PROTOCOL_ERROR. The cursor is used only for speakerRefinementKey/legacy speakerTag correlation, not for deciding whether attributionTag exists. This supersedes earlier guidance that required a complete tag+cursor identity before setting attributionTag.

title: Separate tagged and untagged refinement maps
content: In Yandex getRecognition speaker mode, refinement correlation must keep tagged and untagged identities disjoint: tagged refinements are stored only under (canonicalTag, finalIndex), while untagged refinements are stored only under bare finalIndex. Do not insert tagged refinements into the bare-index map, because they can cross-apply to an untagged or cursorless final sharing that index. This was locked by a mixed tagged/untagged regression test; legacy fields remain temporary compatibility outputs.

title: STT formatter migration leaves parser-only legacy reads
content: STT attribution migration is now FULLY canonical (verified 2026-08-21): `internal/services/stt/formatter.py` consumes ONLY `segment.attributionTag` (renders `[<prefix>#<tag>]` when non-empty and >1 distinct tag) plus result-level `attributionType` (SPEAKER vs CHANNEL). `lib/stt/models.py` declares only `attributionTag: Optional[str]` on TranscriptionSegment and `attributionType` on TranscriptionResult — the legacy `channelTag`/`speakerTag` model fields are GONE from models. The only remaining `channelTag` reads are in `lib/stt/providers/yandex_events.py` where the parser reads the raw WIRE field `envelope.get("channelTag")` (line 226) and normalizes it into the canonical `attributionTag`; `_RawFinal` (yandex_events.py:659) carries `attributionTag` only.

title: STT phase 2 formatter attribution contract
content: `internal/services/stt/formatter.py` (`formatTranscript`) consumes only the canonical `TranscriptionSegment.attributionTag` and `TranscriptionResult.attributionType` — no legacy field fallbacks. ACTUAL rendering rule (code + tests are authoritative): an attribution prefix renders ONLY when the result contains MORE THAN ONE distinct non-empty attribution tag, and this gate applies to BOTH roles — `[Speaker#<tag>]` in SPEAKER mode, `[Ch#<tag>]` in CHANNEL mode. A sole non-empty tag (speaker OR channel) is suppressed and the line renders as `[start..end] text` (formatter.py computes `attributionsCount` over non-empty tags and gates on `attributionsCount > 1`; `tests/services/stt/test_formatter.py::testSpeakerTagRendersForSingleSpeaker` asserts a single speaker tag '1' renders NO prefix, and `testSpeakerTagsRenderOnTheirRespectiveSegments` asserts prefixes appear with tags '1'+'2'). Segment order, timestamps, the single-timestamp form when startMs == endMs, and empty-text skipping are preserved. `STTService` builds its description via `formatTranscript` (internal/services/stt/service.py line 351), so service output follows this boundary. NOTE: docs (`docs/design/lib-stt-v1.md` §6 lines 582-587, `docs/llm/services.md` line 445, `docs/llm/libraries.md` line 872, `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md` line 119) still claim SPEAKER mode renders EVERY non-empty tag — that contradicts the code; treat code/tests as truth per AGENTS.md.

title: STT integration tests use canonical attribution contract
content: STT attribution is fully canonical at the public API and test boundary. `lib.stt` publicly re-exports `STTAttributionType` (`lib/stt/__init__.py` import + `__all__`); provider and golden tests consume only `TranscriptionSegment.attributionTag` plus `TranscriptionResult.attributionType` — no test constructs segments/results with legacy `channelTag=`/`speakerTag=` kwargs (those names appear only in wire-format fixture builders for Yandex envelope JSON and in negative `hasattr` assertions in `tests/lib/stt/test_models.py`). Yandex mono tests verify the exact speaker-labeling request body and `speakerLabelingRequested=True` -> SPEAKER role; stereo tests omit speaker labeling and keep ordinary CHANNEL semantics (`tests/lib/stt/providers/test_yandex_speechkit.py::testMonoInlineSubmitUsesExactSpeakerLabelingRequestAndParserMode`, `::testStereoSubmitOmitsSpeakerLabelingAndPreservesChannelTag`). Golden replay asserts the recorded generic tag set {"0", "1"} with SPEAKER role while preserving privacy/replay-only checks (`tests/lib/stt/golden/test_golden.py`, `EXPECTED_ATTRIBUTION_TAGS` at line 85, assertions at lines 634-638). The earlier transitional phase where legacy fields remained in model/parser compatibility code is COMPLETE — legacy per-segment fields no longer exist anywhere in `lib/stt` or `internal/`.

title: STT legacy attribution fields fully removed
content: The follow-up STT simplification removes `channelTag` and `speakerTag` from provider-neutral models and formatter-facing construction. `lib/stt/providers/yandex_events.py` now reads only canonical `attributionTag` for segment attribution; wire-level Yandex envelope `channelTag` normalization is intentionally retained as the source for that canonical field, while deprecated `final.channelTag` is not consumed. Formatter tests must construct only the canonical model fields. The reviewed diff had no actionable correctness/type/test issues; lint, diff-check, targeted tests (194 passed), and the full suite (3,873 passed, 11 skipped) were green.

title: Archived STT roadmap misstates formatter output
content: docs/archive/design/stt-next-steps.md:53 still describes the formatter as timestamp-only ("the THIN formatter (`[HH:MM:SS.mmm] text` only; no header/escape/truncate/sentinel)") inside its 'Key files to load first' list, which is phrased as current behavior. title: User memories score flow: computed but discarded in injection path
content:
User-memory relevance scores are NOW CAPTURED at injection time (previously discarded). `MessagePreprocessorHandler.injectMemories` (message_preprocessor.py:75-141): in semantic mode (queryEmbedding is not None) it builds `shortTermScores = {m["memory_id"]: m["score"] for m in shortTermMemories if "score" in m}` (line 126) and stores it in `metadata["memories"]["shortTermScores"]` (lines 139-140), typed as `NotRequired[dict[str, float]]` on `CompactMemoryIdsDict` (internal/bot/models/message_metadata.py:85). Only semantic-mode short-term memories carry scores; permanent memories and latest-mode (queryEmbedding=None) retrieval still have none.

Render-time consumption: `EnsuredMessage.formatForLLM` (ensured_message.py ~1154-1166) looks up each short-term id in `shortTermScores` and re-attaches `entry["score"]` after lazy resolution via `cache.getMemoriesByIds`.

Scores are still surfaced directly in the `add_memory` (duplicate/similar_exists) and `search_memories` LLM tool returns.

title: User memories terminology: ephemeral vs short-term and data model
content:
The codebase uses "ephemeral" as the canonical term for what users call "short-term memories". This terminology mapping is important for avoiding confusion.

Terminology mapping:
- User term: "short-term memory" → Code term: "ephemeral memory"
- Database: permanent = 0 (ephemeral), permanent = 1 (permanent)
- Storage field: shortTermIds (compact metadata format in CompactMemoryIdsDict)
- Render field: shortTerm (resolved format in UserMemoriesDict)

Data model (internal/database/migrations/versions/migration_020_user_memories.py:78-94):
Table user_memories with permanent INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 column. 0=ephemeral, 1=permanent. Added deleted_at TIMESTAMP NULL in migration_021 for soft-delete.

Vec0 virtual table (lazy-created at runtime):
- Name: vec_user_memories_{dim} where {dim} is embedding dimension
- Partition keys: chat_id (INTEGER), user_id (INTEGER), model_id (INTEGER)
- Metadata columns: memory_id (TEXT), permanent (INTEGER)
- Vector column: embedding (VECTOR with cosine distance metric)
- NOT in vec0: thread_id, type, tags (applied in JOIN step)

MemoryType enum (docs/llm/memories/user-memories.md:176-192):
- BIO = "bio"
- PREFERENCE = "preference"
- FACT = "fact"
- EVENT = "event"
- RELATIONSHIP = "relationship"

Evidence (internal/database/repositories/user_memories.py):
- Line 460 docstring: "Return newest-updated EPHEMERAL memories..."
- Line 844: WHERE permanent = 0 for ephemeral, WHERE permanent = 1 for permanent

MessageMetadata field names (internal/bot/models/message_metadata.py):
- Line 79: shortTermIds: UUID hex strings of short-term memories
- Line 62: shortTerm: Non-permanent memories

This terminology was clarified in user-memories.md:24-29 where ephemeral is defined as "retrieved per turn, recent, context-dependent" vs permanent as "always present, long-term".

title: Short-term memory score design: injection-time map with render-time merge
content: Design decision for ephemeral memory score feature (from research 2026-08-11): Store a {memory_id → score} map in `metadata["memories"]["shortTermScores"]` at injection time (in `MessagePreprocessorHandler.injectMemories`), then merge scores into each `SingleMemoryDict` at render time (in `EnsuredMessage.formatForLLM`). Scores only present for semantically-searched ephemeral memories; permanent and latest-mode ephemeral memories omit the field entirely. This keeps the cache layer unchanged and reuses the existing resolution path. Requires extending `CompactMemoryIdsDict` with a new optional field and modifying two code sites: injection (store the map) and rendering (merge the scores).

title: Memory score merge constraint: index-based, not ID-based, due to keepId=False
content: Score-merge constraint in `EnsuredMessage.formatForLLM` (implemented, verified 2026-08-20): `CacheService.getMemoriesByIds` is called with default `keepId=False`, so resolved `SingleMemoryDict` entries lack the `id` field — you CANNOT recover the memory id from the entry itself. However, the merge is NOT index-based: `cache.getMemoriesByIds` returns a `{memory_id -> entry}` dict, and the render loop iterates `shortTermIds` so the loop variable `mid` keys BOTH lookups: `entry = resolved.get(mid)` and, when `mid in shortTermScores`, `entry["score"] = shortTermScores[mid]` (ensured_message.py ~1158-1167). Each scored entry is SHALLOW-COPIED (`entry.copy()`) before mutation because `resolved` entries are direct references into the shared LRU cache — mutating in place would leak scores into later scoreless renders (locked by `test_cacheMutation_bug_shortTermScoresLeakBetweenCalls`). The injection site stores the `{memory_id -> score}` map precisely so this id-keyed render-time merge works.

title: Condensed-context path does not render memories
content: `LLMService.condenseContext()` does NOT render or resolve user memories (permanent or short-term). It operates on already-rendered `ModelMessage` objects, not on raw `EnsuredMessage` instances. The method produces condensed summaries via `renderCondensedSummary`, which emits JSON with coverage fields (`messageIds`, `participants`, `dateRange`, `messageCount`) but NO memory content or scores. Therefore, the short-term memory score feature does NOT need to touch the condenseContext path. The only rendering site that matters is `EnsuredMessage.formatForLLM`.

title: Safe to extend CompactMemoryIdsDict with optional shortTermScores
content: Adding a `shortTermScores` field to `CompactMemoryIdsDict` is safe for existing code. All read sites of `metadata["memories"]` are defensive: `getMemoryIds()` and `formatForLLM()` use `.get("permanentIds") or []` and `.get("shortTermIds") or []` patterns; they extract only known keys. The `fromDBChatMessage()` DB loader uses `dbUtils.sqlToTypedDict` with a TypedDict that has `total=False`, so missing fields are handled gracefully. Test mocks won't be surprised by an extra optional field. Type the new field as `NotRequired[Dict[str, float]]` (memory_id → cosine similarity score 0.0–1.0).

content:
