Also updated test class docstrings with ALPN-over-tunnel rationale.

title: ADR update pattern: adding dated follow-up notes for decision reversals
content: When a previously-recorded ADR decision is later reversed or modified (e.g., D3 in ADR-021 disabled HTTP/2 over SOCKS5, but the guard was removed on 2026-08-13 after research proved it was unnecessary), add a dated follow-up note to the existing ADR section explaining what changed and why. Keep the original decision narrative intact for historical context. Also update the ADR's Status section or any pending-manual-smokes lists to reflect the new state. Example: added 2026-08-13 note in ADR-021 D3 explaining guard removal, marked HTTP/2-over-SOCKS probe as RESOLVED.

title: Design doc body vs outcome paragraph staleness anti-pattern
content:
When editing research/design docs like `docs/design/httpx2-migration-research.md`, updating only the OUTCOME paragraph at the top can leave body analysis sections with present-tense factual claims that contradict the corrected outcome.

Example from HTTP/2-over-SOCKS5 research:
- Outcome paragraph (line 11-13): Correctly states probe was RESOLVED, HTTP/2 works over SOCKS5
- Body line 307: Still claims "(SOCKS transport incompatible with HTTP/2.)" as present-tense fact
- Body line 180: States "HTTP/2-over-SOCKS has historically been flaky" without research context

These body sections are historical analysis artifacts describing the pre-migration state, so leaving them frozen is defensible as "research-as-conducted" record. However, for accuracy, consider adding footnotes reconciling body claims with the outcome: "(SOCKS transport incompatible with HTTP/2 — refuted post-migration; see outcome note above and ADR-021.)"

The authoritative ADR in `docs/llm/architecture.md` carries the canonical truth; design doc bodies are historical artifacts. When correcting misconceptions, decide on a per-doc basis whether to scrub body sections or leave them as-is with footnotes.

title: httpx import alias test patching resolution verified safe
content:
When testing code that uses `import httpx2 as httpx`, patching `httpx2.AsyncClient` correctly intercepts production calls to `httpx.AsyncClient`.

Why this works:
- `import httpx2 as httpx` binds `httpx` to the `httpx2` module object
- `httpx.AsyncClient` resolves to `httpx2.AsyncClient` at runtime
- `patch("httpx2.AsyncClient")` patches the exact attribute used by production code

This pattern was verified in `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_yandex_search.py` where the test patches `httpx2.AsyncClient` while production code (line 27) does `import httpx2 as httpx` and calls `httpx.AsyncClient` (line 568). Both resolve to the same module object, so the patch lands correctly.

Alternative approach would be to patch the production namespace (`internal.bot.common.handlers.yandex_search.httpx.AsyncClient`), but patching the library directly (`httpx2.AsyncClient`) is simpler and works because of the alias.

title: Historically-flaky framing was research mischaracterization, not protocol limitation
content:
The "historically-flaky HTTP/2-over-SOCKS" characterization was a misattribution, not a protocol limitation. Post-migration research (captured in docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md line 105, the h2-over-SOCKS verdict entry — NOT line 58) concluded:

- The issue was NOT SOCKS protocol incompatibility with HTTP/2
- The issue was a httpx-socks transport object propagation bug (the third-party library, not SOCKS itself): client-level http2=True does not propagate into a user-supplied transport (romis2012/httpx-socks#2 was a config misunderstanding, closed "working" same day), plus httpx_socks 0.11.0's is_available() hardcoded False breaking h2 pooling
- SOCKS5 is a raw TCP tunnel; HTTP/2 negotiation happens via TLS ALPN above the tunnel (httpcore2 _async/socks_proxy.py does start_tls with ALPN ["http/1.1","h2"])
- httpcore2's SOCKS path supports h2 by construction with graceful ALPN fallback to HTTP/1.1

OUTCOME (landed 2026-08-13, verified 2026-08-20): the D3 guard was REMOVED — internal/bot/common/handlers/yandex_search.py _downloadUrl now passes http2=True unconditionally (line 570); the regression test class was renamed TestHttp2EnabledForAllProxyTypes (tests/bot/common/handlers/test_yandex_search.py:629, 3 methods asserting http2=True for SOCKS5/HTTP/NONE, patching httpx2.AsyncClient); CHANGELOG.md line 27 records the change; ADR-021 (docs/llm/architecture.md line 803) carries the dated removal note: "never a protocol limitation; artifact of the retired third-party httpx-socks transport."

Lesson: when documenting historical decisions, distinguish between actual protocol limitations (rare) and implementation bugs in third-party libraries (common).

title: Code review scope excludes agent-memory artifacts despite git diff inclusion
content:
Gate-1 code reviews focus on source code and user-facing documentation. Agent-memory/tooling artifacts that appear in `git diff` are treated as out-of-scope:

- `.opencode/memory.jsonl` - Append-only opencode memory store, JSON lines of agent working memory
- `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md` - Agent working memory file (chronological log, not user-facing docs)

These files appear in `git diff --stat` but are excluded from review scope because:
1. They are agent bookkeeping, not deliverables
2. They contain working notes that may temporarily disagree with code (e.g., "Guard removal offered to user — pending decision" while the code already removes the guard)
3. Updating them is typically done by the session-analyser agent, not during code review

When task framing lists specific files (e.g., "8 files"), treat agent-memory artifacts in the diff as implicit out-of-scope even if they weren't explicitly listed. If a memory file contains user-facing stale claims (not just working notes), flag that separately.

Example: The HTTP/2-over-SOCKS5 guard removal showed 10 changed files in git diff, but task framed it as 8 files. The 2 extras were `.opencode/memory.jsonl` and `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md`.

title: Documentation correction pattern: minimal edits preserve historical framing in research docs
content:
When correcting historical documentation (especially research documents that serve as point-in-time records), use surgical edits that correct specific inaccuracies while preserving the historical context:

**Pattern applied 2026-08-13 to docs/design/httpx2-migration-research.md:**
- Line ~179-180: Changed "HTTP/2-over-SOCKS has historically been flaky" to "HTTP/2-over-SOCKS had an httpx-socks config/propagation bug" — reframes inherent flakiness claim into a specific, time-bounded implementation bug
- Line ~307: Changed "(SOCKS transport incompatible with HTTP/2.)" to "(SOCKS transport incompatible with HTTP/2 — refuted post-migration; see the outcome note above and ADR-021.)" — adds refutation note with references

**ADR documentation correction (docs/llm/architecture.md):**
- Changed "historically-flaky" to "then-suspect" — uses temporally-accurate language that avoids asserting incorrect historical framing even when the follow-up explains the correction

**Key principle:** Research docs are point-in-time records. Do not rewrite the entire body; make minimal amendments that mark the refutation and point readers to the correction elsewhere in the doc tree (outcome notes, ADRs).

title: lib/stats/ subsystem architecture overview
content:
The statistics-gathering subsystem exists at `lib/stats/` (plural, NOT `lib/stat/`). Core components:

**API surface** (`lib/stats/stats_storage.py`):
- `StatsStorage` ABC with two abstract methods: `async record(stats, *, consumerId, labels, eventTime)` and `async aggregate(*, limit, orphanTimeoutSeconds)`
- `NullStatsStorage` no-op implementation (discards all events, `aggregate()` returns 0)
- `GLOBAL_CONSUMER_ID = "__global__"` sentinel for global rollups

**Database implementation** (`internal/database/stats_storage.py`):
- `DatabaseStatsStorage(db, eventType, *, dataSource)` - DB-backed implementation
- Uses `stat_events` table (append-only log) and `stat_aggregates` table (period buckets)
- Both tables live in the default database (no separate stats DB provider)
- Constructor pattern: `DatabaseStatsStorage(db=self.database, eventType="llm_request", dataSource=statsConfig.get("llm-stats-data-source", self.database.manager.default))`

**Event model**:
- Events are stored in `stat_events` with columns: `event_id` (UUID PK), `event_type` (discriminator), `event_time`, `data` (JSON metrics), `labels` (JSON), `processed` (0/1), `processed_id` (batch UUID), `claimed_at`, `created_at`
- Stats dict must be `dict[str, float | int]` - numeric metrics only (string categorical data goes in labels, not stats)
- Labels dict is `dict[str, str]` - includes `consumer` key (from consumerId param), plus provider/modelName/generationType/status/etc.
- `eventType` discriminator partitions events by consumer (e.g., "llm_request", "stt_request") - same table, different consumers

**Recording API**:
- Async fire-and-forget: `await statsStorage.record(stats, consumerId="chat_123", labels={...})`
- Best-effort contract: implementations must never raise, log errors with `logger.exception()`
- `consumerId` is merged into labels as `{"consumer": consumerId}` before storage

**Aggregation**:
- Claim-first pattern with orphan reclaim in a single UPDATE
- Computes hourly/daily/monthly/total periods via `_computePeriods()`
- Produces per-consumer aggregates + global rollup (consumer replaced with GLOBAL_CONSUMER_ID)
- Upserts into `stat_aggregates` with additive metric_value (summing, not replacing)
- Primary key: (event_type, period_start, period_type, labels_hash, metric_key)

**Current consumers**:
- LLM: `AbstractModel._recordAttemptStats()` at `lib/ai/abstract.py:850-887` - records tokens, request_count, is_error, status_{STATUS}, elapsed_time
- STT: `AbstractSTTProvider._recordStats()` mirrors lib/ai pattern with audio_duration_ms
- Both use best-effort recording after completion (never raises)
- StatsStorage injected into provider constructors, not pulled from service layer

**Wiring**:
- Gated by `[stats].enabled = false` in `configs/00-defaults/stats.toml` (disabled by default until query API exists)
- Wiring layer uses `Optional[StatsStorage]`, consumer layer requires non-Optional (LLMManager converts None → NullStatsStorage)
- In `main.py` lines 90-118: constructs DatabaseStatsStorage instances when enabled, passed to LLMManager and STTService

title: StatsStorage claim-first aggregation with orphan reclaim pattern
content:
The `DatabaseStatsStorage.aggregate()` method uses a **single claim UPDATE with inline orphan reclaim** to process batches of raw events without multi-statement transactions:

**Flow** (internal/database/stats_storage.py:131-276):
1. CLAIM (with inline orphan reclaim + event_type scoping): the inner SELECT is `SELECT event_id FROM stat_events WHERE processed = 0 AND event_type = :eventType AND (processed_id IS NULL OR claimed_at < :orphanTimeout) ORDER BY event_time` wrapped via provider.applyPagination(limit), then `UPDATE stat_events SET processed_id = :batchId, claimed_at = :now WHERE event_id IN (SELECT event_id FROM (<inner>) AS _claim)`. The event_type filter is CRITICAL for multi-storage isolation on a shared stat_events table — without it the first storage claims every type's rows and the upsert misattributes them under its own event_type (that bug was found and fixed post-Phase-2).
2. Read claimed events by `processed_id = :batchId` (no event_type filter needed — batchId is a fresh uuid4 per call, so only this call's claimed rows match).
3. Aggregate in Python; each event produces rows for its own labels AND a global rollup (consumer label replaced with GLOBAL_CONSUMER_ID).
4. Upsert into `stat_aggregates` via provider.upsert with additive expression `metric_value + :metric_value`.
5. Mark claimed rows `processed = 1 WHERE processed_id = :batchId`.

**Key decisions**: double-nested subquery for cross-RDBMS portability (PostgreSQL has no LIMIT-in-UPDATE; MySQL ERROR 1093); no separate orphan-reclaim pass; events are NOT deleted after processing (retention purge is a separate purgeProcessed() call, type-agnostic, day-truncated cutoff); `limit` controls batch size (default 1000; StatsAggregationService passes its configurable aggregation-batch-limit); orphan timeout default 3600s.

**Period computation** (`_computePeriods()`, stats_storage.py:466-488): FOUR periods in one pass — hourly, daily, monthly, total. Total uses fixed epoch sentinel `datetime.datetime(1970, 1, 1, tzinfo=datetime.UTC)` → "1970-01-01T00:00:00+00:00". Returns dict of ISO 8601 strings.

title: StatsStorage wiring layer Optional vs consumer layer required pattern
content:
statsStorage is normalized before consumers see it — at multiple layers; consumers never receive None:

- Factory layer: StatsAggregationService.createStatsStorage(eventType, dataSource) returns NullStatsStorage when [stats] is disabled, the service is uninitialized, or configManager/database is missing — never None (internal/services/stats/service.py:221-235, unregistered no-op instance).
- Manager layer: HandlersManager.__init__ normalizes `self.messageStatsStorage = messageStatsStorage or NullStatsStorage()` (manager.py:444-445; same for commandStatsStorage).
- LLMManager.__init__ still converts None → NullStatsStorage() at lib/ai/manager.py:88 (defense for direct constructions outside main.py wiring).

Implications for testing: tests for LLMManager, AbstractModel, or handlers should use NullStatsStorage() explicitly — never pass None as statsStorage. It is invalid program state that cannot occur in production; recording paths call self.statsStorage.record() without a None guard, so None would crash. (The historical main.py `llmStatsStorage: Optional[StatsStorage] = None` wiring pattern was replaced by the factory; the testStatsStorageNoneDoesNotCrash test removal rationale still holds.)

title: StatsStorage type constraint: numeric metrics only, strings in labels
content:
The `StatsStorage.record()` method (lib/stats/stats_storage.py:27-34) enforces a type constraint that **stats dict must contain only numeric values (`float | int`)**. String-typed categorical data cannot be placed in the `stats` dict - the type system rejects it.

**Correct pattern**:
```python
await statsStorage.record(
    stats={
        "generation_text": 1,          # ✓ numeric
        "request_count": 1,            # ✓ numeric
        "elapsed_time": 3.5,           # ✓ numeric
        "is_error": 0,                  # ✓ numeric
        "status_FINAL": 1,              # ✓ numeric
    },
    labels={
        "provider": "openrouter",       # ✓ string
        "modelName": "gpt-4o",          # ✓ string
        "error_type": "timeout",       # ✓ string (categorical)
    },
)
```

**This was discovered** when trying to add `"error_type": type(error).__name__` to the stats dict in `_recordEmbeddingStats`. The LSP caught the type violation; the error_type entry was removed and instead logged via `logger.warning()`.

**Key takeaways**:
- `stats` = numeric metrics only (float/int) - counters, durations, byte counts
- `labels` = string categorical data (dict[str, str]) - provider names, model IDs, error types, status names
- `consumerId` is merged into labels as `"consumer"` key
- Any string data you want to query or aggregate by should be a label, not a stat metric

title: Stats disabled by default until query API exists
content:
The stats feature remains disabled by default ([stats].enabled = false in configs/00-defaults/stats.toml), but the original rationale is now historical — the deferred follow-up work landed (stats-aggregation-v1 + stats-display-v1, 2026-08-17..19):

- Aggregation trigger EXISTS: StatsAggregationService (internal/services/stats/service.py) rides the shared CRON_JOB 60s tick, gates on elapsed time, drains each registered storage (MAX_AGGREGATION_ROUNDS=10), and purges processed events past events-retention-days.
- Query API EXISTS: StatsStorage.query() (lib/stats/stats_storage.py) + StatsAggregationService.getQueryStorage(eventType).
- Display EXISTS: StatsHandler /stats and /stats_web (internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py, ALLOW_SHOW_STATS chat-setting gated) and server-rendered stats pages (lib/stats/stats_pages/, separately gated by [stats.pages] enabled=false).

Config ([stats]): enabled, five per-event data-source keys (llm/stt/message/tool/command-stats-data-source), aggregation-interval-seconds (3600), aggregation-batch-limit (1000), events-retention-days (30), plus the [stats.pages] child table. Five storages are constructed in main.py via the StatsAggregationService factory (event types llm_request, llm_tool_call, stt_request, message, command).

Implementation pattern for new stats consumers: reuse stat_events/stat_aggregates (migration_016) with a unique eventType discriminator via createStatsStorage — do NOT create new tables; record best-effort (never raise); use a separate [stats].<consumer>-stats-data-source key only if the events must live in another database.

title: Complete handler pipeline order and parallelism configuration
content:
Gromozeka handler registration order in `internal/bot/common/handlers/manager.py` (verified 2026-08-21; the `self.handlers` list is built at manager.py:492-637):

1. **MessagePreprocessorHandler** (SEQUENTIAL) — first; saves message + processes media
2. **SpamHandler** (SEQUENTIAL) — second; blocks spam from other handlers
3. **ConfigureCommandHandler** (PARALLEL)
4. **SummarizationHandler** (PARALLEL)
5. **UserMemoriesHandler** (PARALLEL)
6. **DevCommandsHandler** (PARALLEL)
7. **MediaHandler** (PARALLEL)
8. **CommonHandler** (PARALLEL)
9. **HelpHandler** (PARALLEL) — needs all command handlers registered first
10. **Telegram-only block** (PARALLEL, manager.py:543-564): DeleteFromUserMessageHandler → ReactOnUserMessageHandler → TopicManagerHandler (comment at :546: 'Deletion must run before reaction — no point reacting to a message we're about to delete')
11. **Config-gated** (PARALLEL): WeatherHandler (`openweathermap.enabled`) → YandexSearchHandler (`yandex-search.enabled`) → ResenderHandler (`resender.enabled`) → DivinationHandler (`divination.enabled`) → SandboxHandler (`sandbox.enabled`)
12. **ChatSearchHandler** (PARALLEL, `search-history.enabled`, manager.py:604)
13. **StatsHandler** (PARALLEL, `stats.enabled`, manager.py:613) — /stats and /stats_web commands; added AFTER the earlier handler-chain memories were written
14. **Custom handlers** via CustomHandlerLoader (manager.py:621-629)
15. **LLMMessageHandler** (SEQUENTIAL) — ALWAYS LAST (manager.py:631-637) — catch-all

Invariants: exactly three SEQUENTIAL handlers (MessagePreprocessor, Spam, LLMMessageHandler); LLMMessageHandler must stay last; DeleteFromUserMessageHandler must precede ReactOnUserMessageHandler. Line numbers drift — re-verify before citing.

title: Response rendering patterns in Gromozeka handlers
content:
Established response rendering pattern used throughout Gromozeka handlers:

**Base method**: `internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py:sendMessage()`
- Supports plain text, MarkdownV2 (via `markdownToMarkdownV2()` from `lib/markdown`), and code blocks
- Key parameters: `messageText`, `tryMarkdownV2: bool = True`, `messageCategory`

**Common formatting structures**:
1. **Line-based lists** with bullet points or numbered items
2. **Code blocks** for structured data (JSON, code examples) using triple backticks
3. **Bold/italic emphasis** for key information
4. **Section headers** using text formatting

**Example pattern from chat search handler**:
```python
# Structure:
messageText = f"""**Search Results**
Found {count} messages:

1. **User** (timestamp): {text_preview}
   Category: {category}

2. **User** (timestamp): {text_preview}
   ...
"""

# MarkdownV2 conversion:
respMD = markdownToMarkdownV2(messageText)
await self.sendMessage(ensuredMessage, messageText=respMD, messageCategory=MessageCategory.BOT_COMMAND_REPLY)
```

**Tabular data presentation**:
- Vertical lists with aligned values
- Key-value pairs with colons
- Structured JSON for complex data

**Rich text conventions**:
- Bold emphasis for important values
- Italic for secondary information
- Monospace for technical terms

**Existing stats output example** (`/bayes_stats`):
```
{chatTitle}
```json
{
  "total_messages": 1234,
  "spam_count": 45,
  "ham_count": 1189,
  "confidence_scores": {...}
}
```
```

This pattern provides consistency across all user-facing output and should be followed for any new statistics display commands.

title: Stats library path gotcha: singular vs plural search mismatch
content:
A prior thorough exploration incorrectly concluded that no statistics library existed because it searched for `lib/stat/` (singular) instead of `lib/stats/` (plural). The statistics library path is `lib/stats/` (plural). This naming discrepancy can confuse searches — always check both singular/plural forms when searching for libraries. The library was confirmed to exist with:
- Core: `lib/stats/__init__.py`, `lib/stats/stats_storage.py`
- DB implementation: `internal/database/stats_storage.py`
- Migration: `migration_016_add_stat_tables.py`
- Tests: `tests/lib/stats/` (mirror layout, not collocated)
- Configs: `configs/00-defaults/stats.toml`, `configs/common/10-stats.toml`

The library is fully implemented and integrated on the current branch (`lib-stat-improvement`) and also exists on `remotes/origin/lib-stat`.

title: Stats library event type design: string-based, not enum
content: The stats library's `StatsStorage.record()` method accepts `eventType` as a string parameter, not an enum. This is by design — it provides flexibility for any event type. Examples from docs/tests: `'llm_request'`, `'message'`, `'llm_query'`. The implementation in `DatabaseStatsStorage.__init__(db, eventType, *, dataSource)` writes this string to every event's `event_type` column. When designing against the stats library API, use arbitrary strings for event types rather than looking for a hard-coded enum.

title: eventType is hardcoded in main.py, not configurable
content:
The eventType for each stats storage is hardcoded as a string literal in main.py — five `StatsAggregationService.getInstance().createStatsStorage(...)` call sites:
- Line 97: `"llm_request"` (key llm-stats-data-source)
- Line 109: `"llm_tool_call"` (key tool-stats-data-source)
- Line 119: `"stt_request"` (key stt-stats-data-source)
- Line 125: `"message"` (key message-stats-data-source)
- Line 130: `"command"` (key command-stats-data-source)

No config-driven eventType selection exists. stats.toml controls only enabled/disabled and the five *-stats-data-source keys, not the event type strings. Any new consumer type requires code changes to main.py rather than config additions. (Line numbers verified against main.py on 2026-08-20.)

title: lib/ai record() stat keys and labels
content:
lib/ai/abstract.py has two stats record() call sites (both wrapped in try/except, best-effort, never raise):

**Site 1 — `_recordAttemptStats` (def at line 850, record() at line 865):** invoked once per model attempt from the no-fallback paths of generateText/generateImage/generateStructured (also on exceptions — an ERROR ModelRunResult is recorded in the except block before re-raising).
Stat keys: generation_{generationType} (generation_text / generation_structured / generation_image), request_count, input_tokens, output_tokens, total_tokens, is_error (1 if status in ERROR_STATUSES else 0), status_{STATUS_NAME} (e.g. status_FINAL, status_ERROR), elapsed_time.
Labels: modelName, modelId, provider, generationType, status. NOTE: NO error label on this site.

**Site 2 — `_recordEmbeddingStats` (def at line 889, record() at line 922):** specialised for embedding calls, no token counts.
Stat keys: generation_embeddings, request_count, embedding_attempts (number of tries), is_error (0/1), elapsed_time.
Labels: modelName, modelId, provider, generationType="embedding", status ("FINAL"/"ERROR"), plus optional error label (exception type name) on failure — this is the ONLY site with an error label.

consumerId passes through as the consumer dimension (callers pass str(chatId)). Recording is per model attempt, not per successful generation: each model records its own stats inside its no-fallback generate* path. Attempts executed under _runWithFallback orchestration (lib/ai/abstract.py:607-679) are recorded by the attempted model itself — _runWithFallback performs NO stats recording.

title: message_received event wiring point and context availability
content:
For the `message_received` stats event, the optimal wiring point is `internal/bot/common/handlers/message_preprocessor.py:193` immediately after the `saveChatMessage()` call. At this location, the following context is available via the `ensuredMessage` object:

- `user_id`: `ensuredMessage.sender.id`
- `chat_id`: `ensuredMessage.recipient.id`  
- `chat_type`: `ensuredMessage.recipient.chatType` (ChatType.PRIVATE | GROUP enum)
- `has_media`: `ensuredMessage.messageType != MessageType.TEXT`
- `text_length`: `len(ensuredMessage.messageText)`

MessagePreprocessorHandler runs first in the handler chain (registered at manager.py:482), so this fires once per message AFTER media processing but BEFORE other handlers. This is the earliest point with full EnsuredMessage context that includes both the message and the result of any media processing.

Alternative choke points like HandlersManager._processMessageRec() are earlier but lack direct access to message text/media content.

title: LLM tool call dispatch is centralized at single point covering all tools
content:
All LLM tool calls are dispatched through a SINGLE centralized point in `internal/services/llm/service.py:997` inside `generateTextViaLLM()`'s tool-execution loop: `toolRet = await self.toolsHandlers[toolCall.name].call(extraData, **toolCall.parameters)`. `self.toolsHandlers` is populated by `registerTool()` calls from handler constructors, so this one point covers all registered tools.

**The stats wiring this memory anticipated is NOW IMPLEMENTED** at service.py:989-1019 ('llm_tool_call' event):
- Elapsed time: `time.monotonic()` around the real `.call()` only (lines 996-998); the synthesized-error branch (toolCall.errorMessage, line 990-994) and unavailable-tool branch (lines 999-1007) record elapsed_time=0.0 (elapsed initialized 0.0 at line 989)
- is_error: `isinstance(toolRet, dict) and ("error" in toolRet or "errorMessage" in toolRet)` (line 1014) — inferred from the return value, never from exception handling, because of the never-raise contract
- labels: `{user_id: str(ensuredMessage.sender.id), toolName: toolCall.name}`; consumerId: `str(ensuredMessage.recipient.id)` — both from `extraData.get("ensuredMessage")`; recording skipped entirely when ensuredMessage is absent (lines 1010-1011)
- Raising tools propagate unrecorded (no catch around the dispatch; the record at 1015-1019 never runs)
- stats dict: `{tool_call_count: 1, elapsed_time: float, is_error: 0|1}`

Tests: tests/services/llm/test_tool_stats.py.

title: command event choke point handles ALL slash commands including owner-only
content:
The single choke point for ALL slash command execution is `HandlersManager.handleCommand()` at internal/bot/common/handlers/manager.py:937. It is called from `_processMessageRec()` at manager.py:1117-1120 BEFORE the handler loop (fires exactly once per command message; early-returns if handled). `command, args = commandTuple` at line 954; permission gates (BOT_OWNER/ADMIN/category checks) at lines 972-1036; owner-only commands go through the same path.

**Command stats are NOW IMPLEMENTED here** (event type "command", per design doc D5): after `handlerInfo.boundHandler(...)` executes, manager.py:1051-1056 records success and the except-branch at manager.py:1061-1066 records failure:
- stats: `{command_count: 1, is_error: 0|1}` (is_error=1 when the handler raised)
- consumerId: `str(ensuredMessage.recipient.id)`
- labels: `{user_id: str(ensuredMessage.sender.id), commandName: commandLower}` — command name is LOWERCASED

Commands are also persisted via `handlerObj.saveChatMessage(ensuredMessage, messageCategory=MessageCategory.USER_COMMAND)` at manager.py:1039, so they additionally produce a "message" stats event with message_category=USER_COMMAND (double counting is intentional: separate event types).

Tests: tests/bot/common/handlers/test_manager_command_stats.py (D5 spec, including the owner-only-command-when-permitted case). Storage wiring: main.py:129-131 via StatsAggregationService.createStatsStorage("command", command-stats-data-source) → HandlersManager(commandStatsStorage=...) at manager.py:425, 445.

title: STT stats storage IS fully wired, just needs actual record() calls
content:
STT stats ('stt_request' event) are now FULLY IMPLEMENTED — wiring AND record() calls.

**Wiring (verified)**: main.py:118-121 constructs the storage via `StatsAggregationService.getInstance().createStatsStorage("stt_request", statsConfig.get("stt-stats-data-source", ...))` (factory returns NullStatsStorage when [stats] disabled) and passes it to `STTService.initialize(configManager, statsStorage=...)` (internal/services/stt/service.py:152), which forwards it to the provider constructor at service.py:211.

**Recording (verified)**: template-method pattern in `AbstractSTTProvider` (lib/stt/abstract.py). `transcribe()` (line 106) calls `_recordStats()` at line 146 for EVERY outcome (FINAL, NO_SPEECH, all ERROR variants). `_recordStats` (lib/stt/abstract.py:228-278) records:
- stats: `{generation_stt: 1, request_count: 1, audio_duration_ms: audio.durationMs, elapsed_time: elapsedSeconds, is_error: 0|1, status_<STATUS>: 1}`
- labels: `{provider: type(self).__name__, generationType: "stt", status: result.status, ...self._extraLabels}` plus `errorCode` when set
- consumerId: optional `str(chatId)`; None → global rollup only
- Best-effort, never raises; `except Exception` (not BaseException) so CancelledError propagates (mirrors lib/ai pattern at lib/ai/abstract.py:865, 922).

title: QueueService CRON_JOB pattern for periodic background tasks
content:
QueueService provides a self-rescheduling periodic task pattern using `DelayedTaskFunction.CRON_JOB` (enum in `types.py`). The pattern works as follows:

1. **Register handler**: `self.registerDelayedTaskHandler(DelayedTaskFunction.CRON_JOB, self._yourHandler)` at service.py:301
2. **Seed initial task**: QueueService seeds the first CRON_JOB at `time.time()` (immediate) during initialization at lines 302-307
3. **Self-reschedule**: After completing work, the handler adds a new CRON_JOB task with `delayedUntil` set to the next run time

Example from existing CRON_JOB usage (service.py:301-307):
```python
self.registerDelayedTaskHandler(DelayedTaskFunction.CRON_JOB, self._cronJobHandler)
await self.addDelayedTask(
    delayedUntil=time.time(),
    function=DelayedTaskFunction.CRON_JOB,
    kwargs={},
    skipDB=True,
)
```

To add a new periodic task (e.g., stats aggregation):
1. Add new enum value: `STATS_AGGREGATION` to `DelayedTaskFunction`
2. Register handler: `self.registerDelayedTaskHandler(DelayedTaskFunction.STATS_AGGREGATION, self._statsAggregationHandler)`
3. In handler, reschedule itself: `await self.addDelayedTask(delayedUntil=time.time() + 3600, function=DelayedTaskFunction.STATS_AGGREGATION, kwargs={})`

Multiple handlers can register for the same `DelayedTaskFunction` (e.g., both HandlersManager and ChatSearchHandler have CRON_JOB handlers).

title: DatabaseStatsStorage global rollup semantics — only replaces consumer, keeps other labels
content:
The DatabaseStatsStorage aggregation loop (internal/database/stats_storage.py:206-229) produces "global" rollups by ONLY replacing the `consumer` label with `__global__` while KEEPING all other labels (model, provider, user_id, chat_id, etc.) intact in the labels_hash. This means:

- Each unique combination of labels gets its own global rollup
- Global rollups are NOT true global totals across all users/chats
- Example: `{"consumer": "123", "user_id": "456", "chat_id": "789"}` → `{"consumer": "__global__", "user_id": "456", "chat_id": "789"}`

To get true global totals, you need either: (1) an additional rollup path that strips user_id/chat_id, (2) post-query aggregation across labels_hash values, or (3) recording events with multiple label variations.

This is critical for designing message-stats migration: if user_id/chat_id are labels, global rollups will be per-user-per-chat, not cross-user totals.

title: StatsStorage labels_hash computation — canonical JSON with MD5
content:
The `labels_hash` in stat_aggregates (internal/database/stats_storage.py:240, lines 275-290) is computed as:

1. Merge consumerId into labels dict: `mergedLabels["consumer"] = consumerId or "__global__"`
2. Canonicalize with `libUtils.jsonDumps()` (lib/utils/utils.py:108-113):
   - `sort_keys: True` for deterministic key order
   - `separators: (",", ":")` for compact representation
   - `ensure_ascii: False`
3. Hash the UTF-8 encoded JSON string with MD5 (32-character hex digest)

The MD5 hash is used as a primary key component. Non-cryptographic use; collisions are astronomically unlikely but possible. Full labels JSON is stored alongside for disambiguation if needed.

title: StatsStorage period format and aggregation operations
content:
StatsStorage periods and aggregation semantics (internal/database/stats_storage.py:293-315):

**Periods produced:** hourly, daily, monthly, total

**period_start format:** ISO 8601 string (not epoch int)
- hourly: `2024-08-13T14:00:00` (truncated to hour)
- daily: `2024-08-13T00:00:00` (truncated to day)
- monthly: `2024-08-01T00:00:00` (truncated to month)
- total: `1970-01-01T00:00:00+00:00` (fixed epoch sentinel)

**Aggregation operations:** SUM only
- All metric values are summed: `aggregates[key] = aggregates.get(key, 0.0) + float(metricValue)`
- No avg/min/max operations
- Non-finite values (NaN, infinity) are skipped

**Idempotency:** Claim-based processing
- Events claimed via `UPDATE stat_events SET processed_id = :batchId, claimed_at = :now`
- Orphan reclaim: `claimed_at < :orphanTimeout` events are re-claimed
- Final marking: `UPDATE stat_events SET processed = 1 WHERE processed_id = :batchId`
- Without transactions, crash between upsert and mark-processed could cause double aggregation

title: STT stats keys: generation_stt, request_count, audio_duration_ms, elapsed_time, is_error, status_*
content:
`AbstractSTTProvider._recordStats()` at `lib/stt/abstract.py:264-275` records these specific stats keys via `self.statsStorage.record()`:
- "generation_stt": 1
- "request_count": 1  
- "audio_duration_ms": audio.durationMs
- "elapsed_time": elapsedSeconds
- "is_error": 1 if result.status == STTResultStatus.ERROR else 0
- "status_{result.status}": 1 (dynamic key per status)

The method is called from `transcribe()` at line 146-151 after `_transcribe()` completes. Labels include consumerId and a labels dict built from audio.resultStatus and optional errorCode.

title: Command messages bypass handler pipeline — MessagePreprocessorHandler not called for commands
content:
In `HandlersManager._processMessageRec()` at `internal/bot/common/handlers/manager.py:1078-1084`, when `handleCommand()` returns a non-None value (True/False for handled commands), an explicit `return` at line 1084 exits the function early. This means the subsequent handler loop (starting at line 1086) does NOT execute for command messages. Consequently:
- `MessagePreprocessorHandler.newMessageHandler()` is NEVER called for command messages
- Commands are saved exactly ONCE via `handleCommand()`'s own `saveChatMessage()` call at line 1012
- No double-save risk exists — MessagePreprocessorHandler's `saveChatMessage` at message_preprocessor.py:193 is unreachable for commands

title: saveChatMessage is INSERT-only — edits use separate update methods, no re-fire risk
content:
`ChatMessagesRepository.saveChatMessage()` at `internal/database/repositories/chat_messages.py:118-134` is strictly INSERT-only (new messages only), using pure `INSERT INTO chat_messages VALUES (...)`. Message updates go through separate dedicated methods:
- `updateChatMessageCategory()` at line 554 for category changes
- `updateChatMessageMetadata()` at line 597 for metadata changes

No edit event path re-calls `saveChatMessage()`. Max platform's `MessageEditedUpdate` type exists but is explicitly unhandled per existing documentation. Therefore, hooking an event inside `saveChatMessage()` would fire exactly once per inbound message (command or non-command) with no double-fire or edit-refire risk.

title: LLMService injection uses injectLLMManager, not initialize method
content:
LLMService singleton has NO `initialize()` method. Dependency injection is handled via `injectLLMManager(self, llmManager: LLMManager)` method (internal/services/llm/service.py:207). For new tool-call stats wiring, follow this pattern: add a parallel `injectStatsStorage(self, statsStorage: StatsStorage)` method, not a nonexistent initialize. This was discovered during stats-collecting-v1 design when verifying the injection chain for tool-call recording.

Main.py calls `LLMService.getInstance().injectLLMManager(self.llmManager)` at line 105. The tool-call stats injection should follow immediately after: `LLMService.getInstance().injectStatsStorage(toolStatsStorage)`.

title: Command and message paths converge on BaseBotHandler.saveChatMessage
content:
Both command and regular message processing paths converge on `BaseBotHandler.saveChatMessage()` (internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py:1080), making it a single choke point for message_received stats recording:

1. **Command path**: `HandlersManager.handleCommand()` (manager.py:910) → line 1012: `handlerObj.saveChatMessage(...)` where `handlerObj = handlerInfo.boundHandler.__self__` (arbitrary command-owning handler instance).
2. **Regular message path**: `MessagePreprocessorHandler` → line 193: calls `self.saveChatMessage(...)` (inherited from BaseBotHandler).

The wrapper receives `EnsuredMessage` with complete context: sender.id (userId), recipient.id (chatId), recipient.chatType (ChatType enum), messageType (MessageType enum), messageText. This makes it the ideal recording site for message_received events, providing all required fields without sign-derived chatType calculations.

Key: The command path's handlerObj varies (whichever handler owns the command), but all handlers extend BaseBotHandler and share the same saveChatMessage implementation.

title: Stats recording layering: bot-layer not data-repo layer
content:
Stats recording should happen at the bot/service layer, NOT in the data-repository layer, to maintain architectural purity:

- **LLM stats**: Recorded in `lib/ai/abstract.py` (service/provider layer), not in database repos.
- **STT stats**: Recorded in `lib/stt/abstract.py` (service layer), not in database repos.
- **Message stats**: Design decision for stats-collecting-v1: record in `BaseBotHandler.saveChatMessage()` (bot coordination layer), NOT in `ChatMessagesRepository.saveChatMessage()` (data-repo layer).

Rationale: The repository layer should be pure-persistence. Recording stats at the repo layer would import bot-level concepts like consumer=chatId and event-type semantics into the data layer. The bot layer naturally owns the consumer concept and has the complete EnsuredMessage with typed enums (ChatType, MessageType), making it the correct abstraction boundary.

This pattern was established during stats-collecting-v1 design and applies to all new event types.

title: HandlersManager post-construction attribute injection pattern
content:
HandlersManager supports post-construction attribute setting on handlers to avoid editing constructor signatures across many handler classes. Precedent exists at `internal/bot/common/handlers/manager.py:721`:

```python
await self.cache.injectDatabase(self.db)
```

For stats-collecting-v1 message_received wiring, this pattern is used to inject `messageStatsStorage` into all handlers without editing 15+ handler constructors:
1. `HandlersManager.__init__` gains `messageStatsStorage` kwarg (default NullStatsStorage).
2. After constructing all handlers and building `self.handlers` list, iterate and set:
   ```python
   for handler, _ in self.handlers:
       handler.messageStatsStorage = self.messageStatsStorage
   ```
3. `BaseBotHandler.__init__` initializes `self.messageStatsStorage: StatsStorage = NullStatsStorage()` (default no-op).

This is cleaner than threading the param through every handler constructor call and maintains backward compatibility (handlers default to NullStatsStorage when stats disabled).

title: Tool call error detection and timing rules
content:
For llm_tool_call event recording at `internal/services/llm/service.py:981`, the error detection and timing semantics are:

**Error detection rule**: `is_error = 1` if the result dict contains either `"error"` key or `"errorMessage"` key. This covers three dispatch branches:
- Branch 1 (line 979): toolCall.errorMessage present → synthesized error dict with "error" key.
- Branch 2 (line 981): actual tool call → result may have "error"/"errorMessage" if tool failed.
- Branch 3 (line 986-990): tool not available → synthesized error dict with "error" key.

**Timing**: `elapsed_time` measures only the actual `.call()` in branch 2. Wrap with `time.monotonic()` around the await. For branches 1 and 3 (no real call), set `elapsed_time = 0.0`.

**Exception handling**: Do NOT catch exceptions from tool calls (minimal-change bias). A contract-violating tool that raises propagates unrecorded, preserving current behavior. This is a deliberate trade-off documented in stats-collecting-v1.

**Recording location**: Once per tool call iteration, after obtaining toolRet, with stats: {tool_call_count: 1, elapsed_time, is_error}, labels: {user_id, toolName}, consumerId: str(chatId).

title: Command is_error semantics: exceptions only, not permission denials
content:
For command event recording in `HandlersManager.handleCommand()` (manager.py:910), `is_error` semantics are:

**is_error = 0** (success): Recorded in the success return path (line 1024) after successful handler execution.

**is_error = 1** (error): Recorded in the exception catch block (lines 1025-1034) when a handler raises.

**NOT recorded**: Permission-denied or category-denied commands (early returns at lines 963-974 and 998-1009) are NOT recorded as command events. These rejections happen before the execution attempt, so they don't reflect handler outcomes.

This interpretation aligns with D5 ("Record after execution attempt so is_error reflects the handler outcome") - only commands that reach the try/except block and are actually attempted are counted. Permission denials are not "command executed" events from a usage-stats perspective.

**Recording location**: After the try/except block, with stats: {command_count: 1, is_error}, labels: {user_id, commandName}, consumerId: str(chatId).

title: ChatType enum values match sign-derived chatType strings
content:
`ChatType` StrEnum values at `internal/bot/models/ensured_message.py:57-70` use lowercase string values that exactly match the sign-derived chatType convention used elsewhere in the codebase:

- `ChatType.PRIVATE = "private"` (line 69)
- `ChatType.GROUP = "group"` (line 70)

The established repo-wide convention is: `chatId > 0` → private chat, else group chat. This means:
- For live message_received events: `chatType = message.recipient.chatType.value` gives "private" or "group".
- For backfill from `chat_user_stats`: derive chat_type from chatId sign, producing identical "private"/"group" strings.

This consistency ensures label values are comparable between live events and backfilled historical data. Verified during stats-collecting-v1 design.

title: Stats v3 transaction gap: claim→upsert→mark not atomic
content:
`DatabaseStatsStorage.aggregate()` (internal/database/stats_storage.py:131-276) is NOT transactional — the TODO is now at line 241: "Add sqlProvider.getUpsertQuery + put all queries into batchExecute for transaction".

Current v3 flow (claim-first, reclaim-in-place):
1. Step 1 (line ~170-200): UPDATE claim — claims up to `limit` unprocessed rows (processed=0, event_type match, processed_id IS NULL or claimed_at older than orphanTimeout) by setting processed_id=batchId and claimed_at.
2. Step 2 (line 203): SELECT claimed rows by processed_id=batchId.
3. Step 3 (line 213): aggregate in Python (per-consumer + __global__ rollup).
4. Step 4 (line 240): upsert into stat_aggregates (one execute per row — this is where the TODO sits).
5. Step 5 (line 268): mark claimed rows processed=1.

Gap: a crash between claim (step 1) and mark-processed (step 5) leaves claimed-but-unprocessed rows; they are only recovered after orphanTimeoutSeconds (default 3600) via the stale-claim reclaim in step 1 — and re-processing after orphan reclaim can double-count because the upsert uses SUM accumulation (`metric_value + :metric_value`). Accepted risk, documented in the v3 design doc; fix requires a transactional batch API on BaseSQLProvider.

title: Stats collection event wiring patterns: saveChatMessage choke point, tool dispatch centralization, handleCommand post-execution
content:
Stats event wiring (IMPLEMENTED and verified in current code — line numbers updated):

1. **message events**: `BaseBotHandler.saveChatMessage()` (internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py:1084) is the choke point — both the command path (manager.py:1039) and MessagePreprocessorHandler (message_preprocessor.py:193) flow through it. After the DB save (db call at base.py:1125), stats are recorded at base.py:1143-1159 via `self.messageStatsStorage.record(...)` — gated on messageCategory not in (DELETED, UNSPECIFIED); direction derived from `sender.id == await self.getBotId()`; eventType is "message" (not "message_received").

2. **llm_tool_call events**: single centralized tool dispatch at internal/services/llm/service.py:997 inside generateTextViaLLM() (method def at line 763): `toolRet = await self.toolsHandlers[toolCall.name].call(extraData, **toolCall.parameters)`.

3. **command events**: `HandlersManager.handleCommand()` (internal/bot/common/handlers/manager.py:937-1073) records via `self.commandStatsStorage.record(...)` — is_error=0 in the success path (line 1052) after handler execution (boundHandler call at 1047/1049), is_error=1 in the exception catch (line 1062). Stats: {command_count: 1, is_error}, labels: {user_id, commandName}, consumerId=str(chatId).

Storages are created in main.py (lines 96-129) via `StatsAggregationService.getInstance().createStatsStorage(...)` — five of them: llm_request, tool, stt, message, command; injected into HandlersManager (manager.py:424-445) and fanned out to all handlers (manager.py:648-650). All recording gated by [stats] enabled (NullStatsStorage when disabled).

title: Stat backfill design: 6 rows per source row with global rollups
content:
migration_027 backfill design (CURRENT — source is chat_messages, not chat_user_stats): reads individual `chat_messages` rows, groups by `(chatId, userId, datePart, messageCategory, messageType)`, and produces **12 rows per unique bucket** (3 periods × 2 label-sets × 2 metrics) with event_type="message":
- Periods: `daily` (date truncated to midnight), `monthly` (first of month), `total` (epoch sentinel 1970-01-01). No hourly.
- Label-sets: per-consumer `{consumer: str(chatId), user_id, chat_type, message_category, message_type}` and `__global__` rollup (consumer=GLOBAL_CONSUMER_ID).
- Metrics: `message_count` (+1 per row) and `text_length` (sum of len(messageText)).

Key properties (verified in internal/database/migrations/versions/migration_027_drop_chat_stats_backfill_aggregates.py):
- Exclusions: rows with NULL, DELETED, or UNSPECIFIED message_category are skipped (matches live recording semantics).
- chat_type derived from chat_id sign (`private` if chatId > 0 else `group`).
- Python-side pre-aggregation into a dict keyed by (labelsJson, periodType, periodStart, metricKey), then a replace-style upsert (`metric_value: ExcludedValue()`, NO incremental SUM) — making re-runs idempotent.
- Same canonicalization (lib.utils.jsonDumps) and hashing (_hashLabels from internal.database.stats_storage) as the live aggregator, so hashes match live events.
- Both legacy tables (`chat_stats`, `chat_user_stats`) are dropped with portable DROP TABLE IF EXISTS.

title: Drop-table migrations require 5-site coordination (migration, repository, tests, docs, lint)
content:
**Critical pattern**: When a migration drops tables, coordinated changes across at least 5 locations are required. Creating the migration file alone is insufficient and causes runtime errors.

**The 5 required changes for a table-drop migration:**

1. **Migration file** (`internal/database/migrations/versions/migration_NNN_*.py`):
   - `up()`: Backfill data to new location (if needed), then `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS <table>`
   - `down()`: Recreate empty table with FINAL accumulated schema (not migration_001 original)
   - Use portable `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS`, not bare `DROP TABLE`

2. **Repository code** (e.g., `internal/database/repositories/chat_messages.py`):
   - **REMOVE** all write operations to the dropped tables
   - For example: `chat_stats` and `chat_user_stats` upserts must be deleted from `saveChatMessage()`
   - If code writes to dropped tables, runtime errors occur after migration runs

3. **Tests**:
   - Add new migration test file: `tests/database/test_migration_NNN_*.py`
   - Must use `rollbackTo(targetVersion=...)` NOT `rollback(steps=...)`
   - Test backfill logic, table DROP, and down() recreation
   - Update schema-introspection tests: remove dropped table from expected-tables lists
   - Update repository tests: verify writes no longer occur

4. **Documentation** (multiple files):
   - `docs/database-schema.md`: Remove table section entirely
   - `docs/database-schema-llm.md`: Remove table section, update migration count
   - `docs/llm/database.md`: Update migration count
   - `internal/database/migrations/README.md`: Update migration count
   - `CHANGELOG.md`: Add entry under `[Unreleased]` with "Fixed" or "Changed" header

5. **Lint**:
   - Fix any flake8/isort issues in the migration file
   - Common issues: unused imports, unused variables, missing EOF newline

**Real failure example (migration_027)**: Implementing agent created migration_027 that dropped `chat_stats` and `chat_user_stats` tables, but failed to remove the upserts from `saveChatMessage()`. Result: after migration runs, `saveChatMessage()` would attempt to write to non-existent tables, causing runtime errors.

**Verification pattern**: Use comprehensive 7-item verification checklist (git status, migration structure, repository code changes, tests, documentation updates, test execution, lint) to catch missing coordination steps before the code is deployed.

title: Comprehensive verification pattern for multi-file implementations
content:
**7-item verification checklist for multi-file implementations**: When verifying that an agent completed a multi-file task correctly, use this systematic pattern to catch partial implementations.

**The checklist:**

1. **Git status**: Run `git status --short` to list all modified/new files. Verify branch is correct.

2. **Core implementation files**: Read each file that should have changed. For migrations:
   - Does the file exist at expected path?
   - Are all required changes present (up/down/backfill)?
   - Are specific requirements met (e.g., backfill logic, label sets, periods)?

3. **Repository/service code**: Check if code that interacts with changed structures was updated:
   - Are writes to dropped tables removed?
   - Are reads from dropped tables removed or updated?
   - Are imports/usage patterns updated?

4. **Tests**: Verify test coverage exists:
   - Do new test files exist (e.g., `test_migration_NNN_*.py`)?
   - Do existing tests reflect the changes?
   - Are test patterns correct (e.g., `rollbackTo(targetVersion=...)` not `rollback(steps=...)`)?

5. **Documentation**: Check all doc locations:
   - Schema docs (`docs/database-schema.md`, `docs/database-schema-llm.md`)
   - Operation guides (`docs/llm/database.md`)
   - Migration lists (`internal/database/migrations/README.md`)
   - Changelog (`CHANGELOG.md` under `[Unreleased]`)
   - Are dropped sections removed?
   - Are counts/metrics updated?

6. **Test execution**: Run relevant tests:
   - Migration tests: `./venv/bin/pytest tests/database/test_migration_NNN_*.py -v`
   - Repository tests: `./venv/bin/pytest tests/database/repositories/test_X.py -v`
   - Report pass/fail counts

7. **Lint**: Run `make lint` and report results:
   - flake8 (unused imports, unused variables)
   - isort (import ordering)
   - import main check (circular imports)
   - pyright (type checking)

**Output format**: For each item, give verdict (DONE/PARTIAL/MISSING with specifics). Then overall verdict: complete enough to proceed, partially complete (what's missing), or not actually applied.

**Why this matters**: This pattern catches partial implementations like migration_027 where the file existed but repository code, tests, docs, and lint were all incomplete. The systematic approach ensures no site is missed.

title: SQLite returns timestamps as strings in SELECT queries
content:
When reading timestamp columns from SQLite via SELECT queries, the database returns them as **strings** (ISO format) not as `datetime.datetime` objects. This is a critical gotcha in migration 027:

**The problem**: The migration's `_dayISO()` and `_monthISO()` functions expect `datetime.datetime` parameters, but when reading `chat_user_stats.date` via `provider.executeFetchAll()`, SQLite returns strings.

**The fix**: Convert the string back to datetime using `datetime.fromisoformat()`:
```python
# In migration 027's up() method, when processing source rows:
dateStr = row["date"]  # SQLite returns this as a string
dateVal = datetime.fromisoformat(dateStr)  # Convert to datetime
```

This pattern is needed whenever migrations read timestamp columns from SQLite for processing. The same issue doesn't occur in PostgreSQL/MySQL where the provider handles type conversion differently, but the portable code must handle SQLite's string-returning behavior.

title: Migration test pattern for Gromozeka
content:
Gromozeka uses a consistent pattern for per-migration tests. Example: `tests/database/test_migration_027_drop_chat_stats_backfill_aggregates.py`

**Standard test structure** (4 test functions minimum):

1. **`test_up_<migrationPurpose>()`** - Tests the main migration path:
   - Rollback to previous version: `await database.rollbackTo(targetVersion=26)`
   - Seed test data into source tables (include edge cases: private/group chats, multiple dates, different users)
   - Run `database.migrate()`
   - Assert source tables dropped
   - Assert destination table has correct data with correct labels structure
   - For backfills: verify labels JSON format, labels_hash matches `_hashLabels()`, period_start values for total equals "1970-01-01T00:00:00+00:00"

2. **`test_down_<migrationPurpose>()`** - Tests rollback:
   - Run migration up first
   - Run `database.rollback()`
   - Assert dropped tables are recreated (queryable, may be empty)
   - Verify schema is correct

3. **`test_<repositoryMethod>PostMigration()`** - Tests production code behavior after migration:
   - Use `testDatabase` fixture from tests/conftest.py
   - Run migration up
   - Call repository methods that previously touched dropped tables
   - Assert no exceptions occur
   - Verify correct new behavior (e.g., writes to new tables only)

4. **`test_up_idempotentWhen<Condition>()`** - Tests idempotency:
   - Run migration up twice
   - Assert no errors on second run
   - Verify state is consistent

**Key conventions**:
- Use `rollbackTo(targetVersion=N)` NEVER `rollback(steps=N)`
- Tests are `async def test_...` without decorator (`asyncio_mode = "auto"`)
- Reuse fixtures from `tests/conftest.py` (testDatabase, etc.)
- For label-based stats: verify `labels_hash` equals `_hashLabels(labels)` from `internal.database.stats_storage`
- Test both private chats (chat_id > 0) and group chats (chat_id < 0)
- Include multiple dates spanning same month and different months

title: Test row count expectations must account for UNIQUE constraint collisions with upsert SUM
content:
When testing code that writes to `stat_aggregates` via upsert with SUM accumulation (the UNIQUE key is `(event_type, period_start, period_type, labels_hash, metric_key)`), row-count expectations must account for key collisions that consolidate rows.

Where this applies TODAY: `DatabaseStatsStorage.aggregate()` (internal/database/stats_storage.py:240-266) upserts with `"metric_value": "metric_value + :metric_value"` SUM accumulation. Events with the same labels on the same date collapse into one daily row per label-set; two dates in the same month collapse into one monthly row; per-consumer and `__global__` rollups are separate label-sets (consumer replaced with GLOBAL_CONSUMER_ID) and never collide with each other.

NOTE: migration_027 no longer uses upsert-SUM — it pre-aggregates in a Python dict and upserts with `ExcludedValue()` (replace-style, idempotent re-runs), specifically to avoid accumulation issues.

Methodology (still valid): compute expected unique-key combinations from seeded data by hand (watch date collisions across chats for the same user in the __global__ rollup); if recomputed expectation matches actual, the test was wrong — fix the test; if it differs, the code has a defect. Never weaken an assertion to match buggy output.

title: migration_027 deterministic table existence check via listTables()
content:
migration_027_drop_chat_stats_backfill_aggregates.py uses a deterministic table-existence check instead of a broad `except Exception` around the backfill SELECT (migration_027:122-127):

```python
existingTables = set(await sqlProvider.listTables(likePattern="%"))
if "chat_messages" not in existingTables:
    pass  # skip backfill, proceed to DROP IF EXISTS (no-ops)
```

NOTE: the gated source table is **chat_messages** — the migration was rewritten (2026-08-16 fix-set fcdf5663) to backfill from chat_messages (full message history with real message_category/message_type/message_text), then DROP chat_stats and chat_user_stats. (The original gate checked chat_user_stats.)

`listTables()` is part of the BaseSQLProvider contract (base.py:558, concrete; implemented in sqlite3.py:558) so the check is portable. Real SELECT errors (DB-locked/disk-full/IO) propagate and fail the migration rather than silently proceeding to DROP. Idempotency: table absent on re-run → skip backfill → DROP IF EXISTS no-ops.

title: Migration idempotency pattern: existence check with backfill guard and unconditional DROP
content:
Pattern for idempotent backfill-then-drop migrations (as used in migration_027):

1. Check source table existence deterministically before backfill:
   ```python
   existingTables = set(await sqlProvider.listTables(likePattern="%"))
   if "source_table" not in existingTables:
       sourceRows = []  # Skip backfill, data already gone or never existed
   ```

2. Proceed with backfill loop only if sourceRows is populated (no-op if empty list)

3. Unconditionally DROP IF EXISTS all legacy tables after backfill step

Key rationale:
- `listTables(likePattern: str = "%")` is the portable cross-RDBMS API on BaseSQLProvider
- Setting `sourceRows = []` avoids any SELECT on non-existent tables (no exception handling needed)
- DROP IF EXISTS makes the down-migration safe for re-runs
- Only check the backfill SOURCE table existence, not all dropped tables (some dropped tables may have been write-only)

This pattern ensures the migration can run safely whether:
- Legacy tables exist (normal first-run case)
- Tables already dropped (idempotent re-run case)
- Partial state exists (source missing but other legacy tables present - acceptable per design)

Test coverage: The `test_up_idempotentWhenLegacyTablesGone` test pattern verifies this by:
- Recreating legacy tables, seeding source table, running up()
- Re-running up() and verifying no duplicate rows (guard path exercised)

title: Do not skip git hooks with --no-verify unless explicitly requested
content: Agent mistake (session m0001): When user explicitly stated work was verified and green (lint clean, 3946 passed/11 skipped, check-docs 0 broken), the agent still used `git commit --no-verify` to skip hooks unnecessarily. This violated global rules: "Do not update git config, skip hooks... unless explicitly requested." The agent self-identified this as a mistake.
