title: Copy-paste bug pattern: numerator used instead of sum in average calculations
content:
Recurring bug class found in stats aggregation code (Phase 3b Gate-1, four instances at once): an average computation divides the COUNT by itself (or uses the wrong numerator) — `avgLength = totalMessageCount / max(totalMessageCount, 1)` → always 1.0 — instead of SUM/COUNT.

Why tests missed it: all fixtures used empty rows, and 0/1 == 0.0 matches both the buggy and correct formulas. An average bug is invisible to empty-data tests by construction.

Current seams where the correct pattern lives (verified 2026-08-21):
- Reply path: `StatsAnalyzer.average(valueKey, countKey)` (lib/stats/analysis.py lines 247-271) computes Σvalue/Σcount — use it instead of hand-rolled division
- Web path: generator.py computes e.g. `avgLength = totalLength / totalMessages` and `avgElapsed = totalElapsed / totalRequests` guarded by `if totalX > 0`, where the numerators come from `_groupRowsByMetric` sums

Prevention: (1) when writing aggregation code, name the numerator and denominator explicitly and confirm the numerator is a SUM of a different metric than the count; (2) always include a regression test with non-empty canned data asserting the computed VALUE (not just that a line exists), so a wrong formula yields a wrong number.

title: D15 contract: whole-tier exception wrapping required for feature tiers
content:
D15 whole-tier exception wrapping: best-effort feature tiers must never raise out of the command handler. The stats `--web` tier design (docs/design/stats-display-v1.md §D15, lines 1282-1297) requires the whole tier wrapped in `try/except Exception` + `logger.exception`, delivering the in-chat brief + one-line failure note (WARNING log) on any failure — graceful degradation, not a raw error.

Current state (verified 2026-08-20) — the contract IS satisfied in internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py:
- `statsCommand` wraps the entire `_handleWebMode` invocation in `try/except Exception` + `logger.exception` (stats.py:360-385). This is the outer D15 wrap; if failure happens before the brief is built (e.g. rate-limit RuntimeError), the note '⚠ Генерация веб-страницы не удалась.' is sent alone.
- Inside `_handleWebMode`: `_buildStatsReply` (1253-1274) and `_buildStatsPayload` (1277-1298) each have their own try/except with graceful fallbacks (payload failure still delivers the brief + failure note); template argv resolution catches `(KeyError, AttributeError)` (1307-1317, 'FIX 2' comment); the `RateLimiterManager.applyLimit` call is deliberately unwrapped locally — comment at 1249 states the outer D15 wrap covers the no-limiter RuntimeError (raised at lib/rate_limiter/manager.py:290, 299).

Why tier-level wrapping matters even though the dispatcher catches handler exceptions: the dispatcher (internal/bot/common/handlers/manager.py:1058) is a crash-safety net, not graceful degradation — it logs at ERROR, records `is_error=1` command stats, and may send a generic error reply (gated on `replyErrorOnException`). A tier escape loses the 'in-chat reply always wins' guarantee and misclassifies a best-effort page-tier failure as a command error.

General pattern for ANY best-effort feature tier: wrap the whole tier body (after successful pre-checks, through side-effect invocation, to reply) in `try/except Exception` + `logger.exception`, and deliver partial results (brief + one-line failure note) on failure. Design-doc references: D15 (never raise out of handler), D4 (query layer raise-on-error, caught one level up).

title: D10 validation pattern: list[str] entry types must be checked at construction
content:
When a design requirement specifies "non-empty `list[str]` entries" for command templates (stats-display-v1 D10 :996), validation must check both that the value is a non-empty list AND that all elements are strings.

During Phase 3b, the stats handler at `internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py:155-160` only validated:

```python
if not generateCommand or not isinstance(generateCommand, list) or len(generateCommand) == 0:
    raise RuntimeError(...)
```

This allowed `[123]` or `[null]` to pass construction, then crash at runtime with `AttributeError` at `:1470` (when `arg.format_map(...)` is called). The crash would also escape the handler due to the D15 exception handling gap.

**Correct validation pattern**:

```python
if (
    not isinstance(generateCommand, list) or
    not generateCommand or
    not all(isinstance(part, str) and part.strip() for part in generateCommand)
):
    raise RuntimeError("[stats-pages] generate-command must be a non-empty list[str] when enabled")
```

**Rationale**: Configuration validation at construction exists to catch operator misconfiguration early with clear error messages. Runtime crashes with AttributeError violate both D10 (which demands clear error messages naming the key) and D15 (which mandates no exceptions escape). This is especially important for R8's whole purpose: handling template misconfiguration gracefully.

Apply this pattern to all configuration entries that must be lists of specific types, not just "non-empty list".

title: Subprocess test gaps: argv substitution and empty fixture blindness
content:
Durable test-quality lessons from the Phase 3b stats handler review (re-audited 2026-08-20).

RESOLVED since the original review: argv substitution IS now asserted. TestStatsHandlerWebTierE2E.test_web_mode_e2e_generates_page_and_schedules_deletion (tests/bot/common/handlers/test_stats.py ~lines 1427-1438) does `mockExec.assert_called_once_with("./venv/bin/python3", "-m", "lib.stats.stats_pages", "generate", "--user-id=456", "--chat-id=123", "--platform=telegram", stdin=..., stdout=..., stderr=...)` — template placeholder substitution is pinned.

Still-valid lessons:
1. Empty test fixtures mask math bugs: subprocess e2e fixtures that return empty rows (mockStorage.query -> []) make averaging bugs invisible because all formulas yield 0.0 when counts are 0. For aggregation/math code, include at least one test with non-empty canned data asserting computed values (e.g. rows elapsed=2s/count=1 and elapsed=4s/count=2 → avg must be 2.0, not 1.0).
2. Zero-assertion tests are vacuous: a test that only drives code with no assertions (not even mock.assert_called) proves nothing. Minimum: assert the key collaborator was (or was not) called.
3. `patch.object(module, "fn") as mockExec` DOES let you assert call args even on a real module's attribute — 'we can't directly check the call' is a misconception.

title: StatsAggregateDict mock structure requirement for stats tests
content:
When mocking `storage.query` for stats tests, the mock must return rows in the `StatsAggregateDict` format from lib/stats/types.py (lines 11-31). Required structure:

```python
{
    "periodType": "daily",  # or "hourly", "monthly", "total"
    "periodStart": "2023-08-15T00:00:00Z",
    "labels": {
        "consumer": "123",
        "user_id": "456",
        # ... other label keys
    },
    "metricKey": "elapsed_time",  # or "command_count", etc.
    "metricValue": 2.0
}
```

Common mistake: returning flat dicts like `{"consumer": "123", "user_id": "456", "elapsed_time": 2.0}` which causes `KeyError: 'labels'` in `StatsAnalyzer.filterByLabelIn()` at lib/stats/analysis.py:178-189 (`row["labels"].get(key)` at line 188). The handler path calls it from `StatsHandler._buildStatsPayload` (internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py:1121-1126) for the consumer and user_id filters.

Example of correct mock in tests/bot/common/handlers/test_stats_payload_regression.py:79-222 where multiple rows are mocked with proper structure for each metric (message_count, command_count, tool_call_count, request_count).

title: Subprocess launcher extraction pattern from stats.py
content:
When extracting duplicated subprocess mechanics into a shared launcher, follow these patterns:

**Location**: `lib/stats/stats_pages/launcher.py` (or similar lib-level module for cross-handler reuse)

**Function signature**: `async def runCliCommand(argv: list[str], *, stdinPayload: str | None = None, timeoutSeconds: float = 30.0) -> tuple[int | None, str, str]`

**Pattern to follow**: Mirror `internal/services/proxy/lifecycle.py:105-150` conventions:
- Use `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(*argv, stdin=PIPE, stdout=PIPE, stderr=PIPE)`
- Wrap `communicate(input=stdinPayload)` inside `asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=timeoutSeconds)`
- On timeout: kill process, await cleanup, raise dedicated exception
- Use `errors="replace"` for stdout/stderr decoding

**Exception handling**: Raise dedicated exception with reason enum:
```python
class StatsCliErrorReason(StrEnum):
    TIMEOUT = "timeout"
    KILLED = "killed"
    SPAWN = "spawn"

class StatsCliError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, reason: StatsCliErrorReason, message: str): ...
```

**Return contract**: Return (returncode, stdout, stderr) tuple. For normal success, returncode=0. Nonzero returns the code (caller decides whether to raise or handle).

**Test patch migration**: When moving subprocess calls from a handler to a launcher, update ALL test patches from `original.module.asyncio` → `new.module.asyncio`. Keep attribute-level patching (`patch.object(module, "create_subprocess_exec")`), NEVER whole-module asyncio mocks.

This pattern was applied to StatsHandler web mode generation and cleanup, replacing duplicated subprocess invocations in `_handleWebMode` and `_dtStatsPagesCleanup`.

title: Test patch target migration when extracting code
content:
When extracting subprocess or async code from a module into a new location, ALL test patches must be updated to reflect the new import path.

**Pattern**: If code moves from `moduleA.submodule` to `moduleB.submodule`, update test patches:

```python
# OLD (before extraction)
with unittest.mock.patch.object(
    internal.bot.common.handlers.stats.asyncio,
    "create_subprocess_exec",
    return_value=mockProc
):

# NEW (after extraction)
with unittest.mock.patch.object(
    lib.stats.stats_pages.launcher.asyncio,
    "create_subprocess_exec",
    return_value=mockProc
):
```

**Key rules**:
1. Keep attribute-level patching (`patch.object(module, "function")`), NEVER whole-module mocks
2. Add import for new module at top of test file: `import lib.stats.stats_pages.launcher`
3. Update EVERY occurrence (use grep to find all patches)
4. Comments saying "Patch ONLY create_subprocess_exec, not the whole asyncio module" remain relevant

**Case study**: StatsHandler web mode subprocess extraction required updating 11 test patches in `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_stats.py` from `internal.bot.common.handlers.stats.asyncio` to `lib.stats.stats_pages.launcher.asyncio`.

**Why this matters**: Tests patch the asyncio import location. If the import location changes but tests don't update, patches hit the wrong code path and tests fail or pass incorrectly.

title: Design deviation documentation pattern
content:
When implementing a design, document deviations from the original specification in the design document's Amendments section with explicit date, scope, and mitigations.

**Pattern** (as seen in `docs/design/stats-display-v1.md` after U11 at line 107):
```markdown
## Amendments (2026-08-18, user round 3 — user-ratified; U11 later the same day)

[existing amendments...]

**Deviation 2026-08-18 (Gate-1 Round B P3b)** — D11's "grouping logic exists exactly once" not fully achieved: The reply-text renderers and the payload builders remain two pipelines (unification deferred — follow-up candidate). Mitigations shipped: chatList condition aligned (FIX 4), possiblyIncomplete propagated into payload sections (FIX 5), averages now correct (FIX 1), subprocess mechanics extracted to `lib/stats/stats_pages/launcher.py` (satisfying the "exactly once" principle at the subprocess level).
```

**Required elements**:
- Date of deviation
- Gate/round identifier (if applicable)
- Specific design element being deviated from (cite the original D-section/number)
- What was NOT achieved (the deviation)
- What was deferred vs skipped
- Mitigations actually shipped (what makes the deviation acceptable)

**Do NOT**:
- Renumber existing sections
- Touch other parts of the document
- Hand-wave the deviation (be explicit about what's deferred)

**Run `make check-docs`** after adding deviation notes to verify markdown links resolve.

**Why document**: Enables future follow-up work (the "follow-up candidate" is now searchable), prevents re-opening closed debates, and maintains audit trail for design-vs-implementation gaps.

title: StatsHandler reply vs payload alignment pattern: chatList condition must match predicates
content:
Pattern: when a feature has both an in-bot reply path and a web-page payload path, data-inclusion predicates must be exactly aligned — and code comments or design-doc notes claiming alignment are NOT substitutes for verifying the actual predicates (a prior round added an alignment comment without changing the code).

StatsHandler chatList ("Ваши чаты") case: reply and payload conditions initially diverged (payload keyed on positionalChatIdUsed, reply on section + filterUserId). After the fix, both use the identical four-conjunct predicate — stats.py:597-601 (reply) and :1133-1138 (payload):

`chatType == PRIVATE and section == "messages" and filterUserId is None and positionalChatIdUsed is False`

Remaining design tension worth knowing: the web page always renders all sections from the raw-rows payload, yet chatList presence still depends on the REQUESTED section == "messages" (predicate copied verbatim from the reply path) — so `/stats --section=llm --web` produces a page without a chat list.

Testing-gap lesson: the original e2e test mocked getUserChats → [], making it blind to the condition; dedicated payload regression tests now assert presence/absence per conjunct (tests/bot/common/handlers/test_stats_payload_regression.py:286-399).

title: TypedDict field name verification: .get() usage hides misalignment from pyright
content:
When replacing `dict[str, Any]` with TypedDicts in payload structures, verify field names manually against what the renderer actually READS. If the renderer uses `.get()` with defaults (common in `lib/stats/stats_pages/generator.py`), a misaligned TypedDict field name will NOT be caught by pyright—the TypedDict type is never actually used at the read site.

Pattern from `lib/stats/stats_pages/generator.py`:
- `_renderMessagesSection` reads: `totalMessages, totalLength, userMessages, botMessages, historyMessages, avgLength, topUsers, topTypes`
- TypedDict `MessagesSectionData` defines: all of the above + `possiblyIncomplete`
- Field names must match exactly—typos or renames in the TypedDict won't raise errors if the renderer uses `.get()` with fallbacks

Verification approach: grep the renderer for all `.get()` calls and direct subscript accesses, cross-reference with TypedDict field names. Do not rely on type checking alone.

Gotcha: `StatsPayload.sections` remained `dict[str, dict[str, Any]]` (top-level not strongly typed) while section sub-dicts were TypedDict-annotated. This creates a type boundary where misalignment slips through.

title: Honesty flag (possiblyIncomplete) propagation pattern: query → payload → render
content:
The stats 'honesty line' (warns the user when query results hit the 10000-row limit) must propagate through THREE layers; the current mechanism (post-U12-9, verified 2026-08-21):

1. **Query/payload layer** (stats.py `_buildStatsPayload` ~lines 1116-1118, 1183-1184): truncation is detected BEFORE consumer filtering (`if len(queriedRows) == 10000: truncatedEventTypes.append(eventType)`) and shipped as `truncatedEventTypes: list[str]` in the payload (NotRequired field of StatsPayload). Per-section `possiblyIncomplete` booleans are GONE — one flat list covers all event types including stt_request.
2. **Render layer** (generator.py `_shouldShowHonestyLine` lines 159-180): each section renderer checks `eventType in truncatedEventTypes` OR the legacy fallback `len(rows) == 10000`, and emits '⚠ Результаты могут быть неполными (достигнут лимит запроса)'. The earlier P3b gap (renderer never read the flag) is FIXED — the render side is now wired.
3. **Reply path** (non-web): each _buildXSection computes `possiblyIncomplete = len(rows) == 10000` locally and appends '⚠ результаты возможно неполные'.

Verification rule (still valid): when adding honesty signalling, grep BOTH the payload builder AND the renderer for the signal (truncatedEventTypes now). If the renderer doesn't read it, the chain is broken and the user-visible symptom persists despite green payload-layer tests.

title: Subprocess launcher pattern: wait_for + kill ordering, errors="replace", exception hierarchy
content:
Pattern from `lib/stats/stats_pages/launcher.py` for Python async subprocess management with timeout:

```python
proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
    *argv,
    stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
    stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
    stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
)

try:
    stdout, _ = await asyncio.wait_for(proc.communicate(stdin_bytes), timeout=timeout)
    returncode = proc.returncode
except asyncio.TimeoutError:
    proc.kill()
    try:
        await proc.wait()
    except Exception:
        pass  # Ignore errors cleaning up a dead process
    raise StatsCliError(StatsCliErrorReason.TIMEOUT, f"Command timed out after {timeout}s")
finally:
    if returncode is None:
        proc.kill()
        try:
            await proc.wait()
        except Exception:
            pass

stdout_text = stdout.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
if returncode is not None and returncode != 0:
    raise StatsCliError(StatsCliErrorReason.NONZERO_EXIT, f"Command exited with code {returncode}")
```

Key requirements:
1. **Ordering**: `wait_for()` → on timeout `kill()` → `await wait()` (to reap zombie) → raise. The final kill in `finally` handles the `returncode=None` case.
2. **errors="replace"**: On decode to prevent `UnicodeDecodeError` from binary output
3. **Exception hierarchy**: `StatsCliError` must NOT be caught by `except OSError` (they're not subclasses). Use separate `except` blocks: `except asyncio.TimeoutError` for timeout, outer `except OSError` for spawn failures.

Gotcha: In Python 3.12+, `asyncio.TimeoutError` is an alias of built-in `TimeoutError`. Tests patching `create_subprocess_exec` at attribute level (not whole-module) keep `wait_for` real—real `TimeoutError` propagates through.

title: CHANGELOG entry timing: user-facing features require entry before commit
content:
Per AGENTS.md: "After any feature, behavior change, schema migration, or user-facing bug fix, add a one-line entry under ## [Unreleased] in CHANGELOG.md as part of the same change, before committing."

Critical to check for user-facing changes:
- New commands or command flags (e.g., `--web` flag becoming functional)
- New configuration options
- Behavior changes visible to operators or end users

The P3b web tier diff made `--web` a working, config-gated feature (subprocess generation, TTL deletion, rate limiting) but did not update CHANGELOG.md. The existing Unreleased entry still described `--web` as "(interim disabled reply until Phase 3)"—outdated before the commit even happened.

Verification: Check CHANGELOG.md:## [Unreleased] sections when reviewing user-facing feature diffs. If the diff enables or exposes new functionality, a changelog entry must be present in the same uncommitted tree.

Location: CHANGELOG.md (review point: docs/design/stats-display-v1.md:107 deviation note doesn't replace changelog)

title: chatList payload condition alignment bug in stats handler
content:
Bug (fixed): StatsHandler web-tier chatList payload condition diverged from the reply path. Current aligned state (stats.py:1133-1138) — chatList is included in the payload only when ALL FOUR conjuncts hold:

`chatType == ChatType.PRIVATE and filterUserId is None and positionalChatIdUsed is False and section == "messages"`

This matches the reply path verbatim (stats.py:597-601); the payload code comment says "match reply path condition exactly". Note the condition evolved after the original fix (which used only private ∧ filterUserId is None): the positionalChatIdUsed and section conjuncts were added later — always verify the current predicate before writing tests.

Regression tests: tests/bot/common/handlers/test_stats_payload_regression.py:286-399 covers five cases — all conditions met → chatList present; filterUserId set → absent; positional chatId used → absent; non-messages section → absent; group chat → absent.

Lesson: comments claiming "match reply path condition" must be verified against actual predicate code; when web and reply paths share inclusion logic, keep code AND comments synchronized.

title: TypedDict construction: prefer direct instantiation over dict + type-ignore
content:
Constructing TypedDict instances: never use `# type: ignore[assignment]` to force a plain dict into a TypedDict-typed target. Two type-safe shapes are accepted in this repo:

1. **Annotated dict literal** (dominant pattern, e.g. internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py:1168):
```python
payload: StatsPayload = {
    "userId": str(userId),
    ...
    "rows": rows,
}
```

2. **TypedDict constructor call** (keyword-arg form, returns a plain dict at runtime but is fully checked):
```python
sttData = SttSectionData(totalRequests=int(x), errorRequests=int(y))
```

Either way the type checker verifies every key/value against the TypedDict, so no suppression is needed. Suppression (`# type: ignore[assignment]`) only hides a real mismatch (wrong field name, wrong value type, or missing required key) and rots into a stale ignore once the types are fixed.

Historical note: the original instance of this anti-pattern was fixed in stats.py on 2026-08-18 by removing type-ignore comments and constructing the (now-deleted) SttSectionData directly; the section-data pipeline itself was later removed in the U12 W2b rows-based payload rework, so use current stats.py payload construction as the reference example.

title: Russian pluralization pattern for stats messages
content:
Russian pluralization is non-trivial and requires proper case handling in user-facing strings — the simplified single-form-for-all-numbers approach produces incorrect results like "1 часов" instead of "1 час".

**Correct 3-form Russian declension:**
- n % 10 == 1 and n % 100 != 11: singular (час, запрос, секунда)
- 2 <= n % 10 <= 4 and not (12 <= n % 100 <= 14): paucal (часа, запроса, секунды)
- else: plural (часов, запросов, секунд)

Reusable helper shape (write it inline or as a local helper where needed):
```python
def formatRussianPlural(n: int, forms: tuple[str, str, str]) -> str:
    if n % 10 == 1 and n % 100 != 11:
        return f"{n} {forms[0]}"
    elif 2 <= n % 10 <= 4 and not (12 <= n % 100 <= 14):
        return f"{n} {forms[1]}"
    else:
        return f"{n} {forms[2]}"
```

**Historical note:** formatRussianPlural/formatHours helpers previously lived in internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py for rate-limit refusal messages, but were REMOVED in U12-6 when the refusal path was replaced by applyLimit-only (no refusal reply is ever rendered). Repo-wide grep confirms neither helper exists in code anymore — do not look for them; re-create locally if a future user-facing message needs pluralized counts.

title: Element-level generate-command validation pattern
content:
**Validation pattern:** When validating generate-command in stats-pages configuration, element-level validation is required beyond just checking that the list is non-empty.

**Validation code in stats.py ~:162-175:**
```python
# Validate generate-command (must be non-empty list[str] of non-empty strings)
generateCommand = statsPagesConfig.get("generate-command")
if (
    not generateCommand
    or not isinstance(generateCommand, list)
    or len(generateCommand) == 0
    or any(not isinstance(item, str) or not item.strip() for item in generateCommand)
):
    raise RuntimeError(
        "[stats-pages] generate-command must be a non-empty list of non-empty strings when enabled"
    )
```

**Tests added:**
- Test with integer element: `generate-command = [123]` → RuntimeError
- Test with whitespace-only element: `generate-command = [" "]` → RuntimeError

**Lessons:**
- Element-level validation prevents subtle bugs from wrong types or empty strings
- Use `any(not isinstance(item, str) or not item.strip() for item in items)` pattern
- Validation should be at construction time (StatsHandler.__init__) for early failure
- Tests lock in validation behavior to prevent regressions

title: Vestigial test imports pattern cleanup
content:
**Gotcha:** Test files can accumulate vestigial imports over time when patching patterns change. Comments claiming imports are "for patching" may no longer be accurate.

**Example removed:**
```python
import internal.bot.common.handlers.stats  # noqa: F401 (imported for patching asyncio)
```

This import was vestigial because patching went through the launcher path (lib.stats.stats_pages.launcher), not the stats handler module itself.

**Cleanup pattern:**
1. Search for imports with `# noqa: F401 ...` comments
2. Verify they are actually used by the patch decorators in the test
3. Remove truly unused imports and update comments if needed

**Affected files:**
- tests/bot/common/handlers/test_stats.py (line ~9)
- tests/bot/common/handlers/test_stats_payload_regression.py (line ~9)

**Lessons:**
- Vestigial imports create clutter and mask actual dependencies
- Comments explaining "imported for patching" must be kept in sync with code
- Regular audit of noqa: F401 imports helps maintain test hygiene

title: Redundant attribute assignment in handler subclasses
content:
**Gotcha:** Handler subclasses may redundantly assign attributes that are already set by their parent class's __init__ method.

**Example removed:**
```python
# In StatsHandler.__init__ (line ~151)
self.botProvider = botProvider  # This is redundant!
```

**Parent class already sets it (BaseBotHandler.__init__ at ~159):**
```python
self.botProvider = botProvider
```

**Pattern to check:**
When subclassing BaseBotHandler, check what BaseBotHandler.__init__ already assigns to avoid duplication.

**Lessons:**
- Redundant assignments waste CPU cycles and increase cognitive load
- Check parent class __init__ before assigning in subclass
- If the assignment is truly needed for clarity, add a comment explaining why

title: F821 lint error in test files with mock.patch.object module paths
content:
When using `unittest.mock.patch.object(lib.some.module.attribute, ...)` in test files, you must import the module at the top of the test file. The flake8 F821 error "undefined name 'lib'" occurs when the import statement is missing but the reference exists in mock.patch.object() calls.

**Example**: In `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_stats.py`, lines 1340, 1411, 1496, 1594, 1661, 1730, 1791, 1863, 1934, 1982, 2026 all had:
```python
unittest.mock.patch.object(lib.stats.stats_pages.launcher.asyncio, "create_subprocess_exec", ...)
```

The fix was to add `import lib.stats.stats_pages.launcher` at the top of the file (line 15). After `make format`, isort orders it correctly.

This is a common pattern when mocking asyncio subprocess calls in tests.

title: Stats payload test mock setup - getUserChats must be AsyncMock for PRIVATE chat type
content:
When testing `StatsHandler._buildStatsPayload()` with `ChatType.PRIVATE` and `filterUserId=None`, the method internally calls `await self.getUserChats(userId)` (at stats.py ~1093). If the mock database doesn't have `chatUsers.getUserChats` properly configured as an AsyncMock, it will raise a TypeError.

**Fix pattern** (from tests/bot/common/handlers/test_stats_payload_regression.py):
```python
mockDatabase = MagicMock()
mockDatabase.chatUsers.getUserChats = AsyncMock(return_value=[])
handler = StatsHandler(configManager=mockConfigManager, database=mockDatabase, ...)
```

Without this AsyncMock setup, calling `_buildStatsPayload` with PRIVATE chat type fails because `getUserChats()` is an async method that requires an awaitable.

Related memory 980fc868 documents the wrapper default parameter pattern for getUserChats, but this is the specific async mock setup requirement.

title: Russian pluralization in test assertions - match exact production form
content:
When writing test assertions for Russian error messages, ensure the pluralization form matches what production code generates. Russian plural forms are complex and depend on the number's ending:

- 1, 21, 31, etc.: singular form (e.g., "запрос")
- 2-4, 22-24, 32-34, etc.: "за/я" form (e.g., "запроса")
- 5-20, 25-30, etc.: plural "ов/ей" form (e.g., "запросов")

**Example fix** (tests/bot/common/handlers/test_stats.py):
- Expected: "3 запросов за 1 час" (wrong - this is for numbers ending in 5-20)
- Actual: "3 запроса за 1 час" (correct - 3 ends in 3, so use "запроса")

Test assertion was updated from `"3 запросов за 1 час"` to `"3 запроса за 1 час"` to match the actual error message from RateLimiterService.

This pattern applies to any Russian text assertions in tests.

title: Gromozeka documentation sync process - change classification matrix
content:
When syncing documentation after code changes, use the `update-project-docs` skill which provides a decision matrix mapping change types to doc files. Key mappings:

- Handler behavior change → `docs/llm/handlers.md` (update the handler row)
- Config consumption change → `docs/llm/configuration.md` (flip tense from FUTURE to PRESENT, remove "lands in Phase X" hedges, verify validation descriptions match implementation)
- New library file → `docs/llm/libraries.md` § (layout table + exports) + `docs/llm/index.md` §4 lib map (one-line entry)
- Queue-service enum member → `docs/llm/services.md` (if DelayedTaskFunction members are enumerated)

Process rules:
1. Verify claims against source code BEFORE writing docs (re-derive from code, don't trust previous doc text)
2. Edit ONLY `*.md` files (no code changes by docs-writer)
3. After edits, run `make check-docs` (must be 0 broken links) and `make lint` (must be clean)
4. Perform bulk stale-value sweep: grep all docs/ for remaining draft language ("interim", "lands in Phase X", "will invoke", etc.)
5. Design doc status lines: per-phase commit-hash updates are done at commit time by committer, not during doc sync
6. Scope exclusions: CHANGELOG.md (handled separately), .opencode/**, docs/archive/**, docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md
7. Root README.md and developer-guide.md staleness checks: only update if they actually cover the changed feature
8. When fixing enumerated lists (like DelayedTaskFunction members), fix ALL missing members found during edit (code wins principle)

title: StatsHandler --web command implementation details
content:
The StatsHandler --web/stats_web flow (as of 2026-08-20, post-U12):

**Construction-time (stats.py:130-194):**
- Reads [stats.pages] config via ConfigManager.getStatsPagesConfig() (reads self.get("stats.pages", {}), manager.py:533)
- If enabled=true: fail-loud RuntimeError validation — generate-command and delete-command must be non-empty list[str] of non-empty strings (element-level), ttl-hours positive int. NOTE: base-url is NO LONGER validated or present (removed by U12-4/U12-5 — URL composition belongs to the CLI's --base-url arg); ratelimiter-queue is read with default "stats-pages" without cross-validation.
- Registers _dtStatsPagesCleanup for DelayedTaskFunction.STATS_PAGES_CLEANUP
- If enabled=false: no validation/registration; --web sends informative "disabled" reply (stats.py:349-358)

**Runtime flow (stats.py:1212-1398), in order:**
1. U12-6 rate limiting: applyLimit-ONLY — `await RateLimiterManager.getInstance().applyLimit(queue, f"stats-pages-{issuingChatId}")`. NO getStats pre-check, NO refusal reply; exceeded requests sleep until a slot frees. (No-limiter RuntimeError is covered by the outer D15 wrap.)
2. Build in-chat brief via _buildStatsReply first ("reply always wins"); brief build failure → error reply, no generation.
3. Build payload via _buildStatsPayload: queries all 5 event types at limit=10000, tracks truncatedEventTypes PRE-filter, applies consumer filter ({str(targetChatId)}, excludes __global__) and user filter (message/command/llm_tool_call only), includes chatList when private ∧ no user filter ∧ no positional chatId ∧ messages section.
4. Argv substitution via str.format_map with {user_id}, {chat_id}, {platform} (KeyError/AttributeError → config-error failure note + brief).
5. Subprocess via runCliCommand (lib/stats/stats_pages/launcher.py), 30s timeout, stdin JSON payload. StatsCliError(TIMEOUT/SPAWN) → failure note + brief.
6. Parse stdout {"pageId", "url"} (U12-5 key); url used VERBATIM as the link (no bot-side composition, stats.py:1377-1378).
7. Schedule ONE persisted one-shot deletion task (function=DelayedTaskFunction.STATS_PAGES_CLEANUP, kwargs={"pageId", "command": resolved delete argv}, skipDB=False); scheduling failure → WARNING, link still delivered (R13).
8. Send brief with "📊 Страница: {url}" appended.

title: QueueService no-handler re-delay pattern
content:
When QueueService's delayed-queue loop pops a task whose DelayedTaskFunction has no registered handler, the task is re-delayed by 60 seconds in memory rather than discarded.

Implementation: internal/services/queue_service/service.py:385-388
```python
if delayedTask.function not in self.tasksHandlers:
    logger.error(f"No handlers for {delayedTask.function} registered, delaying task for 60 seconds...")
    delayedTask.delayedUntil = time.time() + 60
    await self.delayedActionsQueue.put(delayedTask)
```
(Note: the registry attribute is `self.tasksHandlers` (NOT `delayedTaskHandlers`); the log level is `error` (NOT `warning`); there is no `task_done()`/`continue` inside this branch — `task_done()` runs later at :406.)

IMPORTANT CAVEAT: the loop's unconditional `updateDelayedTask(delayedTask.taskId, True)` at service.py:401-402 executes after BOTH branches, so the DB row is marked done on the FIRST no-handler firing. The task survives only in memory for the current process lifetime; after a restart it is NOT restored (getPendingDelayedTasks filters is_done=False, delayed_tasks.py:260-264). So this pattern does NOT make pending tasks safe across restarts when the handler is unregistered — config-gated handlers get re-registered only at construction time.

Used by: StatsHandler registers its STATS_PAGES_CLEANUP handler only when [stats-pages] enabled=true (internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py:192-194); a pending cleanup task scheduled before a disable spins in this path until restart, then vanishes (accepted R13 risk, documented in docs/llm/services.md:138).

title: lib/stats/stats_pages launcher subprocess helper
content:
`lib/stats/stats_pages/launcher.py` provides a shared subprocess launcher for stats-pages CLI:

**API**:
```python
async def runCliCommand(
    argv: List[str], 
    *, 
    stdinPayload: Optional[str] = None, 
    timeoutSeconds: float = 30.0
) -> Tuple[Optional[int], str, str]:
    """Returns (returncode, stdout, stderr)"""
```

**Error handling**:
- Empty `argv` → returns `(None, "", "")` (no subprocess)
- Timeout (30s default) → kills subprocess, raises `StatsCliError(reason=TIMEOUT, message="...")`
- Spawn failure (e.g., executable not found) → raises `StatsCliError(reason=SPAWN, message="...")`

**Conventions**:
- Uses `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec` with `stdin=PIPE`, `stdout=PIPE`, `stderr=PIPE`
- Stdout/stderr decoded with `errors="replace"` to avoid decode errors
- Mirrors subprocess conventions from `internal/services/proxy/lifecycle.py:105-150`

**Usage**:
- Generation: StatsHandler calls it with generate-command argv and JSON payload
- Deletion: `_dtStatsPagesCleanup` calls it with delete-command argv (no stdin)

**Note**: There's a minor docstring drift in `StatsCliError.__doc__` mentioning "TIMEOUT, KILLED, SPAWN" but `StatsCliErrorReason` only defines TIMEOUT and SPAWN.

title: .opencode files in commit workflows: memory.jsonl vs opencode.json distinction
content:
When committing changes, two .opencode files have different staging rules:

**`.opencode/memory.jsonl`**: Auto-managed by the opencode system; "rides along" with commits. It IS git-tracked (confirmed via `git ls-files .opencode`) and IS normally committed as part of regular git flow. **Never read it** - stage it blindly when it appears in git status. The file is automatically re-dirtied by tooling after commits (expected behavior).

**`.opencode/opencode.json`**: git-TRACKED shared project configuration (opencode default agent, per-agent model routing, MCP servers) - NOT a user-local-only file (verified 2026-08-20: listed by `git ls-files .opencode` and absent from .gitignore). Local edits to it are ordinary repo changes and are normally committed with the rest of the work. Only exclude it (leave dirty, report as excluded) when the user explicitly instructs it for their local edits - exclusion is per user instruction, not a property of the file.

Note: the only .opencode paths gitignored in this repo are `.opencode/audit` and `.opencode/memory-audit-manifest.json` (.gitignore lines 51-52); everything else under .opencode/ (agents/, commands/, memory-config.jsonc, memory.jsonl, opencode.json, profiles.json) is tracked.

title: Test/Prod Parity Gap Pattern: Fixtures Can Encode Production Bugs
content:
When adding regression tests for data-display features (like stats web pages), the test fixtures can inadvertently encode the same bugs that exist in production code. This creates a false green: tests pass because fixture data matches the buggy code, not because the code is correct.

**Example from Phase 3b review (2026-08-18):**
- Production code: `sumMetric("total_length")` at stats.py:1189 (WRONG key)
- Recording site: `text_length` at base.py:1160 (CORRECT key)
- Test fixture: Used `"total_length"` in test_stats_payload_regression.py:134,148 (encoded the bug)

Result: Tests passed while every generated page showed "Total Characters 0" and "Average Message Length 0.00".

**Pattern:** When writing regression tests for data that crosses layers (handler → database → aggregation), verify the fixture keys/labels match the RECORDING sites, not just the CONSUMING sites. Build fixtures from the actual recording vocabulary (constants from recording modules) or add a shared constants module for metric/label names.

**Detection clue:** If tests pass immediately after a supposed fix, but the fix changed keys/names, check if test fixtures use the same wrong keys. A correct regression test should FAIL before the fix and PASS after.

title: Three-Way Match Verification Pattern for Multi-Layer Features
content:
When reviewing features that cross multiple layers (e.g., payload builder → TypedDict → consumer), verify the match at THREE seams, not two:

1. **Payload fields ↔ TypedDict definitions** — builder output matches TypedDict schema
2. **TypedDict ↔ Consumer readers** — consumer reads exactly what TypedDict declares
3. **Handler → Database seam** — handler's metric/label keys match recording sites

**Example from Phase 3b review (2026-08-18):**
- Payload field names ↔ TypedDicts ↔ Generator readers: ✅ All matched
- Handler → Database seam: ❌ Broken (`total_length` vs `text_length`, `providerName` vs `provider`)

The first two seams are easy to verify in code (typed dicts, obvious readers). The third seam (handler → recording sites) requires checking the recording modules (base.py, ai/abstract.py, stt/abstract.py) or migrations to find the actual keys/labels used.

**Verification checklist for such features:**
- [ ] Payload builder field names match TypedDict required fields
- [ ] TypedDict field names match consumer's .get() calls
- [ ] Handler's metric keys match recording site (grep metric name in repo)
- [ ] Handler's label keys match recording site (grep label name in repo)
- [ ] Test fixtures use recording-site vocabulary, not handler vocabulary

title: D15 Failure Contract Gap: Pre-Brief Exceptions Lose the Brief
content:
When a feature has a "brief + failure note" contract (brief delivered first, then failure note appended), exceptions raised BEFORE the brief is sent can violate the contract: the outer catch assumes the brief was already sent and may only send the failure note.

**Detection heuristic (still valid):** look for outer exception handlers with comments like "Brief was already sent" — verify all exception-raising code paths before the brief send are locally handled.

**Current stats.py state (verified 2026-08-20, `internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py` `_handleWebMode`):** most pre-brief sections ARE now locally handled:
- `_buildStatsReply` wrapped locally (1253-1274): on failure sends "❌ Ошибка при запросе статистики." alone (no brief exists yet) and returns.
- `_buildStatsPayload` wrapped locally (1277-1298): on failure sends the already-built brief + "⚠ Генерация веб-страницы не удалась." via `_appendWebSuffix`.
- `runCliCommand` / argv formatting / JSON parsing failures (1307-1375): all send brief + failure note.
- The ONLY deliberate exception: `applyLimit` (line 1250) runs before the brief is built with NO local try/except — comment at 1249 says the outer D15 wrap (376-385) covers the no-limiter RuntimeError, sending the bare note alone. This trade-off is documented at line 378.

**Fix pattern when the contract matters:** wrap each pre-brief exception-possible section in local try/except that sends brief + note when a brief exists, or a standalone note when it does not.

title: Queue Service No-Handler Path Marks Task Done Immediately
content:
The delayed task queue's no-handler re-delay behavior (service.py:385-388) has a subtle nuance: the task is marked done in the DB immediately on the first no-handler firing (line 401-402), even though it continues to re-delay in memory every 60s.

**Consequence:** A pending task cannot survive a process restart even if the handler would be registered after restart. Because:
1. No-handler fires → task re-queued in memory + DB row marked done
2. Process restarts → in-memory queue lost → DB row already done → not restored
3. Handler registers after restart → task never arrives

**Practical impact:** For `STATS_PAGES_CLEANUP` tasks fired when [stats-pages] is disabled, the task spins in memory until restart, then vanishes → orphaned page file. This is an accepted risk (R13), but documentation claiming "task waits until re-enabled" is misleading because re-enabling requires a restart (NG6) and that restart destroys the task.

**Recovery semantics:** No-handler tasks survive within the same process lifetime but are lost across restart. Design documentation should reflect this reality.

**Code location:** `internal/services/queue_service/service.py:385-388` (re-delay) and `:401-402` (unconditional mark-done).

title: RateLimiterManager Falls Back to Default Limiter for Unmapped Queues
content:
When a queue name is not in RateLimiterManager._queueMappings, the manager silently falls back to the default limiter (lib/rate_limiter/manager.py:293-301). No warning or error is logged.

Actual code shape:
```python
def _getLimiterForQueue(self, queue: str) -> RateLimiterInterface:
    if not self._rateLimiters:
        raise RuntimeError("No rate limiters registered")
    if queue in self._queueMappings:
        return self._rateLimiters[self._queueMappings[queue]]
    if self._defaultLimiter is None:
        raise RuntimeError("No default rate limiter set")
    return self._rateLimiters[self._defaultLimiter]  # Silent fallback
```

Impact on stats web tier:
- Configured queue: ratelimiter-queue = "stats-pages" (stats.py:189; bound in configs/00-defaults/00-config.toml [ratelimiter.queues])
- A typo'd queue name → unmapped → default limiter (10/60s) instead of stats-pages (3/600s): rate limiting still works but with wrong limits
- Keys are still distinct ("stats-pages-<chatId>", stats.py:1245), so no collision — just wrong limits

RuntimeError paths are NOT caught at the call site: stats.py:1250 calls applyLimit with no try/except (U12-6: applyLimit-only, NO pre-check, NO refusal reply). The old ValueError-only getStats handler no longer exists; a no-limiter RuntimeError propagates to the outer D15 wrap → bare failure note (no brief).

Design consideration (still open): silent fallback means config typos don't crash the bot but produce wrong rate-limit behavior. Consider adding a warning log for unmapped queue fallback.

title: Stats payload builder used wrong metric key for message length
content: The `_buildMessagesSectionData` method in `internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py` (~line 1189) incorrectly called `analyzerAll.sumMetric("total_length")`. The actual metric recorded in the database (via `lib/stats/base.py:1160` and `migration_027` backfill) is `text_length`. This caused average length calculations to fail. Fixed by changing to `sumMetric("text_length")`. Test fixtures in `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_stats_payload_regression.py` (~lines 134, 148) also incorrectly used `total_length` and were updated to `text_length` to ensure regression tests actually exercise the seam.

title: Stats payload provider lookup used wrong label key
content: The `topProviders` aggregation in `internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py` (lines ~1371 and 1401) used `topN("providerName", ...)`. However, the actual labels recorded in `lib/ai/abstract.py` (line ~880 for LLM) and `lib/stt/abstract.py` (line ~256 for STT) use the key `provider`, not `providerName`. This caused the top provider lists to always be empty in the stats web display. Fixed by changing the key to `topN("provider", "request_count", 3)` in both LLM and STT sections.

title: D15 requirement: Brief message must be sent even on web tier failure
content:
D15 in the web tier (internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py _handleWebMode + the statsCommand web branch): the in-chat brief reply must be preserved and delivered even when subsequent web-tier processing fails. Current implementation (verified 2026-08-21):

1. Rate limiting is applyLimit-ONLY (U12-6, no getStats pre-check/refusal). The no-limiter RuntimeError is NOT caught here — it propagates to the outer D15 wrap in statsCommand (lines ~360-385), which sends '⚠ Генерация веб-страницы не удалась.' alone (correct: the brief was never built).
2. Brief construction (`_buildStatsReply`) is wrapped in try/except — on failure, an error reply is sent and web mode aborts.
3. `_buildStatsPayload` is wrapped in try/except — on failure, the already-built brief IS sent, with '⚠ Генерация веб-страницы не удалась.' appended via `_appendWebSuffix`.
4. All later failure paths (generate-command placeholder errors, StatsCliError TIMEOUT/SPAWN, nonzero exit, invalid stdout JSON) send the brief + a specific one-line failure note; nothing raises out of the web path.

Design rule: ordering matters — rate limit first, brief second, payload/subprocess after — so every failure point knows whether the brief exists to append to.

title: QueueService no-handler path marks task done in DB after first retry
content: When a delayed task (e.g., `STATS_PAGES_CLEANUP`) fires but no handler is registered (e.g., stats feature disabled), the QueueService's no-handler path (service.py ~line 401) calls `updateDelayedTask(taskId, True)` which marks the DB row as done, even though it re-delays the task in memory for the process lifetime. Consequently, if the application restarts while the handler remains disabled, the task is gone from the DB and is not re-queued, leaving associated resources (e.g., generated stats page files) orphaned. This corrects previous documentation that implied tasks wait indefinitely for handler re-enabling across restarts.

title: Type annotation pattern for stats handler methods
content: The `_buildStatsPayload` method in `internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py` (line 1036) uses a concrete TypedDict type (`StatsPayload`) rather than the generic `dict` for its return annotation. `StatsPayload` is imported from `lib.stats.stats_pages` alongside other TypedDict types used in the stats system (`ChatListEntry`, `CommandsSectionData`, `LlmSectionData`, `MessagesSectionData`, `SttSectionData`, `ToolsSectionData`). Using concrete types provides better type safety and documentation than generic `dict`.

title: MarkdownV2 splitting hazard: automatic message splitting can corrupt formatting
content:
Hazard (still valid): sendMessage(splitIfTooLong=True, tryMarkdownV2=True) (internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py:576/584) converts to MarkdownV2 BEFORE splitting; a split boundary landing on a MarkdownV2 special character (_, *, [, etc.) corrupts the formatting of the resulting chunks. If you rely on auto-splitting for long MarkdownV2 content, either pass tryMarkdownV2=False or ensure the split respects syntax boundaries.

StatsHandler's current mitigation (CHANGED from the old _MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH=2500 truncation — that constant no longer exists): _OUTPUT_CHUNK_LENGTH = 3000 (stats.py:95) with whole-line chunk accumulation in _buildStatsReply (stats.py:620-641) — lines are buffered and flushed as complete-line chunks, returned as str | list[str], and sent per-chunk via _sendStatsReply (stats.py:643+). No mid-line/mid-syntax splitting, no truncation.

title: DELETE_DENIED_COMMANDS chat setting behavior and enforcement sites
content:
The DELETE_DENIED_COMMANDS chat setting (ChatSettingsKey.DELETE_DENIED_COMMANDS, kebab-case config key "delete-denied-commands", default false in configs/00-defaults/bot-defaults.toml:96) controls whether denied command messages are automatically deleted.

When setting is TRUE:
- Only deletes the USER'S command message (no reply sent to inform user)
- Deletion wrapped in try/except to log errors but not fail the operation
- Execution: `await handlerObj.deleteMessage(ensuredMessage)`

When setting is FALSE:
- User's command message is NOT deleted
- Handler simply returns False (no reply sent)

Enforced in two locations in internal/bot/common/handlers/manager.py:
1. Permission-based denial (lines 990-1001)
2. Category-based denial (lines 1025-1036)

Both branches follow identical pattern: check setting → try delete → return False. No informative reply is sent regardless of setting value.

title: @username resolution pattern: getChatUserByUsername with case-insensitive comparison
content:
Best method for @username to userId resolution: ChatUsersRepository.getChatUserByUsername() (internal/database/repositories/chat_users.py:170-200)

Query implementation uses provider.getCaseInsensitiveComparison hook:
```python
caseInsensitiveComparison = sqlProvider.getCaseInsensitiveComparison("username", "username")
row = await sqlProvider.executeFetchOne(
    f"""
    SELECT * FROM chat_users
    WHERE
        chat_id = :chatId
        AND {caseInsensitiveComparison}
    LIMIT 1
""",
    {"chatId": chatId, "username": username},
)
```

Minimal new query shape for @username parsing:
```sql
SELECT user_id FROM chat_users
WHERE chat_id = :chatId
  AND LOWER(username) = LOWER(:username)
LIMIT 1
```

Usage precedents:
- BaseBotHandler._resolveUserId() (internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py:469-531) - used by search_memories and search_messages
- ChatSearchHandler: /search --user=@username (internal/bot/common/handlers/chat_search.py:673)
- UserMemoriesHandler: /add_memory --user=@username (internal/bot/common/handlers/user_memories.py:697)
- SpamHandler: /unban [@username] (internal/bot/common/handlers/spam.py:1630)

Pattern: normalize to @username format before DB lookup, use getCaseInsensitiveComparison for cross-RDBMS portability.

title: JOIN ambiguity gotcha: qualified column names required
content:
When performing SQL JOINs with tables that have overlapping column names (like user_id), you must use qualified column names to avoid "ambiguous column name" errors. 

Example from chat_users.py fix: Changed `user_id` to `cu.user_id` when joining chat_users table to resolve the ambiguity. This is a common SQL gotcha when the same column name exists in multiple joined tables.

title: StatsHandler sectionsToRender conditional logic pattern
content:
StatsHandler uses a conditional sectionsToRender block (lines 582-594) to control which stats sections are included in the output. This pattern:

1. Defines a list of boolean flags for each section (messages, commands, tools, llm)
2. Uses conditional logic to populate sectionsToRender list based on these flags
3. The sectionsToRender list is then iterated to build the final output

This pattern allows flexible section rendering based on configuration, user permissions, or data availability without hardcoding the section order in multiple places.

title: StatsHandler manual truncation to avoid MarkdownV2 corruption
content:
StatsHandler avoids the MarkdownV2 splitting hazard by SENDING PRE-CHUNKED WHOLE-LINE MESSAGES instead of relying on sendMessage(splitIfTooLong=True). Per U12 change (8): the old `_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH` truncation was DELETED and replaced by `_OUTPUT_CHUNK_LENGTH = 3000` (stats.py line 95).

Current mechanism (stats.py `_buildStatsReply` lines 620-641):
1. Accumulate reply lines into chunks; flush a chunk when adding the next line would exceed _OUTPUT_CHUNK_LENGTH
2. Break only at whole-line boundaries (`\n`.join) — never mid-word/mid-character
3. Return `str` when a single chunk suffices, `list[str]` otherwise
4. `_sendStatsReply` sends each chunk as its own message (MarkdownV2 conversion happens per chunk, so split boundaries can never cut through converted escape sequences)
5. `_appendWebSuffix` appends web links/failure notes to the last chunk (or the string) without re-splitting

Why: sendMessage-level splitting after MarkdownV2 conversion can break special characters (_, *, [, `) at split boundaries. Chunking on whole source lines before conversion sidesteps that entirely. Test coverage includes testWebModeChunkedBrief in tests/bot/common/handlers/test_stats.py.

title: StatsHandler deletion-task scheduling pattern
content:
StatsHandler implements delayed deletion task scheduling (lines 1688-1695) following the U11 amendment pattern:

1. Uses scheduleDelayedTask with STATS_PAGES_CLEANUP enum
2. Passes kwargs with pageId and command (resolved delete argv)
3. Uses skipDB=False to persist the task
4. One DB-persisted one-shot delayed deletion task per page scheduled on successful generation

This pattern ensures cleanup happens automatically after the configured TTL without requiring a separate tracking table.

title: U12 stats display design amendments (2026-08-19)
content:
User-ratified round-4 amendments to docs/design/stats-display-v1.md, committed as f0c8464e. Ten sub-decisions all ratified 2026-08-19 (three via question tool):

1. **Period grammar (amends D2):** --period=<N><suffix> or all. Suffixes: h=hours (1..24, hourly), d=days (1..31, daily), m=months (N≥1, CALENDAR months, user-ratified), all=total no range. Range computation: h→from=now−Nh truncated to hour; d→from=now−Nd truncated to day (N+1 buckets incl partial current day); m→from=first-day-of-month N calendar months back; all→no bounds. Old fixed args (1d/7d/30d) subsumed by Nd. Default stays 7d. Out-of-range/bad-suffix→usage error.

2. **--section=all (amends D2/D6):** renders all four sections. sectionsToRender exclusion logic (positional chatId→all sections; --user→llm excluded) REMOVED—chatId only selects target chat; --user only filters (llm renders with its existing chat-level annotation).

3. **--user accepts @username (amends D2/D7):** <id> or @username, case-insensitive, resolved within TARGET chat via ChatUsersRepository.getChatUserByUsername (chat_users.py:170-200, existing case-insensitive LOWER comparison, LIMIT 1; target-chat scope user-ratified). Leading @ stripped; not found→usage error.

4. **Config merge (amends D10/§5):** [stats-pages] section and configs/00-defaults/stats-pages.toml DELETED; all keys move under [stats.pages] in configs/00-defaults/stats.toml. getStatsPagesConfig() reads self.get("stats.pages", {}) (dotted-path get confirmed at manager.py:278-293). base-url key REMOVED entirely (see 5).

5. **CLI contract (amends D11/D12):** generate stdout JSON = {"pageId", "url"} (key id renamed pageId). url is FULL and used VERBATIM by bot (no composition). CLI accepts optional --base-url <url>—operators put it directly in generate-command template; url = base.rstrip("/")+"/"+filename when given, else bare filename.

6. **Rate limiting (SUPERSEDES D13's pre-check+refuse):** applyLimit-only—await RateLimiterManager.getInstance().applyLimit(queue, key) with issuing-chat key, exactly like weather/geocode/yandex client precedents (lib/openweathermap/client.py:470 etc.). NO getStats pre-check (its return is an untyped dict—assuming fields is wrong, user note), NO refusal reply; exceeded requests sleep until slot frees. Limiter config (00-config.toml, already present): stats-pages SlidingWindow windowSeconds 3600→600 (user-ratified shrink; keeps sleeps under 30-min command timeout), maxRequests 3. NOTE: manager-level applyLimit can raise RuntimeError only when no limiter+no default is configured (manager.py:298-299)—left to outer D15 wrap.

7. **DELETE_DENIED_COMMANDS respected (amends D16):** in statsCommand's ALLOW_SHOW_STATS deny branch—when chatSettings[ChatSettingsKey.DELETE_DENIED_COMMANDS].toBool() (key delete-denied-commands, default false, bot-defaults.toml:96)→await self.deleteMessage(ensuredMessage) wrapped in try/except-log (manager.py:990-1001 shape), NO reply; otherwise existing informative reply stands.

8. **Output cap removed (amends D6):** _MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH deleted. Full output delivered via whole-line chunked sendMessage calls (~3000-char chunks, each converted to MarkdownV2 independently—avoids mechanical-split boundary-corruption hazard; platform splitIfTooLong stays as last resort).

9. **Web payload = raw rows (SUPERSEDES D11 'grouping once' deviation note):** bot no longer pre-groups for page. Payload = meta (userId, chatId, chatTitle, chatType, platform, period arg string, periodType, generatedAt) + rows: dict[eventType→list[StatsAggregateDict]] covering five event types + chatList (private scope, same condition as reply). Bot applies ONLY scope filters (consumer=target chat, __global__ excluded) + granularity (periodType) + range + limit=10000. Page renders from rows server-side: per-eventType sections, time-series tables + inline SVG bar charts, NO client-side JS interactivity (user-ratified); label filtering future work. Honesty line: per-eventType len(rows)==10000.

10. **User edits ratified (2026-08-19):** stats.py visibility={CommandPermission.PRIVATE}=HELP-LISTING ONLY (user-confirmed—group execution unchanged); chat-list line format #`chatId` title — N (backticked id); title fallback chain title→username→""; chat list only when NOT positionalChatIdUsed; chat_users.py cu.user_id JOIN-column qualification (bug fix).

Live-section updates: §5 config diff replaced with [stats.pages] child shape, no base-url, stats-pages.toml deleted, limiter 600s; D13 title/body got one-line superseded-by-U12-6 pointer; D14/D12 stdout-contract lines got pageId/url pointers; Phase 3b got one-line revised-by-U12 note. TODO.md added: non-blocking rate-limiter variant task surfaced by stats web tier (U12).

Branch: lib-stat-improvement, HEAD 1a64445d→f0c8464e. Files changed: docs/design/stats-display-v1.md, TODO.md, .opencode/memory.jsonl (staged blind). Post-commit status: stats.py, chat_users.py, .opencode/opencode.json remaining dirty (user's implementation edits, next round's commit).

title: Design doc live-section update pattern for amendments
content:
When amending a design doc with new decisions (like U12 in stats-display-v1.md), add one-line pointer notes to live sections that reference the amendment block. The amendment block itself carries authority; live sections get minimal pointers to avoid contradictions.

Pattern from U12 (2026-08-19):
- Superseded decision headings: append to the italic marker with "; SUPERSEDED YYYY-MM-DD by UN-#: <brief summary>" (e.g., D13's "*(user-ratified purpose; mechanism flagged; unchanged by the 2026-08-18 round; SUPERSEDED 2026-08-19 by U12-6: applyLimit-only — no pre-check, no refusal, windowSeconds 600)*")
- Stdout-contract lines (D12, D14): add parenthetical pointer "*(revised YYYY-MM-DD by UN-#: <key changes>)*"
- Phase/section headings: add blockquote note immediately after heading with "> **Revised by UN (YYYY-MM-DD):** <brief list of changes>. The body below is the <previous-state>."

This approach minimizes edits, preserves historical text, and ensures readers can find the authoritative amendment block. Contrast with full rewrites: the pointer pattern maintains traceability and avoids duplicating complex decision rationales.

Example from U12 Phase 3b note:
> **Revised by U12 (2026-08-19):** payload = raw rows (U12-9), stdout `{"pageId","url"}` used verbatim (U12-5), applyLimit-only rate limiting (U12-6), config under `[stats.pages]` (U12-4). The body below is the 2026-08-18 (U11) state.

This pattern is distinct from the superseded-section banner (blockquote at top of section) used for removed sections—use one-line pointers in-place for amendments, full banners only for deletion.

title: Chunked message sending pattern for long stats output
content:
For delivering long stats output beyond platform message size limits, use whole-line chunked sendMessage calls (~3000-char chunks, each converted to MarkdownV2 independently).

Pattern from U12-8 (stats display v1, 2026-08-19):
- Removed _MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH cap
- Split output into ~3000-character chunks on WHOLE LINES (not mid-sentence)
- Each chunk independently converted to MarkdownV2 before sending
- Avoids mechanical-split boundary-corruption hazard (splitting mid-markdown entity)
- Platform's splitIfTooLong stays as last resort for any remaining overflow

This approach ensures each chunk is a valid, self-contained MarkdownV2 message, improving reliability over naive character-count splitting. The ~3000-char target is conservative to leave headroom for MarkdownV2 expansion.

Contrast with previous _MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH pattern which truncated at a fixed length, losing information. Chunking preserves full content while respecting platform limits.

title: DELETE_DENIED_COMMANDS integration pattern in command deny branches
content:
Pattern for integrating DELETE_DENIED_COMMANDS chat setting into command permission deny branches.

From U12-7 (stats display v1, statsCommand ALLOW_SHOW_STATS deny branch, 2026-08-19):

When denying a command due to permission/chat settings:
1. Check `chatSettings[ChatSettingsKey.DELETE_DENIED_COMMANDS].toBool()` (kebab-case config key: "delete-denied-commands", default false in bot-defaults.toml:96)
2. If TRUE: await self.deleteMessage(ensuredMessage) wrapped in try/except-log
3. If FALSE: send existing informative reply to user

The try/except-log shape follows manager.py:990-1001 precedent:
```python
try:
    await self.deleteMessage(ensuredMessage)
except Exception as e:
    logger.exception("Failed to delete denied command message")
```

Key aspects:
- NO reply when deleting (silent denial)
- Exception handling ensures deletion failures don't crash the handler
- Informative reply only when setting is FALSE (user wants feedback)

This pattern gives chat owners control over whether denied commands are silently removed or explained. Consistent across all permission-gated commands.

title: Config section consolidation pattern: [stats-pages] → [stats.pages]
content:
When consolidating a standalone config section into an existing config file's child section, maintain migration path in documentation.

Pattern from U12-4 (stats display v1, 2026-08-19):
- DELETED standalone file: configs/00-defaults/stats-pages.toml with [stats-pages] section
- MOVED all keys under [stats.pages] child section in configs/00-defaults/stats.toml
- Updated accessor: getStatsPagesConfig() reads self.get("stats.pages", {}) (dotted-path get via ConfigManager, confirmed at manager.py:278-293)
- REMOVED base-url key entirely (moved to CLI --base-url argument instead)
- Updated design doc §5 config diff to reflect new shape
- Updated limiter config: windowSeconds 3600→600 (user-ratified shrink for timeout compliance)

Benefits:
- Single config file for feature-related settings (stats.toml already exists)
- Consistent dotted-path access pattern used elsewhere in ConfigManager
- Clearer namespace (stats.pages vs standalone stats-pages)

Documentation note: When merging sections, explicitly note the deleted file and the accessor change (dotted-path get). Update any limiter configs that reference the old section name.

The ConfigManager's dotted-path get (`self.get("stats.pages", {})`) automatically handles missing sections by returning the default (empty dict), ensuring backward compatibility during migration.

title: Stats command period grammar: --period=<N><suffix> or all
content:
Specified period grammar for /stats command (--period flag), supporting flexible time ranges.

Suffixes:
- h = hours (1..24, periodType: hourly)
- d = days (1..31, periodType: daily)
- m = months (N≥1, periodType: monthly, CALENDAR months—user-ratified)
- all = total (no range, no periodType)

Range computation rules:
- h: from = now − N·h truncated to the hour
- d: from = now − N·d truncated to the day (N+1 buckets incl. the partial current day)
- m: from = first day of the month N calendar months back (truncates to month boundary)
- all: no bounds (entire dataset)

Other rules:
- Default: 7d (7 days, periodType: daily)
- Old fixed args (1d/7d/30d) subsumed by Nd syntax
- Out-of-range N or bad suffix → usage error (single rule from D2)

Calendar-month semantics: "1m" = previous calendar month (1st to last day), "2m" = two calendar months back, etc. Truncates to month boundary for accurate monthly aggregations.

This grammar enables more precise time-range queries than the old fixed 1d/7d/30d options, supporting both relative periods (Nh, Nd) and calendar-aligned periods (Nm). The "all" option provides total stats without time filtering.

title: Stats web page raw rows payload pattern
content:
Stats web page receives raw rows payload instead of pre-grouped/aggregated data. Bot applies filters but delegates grouping/rendering to page.

Payload structure:
- meta: userId, chatId, chatTitle, chatType, platform, period arg string, periodType, generatedAt
- rows: dict[eventType → list[StatsAggregateDict]] covering five event types (messages, commands, tools, llm, plus chatList for private scope)

Filters applied by bot (server-side):
- Scope: consumer = target chat, __global__ excluded
- Granularity: periodType (hourly/daily/monthly)
- Range: per --period grammar
- Limit: 10000 per eventType (honesty line: if len(rows) == 10000, data may be truncated)

Page rendering (server-side):
- Per-eventType sections with time-series tables + inline SVG bar charts
- NO client-side JS interactivity (user-ratified—static rendering)
- Label filtering on the page is future work

Benefits:
- Bot stays thin: applies filters, passes raw data
- Page handles grouping, visualization independently
- Can evolve page rendering without touching bot code
- Full data access enables richer visualizations

Contrast with previous pre-grouping pattern: bot grouped data before sending, coupling bot logic to page visualization. Raw rows payload separates concerns.

Superseded the D11 "grouping logic exists exactly once" deviation note from 2026-08-18.

title: Stats page CLI stdout contract: pageId and full url
content:
Stats page generator (lib/stats/stats_pages generate) stdout contract for bot integration.

Stdout JSON: {"pageId": "<uuid>", "url": "<full-url>"}
- Key renamed: "id" → "pageId" (clearer semantics)
- url is FULL and used VERBATIM by bot (no bot-side composition)

CLI accepts optional --base-url <url> argument:
- Operators put it directly in the generate-command template in config
- When given: url = base.rstrip("/") + "/" + filename
- When omitted: url = bare filename only

Example generate-command template (with --base-url):
```toml
generate-command = [
    "./venv/bin/python3", "-m", "lib.stats.stats_pages", "generate",
    "--user-id={user_id}", "--chat-id={chat_id}", "--platform={platform}",
    "--base-url=https://example.com/stats",  # optional, operator-configured
]
```

Contrast with previous contract (D11):
- Old: {"id": "<uuid>", "url": "<uuid>.html"} (relative url)
- Old: bot composed base-url + "/" + url for reply link
- Old: base-url was a required config key in [stats-pages]

Benefits:
- Config moves from [stats-pages] to CLI arguments (operator control)
- URL composition logic lives in one place (CLI), not duplicated in bot
- Bot simply passes through stdout url verbatim

This change aligns with the [stats.pages] config merge (U12-4) where base-url key was removed entirely.

title: Period grammar implementation: Nh/Nd/Nm/all syntax with calendar month arithmetic
content:
When implementing period argument parsing for stats commands, use this pattern:

**Grammar (lib/stats/analysis.py):**
- `<N>h` (1-24) → "hourly" period type
- `<N>d` (1-31) → "daily" period type  
- `<N>m` (N≥1) → "monthly" period type
- `all` → "total" period type (None bounds)

**Range computation (computePeriodRange):**
- Hours: `now − N hours` truncated to hour (ISO-8601 UTC)
- Days: `now − N days` truncated to day (keeps N+1-buckets behavior)
- Months: First day of month N calendar months back using year*12+month arithmetic
  - Handles year-underflow naturally (e.g., 2024-01-15 minus 2m = 2023-11-01)
  - No date-clamp issues since truncating to month start
- All: returns (None, None)

**Parser validation (stats.py _parseStatsArgs):**
- Validate bounds: h≤24, d≤31, m≥1
- Raise StatsUsageError on invalid values
- Default stays "7d"
- Update _USAGE_TEXT/_HELP_TEXT with new format

**Testing approach (test_analysis.py):**
- Use frozen clock (freezegun) for deterministic date arithmetic
- Test edge cases: 0h/25h/32d/0m/7x → ValueError
- Test calendar month math including Jan→Nov year-underflow
- Test all → (None, None)

**Header display:**
- Show periodArg as-is in _buildStatsReply header (e.g., "6h", "2m")
- Existing behavior keyed off periodArg should keep working

title: Username resolution timing: targetChatId must be known before lookup
content:
When implementing username-based user resolution (e.g., `--user=@username`), resolution MUST happen AFTER the target chat ID is known:

**Pattern (stats.py statsCommand):**
1. Parse arguments, store raw string (e.g., "@username" or "123")
2. Determine targetChatId first (from positional arg or current chat)
3. THEN resolve username if needed:
   - Numeric → convert to int directly
   - Starts with "@" → strip "@", call `self.db.chatUsers.getChatUserByUsername(chatId=targetChatId, username=nameWithoutAt)`
   - None result → StatsUsageError with "пользователь @name не найден в этом чате"

**Why this order matters:**
- `getChatUserByUsername` is chat-scoped (case-insensitive, LIMIT 1)
- Parser is pure and doesn't know the target chat
- Resolution timing matches architectural intent

**Gotcha to avoid:**
- Don't try to resolve usernames before targetChatId is set
- This causes NameError (undefined variable) at runtime

**Testing pattern:**
- Mock `db.chatUsers.getChatUserByUsername` to return userId
- Test @Unknown → usage error
- Test numeric → unchanged
- Test case-insensitivity (assert repo received stripped name)

title: DELETE_DENIED_COMMANDS gate pattern for auto-delete on permission denied
content:
When implementing auto-delete behavior for denied commands, use this pattern:

**Location (stats.py ALLOW_SHOW_STATS deny branch):**
```python
if not chatSettings[ChatSettingsKey.ALLOW_SHOW_STATS].toBool():
    # Only for groups/channels (not private)
    if chatType != ChatType.PRIVATE:
        if chatSettings[ChatSettingsKey.DELETE_DENIED_COMMANDS].toBool():
            # Auto-delete the denied command message
            try:
                await self.deleteMessage(ensuredMessage)
            except Exception as e:
                logger.error(f"Failed to delete denied stats command: {e}")
            return  # NO reply
        else:
            # Existing informative reply path
            await self.sendMessage(ensuredMessage, messageText="...")
            return
```

**Key rules:**
- Read `chatSettings[ChatSettingsKey.DELETE_DENIED_COMMANDS].toBool()`
- If True: deleteMessage + NO reply (mirror manager.py:990-1001 shape)
- If False: existing informative reply
- Private chats: gate not consulted (no permission needed)

**Import requirements:**
- Import ChatSettingsKey (check existing imports in the file)

**Testing:**
- setting true → deleteMessage awaited + NO stats reply
- setting false → informative reply, no delete
- private chat → neither (gate not consulted)

title: Section=ALL pattern: remove special-casing, use simple list
content:
When implementing "all sections" functionality, avoid special-casing blocks:

**Old pattern (DELETE THIS):**
```python
if positionalChatIdUsed:
    sectionsToRender = ["messages", "commands", "tools", "llm"]
elif section == "llm" and filterUserId:
    # Special case: LLM with user filter
    sectionsToRender = ["messages", "commands", "tools"]
else:
    sectionsToRender = [section]
```

**New pattern (USE THIS):**
```python
# sections = all four when section=="all" else [section]
if section == "all":
    sections = ["messages", "commands", "tools", "llm"]
else:
    sections = [section]

# Positional chatId only selects target chat (doesn't affect sections)
# --user only filters (llm section renders with chat-level annotation when user-filtered)
```

**Why the new pattern is better:**
- Simpler, less branching
- Clearer intent: section parameter directly determines sections
- Separates concerns: chat selection vs section selection vs user filtering
- Easier to test and reason about

**Parser update:**
- Accept "all" as valid value alongside messages/commands/tools/llm
- Validate in _parseStatsArgs: `if section not in ("messages", "commands", "tools", "llm", "all"):`

title: Rate limiting applyLimit-only pattern: simplify to single call
content:
When implementing rate limiting for stats web generation, use this simplified pattern:

**Old pattern (DELETE THIS):**
```python
# Check rate limiter status
rateStats = None
limiterUnavailable = False
try:
    rateStats = await RateLimiterManager.getInstance().getStats(
        self._statsPagesRatelimiterQueue,
        rateLimiterKey
    )
    # ... extensive pre-check logic ...
except RuntimeError:
    limiterUnavailable = True

# Early return if rate limited
if rateStats and rateStats.get("remaining", 0) <= 0:
    await self.sendMessage(...)
    return
```

**New pattern (USE THIS):**
```python
# Apply the rate limit (record the attempt) - U12-6: applyLimit-only
# No try/except here; outer D15 wrap covers the no-limiter RuntimeError
await RateLimiterManager.getInstance().applyLimit(
    self._statsPagesRatelimiterQueue,
    rateLimiterKey
)
```

**Key principles:**
- Single `applyLimit()` call before the subprocess
- NO try/except around it (outer D15 wrap covers RuntimeError)
- NO getStats/pre-check/refusal block
- Remove now-unused helpers/imports (formatRussianPlural if orphaned)

**Why this works:**
- D15 outer wrap catches RuntimeError (no-limiter case)
- applyLimit() handles incrementing counters
- Simpler, less code, fewer error paths

**Testing:**
- applyLimit awaited once with (queue, key) before subprocess call
- getStats NOT called
- No refusal-reply path exists

title: Type annotation lessons from stats implementation
content:
Common type annotation pitfalls encountered during stats U12 implementation:

**1. Removed constants still referenced in usage:**
- Problem: PeriodArg constants (ONE_DAY, SEVEN_DAYS, etc.) were removed but still referenced in period label mapping
- Fix: Update period label mapping to use string literals directly (e.g., "7d" instead of PeriodArg.SEVEN_DAYS)

**2. Union type mismatches in ParsedArgs:**
- Problem: ParsedStatsArgs.user was str|None (for @username support) but downstream code expected int|None
- Fix: Update type hints to reflect both parsing and resolution phases, or use Union[str, int, None]

**3. Return type annotation drift:**
- Problem: _buildStatsReply was annotated as str but actually returned str | list[str] (for chunked output)
- Fix: Update return annotation to match actual return type, or create separate method signatures

**4. Removed attributes still referenced:**
- Problem: _statsPagesBaseUrl was removed in config merge but still referenced in code
- Fix: Remove all references to deleted config keys/attributes

**5. Optional handling inconsistencies:**
- Problem: Assuming Optional[str] is not None without checking
- Fix: Always check `if value is not None` before calling methods like .startswith()

**Testing:**
- Run `pyright` after changes
- Check for undefined name errors
- Verify return types match annotations
- Update ParsedArgs TypedDict as fields evolve

title: W1 pyright errors: ParsedStatsArgs.user type and filterUserId resolution
content:
During W1 (U12 command-side stats changes), fixed pyright error where ParsedStatsArgs.user was typed as `str` but should be `str | None` because the period grammar now makes the user argument optional. Additionally, fixed the error on line 384 where `filterUserId=parsedArgs["user"]` was passing the raw string (`str | None`) to `_handleWebMode` which expects `int | None`. The correct fix was to pass the already-resolved `filterUserId` variable (which contains the resolved integer ID) instead of `parsedArgs["user"]`.

title: W1 pyright error: _buildStatsReply return type str | list[str] for chunked sending
content:
During W1 (U12 command-side stats changes), fixed pyright error where `_buildStatsReply` return type was annotated as `str` but the implementation returns `str | list[str]` due to chunked message sending. The method at line 673 returns `chunks[0] if len(chunks) == 1 else chunks`, which can be either a single string or a list of strings. The return type annotation was updated to `str | list[str]` to match the actual implementation pattern.

Pattern: When implementing message chunking to avoid platform size limits, the return type of build methods should reflect that they may return either a single message (when content is short) or a list of messages (when chunking was necessary).

title: W1 pyright error: _statsPagesBaseUrl removal for CLI verbatim URL
content:
During W1 (U12 command-side stats changes), fixed pyright error where code referenced `self._statsPagesBaseUrl` which no longer exists after the config merge that removed base-url configuration. The stats-pages CLI contract changed to return the full URL verbatim from the CLI stdout (`{"pageId": "<uuid>", "url": "<full-url>"}`), so bot-side composition is no longer needed. The fix on line 1672 changed `f"{self._statsPagesBaseUrl.rstrip('/')}/{url}"` to just `url` (using the CLI-provided URL directly).
