title: _extractImagePrompt helper: Images API path requires textual prompt, merges messages
content: Module-level helper `_extractImagePrompt()` at `lib/ai/providers/basic_openai_provider.py:54-89` feeds the Images API transport (`_generateImageViaImagesApi`). The OpenAI Images API takes a single string prompt, so the helper joins all textual content across messages with double newlines and logs a warning when more than one message is given ("they will be merged into one"). It accepts string content or content lists containing `{"type": "text"}` blocks, extracting text via `block.get("text")` — the standard OpenAI shape, notably NOT the `{"type": "text", "content": ...}` shape that `ModelImageMessage.toDict()` emits (see the open bug about that key). Raises `ValueError("No textual content found in messages for image generation")` when no textual content is found — an image-only message list cannot be sent through the Images API transport.

title: SandboxHandler registers delayed-task lifecycle hooks: startup recovery, 30-min GC, shutdown cleanup
content:
During `SandboxHandler.__init__` (internal/bot/common/handlers/sandbox.py, lines 94-97, only when sandbox config is enabled), the handler registers two delayed-task handlers and lifecycle state that none of the existing sandbox-handler memories cover:

- `self.queueService.registerDelayedTaskHandler(function=DelayedTaskFunction.CRON_JOB, handler=self._dtCronJob)` — `_dtCronJob` (lines 211-230) performs a ONE-TIME startup recovery on the first cron tick (`SandboxManager.getInstance().recover()`, guarded by `self._recoveryDone`), then runs garbage collection via `manager.collectGarbage()` at most every 1800 seconds (30 min, tracked by `self._lastCronRun`).
- `self.queueService.registerDelayedTaskHandler(DelayedTaskFunction.DO_EXIT, handler=self._dtOnExit)` — `_dtOnExit` (lines 232-245) calls `SandboxManager.getInstance().shutdown(cleanVolumes=False)` on application shutdown.

Gotcha: these registrations happen AFTER the early `return` on disabled sandbox config (line 88), so with `[sandbox] enabled = false` there is no sandbox recovery, GC, or graceful shutdown hook at all. Also both `/run` and the `run_python` LLM tool execute code with `network=NetworkPolicy(enabled=True)` (lines 296, 724) — network access is deliberately enabled for sandboxed code execution.

title: scripts/_lib/bootstrap.py — shared bootstrapProxy helper for scripts/ (ProxyHelper init + httpx2 alias)
content:
All standalone scripts under `scripts/` that construct ConfigManager and then build any proxy-consuming service (LLMManager, Database with sqlink, any httpx client resolving proxy via ProxyConfig) MUST call `bootstrapProxy(configManager)` from `scripts/_lib/bootstrap.py` AFTER ConfigManager construction and BEFORE the first proxy-consuming service. It wraps `ProxyHelper.getInstance().setGlobalProxyConfig(configManager.getProxyConfig())` and is idempotent.

Critically, merely IMPORTING the module runs `httpx2.alias_httpx()` — making `import httpx` resolve to httpx2 process-wide so the openai SDK's internal httpx.AsyncClient becomes an httpx2.AsyncClient — which must happen before any import that transitively pulls httpx (see docs/design/httpx2-migration-v1.md §6).

Without the proxy bootstrap, `ProxyConfig.getCombined()` raises TypeError from inside `BasicOpenAIProvider._initClient()`, every provider fails to register, and the script silently exits with "0 text-capable models" (this originally bit check_image_parsing.py). Current users include check_condensing.py, reproduce_llm_dialog.py, and run_llm_debug_query.py. Production equivalent: `ProxyService.getInstance().initialize(configManager.getProxyConfig(), loop=loop)` at main.py:86, which internally calls setGlobalProxyConfig (internal/services/proxy/service.py:103).

title: embedding-model-lookup: canonical durable record lives in docs/llm/memories/embedding-model-lookup-refactor.md
content: The embedding-model-lookup refactor (migration_025, EmbeddingModelsRepository, D10 modelIdResolver injection, dataSource plumbing, 2026-07-21 simplification pass) has a complete canonical durable record in the repo at docs/llm/memories/embedding-model-lookup-refactor.md (archived from teamlead-memory.md on 2026-08-08, marked COMPLETE 2026-07-21). Before creating or trusting agent memories on this topic, check that doc first — the 2026-07-21 session-analyser memories (migration no-backfill state changes, single-branch predicate, dataSource contract evolution, refactor-landed status) were all absorbed into it and were deleted from memory during the 2026-08-20 audit as duplicates. Remaining non-doc facts still true in code (verified 2026-08-20): Database.__init__ constructs embeddingModels FIRST (database.py:236) because its bound getOrCreateModelId is injected into the three embedding repos; getOrCreateModelId is cache-first (a hit never acquires a provider, so dataSource only routes on miss — embedding_models.py:114-120); callers passing an unseen model name to deleteObsolete*Embeddings wipes all embeddings for the chat (probe-then-insert allocates a fresh id that matches nothing).

title: STT service is now a stateless singleton — registry/coordinator/dedup architecture was removed
content: internal/services/stt/ was refactored to a minimal shape: only __init__.py (exports STTService, STTOutcome), service.py (352 lines), and formatter.py. STTService is a stateless singleton mirroring ProxyService (class-level _instance/_lock, hasattr 'initialized' guard, separate initialize(configManager, statsStorage=...)): constructs or skips the provider from [stt] config (STT_PROVIDERS_MAP: only 'yandex-speechkit'), resolves proxy via ProxyService.resolveProxy, and exposes transcribeMedia(data, chatId) -> STTOutcome — a never-raise pipeline (STT_DISABLED gate → SOURCE_TOO_LARGE vs max-source-bytes (default 1 GiB) → per-chat/global rate limiter queues → asyncio.Semaphore(max-concurrency) → provider.stt → _mapOutcome with formatTranscript). The service does NOT touch the database — the handler (BaseBotHandler._processMediaV2) owns the full media_attachments row lifecycle. The earlier P8-era machinery (STTCoordinator, STTInFlightRegistry, dispatchTranscription, queue-tracking tasks, types.py) no longer exists; old memories about registry lifecycle/shutdown-drain/dispatch-rejection describe removed code. aclose() is a best-effort provider.aclose() wrapped in try/except Exception (never raises).

title: storeAttachment is lock-free and synchronous-on-the-loop (dedup via exists-then-store)
content: BaseBotHandler.storeAttachment (internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py:2050-2085) is the sole attachment-storage path: SHA512-content-addressed key `{prefix}{mediaType}-{sha512}.{mimeSubtype}`, MIME via magic.from_buffer, dedup via `if not self.storage.exists(key): self.storage.store(key, data)`. Notable current properties: NO asyncio.Lock striping (an earlier striped-lock design was removed — no locks exist anywhere in the attachment path), NO asyncio.to_thread offload (the exists/store calls run synchronously on the event loop; for the S3 backend these are boto3 network calls — same hazard class as the boto3-offload gotcha in lib/stt/providers/yandex_object_storage.py), and the exists-then-store dedup has a check-then-act race for concurrent first delivery of identical content (harmless for content-addressed keys — worst case a duplicate put of the same key). Errors are swallowed to None by a broad except (logger.error + exception), matching the error-to-None contract callers rely on.

title: Pyright narrows NotRequired TypedDict access with `in` guards but NOT with .get() truthiness guards
content:
Complements the walrus-comprehension (1aba5009) and sort-lambda `.get(key, default)` (c3b784cd) patterns. Pyright (basic mode) accepts direct bracket access to a `NotRequired` TypedDict key when guarded by a membership check — `if "key" in d:` — but does NOT narrow when guarded by `.get()` truthiness (`if d.get("key"):` still leaves `d["key"]` flagged by reportTypedDictNotRequiredAccess).

Verified in production code, internal/bot/common/handlers/message_preprocessor.py:126:
```python
shortTermScores = {m["memory_id"]: m["score"] for m in shortTermMemories if "score" in m}
```
Here `SingleMemoryDict.score` is `NotRequired[float]` (internal/bot/models/message_metadata.py:41) and the `in` guard lets `m["score"]` pass pyright cleanly, unlike the walrus site at line 135 which needs `(mid := m.get("id"))` because it also extracts the value.

Rule of thumb for NotRequired TypedDict keys:
- guard-only + direct access → `if key in d:` then `d[key]`
- filter + collect in a comprehension → walrus `(v := d.get(key))`
- default-value extraction (sort lambdas, lookups) → `d.get(key, default)`

title: migration_025 embedding-model-lookup refactor: user_memories provenance is a single model_id FK
content:
The embedding-model-lookup refactor (migration_025, plan docs/plans/embedding-model-lookup-refactor-v1.md, decisions D2/D6/D9/D10) reshaped the user-memories embedding layer — several pre-2026-07-21 memories reference the OLD shape and are wrong about it:

1. **Provenance columns:** `user_memories.embedding_model` / `embedding_dimensions` (migration_020 shape) are GONE. A single nullable `model_id INTEGER` column FKs into a new `models` lookup table (`model_id INTEGER PK, model TEXT, dimensions INTEGER NOT NULL, UNIQUE(model, dimensions)`) — migration_025:161-194.
2. **Model-id resolver injection:** `UserMemoriesRepository.__init__` takes a `modelIdResolver` (wired to `EmbeddingModelsRepository.getOrCreateModelId`). Every embedding-touching method resolves the model NAME string at its public boundary via `_resolveModelId(model, dimensions, dataSource=...)`; handler-facing signatures still pass name strings.
3. **vec0 partition key:** `vec_user_memories_{dim}` tables now carry `model_id INTEGER PARTITION KEY` (was `model TEXT`); `_semanticSearchMemories` filters vec0 on `model_id = :modelId`.
4. **Dimensions are never None:** `AbstractModel.getDimensions() -> int` (lib/ai/abstract.py:589) always returns int; `getOrCreateModelId(model: str, dimensions: int)` and `deleteObsoleteMemoryEmbeddings(currentDimensions: int)` require int. `getMemoriesWithoutEmbeddings(modelName=None, dimensions=None)` keeps optional params handled inline via the SQL guard `(:currentModelId IS NOT NULL AND model_id != :currentModelId)`.
5. **Migration dropped vectors:** migration_025 dropped `message_embeddings` (BLOB) and all vec0 tables, and set `user_memories.model_id = NULL` for every row — forcing a full re-embed via the regen cron rather than marking rows embedded with no searchable vector.

Canonical doc: docs/llm/memories/embedding-model-lookup-refactor.md.

title: ConfigManager.get() supports dot notation for nested keys — supersedes old 'dotted keys never work' gotchas
content:
`ConfigManager.get(key, default)` (internal/config/manager.py:278-304) supports dotted-key traversal: keys containing "." are split and the nested dict chain is walked; if any segment is missing or an intermediate value is not a dict, the default is returned. E.g. `configManager.get("sandbox.bootstrap", {})` works.

This supersedes several older memories (and an old sandbox_bootstrap.py workaround pattern) that claimed get() was a plain top-level dict lookup and that dotted keys 'are treated as literal top-level key names and will never match' — that was true of an earlier version of the method but is no longer.

Note: many call sites still read the top-level section and traverse manually (e.g. scripts/sandbox_bootstrap.py:132-138); that pattern still works. Typed per-section accessors (getBotConfig(), getDatabaseConfig(), ...) remain the preferred style.

title: Stats 'sent' label semantics: True=bot-sent, False=human-sent, absent=backfill history
content:
In Gromozeka stats labels, `sent` encodes direction by SENDER IDENTITY, not category: sent="True" when sender.id == getBotId() (bot-sent), sent="False" otherwise (human-sent). Locked by test_direction_rule_sender_driven_not_category in tests/bot/common/handlers/test_message_stats.py; recording logic in BaseBotHandler.saveChatMessage (internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py).

The stats pages generator (lib/stats/stats_pages/generator.py:549-568) buckets message rows into three groups by the sent label: Bot Messages (sent="True"), User Messages (sent="False"), and History/backfill (no sent label — migration_027 backfill rows never carry sent). "Top Users by Messages" includes ONLY sent="False" rows (line ~566).

This inversion is a recurring trap: during a 2026-08 audit, two session memories stated the filter direction backwards. Remember: sent means 'the BOT sent it'.

title: Current stats-pages architecture post-U12: [stats.pages] in stats.toml, raw-rows payload, verbatim CLI URL
content:
The stats-pages web tier reached its current shape after the U12 amendments (2026-08-19, docs/design/stats-display-v1.md:1158,1423-1447,1677-1678). Key facts that supersede several earlier iterations:

**Config location:** `configs/00-defaults/stats.toml` section `[stats.pages]` (dot notation) — there is NO separate stats-pages.toml and NO `base-url` key (U12-5 removed it). Keys: enabled (false), ttl-hours (24), ratelimiter-queue ("stats-pages"), generate-command, delete-command (with `{page_id}` placeholder). Operators who want full URLs append the CLI's `--base-url=...` flag to generate-command.

**CLI contract (U12-5):** stdout is `{"pageId": "<uuid>", "url": ...}` — key renamed from `id` to `pageId`; the bot uses the url VERBATIM with no composition (stats.py:1364-1378, `fullLink = url`).

**Payload contract (U12-9):** StatsPayload (lib/stats/stats_pages/generator.py:40-75) carries raw aggregate ROWS keyed by eventType (`rows: dict[str, list[StatsAggregateDict]]`), NOT pre-computed section view-models. The bot applies only scope filters + limit=10000; all grouping, time-series, and rendering happen in the generator. Truncation is signalled via the optional `truncatedEventTypes: list[str]` field, not per-section possiblyIncomplete flags.

**Section TypedDicts are gone:** MessagesSectionData/CommandsSectionData/ToolsSectionData/LlmSectionData (the earlier section-payload design) no longer exist in generator.py.

title: ConfigManager.get() now supports dot-notation nested-key traversal — project docs still say never use dotted keys
content:
`internal/config/manager.py` `ConfigManager.get()` (lines 278-304) supports dotted paths: keys without a dot go through `self.config.get(key, default)`; keys containing dots are split on '.' and traversed through nested dicts, returning the default if any segment is missing or a non-dict is encountered mid-path. The docstring explicitly shows `config_manager.get("bot.token")` and `config_manager.get("database.type", "sqlite")`.

This supersedes older guidance (and older memories) claiming `get("sandbox.bootstrap", {})` always returns the default `{}`. Stale docs still instruct the opposite: docs/llm/tasks.md (~line 485) says "never use dotted keys like configManager.get('sandbox.bootstrap.starter-packages')" and docs/llm/sandbox.md (~line 261) says "NEVER use dotted-key access". `scripts/sandbox_bootstrap.py` still uses nested dict traversal (lines 132-138), which remains correct — just no longer the only option. Nested traversal is still the de-facto project pattern until docs are reconciled.

title: YC SDK provider now supports structured output — config enabled for several yc-sdk models
content:
The YC SDK provider (`lib/ai/providers/yc_sdk_provider.py`) implements `_generateStructured` (flat `response_format={"json_schema": schema, "name": schemaName, "strict": strict}` dict passed to `_getModel(**modelKwargs)` → SDK `.configure()`), and `configs/00-defaults/yc-sdk-models.toml` now sets `support_structured_output = true` for three models (lines 24, 37, 50; only the embeddings entry stays false). This supersedes the earlier "yc-sdk: deferred" stance.

Two stale-doc consequences found during audit (Aug 2026):
1. `tests/lib/ai/golden/STRUCTURED_OUTPUT.md` line 21-22 still says "YC SDK does not support structured output (see docs/plans/lib-ai-structured-output.md §3.6)" — both claims are now wrong (support exists; the plan doc is deleted).
2. The `_generateStructured` docstring in yc_sdk_provider.py claims it lowers temperature to min(configured, 0.3) — the code does no such thing (it just copies customParams).

title: Drift: documentation-review-process.md:750 claims run-quality-gates skill covers make check-docs — it does not
content: Open doc-drift item found during the 2026-08-20 memory audit (topic documentation-drift-automation): `docs/documentation-review-process.md:750` describes the `run-quality-gates` skill as the "Exact `./venv/bin/python3` / `make format lint` / `make test` / `make check-docs` workflow" — but `.agents/skills/run-quality-gates/SKILL.md` (full read) contains ZERO mentions of `make check-docs`; nor does AGENTS.md's description of that skill. Only `.agents/skills/update-project-docs/SKILL.md:179-180` gates on check-docs among the skills. This matters because the docs-only gate convention (lint + check-docs, no make test) leans on agents finding check-docs guidance via the quality-gates skill. Fix either way: add check-docs to run-quality-gates/SKILL.md (preferred — it is the canonical quality-gate skill and docs-only changes are its stated non-use carve-out), or correct the doc line. Adjacent drift in the same skill file: run-quality-gates/SKILL.md:112 still claims tests are "collocated under `lib/` and `internal/`", contradicting current AGENTS.md (all tests live under `tests/`). Note `.agents/` and `docs/` ARE scanned by check-docs, so fixing the :750 line requires no link repair, just prose.

title: Recovery gap: message-side vec0 write failures are permanent until model drift (unlike user_memories)
content:
Post-migration_025 asymmetry in embedding write ordering (internal/database/repositories):

- `ChatEmbeddingsRepository.saveMessageEmbedding` (chat_embeddings.py L184-216) UPDATEs `chat_messages.model_id` FIRST, then attempts the vec0 insert (failures logged + swallowed). `getMessagesWithoutEmbeddings` (L450) discovers backfill candidates solely via the `chat_messages.model_id` predicate (NULL or != current model_id) — so if the vec0 write fails after model_id was set, the row is never re-discovered: the message is silently excluded from semantic search until the chat's embedding model changes (model-drift cleanup nulls model_id) or EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED is toggled.
- `UserMemoriesRepository.saveMemoryEmbedding` (user_memories.py ~L1150-1155) does the opposite: the vec0 write must SUCCEED before `user_memories.model_id` is set, so a failed vec0 write leaves model_id NULL and the regen cron retries it.

Potential fix direction: flip the message-side ordering to match the memories side, or make backfill discovery verify vec0-row existence. Not documented in docs/llm/memories/vector-search.md or docs/database-schema.md as of 2026-08-20.

title: STT docs reorganization: plans → design, roadmap archived
content:
The STT documentation was reorganized after the feature shipped (multiple older memories reference stale docs/plans/ paths):
- `docs/plans/` no longer contains ANY STT docs — only llm-empty-truncated-final-handling-v1.md, embedding-model-lookup-refactor-v1.md, python-sandboxing-v1.md remain there.
- `docs/design/lib-stt-v1.md` — authoritative lib/stt spec (moved from docs/plans/).
- `docs/design/media-transcription-stt-v1.md` — parent v1 plan (moved from docs/plans/); §13.3 release gates defer to lib-stt-v1.md as authoritative.
- `docs/design/stt-v1.1.md` — v1.1 gate-3/gate-4 design; its companion-docs header (line 6) links all siblings.
- `docs/archive/design/stt-next-steps.md` — the integration roadmap, now ARCHIVED (feature implemented and shipped default-off).
When an older memory or brief cites a docs/plans/ STT path, resolve it against these current locations; `make check-docs` validates the new link graph.

title: migration_025 reshaped the embedding storage stack — many pre-2026-08 memories reference the removed shape
content:
The embedding-model-lookup refactor (migration_025, docs/plans/embedding-model-lookup-refactor-v1.md) landed and changed the storage model significantly:
- `message_embeddings` BLOB table DROPPED (with its migration_018 index); `getMessageEmbedding`/`deleteChatEmbeddings`/`_loadEmbeddingsFromDb` deleted.
- Provenance now lives in `chat_messages.model_id` (FK to a new `models` lookup table via EmbeddingModelsRepository); embeddings live ONLY in vec0 virtual tables (partition keys now chat_id + model_id INTEGER, replacing model TEXT — all legacy vec_message_embeddings_{N} tables were dropped and are lazily recreated).
- numpy fully retired from production (no imports in internal/ or lib/); removed from requirements.direct.txt, remains an unresolved transitive of fastembed in requirements.txt. searchChatMessages returns [] when vec0 is unavailable.
- Repository count is now 16 (embedding_models.py added); migrations now number 28.
When reading older memories/docs that mention message_embeddings, model TEXT partition keys, numpy cosine fallback, or 15 repos, treat them as pre-025 history.

title: Chat accessibility/bot-status tracking subsystem (migration_026) — discovered during audit
content: A chat-lifecycle subsystem exists that older memories don't cover: migration_026_chat_accessibility_bot_status introduced chat accessibility/bot-status tracking. MessagePreprocessorHandler.newMessageHandler (message_preprocessor.py:165-171) performs cache-aside recovery: `if await self.cache.isChatInaccessible(chatId): await self.cache.markChatActive(chatId)` — an inbound message in a chat marked INACCESSIBLE recovers it to ACTIVE with an info log. Also present: chat_info gained bot-status columns and HandlersManager now takes messageStatsStorage/commandStatsStorage (StatsStorage) constructor params, wiring per-message/per-command stats (NullStatsStorage default). Related migrations: 016 (stat tables), 026 (chat accessibility), 027 (drop chat_stats backfill aggregates), 028 (stat events retention index).

title: PyAV is a hard dependency of lib/stt — no lazy/guarded import
content: PyAV (`av==18.1.0`, pinned in requirements.direct.txt and requirements.txt) is an unconditional hard dependency: lib/stt/audio.py does a plain top-level `import av` with NO `try/except ImportError` / `_AVAILABLE` guard, and lib/stt/__init__.py eagerly re-exports `extractAudio`, so any `import lib.stt.*` (including via internal/services/stt/service.py and main.py) requires PyAV at import time regardless of `[stt].enabled`. The pre-simplification guarded-import design was deliberately removed (docs/design/lib-stt-v1.md §2 'simplification trade-off'; restore the `_PYAV_AVAILABLE` pattern per AGENTS.md Hard rules only if a future module needs lib/stt types without PyAV). STTService.initialize() performs no PyAV availability probe — a missing/unusable PyAV surfaces as an import error or at first transcription, not as an enabled-only startup validation error. Note: docs/llm/configuration.md §[stt] still says 'PyAV is not loaded for STT' when disabled — stale phrasing contradicting lib-stt-v1.md §2.

title: sqlToCustomType/_checkType support PEP 604 X | Y union syntax via types.UnionType
content: `_checkType()` and `sqlToCustomType()` in `internal/database/utils.py` handle both union spellings: legacy `typing.Union[X, Y]` (detected via `get_origin(expectedType) is Union`) AND PEP 604 `X | Y` syntax (detected via `isinstance(expectedType, types.UnionType)`). The checks are `origin is Union or isinstance(expectedType, types.UnionType)` — at `_checkType` line ~63 (delegates to `any(_checkType(value, arg) for arg in get_args(expectedType))`) and at `sqlToCustomType` line ~129 (enters the two-loop union member iteration). This matters because newer code in the repo annotates with `X | None` instead of `Optional[X]`; both take the identical union-member code path. Regression-tested by `testUnionWithNoneViaNewSyntax` in `tests/database/test_utils.py` (~line 1593): `sqlToCustomType(None, int | None)` → `(True, None)` and `sqlToCustomType(b"42", int | None)` → `(True, 42)`. Note: `None` alone in `X | Y` is a `types.UnionType` member handled by the `type(None)` branch in `_checkType` (line ~71).

title: Divination code-drift traps: returnToolJson docstrings + unimplemented negative-cache TTL
content:
Two verified drifts in internal/bot/common/handlers/divination.py (as of Aug 2026):

1. The tool-path flag was renamed to `isLLMCall` (signature line ~584), but several docstrings still say `returnToolJson` — in `_runReadingForTool` (~line 443) and the `_handleReading` pipeline docstring (~lines 599-603). Trust the signature, not those docstrings; any doc-sync pass should fix them.

2. The log message at the negative-cache save site (~line 972) claims 'saving negative cache entry (24h TTL)', but NO TTL is implemented anywhere: `DivinationsRepository.isNegativeCacheEntry` (internal/database/repositories/divinations.py lines 233-253) checks only empty names + n_symbols=0 + positions=[] with no age check, and nothing purges old negative entries. A failed discovery therefore permanently blocks that layout name until a successful `saveLayout` upsert overwrites the row.

title: Stale docstrings in lib/sandbox module headers and docs/llm/sandbox.md examples
content: Confirmed doc-drift findings (Aug 2026 audit; code is correct, docs are stale): (1) docs/llm/sandbox.md §Critical Coding Constraints uses `PythonRuntimeConfig` in import examples and says 'currently only PythonRuntimeConfig is handled' — the actual class is `BasicRuntimeConfig` (lib/sandbox/config.py line 289); no PythonRuntimeConfig class exists anywhere. (2) lib/sandbox/__init__.py module docstring (~line 30) describes SessionLockRegistry as 'per-session semaphore-based' — it is asyncio.Lock + waiter-counter based (locks.py). (3) lib/sandbox/backends/base.py module docstring claims the module defines ContainerSpec/ContainerOutcome/ManagedContainerInfo — they are defined in lib/sandbox/types.py and only imported here (line 18). (4) lib/sandbox/metadata/filesystem.py module docstring mentions overlapping `saveRuntime` calls, but the MetadataStore ABC has no saveRuntime/loadRuntime methods. (5) lib/sandbox/config.py module docstring class list includes 'PythonRuntimeConfig'. These are doc-only fixes for a cleanup pass.

title: Scheduler shutdown hardening was added then deliberately removed (Jul-Aug 2026)
content: The complex scheduler-shutdown machinery described by 2026-07-28-era memories — main.py `_close()`, `_closeProxyServiceAfterSchedulerFailure()`, the `proxy-shutdown-fallback` synthetic DelayedTask calling ProxyService._dtOnExit directly, explicit `_schedulerTask.cancel()`, startup `_schedulerTask.done()`/`result()` fail-fast checks, and BaseException isolation — was introduced in commit ba868907 ('Add lot's of ai-slop', 2026-07-31) and removed in commit 60ef1ce2 ('Simplify STTService', 2026-08-02). At HEAD, shutdown is the simple `_shutdown()` (main.py:157-199): beginShutdown() -> await _schedulerTask under `except Exception` -> rate limiters -> LLM manager -> STT -> database; proxy stops happen only via the scheduler's DO_EXIT dispatch, never directly from main.py. The removed machinery survives only on the stale remote branch `add-audio-transcribation` — do not treat that branch as current design. The current simple contract is documented in docs/llm/memories/proxy-lifecycle.md (line ~79).

title: user_memories.py refinement flow is a second production consumer of dict-form useTools
content:
`internal/bot/common/handlers/user_memories.py` (~line 1306, the generateTextViaLLM call in the memory-refinement flow) passes a per-tool `useTools={...}` dict — joining the divination discovery flow (divination.py:1040-1043, enabling only WEB_SEARCH + GET_URL_CONTENT) as a PRODUCTION consumer of the dict form of `useTools`. The boolean-form call sites remain dev_commands.py:1025 (`USE_TOOLS.toBool()`) and llm_messages.py (threaded `useTools` param / `useTools=True` at line 1053).

Implication: any change to `_resolveTools()` or the filteredToolNames consistency chain in internal/services/llm/service.py must account for BOTH real dict consumers (divination + user_memories), not just the tests. Complements memories cbc723dc / fc14d195, which record divination as the first consumer.

title: Stats storage construction centralized in StatsAggregationService factory (5 event types)
content:
All stats storages are now constructed through one factory: `StatsAggregationService.getInstance().createStatsStorage(eventType, dataSource)` (internal/services/stats/service.py:204). The factory reads the cached `[stats] enabled` flag (parsed once at initialize, main.py:90) and returns a registered `DatabaseStatsStorage` when enabled or `NullStatsStorage` when disabled — so main.py no longer gates storage construction on `statsEnabled` explicitly.

Five event types are wired in main.py:96-131, each with a `*-stats-data-source` key in configs/00-defaults/stats.toml:
1. `llm_request` (llm-stats-data-source) → LLMManager
2. `llm_tool_call` (tool-stats-data-source) → LLMService.injectStatsStorage() (service.py:221-230, stored as self.toolStatsStorage)
3. `stt_request` (stt-stats-data-source) → STTService.initialize(statsStorage=...)
4. `message` (message-stats-data-source) → bot application → HandlersManager(messageStatsStorage=...) → post-construction injection into every handler (manager.py:648-650; BaseBotHandler default NullStatsStorage at base.py:167)
5. `command` (command-stats-data-source) → HandlersManager(commandStatsStorage=...) (manager.py:425-445)

Related config in stats.toml: aggregation-interval-seconds=3600, aggregation-batch-limit=1000, events-retention-days=30, and a [stats.pages] section (offline HTML page generation via lib.stats.stats_pages). Cross-event payload regression coverage: tests/bot/common/handlers/test_stats_payload_regression.py (asserts per-event label shapes, e.g. llm_request/stt_request carry no user_id label while message/command/tool do).

title: I6 memory-dedup fix incomplete in code: base.py pinned block never seeds excludedMemoryIds; TestGetThreadByMessageForLLMMemoryDedup is an empty test-less shell
content:
Audit finding (2026-08-21, misc27 audit). In `BaseBotHandler.getThreadByMessageForLLM` (internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py) the I6 double-injection fix is only HALF implemented:

- base.py:800-808: a comment describes a shared `excludedMemoryIds` accumulator 'across BOTH the first-N (pinned) block and the tail loop', with the pinned block rendering 'against an empty set ... then seeds it with the rendered IDs'.
- base.py:813-824 (actual code): the pinned loop still passes a throwaway `excludeMemoryIds=set()` and NEVER calls `excludedMemoryIds.update(eMessage.getMemoryIds())` — the seeding step is missing. Only the tail loop threads (871) and seeds (873) the accumulator (grep confirms 3 usages total: 808 init, 871, 873).

Net behavior: tail-vs-tail memory dedup works, but a permanent memory shared between a PINNED message and a TAIL message is still injected TWICE — the exact bug (I6) the comment claims was fixed.

Compounding factor: `TestGetThreadByMessageForLLMMemoryDedup` (tests/bot/common/handlers/test_base.py:547) contains only a docstring describing the bug/fix and the `_makeMsg` helper — it has ZERO test methods (the next class starts at :622), so nothing in the suite pins the fix and `make test` stays green despite the missing seeding.

Fix: add `excludedMemoryIds.update(eMessage.getMemoryIds())` after the pinned block's `ret.extend(mMessages)` (base.py ~824), and restore a real test method inside the empty class (the docstring's own recipe: class-level patch of EnsuredMessage.fromDBChatMessage + Mock db.chatMessages + a shared permanent memory ID on both root and tail rows, asserting the content appears exactly once).

title: requirements.txt has drifted from ADR-021: no httpx pin, httpcore still pinned
content:
Audit finding (2026-08-20): the frozen requirements.txt no longer matches ADR-021's dependency description. ADR-021 (docs/llm/architecture.md:793) states "httpx and httpcore REMAIN pinned in requirements.txt as shadowed transitive dependencies of python-telegram-bot and openai" — but the current lockfile contains httpcore==1.0.9 (line 38), httpcore2==2.10.0 (39), httpx2==2.10.0 (40) and NO httpx entry at all. The lockfile was regenerated at some point after the migration (openai is now 3.0.0 vs 2.45.0 at migration time; yandex-ai-studio-sdk 0.22.1; httpx-sse and python-socks gone; requests/urllib3 now present as transitives).

Implications:
- python-telegram-bot==22.8 is still pinned; if its httpx requirement still applies, a fresh `pip install -r requirements.txt` may pull an unpinned httpx transitively — reproducibility should be re-verified before dependency work.
- The runtime story is unchanged: httpx2.alias_httpx() at process start makes `import httpx` resolve to httpx2 regardless of whether httpx is installed.
- ADR-021 line 793 needs a doc update to describe the current lockfile.

title: AGENTS.md hard-rules example still shows the retired httpx_socks conditional import
content:
AGENTS.md line 66 (the 'No imports inside methods' hard rule) still uses the retired pattern as its illustrative example:

```python
try:
    from httpx_socks import AsyncProxyTransport
    _HTTPX_SOCKS_AVAILABLE = True
except ImportError:
    _HTTPX_SOCKS_AVAILABLE = False
```

httpx_socks was removed from the repo entirely during the 2026-08-13 httpx→httpx2 migration (ADR-021 D2) — there is no httpx-socks package, no AsyncProxyTransport, and no _HTTPX_SOCKS_AVAILABLE flag anywhere in owned code (verified by grep: zero matches in lib/, internal/, tests/). The canonical optional-dependency example in AGENTS.md should be swapped for a live one (e.g. sqlite-vec's _SQLITE_VEC_AVAILABLE, which docs/llm/database.md §7 documents, or boto3's _BOTO3_AVAILABLE from the STT design). Docs elsewhere (docs/llm/memories/proxy.md, dependency-usage-tests.md) already carry the correct 'removed during the httpx2 migration' notes — AGENTS.md is the remaining stale site.

title: ChatInfoRepository.updateChatInfo always overwrites bot_status (default ACTIVE) — no None-omit
content: `ChatInfoRepository.updateChatInfo` (internal/database/repositories/chat_info.py:42-95) writes `bot_status` UNCONDITIONALLY: the keyword param is `botStatus: Optional[ChatBotStatus] = ChatBotStatus.ACTIVE` (default ACTIVE, not None), and both the values dict (line 84) and updateExpressions (line 93: `"bot_status": ExcludedValue()`) always include bot_status. There is no Optional-parameter/None-omit conditional-upsert pattern left in this repo — an earlier design (bot_status preservation via None→omit) was removed during the chat-accessibility simplification. Consumers that want to preserve the stored status must read it first and pass it back explicitly.

title: proxy-wiring anchor: SOCKS5 mechanism rewritten by httpx2 migration (2026-08-13, ADR-021)
content: Any proxy-wiring memory mentioning `AsyncProxyTransport`, `httpx_socks`, `_HTTPX_SOCKS_AVAILABLE`, a `transport` key in `ProxyKwargs`, `toKwargs(verify=...)`, or disabling HTTP/2 for SOCKS5 describes PRE-2026-08-13 code and is stale. The httpx→httpx2 migration (docs/llm/architecture.md ADR-021 decisions D2/D3; docs/design/httpx2-migration-v1.md) removed all of it: `ProxyKwargs` is now a single-key `{proxy: str}` for both HTTP and SOCKS5; `toKwargs()` takes no `verify` argument (callers apply `verify=<sslContext>` at the `httpx2.AsyncClient` level uniformly); `import httpx` resolves to httpx2 process-wide via `httpx2.alias_httpx()` in main.py (must run before any httpx-transitive import, e.g. PTB/Max applications); HTTP/2-over-SOCKS5 works natively (negotiated via TLS ALPN above the tunnel — the old disable guard was removed). Dependencies: httpx2==2.10.0 + socksio==1.0.0 (no httpx-socks).

title: YC SDK pin bumped 0.22.0 → 0.22.1; docs/other/yc-ai-sdk/ bundle not yet re-verified — search tools REMOVED in 0.22.1
content:
Found during the 2026-08-20 memory audit. `requirements.direct.txt` and `requirements.txt` now pin `yandex-ai-studio-sdk==0.22.1`, and the venv (`venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/yandex_ai_studio_sdk/__init__.py`) confirms `__version__ = "0.22.1"`. However, every file in `docs/other/yc-ai-sdk/` still says "verified against pinned v0.22.0, 2026-07-18" — and `index.md` (lines 24-26) states its own policy: bump the pin in requirements.direct.txt → re-run the verification pass. **Action for the next docs pass:** re-verify the bundle against 0.22.1 (prioritize tools-and-structured-output.md), update all H1s/banners and the index.md pin, and re-check the undocumented-subpackages list (`_assistants`, `_files`, `_vision`, `_threads`, `_runs`, `_messages`, `_experimental`) for changes.

title: Memory audit apply lifecycle: .applied-<timestamp> marker + applied/ subdirectory in .opencode/audit/
content:
Applying memory-audit artifacts leaves persistent on-disk evidence, discovered during the 2026-08-20 re-audit of the memory-audit-workflow topic:

1. **Marker file**: `.opencode/audit/.applied-<ISO-timestamp>` (current: `.applied-2026-07-14T19-28-53-578Z`) records when an apply pass ran.
2. **Applied copies**: per-topic artifacts are recorded under `.opencode/audit/applied/` (118 files as of 2026-08-20, including memory-audit-workflow.json itself).

Hazards:
- **Double-apply risk**: before dispatching any 'apply' pass, check for an existing `.applied-*` marker. At least one prior memory (d37c3945) wrongly asserted actions were 'not yet applied' months after the apply had run.
- **Root vs applied/ divergence**: root artifacts in `.opencode/audit/` can be REGENERATED by later re-audits, making them newer than their applied/ copies. Confirmed instance: documentation-drift — root artifact shows 124 memories (59 kept / 53 deleted / 12 replaced / 2 new) while its applied/ copy shows 103 (55/41/7/0). The applied/ copy is the snapshot of what was actually applied; the root artifact is the latest audit verdict.

title: YandexSpeechKitProvider v1.1 simplified lifecycle and known open gaps
content: Audit-verified state of lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py at 2026-08-20 (post-rewrite; all pre-2026-08-04 stateful machinery — _closeTask, _pollLock, _waitForPollSlot, _closeResponse, attempt deadlines, streamed response handling — is gone, grep-verified). Current shape: submit POST (NEVER retried, explicit 2xx range check) → poll/fetch via shared `_getWithRetry` (retries transport/429/5xx only; 4xx terminal; Retry-After delta-seconds only) → best-effort `_bestEffortDelete` + `_bestEffortDeleteObject` in `finally` OUTSIDE the asyncio.timeout budget → parseRecognitionEvents wrapped in its own except Exception → PROTOCOL_ERROR; result bodies buffered via response.content (no manual streaming/aclose). Open gaps verified at HEAD: (1) `_getWithRetry` returns 3xx responses as success (only 429/5xx/>=400 handled) — an empty 302 getRecognition body would parse as NO_SPEECH and discard the operation; (2) an operation shaped {"done": false, "error": {...}} keeps polling until maxPolls because _hasError is checked only inside the done branch; (3) no shared cross-transcribe poll-rate throttling despite design §7.4's aggregate-quota wording; (4) constructor accepts nan/inf numeric caps (only <= 0 checks — nan passes); (5) test suite lacks: auth-header assertions on poll/fetch/delete (submit only), getRecognition retry tests, poll transport-error and terminal 401/403 tests.

content:

title: Doc drift: design doc and services.md contradict shipped chat-accessibility code
content:
Two documentation spots contradict the shipped chat-accessibility-tracking code (verified 2026-08-20):

1. docs/design/chat-accessibility-tracking.md Implementation Divergence bullet (line ~63-65): 'The BaseBotHandler.getUserChats wrapper was REMOVED. Consumers call self.db.chatUsers.getUserChats(...) directly.' — FALSE. The wrapper exists at internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py:1322-1355 (keyword-only botStatus param, default ChatBotStatus.ACTIVE, filters out chats the user left via parseUserMetadata), and all listed consumers (configure.py:191, topic_manager.py:112, summarization.py:381, user_memories.py:1648, stats.py:287/605/1139, common.py:418) call self.getUserChats(...) through it. Only spam.py:1134 and common.py:416 call the repository directly. Code is the source of truth.

2. docs/llm/services.md line ~101 'Post-refresh nuance' claims that after the ~12h chat-info refresh a cache entry 'may briefly lack a bot_status field' so isChatInaccessible returns False for actually-INACCESSIBLE chats while 'the DB value stays correct'. — STALE (non-clobber-era text). Under the shipped self-heal design, TheBot.getChatInfo hardcodes bot_status=ACTIVE and setChatInfo/updateChatInfo always write it, so the refresh FLIPS an INACCESSIBLE chat to ACTIVE in both cache and DB (intended self-heal; receiving a message proves accessibility). Contradicts docs/llm/handlers.md:521 and docs/database-schema.md which correctly describe self-heal.

Per AGENTS.md 'When Documentation and Code Disagree': follow the code, fix the docs.

title: STT v1.1 gate-3: Object Storage routing, max-inline-bytes, OBJECT_STORAGE_ERROR
content:
STT v1.1 (docs/design/stt-v1.1.md) added Object Storage routing to the Yandex provider:

- `max-inline-bytes` (default 41943040 = 40 MiB, configs/00-defaults/stt.toml:27) is the routing threshold measured on `len(audio.data)`: below it clips go inline (base64); at/above it they route to Yandex Object Storage (S3-compatible, `YandexObjectStorage.upload()` in lib/stt/providers/yandex_object_storage.py) when configured, else fail with SOURCE_TOO_LARGE.
- Object Storage is implicitly enabled when `object-storage-bucket` + `object-storage-key-id` + `object-storage-key-secret` are ALL set (all four keys incl. prefix are commented out in the shipped config — inline-only by default). Partial configuration raises ValueError at startup (provider __init__ cross-field check; test-covered by TestPartialObjectStorageConfigRaisesValueError).
- Unresolved `${...}` placeholders in object-storage strings fail startup, same rule as api-key/folder-id.
- New enum member `STTErrorCode.OBJECT_STORAGE_ERROR = "object-storage-error"` (provider-owned; a best-effort delete failure does NOT surface as this code).
- SOURCE_TOO_LARGE is therefore dual-owned: STTService emits it for the source-byte cap, the provider surfaces it for the extracted-payload inline threshold.

title: STT handler wiring: _transcribeMedia background task + plain updateMediaAttachment terminalization
content:
STT is fully wired into the handler layer (not a separate STTHandler — folded into the media pipeline):

- `BaseBotHandler._processMediaV2` (internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py) gates transcription on FOUR conditions: `_sttEnabled` (cached `[stt].enabled` at __init__) AND mediaType in {VIDEO, VIDEO_NOTE, VOICE, AUDIO} AND `PARSE_ATTACHMENTS` AND `TRANSCRIBE_MEDIA` chat settings (both default false; TRANSCRIBE_MEDIA is FRIEND-page). DONE rows always early-return (no reprocessing).
- The gate-on path persists the row as PENDING, downloads bytes ONCE in a shared synchronous block (reused when SAVE_ATTACHMENTS is also on via the `if mediaData is None` guard), then schedules `asyncio.create_task(self._transcribeMedia(ret.id, chatId, data=mediaData))` with `ret.task = sttTask` (mirrors image parsing, so `EnsuredMessage.updateMediaContent()` can await it).
- `_transcribeMedia(mediaId, chatId, data)` (base.py:1416-1453) does NOT download — it calls `STTService.getInstance().transcribeMedia(data, chatId=chatId)` and terminalizes via plain `updateMediaAttachment` (PENDING→DONE+description | PENDING→FAILED). No CAS — `setStatusVerified` was deleted 2026-08-04 (single attachments have no concurrent writes; last-write semantics suffice).
- `asyncio.CancelledError` propagates (not caught by `except Exception`), leaving the row PENDING; orphan-reclaim in `_processMediaV2` reprocesses rows PENDING longer than `constants.PROCESSING_TIMEOUT` = 30 min (base.py:1885).
- The transcript lands in `media_attachments.description` and reaches the LLM as the structured JSON `mediaDescription` field via `EnsuredMessage.formatForLLM()` — this structural delivery is the accepted prompt-injection mitigation (no text header needed).

title: STTService.initialize is idempotent and injects statsStorage
content:
`STTService.initialize(configManager, *, statsStorage: Optional[StatsStorage] = None)` (internal/services/stt/service.py:152):

- **Idempotent**: `__init__` sets `self._initialized = False` (distinct from the `hasattr(self, 'initialized')` singleton sentinel) and initialize() early-returns on `if self._initialized` (lines 180-182). Locked in by TestInitializeIsIdempotent.
- **statsStorage injection**: forwarded to the provider constructor; `None` (default) selects the no-op NullStatsStorage inside the provider base (lib/stt/abstract.py:87). Wired in main.py:121 as `STTService.getInstance().initialize(self.configManager, statsStorage=sttStatsStorage)` gated on `[stats].enabled`; shutdown calls `await STTService.getInstance().aclose()` (main.py:189).
- `_enabled = True` is set only AFTER successful provider construction (service.py:241), so `isEnabled()` is False after a failed initialize (locked in by TestIsEnabledFalseAfterFailedInitialize).
- The startup log uses the actual provider variable: `f"STT service initialized (provider={provider})."`.

title: No-handler delayed task re-delay marks the DB row done: task does not survive restart
content:
**QUEUE SERVICE NO-HANDLER GOTCHA (generic, applies to any DelayedTaskFunction):**

When a delayed task fires and no handler is registered for its function (internal/services/queue_service/service.py:385-388), the loop logs an error, sets delayedUntil = now + 60s, and re-puts the task in the in-memory queue. BUT the code then falls through (no `continue`) to the unconditional updateDelayedTask(taskId, True) at service.py:401-402 — the DB row is marked done on the FIRST firing.

Consequence: the re-delay loop keeps the task alive only in memory for the current process lifetime. After a restart, getPendingDelayedTasks() no longer returns the row, so the task is gone permanently.

This matters for config-gated handlers (e.g. STATS_PAGES_CLEANUP registered only when [stats]/[stats-pages] enabled): disabling the feature while tasks are pending means those tasks fire repeatedly (+60s) with error logs until the process restarts, then vanish — the deferred-work-until-re-enable expectation only holds within one process lifetime. Documented for the stats case as risk R10 in docs/design/stats-display-v1.md (lines 1247-1253); the queue-service-level behavior is generic.

title: test_httpx2.py — version-only dependency pin; suite recomposed to 6 modules
content: tests/dependencies/test_httpx2.py (added 2026-08-13 with the httpx→httpx2 migration) is a VERSION-ONLY pin: a single TestPinnedVersion asserting importlib.metadata.version("httpx2") == "2.10.0", with no behaviour pins — unlike the other suite members, which pin call-site behaviour. httpx2[http2,socks]==2.10.0 is a direct dependency (requirements.direct.txt:9), a Pydantic-org fork of httpx 0.28.1 that is API-identical but adds native SOCKS5 `proxy=` support; the module docstring records that rationale. It follows the suite's PINNED_VERSION + `#:` comment + TestPinnedVersion pattern. With it the suite is 6 modules: five importlib.metadata-pinned + sqlite-vec's native `SELECT vec_version()` probe. Documentation has not caught up: tests/dependencies/__init__.py enumerates only five libraries (no httpx2), and docs/llm/testing.md plus docs/llm/memories/dependency-usage-tests.md still say '5 files / 58 tests'.

title: TTLDict tests use fakeClock() context manager — never real sleeps; June-era line refs are stale
content: tests/lib/utils/ttl_dict_test.py defines a module-level `fakeClock()` context manager (lines 14-48) that patches `time.time` and `time.sleep`: time.time() reads a single mutable epoch-seconds holder, and time.sleep(N) advances that holder by N seconds instead of blocking. All expiration tests wrap their bodies in `with fakeClock():`. This is safe because the production TTLDict resolves expiry exclusively via time.time() (it never calls time.sleep). Rationale documented in the helper: tests are unittest.TestCase methods, so pytest fixtures cannot inject values — the context manager is the per-test-scoped equivalent. Convention: new TTLDict TTL tests should use fakeClock(), not real sleeps. Side effect: the file grew ~40-50 lines below line 50 when this helper and expanded docstrings were added (after late June 2026), so line-number references from June-2026 memories of this test file are systematically off by roughly that amount.

title: configs/common/ stays platform-agnostic via ${PLATFORM} env substitution
content: The shared configs/common/ layer selects Telegram vs Max at load time via ${PLATFORM} substitution rather than per-platform file forks: configs/common/00-config.toml sets root-dir = "storage/${PLATFORM}" and bot mode = "${PLATFORM}"; configs/common/01-bot-defaults.toml sets save-prefix = "${PLATFORM}-". PLATFORM is defined only in the per-platform .env files (.env.local-telegram and .env.prod-telegram define PLATFORM="telegram"; .env.local-max and .env.prod-max define PLATFORM="max"), NOT in the root .env. Because ConfigManager substitutes ${VAR} once over the fully merged config at construction (internal/config/manager.py:130), platform-specific values resolve per environment. When adding shared config that must differ per platform, prefer ${PLATFORM} substitution (or a new env var) over duplicating files into the *-telegram/*-max override dirs.

title: yandex-ai-studio-sdk pin bumped to 0.22.1 — yc-ai-sdk doc banners still claim 0.22.0
content: Discovered during the 2026-08-21 memory audit: `requirements.direct.txt:18` and `requirements.txt:95` now pin `yandex-ai-studio-sdk==0.22.1`, but the `docs/other/yc-ai-sdk/` bundle banners (e.g. index.md H1 and per-file version-drift banners) still say "verified against pinned v0.22.0" (see index.md:34 `pip install yandex-ai-studio-sdk==0.22.0`). Implications: (1) any agent re-auditing the yc-ai-sdk docs must first rebuild the venv and re-capture against 0.22.1; (2) the banner version labels are now stale by one patch release and should be refreshed whenever the bundle is next touched; (3) the 2026-07-18/19 SDK-behavior memories (text_embeddings alias behavior, _get_model_uri passthrough, ChatModelResult shape, wheel layout) were verified against 0.22.0 and carry a re-verify caveat.

title: DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE is a phantom: refactor memories/docs reference a constant that was never committed
content:
Discovered during the 2026-08-20 memory audit of the lib/ai customParams refactor. Several refactor-era artifacts reference a module constant `DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE = 0.5` in lib/ai/abstract.py and a YC SDK structured-output clamp `min(self._customParams.get("temperature", DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE), 0.3)` — NEITHER exists in the committed code. Verified: grep of working tree and HEAD finds no DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE anywhere in lib/, internal/, or tests/ source; `git log --all -S "DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE" -- lib/ai/abstract.py` returns no commits; abstract.py:44 is `_R = TypeVar(...)`. The constant and clamp existed only in the 2026-07-20 pre-commit working tree that the in-flight status memories described; commit 149b3dbc ('lib/ai - add customParams + move temperature there', the only commit touching these files) landed without them. Behavior now: absent temperature key is simply omitted from requests (API-side default applies); docstrings saying "default 0.5" (abstract.py:60-61, 105-106) are descriptive only.

**Stale references to clean up (docs drift, found 2026-08-20):**
- docs/llm/configuration.md:220 — 'see DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE in lib/ai/abstract.py' (broken pointer)
- docs/llm/memories/llm-customparams-refactor.md:5,13,21 — constant + clamp described; line 21 tells agents to import it (would ImportError)
- docs/other/yc-ai-sdk/gap-analysis.md:13 — 'lowers temperature to min(configured, 0.3)' for structured output
- lib/ai/providers/yc_sdk_provider.py:565-566 — _generateStructured docstring claims the lowering behavior the code no longer implements (line 583 is a plain `self._customParams.copy()`)
- tests/lib/ai/test_manager.py:842 — comment references the constant

**Lesson for agents:** do not trust constant names cited in docs/llm/memories/*.md without a grep; when a doc tells you to import something, verify it exists first.

title: user_data feature was dropped: UserDataHandler → UserMemoriesHandler (migration_022)
content: The legacy `user_data` feature was fully removed: `internal/bot/common/handlers/user_data.py` and `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_user_data.py` no longer exist, and `migration_022_drop_user_data.py` drops the table (legacy facts were backfilled into `user_memories` by migration_020 Backfill A+B). The successor is `UserMemoriesHandler` (`internal/bot/common/handlers/user_memories.py`) with tests in `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_user_memories.py`. It owns the `[user-memory]` config section, caches it ONCE in `__init__` (~lines 188-193: `userMemoryConfig = configManager.get("user-memory", {})`, `self._memoryRefineEnabled = userMemoryConfig.get("enabled", False)`), registers memory LLM tools gated on that kill switch, and runs the refinement cron. Memories referencing UserDataHandler/user_data.py are stale on this point.

title: Post-migration_025 vector stack shape: model_id lookup + native vec0, numpy and MessageEmbeddingDict retired
content:
The embedding/vector stack after `migration_025_embedding_model_lookup`:
- Embedding provenance (model name + dimensions) is normalized into a `models` lookup table keyed by integer `model_id`; repositories resolve `(model, dimensions)` → `model_id` via an injected `EmbeddingModelsRepository.getOrCreateModelId` resolver (with caching).
- vec0 virtual tables (`vec_message_embeddings_{N}`, `vec_user_memories_{N}`) use `model_id INTEGER PARTITION KEY` (not a model-name string).
- Semantic search delegates to the provider's native vec0 KNN via `ChatSearchRepository._nativeVectorSearch`; numpy cosine ranking was fully retired (Decision D8) — no in-process fallback exists; unavailable/failed vec0 returns `[]`.
- `MessageEmbeddingDict` and `ChatEmbeddingsRepository.getMessageEmbedding` were removed; `getMessagesWithoutEmbeddings` still returns `List[ChatMessageDict]`.
- New repositories follow this shape: see `UserMemoriesRepository` (`_upsertVecMemoryEmbedding`, `_semanticSearchMemories`) for the second implementation of the pattern.

title: Embedding provenance normalized into models lookup table (migration_025) — model_id replaces (embedding_model, embedding_dimensions)
content:
Discovered during audit (2026-08-21): migration_025 normalized embedding-model provenance. `user_memories` (and the chat-history embedding path) no longer store `(embedding_model, embedding_dimensions)` per row — instead a `models` lookup table maps `(model_name, dimensions)` → canonical `model_id`, and rows carry `user_memories.model_id` (NULL until a vec0 insert succeeds).

Key pieces:
- `internal/database/repositories/embedding_models.py` — new `EmbeddingModelsRepository` backing the lookup table.
- `_resolveModelId(model, dimensions, *, dataSource=None)` on `ChatSearchRepository`, `ChatEmbeddingsRepository`, and `UserMemoriesRepository` — resolves the canonical id; takes an injectable resolver in tests.
- `getMemoriesWithoutEmbeddings` stale predicate is now `model_id IS NULL OR model_id != :currentModelId` (single-table, no vec0 JOIN).
- `deleteObsoleteMemoryEmbeddings` resets `model_id = NULL` (plus best-effort vec0 cleanup across `vec_user_memories_{N}` tables, skipping sqlite-vec shadow tables matched by `^vec_user_memories_\d+$`).
- Related plan doc: `docs/plans/embedding-model-lookup-refactor-v1.md` (one of the 3 surviving plans in docs/plans/).

Older memories describing `embedding_model`/`embedding_dimensions` column predicates predate this refactor.

title: StatsAggregationService.getQueryStorage: handler-side read-only seam into the storage registry
content: StatsAggregationService exposes `getQueryStorage(eventType: str) -> StatsStorage` (internal/services/stats/service.py:248-261) for handler-side READ-ONLY queries. It returns the registered storage for the eventType, or a FRESH NullStatsStorage instance if the service is uninitialized or the eventType is not registered (e.g., stats disabled). This complements createStatsStorage (write-path factory) as the query seam used by stats consumers like the /stats bot handlers (see tests/bot/common/handlers/test_stats.py, which reset StatsAggregationService._instance per test). Note it returns a new NullStatsStorage on each miss, not a shared instance. Covered by TestGetQueryStorage in tests/services/stats/test_service.py (~lines 986-1081, 5 tests: registered/unregistered/not-initialized/fresh-null-each-call/disabled-stats).

title: Doc drift: immediate-mode GET /updates returns a compound marker, not null — docs say otherwise
content:
docs/llm/architecture.md (ADR-013, delivery-semantics bullet, line 476) and docs/llm/libraries.md (line 474) both claim that in immediate/at-most-once mode (`mark-on-subsequent-poll = false`) the receiver's `GET /updates` response carries `marker: null` ("there is nothing to acknowledge on the next poll").

The CODE does otherwise: `handleGetUpdates` in internal/max_webhook_receiver/app.py:216-220 computes `newMarker = f"{lastRow['received_at'].isoformat()}|{lastRow['id']}"` and returns it in BOTH modes — the `if not markOnSubsequent:` branch only adds the `markProcessed(rowIds)` call; the marker construction is unconditional. `tests/max_webhook_receiver/test_app.py::testImmediateMode_marksOnRead` (line 266) explicitly asserts `payload["marker"] is not None`, so the tests pin the code behavior, not the docs.

Impact is benign (the bot treats the marker as opaque and, in immediate mode, acking is a no-op since rows are already processed) but the two doc statements are factually wrong vs code+tests and should be corrected in a doc-sync pass.

title: lib/sandbox/manager.py documents `self` in Args: sections — a convention unique to that file
content:
Every public and private method docstring in `lib/sandbox/manager.py` explicitly documents `self` as the first Args entry: `self: The SandboxManager instance.` (22 occurrences, lines 148-1277, including `__init__`, `createSession`, `recover`, `_refreshPackageList`, etc.).

This is NOT followed anywhere else in `lib/sandbox/` — `locks.py` and `errors.py` `__init__` docstrings omit `self`. It appears to be a manager.py-specific style introduced during the June 2026 docstring audit pass.

When editing or adding docstrings in manager.py, preserve this pattern for consistency with the file; do not "clean it up" to match the rest of the package unless doing a deliberate file-wide normalization.

title: STT stale-docstring leftovers: models.py references removed STTLoaderResult; design doc pins old boto3 version
content: Post-stateless-refactor leftovers found during the 2026-08-20 STT memory audit: (1) lib/stt/models.py module docstring (lines 20-21) still advertises 'STTLoaderResult + STTMediaLoader: the typed async loader boundary' — both types were REMOVED when STTService became stateless (the service now passes raw bytes to provider.stt(data)); grep confirms no definitions remain anywhere in the repo. (2) docs/design/stt-v1.1.md references boto3==1.43.48 (~lines 71/155/729) while requirements.direct.txt:6 now pins boto3==1.43.70 — cosmetic drift. Neither affects behavior; fix opportunistically in a docs pass.

title: run_python LLM tool result includes workspace-relative workDir file listing
content: `_llmToolRunSandboxCode` in `internal/bot/common/handlers/sandbox.py` (lines 337-346) scans the run's workDir after execution and includes a `files` key in the tool result: `[{"path": str, "sizeBytes": int, "isDirectory": bool}]`, where paths are workspace-relative (e.g. `.run/<runId>/work/report.csv`). This is the mechanism by which the LLM learns where created files live — important because the file-browsing tools (`sandbox_list_files`, `sandbox_read_file`) and `/sandbox files|read` commands still default to the session workspace root, not the per-run workDir. The `/run` slash-command handler has the same workDir scan (around line 787). `RunResult.workDir` (types.py) carries the `.run/<runId>/work` path that feeds this scan.

title: Current stats stack architecture: factory + CRON_JOB rider + /stats query surface
content:
Post-stats-collecting-v1/aggregation current architecture (verified 2026-08-21):

1. **StatsAggregationService** (internal/services/stats/service.py) is the single construction seam AND the periodic coordinator. initialize(configManager, database) parses [stats] config once (interval/retention/batch-limit/enabled, clamped, fail-loud ValueError) and registers _dtCronJob on the shared DelayedTaskFunction.CRON_JOB 60s tick — NO self-seeding addDelayedTask and NO rescheduling; elapsed-time is gated in-memory via _lastRunTime. It owns the storage registry; createStatsStorage(eventType, dataSource) returns DatabaseStatsStorage (registered) when enabled, else an unregistered NullStatsStorage; getQueryStorage(eventType) is the handler-side read access (NullStatsStorage fallback).

2. **main.py builds five storages through the factory**: llm_request (→LLMManager), llm_tool_call (→LLMService.injectStatsStorage), stt_request (→STTService), message, command (both →bot applications → HandlersManager).

3. **message events record BOTH directions** (Phase 4): only DELETED/UNSPECIFIED excluded; direction via `sent` label = sender.id == getBotId() (TTL-cached 3600s, Max uses getMyInfo(useCache=False)).

4. **/stats handler** (internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py) is the production query surface: getQueryStorage → storage.query(...) → StatsAnalyzer (filterByLabel/topN/sumMetric) across all five event types. Note: backfilled rows carry no `sent` label.

5. **Aggregation cycle**: per storage, drain aggregate(limit=batchLimit) up to MAX_AGGREGATION_ROUNDS=10, then purgeProcessed(retentionDays) — per-storage try/except isolation, handler never raises.

title: extraData typing has three generations; ExtraDataDict (TypedDict) is the most typed and used by chat_search tool handlers
content:
LLM tool handler `extraData` parameter typing exists in three styles in the codebase (verified 2026-08-20):

1. **Oldest** — `Optional[Dict[str, Any]]` (or `Dict[str, Any]` in divination.py): weather.py, media.py, divination.py, common.py:165, example.py:115, and the sandbox tool handlers.
2. **Newer** — `Optional[Dict[str, object]]` (repo no-`Any` rule): user_memories.py `_llmToolAddMemory` (line 400) and `_llmToolSearchMemories` (line 647). This is what `.agents/skills/add-llm-tool/SKILL.md` Site 3 prescribes for new tools.
3. **Most typed** — `Optional[ExtraDataDict]`: a `TypedDict(total=False)` defined in `internal/services/llm/models.py` with fields `ensuredMessage: EnsuredMessage`, `typingManager: Optional[TypingManager]`, `isRefinement: bool`. Used by all four ChatSearchHandler tool methods (chat_search.py lines 580/774/861/927; imported at line 61), as the service-level extraData parameter type in `LLMService.generateTextViaLLM` (service.py:774), and in intermediate-callback signatures (llm_messages.py:170/1023, dev_commands.py:990, user_memories.py:1287).

title: Empty-text abstention guard: in ("<skip>", "") treats bare empty LLM output as SKIPPED_BY_MODEL
content: In `internal/bot/common/handlers/llm_messages.py` (~line 401), the abstention guard in `_sendLLMChatMessage` is now `if imagePrompt is None and lmRetText.strip().strip("`").strip() in ("<skip>", ""): return LLMReplyOutcome.SKIPPED_BY_MODEL`. The `""` clause is NEW relative to older skip-sentinel memories: bare empty text (e.g. reasoning-budget exhaustion producing finish_reason="length" with empty content, surfacing as status=TRUNCATED_FINAL, resultText="") is treated as model abstention so it never reaches `sendMessage` (which would raise BadRequest: Message text is empty). This is the handler-half of Option B from `docs/plans/llm-empty-truncated-final-handling-v1.md` (commit 7e2b5501); a sibling service-layer post-budget synthesizer (service.py:926-951) fires only when budgetExhausted=True (tool-call round cap hit), so single-shot empty FINAL relies entirely on this handler guard. Backtick-only and whitespace-only outputs also collapse to "" and abstain. Pinned by `TestLLMEmptyResponseGuard` (~line 867 of tests/bot/common/handlers/test_llm_messages.py). Note: the code snippet in docs/llm/configuration.md (~lines 77-80) still shows the old `== "<skip>"` form — doc drift.

title: Per-migration test helpers: when migration NNN's down() is a no-op, rollbackTo(NNN-1) is NOT enough — roll back below the table-creating migration and re-apply it
content:
Nuance of the `rollbackTo(targetVersion=NNN-1)` convention (memory `5d01e6cb`), observed in `tests/database/test_migration_021_user_memories_soft_delete.py`.

Some migrations have an intentionally no-op `down()` — portable `DROP COLUMN` is unavailable across SQLite/PostgreSQL/MySQL, and a nullable additive column is safe to leave on rollback (e.g. migration_021's `deleted_at`). For such a migration, `rollbackTo(targetVersion=NNN-1)` leaves its column in place, so the test cannot reach the true pre-NNN schema.

The fix used by test_migration_021: roll back BELOW the migration that created the underlying table (`rollbackTo(targetVersion=19)`, i.e. pre-020), then re-create the table in its pre-NNN shape by calling the creating migration's `up()` directly (`Migration020UserMemories().up(provider)` — its backfills are no-ops on the empty legacy tables the rollback leaves behind).

Rule when writing `tests/database/test_migration_NNN_*.py`: check whether NNN's `down()` actually undoes the schema change. If it's a no-op, the helper must target an earlier version (typically the version before the migration that created the affected table) and re-apply that migration's `up()` to reconstruct the pre-NNN shape. This is why test_migration_021 targets 19 while its siblings target NNN-1.

title: No-op pacing-sleep autouse fixtures: naming convention, scoped patch target, and infinite-loop hazard
content:
**Verified 2026-08-20.** The handler-test variant of the fake-clock family (item 4 of memory `d4a5d0e3`) has a concrete convention worth naming:

**Pattern:** class-scoped `@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)` helpers that no-op PRODUCTION pacing sleeps by patching `asyncio.sleep` scoped to the production module (NOT globally):
- `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_chat_search.py:1109` — `_noOpBackfillPacingSleep` patches `internal.bot.common.handlers.chat_search.asyncio.sleep` to `AsyncMock()`. Rationale in docstring: unmocked it costs `batchSize * 0.1s` real wall-clock per test (~5s for the full-batch regression).
- `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_resender.py:350` — `_noOpSendPacingSleep` no-ops the inter-send exponential-backoff cushion (`resender.py:476`, 0.25 doubling to 10s) and the inter-forward 0.1s pause (`resender.py:474`).
- Precedent chain: both docstrings cite `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_user_memories_memory_regen.py` (~line 676) as the pioneer for the identical `user_memories.py` backfill pacing constant.

**Naming convention:** underscore-prefixed `_noOp<What>PacingSleep` — the underscore signals implementation-detail fixture to pytest.

**HAZARD (documented in test_resender.py:337-340):** production wait loops that advance via real `asyncio.sleep` MUST NOT be no-op'd — the media-group wait loop in `resender.py` (~383-389) would infinite-loop. Media-group forwarding tests are therefore in a SEPARATE class without the no-op fixture. When adding a new no-op pacing fixture, audit every `asyncio.sleep` in the patched module for wait-until-condition loops first.

**Known doc drift:** `_noOpBackfillPacingSleep`'s docstring cites 'chat_search.py ~line 439' but the sleep is at line 513 as of 2026-08-20 (constants extracted to `internal/bot/constants.py`).

title: STT golden tests: 6th golden suite covering the Yandex SpeechKit STT v3 wire lifecycle
content:
`tests/lib/stt/golden/` (added ~2026-08) is the 6th golden-data suite, after ai, divination, geocode_maps, openweathermap, and yandex_search. title: _dtOnExit/_cleanupOldData now does per-namespace cache TTLs + bayes-token purge (not '>90d cache')
content:
`HandlersManager._dtOnExit` (registered as the QueueService DO_EXIT handler at internal/bot/common/handlers/manager.py:645, method at line 652) forwards to `_cleanupOldData()` (lines 707-730). As of 2026-08-20 that method performs four sweeps driven by module-level constants (lines 94-139):

title: StatsAggregationService is the stats wiring hub: CRON_JOB aggregation + storage registry
content:
internal/services/stats/service.py defines `StatsAggregationService` (singleton, `getInstance()`), which centralizes stats wiring:
- `initialize(configManager, database)` reads [stats] config once (enabled, aggregation-interval-seconds min 60, events-retention-days, aggregation-batch-limit) and registers `self._dtCronJob` as a QueueService CRON_JOB handler (line 196) — the aggregation trigger rides the shared 60-second CRON tick, gated by elapsed interval (default 3600s).
- `createStatsStorage(eventType, dataSource=None)` (line 204) is the factory: returns an UNREGISTERED NullStatsStorage when stats disabled, otherwise a registered DatabaseStatsStorage keyed by eventType.
- main.py (lines 96-129) creates five storages this way — llm_request, tool, stt, message, command — and injects message/command storages into HandlersManager, which fans messageStatsStorage out to all handlers (manager.py:648-650).
- Aggregation iterates registered storages calling aggregate() and purgeProcessed() per retention config.
This supersedes the old 'deferred: aggregation trigger' item from docs/archive/plans/lib-stats-stats-library-v3.md §10; the query-API side lives in lib/stats/analysis.py (StatsAnalyzer) and lib/stats/stats_pages/ plus the /stats command.

title: configs/ deployment layers are gitignored — glob/grep miss them; configs/common/ exists
content:
The configs/ tree has two kinds of subdirectories: the git-tracked defaults (configs/00-defaults/) and GITIGNORED deployment layers: common/, local/, local-max/, local-telegram/, prod/, prod-max/, prod-telegram/.

Because glob/grep tools that respect .gitignore skip ignored paths, searching for e.g. `bot-defaults.toml` returns only the 00-defaults copy and can lead an auditor to FALSELY conclude the other files 'do not exist'. This happened at least twice: a 2026-06-29 memory audit recorded 'configs/common/ no longer exists', yet a 2026-08-20 re-verification found configs/common/ with 13 TOML files (incl. 01-bot-defaults.toml, which overrides [bot.defaults] keys such as `chat-prompt` at line 57, bot-nicknames, model choices, tier defaults). docs/max-webhook-setup.md documents `--config-dir ./configs/common` in real deployment commands.

Rules:
- When verifying claims about config files, use direct directory reads (not gitignore-filtered glob/grep).
- Remember deployment layers legitimately OVERRIDE 00-defaults values — 'key X lives exclusively in 00-defaults' claims are wrong whenever an ignored layer redefines the key.
