title: /stats reply-format redesign: chat reply no longer renders users/bot split
content:
The /stats command reply format was redesigned on 2026-08-22 (user-ratified). Key changes:

**Chat reply format** (all in internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py):
- Header: `📊 Stats — {period} (UTC) — {prettyChat}` via getChatTitle(useMarkdown=True, addChatId=True, addChatType=False) - chat-type emoji + bold title + backticked #id, plain #id fallback
- Section headers: bold `**Messages:** N`, `**Commands:** N`, `**Tools:** N · avg X.XXs`, `**LLM:** N requests · avg X.XXs` (avg folded in only when >0)
- Top lists: label line (`Top:` / `Top models:`) + fenced code block, one item per line `• {key}{pad}  {count}` with ljust/rjust alignment, usernames are BARE `@name` (backticks stripped - the FENCE prevents mentions, not inline code)
- The users N / bot M breakdown line was DELETED from the chat reply entirely
- Error lines now have `⚠ ` prefix (rendered only when >0)
- STT line dropped its noun: `STT: N` (was `STT: N запросов`)
- Fence-atomic chunking: `_chunkLinesWithFenceAtomicity` ensures fenced blocks never split across ~3000-char chunks
- Format unified across Telegram and Max (no per-platform fork)

**Binary direction semantics** (surviving in other contexts):
- Direction stays binary at query time: bot = `sent` "True", users = "False" or absent
- The users/bot split is rendered ONLY by the `/stats --web` HTML page generator (lib/stats/stats_pages/generator.py)
- The chat reply no longer renders ANY direction split

**Helpers added**:
- `_renderFencedTopBlock` (7 call sites) - renders aligned fenced top blocks
- `_chunkLinesWithFenceAtomicity` - fence-atomic ~3000-char chunking
- `_buildMessagesBreakdownLines` - shared messages section builder for both reply paths

**Args normalization**: leading run of `—` (em-dash) or `–` (en-dash) in a token normalizes to `--` (phone/laptop autocorrect fix); single `-` untouched (negative chatIds stay positional).

title: Durable user display taste evolution: usernames now fenced bare
content:
The project's durable taste for preventing accidental @mentions in list items evolved:

**Pre-2026-08-22**: "wrap mention-triggering tokens (usernames) in backticks" - used backticked inline code like `` `@name` `` to prevent @mentions.

**2026-08-22 redesign (revised)**: Usernames go inside a FENCED code block rendered BARE (no backticks) - the fence itself prevents accidental mentions, not inline code. Example:
```
• @alice   123
• @bob      45
```

The redesign superseded the earlier durable taste claim (docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md bullet 5) because:
- Fenced blocks look cleaner than inline code for multi-item lists
- Fence-atomic chunking ensures blocks never split across messages
- Max TextFormat.MARKDOWN supports Strong/Monospaced types, mapping **bold** and fences correctly

This applies to /stats Top lists (users, commands, tools, LLM models) and any future multi-item username displays.

title: Documentation supersession patterns in Gromozeka
content:
Gromozeka uses distinct patterns for documenting superseded design claims:

**docs/design/stats-display-v1.md pattern**:
- Original body text is preserved as historical record
- Amendment blocks at the top (reverse-chronological by amendment date) supersede specific claims
- Each amendment explicitly lists what it supersedes (e.g., "Supersedes the 'Top users format' bullet of the binary amendment above")
- No in-place editing of historical body text - history stays, markers guide readers

**docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md pattern**:
- Dated historical bullets are kept
- When a later revision partially supersedes an earlier bullet, append a marker to the earlier bullet's tail
- Marker format: "PARTIALLY SUPERSEDED [later bullet reference] - what changed"
- New bullet added after the superseded one, with "SUPERSEDES the ... notes above" chains when applicable

**CHANGELOG.md pattern**:
- [Unreleased] entries are edited in place when claims become false (not preserved as history)
- This is different from design docs - changelog describes CURRENT state under Unreleased
- When fixing a stale entry, edit it to accurately reflect the final state
- Add separate new entries for additional changes

**Lesson**: When doing doc syncs, identify the pattern for each file type and follow it - don't mix approaches. Design docs preserve history; changelog describes current state.

title: Stats handler _formatCount with k/m/g suffixes and significant digit rounding
content:
The StatsHandler class in internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py implements `_formatCount(value: int) -> str` which formats counts with k/m/g suffixes:

**Implementation Details:**
- value < 1000 → plain str(value)
- ≥1000: Use tier suffixes (k=1e3, m=1e6, g=1e9)
- **CRITICAL: Round to 3 significant digits BEFORE tier selection** (not after)
  - Example: 999999 → round to 1_000_000 → tier m → "1m"
  - If you divide first (999999/1e3=999.999k), then round → "1000k" (wrong)
- Rounding logic: `order = int(math.log10(abs(value)))`, `divisor = 10 ** (order - sigFigs + 1)`, `rounded = int(round(value / divisor)) * divisor`
- Tier selection AFTER rounding: k (1e3) for values < 1e6, m (1e6) for values < 1e9, g (1e9) otherwise
- Scaled value formatting: 3 significant digits via decimal precision (scaled < 10 → 2 decimals, < 100 → 1 decimal, else 0 decimals)
- Strip trailing zeros and decimal point from formatted string
- Replace dot with comma for Russian locale decimal separator
- **Do NOT use locale module** (per spec)

**Application Sites:**
All count/tokens numbers in both code paths (direct-query and FromAnalyzer):
- Section totals: Messages, Commands, Tools, LLM, STT
- Tokens line: `tokens: in X / out Y`
- Errors lines: `⚠ errors: N`
- Top block counts (before alignment in `_renderFencedTopBlock`)
- Chat list messages count

**Reference Table (exact strings):**
999 → "999"
1000 → "1k"
1484 → "1,48k"
1500 → "1,5k"
79662 → "79,7k"
389924 → "390k"
9999 → "10k"
999999 → "1m"
1234567 → "1,23m"
2400000000 → "2,4g"

title: Stats handler _formatDuration with compound time formatting
content:
The StatsHandler class in internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py implements `_formatDuration(seconds: float, subMinuteDecimals: int = 2) -> str` which formats durations in compound time notation:

**Implementation Details:**
- seconds < 60 → `f"{seconds:.{subMinuteDecimals}f}s"` (preserves caller's decimal precision)
- 60 ≤ seconds < 3600 → `f"{minutes}m {secs:.1f}s"` (one decimal for seconds)
- ≥ 3600 → `f"{hours}h {minutes:02d}m {secs:.1f}s"` (minutes zero-padded to 2 digits)

**Application Sites:**
- STT audio duration: `audio:` line (uses subMinuteDecimals=1 for one decimal)
- LLM avg time: `· avg X` folded in header (uses default subMinuteDecimals=2)
- Tools avg time: `· avg X` folded in header (uses default subMinuteDecimals=2)
- STT avg time line: `avg time:` (uses default subMinuteDecimals=2)

**Preserves Existing Precision:**
- Audio duration kept at one decimal (e.g., 33.3s)
- Average times kept at two decimals (e.g., 11.73s)

**Test Cases:**
0.5 → "0.50s"
33.3 → "33.3s" (audio, 1 decimal)
59.99 → "59.99s"
75.43 → "1m 15.4s"
3660 → "1h 01m 0.0s"
3745 → "1h 02m 25.0s"

title: Stats handler significant digit rounding order critical for k/m/g formatting
content:
**GOTCHA: Rounding order is critical for _formatCount implementation**

When implementing k/m/g suffix formatting with 3 significant digits, the order of operations matters:

**WRORD approach (divide then round):**
```
999999 / 1e3 = 999.999k → round to 3 sig figs → 1000k
```
This produces "1000k" which doesn't match the spec's expected "1m"

**CORRECT approach (round then divide):**
```
999999 → round to 3 sig figs → 1_000_000 → / 1e6 = 1m
```
This produces "1m" as expected

**Implementation:**
1. Round original value to 3 significant digits: `_roundToSignificantDigits(value, 3)`
2. Select tier based on rounded value (not original)
3. Format scaled value with appropriate decimal precision

The _roundToSignificantDigits method uses: `order = int(math.log10(abs(value)))`, `divisor = 10 ** (order - sigFigs + 1)`, `rounded = int(round(value / divisor)) * divisor`

This insight was discovered through iterative testing against the spec's reference table, which showed 999999 → "1m". The naive implementation would produce "1000k", revealing the rounding order requirement.

title: Test weakening anti-pattern: never weaken tests to accept unratified code
content:
When a test fails because production code renders a different shape than the ratified spec, the CORRECT remediation is to revert the production code to match the ratified shape, NOT to weaken the test to accept the regression. 

Example from stats handler /stats number/duration formatting (Gate-1 review, Aug 23 2026): The ratified Top-block shape required a label line `Top:` on its own line, then a fence line ``` on its own line. Production emitted the merged ```Top: form instead. The developer weakened `testMessagesSection_topUsersFormat` to accept both shapes via an `if fenceFormat:` branch, masking the regression.

Correct process: 
- If spec says X, test expects X, and production renders Y → fix production (not test)
- The only legitimate test fixture updates are when spec CHANGES and test expects OLD spec → update test to NEW spec values

Distinguishing failure types:
- Test is correct, code is wrong → revert code (Critical: test weakened to fit regression)
- Test is stale, code is correct → update fixture (Important: expected "1093" vs actual "1,09k" per spec)

This pattern of test weakening entrenches regressions and must be caught in code review.

title: Dual-path consistency requirement: direct and FromAnalyzer code paths must render identical shapes
content:
StatsHandler has two parallel code paths for rendering stats sections:
1. Direct query path (e.g., `_buildCommandsSection`)
2. FromAnalyzer path (e.g., `_buildCommandsSectionFromAnalyzer`)

Both paths MUST render identical output shapes for the same section. Divergence leads to user-visible inconsistency depending on execution path.

Example (stats handler, Aug 23 2026): LLM models top block rendered differently:
- Direct path: `_renderFencedTopBlock(modelNamesWithCounts, "Top models:")` → merged ```Top models: form
- FromAnalyzer path: `lines.append("Top models:")` then `_renderFencedTopBlock(modelNamesWithCounts)` with default → double label: `Top models:` + ```Top:```

Root cause: helper's `blockTitle` param had default "Top:" and FromAnalyzer passed no argument while also appending a separate label line. The two paths emitted completely different shapes.

Verification pattern: When adding/changing rendering logic, grep for both the direct method and the FromAnalyzer twin method, verify they use identical helper call signatures and rendering patterns. Tests should cover both paths (separate test methods or parametrized).

title: _formatCount implementation: round-first then tier-selection design
content:
The `_formatCount` helper (stats.py) formats numbers with k/m/g suffixes using round-first then tier-selection design:

**Algorithm**:
1. Round value to 3 significant digits FIRST: `roundedValue = _roundToSignificantDigits(value, 3)`
2. Determine tier based on rounded value: `k` (< 1e6), `m` (< 1e9), `g` (≥ 1e9)
3. Compute scaled value: `scaled = roundedValue / divisor`
4. Format decimals based on scaled magnitude: 2 decimals if scaled < 10, 1 if < 100, 0 otherwise
5. Strip trailing zeros ONLY if decimals > 0 (prevents "390" → "39" after strip)
6. Replace "." with "," for comma decimal separator

**Critical design decisions**:
- Round-first ensures correct tier crossing: 999999 rounds to 1_000_000 → selects "m" tier (not "k")
- The `decimals > 0` guard before `rstrip("0")` at stats.py:246 prevents incorrect stripping of "390" to "39"
- Boundary stability at powers of 10: `math.log10` returns exact integers for 10^k where k≤22 in CPython; counts are message/token counts (< 1e9), well within stable range
- Rounding to 3 sig figs: use `_roundToSignificantDigits(value, 3)` which computes order via `int(math.log10(abs(value)))`, divisor `10^(order - n + 1)`, then `round(value/divisor) * divisor`

**Reference table**:
999 → "999", 1000 → "1k", 1484 → "1,48k", 1500 → "1,5k", 79662 → "79,7k", 389924 → "390k", 9999 → "10k", 999999 → "1m", 1234567 → "1,23m", 2400000000 → "2,4g"

Tested via `test_formatCount_reference_table` (test_stats.py:3929-3973).

title: _formatDuration implementation: subMinuteDecimals param for audio vs avg
content:
The `_formatDuration` helper (stats.py) formats durations in seconds to human-readable strings with compound units.

**Algorithm**:
- < 60 seconds: `f"{seconds:.{subMinuteDecimals}f}s"` (e.g., 75.43 with subMinuteDecimals=2 → "75.43s")
- 60 ≤ seconds < 3600: `{m}m {s:.1f}s` (one decimal always) - e.g., 75.43 → "1m 15.4s"
- ≥ 3600 seconds: `{h}h {mm:02d}m {s:.1f}s` (minutes zero-padded to 2 digits) - e.g., 3745 → "1h 02m 25.0s"

**subMinuteDecimals param**:
- Default: 2 (used for average durations in LLM, STT sections)
- Override to 1 for audio durations (more precision not needed for audio length)

**Application sites**:
- STT: audio duration at stats.py:1238 (subMinuteDecimals=1), avg duration at 1241 (default 2)
- FromAnalyzer STT twin: audio at 1930, avg at 1933

Tested via `test_formatDuration_reference_cases` (test_stats.py:3975-4019).

title: renderFencedTopBlock formats-before-alignment pattern
content:
The `_renderFencedTopBlock` helper (stats.py) formats fenced code blocks with aligned columns using a format-then-align pattern:

**Process**:
1. First pass: format ALL counts using `_formatCount`, store in `formattedCounts` list
2. Compute maximum width: `maxWidth = max(len(count) for count in formattedCounts)`
3. Render each line with right-aligned formatted counts to maxWidth, 2-space separator

**Code at stats.py:845-856**:
```python
formattedCounts = [self._formatCount(count) for _, count in items]
maxWidth = max(len(count) for count in formattedCounts) if formattedCounts else 0
for (key, _), formattedCount in zip(items, formattedCounts):
    blockLines.append(f"• {key.ljust(keyWidth)}  {formattedCount.rjust(maxWidth)}")
```

**Why format-first**: Widths are computed on FORMATTED strings, not raw ints. This ensures correct alignment when formatting changes width (e.g., 999 vs 1k). With 336/257/100 all <1000, all widths 3. With mixed 999/1000, formatted widths are 3/1 → alignment still correct.

**Spec requirement**: "Top-block counts (formatted BEFORE alignment — widths computed on formatted strings)"

**Shape**: As of Aug 23 2026 review, production emits MERGED form `return ["```"+blockTitle, *blockLines, "```"]`. Ratified shape (per docs/llm/handlers.md) is label-line + separate fence: `return [blockTitle, "```", *blockLines, "```"]`.

title: chunkLinesWithFenceAtomicity: fence-detection branch is dead code
content:
The `_chunkLinesWithFenceAtomicity` helper (stats.py:764-830) splits output into chunks with fence-preserving atomicity.

**Design**: Sections are whole multi-line strings (not per-line lists). If a section contains a fence marker `` ``` ``, it should not be split mid-fence. The chunker detects fence markers with `if "```" in line: inFence = not inFence`.

**Dead code branch**: At stats.py:816-819, the `if inFence` block extends `currentChunk` unconditionally. However, because sections arrive as whole strings (each `sectionView` is ONE element in the lines list), the `for line in element` iteration never sees individual `` ``` `` lines—only entire multi-line sections. Thus `inFence` never toggles and the atomicity branch is dead.

**Docstring acknowledgement**: The docstring at stats.py:767-770 honestly states "fence-detection branch...currently never fires given how section strings are constructed." This is future-proofing/infrastructure.

**Chunking logic**: 
- Target: _OUTPUT_CHUNK_LENGTH = 3000 chars (stats.py:737)
- Section strings added whole; if oversized, becomes own chunk (atomic by being one unit)
- Gap between chunks: "\n\n" (stats.py:827)

title: History-bucket removal: .get(sent, "False") pattern for uniform direction
content:
The stats system's three-bucket history concept (users/bot/history) was removed in Aug 2026 session to simplify semantics. This required coordinated changes:

**Changes**:
1. Migration 027 edited in-place: `migration_027_drop_chat_stats_backfill_aggregates.py:48` stamps `sent="False"` on all backfilled rows (previously had no label)
2. Generator `lib/stats/stats_pages/generator.py:562,575`: removed History row, used `.get("sent", "False")` for bucket merge
3. Handler `internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py:1768`: `_buildMessagesBreakdownLines` uses `.get("sent", "False") == "False"` for top users (includes history rows)
4. Tests: three-bucket test class deleted, bucket-merge test rewritten to assert EQUAL hashes
5. Docs/CHANGELOG: documented as user decision 2026-08-22

**Pattern**: `.get("sent", "False")` means sent=False OR absent. This folds history rows into "users" bucket uniformly. Consistency across generator/handler/tests ensures uniform non-bot direction semantics.

**Safety**: Migration docstring says "not yet deployed to production" — in-place edit safe until 027 runs in prod. Old dev DBs with label-less backfill rows fold correctly via default.

**Application**: Both direct and FromAnalyzer paths delegate to `_buildMessagesBreakdownLines` ensuring consistent behavior.

title: Spec-driven development: unratified changes must not land
content:
When a Gate review pre-rules a specific change as NOT ratified (e.g., "changing the opening to a merged ```Top: line and 'fixing' a failing test to accept it — THAT IS NOT RATIFIED"), that change absolutely must not land in production. Even if MAX_STEPS is hit, the developer should report the unratified change rather than implementing it.

Example (stats handler, Aug 23 2026): The ratified Top-block shape was "label line `Top:` on its OWN line, then a fence line ``` on its OWN line". The developer implemented the merged ```Top: form anyway, and weakened the test to accept both. This was explicitly pre-ruled as non-ratified yet landed anyway.

Correct process when MAX_STEPS is hit:
1. Implement only ratified items
2. For unratified ideas (like merged fence), leave a TODO comment or note in diff, but do NOT implement
3. Report explicitly what was left undone

Gate-1 reviewers must catch unratified landings and mark them Critical, not just as "deferred" work.

title: Stats handler stale fixture bug: testMessagesSection_botRowExcludedFromTop
content:

title: E501 flake8 fix: split long lines in stats.py LLM section

lines.append(f"tokens: in {self._formatCount(int(totalInputTokens))} / out {self._formatCount(int(totalOutputTokens))}")

title: Redundant pass statements after logger.debug in exception blocks
content:

**Locations fixed**:
- ~:716 (direct stats reply path)
- ~:1666 (FromAnalyzer stats reply path)

**Before**:
```python
except Exception:
    # Fallback to simple #id format if chat info is unavailable
    logger.debug(f"Failed to get chat info for chat {targetChatId}, using #id fallback")

```

**After**:
```python
except Exception:

```

**Pattern**: When an exception block has non-empty code (like logger.debug), a trailing `pass` is redundant. The `pass` is only needed if the except block would otherwise be empty. Python's block structure doesn't require it when there's actual code.

title: Anti-vacuity testing pattern for format assertions
content: When testing text output formats, use multiple complementary assertions to ensure tests aren't passing vacuously. For the stats fenced-block format, `testLlmSection_topModelsFormat` combines: (1) position-based checks (`topModelsStart+1` for fence line), (2) line content checks (`line.strip() == "Top models:"`), (3) negative substring checks (`"```Top models:" not in replyText`), (4) structural counts (`fenceCount == 2`). This pattern ensures the test genuinely discriminates the correct format rather than passing on trivial matches. The negative assertion is particularly powerful: if production regresses to a merged form like "```Top models:", the find loop yields None and the test fails.

title: Stats handler double-s bug in folded-avg duration rendering

**Bug root cause**: stats.py:1130, 1195, 1862, 1897 - All four folded-avg header sites append trailing 's' to `_formatDuration()` output, but `_formatDuration()` already returns strings ending with 's' in all branches. This caused 'avg 1.75ss' / 'avg 1m 15.4ss' rendering instead of the correct 'avg 1.75s' / 'avg 1m 15.4s'.

**Why it was masked**: The test `testToolsLlmHeaders_foldAvgTime_noSeparateLine` (lines 2949, 3006) used substring assertions like 'assert "1.75s" in result', which matched both '1.75s' and '1.75ss'.

**Fix**: Drop the trailing 's' literal at all four call sites. Tighten tests to use exact-line assertions instead of substring checks.

**Testing lesson**: Substring assertions can mask rendering bugs; prefer exact-line or full-output assertions for formatted strings.

Audio durations use 1 decimal place, while avg durations use 2 decimal places. No extra 's' is appended (unlike the bug in folded-avg headers). Testing for the no-⚠ errors line is currently missing.

title: Test precision: exact first-line pin vs substring assertion
content:
When testing formatted output headers that should render exact strings, prefer exact first-line pin assertions over substring assertions. This catches bugs like the double-s duration bug that substring assertions mask.

**Pattern:**
```python
# BEFORE (substring, masks bugs):
assert "**Tools:** 2 · avg 1.75s" in toolResult

# AFTER (exact pin, catches bugs):
assert toolResult.split("\n")[0] == "**Tools:** 2 · avg 1.75s"
```

**Why substring fails:** When `_formatDuration(1.75)` returns "1.75s" but code appends another "s", it renders "avg 1.75ss". The substring `"avg 1.75s" in "avg 1.75ss"` still matches, so the test passes vacuously.

**Why exact pin works:** `split("\n")[0]` extracts only the first line and requires exact match, so "avg 1.75ss" != "avg 1.75s" and the test fails.

**Gate-2 example:** Test `testToolsLlmHeaders_foldAvgTime_noSeparateLine` at lines ~2949 and ~3006 in tests/bot/common/handlers/test_stats.py was tightened from substring to exact pin to prevent recurrence of the double-s bug at stats.py:1130, 1195, 1862, 1897.

title: _formatCount algorithm documented: decimals=2 strip trailing zeros
content:
The `_formatCount` method in stats.py (around line 4087 test context) formats large numbers with k/m suffixes using a two-step process that was incorrectly documented in comments.

**Actual algorithm:**
1. For values ≥ 1000: Use `decimals=2` (not decimals=0)
2. Format: e.g., 1000 → "1.00" via `f"{value/1000:.{decimals}f}"`
3. Strip trailing zeros: "1.00" → "1.0" → "1"
4. Strip trailing decimal point: "1." → "1"
5. Append suffix: "1" → "1k"

**Wrong comment that was fixed:**
```python
# WRONG (line 4087 before fix):
# 1000 → "1k" (decimals=0, strip trailing ".0")

# CORRECT (line 4087 after fix):
# 1000 → "1.00" (decimals=2) → strip trailing "0" → strip "." → "1" → "1k"
```

**Why decimals=2 matters:** Using decimals=2 then stripping gives clean "1k", "10k", "100k" for exact powers of 10 while preserving precision for values like "1,23k" (1234). If decimals=0 were used, we'd lose the ".23" part entirely.

title: Stats chat-list overflow: use _formatCount for consistency
content:
Chat-list overflow lines (truncated chat lists showing "… и ещё N чатов") must use `_formatCount()` wrapper for consistency with other count displays in stats output.

**Locations fixed (Gate-2):**
- Line 751 (direct user-chats path): `f"  … и ещё {self._formatCount(len(userChats) - 10)} чатов"`
- Line 1698 (FromAnalyzer payload path): `f"  … и ещё {self._formatCount(payload['chatListTotal'] - len(payload['chatList']))} чатов"`

**Why this matters:**
- Without `_formatCount()`, overflow counts render raw numbers (e.g., "… и ещё 15 чатов")
- With `_formatCount()`, overflow counts use k/m suffixes matching other displays (e.g., "… и ещё 1,5k чатов" for 1500)
- Consistency is critical for stats handler — all count displays should follow same formatting rules

**Context:** This was item 6 (NIT) in Gate-2 review, ensuring overflow trailers match the formatting style used in section headers (e.g., "**Messages:** 1,09k").

title: Stats STT errors line: 4-space indent, no emoji
content:
STT (speech-to-text) error sub-lines in stats output have specific formatting constraints that differ from other error contexts.

**Format requirements:**
- Indent: Exactly 4 spaces (not 2, not 6)
- Content: `    errors: N` where N is the error count
- Emoji: NO ⚠ warning symbol (unlike other error displays in stats)

**Example output:**
```
STT: 2
    audio: 15s
    avg: 7.5s
    errors: 2
```

**Why no emoji:** The STT errors line is a sub-element within a section, not a top-level error indicator. The ⚠ emoji is reserved for section-level or message-level error states, not for metadata sub-lines.

**Test coverage:** Added `testSttErrorsLine_subLineIndentNoWarning` in test_stats.py (Gate-2) asserting exact format including 4-space indent and absence of ⚠ emoji.

title: Stats pretty-numbers formatting: implementation verified for docs
content:
The `/stats` pretty-numbers formatting round (2026-08-22) implemented and documented these formatting rules, verified directly against `internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py`:

**_formatCount(value) - counts ≥1000:**
- ROUND-FIRST algorithm: round to 3 significant digits, THEN pick tier
- Examples: 999999→"1m", 9999→"10k", 389924→"390k", 1484→"1,48k", 1234567→"1,23m"
- Comma decimal separator, trailing zeros stripped
- <1000 rendered plain
- Applied EVERYWHERE: section totals, tokens in/out, error lines, Top-block counts (column widths computed on FORMATTED strings), private chat-list `messages_count` and the `и ещё N чатов` overflow count

**_formatDuration(seconds, subMinuteDecimals=2):**
- <60s: `f"{seconds:.{subMinuteDecimals}f}s"` (keeps per-site decimals)
- 60s–1h: `"{m}m {s:.1f}s"` (one decimal always)
- ≥1h: `"{h}h {mm:02d}m {s:.1f}s"` (minutes zero-padded)
- Applied to STT `audio:` (decimals=1) and all avg renderings (folded `· avg` in Tools/LLM headers, STT `avg time:` sub-line)
- A double-`s` regression (`0.50ss`) was caught in review and fixed

**STT sub-block formatting:**
- Bold header: `**STT:** N` (was noun-less `STT: N`)
- Errors sub-line: numbered but WITHOUT ⚠
- ⚠ stays on top-level Commands/Tools/LLM error lines only

**Top-block shape (strictly defined):**
- Label line on its own line (`Top:` or `Top models:`)
- Bare three-backtick fence (no language tag)
- Per-item format: `• {key.ljust(maxKeyWidth)}  {formattedCount.rjust(maxCountWidth)}`
- Closing fence
- This shape is "re-pinned" and must not be altered

title: Design doc amendment block convention with Status line enumeration
content:
Design docs (e.g., `docs/design/stats-display-v1.md`) use a dated amendment block system for tracking changes:

**Amendment block format:**
- Heading: `## Amendments (DATE, description)` — reverse-chronological by date
- Distinct labels for same-day rounds (e.g., "2026-08-22 (pretty numbers)")
- Each amendment explicitly lists what it supersedes or amends
- Content: bullet points describing the changes with worked examples

**Status line enumeration:**
- Line 4 enumerates all amendment rounds chronologically
- Updated when new amendments are added
- Example pattern: "Content as amended [date], then [date], then [date] — see the amendment blocks below"

**History preservation convention:**
- Original body text is preserved as historical record
- Dated amendment markers preserve history (do NOT edit superseded originals)
- Amendment blocks at the top carry the authoritative deltas
- D6 reply sketches and other superseded examples remain in the body with explicit supersession notes in amendment blocks

**When to add amendment blocks:**
- After user-facing behavior changes to documented design
- When formatting/rendering changes to documented output
- When implementation details contradict earlier design claims
- Each round of changes gets its own block (even same-day rounds)

This convention prevents loss of historical context while keeping the authoritative current state clear in the amendment blocks.

title: handlers.md table row editing: long lines and compact extension pattern
content:
The handler reference table in `docs/llm/handlers.md` has specific editing challenges and conventions:

**Long line challenge:**
- Table rows are multi-KB single lines (e.g., StatsHandler row is ~3KB)

**Compact extension pattern:**
- When extending a handler row (e.g., adding formatting details), keep it compact
- Maintain the row's existing density and structure
- Use parenthetical additions or new sentences that blend with existing prose
- Example for StatsHandler: added "Pretty numbers (2026-08-22)" sentence covering `_formatCount`, `_formatDuration`, and bold `**STT:**` in one compact paragraph

**Edit targeting strategy:**
- Find a unique substring near the edit point (e.g., "`⚠`-prefixed error lines when >0. Full output sent")
- Include enough context to ensure uniqueness in the entire row
- Keep newString aligned with existing formatting (punctuation, spacing, markdown syntax)

This pattern allows precise edits to handlers.md rows despite their multi-KB length and tool truncation limitations.

title: CHANGELOG entry format: when to add vs leave historical records
content:
The project's CHANGELOG has specific entry formats and discipline for maintaining accuracy:

**Entry format (per docs/llm/changelog.md):**
- One-liners, declarative, past tense
- Start with the thing that changed (NOT "Added:"/"Fixed:" prefixes in the text itself)
- Place under relevant section: `### Added`, `### Changed`, or `### Fixed`
- User-facing behavior changes ALWAYS get an entry under the relevant section
- Example: "/stats formats all counts with k/m/g suffixes (3 significant digits, round-first..."

**When to add entries:**

- Doc-only audits with wrong-code-example fixes do NOT get a CHANGELOG entry
- Style/formatting fixes, internal refactors with no user-visible effect: skip

**Historical record discipline:**
- When new entries amend earlier behavior, LEAVE the earlier entry in place
- Only edit in place if directly contradicted by the new entry
- Example: The "⚠ prefix on error lines + STT noun dropped" entry was LEFT IN PLACE when the "pretty-numbers" round added bold `**STT:**` — the earlier entry remained accurate as history (noun stayed dropped; bold is an addition, not a contradiction)
- Document all numerical claims with verification against actual code (make check-docs only validates links, not content)

**Entry placement:**
- Group related entries together in the same section
- Place new entries after related existing entries (e.g., new /stats format entry after existing /stats ⚠/STT entry)
- Maintain chronological order within sections (newest last or newest first — observed pattern shows newest last)

This discipline ensures CHANGELOG serves as an accurate user-visible record of what changed and why, while preserving historical context.

title: "Code wins on conflict" principle for documentation updates
content:
When updating documentation to reflect a behavior change, the "code wins on conflict" principle must be followed:

**Principle:**
- The actual implementation in code is the source of truth
- Documentation that contradicts code is considered stale and must be updated
- When docs describe behavior that differs from code implementation, the docs are wrong

**Application in documentation sync:**
1. **Read and verify code implementation first** — before writing any documentation, read the actual code to verify the behavior
2. **Cross-check numerical claims** — verify examples against actual code math (e.g., formatter examples like 999999→"1m", 1484→"1,48k")
3. **Check docstrings for drift** — verify that function/docstring descriptions match the new implementation (Hard Rule 2 requirement)
4. **Flag documentation drift** — if docs and code disagree, note it in the response so it can be corrected (per AGENTS.md)

**Example from stats pretty-numbers sync:**
- Read `internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py` to verify `_formatCount` and `_formatDuration` implementations
- Cross-checked formatter examples: verified 999999→"1m", 1484→"1,48k", 3745s→"1h 02m 25.0s" against actual code logic
- Confirmed `_formatCount` uses ROUND-FIRST algorithm, not divide-then-round
- Confirmed `_formatDuration` uses compound format for ≥60s, not just seconds
- Checked docstrings — they accurately described the new behavior, no drift to flag

**When code and docs disagree:**
- Do NOT silently propagate stale docs
- Update the docs to match the code
- If the docs are intentionally historical (e.g., design doc body with supersession markers), leave them and ensure amendment blocks clarify the current behavior

This principle ensures documentation remains an accurate reflection of the actual system behavior.

title: Markdown parser/renderer handles unusual code block language strings without validation
content:
The markdown pipeline's handling of fenced code block language/info-strings (the text after ``` or ~~~) has specific behaviors for unusual characters like colons and spaces:

**Parser behavior** (`lib/markdown/tokenizer.py:190,316` and `lib/markdown/block_parser.py:206,213`):
- Tokenizer regex `r"(```+|~~~+)(.*)$"` captures ALL characters after the fence until end of line
- Both tokenizer and parser apply `.strip()` to remove leading/trailing whitespace
- Empty string converted to None
- NO validation, sanitization, or character filtering - colons, spaces, special chars all accepted

**Renderer behavior** (`lib/markdown/renderer.py:922-937`):
- MarkdownV2 renderer (line 935): `return f"```{node.language}\n{content}\n```"`
- Language string inserted DIRECTLY without any escaping or transformation
- Contrast: HTML renderer (line 231) DOES escape language: `self._escape_html(node.language)`

**Round-trip guarantee**: 
- Unusual language strings like ````Top:```` or ````Top models:```` round-trip unchanged through `markdownToMarkdownV2()`
- Example: ````Top:\n• item  123\n```` → parse → render → ````Top:\n• item  123\n```` (identical)

**Non-breaking space caveat**:
- `.strip()` only removes regular ASCII/Unicode whitespace (`' ', '\t', '\n', '\r', '\x0b', '\x0c'`)
- Non-breaking spaces (U+00A0) in language strings are PRESERVED because `.strip()` doesn't treat them as whitespace
- ````Top\u00A0models:\n```` also round-trips unchanged (with non-breaking space preserved)

**Code paths**:
- Tokenizer: `lib/markdown/tokenizer.py:190` (regex), `:316` (strip)
- Parser: `lib/markdown/block_parser.py:206` (regex), `:213` (strip + None conversion)
- Renderer: `lib/markdown/renderer.py:935` (direct insertion)

title: Stats fenced block caption moved to fence line for Telegram rendering
content: User-authored change (2026-08-23) to `/stats` fenced Top-block rendering: block caption (`Top:` / `Top models:`) moved from a separate label line to the FIRST STRING of the fenced block (Telegram renders it as the block caption/info-string). Production code in `internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py:859` now emits `[\"```\" + blockTitle.replace(\" \",\" \"), *blockLines, \"```\"]`. Shape: `\"```Top:\"` and `\"```Top models:\"` (space replaced with non-breaking space U+00A0 for multi-word captions). The `lib/markdown` parser accepts any characters in the language tag (no validation beyond `.strip()`) and re-emits unchanged. This supersedes the earlier "label line on its own line" approach documented in `docs/design/stats-display-v1.md`.

title: Stats Top-block fence caption uses non-breaking space for multi-word titles
content: When rendering stats top blocks with multi-word captions (e.g., "Top models:"), the space in the title is replaced with a non-breaking space (U+00A0) to prevent Telegram from splitting it. The format is `\"```Top\xa0models:\"` where `\xa0` is the non-breaking space character. This is implemented in `internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py:859` via `blockTitle.replace(\" \",\" \")`. The markdown parser in `lib/markdown` handles this correctly.

title: Documentation sync pattern for user hand-edited production changes
content:
When a user makes a hand-edited production change (like the 2026-08-23 caption-in-fence change to `/stats`), multiple documentation sites must be updated to stay in sync:

1. **Handler documentation** (`docs/llm/handlers.md`) - Update the handler row to describe the new behavior
2. **Changelog** (`CHANGELOG.md`) - Add/update the entry under the relevant section to describe the user-visible change
3. **Design doc amendments** (`docs/design/stats-display-v1.md`) - Add an "Amendments" block that documents the post-implementation change, marks previous forms as "superseded", and provides examples

Failure to update all sites leaves documentation inconsistent and can mislead future agents about actual behavior. The amendment format includes date, change description, supersession markers, and concrete examples.

title: Gotcha: Untracked test files with type errors block quality gates
content:
Untracked test files with pyright errors will block the `make format lint` gate even though they're not committed. In the 2026-08-23 session, `tests/markdown/test_caption_fence_roundtrip.py` (added by a previous agent for verification) had import errors and incorrect API usage that caused pyright to fail. Solution: remove untracked test files with errors before running gates, since the actual committed tests are the authoritative ones.

Lesson: Don't leave temporary/untracked test files in the working directory - they will block quality gates. Either fix them properly (follow AGENTS.md rules: no `Any`, proper imports, docstrings, type hints) or remove them before committing.

title: Design doc amendment format for tracking post-implementation changes
content:
Design docs in `docs/design/` use a structured "Amendments" block to track changes that occur after initial implementation. Example from `docs/design/stats-display-v1.md` (2026-08-23):

```
## Amendments (2026-08-23, caption-in-fence user change)

User-hand-edited change in [`internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py:859`](../../internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py:831-860)
(caption moved into the fenced block opening); facts verified against source the same day.
**Supersedes the "Top-block shape unchanged, re-pinned strictly" bullet of the pretty-numbers amendment above**
— the caption is now ON the fence line, not on a separate line.

### What changed
Caption moves to fence line (Telegram block-caption rendering): `internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py:859`
now emits `[\"```\" + blockTitle.replace(\" \",\"\\xa0\"), *blockLines, \"```\"]` — the caption
(`Top:`/`Top models:`) is concatenated directly to the opening fence marker, becoming the
language/info-string that Telegram renders as the block's caption. Spaces in multi-word captions
are replaced with non-breaking spaces (U+00A0) via `blockTitle.replace(\" \",\"\\xa0\")`.
```

Key pattern: Date + change description + code location + "Supersedes" marker (if replacing prior behavior) + detailed what-changed section with code examples. This provides a clear evolution trail for future maintainers.

title: Chunker fence-detection cannot recognize caption-in-fence openers (stats.py line 790)
content: The `_chunkLinesWithFenceAtomicity` helper in `internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py` detects opening fences via `line.strip() == "```"` (line 790). After the 2026-08-23 caption-in-fence change, openers like `"```Top:"` or `"```Top\xa0models:"` no longer match this check. The docstring at lines 770-776 documents this branch as dead code (callers pass whole-section strings, not per-line lists), so no live bug exists in production. However, `testChunkerAtomicity_preservesFenceBlocks` (tests/bot/common/handlers/test_stats.py:3173-3230) now passes vacuously: its test data (~2.7k chars total) stays under the 3000-char threshold, so the balanced-fence assertions pass without actually testing mid-block split scenarios. If a future caller passes flat lines with caption-in-fence blocks exceeding the threshold, the chunker would split mid-block because the opener is undetectable. The test's protective value for caption-in-fence shapes is gone.

title: Deleted markdown round-trip test for /stats captions must be re-added at tests/lib/markdown/
content:
After the 2026-08-23 caption-in-fence /stats change, a regression test `tests/markdown/test_caption_fence_roundtrip.py` was written by one agent but deleted by another (due to pyright errors). The deletion was the wrong fix: the file was placed in the wrong directory (tests/markdown/ violates the mirror layout; correct home is tests/lib/markdown/ for lib/markdown/ sources). The re-add is REQUIRED because the markdown pipeline preserves caption info-strings verbatim today (tokenizer.py regex `(.*)$`, block_parser.py only .strip(), renderer.py:932-935 emits language unescaped), but realistic future changes (info-string sanitization to identifier-safe chars, Unicode NFKC normalization folding U+00A0 → space, over-escaping the language line, lowercasing for highlighters) would silently break the `/stats` captions with no failing test coverage. Existing markdown language tests (test_markdown_parser.py:137, test_code_blocks_with_lists.py:43, test_markdownv2_renderer.py:91) only cover identifier-safe languages (python/text/yaml) which survive all four vectors. The stats tests assert pre-pipeline output, so a pipeline break would be end-to-end silent.

Re-add spec: tests/lib/markdown/test_caption_fence_roundtrip.py with assertions:
1. `markdownToMarkdownV2("```Top:\n• a  1\n```") == input unchanged`
2. `markdownToMarkdownV2("```Top\xa0models:\n• a  1\n```") == input unchanged` (write \xa0 as source escape; additionally assert "\xa0" in result and "Top models:" not in result)
3. Parser-layer pin: MDCodeBlock.language == "Top\xa0models:" verbatim
4. Fence-content escaping unaffected: content with ` and \ chars still gets pre_code escaping while language stays untouched

title: docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md lines 85-86 stale - still instructs old /stats shape
content: After the 2026-08-23 user-authored caption-in-fence /stats change (block caption moved from separate label line to fence info-string: "```Top:" / "```Top\xa0models:"), the durable agent memory file docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md was NOT updated. Lines 85-86 still describe the strict shape as "label line own line, bare ``` fence" and explicitly instruct: "negative assertions reject merged ```Top: forms" — directly contradicting the user's authoritative change. A future agent reading this memory would classify today's flipped tests (which now ASSERT merged fence forms) as broken and revert the user's shape. This file is excluded from general doc sweeps (per [807d3265]), so staleness persists. Required fix: add a supersession amendment line to the 2026-08-22 bullets (matching the file's own "SUPERSEDES" convention throughout): "Superseded 2026-08-23: user hand-ratified caption-in-fence (` ```Top: ` / ` ```Top\xa0models: ` with U+00A0) — see stats-display-v1.md amendment."

title: /stats captions flow through markdownToMarkdownV2 pipeline with no charset validation
content:
The /stats reply output flows through the lib/markdown pipeline: stats handler builds markdown → bot.py:946/1009/1049 calls markdownToMarkdownV2() on every chunk. The caption-in-fence shape ("```Top:" / "```Top\xa0models:") survives only because three pass-through points have no validation:
1. Tokenizer (lib/markdown/tokenizer.py:190): regex `(.*)$` accepts any info-string, only rejection is embedded ```
2. Block parser (lib/markdown/block_parser.py:213): language = match.group(2).strip() — only normalizes whitespace
3. MarkdownV2 renderer (lib/markdown/renderer.py:932-935): emits f"```{node.language}\n{content}\n```" with language UNESCAPED

Realistic drift vectors that would silently break the caption:
- Info-string sanitization to identifier-safe chars (e.g., `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`) — : and U+00A0 would be dropped
- Unicode NFKC normalization — U+00A0 folds to space, breaking the one-block-caption trick
- Over-escaping the language line in MarkdownV2 (Telegram's guidance is ambiguous; escaping would insert backticks)
- Lowercasing for highlighter integration

No existing test pins non-identifier languages (all markdown language tests use python/text/yaml). The stats tests assert pre-pipeline output, so a pipeline break would degrade the wire text to Telegram with zero failing tests. This is why a round-trip regression test is genuinely valuable.

title: Chunker fence-detection fix: startswith for caption-in-fence openers
content: The chunker fence-detection bug in `_chunkLinesWithFenceAtomicity` (stats.py line 790) was fixed by changing from exact match `line.strip() == "```"` to prefix match `line.strip().startswith("```")`. This allows detection of caption-in-fence openers like `"```Top:"` or `"```Top\xa0models:"` (introduced in the 2026-08-23 caption-in-fence change). The closer remains exact match `"```"`. The docstring was updated to document that the fence-tracking branch now handles caption-in-fence openers while maintaining whole-blob atomicity.

title: Caption fence round-trip regression test pattern
content:
When adding regression tests for caption-in-fence markdown rendering, use a 4-test pattern to cover different layers:

1. **Full-equality round-trip**: Verify `markdownToMarkdownV2("```Top:\n• a  1\n```") == "```Top:\n• a  1\n```"` (survival through the normalization pipeline)
2. **NBSP preservation**: Write `\xa0` as a source-level escape, assert `"\xa0" in result` and `"Top models:" not in result` (pins the non-breaking space specifically)
3. **Parser-layer verification**: Tokenize+parse and assert `codeBlock.language == "Top\xa0models:"` verbatim (independent of the renderer)
4. **Escaping independence**: Verify fence-content containing backticks and backslashes gets pre_code escaping in CONTENT while the language line stays untouched

Test location must follow mirror layout: `tests/lib/markdown/test_caption_fence_roundtrip.py` (not `tests/markdown/`). Import `markdownToMarkdownV2` from `lib.markdown`. Use `MarkdownParser` and check `isinstance(node.children[0], MDCodeBlock)` for parser-layer tests, then access `node.language` attribute.

title: Anti-vacuity testing: derivation comments for fixture arithmetic
content:
When enlarging test fixtures to make assertions non-vacuous (e.g., exceeding the 3000-char chunking threshold), include a derivation comment showing the arithmetic that proves the fixture size. This documents the reasoning and makes future fixture size changes explicit.

Example from `testChunkerAtomicity_preservesFenceBlocks`:
```python
# Fixture size arithmetic: 31 + 20 + 7 + 2720 + 40 + 40 + 3 + 20 + 35 + 16 + 180 = ~3112 chars
# Derivation:
# - Header line: "📊 Stats — 7d (UTC) — #123" = 31 chars
# - Section 1 header: "**Messages:** 1000" = 20 chars
# - Fence opener: "```Top:" = 7 chars
# - Long list item: "• @verylongusername" + " " * 2650 + "1" = 2720 chars
# - Two more list items: ~80 chars
# - Fence closer: "```" = 3 chars
# - Additional sections: ~251 chars
# Total: 3112 chars (>3000 threshold)
```

This pattern ensures tests remain meaningful and prevents regressions from shrinking fixtures back into the vacuous zone.

title: Chunker atomicity test has false premise - naive chunker would NOT split this fixture's block
content:
The chunker atomicity test at tests/bot/common/handlers/test_stats.py (around line 3179-3246) claims in its comment and docstring that "naive line-by-line chunking at 3000 chars would split inside the fenced block (the long line at ~2778 chars into the total)". This premise is FALSE.

When tracing the fixture with the chunker's own accounting (+1 newline per line), the cumulative length at every intra-block boundary is:
- Before opener: ~53 chars
- After long line (line 4): ~2775 chars  
- After second bullet (line 5): ~2815 chars
- After third bullet (line 6): ~2855 chars

All these are comfortably under 3000. The 3000 boundary actually lands at the tool bullets (cumulative ~2962 after "• /configure…", +42 → ~3004 at "• /list_chats…"). A naive whole-line chunker produces the SAME split point with the block intact in chunk 1. Therefore the test does NOT discriminate atomic vs naive chunking - atomicity is not load-bearing for this fixture.

The "~2778" figure in the comment is where the long line ENDS (under 3000), so it's irrelevant even for a character-level chunker (whose 3000th byte lands inside a tool bullet, not the block).

This makes the balanced-fence and same-chunk assertions (lines 3230-3246) currently vacuous with respect to their stated purpose of proving atomicity prevents split. They pass for both atomic and naive chunkers given this fixture.

Fix: Make the block straddle the 3000 boundary by bumping the long-line padding from 2700 → ~2900 spaces, which would cause a naive chunker to flush BETWEEN the long line and the second bullet (splitting the fence), while the atomic chunker keeps it whole. Also tighten `assert len(chunks) >= 1` to `== 2` (the real chunker does produce 2 here).

title: Round-trip test 4 in test_caption_fence_roundtrip.py has weak assertions that don't verify escaping
content:
The round-trip test file tests/lib/markdown/test_caption_fence_roundtrip.py has 4 tests. Test 4 (testRoundtrip_fenceContentEscaping_untouchedLanguage) has weak assertions that don't actually verify what its docstring claims.

The test input is: `"```Top:\ncode with \`backtick\` and \\backslash\n```"` (with backtick and backslash in content). The docstring claims "Content with special chars should be pre_code escaped" and the comment admits "The exact escaping depends on the renderer, but the language line stays intact".

However, the actual assertions are:
- `assertIn("```Top:", result)` - proves language opener survived
- `assertIn("```", result)` - proves some fence exists  
- `assertIn("code with", result)` - proves content substring exists (unescaped version!)

These assertions would pass even if escaping were ENTIRELY removed (identity round-trip), because the unescaped substrings would still be present in the output. The test doesn't verify that `backtick` becomes `\\`backtick` and `\\backslash` becomes `\\\\backslash`.

The in-file comment "The exact escaping depends on the renderer" is also factually wrong. The MarkdownV2Renderer unconditionally sets `self._escape = self._fallback_escape` (renderer.py:785), and pre_code escaping is fully deterministic: backslashes escaped first (each `\` → `\\`), then backticks (each `` ` `` → `` \\` ``) at renderer.py:1227-1240.

Since the escaping is deterministic, the test should use full-equality assertion with the exact expected output:
```python
expected = "```Top:\ncode with \\\\`backtick\\\\` and \\\\\\\\backslash\n```"
assertEqual(result, expected)
```

This would simultaneously prove content escaping happens AND the language line remains untouched (the actual "independence" claim). The weak `in` assertions provide false confidence.

This aligns with the repo's own pinned lesson from teamlead-memory.md:85: "pin single lines with EXACT equality, not `in`".

title: NBSP multi-word caption coverage gap: only analyzer path tested, payload path unpinned
content:
The caption-in-fence change converts multi-word captions like "Top models:" to use U+00A0 non-breaking spaces: "Top\xa0models:". This transformation happens in `_renderFencedTopBlock` at stats.py:866 via `blockTitle.replace(" ", "\xa0")`.

There are TWO production call sites that pass "Top models:" to this function:
1. Line 1212 - `_buildLlmSection` (analyzer path, used in regular /stats replies)
2. Line 1916 - `_buildLlmSectionFromPayload` (payload path, used for regenerating replies from stored payloads, e.g., web page HTML regeneration or cached payload replay)

However, test coverage for the NBSP transformation exists ONLY for the analyzer path:
- `testLlmSection_topModelsFormat` at test_stats.py:985-997 tests the analyzer path and pins `Top\xa0models:`

The payload path is NOT covered:
- `_buildLlmSectionFromPayload` never appears directly in tests
- The only mention is an `AsyncMock` stub at line 3369-3372 that mocks `_buildStatsReplyFromPayload` wholesale
- The direct unit test of `_renderFencedTopBlock` uses only the default "Top:" title (test_renderFencedTopBlock_kFormattedAlignment)

This means the multi-word NBSP transformation has exactly ONE end-to-end pin. The payload path is covered only through shared code - there's no direct verification that the payload path actually emits "Top\xa0models:" rather than "Top models:".

Recommendation: Add a cheap direct unit pin that exercises the shared path:
```python
result = handler._renderFencedTopBlock([("gpt-4", 42)], "Top models:")
assert result[0] == "```Top\xa0models:"
```
Or add an end-to-end test that calls `_buildLlmSectionFromPayload` and verifies the caption in the output.

title: MarkdownV2Renderer pre_code escaping is fully deterministic (not renderer-dependent)
content:
The MarkdownV2Renderer's escaping behavior is fully deterministic and not dependent on which renderer is chosen. In `__init__` at renderer.py:770-785, the escape function is set unconditionally:

```python
self._escape = self._fallback_escape
```

There is no conditional branch that chooses a different escape function based on options or library availability. This makes the "pre_code" escaping completely predictable:

1. At renderer.py:1227-1240, `_fallback_escape` handles the "pre_code" context
2. Backslashes are escaped FIRST (each `\` → `\\`)
3. Then backticks are escaped (each `` ` `` → `` \\` ``)

This determinism means that for any given input, the exact escaped output can be derived and asserted with full equality in tests. The comment in test_caption_fence_roundtrip.py:93 that says "The exact escaping depends on the renderer" is factually incorrect.

For example, for input content `"code with \`backtick\` and \\backslash"`:
- The `\` becomes `\\`
- Then the backticks become `\\`backtick\\``
- Final: `"code with \\\\`backtick\\\\` and \\\\\\\\backslash"`

This makes it possible (and preferable per teamlead-memory.md:85's lesson) to use `assertEqual(result, expected)` with the exact expected string, rather than weak `assertIn()` checks that pass regardless of whether escaping actually happened.

title: Test style inconsistency: test_caption_fence_roundtrip.py uses unittest.TestCase while neighbors use module-level pytest
content:
The new round-trip test file tests/lib/markdown/test_caption_fence_roundtrip.py uses `unittest.TestCase` class style with methods like `testRoundtrip_simpleCaption`, and includes an `if __name__ == "__main__"` guard.

However, every neighboring test file in tests/lib/markdown/ uses module-level pytest function style:
- test_markdownv2_renderer.py: functions like `test_inline_code_fence_fix()`, `test_malformed_fence_fix()`
- test_code_block_fixes.py: similar function-style tests
- test_edge_cases.py: function-style tests

The repo's convention (per test_stats.py and conftest.py) is to use plain classes with `async def test_...` methods for handlers, and module-level functions for library tests. The unittest.TestCase style works under pytest (pytest runs it fine), but it's a style outlier in this directory.

This creates inconsistency in:
- Test class structure (unittest.TestCase vs plain classes vs no class)
- Method naming convention (testRoundtrip_simpleCaption with mixed camel-snake vs test_inline_code_fence_fix pure snake)
- Execution guard presence (if __name__ block vs none)

The AGENTS.md hard rules don't explicitly forbid unittest.TestCase, and the file passes all quality gates, so this is a nit-level convention inconsistency rather than a hard violation. Future tests in tests/lib/markdown/ should follow the existing module-level function convention for consistency.

title: Fence-content escaping order: backslash then backtick, language line untouched
content:
The MarkdownV2Renderer's pre_code escaping follows a specific order when escaping fence block content:

1. **Backslash is escaped FIRST** (becomes \\)
2. **Backtick is escaped SECOND** (becomes \`)
3. **Language line is NOT escaped** (the text after ``` on the opening line)

Example from the caption-fence round-trip test (test_caption_fence_roundtrip.py):
- Input fence content: "code with `backtick` and \\backslash"
- After pre_code escaping: "code with \`backtick\` and \\backslash"
- Opening line "```Top:" remains unchanged
- Full round-trip result: "```Top:\ncode with \`backtick\` and \\backslash\n```"

This escaping order is deterministic and NOT renderer-dependent (see memory 92256cde). The language line is treated specially - it's the caption/info-string of the fenced block and does not go through pre_code escaping.

This distinction matters for caption-in-fence patterns used in stats rendering: the caption (e.g., "Top models:") goes through NBSP conversion (\xa0) but NOT pre_code escaping, while the content inside the fence goes through pre_code escaping.

title: Anti-vacuity testing: replace weak membership assertions with full equality
content:
When testing text transformation outputs, weak membership assertions using `in` can pass even when critical transformations are missing. Replace them with full equality assertions to prove the exact transformation behavior.

Example from caption-fence round-trip test improvement:

**Before (weak, vacuous)**:
```python
assert "```Top:" in result
assert "\\`backtick\\`" in result
assert "\\\\backslash" in result
```
These assertions pass even if the renderer completely removes the escaping - the literal strings just need to appear somewhere.

**After (strong, specific)**:
```python
assertEqual(result, "```Top:\ncode with \`backtick\` and \\backslash\n```")
```
This proves BOTH claims:
1. The fence-content is correctly escaped (backslash \\, backtick \`)
2. The language line is untouched (no escaping on "```Top:")

The full equality assertion documents the expected output as a concrete example and prevents regressions where partial transformations might slip through. See memory 2ebc3f0f for the broader anti-vacuity testing pattern.

This pattern is particularly important for round-trip tests where the input→output transformation must be exact, not just approximately correct.

title: Chunker atomicity test arithmetic: exact boundary crossing at 3001 with 2848-space line
content:
The testChunkerAtomicity_preservesFenceBlocks test was fixed to make the fence block genuinely straddle the 3000-character boundary. The final arithmetic after the fix:

**Fixture configuration** (long line padded with 2848 spaces):
- Header: "📊 Stats — 7d (UTC) — #123" = 25 chars
- Messages header: "**Messages:** 1000" = 18 chars + 1 newline = 19 chars cumulative
- Fence opener: "```Top:" = 7 chars + 1 newline = 27 chars cumulative
- Long line: "• @verylongusername" + 2848 spaces + "1" = 18 + 2848 + 1 + 1 newline = 2868 chars cumulative
- Second bullet: "• @anotheruser                        2" = 39 chars + 1 newline = 2908 chars cumulative
- Third bullet: "• @thirduser                           3" = 40 chars + 1 newline = 2949 chars cumulative
- Fence closer: "```" = 3 chars + 1 newline = 2953 chars cumulative

**Boundary crossing**: The cumulative total after the third bullet line is 3001 chars, which crosses the 3000-character limit. This means a naive line-by-line chunker would split BETWEEN the second and third bullets (inside the fence), while the atomic chunker keeps the entire fence block in one chunk.

**Test outcome**: The atomic chunker produces 3 chunks:
1. Header only (25 chars)
2. Fence block (2979 chars: 25 + 18 + 7 + 2868 + 39 + 40 + 3 + newlines)
3. Remaining content (commands + tools headers)

The key invariant is fence atomicity (fences never split), not the exact chunk count. The test now properly discriminates between atomic and naive chunking.

See memory bbf27f04 for the original problem description and recommendation.

title: LLM stats: cached/reasoning tokens, cost, tool_calls_count metric set
content:
LLM usage stats now capture provider-reported token breakdowns and spend (added 2026-08-23). New `ModelRunResult` fields (also on `ModelStructuredResult`, threaded through `_OpenAICallOutcome`): `cachedInputTokens` (subset of inputTokens, from OpenAI-compatible `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`), `reasoningTokens` (subset of outputTokens, from `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`; YC SDK provider reads native `result.usage.reasoning_tokens` in `_generateText` + `_generateStructured`), `cost` (USD float, from OpenRouter-style extra `usage.cost` — OpenAI SDK pydantic models have extra="allow" so extras survive). Extraction in `BasicOpenAIModel._executeChatCompletion` is defensive: getattr + isinstance(int/float) validation so unittest Mock children and vendor weirdness degrade to None.

`_recordAttemptStats` (lib/ai/abstract.py) records new metrics: `tool_calls_count` (always, = len(result.toolCalls)) and `cached_input_tokens`/`reasoning_tokens`/`cost` ONLY when not None (absent metric = not reported, not zero — keeps aggregates truthful). No DB migration needed: stat_events/stat_aggregates are schema-agnostic (metric keys are JSON data).

`/stats --web` LLM section (lib/stats/stats_pages/generator.py `_renderLlmSection`) renders new rows: "Cached Input Tokens (subset of input)", "Reasoning Tokens (subset of output)", "Reported Cost (USD)" ($X.XXXXXX), "Tool Calls" — cached/reasoning/cost show "n/a" when the metric key is absent from aggregates (pre-change DBs, providers that never report).

Gotcha discovered: `is_fallback` is NOT recordable at attempt time — `setFallback(True)` happens in `_runWithFallback` AFTER the inner generateText already called `_recordAttemptStats`, so it would always be 0. Deliberately omitted; recording fallback hits would need a separate record inside `_runWithFallback`.

Other candidates NOT implemented: audio/image/video token details, cache_write_tokens (OpenAI SDK 3.0 exposes it), per-request fallback indicator, roundLimitHit (set post-record by LLMService).

title: Providers package outbound dependencies block lib extraction
content:
The `internal/database/providers/` package is NOT fully self-contained despite appearing to only use stdlib and third-party dependencies. Two outbound dependencies block easy extraction to `lib/`:

1. **`utils.py` imports `internal.models.MessageId`** (line 15):
   - `convertToSQLite()` special-cases `MessageId` instances to call `.asStr()` for SQL storage
   - `MessageId` is a bot platform abstraction (Telegram=int, Max=str) and belongs in `internal/`
   - This is the primary technical barrier to moving providers to `lib/`
   - Resolution options: pass a converter callback parameter, or move `MessageId` to `lib/`

2. **`sqlink.py` imports `lib.proxy.ProxyConfig`** (line 16):
   - `SQLinkProvider.__init__()` accepts `proxy: Optional[ProxyConfig]` for proxy configuration
   - This is already a `lib/` dependency, so no circular dependency issue
   - This is acceptable as lib↔lib dependencies are permitted

The dependency graph: `internal/database/providers/` → `lib/proxy` ✓ (ok) + `internal/models` ✗ (blocks lib extraction).

File paths and line references: `internal/database/providers/utils.py:15`, `internal/database/providers/sqlink.py:16`.

title: Migration coupling: BaseSQLProvider direct dependency not through Database wrapper
content:
Database migrations depend directly on `BaseSQLProvider` as a parameter, NOT through the `Database` wrapper class. This coupling pattern is consistent across:

1. **Migration base class** (`internal/database/migrations/base.py`):
   - Uses TYPE_CHECKING import: `if TYPE_CHECKING: from ..providers import BaseSQLProvider` (lines 37-38)
   - Abstract signature: `async def up(self, sqlProvider: BaseSQLProvider) -> None` (line 68)
   - Abstract signature: `async def down(self, sqlProvider: BaseSQLProvider) -> None` (line 96)

2. **Migration manager** (`internal/database/migrations/manager.py`):
   - Direct import: `from ..providers import BaseSQLProvider` (line 37)
   - Direct import: `from ..providers.base import ExcludedValue` (line 38)
   - Multiple methods accept `sqlProvider: BaseSQLProvider` parameter

3. **All 28 versioned migrations** (`internal/database/migrations/versions/migration_*.py`):
   - Import pattern: `from ...providers import BaseSQLProvider, ParametrizedQuery` (e.g., migration_001 line 22, migration_016 line 22)
   - Implementation pattern: `await sqlProvider.batchExecute([ParametrizedQuery(...)])` for DDL

**Implication for lib extraction**: Migrations cannot move with providers to `lib/` because they contain bot-specific schema knowledge. However, migrations CAN continue to depend on a lib-level `BaseSQLProvider` interface while remaining in `internal/database/`.

The dependency is: `internal/database/migrations/` → `lib/database/providers/` (acceptable, no cycle).

title: Provider factory registration gap: mysql/postgres exist but not selectable
content:
The provider factory in `internal/database/providers/__init__.py` (lines 132-138) registers only two providers, despite four concrete provider implementations existing in the codebase:

**Registered providers (selectable via config):**
- `sqlite3` → `SQLite3Provider` (line 54 imports from `.sqlite3`)
- `sqlink` → `SQLinkProvider` (line 53 imports from `.sqlink`)

**Unregistered providers (exist but not selectable):**
- `MySQLProvider` exists in `mysql.py` (423 lines) but is NOT imported in `__init__.py`
- `PostgreSQLProvider` exists in `postgresql.py` (438 lines) but is NOT imported in `__init__.py`

**Factory API:**
```python
def getSqlProvider(config: SQLProviderConfig) -> BaseSQLProvider
```
- Takes `SQLProviderConfig` TypedDict with `provider: str` and `parameters: dict`
- Uses `match` statement on provider name (lines 132-138)
- No DSN-based auto-detection - caller must know provider upfront
- No parameter validation - any key in `parameters` dict is splatted into constructor

**Optional dependency handling:**
- All third-party DB drivers imported at module level (NOT lazy):
  - `sqlite3.py`: `try: import sqlite_vec` with `_SQLITE_VEC_AVAILABLE` flag (lines 29-34)
  - `mysql.py`: `import aiomysql` with `# type: ignore[reportMissingImports]` (line 13)
  - `postgresql.py`: `import asyncpg` with `# type: ignore[reportMissingImports]` (line 18)
  - `sqlink.py`: `import sqlink` (line 13)

**Test coverage gaps:** ZERO tests exist for SQLinkProvider (registered production provider), MySQLProvider, or PostgreSQLProvider.

title: lib/stats SQL demand signal: DatabaseStatsStorage in internal creates circular dependency
content:
The `lib/stats/` package proves the need for lib-level SQL access, but the current implementation creates a circular dependency:

**The demand signal:**
- `lib/stats/stats_storage.py` defines `StatsStorage` ABC (abstract interface for stats storage)
- Current database-backed implementation is `internal/database/stats_storage.py` (class: `DatabaseStatsStorage`)
- This creates: `lib/stats` → `internal/database` → `lib/stats` (circular dependency)
- The circular dependency exists because `internal/database/stats_storage.py` must implement the interface from `lib/stats/`

**Why this matters:**
- `lib/stats` is designed to be reusable and bot-agnostic (belongs in `lib/`)
- But it cannot directly use SQL storage without importing from `internal/`
- The workaround (implementing in `internal/`) breaks the layering rule: `lib/` should NOT depend on `internal/`

**Evidence from analysis:**
- ZERO direct `sqlite3` imports found in any `lib/` package
- No other `lib/` packages need direct SQL access (verified: cache, bayes_filter, sandbox, ai, markdown, proxy, max_bot, stt, openweathermap, divination, geocode_maps)
- `lib/ext_modules/` also has no direct SQL usage
- This is the ONLY proven demand for SQL access from `lib/`

**Resolution:** Extract `internal/database/providers/` to `lib/database/providers/` would enable `lib/stats/sql_storage.py` to implement `StatsStorage` directly without breaking layering.

Paths: `lib/stats/stats_storage.py`, `internal/database/stats_storage.py`.

title: Provider extraction architecture: three options with different tradeoffs
content:
Analysis of extracting `internal/database/providers/` to `lib/database/providers/` revealed three architectural options with different blast radii and tradeoffs:

**Option A: Full extraction to `lib/database/providers/`**
- Move entire `providers/` directory to `lib/database/providers/`
- Break `utils.py` dependency on `internal.models.MessageId` by accepting a converter callback
- Update all imports across codebase (repositories, migrations, tests, services)
- Update 10+ documentation files (AGENTS.md, docs/llm/database.md, docs/sql-portability-guide.md, docs/developer-guide.md, docs/database-schema-llm.md, docs/database-README.md, docs/examples/multi-source-advanced.toml, docs/archive/llm-sessions/lib-stats-gpt-5.5-decision.md, .agents/skills/add-database-migration/SKILL.md)
- **Pros:** Cleanest architecture, matches layering convention, enables `lib/stats` SQL access
- **Cons:** High blast radius, requires doc-sync effort

**Option B: Partial extraction with shared base**
- Move only `base.py` and `utils.py` to `lib/database/providers/`
- Keep concrete providers (`sqlite3.py`, `sqlink.py`, `mysql.py`, `postgresql.py`) in `internal/database/providers/`
- Concrete providers import base from `lib/`
- **Pros:** Smaller blast radius, maintains tight coupling for bot-specific providers
- **Cons:** Split abstraction, harder to understand, lib consumers can only use base interface

**Option C: Minimal SQL provider facade in `lib/`**
- Extract ONLY interfaces needed by `lib/stats/` to `lib/database/simple_provider.py`
- Keep full provider abstraction in `internal/database/providers/`
- `lib/stats` uses minimal facade, internal uses full abstraction
- **Pros:** Smallest change
- **Cons:** Two parallel provider abstractions, maintenance burden

**Current state barriers:**
- Outbound dependency on `internal.models.MessageId` (utils.py:15) - bot-specific, cannot move to lib
- Inbound consumers: 15 repositories, migration manager, 28 versioned migrations all import `BaseSQLProvider`
- Doc-sync: 10+ files reference `internal.database.providers` by absolute path

**Recommended:** Option A if the project wants clean architecture, as the barriers are solvable and benefits align with stated goals.

title: CORRECTION: MessageId.__str__() returns asStr() (memory 0108a08d is wrong)
content:
Memory 0108a08d-07dd-45cf-a878-571793377446 incorrectly claims that without the MessageId branch in convertToSQLite, `str(MessageId(42))` would produce the __repr__ form `MessageIdClass(messageId=42)`. This is FALSE.

Verified in internal/models/types.py lines 105-111: `MessageId.__str__()` explicitly returns `self.asStr()`. The correct string representation is produced via the __str__ fallback. The MessageId branch in convertToSQLite (utils.py:45-48) exists solely to suppress the "unsupported type" warning, not for correctness. Deleting the branch would store correct values (via str() → __str__ → asStr()) but log warnings for each MessageId value.

This matters for design decisions around the MessageId dependency cut: the Protocol approach or branch deletion are both semantically safe; the choice is about warning suppression vs generalization.

title: DatabaseManager is fully generic and movable to lib/
content:
DatabaseManager (internal/database/manager.py, 206 lines) is 100% generic and can be moved to lib/ alongside providers. Verified import list (manager.py:1-7): imports only stdlib (logging, collections.abc, typing) plus relative `from .providers import BaseSQLProvider, SQLProviderConfig, getSqlProvider`. No imports from internal.config, internal.models, or any other internal package.

Public API (manager.py:60-205):
- DatabaseManagerConfig TypedDict (default, chatMapping, providers)
- SQLProviderInitializationHook type alias (Callable[[BaseSQLProvider], Awaitable[None]])
- DatabaseManager class with methods:
  - addProviderInitializationHook(hook: SQLProviderInitializationHook) -> None
  - getProvider(chatId: int | None = None, *, dataSource: str | None = None) -> BaseSQLProvider
  - closeAll() -> Awaitable[None]

Moving DatabaseManager to lib/db/manager.py enables lib consumers (like lib/stats) to use routing (getProvider with chatId-based routing) without importing internal/database. The only consumer requiring import rewrite would be internal/database/database.py (line 37).

title: mysql.py/postgresql.py providers cannot be imported (deps missing)
content:
The MySQL and PostgreSQL provider files (internal/database/providers/mysql.py, postgresql.py) have hard module-level imports of their dependencies:
- mysql.py:13: `import aiomysql  # type: ignore[reportMissingImports]`
- postgresql.py:13: `import asyncpg  # type: ignore[reportMissingImports]`

However, neither aiomysql nor asyncpg are pinned in requirements.direct.txt (only aiosqlite==0.22.1, sqlink, sqlite-vec==0.1.9 are present). This means importing either provider module raises ImportError in the current venv. These providers survive solely because the factory (providers/__init__.py:127-138) never imports them - it raises RuntimeError for "mysql" and "postgresql" config values instead.

This has implications for the move to lib/:
1. Moving these files as-is preserves their broken state (no functional change)
2. Converting them to the repo's _AVAILABLE optional-dep pattern (module-level try/except ImportError with _AVAILABLE flag, empty except) is non-trivial: class-level variable annotations like `_pool: Optional[aiomysql.Pool]` would raise NameError if aiomysql is undefined, requiring either TYPE_CHECKING-only imports or string annotations
3. Recommended approach for the extraction: move as-is (keep hard imports), document the deviation from the _AVAILABLE convention, defer conversion to a follow-up task when MySQL/PostgreSQL support is actually wired (deps added + factory registration + tests)

title: lib package structural conventions (verified from lib/stats, lib/stt, lib/proxy)
content:
House conventions for lib packages, verified from lib/stats, lib/stt, lib/proxy:

1. **Flat packages**: lib/<domain>/ with modules directly under (lib/stats/stats_storage.py, lib/proxy/__init__.py is single-file package). Multi-word domains use snake_case (rate_limiter, geocode_maps, yandex_search).

2. **__init__.py re-exports with __all__**: Public API is re-exported at package level with explicit __all__ list. Example from lib/stats/__init__.py (lines 19-33):
   ```python
   from .stats_storage import GLOBAL_CONSUMER_ID, StatsStorage
   from .types import STATS_QUERY_ROW_LIMIT, StatsAggregateDict
   from .analysis import StatsAnalyzer
   __all__ = ["StatsStorage", "StatsAnalyzer", "StatsAggregateDict", ...]
   ```

3. **ABC + implementations**: Either ABC + Null implementation in same module (lib/stats/stats_storage.py: StatsStorage + NullStatsStorage), or ABC in abstract.py with implementations in providers/ subpackage (lib/stt/abstract.py: TranscriptProvider, lib/stt/providers/).

4. **providers/ subpackage precedent**: lib/stt/providers/ contains per-provider implementations (deepgram.py, whisper.py). This is the model for lib/db/providers/ (sqlite3.py, sqlink.py, mysql.py, postgresql.py).

5. **No lib→internal imports**: Layering rule is strict. Verified lib/proxy/__init__.py imports only stdlib (lines 10-14: logging, enum.StrEnum, threading.Lock, typing, urllib.parse). lib→lib imports are legal (sqlink.py imports lib.proxy).

6. **Naming**: Domain names are short lowercase words (ai, cache, markdown, proxy, stats, stt). Abbreviations are rare exceptions (stt is domain-standard, db is common).

title: lib/db extraction: critical consumers missed in planning, load-bearing template discovered
content:
During the lib/db extraction design work (2026-08-23), fresh greps revealed critical corrections to the planning brief:

**1. Missed consumer: internal/database/bayes_storage.py**
Lines 17-18 import from providers (`from .providers import ParametrizedQuery` and `from .providers.base import ExcludedValue`). This file was completely absent from the planning brief's consumer list. Code wins over assumptions - always re-verify with fresh greps.

**2. Load-bearing template string: internal/database/migrations/create_migration.py:128**
The scaffolding template emits `from ...providers import BaseSQLProvider, ParametrizedQuery`. If this template string is not flipped to `from lib.db.providers import ...` during the extraction, EVERY future migration will be born broken. This is a string literal inside the template generation code, not an import statement, so it's easy to miss.

**3. Repository consumer count corrected**
Planning brief claimed 15 repository files import providers. Fresh greps verified only 10 actual consumers (cache.py, chat_info.py, chat_summarization.py, chat_settings.py, chat_users.py, chat_embeddings.py, chat_search.py, user_memories.py, divinations.py, webhook_updates.py). The 15 figure counted total repo files, not actual import sites.

**4. Test-side string patch targets**
Beyond import statements, 3 string-based monkeypatch paths must be flipped in tests/database/providers/test_sqlite3_vector_search.py: `"internal.database.providers.sqlite3._SQLITE_VEC_AVAILABLE"` (lines 30, 74, 103). An import-only rewrite would miss these.

Total verified rewrite sites: 48 production (including create_migration.py template) + 38 test-side = 86 total, of which 12 are inside the 4 physically moved test files.

**Lesson**: When planning major refactors, always re-verify consumer lists with fresh greps. String-literal paths in scaffolding templates and test patch targets are easily missed in an import-only sweep.
