title: Explicit commit tasks: rider exclusions override default staging conventions
content:
Refinement of two existing git-workflow memories (commit-scope validation 7520ce60; .opencode/memory.jsonl normally-committed rule e7863703):

When the user hands over an explicit commit task with a literal file list, the list is EXHAUSTIVE and overrides general staging conventions:
- Stage exactly the listed files with explicit `git add <files>` — NEVER `git add -A`.
- Explicitly excluded modified-but-tracked files ("riders") — commonly `TODO.md` and `.opencode/memory.jsonl` — must remain unstaged even though e7863703 says memory.jsonl is normally committed. The explicit exclusion list wins over the default convention.
- Use the provided commit message verbatim (heredoc form); do not paraphrase.
- Task protocol expected by the user: (1) ground-truth check FIRST (`git log -N --oneline` + `git status --porcelain`) because tasks are IDEMPOTENT — if ground truth shows the change already landed, skip and report instead of re-doing; (2) commit; (3) report `git log -1 --stat` and final `git status --porcelain` against expectations; no push unless asked. No lint/test run needed when the session is commit-only of an already-verified working set.

title: Fixed: httpx2 alias ordering crashed all 9 httpx-pulling standalone scripts
content:
Since commit `4742f1b5` ("Migrate to httpx2 phase A") added a module-level `httpx2.alias_httpx()` to `scripts/_lib/bootstrap.py:32`, NINE scripts under `scripts/` crashed at import time when run standalone (`./venv/bin/python3 scripts/<x>.py --help` too): check_condensing, check_image_parsing, check_structured_output, check_tool_calling, list_models, reproduce_layout_extraction, reproduce_llm_dialog, run_llm_debug_query, transcribe. Error: `RuntimeError: httpx was already imported; call alias_httpx() before any import httpx`.

ROOT CAUSE (structural): every script's project-import block is contiguous and isort sorts it alphabetically (`internal` < `lib` < `scripts`), so `from scripts._lib.bootstrap import ...` ALWAYS lands LAST — after imports that transitively pull real httpx. Class (a) "bootstrap imported first" is structurally empty; no reorder-within-block can ever be safe.masked-detection: pytest suite stayed green because `tests/conftest.py` runs the alias before any test module loads.

FIX APPLIED (house pattern from main.py:16-37): uniform insert between the logging-silencing statements and the FIRST project import of each of the 9 scripts: `import httpx2  # noqa: E402` + rationale comment + bare `httpx2.alias_httpx()`. The bootstrap import stays where isort puts it (its repeat call is idempotent). Rejected alternative: hoisting the bootstrap import above internal/lib fights isort within a contiguous block.

Regression test: `tests/scripts/test_httpx_alias_import.py`, parametrized over all 9 scripts, FAIL-first verified via `git stash push -- scripts/` (9 failed unfixed → 9 passed fixed). Full suite: 4416 passed / 11 skipped (baseline 4407). CHANGELOG entry added under [Unreleased].

title: Real-httpx puller chain through project imports (first offender: internal.bot.models)
content:
When placing `httpx2.alias_httpx()` (or auditing a new entry point), know which project imports actually pull REAL httpx (third-party packages sqlink and the openai SDK do plain `import httpx`; project code migrated to `import httpx2 as httpx`). Verified first-puller chains (fresh-interpreter probe):

- `internal.bot.models` (e.g. line :72 of many scripts) is typically the FIRST puller — earlier than the commonly-blamed `internal.database`. Chain: `internal/bot/models/__init__.py:23` → `chat_settings.py:11` → `lib/ai/abstract.py:31` → `lib/stats/__init__.py:20` → `sql_storage.py:18` → `lib/db/__init__.py:32` → `manager.py:11` → `providers/__init__.py:53` (EAGER `from .sqlink import SQLinkProvider`) → `sqlink.py:14` → `_transport.py:17 import httpx`.
- Also pulling real httpx transitively: `internal.database`, `lib.ai` itself, and `internal.services.proxy.service`.
- `internal.config.manager` does NOT pull httpx (safe before the alias).

Consequence: fixes must place the alias before ALL project imports, not just above whichever line was flagged. Detection technique that worked: meta-path finder whose find_spec watches for "httpx" and prints traceback.print_stack(); or per-import `sys.modules.get("httpx")` probes in a fresh interpreter per candidate import.

title: By-path importlib loading must register module in sys.modules BEFORE exec_module (dataclasses artifact)
content:
Loading a script/module by path via `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)` + `spec.loader.exec_module(module)` WITHOUT registering it in `sys.modules` first makes any module-level `@dataclasses.dataclass` fail with:

```
ns = sys.modules.get(cls.__module__).__dict__
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute '__dict__'
```

because `dataclasses._is_type` resolves string annotations via `sys.modules.get(cls.__module__)`.

Correct pattern (house helper, tests/scripts/test_check_structured_output.py:35):
```python
module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
sys.modules.setdefault(spec.name, module)   # <-- REQUIRED before exec_module
spec.loader.exec_module(module)
```

This gotcha caused false positives during a hazard sweep: pure-stdlib `scripts/check_docs.py` "failed" under by-path loading while running perfectly via `--help`. Never trust by-path-load failures without cross-checking direct invocation.

title: Script import-order regressions need fresh-subprocess tests (conftest aliasing masks them in-process)
content:
To regression-test STANDALONE script import behavior (e.g., import-time crashes like the httpx2 alias RuntimeError), an in-process pytest load is useless: `tests/conftest.py:8-13` aliases httpx before any test module loads, masking exactly the failure mode that bites real users (`./venv/bin/python3 scripts/x.py`). Required shape (new file `tests/scripts/test_httpx_alias_import.py`, house precedent `tests/lib/max_webhook_receiver/test_init.py`):

1. Fresh subprocess: `subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", childCode], cwd=REPO_ROOT)` — embedded `-c` inside a pytest test is sanctioned (documented exemption in test_init.py's docstring; the repo's no-`python -c` rule covers ad-hoc manual testing only).
2. Child registers the target in `sys.modules` before exec_module (see dataclasses gotcha).
3. Assert returncode == 0 AND `sys.modules["httpx"] is httpx2` (identity-check proves the alias is active, not just absence-of-crash); surface full stderr in the assertion message.
4. Parametrize over affected scripts; to re-verify FAIL-first against an already-fixed tree use `git stash push -- scripts/` then pop.

Also confirmed: the whole-suite green state can hide broken standalone scripts whenever conftest pre-aliases imports — any import-order invariant tied to process-global state needs at least one subprocess-based test.

title: httpx2 alias regression test — manual list contract + why subprocess-only
content:
From the Gate-1 review of tests/scripts/test_httpx_alias_import.py (added by the httpx2 9-script fix):

1. **Manual list contract**: the parametrized script inventory lives in module constant `_ALIASING_SCRIPTS`. When adding ANY new script under `scripts/` that imports project code (`internal.*`/`lib.*`), the list must be extended BY HAND — nothing auto-discovers. Deliberate trade-off: auto-discovery would flag `scripts/prune_unknown_chat_settings.py`, which is intentionally excluded (class (c): imports `internal.bot.models.chat_settings` with NO bootstrap import → cannot crash, silently on real httpx by design).
2. **Subprocess isolation is mandatory, not stylistic**: `tests/conftest.py` calls `httpx2.alias_httpx()` as its FIRST executable statement, so the pytest process itself always shows `sys.modules['httpx'] is httpx2` regardless of any in-process load order. An in-process alias assertion is therefore vacuous — only a fresh interpreter (`[sys.executable, "-c", childCode]`, precedent tests/lib/max_webhook_receiver/test_init.py:40, documented exemption in both docstrings) can honestly reproduce standalone-run import ordering.
3. **House loader shape**: load each script via `spec_from_file_location(target.stem, target)` then `sys.modules[target.stem] = mod` BEFORE `exec_module(mod)` (precedent test_check_structured_output.py:35) — prevents spurious dataclass annotation failures.
4. **Child assert propagation**: the identity assertion `sys.modules['httpx'] is httpx2` runs inside the child process and propagates failure purely via exit code ≠ 0 (with stderr surfaced); the parent asserts only returncode == 0.
5. **isort mechanics**: an executable statement (`httpx2.alias_httpx()`) between import groups acts as a section split — isort neither hoists imports above it nor moves it, so the block placement survives `isort --check-only` when subsequent project imports carry `# noqa: E402`.
6. Scripts resolve the repo root from `__file__` (e.g. check_condensing.py:60–62), so their imports are cwd-independent and work under both direct invocation and `-m`; the test pins cwd=REPO_ROOT harmlessly since only import-time behavior is exercised.

title: Scripts' httpx2 setLevel(WARNING) is a defensive no-op — don't remove it
content:
In the nine `scripts/` dev scripts (check_condensing, check_image_parsing, check_image_parsing, check_structured_output, check_tool_calling, list_models, reproduce_layout_extraction, reproduce_llm_dialog, run_llm_debug_query, transcribe), each calls `logging.basicConfig(level=logging.WARNING)` and then `logging.getLogger("httpx2").setLevel(logging.WARNING)` (e.g. transcribe.py:42). Because the scripts' root logger is already WARNING, the httpx2 setLevel is technically a NO-OP there (httpx2 inherits WARNING by default).

In `main.py` the same line (:42) IS load-bearing: root is INFO via basicConfig(INFO), so without the explicit raise, httpx2 would emit INFO-level GET/POST request logs.

Convention: keep the line in the scripts anyway as defensive verbatim mirroring of main.py — it protects against a script later lowering its root level (e.g. a --verbose flag). Flagged as a nitpick in the Gate-1 review (2026-08-28) and judged acceptable; do not "clean up" as dead code. Note the OLD pre-fix line used `getLogger("httpx")` + ERROR level, which also suppressed httpx2 warnings (wrong name post-alias); the new WARNING level is strictly more faithful.

title: All 32 pytest warnings = single PTB RetryAfter deprecation; anatomy + validated filter fix
content:
Triage result (2026-08-28, branch extract-max-webmessage, HEAD 112d081d, investigation-only session): the suite's 32 warnings are ONE unique warning — PTBDeprecationWarning raised at `venv/.../telegram/error.py:243` (`RetryAfter.retry_after` property → `get_timedelta_value` in `telegram/_utils/datetime.py`, which warns on EVERY property access while `PTB_TIMEDELTA` env is unset; PTB 22.8 installed; env unset repo-wide). Exclusively emitted by 4 tests in `tests/bot/common/test_bot.py::TestTelegramSendRetry`.

Emission anatomy:
- `RetryAfter.__init__` (error.py:235-238) reads `self.retry_after` twice (isinstance + message f-string) → 2 warnings per construction.
- Production `TheBot._retryTelegramSend` (internal/bot/common/bot.py:810-825) reads `e.retry_after` three times per caught-and-retried exception (isinstance :815, conversion :816/:818, log f-string :822). Final exhausted attempt re-raises at :811-813 BEFORE any read → 0 warnings.

Per-test reconciliation (empirically verified per-test): honorsRetryAfter=5 (1 constr×2 + 1 retried×3), cappedAt60=10 (2×2+2×3), AsTimedelta=5 (1×2+1×3), Exhausted=12 (3×2+2×3). Total = 14 (7 constructions) + 18 (6 retried) = 32 exactly. Note: `AsyncMock(side_effect=[...])` lists construct RetryAfter eagerly at arrange time.

Validated one-line fix in pyproject `[tool.pytest.ini_options].filterwarnings`: `"ignore:.*retry_after.*datetime[.]timedelta"` — verified via temp `-c` config: 14 passed, 0 warnings. Alternative [TEST] approach: `pytest.warns(PTBDeprecationWarning)` wraps in the 4 tests (fails loudly when PTB flips default; more churn). Do NOT set PTB_TIMEDELTA=1 in test env to silence (flips which prod branch runs — see separate memory on dead timedelta branch).

Baseline for before/after: `4421 passed, 11 skipped, 32 warnings, 194 subtests passed in ~77.5s` on CPython 3.14.6 venv. `make test` = `time timeout 5m pytest --durations=4` — no warning-relevant difference. No `utcnow(` anywhere in internal/lib/tests (3.14 stdlib-deprecation concern moot). pyproject already globally ignores ResourceWarning (pre-existing blanket hide). Micro-observation: hoisting the 3× `e.retry_after` reads in bot.py to one local would cut warnings 18→6 but is not a fix by itself.

title: pytest filterwarnings: category-path form breaks suite via httpx2 alias; colon-split and escape-flag gotchas
content:
Three empirically proven gotchas when writing pytest warning filters in this repo (pytest 9.1.1):

1. **Category-path filters break the whole suite.** `ignore::telegram.warnings.PTBDeprecationWarning` (any third-party category module) causes pytest to import the category module in `pytest_load_initial_conftests` — BEFORE conftest import. `import telegram` imports real `httpx`, then `tests/conftest.py:13` `httpx2.alias_httpx()` raises `RuntimeError: httpx was already imported`. Applies to both ini `filterwarnings` and CLI `-W` forms (verified 2026-08-28). Fix: use message-anchored filters with NO category (defaults to builtin `Warning`, no import), e.g. `"ignore:.*retry_after.*datetime[.]timedelta"`.

2. **Message regex must be colon-free.** `parse_warning_filter` does a naive `arg.split(":")` over `action:message:category:module:lineno`. The actual PTB message text contains a colon ("Deprecated since version v22.2: ..."), so the literal message can't be pasted; use a `.*`-prefixed regex avoiding colons.

3. **CLI `-W` dry-runs mislead.** Cmdline `-W` filters are parsed with `escape=True` (regex metacharacters literalized → literal substring match), while ini `filterwarnings` entries use `escape=False` (raw regex). A regex that works in ini silently does nothing via `-W` — a CLI "it didn't work" result is NOT evidence against the ini form.

Validation technique avoiding repo edits: write a temp pyproject.toml in the sanctioned temp dir replicating the repo's `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` (asyncio_mode, asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope, python_files/classes/functions, existing filterwarnings) plus the candidate entry, then run `./venv/bin/pytest -c /path/to/temp/pyproject.toml <target tests> -q --tb=no -p no:cacheprovider`.

title: PTB_TIMEDELTA unset: timedelta branch in _retryTelegramSend is dead code; AsTimedelta test exercises int path
content:
Coverage-drift finding from warnings triage (2026-08-28), extends the existing int|timedelta handling memory:

With `PTB_TIMEDELTA` unset (current state of BOTH prod and test env), PTB 22.8's `get_timedelta_value` converts back to int — proven by probe: `RetryAfter(retry_after=timedelta(seconds=3)).retry_after` returns `int 3`, and `isinstance(..., timedelta)` is False. Therefore the timedelta branch at `internal/bot/common/bot.py:815-816` (`isinstance(e.retry_after, timedelta)`) is dead code in both environments.

Consequence: `test_retryTelegramSend_retryAfterAsTimedelta_honored` passes entirely via the int path (`float(3) == 3.0`) — its docstring claim (timedelta converted to float seconds via the timedelta branch) is NOT actually exercised. The branch only runs if someone sets `PTB_TIMEDELTA=1`.

Right follow-up (its own ticket): a parametrized dual-mode test using `monkeypatch.setenv("PTB_TIMEDELTA", "1")` alongside the default-mode variant, so both branches of `_retryTelegramSend` stay covered. Do NOT set the env var globally for the test suite — that silently flips coverage away from today's default int path instead of adding coverage.

title: PTB retry_after deprecation warnings asserted via pytest.warns, not filtered
content: Decision confirmed 2026-08-28 (branch extract-max-webmessage): PTB v22.x emits a `PTBDeprecationWarning` on EVERY `RetryAfter.retry_after` property access while env `PTB_TIMEDELTA` is unset (warning raised in `telegram/error.py` `__init__` — 2 per construction via isinstance + f-string — plus per read). The repo's chosen handling in `tests/bot/common/test_bot.py::TestTelegramSendRetry` is ASSERTION, not filtering: the 4 RetryAfter tests wrap their whole bodies (after docstring — must start before the eager `RetryAfter(...)` constructions in `AsyncMock(side_effect=[...])` lists and enclose the awaited `_retryTelegramSend` call) in `with pytest.warns(PTBDeprecationWarning):`. Import: `from telegram.warnings import PTBDeprecationWarning` (safe in test files; tests/conftest.py aliases httpx→httpx2 before test imports). Explicitly NO `filterwarnings` entry in pyproject.toml — the two approaches are mutually exclusive, and `pytest.warns` acts as a tripwire that FAILS when PTB flips the `retry_after` default to `timedelta`. Class docstring documents the forward-compat rationale. Production-side context: `internal/bot/common/bot.py:815-822` reads `e.retry_after` 3× per caught-and-retried exception (known redundancy, deliberately left out of scope). Applying the same pattern to future PTB-deprecation-emitting tests: wrap in `pytest.warns`, never filter.

title: pytest.warns DID NOT WARN requires ZERO emitters inside the block
content: Gotcha verified 2026-08-28 while sanity-checking `pytest.warns` wraps in `tests/bot/common/test_bot.py::TestTelegramSendRetry`: `pytest.warns(...)` fails with "DID NOT WARN" only when ZERO warnings of the target class are emitted inside the `with` block. Moving ONE test-side `RetryAfter(...)` construction outside the `with` (a plausible-sounding "break the wrap" mutation) does NOT trip the assertion, because production-side `e.retry_after` reads during the awaited `_retryTelegramSend` call (`internal/bot/common/bot.py:815-822`, 3 reads per caught-and-retried RetryAfter) remain inside and still satisfy it — the leaked construction warnings just surface in pytest's warnings summary. To prove a `pytest.warns` wrap is a real assertion, the block must be emptied of ALL emitters (e.g. temporarily narrow it so both the constructions AND the awaited call sit outside, leaving `with pytest.warns(...): pass`); the failing test then shows `Failed: DID NOT WARN. No warnings of type ... were emitted.` Revert with the exact reverse edit. When a task spec suggests a mutation-based sanity check, check the emitter inventory first — the literal suggestion may physically be unable to fail.

title: filterwarnings category-path form is forbidden: imports telegram before conftest httpx2 alias → suite-wide RuntimeError
content: Gotcha for any future "just filter the warning" temptation in this repo: NEVER use the category-path filterwarnings form, e.g. `filterwarnings = ["ignore::telegram.warnings.PTBDeprecationWarning"]` in pyproject.toml. Pytest resolves filter CATEGORIES at collection/conftest-import time BEFORE `tests/conftest.py` executes, so mentioning `telegram.warnings` imports the telegram package (→ real httpx) before conftest runs its httpx→httpx2 aliasing (`alias_httpx()`), raising a RuntimeError that breaks the ENTIRE suite at startup. The message-pattern form IS safe because it imports nothing: `"ignore:.*retry_after.*datetime[.]timedelta"` was empirically validated (14 passed, 0 warnings via temp `-c` config). But the repo's ratified approach is neither — it is assertion via `pytest.warns(PTBDeprecationWarning)` wraps (see the separate decision memory), because the message-filter silently hides the deprecation while the wrap trips exactly when PTB flips the `retry_after` default. Also: importing `telegram.warnings` at the TOP of a test file is safe (conftest aliases first); the hazard is specific to pytest's own filter parsing order.

title: Review/gate requests must declare ALL working-tree files; session-journal riders sneak in

title: PTBDeprecationWarning fires on every retry_after property access (PTB_TIMEDELTA unset)
content:
PTB (python-telegram-bot) emits `PTBDeprecationWarning` on EVERY access of the `telegram.error.RetryAfter.retry_after` property while the `PTB_TIMEDELTA` env var is unset — the warning fires on property READ, not on exception construction.

Consequence: a single logical issue multiplies across the suite. `TheBot._retryTelegramSend` reads `retry_after` 3 times per retry, so the 4 `TestTelegramSendRetry` tests in `tests/bot/common/test_bot.py` produced all 32 suite warnings from one warning class.

Deliberate design: the tests construct `retry_after` in the INT form on purpose (forward-compat with the current int default, waiting for PTB to flip to timedelta).

Fix pattern (commit a4ae0a17, branch extract-max-webmessage): wrap the exception construction AND the awaited send call in `pytest.warns(PTBDeprecationWarning)` — an assertion/tripwire, NOT suppression (no `filterwarnings` ignore). The suite reports zero warnings, and the tests fail loudly the moment PTB flips the timedelta default, forcing an update to the int/timedelta handling in `_retryTelegramSend` (which already handles both forms).

title: Code-reviewer sandbox permissions: read-only git + quality gates only; verify libraries by reading venv source
content: Environment constraint confirmed during the 2026-08-28 Gate-1 review (useful for future reviewer agents): bash is allowlisted to read-only inspection — git status/diff/log/show/ls-files etc., `ls`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `rg`, `grep`, `sed -n`, `awk`, `wc`, `sort`, `diff` — plus exactly `make lint`, `make test`, `make check-docs`, and `./venv/bin/pytest *`. Everything else is denied, notably ad-hoc `./venv/bin/python3 -c` probes. Workaround that worked well: verify third-party library behavior by READING installed sources directly, e.g. `venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/telegram/error.py`, `telegram/_utils/datetime.py`, `telegram/warnings.py` (note: venv is CPython 3.14). Tooling gotcha in the same session: `rg <pattern> venv/...` as a DIRECTORY search silently returns nothing because rg honors .gitignore (venv/ is ignored) — pass the explicit FILE path and it works. This also means reasoning-only analysis plus the `make test` zero-warnings summary line (pytest omits the warnings segment only when count is zero) can substitute for runtime probes.

title: Tripwire failure mode when PTB flips retry_after default: only the 4 pytest.warns fail; value assertions stay valid
content: Extension of the dead-timedelta-branch memory (fdbb6ed2) — what actually happens when PTB removes the int back-compat (PTB_TIMEDELTA default flips to timedelta, or the env var is removed): `get_timedelta_value` stops warning in default mode → exactly the 4 wrapped tests in `TestTelegramSendRetry` fail with `Failed: DID NOT WARN` while ALL value assertions keep passing, because `bot.py:815`'s isinstance branch becomes live and `total_seconds()` yields the same numbers (sleep assertions 2.0/60.0/3.0/1.0 remain correct for both int and timedelta paths). So the tripwire fails for precisely the right reason and the update is mechanical: drop or adjust the `pytest.warns` wraps; no assertion rewrites needed. Corollary env-coupling risk: if any CI or dev shell exports `PTB_TIMEDELTA=true`, these 4 tests fail with DID NOT WARN out of the box — that is the tripwire firing by design, not a flake. Version attribution nit for the record: the deprecation was introduced in PTB v22.2 (per the warning's own version string); 22.8 is just the installed/pinned version (`requirements.direct.txt:15`).

title: PTB_TIMEDELTA mechanics verified: per-access getenv, in-process dual-mode tests viable, symmetric int→timedelta, silent in timedelta mode
content:
Empirical verification (2026-09-01, PTB 22.8, pytest 9.1.1, Python 3.14.6) of the dual-mode test design recommended in memory fdbb6ed2 — all mechanics now proven, no subprocess needed:

1. **Per-access read, NOT import-time cached.** `PTB_TIMEDELTA` is read inside `get_timedelta_value` at `telegram/_utils/datetime.py:274`: `if os.getenv("PTB_TIMEDELTA", "false").lower().strip() in ["true", "1"]: return value`. This is the ONLY read site in the whole telegram package (`rg --no-ignore PTB_TIMEDELTA` verified — rg needs --no-ignore because venv/ is gitignored). No module-level flag attribute exists, so the setattr approach is N/A.

2. **`monkeypatch.setenv("PTB_TIMEDELTA", "1")` works regardless of import order** (conftest importing telegram early is irrelevant). `monkeypatch.undo()` restores int behavior + PTBDeprecationWarning; a subsequently-run test sees default env. Disturbance check: a flag-flipping test followed by `tests/bot/common/test_bot.py::TestTelegramSendRetry` in one session → 15 passed.

3. **Symmetric conversion guaranteed by construction:** `RetryAfter.__init__` (telegram/error.py:233) ALWAYS stores `self._retry_after = to_timedelta(retry_after)` (int/float → timedelta via `_utils/argumentparsing.py`); the property re-exposes per env. Under flag=1, int-constructed `RetryAfter(retry_after=3).retry_after` → `timedelta(seconds=3)`, `.total_seconds() == 3.0`. So existing INT-form retry tests stay green in dual mode: value flows into bot.py's isinstance-timedelta branch → total_seconds() → same floats → sleep assertions hold (verified for value 3).

4. **No PTBDeprecationWarning in timedelta mode:** `get_timedelta_value` returns at :275 BEFORE `warn()` at :276 (verified with `warnings.simplefilter("error")` around construction AND access). Dual-mode timedelta tests need NO pytest.warns; int-mode tests still do — note one int-mode construction itself warns once (via `__init__:235` message formatting reading the property) plus once per access.

5. **Blast radius while flipped (process-global until monkeypatch teardown):** every property routed through `get_timedelta_value` returns raw timedelta and stops warning — RetryAfter.retry_after (error.py:243), ChatFullInfo.slow_mode_delay, Poll.open_period, ChatInviteLink.subscription_period, MessageAutoDeleteTimerChanged.message_auto_delete_time, VideoChat props, Voice/Video/VideoNote/Animation/Audio/PaidMedia/InputMedia durations, InlineQueryResult{Gif,Mpeg4Gif,Video,Audio,Voice} durations, live_period ×3. All per-access → clean revert.

6. **Int-mode edge:** fractional seconds → float (3.5s → 3.5), whole → int. Flag also accepts "true"/"TRUE" (lower().strip()).

title: ResourceWarning invisible under pytest 9.1.1 even with ini ignore line removed — removal experiment vacuous; census requires always::ResourceWarning
content:
Gotchas for any future pytest warning-filter work in this repo (verified 2026-09-01):

1. **Python 3.14 interpreter default filters include `('ignore', None, ResourceWarning, None, 0)`** (verified by dumping `warnings.filters`). pytest 9.1.1's `_pytest/warnings.py:39-42` force-enables ONLY DeprecationWarning + PendingDeprecationWarning (`if not sys.warnoptions:` block) — ResourceWarning falls through to the interpreter default ignore.

2. **Consequence: removing `"ignore::ResourceWarning"` from pyproject.toml filterwarnings is a functional NO-OP and a "0 warnings" result after removal proves NOTHING.** The current blanket ignore line merely re-asserts the interpreter default; `make coverage` adds no -W flags (Makefile:95-99).

3. **To actually census ResourceWarnings, use `filterwarnings = ["always::ResourceWarning"]`.** Positive control (deliberately leaked file handle + gc.collect()): invisible under the removed-line config, surfaced under the always config ("1 passed, 1 warning" with full message).

4. **ini filter precedence gotcha:** `apply_warning_filters` calls `warnings.filterwarnings` per ini line in file order; each PREPENDS → the LAST ini line ends up highest-priority. To show all ResourceWarnings except one module, put `ignore::ResourceWarning:<module>` LAST.

5. **Experiment technique that works:** `./venv/bin/pytest -c /tmp/<dir>/config.ini tests lib internal` from repo root — explicit args REQUIRED for collection parity with testpaths (verified 4432 = 4432); with only testpaths and a temp config, rootdir/config resolution can misbehave. Do NOT use CLI `-W` (escape=True parsing, misleading — confirmed earlier). `PYTHONDEVMODE=1` additionally surfaces warnings emitted OUTSIDE pytest catch contexts (e.g. interpreter shutdown) to stderr; note it sets sys.warnoptions, skipping pytest's deprecation force-enable block (ini filters still apply inside contexts).

6. Blind spot of any pytest census: warnings swallowed inside a test's own nested `warnings.catch_warnings(record=True)` never reach pytest's warnings summary.

title: ResourceWarning filter history, empty census at a4ae0a17, tripwire recommendation
content:
Findings + recommendation for the `filterwarnings = ["ignore::ResourceWarning"]` line in pyproject.toml (branch extract-max-webmessage @ a4ae0a17, investigated 2026-09-01):

**History:** `c19e9cbc` "add `make coverage`" (2025-10-28, pytest 8.4.2 era) added the NARROW `["ignore::ResourceWarning:unittest.mock"]` together with a tearDown in `internal/services/cache/test_cache_service.py` clearing `cache.dbWrapper`/`mockDb` ("Clear the database reference to avoid resource warnings"). `1e2c62ec` "Even More tests (phase 4)" (same day, +9691 lines) widened it to the blanket `"ignore::ResourceWarning"` with no recorded rationale (both commit bodies empty) — cargo-cult widening. (`git log -S` misses the widening because the string count is unchanged; use `git log -L` on the block.)

**Census result:** with `filterwarnings = ["always::ResourceWarning"]`, full suite (4432 collected / 4421 passed / 11 skipped) emitted ZERO ResourceWarnings — stable across two consecutive runs AND under PYTHONDEVMODE=1 (covers shutdown-time emission). No test-code leaks, no third-party noise, no production leaks observable. The one historical leak (cache dbWrapper) is already fixed in-tree.

**Recommendation delivered:** replace the blanket ignore (a no-op today, see related gotcha memory) with the tripwire `filterwarnings = ["always::ResourceWarning"]` — free today (deterministic across 3 runs; positive control proves it fires when a leak exists) and converts silent masking into regression protection. If an unfixable GC-timed third-party warning ever appears, add a module-scoped ignore as the LAST ini entry (later lines take precedence).

title: PTB_TIMEDELTA=1 dual-mode test recipe for RetryAfter timedelta branch
content:
Verified recipe (2026-09-01, PTB 22.8) for testing the `isinstance(e.retry_after, timedelta)` branch of `TheBot._retryTelegramSend`, which is DEAD under the default env (property converts timedelta→int per access while PTB_TIMEDELTA is unset):

- `PTB_TIMEDELTA` is read PER-ACCESS via `os.getenv("PTB_TIMEDELTA", "false").lower().strip() in ["true", "1"]` in `telegram/_utils/datetime.py:272-289`. Therefore `monkeypatch.setenv("PTB_TIMEDELTA", "1")` flips behavior in-process and is cleanly reversible — no reimport needed.
- In timedelta mode: `RetryAfter.retry_after` returns `datetime.timedelta` regardless of int-or-timedelta construction (`to_timedelta` canonicalizes at `__init__`); the PTBDeprecationWarning does NOT fire there (early return before `warn()`) — so such tests need NO `pytest.warns`.
- Forward-compat pin: int-constructed `RetryAfter(3)` → `timedelta(seconds=3)` → `total_seconds() == 3.0` in this mode.
- Property annotation is `int | dtm.timedelta` (telegram/error.py:241).
- CRITICAL ordering: set the env var BEFORE constructing `RetryAfter` in the test.
- Landed as `TestTelegramSendRetryTimedeltaMode` (3 tests) at `tests/bot/common/test_bot.py:872-974`, mirroring sibling tests' AsyncMock-side_effect + patched `internal.bot.common.bot.asyncio.sleep` structure; asserts sleep args 3.0 / 3.0 / 60.0 (over-cap test).

title: make test now runs ~4:30–4:51 — dangerously close to its own timeout 5m cap
content:
Suite duration data point (2026-09-01, branch extract-max-webmessage @ a4ae0a17 + 3 new tests): **4424 passed, 11 skipped, 0 warnings in 267–292s (~4:27–4:51)**. This supersedes the ~108s figure recorded 2026-07-11 — the suite has grown ~2.7×.

title: User requires mutation sanity (sabotage→FAIL, revert→PASS) for branch-coverage tests
content:
User preference observed in worker-brief acceptance criteria (2026-09-01): when adding tests that exercise a branch (especially one dead under the default environment), the brief mandates a **mutation sanity check** and the report must paste BOTH runs:

1. Temporarily sabotage the target branch (e.g., make it compute `0.0` instead of the real value).
2. Run the new tests → expect ALL of them FAILED (proves each test actually exercises the branch).
3. Revert the sabotage, rerun → expect all PASSED.

Applied to `TestTelegramSendRetryTimedeltaMode`: sabotage → `3 failed` (`assert 0.0 == 3.0` ×2, `assert 0.0 == 60.0`), revert → `3 passed`. This catches vacuous tests that appear green via a different code path — complements the write-regression-test skill's "must FAIL before the fix" rule for bugfix tests.

title: Worktree can get dirty from concurrent user activity even when the brief says "clean"
content:
Observed 2026-09-01: a task brief stated the worktree was "clean except hands-off rider `.opencode/memory.jsonl`", yet during the task `git status` also showed unrelated modifications — `.gitignore`, `.opencode/opencode.json`, `TODO.md`, and untracked `.markdown-mcp.toml` — all from concurrent user activity (local markdown-mcp tool setup + personal TODO notes), not from the agent.

Guidance for future sessions: before assuming ownership of unexpected worktree changes, inspect them with `git diff` / `git log` and match against your own edits. Leave unrelated files untouched (do NOT revert them — they may be the user's in-flight work), and report them explicitly as deviations in the handoff. Briefs' "clean tree" claims are point-in-time and can go stale in this multi-session environment.

content:
RESOLVED 2026-09-01 (branch extract-max-webmessage @ a4ae0a17, gate-1 review PASS): the drift recorded in memory fdbb6ed2 ("timedelta branch is dead code, AsTimedelta test passes via int path, NOT fixed") is now fixed by an uncommitted 4-file diff:

title: aiohttp run_app readiness banner is print() — invisible under file redirection
content:
aiohttp's `web.run_app` emits the `======== Running on http://host:port ========` banner via plain `print()` to **stdout** (not the logging module). Python block-buffers stdout when it is a regular file, so under `> logfile`, nohup, or init-system `output_log=` redirects the banner never appears until the process exits — while stderr logging lines appear immediately (stderr is line-buffered/unbuffered). Empirically reproduced with the Max webhook receiver: banner appeared in the captured log only after SIGTERM, ~57 s after the socket was already LISTENing.

Consequences / right way:
- Never use the banner as a readiness signal in scripts or service configs with redirected output. Use a stderr log line from the app itself (e.g. `Database initialized` from lib.db.manager) or probe the port (`lsof`/`nc`/curl).
- In containers this bites only if `PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1` is absent — Gromozeka's `lib/max_webhook_receiver/Dockerfile` sets it, so the Docker path works while the OpenRC host path silently hides the banner.
- If a Gromozeka service ever needs a log-based readiness signal, emit it via `logging` (stderr), not `print`.

title: load_dotenv silently skips lines whose value contains '='
content:
`lib/utils/utils.py` `load_dotenv` (default `.env`, used by main.py and the Max webhook receiver launcher) parses only lines where `split("=")` yields EXACTLY 2 parts. Any line with more than one `=` — i.e. a value containing `=` such as base64 padding (`SECRET=abc123==`) or inline `KEY: VALUE = x=y` forms — is silently skipped, no warning. It also has no `export` prefix or quoted-value unquoting support beyond what the split allows.

Safe in current flows because the documented secret recipe is `openssl rand -hex 32` (hex, no `=`) and receiver config uses literal literals or `${VAR}` references, not inline secrets. Gotcha to remember when adding new env-provided values: keep secrets `=`-free or the variable will appear unset downstream (`substituteEnvVars` then leaves `${VAR}` untouched, and the receiver/bot secret guards exit 1 with "unresolved placeholder" — misleading root cause).

Related verified behavior: missing dotenv file → `logger.error("File {path} not found")` and continues; `substituteEnvVars` leaves unresolved `${VAR}` untouched (`os.getenv(key, match.group(0))`).

title: "Database initialized" is NOT a listener-readiness signal for Max webhook receiver (pre-bind)
content:
Root cause found during Gate-1B review (2026-09-02): the stderr log line `Database initialized: {...}` is emitted at INFO by `lib/db/manager.py:93` during DatabaseManager construction, which runs at `lib/max_webhook_receiver/__main__.py:107` — BEFORE TLS certificate loading (`__main__.py:124-126`), before `web.run_app()` (`__main__.py:128`), before the app-startup schema init (`ensureWebhookUpdatesSchema`), and before aiohttp binds the socket. So the line can appear even when startup subsequently fails (e.g. port 8443 already occupied). Any doc instructing "wait for Database initialized, then start the bot" is wrong.

Correct readiness checks:
- Authoritative: curl port probe WITHOUT `--fail`: `curl -sS -o /dev/null 'http://127.0.0.1:8443/updates?timeout=0'` in an until-loop. Any HTTP answer including 403 (auth check at `app.py:176-179` when get-updates-secret is set) means the listener is up; `timeout=0` is accepted via clamping (`app.py:182`) so there is no long-poll wait. Without `--fail`, curl only fails on connection-level errors.
- The aiohttp `======== Running on ========` banner is a plain `print()` to STDOUT (venv aiohttp/web.py:406-411, emitted after sites start), so it is block-buffered and invisible under OpenRC `output_log` redirection until process exit; it appears immediately only on a terminal and in Docker (`PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1`, Dockerfile:35-36).
- Logging config: `logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)` at `__main__.py:30` → log lines go to stderr.

Related: `.dockerignore:23-25` already ignores `**/*.db`, `**/*.db-wal`, `**/*.db-shm` (recursive, independent of the root-anchored `.gitignore` patterns).

title: Reviewer sandbox bash allowlist: git check-ignore denied — use ls-files + static analysis

title: Webhook receiver readiness: port probe only, "Database initialized" log is not a signal
content:
Gate-1B fix (branch `extract-max-webmessage`) to `docs/max-webhook-setup.md` Step 9: the `Database initialized: {...}` log line is NOT a listener-readiness signal. It is emitted from `DatabaseManager.__init__` (`lib/db/manager.py:93`, called at `lib/max_webhook_receiver/__main__.py:107`) — BEFORE TLS cert loading (`__main__.py:124-126`), before `web.run_app()` (`:128`), and before aiohttp binds the socket — so it appears even when binding subsequently fails (e.g. port already occupied). The port probe is the only authoritative readiness check.

Readiness probe pattern (now codified in Step 9): `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' 'http://127.0.0.1:8443/updates?timeout=0'` — any HTTP answer, including `403` once `get-updates-secret` is set, means the listener is up. There is no dedicated health endpoint. For scripted start order use `until curl -s -o /dev/null 'http://127.0.0.1:8443/updates?timeout=0'; do sleep 1; done` — without `--fail`, curl exits 0 on ANY HTTP answer (including 403) and fails only on connection-level errors. The aiohttp `======== Running on ========` banner is not usable under redirected logs: it goes to stdout and is block-buffered (may lag until shutdown); it appears immediately only on a terminal and in the Docker image.

The doc was corrected to demote the log line to "startup progress" and make the port probe the primary check; banner caveat kept verbatim.

title: User workflow: surgical doc-fix tasks come with strict scope, no-commit, and exact verification gates
content: The user's doc-fix tasks in this repo (e.g. Gate-1B rounds on `docs/max-webhook-setup.md`) follow a strict specification pattern that must be honored exactly: (1) surgical scope — touch ONLY the specified lines/sections, never other steps, Docker sections, or Troubleshooting; (2) an uncommitted working tree often carries riders (`.gitignore`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md`, `.opencode/memory.jsonl`) that must be left untouched; (3) never commit unless explicitly asked; (4) verification is specified with exact expected outputs — `git diff -- <file>` hunks must be confined to the target area, `make check-docs` must report `0 broken` (baseline Sep 2026: `Checked 129 markdown files, 2992 links; 0 broken`), and `git status --porcelain` must show the identical pre-edit file set; (5) target wording is often supplied verbatim to adapt into the guide's existing formatting/tone (e.g. keep existing caveat sentences verbatim). Note: `git diff` against HEAD shows the cumulative working-tree change (earlier uncommitted edits + your delta), so hunk-confinement checks must account for pre-existing uncommitted edits in the same file.

title: .opencode/memory.jsonl insert count drifts mid-session in diff-stat checks
content:
`.opencode/memory.jsonl` grows DURING a session, not just between sessions. Observed during a review-only Gate-1B round-2 session (branch `extract-max-webmessage`, 2026-09-02): two `git diff --stat` checks within the same session showed the file's insert count grow from +9 to +11 lines while the agent made no edits to it — session infrastructure writes memory entries as the session progresses.

Implication for working-tree scope verification: when a task defines an expected diff scope that includes `.opencode/memory.jsonl` (e.g. as a known "hands-off rider"), treat only the FILE LIST as the stable check; the insert-count for this file is non-deterministic within a session and will drift between checks. Do not fail a scope check because memory.jsonl's `+N` grew — only fail if an unexpected PATH appears in `git status --porcelain`.

title: Byte-exact verbatim-copy verification: git diff --no-index -U0 + grep '^+'
content:
Technique proven 2026-09-02 during the 8-file extraction pass from `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md` into `docs/llm/memories/*.md`, where bodies had to be copied VERBATIM byte-for-byte (including >2000-char lines) through the `write` tool (transcription by hand, no sed/redirect available).

After writing an extracted file, run:
`git diff --no-index -U0 docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md docs/llm/memories/<slug>.md | grep '^+'`

Because the copied block is contiguous in the source, diff aligns it as common context. Correctness criterion: the ONLY `+` lines are the intentionally new lines (the `#` heading + the "Archived durable notes from..." context line; plus any deliberately promoted/adapted headings, e.g. `###`→`##` promotion, or a heading clause deliberately dropped). ANY other `+` line = a transcription error in a copied line — go fix it. Complementarily, `-` lines should only be the original `##`-level heading lines that were replaced.

Same trick verifies appends: if an appended line byte-matches its source line, it appears as diff CONTEXT (no `+`), e.g. a bullet appended to `user-memories.md` from source line 230 showed no `+` line containing it — only the new `##` heading did.

This works even though the diff of a ~300KB source vs an ~80KB extract is huge: the `grep '^+'` filter reduces output to a handful of short lines, staying under the 51200-byte bash output cap. Commands starting with `git diff` match the docs-writer allowlist (`git diff*`), including the pipe.

title: Truncated bash output: "full output saved to file" can be incomplete — check with wc -l
content:
Gotcha discovered 2026-09-02: when a bash command's output exceeds the cap (2000 lines / 51200 bytes), the tool message says "Full output saved to: /Users/vgoshev/.local/share/opencode/tool-output/tool_XXXX" — but the saved file may NOT be the full output. During a `grep -n '' docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md` dump (587 lines), the saved file contained only 383 lines (a head+tail stitched artifact of the truncated display, missing source lines ~385-587 entirely).

Consequence: slicing the saved file with further greps silently returns nothing for the missing ranges. ALWAYS verify the saved file's extent first with `wc -l <saved-file>` (wc is allowlisted), and re-fetch missing ranges directly from the source with anchored greps instead, e.g. `grep -n -A 16 '^## ChatSettingsPage' docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md` (an `-A N` after a unique anchor is a line-range selector substitute when sed is denied).

Related: individual lines are NOT truncated in bash tool output (a ~4.4K-char line displays fully) — the 2000-char truncation is a read-tool limit only. So for verbatim copying of long lines, small-batch `grep -n` with numeric-prefix patterns like `grep -E '^(29|3[0-9]|4[0-8]):' <dump-file>` is the reliable extraction path; keep each batch well under ~50KB.

title: Permission glob matches whole command string: pipes pass, `;`-chained non-allowlisted commands break the match
content:
Refinement of memory 140bc9e7 (docs-writer granular bash allowlist), observed 2026-09-02: the permission matcher evaluates the ENTIRE command string against each glob pattern, not just the first token.

- `git diff --no-index -U0 a b | grep '^+'` → ALLOWED. The `git diff*` glob matches the whole string including the pipe to grep (grep is itself allowlisted, but matching succeeded on the `git diff` prefix alone).
- `git diff ... | grep ...; printf 'x'` → DENIED. Appending a `;`-chained `printf` after an allowed prefix broke the match (printf is not allowlisted anywhere in the chain, and the matcher rejects the composite).

Practical rules: pipelines of allowlisted commands are fine; never append non-allowlisted commands with `;` or `&&`; there is no file-writing shell escape (no sed/awk/tee/redirect heredocs) — all writes must go through the write/edit tools, which is why the git-diff verification technique (see companion memory) matters for byte-exact doc extraction.

title: .opencode/memory.jsonl: hands-off, shows as modified in git status due to harness auto-management
content:
Confirmed 2026-09-02 during a docs-writer extraction task: `.opencode/memory.jsonl` shows as `M` (modified) in `git status` even when the agent never touched it — the opencode harness auto-appends to it during sessions. Standing rules for any agent doing repo work, especially doc-only tasks with a "changed files" acceptance criterion:

- NEVER read, edit, or stage `.opencode/memory.jsonl`.
- When using `git status --porcelain` to prove scope ("only my intended files changed"), expect `.opencode/memory.jsonl` to appear as modified and explicitly attribute it to harness auto-management — do not treat it as your own change and do not revert/stage it.
- Similarly check whether other dirty files (e.g. `TODO.md` was dirty this session) pre-date the task; attribute honestly in the final report rather than "cleaning them up".

`docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md` verification note: after an extraction pass that must leave it UNMODIFIED, its absence from the `git status --porcelain` output is the proof.

title: memories extraction: `](` grep hits inside inline code are false-positive links; make check-docs is the arbiter
content:
Complement to memory 7a4d0261 (memory-file preamble template): when extracting sections from `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md` into `docs/llm/memories/<slug>.md`, the task rule is "scan every copied line for relative markdown links and add one `../` (docs/llm/ → docs/llm/memories/)". A raw `\]\(` grep over the source produces FALSE POSITIVES that need no fix — `](` sequences inside inline code, e.g. the MarkdownV2 escape-set string `_*[]()~>#+-=|{}.!` and Python indexing like `STT_PROVIDERS_MAP[providerName](`. In the 2026-09-02 pass over 8 extraction ranges, zero genuine relative links existed; all path mentions were backticked inline code, which per the rules needs NO change.

Workflow: do the `\]\(` grep scan to know what *might* need fixing, judge each hit (inline code → skip), then let `make check-docs` arbitrate (it resolves actual link targets). Baseline after this pass: "Checked 137 markdown files, 3008 links; 0 broken." (129 files/2981 links before). Note `make check-docs` output line is the acceptance-citation format used by these tasks; do NOT run `make test` for docs-only extraction passes, and add NO CHANGELOG entry (internal docs maintenance, per docs/llm/changelog.md skip rules).

title: check-docs blind spot #2: dangling prose cross-references survive stub rewrites
content: Follow-up to memory f45ae885 (check-docs validates links only): the gate ALSO cannot see dangling PROSE cross-references. Concrete instance (2026-09-02, verification pass after the 8-file memory extraction): `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md` line 42 heading `## Max webhook receiver → lib extraction (opened 2026-08-25 — COMPLETE 2026-08-26; see "IMPLEMENTATION" bullets below for commit series)` retained the stale clause verbatim even though the IMPLEMENTATION bullets had been extracted into `memories/max-webhook-receiver-extraction.md` — the section body below is now only the stub pointer line, so the clause dangles. `make check-docs` passed clean (137 files / 3019 links / 0 broken) because the dangling reference is prose, not a markdown link. Fix belongs to the teamlead (hub file was off-limits for the doc-writer): drop the clause or repoint it at the commit-series content inside `memories/max-webhook-receiver-extraction.md`. Lesson: after any stub-extraction rewrite of teamlead-memory.md, grep the hub for prose phrases like "see ... below" / "bullets below" that reference relocated content.

title: Sentinel-grep verification protocol for teamlead-memory.md stub rewrites
content:
Verification protocol used (and expected by the teamlead) for the 2026-09-02 gate after rewriting `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md` to one-line stubs pointing at 8 new `docs/llm/memories/` files. Four checks:

1. `make check-docs` from repo root must report 0 broken.
2. **Sentinel residue check**: grep the hub file for exact sentinel phrases of relocated content (e.g. `httpx2 is REAL`, `Added retry to Telegram sends`, `STT mono/speaker enhancement`). Each must have ZERO matches in teamlead-memory.md, with ONE sanctioned exception class: phrases inside the `See [memories/<slug>.md]` stub pointer line itself (e.g. `PTBDeprecationWarning` allowed once at the Telegram Send Retry stub, line 36). A sentinel with zero matches ANYWHERE (even in the destination memory file) is still a PASS — relocation may rephrase; observed with `ChatSettingsPage IntEnum` (0 matches in all of docs/llm).
3. **Structure check**: each stub heading (`## lib/stats subsystem`, `## Telegram Send Retry`, `## lib/db extraction`, `## Max webhook receiver → lib extraction`, `## ChatSettingsPage System`, `## httpx vs httpx2 …`) exists exactly once and is immediately followed by a `See [memories/<slug>.md](memories/<slug>.md)` pointer line; kept sections (User Preferences, Task-Specific Memory Files, Repo Facts And Gotchas, Teamlead Workflow Lessons, Reviewing Large Changes) present with non-trivial content.
4. **Corruption spot-check**: long kept bullets must end with their exact known terminal phrases (e.g. freeze-requirements bullet → `` `freeze-requirements` = `pip freeze`. ``; rollbackTo bullet → "always use `rollbackTo(targetVersion=K)`."; CACHE-MUTATION GOTCHA → "augments a cache-returned dict."; getLikeComparison → `short-circuits to "no filter".`; Embedding trio = header + 3 complete sub-bullets).

Constraint set for such verification tasks: read-only except tiny fixes under `docs/llm/memories/**`; NEVER read/edit/stage `.opencode/memory.jsonl` or touch `.opencode/**` / `.agents/**`; do NOT run `make test` for doc-only gates; defects in the hub file (teamlead-memory.md) are REPORT-ONLY, never self-fixed. Result of this pass: everything clean except the line-42 dangling webhook heading clause (see companion gotcha memory).

title: opencode grep tool: file path in `path` param searches parent subtree
content: Environment gotcha observed 2026-09-02: the opencode `grep` tool's `path` parameter, when pointed at a single FILE (e.g. `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md`), effectively searched the whole parent-directory subtree — results included hits in `docs/llm/memories/*` files. Consequence: per-file match counts for residue checks must be derived by filtering tool results to the target file, not trusted from the path argument. When exact scoping matters (residue/corruption checks where "zero matches in file X" is a pass condition), either filter results manually by path or verify that the target file was actually within the searched scope before reporting counts.

title: Refine-memory two-phase dispatch ordering + byte-exactness verification recipe
content:
When running the teamlead-memory.md → memories/ refinement (refine-memory slashcommand), the dispatch ORDER is load-bearing:

1. **docs-writer creates the archive files from the INTACT teamlead-memory.md FIRST**, then teamlead stubs the main file, then docs-writer runs the final `make check-docs`. NEVER stub first: recovering verbatim section content from `git show HEAD:` is unreliable because teamlead-memory.md frequently has uncommitted changes. One docs-writer dispatch for ~8 file creations + index update + append fits its step budget fine when the work is mechanical copying from a source it reads itself (don't paste huge verbatim content into briefs — transcription risk).
2. Edit split: teamlead edits ONLY docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md (its sanctioned exception); docs-writer owns docs/llm/memories/**, index.md, and ALL `make check-docs` runs (teamlead has bash: deny).

Verification recipe proven in the 2026-09-02 run (8 files extracted, 587→~250 lines):
- **Byte-exactness**: `git diff --no-index -U0 <source section lines> <new file>` — the only `+` lines should be the intended header (H1 + context line).
- **Residue**: grep sentinel phrases of extracted content; must be 0 matches in the stubbed main file (matches allowed only inside stub pointer lines). Gotcha: sentinels copied from markdown must account for backticks inside the text — a backticked word inside the sentinel makes exact-match grep false-negative (the "ChatSettingsPage IntEnum" sentinel matched 0 because of surrounding backticks).
- **Structure**: each stub heading exists exactly once with a pointer line to memories/<slug>.md immediately after; all stub links resolve (check-docs).
- **Corruption**: after a full-file rewrite, spot-check that long KEPT lines still end at their expected terminal phrases (detects transcription slips).

title: Edit tool can't remove regions containing >2000-char truncated lines — full-file write + verification
content:
In opencode, the `read` tool truncates file lines at 2000 chars, and the `edit` tool requires the ENTIRE oldString to match exactly. Consequence: content regions containing any truncated long line CANNOT be removed or replaced via `edit` — you cannot reconstruct the exact oldString. Hit for real in the 2026-09-02 refine-memory run: teamlead-memory.md sections to be stubbed out contained many >2000-char lines, making edit-based removal impossible.

Right way: use full-file `write` to rewrite the whole file (feasible when the truncated lines all sit inside REMOVED regions and every KEPT line was read completely — check truncation markers first). Mitigate transcription risk with post-write verification: sentinel greps (extracted content must be 0 matches), structure check (each stub heading + pointer line present exactly once), and terminal-phrase spot checks of the longest kept lines. Have a follow-up subagent dispatch run these checks read-only plus `make check-docs`; it will catch defects a solo write silently introduces (in this run it caught one dangling heading clause).

title: Dangling heading cross-references after memory extraction — check-docs is blind to them
content:
After extracting a section out of docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md into memories/<slug>.md, headings that embed cross-reference clauses dangle silently — e.g. "see bullet above for final state" (httpx2 section) and "see \"IMPLEMENTATION\" bullets below for commit series" (max-webhook-receiver section). `make check-docs` cannot catch these (it validates link paths only, never prose references), and both were missed in the initial rewrite; a read-only verification dispatch flagged them.

Convention adopted (2026-09-02):
- Drop the dangling clause from the LIVE stub heading in teamlead-memory.md (keep the rest of the heading verbatim).
- Keep the heading fully verbatim in the ARCHIVE file only if the clause is still true there — the webhook archive file legitimately keeps "see IMPLEMENTATION bullets below" because those bullets were extracted into it.
- When relocating a `###` subsection standalone, promote it to `##` (formatting-only change, body verbatim — documented as a sanctioned deviation).
- Headingless orphan content (feature log with no `##` heading) gets an invented descriptive H1, e.g. `# Telegram Send Retry (TheBot._retryTelegramSend)`; state the deviation in the run summary.

Related archive-file conventions: new slug vs reuse — related-but-distinct arcs get SEPARATE files (precedent: `proxy.md` vs `proxy-lifecycle.md`, likewise `max-webhook-support.md` vs new `max-webhook-receiver-extraction.md`); reuse an existing slug only when the same subsystem is already covered (relevance-score bullet appended into existing `user-memories.md` with a dated `##` heading). Relative links inside moved content need one extra `../` — though in practice extracted memory content contains almost no markdown links (paths are inline code), so verify rather than assume.

title: Max bot exit hang root cause
content:
Investigation 2026-09-03 (bot hangs on Ctrl+C in Max mode):

PROVEN CHAIN:
1. httpx2 (Pydantic-org fork, external dep) uses truststore.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_CLIENT) as default verify=True context (httpx2/_config.py:40). truststore.SSLContext SUBCLASSES ssl.SSLContext.
2. httpcore2 AutoBackend uses AnyIOBackend even under asyncio; start_tls calls anyio.streams.tls.TLSStream.wrap.
3. anyio/streams/tls.py wrap(): `if type(ssl_context) is ssl.SSLContext` inline else `to_thread.run_sync(ssl_context.wrap_bio,...)` → because truststore is a subclass, EVERY HTTPS connection offloads wrap_bio to a single non-daemon "AnyIO worker thread" (11,059 times in the hung 11-day run; single WorkerThread instance, anyio 4.14.2 WorkerThread has NO daemon=True at _backends/_asyncio.py:990).
4. Worker cleanup = root_task.add_done_callback(worker.stop) → queue sentinel None → worker exits ONLY after current func returns. Production worker was mid-func blocked forever on a Python threading lock (macOS sample showed context_run → method_vectorcall_VARARGS_KEYWORDS → lock_PyThread_acquire_lock; exact line hidden by 3.14 JIT frame elision).
5. main() returned, cProfile dumped (logs/profile.2026-08-23_20-28-34.profile mtime 20:11 == Ctrl+C time), then _Py_Finalize → wait_for_thread_shutdown → threading._shutdown → ThreadHandle_join on the worker → INFINITE HANG. Process 6244 (killed later by failed lldb attach attempt).

KEY FACTS:
- atexit module handlers do NOT run before the join (empirically verified — repro_atexit_order.py hung in threading._shutdown:1583 without printing).
- threading._shutdown runs _threading_atexits callbacks (registered via threading._register_atexit, used by concurrent.futures) in REVERSE registration order BEFORE joining non-daemon threads → correct hook point for an exit guard.
- Idle anyio worker exits cleanly after root task completes (worker.stop sentinel) — local repro with httpx2 AsyncClient + example.com exited 0. Hang requires worker stuck mid-func.
- MaxBotClient with max-ca-bundle set passes plain ssl.SSLContext (inline branch); the 11k offloads came from other httpx2 clients (LLM providers etc.) with default verify=True.
- PID 6244 was run under `-m cProfile`; sample analysis (C stacks) in /var/folders/.../sample_6244.txt; profile analysis scripts repro_hang.py/analyze_profile*.py in same temp dir.

FIX DIRECTION: exit guard in main.py registered via threading._register_atexit at start of main() (runs after executor cleanup, before joins): grace-wait for live non-daemon threads, dump their stacks via sys._current_frames, warn, os._exit(0). No dependency/trust changes. Regression test via subprocess (stuck non-daemon thread + installed guard → must exit 0 within timeout). Follow-up to surface: truststore→anyio worker offload on every HTTPS conn (consider explicit plain ssl contexts for httpx2 clients).

title: Fixed: install-container.timeout-seconds config was dead — installRuntimeLibraries always used 600s default
content:
Fixed (2026-09-03): `installRuntimeLibraries()` (lib/sandbox/manager.py) had `timeoutSeconds: int = 600` as a method-parameter default and never read `installContainerConfig.timeoutSeconds` — the `[sandbox.runtimes.python.install-container] timeout-seconds` config key was dead (parsed at config.py:282, zero consumers). Both callers (`/sandbox install` handler internal/bot/common/handlers/sandbox.py, `scripts/sandbox_bootstrap.py`) omit the arg, so installs were always watchdog-killed at 600+60+1=661s. Discovered via docker inspect: ExitCode 137 with StartedAt→FinishedAt exactly 661.17s while other config overrides (memory-mb=8096, user=2012:2012) HAD applied.

Fix: signature now `timeoutSeconds: int | None = None`; ContainerSpec gets `timeoutSeconds if timeoutSeconds is not None else installContainerConfig.timeoutSeconds`. Explicit arg still wins. Regression tests: tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py::TestInstallRuntimeLibrariesTimeout (3 tests, mock backend, assert `runOneshot.await_args_list[0].kwargs["spec"].limits.timeoutSeconds`).

Still hardcoded (deliberately left): `_refreshPackageList` uses timeoutSeconds=300 for its list container (manager.py). Gotcha for future configs: when adding a config key that mirrors a method param, grep for consumers of the parsed field — a parsed-but-unread field is invisible until a timeout kill exposes it.

title: installRuntimeLibraries container leak fixed: remove on success, keep on failure for docker logs inspection
content:
FIXED (2026-09-03): installRuntimeLibraries container leak closed. Previously the install container was never removed by the caller on ANY outcome (violating the runOneshot caller-cleanup contract; containers lingered until recover() at next startup). Now (lib/sandbox/manager.py, after the success determination):
- Success → best-effort `removeContainer(outcome.containerId)` wrapped in try/except (removal failure logged, does not fail the install).
- Failure → container deliberately KEPT for post-mortem `docker logs <containerId>` inspection (user requirement); a warning logs the container id; GC reaps it per `sandbox.gc.orphan-container-retention-minutes` (default 10 min).

runOneshot cleanup contract (lib/sandbox/backends/docker.py) now honored by all three callers: runCode (nested try/finally), _refreshPackageList (removes its own list container, best-effort), installRuntimeLibraries (success-conditional). Regression tests: tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py::TestInstallRuntimeLibrariesContainerCleanup (3 tests: removed-on-success with distinct install/list container ids, kept-on-failure via assert_not_awaited, remove-failure non-fatal). Test gotcha: on the success path runOneshot is called TWICE (install + list refresh) — use AsyncMock(side_effect=[installOutcome, listOutcome]) with distinct containerIds, else removeContainer assertions are ambiguous.

title: Sandbox /sandbox update: upgrade plumbing exists end-to-end, unused by bot
content:
Exploration (2026-09-03) for the planned `/sandbox update` command (TODO.md:3 `- [ ] /sandbox update to update packages`):

**Upgrade plumbing already exists end-to-end but is never exercised by the bot:**
- `SandboxManager.installRuntimeLibraries(packages: Sequence[str], *, runtime: RuntimeName, upgrade: bool = False, timeoutSeconds: int | None = None) -> bool` — lib/sandbox/manager.py:904.
- `Runtime.installCommand(packages, *, upgrade: bool)` (runtimes/base.py:86-101) → `PythonRuntime.installCommand` appends `--upgrade` to `python -m pip install --target /sandbox/libs --no-cache-dir --no-input` (runtimes/python/runtime.py:114-115).
- ONLY caller passing `upgrade=True`: `scripts/sandbox_bootstrap.py --upgrade` (argparse flag lines 82-86, passed at line 180). `/sandbox install` handler (sandbox.py:1194) never passes it.
- No update-all / `pip list --outdated` / version-refresh logic anywhere. `_refreshPackageList` (manager.py:1289) only re-enumerates INSTALLED versions into packages.json.
- Adjacent unused refresh: `prepareRuntime(runtime, *, rebuildImage=False)` (manager.py:225) + `DockerBackend.ensureImage(..., rebuild=...)` — no production caller passes True. Rebuilding the install image does NOT touch the host-side lib pool.

**Ready-made design path:** update-all = `listRuntimeLibraries()` names → `installRuntimeLibraries(packages=[p.name for p in packages], runtime=RuntimeName.PYTHON, upgrade=True)`; per-package selection mirrors `/sandbox install` grammar (`/sandbox update [packages...]`, whitespace-split at sandbox.py:1184). Bare PEP 508 names pass `_validatePackageSpec` (manager.py:1264) + `PythonRuntime.validatePackageSpec` (packaging.requirements.Requirement, runtime.py:164-179).

**Constraints:** update must be owner-only like install (`isBotOwner` check at sandbox.py:1168) because the lib pool is global per-runtime (affects all chats); also gate on `_checkSandboxAccess` (sandbox.enabled + ALLOW_SANDBOX chat setting, sandbox.py:629-656); reuse `locks.poolLock(runtime, poolDir)` (fcntl) for cross-process safety; the 600s install-container timeout (`[sandbox.runtimes.python.install-container] timeout-seconds`) applies per invocation — may need revisiting for update-all.

title: Sandbox package state: host-side lib pool, no DB, installs global per-runtime
content:
Package-state model confirmed 2026-09-03 (relevant to any install/update work):

- Installed packages live in a HOST-side "library pool": `<sandbox.storage.root-dir>/runtimes/python/libs/` (default `/var/lib/gromozeka/sandbox/runtimes/python/libs`). Run containers mount it READ-ONLY at `/sandbox/libs` with `PYTHONPATH=/sandbox/libs`. This is why package state survives container restarts — containers are fully ephemeral one-shot (`DockerBackend.runOneshot`, always removed), never persistent.
- Metadata cache: `<root-dir>/meta/runtimes/python/packages.json` (lib/sandbox/metadata/filesystem.py:274-316), read by `listRuntimeLibraries` (manager.py:887-902); refreshed only after successful install or `recover()`. NO DB table — all sandbox metadata is filesystem JSON (TODO for DB MetadataStore at manager.py:168).
- The pool is GLOBAL per-runtime, shared by all chats/sessions → installs/upgrades affect every chat; that's why `/sandbox install` is owner-only.
- `[sandbox.bootstrap] starter-packages` (configs/00-defaults/sandbox.toml:64-74) is used ONLY by scripts/sandbox_bootstrap.py — NOT an install-time allowlist; any PEP 508 spec is accepted.
- Install container: image `gromozeka-sandbox-python:install` (Alpine + build-base), pool mounted rw, network bridge, writable rootfs, 1024 MB / 256 pids / 600s timeout, grace hardcoded 60 (manager.py:1000-1004). List container timeout hardcoded 300s (manager.py:1346).

Access control map: exactly two `@commandHandlerV2` commands — `/run` (alias `/python`, sandbox.py:658-667) and `/sandbox` (sandbox.py:847-855); both visibility={PRIVATE}, availableFor={DEFAULT}; no decorator-level tier/owner checks. Runtime checks: `_checkSandboxAccess` (sandbox.py:629-656) = sandboxEnabled + `ChatSettingsKey.ALLOW_SANDBOX` chat setting for ALL subcommands; install adds `isBotOwner` (sandbox.py:1168). Five LLM tools (constants.py:59-63: run_python, sandbox_list_files, sandbox_read_file, sandbox_send_file, sandbox_list_libraries) gated in 3 layers: registration-only-if-handler-constructed (handlers/manager.py:598), per-call sandboxEnabled+ALLOW_SANDBOX, and chat-time useTools filtering (llm_messages.py:288-297).

title: Sandbox gotchas: help-text drift, failure semantics, timeout clamps
content:
Gotchas found during 2026-09-03 sandbox exploration:

1. **Internal doc drift in handler**: the `/sandbox` decorator `helpMessage` (sandbox.py:850) and the usage text in `sandbox_command` (sandbox.py:886-893) still say `<files|read|status|install>` and OMIT the `packages` subcommand (dispatched at sandbox.py:912-913). When adding any new subcommand (e.g. `update`), update BOTH texts + docs/llm/sandbox.md §Bot Integration + docs/llm/handlers.md:46 + CHANGELOG.md. README.md documents NO sandbox commands at all.
2. **Failure semantics of install**: failed install containers are deliberately KEPT for `docker logs` post-mortem, GC reaps them after `orphan-container-retention-minutes = 10` (manager.py:1026-1041); successful ones are removed + `_refreshPackageList` runs best-effort.
3. **Validation/return contract**: `installRuntimeLibraries` returns `bool`; raises `InvalidPackageSpec` only when ALL specs fail; individual spec failures are logged and skipped (manager.py:947-966). `LibraryPoolLocked` propagates if the fcntl pool lock is held.
4. **Timeouts**: `ResourceLimits` clamps minimum run timeout to 30s (types.py:109-112); DockerBackend watchdog = `timeoutSeconds + timeoutGraceSeconds + 1` (backends/docker.py:276); run containers get inner coreutils `timeout -s TERM -k <grace>` wrapper AND backend watchdog (belt-and-suspenders).
5. **Recovery/lifecycle**: handler schedules one-time `SandboxManager.recover()` on first cron tick (kills managed containers, reconciles metadata, marks stale RUNNING as FAILED, refreshes package lists) then GC every 30 min (sandbox.py:211-230); `DO_EXIT` → `shutdown(cleanVolumes=False)` (sandbox.py:232-245).
6. **Decorator semantics** (internal/bot/models/command_handlers.py:125-158): `visibility` = where shown in help; `availableFor` = where actually allowed — they are independent sets.

title: /sandbox update design ratified — sandbox-update-v1.md
content: Design doc at docs/plans/sandbox-update-v1.md (2026-09-04). Status: Design — ratified 2026-09-03 (D1-D4 user-approved; D5-D7 resolved in doc). Key decisions: D5 helper DELIVERED BY MOUNT (lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/pool_remove_packages.py mounted ro at /sandbox/pool_remove_packages.py into the one-shot update container; host path derived Path(installDockerfile).parent/"pool_remove_packages.py" — NO new config keys; NOT baked into Dockerfile.install because prepareRuntime only builds missing images → baked copy silently diverges, and mounted file is lintable/importable/testable). D6 dedicated SandboxManager.updateRuntimeLibraries(packages: Sequence[str]|None, *, runtime, timeoutSeconds=None) -> LibraryUpdateResult (NOT a preRemove flag on installRuntimeLibraries; one container, one poolLock hold; failure keeps container, success removes + _refreshPackageList; LibraryPoolLocked propagates). D7 update-ALL is POOL-DRIVEN: helper --all enumerates *.dist-info in-container (avoids fragile host-side dist-info name parsing); packages.json only provides old-version baseline for diff + empty-pool check. Mechanism (ratified D1): RECORD-based pre-remove inside container (canonicalize PEP 503 both sides, resolve+relative_to jail vs pool root, missing RECORD → skip package), then ONE pip install of bare names (no --upgrade). Handler: _handleUpdateCommand mirrors _handleInstallCommand (isBotOwner + _checkSandboxAccess), no-arg = update all; fixes pre-existing help/usage drift (missing packages subcommand). New import LibraryPoolLocked in handler. Reply shows name old → new diff; in-flight-run hazard accepted (D3) and noted in reply. Tests: tests/lib/sandbox/runtimes/test_pool_remove_packages.py (new) + extend test_manager.py / test_python_runtime.py / tests/bot/test_sandbox.py. 3 phases for software-developer. TODO.md line 3 tracks. Verification NOTE: make lint / make check-docs NOT runnable from architect role (no command exec); all 15 relative link targets manually verified to exist; run both commands before merge.

title: pip install --target gotchas + sandbox update-container constraints
content:
Gotchas discovered while designing `/sandbox update` (docs/plans/sandbox-update-v1.md), applicable to any future pool/install work:

1. **Root cause of duplicate-package disease**: `pip install --target <dir> --upgrade` does NOT remove old versions — old `.dist-info` dirs accumulate alongside new ones → import-order nondeterminism (which dist-info Python sees first decides the version). This is why the ratified design (D1) does RECORD-based pre-remove inside the container instead of relying on pip. Never "fix" pool updates with `--upgrade` alone.

2. **Partial-failure honesty**: with pre-remove + one batched `pip install`, a mid-batch pip failure can leave packages REMOVED but NOT reinstalled (worse than duplicates). Accepted risk (owner-only op, no rollback machinery); reply text must tell the user to re-run update/install to restore.

3. **Docker file-bind footgun**: bind-mounting a single host file whose path doesn't exist at container-create time makes Docker silently create a DIRECTORY at the container path. Manager must pre-check the helper script exists host-side and raise `ConfigError` before building the ContainerSpec.

4. **`gromozeka-sandbox-python:install` (Alpine) lacks the `packaging` module** — any helper script mounted into a sandbox container must be STDLIB-ONLY (argparse/csv/pathlib/re/shutil/subprocess/sys). PEP 503 canonicalization is 3 lines of `re` (lowercase; runs of `-_.` → `-`) and PEP 508 name extraction is a small regex (`^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*`) — implement locally rather than importing packaging. The HOST venv does have `packaging` (PythonRuntime uses `packaging.requirements.Requirement` for validation).

5. **No shell in container commands**: the update helper runs pip itself via `subprocess.run(argv_list)`; the container command is a single argv (no `sh -c`, no quoting surface). Tradeoff: helper's pip flags duplicate `installCommand`'s — keep in sync via a host-side parity test (helper exports `PIP_INSTALL_ARGS`; compare against `PythonRuntime.installCommand`).

6. **Helper deletion safety rules** (same idiom as `resolveWorkspacePath` in lib/sandbox/storage.py): every RECORD-listed file resolved then `relative_to(poolRoot.resolve())` jail check; symlink escapes caught by resolve+jail; missing/unreadable RECORD → SKIP the whole package (never delete unaccounted files — correctness of deletion outranks dedup); delete files individually, `shutil.rmtree` the dist-info dir only after its own jail check.

title: docs/plans/ conventions: check-docs link rules for design docs
content:
Conventions for writing design/plan docs under docs/plans/ (learned writing sandbox-update-v1.md):

- House style: `# Plan: <title> v1` H1, then a status line like `Status: **Design — ratified <date>**` (or `**APPROVED**` / `**implemented**` per doc state), `Date:`, `Companion:` links; numbered `## N. Section` headings; `file.py:line` citations with `~` prefix for approximate lines; technical English; budget ~400 lines.
- Relative links from docs/plans/ to repo root use `../../` (e.g. `../../lib/sandbox/manager.py`); to docs/llm/ use `../llm/…`; sibling plan docs link bare (`python-sandboxing-v1.md`). Directory links are acceptable (precedent: `../../lib/` in python-sandboxing-v1.md) — check-docs resolves them.
- **check-docs gotcha**: every link TARGET must exist on disk. For files that are PLANNED but don't exist yet (e.g. a new helper script), use a plain code span — never a markdown link to a real file with mismatched text (a link labeled `pool_remove_packages.py` targeting `runtime.py` passes link resolution but misleads readers; a link whose target is the nonexistent planned file would FAIL check-docs).
- Design docs must follow AGENTS.md code rules in every snippet (camelCase, docstrings with Args:/Returns:, type hints, no Any).
- Verification habit: architect role cannot execute commands — manually verify all relative link targets (read/glob) and explicitly tell the user to run `make lint` + `make check-docs` before merge; do not run `make test` for docs-only changes.

title: Sandbox update v1 plan doc ratified in docs/plans/ (2026-09-04)
content: New ratified design doc `docs/plans/sandbox-update-v1.md` added 2026-09-04 ("Plan: `/sandbox update` — Sandbox Library Pool Updates v1"), companion to `docs/plans/python-sandboxing-v1.md` and tracking `TODO.md` item "/sandbox update to update packages". Scope: owner-only `/sandbox update [packages...]` subcommand updating the GLOBAL per-runtime Python pool (`runtimes/python/libs`, no DB; `packages.json` is derived metadata), with RECORD-based pre-remove of old versions and a before/after diff report; reuses the existing install-container machinery (same image, limits, `fcntl` pool lock, keep-container-on-failure semantics). Motivating gotcha documented in §1: `pip install --target ... --upgrade` does not remove old versions, so `installRuntimeLibraries(upgrade=True)` currently accumulates duplicate `.dist-info` dirs with nondeterministic import order — this is why the update path needs pre-remove. Note: per the docs/plans historical-record policy (memory 84cb5818), read implementation details from the doc itself; it is retained as a design reference, not kept in sync.

title: Chained bash commands (a && b) denied even when each part is individually allowlisted
content:
OpenCode's bash permission layer evaluates the ENTIRE command line as one string against the allowlist patterns — `&&`-chained commands are not decomposed into parts. Observed 2026-09-04 (docs-writer agent, one-line docs edit task): `git status && git diff HEAD` was DENIED even though both `git status*` and `git diff*` were individually in the agent's allowlist. The chained form matched no pattern, so the whole call was rejected.

Workaround: run each command as a separate tool call instead of chaining with `&&`. This extends the known exact-match rule (allowlist patterns match exactly unless they end with `*` — see related memory eefc752f): not only pipes/redirection suffixes but also command chaining breaks the match. When authoring `.opencode/agents/*.md` allowlists, remember that any prompt suggesting compound commands will fail unless a pattern explicitly matches the full chain.

title: /sandbox update design: D1 superseded by post-remove mechanism
content: docs/plans/sandbox-update-v1.md revised 2026-09-04: D1 (RECORD-based pre-remove) superseded by post-remove / upgrade-then-dedup, re-ratified by user. Helper renamed pool_remove_packages.py → pool_update_packages.py (container path /sandbox/pool_update_packages.py, constant UPDATE_HELPER_CONTAINER_PATH). Mechanism: snapshot dist-infos → pip install --upgrade (one invocation, only-if-needed strategy) → ALWAYS-run dedup deleting old RECORD − union(new RECORDs) → exit code = pip's. Motivation: pre-remove had holes-on-failure, wasteful full re-downloads (~100+ MB), and a dependency-induced duplicates bug. Load-bearing rule: set subtraction keeps same-path files (e.g. numpy/__init__.py) that were overwritten in-place. D2–D7 unchanged. Doc is 327 lines; implementation not started (3 phases in §14).
