title: Read-only quality-gate runs: report exit status/duration/exact failures, never auto-fix
content:
When the user asks for quality-gate verification runs (e.g. `make lint`, `make check-docs`), they may explicitly require read-only report-only mode: run the gates, do NOT edit/fix any files, and if a gate fails capture the exact failing output (file + line + message) verbatim for reporting. Complements the scoped read-only code-review preference (memory 1ada2082, 2026-07-28): the user routinely runs agents in verification-only mode where auto-fixing is out of scope unless requested.

title: Git commit style on master re-confirmed: imperative free-form, short bodies OK, drop suggested prefixes
content:
Re-confirmed 2026-09-04 from `git log --oneline -8` on master (prior confirmations 12da30a8 / 87455d7c were on other branches/dates): Gromozeka commit subjects are imperative-mood, capitalized, with NO conventional-commit prefixes. Fresh examples: 06299dc1 "Remove install container on success; keep it on failure for log inspection", 6333efd3 "Honor install-container timeout-seconds config in sandbox installs", 40edad4b "Fix Ctrl+C exit hang: guard against stranded non-daemon threads", 0c8b8e05 "Refine teamlead memory".

Two nuances beyond the earlier notes (12da30a8 said "no body"):
1. A short body line is acceptable when one commit bundles two concerns — commit 1cebcba9 used subject "Add /sandbox update design doc (post-remove mechanism)" + body "Also records teamlead-memory and session memory updates from this session." with no objection.
2. Real scenario: user suggested a conventional-commit-style message ("docs: add /sandbox update design doc ..."); correct behavior was to DROP the `docs:` prefix and keep the imperative subject, matching observed repo conventions. When a user's example message carries a type prefix, treat it as content guidance, not a style directive.

title: .opencode/memory.jsonl staging conflict resolved: hands-off = never read, not never commit
content:
Existing memories conflict on `.opencode/memory.jsonl` staging: 981fabf2 / dcd918fe / ada19995 say it "rides along" and is routinely committed, while fe5c8e74 (2026-08-23) claims it must never be staged and should be excluded via `git add -A -- ':(exclude).opencode/memory.jsonl'`.

Resolved 2026-09-04 by explicit user instruction in a commit-only task: ".opencode/memory.jsonl (auto-managed session memory — hands-off rule: never read/inspect its contents, just let it be staged as-is with the rest)". The file was explicitly included in `git add` and committed in 1cebcba9 (3 files, 351 insertions) with no problem.

Correct interpretation: hands-off means never READ/edit/inspect the file's contents; staging and committing it as-is is correct whenever it is part of the intended changeset (including when the user's explicit file list names it). The blanket "never stage / pathspec-exclude it" pattern from fe5c8e74 is wrong for such tasks. Also note the file can keep growing mid-session, so diff-stat insert counts for it are unstable (f9ec7d2c) — don't be surprised by drift between status checks.

title: sandbox-update Phase 1 implemented — lib/sandbox core complete
content:
Phase 1 of docs/plans/sandbox-update-v1.md was implemented (2026-09-04) and fully verified; Phases 2–3 remain.

Delivered:
- `lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/pool_update_packages.py` (NEW, ~422 lines): stdlib-only in-container helper implementing the four-step contract (snapshot dist-infos → pip via subprocess.run argv → always-run dedup → exit code = pip's). Exports `PIP_INSTALL_ARGS`, `canonicalizeName`, `extractSpecName`, `enumerateDistInfos`, `readRecordPaths`, `dedupPool`, `main`. Dist-info name comes from METADATA `Name:` header with dir-stem rpartition fallback (never hyphen-split alone — doc §6 fragility).
- `lib/sandbox/types.py`: `PackageUpdate(name, oldVersion, newVersion)`, `LibraryUpdateResult(runtime, success, updated, unchanged, failedSpecs, containerId, metadataRefreshed)`.
- `lib/sandbox/runtimes/base.py`: abstract `updateCommand(packages: Sequence[str] | None) -> list[str]`, `updateHelperHostPath() -> Path`, plus annotation-only `UPDATE_HELPER_CONTAINER_PATH: str` on the Runtime ABC (same pattern as `name: RuntimeName`) so SandboxManager reads it pyright-safely; the value lives only on PythonRuntime.
- `lib/sandbox/manager.py`: `SandboxManager.updateRuntimeLibraries(packages, *, runtime, timeoutSeconds=None) -> LibraryUpdateResult` + private `_snapshotPackageVersions` (keys canonicalized via `packaging.utils.canonicalize_name` — host-side where packaging exists). Flow mirrors installRuntimeLibraries: partial spec validation (failedSpecs; all-fail → InvalidPackageSpec before any container), before-snapshot from metadata, empty-pool no-arg early return, host-side helper pre-check → ConfigError, one poolLock hold, one ContainerSpec (labels sandbox.purpose="update", pool rw + helper file ro), keep-container-on-failure with containerId set, remove + best-effort _refreshPackageList on success, diff from before/after metadata reads.
- NO ContainerSpec/DockerBackend extension was needed (single-file bind works via generic mounts — see related memory).

Tests: `tests/lib/sandbox/runtimes/test_pool_update_packages.py` (NEW, 20 tests, fake pools from real files + hand-written RECORD/METADATA, pip monkeypatched and able to mutate the pool mid-"pip"), `test_python_runtime.py` +5 (argv shape, --all, host path, PIP parity), `test_manager.py` +11 (spec shape/labels/mounts, lock propagation, keep-on-failure, diff, early returns, ConfigError, timeout).

Verification: make format lint clean (flake8/isort/import-main/pyright 0 errors); make test 4472 passed / 11 skipped (~172s); §14 mutation checks confirmed (neutralizing jail check, canonicalization, or set-subtraction each turns the corresponding tests red; all reverted).

REMAINING: Phase 2 = internal/ handler wiring; Phase 3 = docs sync (docs/llm/*, CHANGELOG.md, TODO.md — deliberately untouched in Phase 1).

title: Single-file Docker bind mounts work via generic ContainerSpec.mounts — no backend extension
content:
`ContainerSpec.mounts` is a generic `list[dict[str, str]]` with keys hostPath/containerPath/mode, and `DockerBackend._specToContainerConfig` (lib/sandbox/backends/docker.py) renders each entry as a Binds-format string `hostPath:containerPath:mode` (the Binds format is itself required for Colima/macOS compatibility — see earlier memory). Docker accepts a single-FILE host path in Binds exactly like a directory.

Confirmed in practice (sandbox-update Phase 1, 2026-09-04): the update helper script is file-bound read-only into the one-shot container (`hostPath=<repo>/lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/pool_update_packages.py` → `containerPath=/sandbox/pool_update_packages.py`, mode `ro`) alongside the usual rw libs-dir mount, with zero changes to ContainerSpec or DockerBackend. Any future "bind one file into the sandbox container" need can reuse this pattern directly; do not extend the spec for it.

title: sandbox update: implementation judgment calls where the design doc left room
content:
Judgment calls made while implementing SandboxManager.updateRuntimeLibraries / pool_update_packages.py where docs/plans/sandbox-update-v1.md left room (not yet in project docs — docs sync is Phase 3):

1. `PIP_INSTALL_ARGS = ["install", "--no-cache-dir", "--no-input", "--upgrade"]` deliberately excludes the `python -m pip` executable prefix AND the `--target <dir>` pair (dir comes from runtime config). The parity test derives its expected list by stripping `installCommand(upgrade=True)` output itself, so drift on either side fails the test.
2. Dedup skips an entire canonical name when ANY involved RECORD is unreadable — including a NEW dist-info's RECORD, not just the old side the doc mandates. Rationale: "never delete what we cannot account for" cuts both ways; a partial union could delete shared files.
3. `packages=[]` (empty list, distinct from `None`="all") returns an immediate empty SUCCESS result with no container — mirrors install's empty-input no-op without the ambiguity of treating [] as "all".
4. The empty-pool no-arg early return sets `metadataRefreshed=False` (accurate: no refresh happened; there is no diff at all).
5. The helper warns on stderr when a named spec's canonical name is not in the snapshot — gives the doc §5.4 spec→name regex a real use; stderr never affects the exit code.
6. `pip install --target` ordering inside the helper reproduces installCommand's flag order (install, --target, dir, --no-cache-dir, --no-input, --upgrade) by inserting the target pair right after the "install" subcommand taken from PIP_INSTALL_ARGS.
7. Before-snapshot is taken BEFORE the empty-pool early return (doc §5.1 ordering; the brief ordered it after — followed the doc; costs one wasted metadata read on the early-return path).

title: Gotcha: file-write tool can drop the opening triple-quote of a new Python module
content:
While creating `lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/pool_update_packages.py`, the file-write tool stripped the module docstring's opening `"""` (the file started mid-docstring). Downstream symptoms were misleading: LSP reported dozens of "Statements must be separated by newlines" / "Expected \"in\"" errors, and `./venv/bin/python3` reported `SyntaxError: invalid character '—' (U+2014)` — the em-dash inside the docstring was only illegal because the parser saw it as code.

Lesson: when a freshly tool-written Python file produces a flood of tokenizer/LSP errors from line 1, first check that the file actually starts with its intended `"""` opener before hunting for a content bug. Verify with `./venv/bin/python3 -m py_compile <file>` (plus a `--help` run for CLI helpers) immediately after the write.

title: Gotcha: chmod 000 is not a reliable "unreadable file" simulation in tests (CI runs as root)
content: Do not simulate "unreadable file" in tests with `chmod 0o000`: tests running as root (e.g. `make ci` in the Alpine container) can read 0o000 files, so the test passes locally as a normal user but FAILS in root-run CI. Deterministic uid-independent alternative (used in `tests/lib/sandbox/runtimes/test_pool_update_packages.py` for the unreadable-RECORD case): replace the file with a DIRECTORY of the same name — attempts to `.open()` it raise `IsADirectoryError` (an OSError subclass) regardless of the effective uid, and no cleanup/permission-restore bookkeeping is needed.

title: Review findings on pool_update_packages.py: symlink-deletes-target wrinkle + untested dist-info jail branch
content:
2026-09-04 read-only code review of lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/pool_update_packages.py + tests/lib/sandbox/runtimes/test_pool_update_packages.py (baseline commit 1cebcba9, untracked files). Verdict: no blockers/majors; 4 minors + 4 nits. Findings NOT yet fixed as of review:

**Minor (code)**: File-entry deletion (~line 270) unlinks the RESOLVED path (`resolved.unlink(missing_ok=True)`). An old-only RECORD entry that is an in-pool symlink deletes its *target* instead of the link — worst case: old v1.0 ships symlink `x/link.py -> x/real.py`, v2.0 drops the link and ships a real file at `x/real.py` (so `x/real.py` ∈ newPaths) → dedup deletes the new install's file, the §9 corruption class via a different door. Asymmetric with the dist-info branch (lines 278-279) which correctly unlinks the link when `distInfoDir.is_symlink()`. Suggested fix: jail-check the resolved path as now, but unlink the unresolved candidate after verifying the candidate's *parent* resolves inside the pool (`candidate.parent.resolve().relative_to(poolRootResolved)`), falling back to resolved.unlink only for regular files.

**Minor (test gap, highest value)**: The dist-info-dir jail branch (lines 271-281, including symlinked-dist-info unlink) has ZERO coverage — all three jail tests (traversal/absolute/symlink at test lines 273/308/349) jail only RECORD file entries with real in-pool dirs, so deleting helper lines 271-277 fails no test. A symlinked `*.dist-info` pointing outside the pool is the only input that could steer `shutil.rmtree` outside — the highest-consequence branch. Fix: test with `evil-1.0.dist-info` as symlink to an outside dir (METADATA+RECORD there) gaining a real evil-2.0 this run; assert outside dir + dangling link survive + warning; plus inside-pool symlinked-dist-info variant asserting link-only removal.

**Minor (test gaps)**: UnicodeDecodeError/csv.Error degradation paths (helper lines 316, 328) untested — removing either from the except-tuples passes the suite; a non-UTF-8/malformed-CSV old RECORD would abort the whole dedup pass via main's catch-all instead of per-package skip. Also two-old-versions-plus-one-new (len(oldDirs)>1 WITH newDirs) untested — mutations like iterating only the first oldDir or dropping `missing_ok=True` survive.

**Nits**: dead `not resolved.is_symlink()` at line 264; `set(oldDirs)` rebuilt per current entry at line 303 (hoist); `--all` with empty snapshot (or named mode with zero specs) runs pip with zero requirements → pip usage-error exit becomes process exit (contract technically holds; host-side early return per §9 normally prevents); signal-killed pip returns negative returncode and `sys.exit(-9)` yields POSIX status 247, so "exit code = pip's" is literal only for 0-255.

**Deviations evaluated SOUND** (were self-reported): (1) dedup also skips on unreadable NEW record — subtracting against an incomplete union(new) would delete shared files and corrupt the new install, strictly worse than §9's forbidden blind-deletion; skipping keeps duplicates (safe degradation, per-name contained, exit code untouched; module docstring line 21 already covers both sides generically). (2) stderr warning when named spec absent from snapshot — informational only, pip still runs (pinned by testNamedSpecNotInstalledWarnsButStillRunsPip:757), suppressed when extractSpecName yields empty.

PIP_INSTALL_ARGS parity claim in helper docstring is asserted host-side in tests/lib/sandbox/runtimes/test_python_runtime.py:207-228.

title: pathlib gotchas: resolved.is_symlink() always False; symlink deletion deletes target; sys.exit(negative) maps to 256+n
content:
Gotchas verified during the pool_update_packages.py review (2026-09-04), applicable anywhere in the repo that does resolve-then-delete path handling:

1. `Path.resolve()` fully resolves symlinks, so on its output `is_symlink()` is ALWAYS False — any `resolved.is_dir() and not resolved.is_symlink()` style guard is dead code. To check "is the original path a symlink", test the UNRESOLVED path.
2. Unlinking a resolved path deletes the symlink's TARGET, not the link — leaves dangling links or, worse, deletes a file belonging to another component (e.g. the new install in the dedup case). Correct idiom for "jail then delete, preserving links": jail-check via `resolve()` for containment, but perform the unlink on the unresolved candidate after verifying the candidate's parent resolves inside the root (`candidate.parent.resolve().relative_to(rootResolved)`). Note pathlib join semantics: `Path("/pool") / "/abs"` → `Path("/abs")` (absolute operand replaces), so absolute RECORD entries bypass the join but are still caught by the `relative_to` jail.
3. Python ≥3.12 non-strict `Path.resolve()` (via posixpath.realpath) does NOT raise on symlink loops — it returns a partially-resolved path; older RuntimeError-on-loop behavior is unreachable on supported versions.
4. `sys.exit(negative_returncode)` (e.g. pip SIGKILLed → returncode −9) produces POSIX exit status 256−9=247, not −9 — "exit code equals child's" is literal only for 0-255; failure semantics (non-zero) still hold.

Jail idiom reference implementation: `resolveWorkspacePath` in lib/sandbox/storage.py (~lines 100-109): `resolve()` + `relative_to()`, catching `(OSError, ValueError)`.

title: Sandbox runtimes tests use flattened tests/lib/sandbox/runtimes/ path (no python/ level)
content: Convention confirmed 2026-09-04: tests for `lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/*.py` live FLATTENED at `tests/lib/sandbox/runtimes/test_*.py` — WITHOUT the extra `python/` directory level (e.g. `test_python_runtime.py` for `lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/runtime.py`, `test_pool_update_packages.py` for `lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/pool_update_packages.py`). The AGENTS.md mirror rule read strictly would suggest `tests/lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/test_pool_update_packages.py`, but the established sibling convention plus explicit ratification in docs/plans/sandbox-update-v1.md §12 fix the flattened path. New sandbox-runtime tests should follow the flattened layout, not the generic mirror rule.

title: _refreshPackageList ignores list-container outcome — can clobber packages.json with [] and claim metadataRefreshed=True
content:
Root cause (found in 2026-09-04 Phase 1 `/sandbox update` code review, fix still pending): `SandboxManager._refreshPackageList` (lib/sandbox/manager.py:1590-1608) never inspects the `ContainerOutcome` returned by the `pip list` `runOneshot` call. `PythonRuntime.parseListCommandOutput` (lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/runtime.py:176-203) deliberately ignores `outcome` (its docstring says "unused but part of protocol") and returns `[]` for empty stdout. So if the list container fails — non-zero exit, watchdog timeout (signal=SIGKILL), or empty stdout — the code still calls `savePackagesInfo(runtime, [])` (manager.py:1603), overwriting packages.json, and returns `True` (manager.py:1608) → `metadataRefreshed=True` on a corrupted baseline.

Impact: `updateRuntimeLibraries` treats packages.json as the before/after diff baseline, so one failed refresh makes every pool package report `updated (x → None)` ("vanished") with a True freshness flag — exactly the corruption mode the plan anticipated only for the *exception* path. The pool itself is unharmed and self-heals on the next successful refresh; `installRuntimeLibraries` shares the latent bug (blast radius there: blank `/sandbox packages` listing). Note `testSuccessRemovesContainerAndRefreshes` (tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py:686-704) exercises the empty-stdout→`[]` save path and asserts `metadataRefreshed is True` — it pins the corrupting behavior.

Fix: in `_refreshPackageList`, after `runOneshot`, gate before parse/save: `outcome.exitCode == 0 and outcome.signal is None and not outcome.oomKilled`, else log error and return False. The update path already assigns `metadataRefreshed = await self._refreshPackageList(...)` (manager.py:1238), so a False return flows through correctly. Pin with a regression test (mock outcome exitCode=1 → assert `metadataRefreshed=False` and packages.json untouched).

title: Sandbox update Phase 1 review: four spec deviations evaluated and accepted (with rationale)
content:
The 2026-09-04 Phase 1 code review of `/sandbox update` (manager/runtime/types, spec docs/plans/sandbox-update-v1.md) evaluated four implementation deviations from the ratified spec and accepted all four:

1. **Annotation-only ABC constant** `UPDATE_HELPER_CONTAINER_PATH: str` (lib/sandbox/runtimes/base.py:32-37, value set only in runtime.py:41-42) — mirrors the existing `name: RuntimeName` precedent (base.py:30); pyright-safe because the manager accesses it via the annotated base type (manager.py:1178); a future runtime that omits it fails loudly (AttributeError) on first update rather than silently mounting a wrong path. Abstractmethod-ing it would be wrong (data, not behavior).

2. **Before-snapshot taken outside poolLock** (snapshot at manager.py:1136, lock at manager.py:1159; also the empty-pool glob at manager.py:1140) — narrow race window; worst case is mis-attributed diff lines (render as "no prior version recorded", still truthful). Pool safety unaffected: pip + dedup + refresh all run inside the single lock hold. Same-process/cross-process competitors get LibraryPoolLocked immediately (non-blocking flock). Optional zero-cost hardening: take the before-snapshot just inside the `async with locks.poolLock(...)` block.

3. **Dedup skips the entire package when the NEW RECORD is unreadable** (lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/pool_update_packages.py:313-322, docstring 291-293) — correct and load-bearing: the subtraction set is the union of new RECORDs; a partially-read union makes `old − new` too large, so deleting per old RECORD could destroy files the new install owns. Extends the spec's old-RECORD rule in the only safe direction ("never delete what we cannot account for"). GAP: only the old-RECORD case is pinned in tests (tests/lib/sandbox/runtimes/test_pool_update_packages.py:478-514) — a new-RECORD-unreadable regression test is still needed (spec §12 only lists the old-RECORD case).

4. **Helper warns on stderr when a named spec is absent from its own snapshot** (pool_update_packages.py:398-404) — accepted: stderr-only, cannot affect the exit code (Step 4 contract), improves `docker logs` triage, consistent with spec §9 row 3 (pip installs fresh).

title: Sandbox gotchas: flock is per-fd (same-process lock tests work), Path.glob on missing dir is safe, runOneshot timeout/GC contract
content:
Three verified facts from the 2026-09-04 `/sandbox update` Phase 1 review that are easy to get wrong:

1. **flock exclusivity is per open-file-description, not per process.** Pre-holding the sandbox pool lock in the same test process via a separate `open()` on `poolDir/pool.lock` correctly makes a second LOCK_NB acquisition raise `LibraryPoolLocked` — this is the realistic technique in `testLibraryPoolLockedPropagates` (tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py). Do not assume flock is per-process and "can't be tested in-process".

2. **`Path.glob` on a nonexistent directory yields empty; it does not raise.** The manager's empty-pool check `libsDir.glob("*.dist-info")` is safe with no `is_dir()` guard (updateRuntimeLibraries early-return path).

3. **DockerBackend.runOneshot lifecycle contract:** it removes the container itself if it raises (no leak on backend errors, docker.py:320-327), but on the watchdog timeout path it *returns* an outcome with `signal="SIGKILL"` (docker.py:300-306) and leaves the container for the caller. Hence the manager's success predicate `all([not oomKilled, signal is None, exitCode == 0])` (identical for install and update) and keep-container-on-failure semantics; kept containers carry `sandbox.managed=true` and no active runId, so the GC orphan reaper collects them after `orphanContainerRetentionMinutes` (gc.py:186-203).

title: Phase 1 /sandbox update review: NEEDS-FIXES verdict — 3 majors, 4 minors
content:
Review 2026-09-04 of uncommitted Phase 1 `/sandbox update` files (baseline commit 1cebcba9) vs docs/plans/sandbox-update-v1.md, by code-reviewer agent. Baseline verification green: `make lint` clean (pyright 0 errors), `make test` 4472 passed / 11 skipped, Phase 1 tests 66 passed. Verdict: NEEDS-FIXES — majors 1–3 before Phase 1 acceptance.

MAJORS:
1. pip argument injection from pool metadata in --all mode (lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/pool_update_packages.py:139-146,342-355,394-407): METADATA `Name:` canonicalized (PEP 503) but not validated; `-`-leading / absolute-path names flow verbatim into pip argv as options. Fix BOTH: validate snapshot keys against `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$` (skip+warn) AND insert `"--"` before `cmd.extend(specs)` in buildPipCommand. (See dedicated memory for the verified exploitation chain.)
2. `_refreshPackageList` ignores container outcome (lib/sandbox/manager.py:1547-1608): failed list run saves empty packages.json and returns True → update diff reports every package vanished with metadataRefreshed=True. Fix: gate on exitCode==0 && signal is None && !oomKilled before parse/save, return False on failure (update path already flows False through manager.py:1238). (See dedicated memory.)
3. Version snapshots outside poolLock (manager.py:1136 beforeVersions + empty-pool check BEFORE lock; after-snapshot at :1246 AFTER release): another install/update can interleave → returned diff includes foreign changes or stale baseline (the mutation itself IS serialized). Fix: move before-snapshot + empty-pool check inside `async with locks.poolLock(...)`, take after-snapshot before release; diff computation may stay outside using captured dicts. Add concurrency regression test.

MINORS:
4. RECORD symlink deleted via resolved target (pool_update_packages.py:255-270): old-only symlink entry unlinks the TARGET → can delete new-install file, leaves dangling link. Fix: jail-check resolved but `unlink()` the unresolved candidate when candidate.is_symlink() (jail the link's parent); asymmetric with dist-info branch :278-279 which already unlinks the link. (See dedicated jail-idiom memory.)
5. RECORD subtraction compares raw strings while deletion uses resolved identity (readRecordPaths :210-218): `./pkg/x.py` vs `pkg/x.py` alias → shared file deleted from malformed old RECORD. Fix: symmetric `posixpath.normpath` in readRecordPaths. (See dedicated pip-internals memory.)
6. `PackageUpdate` / `LibraryUpdateResult` NOT re-exported from lib/sandbox/__init__.py:94-166 (`.types` import block + `__all__`), unlike every other public sandbox type.
7. Missing mutation-sensitive tests: (a) dist-info-dir symlink-escape jail branch (deleting :271-277 shutil.rmtree jail passes suite today — highest-consequence untested branch); (b) unreadable NEW RECORD skip (:313-322 = deviation #3); (c) UnicodeDecodeError/csv.Error per-package containment (mutation-fragile except-tuples); (d) two-old-versions-plus-one-new dedup shape (len(oldDirs)>1 WITH newDirs); (e) update-container timeout config fallback (install side pins both, update pins only override); (f) empty-named-list early-return branch (metadataRefreshed=False overstated — cosmetic).

CLEAN (no findings): no shell anywhere (argv lists); RECORD-entry jail rejects traversal/absolute/symlink-escape correctly; set-subtraction semantics right (shared survive, old-only deleted, break-on-unreadable-old); dedup runs after pip failure + exit code passthrough exact; ContainerSpec parity with install (purpose="update", helper ro-mount, libs rw); shared pool.lock file makes install/update mutually exclusive cross-process; keep-container-on-failure containers carry sandbox.managed=true and are reaped by orphan GC (gc.py:186-203); conventions fully compliant (camelCase, docstrings Args/Returns, type hints, no Any, imports top, ≤120 cols).

DEVIATION ASSESSMENTS (from spec §14 self-reports): annotation-only UPDATE_HELPER_CONTAINER_PATH on base Runtime — ACCEPT (mirrors `name: RuntimeName` precedent, base.py:30-37; it's data not behavior; a ClassVar[str] would be marginally better); skip-on-unreadable-NEW-RECORD — SOUND and load-bearing (incomplete union inflates old−new set → could delete new-owned files); stderr warning for named spec absent — SOUND (informational, exit code untouched); before-snapshot ordering — NOT sound under concurrency → became major 3.

title: pip argv injection via METADATA Name in /sandbox update all — verified chain + fix
content:
Major finding from Phase 1 review 2026-09-04, verified against pip 26.2.1 + CPython 3.14 optparse in the repo venv (NOT assumed):

CHAIN: in `pool_update_packages.py` --all mode, snapshot keys (canonical names from dist-info METADATA `Name:` header, taken with .strip()) flow verbatim into pip argv (`specs = sorted(snapshot.keys())` → `cmd.extend(specs)` → `subprocess.run(argv)`). Hostile names survive PEP 503 canonicalization (`[-_.]+ → -` + lower only): `Name: -r` stays `-r`, `Name: /sandbox/libs/pwn` stays absolute.
- pip's optparse has `allow_interspersed_args = True` (optparse.py:1184); pip's CustomOptionParser/ConfigOptionParser never override `_process_args`; a bare `-r` element consumes the NEXT argv element as its value (`_process_short_opts`).
- Gadget is deterministic: `sorted()` puts `-` (0x2D) before `/` (0x2F) before alphanumerics, so planted `-r` + `/sandbox/libs/pwn` are adjacent and precede all real names → `pip install --target /sandbox/libs … -r /sandbox/libs/pwn numpy …` = attacker requirements file (direct-URL sdists → arbitrary build code; update container has network bridge) or `-i <url>` = whole-batch index hijack.
- Planting needs NO install-time code execution (passive wheel): pip's wheel path NEVER compares METADATA `Name:` header to the request — filename/version only (wheel_builder.py:92-99), dist-info DIR name startswith(canonical) (utils/wheel.py:57-62), no Name check anywhere incl. PEP 658 shallow-metadata path (_dists.py:119-143). Extra dist-info dirs plant via wheel `.data/purelib/<path>` entries copied verbatim into the scheme dir = the pool itself under `--target` (operations/install/wheel.py:510-564); the multiple-dist-info rejection only inspects top-level. `enumerateDistInfos` also follows dir symlinks (jail exists only on the deletion path).
- Named mode NOT exposed: `_validatePackageSpec` (manager.py:1505-1512) rejects `-`-leading specs/metacharacters host-side; pool names used there only for advisory comparison.
- `--` IS supported (verified, not assumed): stdlib optparse treats bare `--` as end-of-options (optparse.py:1412-1414); pip doesn't interfere; placement trivially right since all options precede specs in buildPipCommand.

SEVERITY calibration: major, not blocker (requires a prior owner-gated install of a hostile package; sandbox model already accepts untrusted in-container code writing the rw pool; no host boundary crossed) — but it violates python-sandboxing-v1.md:718 "reject `-`-leading specs pre-parse" via pool names, trigger is the routine `update all`, payoff is code-exec in the update container.

FIXES (both cheap, do both, version-independent): (1) `"--"` before `cmd.extend(specs)` in buildPipCommand (:352-356) — prevents option parsing but not absolute/local-path requirements, hence also (2) filter --all snapshot keys to `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$` with skip+warn (real PEP 503 names can never violate this). Optionally also skip symlinked dist-info entries in enumerateDistInfos to align enumeration with the deletion-path jail posture. Regression tests: plant dist-info with `Name: -i` / `Name: /x`, assert argv contains `--` before specs / no option-consumable token. Caveat: container image pins its OWN pip from Dockerfile.install — reconfirm pip's leniency there, but the fixes don't depend on it.

Cosmetic aside: `entry.name` printed to stderr (:182) — POSIX filenames may contain `\n` → trivial stderr log-injection, nit.

title: pip RECORD phantom rows & non-normalized alias paths (gotcha)
content:
Verified against pip 26.2.1 source + the wheel spec (packaging.python.org "Binary distribution format") during Phase 1 review 2026-09-04:

- The wheel spec does NOT require normalized RECORD/archive member paths — `./`, `//`, `a/../b` spellings are permitted; normalization is a pip implementation property, not a standard guarantee.
- pip REGENERATES the installed RECORD (not copied): rows seeded from the embedded RECORD via `get_csv_rows_for_installed`, real files recorded via `_fs_to_record_path` = `os.path.relpath` with separators folded. THE LEAK: `installed.pop(old_record_path, old_record_path)` (operations/install/wheel.py:246) keeps the embedded RECORD's RAW STRING for any row that does not correspond to an installed file → "phantom rows" from a malformed/buggy build backend. pip only warns on >3-field rows; doesn't reject.
- pip writes archive members as REGULAR files — in-wheel symlinks are NOT recreated (the file's content becomes the target string). An in-pool symlink dir is necessarily planted/external, never pip-produced.
- Consequence for `pool_update_packages.py` dedup: raw-string set subtraction while deletion uses resolved identity → old phantom row `./pkg/x.py` vs new `pkg/x.py` alias to the same file → shared (new-owned) file deleted. Aliasing grants NO new adversarial capability (direct path naming already passes the jail) but is real for the non-adversarial malformed-wheel path.
- FIX at the single choke point `readRecordPaths` (:210-218): `paths.add(posixpath.normpath(first))` — applied to BOTH sides since snapshot-time and current-time reads share the function → merges aliases; the deletion set can only SHRINK (fail-safe). Do NOT drop weird rows on the new side (reclassifying a shared file as old-only reintroduces the bug); do NOT resolve paths at subtraction time (collapses link/x.py vs real/x.py into exactly the wrong merge). `..`-escape/absolute rows normalize to escape-shaped strings and remain caught by the deletion jail.
- Mutation-sensitive tests to add (all fail against current code): old `./pkg/shared.py` vs new `pkg/shared.py` → shared survives; variants with `pkg//shared.py` and `pkg/../pkg/shared.py`; pip-faithful phantom construction (old RECORD row with no payload file, new RECORD real file → survives). Current `_makeDistInfo` test helper (:26-67) only writes verbatim canonical paths.
- Caveat: pip-version-scoped (writer chain above is 26.2.1); container image pins its own pip via Dockerfile.install — reconfirm there if the phantom-row claim must hold for the deployed image.

title: _refreshPackageList ignores run outcome — empty packages.json saved and reported as success
content:
Root cause (Phase 1 review 2026-09-04, lib/sandbox/manager.py:1547-1608): the `runOneshot` outcome is obtained (:1588) but NEVER inspected — `exitCode` / `signal` / `oomKilled` unchecked. Downstream enabler: lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/runtime.py:176-203 `parseListCommandOutput` deliberately ignores the outcome ("unused but part of protocol" per its own docstring) and `if not stdout: return ret` yields `[]`. So a failed / timed-out / empty-stdout pip-list container still triggers `savePackagesInfo(runtime, [])` (:1603) and returns `True` (:1608).

NEW blast radius since `updateRuntimeLibraries` (Phase 1): the post-run snapshot reads the emptied packages.json → `afterVersions = {}` → EVERY pool package reported as `updated (x → None)` i.e. "vanished", with `metadataRefreshed=True` — silently violating the flag semantics in types.py:407-409. This is the corruption mode the plan §9 anticipated only for the exception path; this failure is a normal return, not an exception. The pool itself is unharmed and self-heals on next successful refresh; the code predates Phase 1 (install shares it, where the blast radius was just a blank `/sandbox packages` listing) — but `updateRuntimeLibraries` is the first consumer treating packages.json as a diff baseline, making this load-bearing.

FIX: after `runOneshot`, gate before parsing/saving:
`listOk = outcome.exitCode == 0 and outcome.signal is None and not outcome.oomKilled`; on failure log + return False (keep previous metadata). The update path already assigns `metadataRefreshed = await self._refreshPackageList(...)` (manager.py:1238), so False flows through correctly. Non-empty-but-partial stdout on a failed run is also covered by gating.

REGRESSION TEST gotcha: current `testSuccessRemovesContainerAndRefreshes` (tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py:686-704) actually exercises the empty-stdout → `[]` save path and asserts `metadataRefreshed is True` — it PINS the corrupting behavior and must be updated alongside the fix. New test: mock outcome `exitCode=1` → assert `metadataRefreshed is False` and packages.json untouched.

Related existing memories: dba0a633 (try/except around the call — exception path only, distinct gap), 83b10649 (container-launch discovery — still accurate), 52261eaa (container cleanup failure non-fatal — still accurate).

title: Jail idiom gotcha: unlink resolved path deletes symlink TARGET, not the link
content:
The lib/sandbox jail idiom (`_resolveJailed`: `target.resolve()` + `resolved.relative_to(poolRootResolved)`, mirroring lib/sandbox/storage.py:100-109) VALIDATES containment correctly — it rejects `../..` traversal, absolute RECORD entries (pathlib operand replacement turns `(poolRoot) / "/abs"` into `/abs`), and outside-pointing symlinks — but it RETURNS the fully-resolved path. Unlinking that deletes the symlink's TARGET, not the link.

In pool_update_packages.py:255-270, an old-only RECORD entry that is a symlink gets `resolved.unlink(missing_ok=True)` → deletes the target file and leaves a dangling link. Worst case: old v1.0 ships `x/link.py → x/real.py`; v2.0 drops the link and ships a regular `x/real.py` (so `x/real.py` ∈ new RECORD) → `old − new = {"x/link.py"}` → resolving lands on the new install's file → deleted. This is the exact §9 corruption class ("deleting per old RECORD blindly would corrupt it") via a different door. Note the asymmetry: the dist-info branch (:278-279) correctly unlinks the LINK when `distInfoDir.is_symlink()`.

FIX: jail-check the resolved path as now, but `unlink()` the unresolved candidate when `candidate.is_symlink()` — guard by jailing the link's PARENT (`candidate.parent.resolve().relative_to(poolRootResolved)`); fall back to `resolved.unlink(missing_ok=True)` only for regular files. Also nit: `not resolved.is_symlink()` at :264 is dead code (output of resolve() is never a symlink) and advertises intent the code doesn't implement.

Related sound-decision assessments from the same review (keep as-is): (1) annotation-only `UPDATE_HELPER_CONTAINER_PATH` on base Runtime mirrors the existing `name: RuntimeName` precedent (base.py:30) — data not behavior, an @abstractmethod would be wrong, ClassVar[str] marginally better; (2) skip-package-on-unreadable-NEW-RECORD (:313-322) is LOAD-BEARING: with an incomplete union(new RECORDs) the `old − new` set is too large and could delete new-owned files — skipping the whole canonical name is the only safe direction of the "never delete what we cannot account for" invariant; it must be pinned by a test (currently unpinned); (3) stderr warning for named spec absent from snapshot is informational-only (pip still runs, exit code untouched).

title: _refreshPackageList parse failure wipes packages.json silently (review finding, Major)
content:
Major review finding from the 2026-09-04 `/sandbox update` Phase 1 review (unfixed at review time). A list container that **exits 0 with malformed stdout** silently wipes pool metadata and reports success:

- `SandboxManager._refreshPackageList` (lib/sandbox/manager.py:1628-1629) unconditionally calls `savePackagesInfo(...)` with whatever `parseListCommandOutput` returns, and returns True on the `refreshOk` path — it only guards on the container outcome (`refreshOk`, manager.py:1603-1626), never on parse success.
- `PythonRuntime.parseListCommandOutput` (lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/runtime.py:200-202) catches ONLY `json.JSONDecodeError` and returns `[]`; runtime.py:192-194 also returns `[]` for non-list JSON; runtime.py:196-198 silently SKIPS non-dict elements → partial wipe.
- Result: `packages.json` overwritten with `[]` (or a partial list) AND `metadataRefreshed=True` returned — violating the method's own documented contract at manager.py:1540-1543 ("in failure cases the existing packages.json metadata is preserved untouched"). This re-opens, via the parse path, the exact silent-wipe bug class the `refreshOk` outcome guard was added to fix.
- Impact chain: `runCode`'s required-package gate (manager.py:557-562) compares required packages against `listRuntimeLibraries()` metadata → after a wipe, every run with required packages raises `MissingDependenciesError`; the next `updateRuntimeLibraries` diff reports every package as `old=X → new=None` (mass removals).
- Proposed fix (one line): make `parseListCommandOutput` raise on JSON decode / non-list output instead of returning `[]`, so the existing exception path (manager.py:1241-1246, 1608-1626) preserves metadata and reports `metadataRefreshed=False`.

title: _refreshPackageList caller map: recover() is the only caller without the pool lock
content:
From the 2026-09-04 `/sandbox update` Phase 1 review. `_refreshPackageList(runtime, libsDir) -> bool` has exactly THREE call sites, with differing lock discipline:

1. `installRuntimeLibraries` — manager.py:1052, INSIDE `locks.poolLock`; return value ignored and the call wrapped in try/except that swallows exceptions (manager.py:1050-1057), so install returns True even when refresh fails (pinned by `testInstallSucceedsEvenWhenListRefreshFails`, tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py:877).
2. `updateRuntimeLibraries` — manager.py:1240, INSIDE `locks.poolLock`; return value becomes `LibraryUpdateResult.metadataRefreshed`; a raised exception is caught → False (manager.py:1241-1246).
3. `recover()` — manager.py:1440, **NO pool lock** — the only lock-free caller (Minor finding, unfixed at review time). Distinct from the known session-lock asymmetry (recover skips the session lock registry too): here the cross-process `fcntl.flock` pool lock is skipped, so recover's list container can run while another process/task holds the flock mid-install — reading a torn pool and writing a packages.json that reflects no committed state, and poisoning an in-flight update's after-snapshot (manager.py:1251), which is exactly the corruption the Step 3/Step 5 snapshot-inside-lock invariants (manager.py:1144-1147, 1248-1251) prevent for lock holders. recover() is runtime-triggerable from the sandbox delayed-task cron's first tick (internal/bot/common/handlers/sandbox.py:211-217), not purely a pre-serving startup path. Proposed fix: wrap manager.py:1437-1440 in `async with locks.poolLock(name, poolDir)`.

Install-path regression check (review conclusion): the change of `_refreshPackageList` to return False + preserve packages.json on container failure is safe for all callers — signature/return shape unchanged, install ignores the bool, recover ignores it, only update consumes it.

Context: `updateRuntimeLibraries` had NO production caller as of 2026-09-04 (tests only) — don't waste time hunting for a handler call site when tracing.

title: updateRuntimeLibraries snapshot/diff design + failure-path misleading diff (review findings)
content:
From the 2026-09-04 `/sandbox update` Phase 1 review of `SandboxManager.updateRuntimeLibraries` (lib/sandbox/manager.py:1061-1274):

**Snapshot/diff design (correct):** before-snapshot, list-refresh, and after-snapshot all run INSIDE `locks.poolLock` (manager.py:1147, 1240, 1251); the old→new diff is computed OUTSIDE the lock from the point-in-time dicts (manager.py:1253-1264), so a pool operation acquiring the lock right after cannot leak into the diff. Diff keys are canonicalized package names (`canonicalize_name`) via `_snapshotPackageVersions`; `updated` is sorted by canonical name; `unchanged` = identical old/new versions. `testConcurrentOperationBetweenSnapshotPointsDoesNotCorruptDiff` (test_manager.py:902) legitimately exercises this by monkeypatching `sandboxLocks.poolLock` — works because manager.py binds the module (`from . import locks`) and resolves `locks.poolLock` at call time.

**Gotcha — failure-path diff is misleading (Minor, unfixed at review time):** the after-snapshot (manager.py:1251) runs even when `success is False`, but `_refreshPackageList` was skipped, so afterVersions == beforeVersions and the result reports `updated=[]` + `unchanged=[entire pool]` with `success=False` — while a killed pip run may have partially mutated the pool. `LibraryUpdateResult.metadataRefreshed`'s doc (lib/sandbox/types.py:407-409) only covers the success case, inviting callers to read `unchanged` as fact. Fix: skip snapshot/diff when `not success`, or document the diff as meaningful only when `success=True`.

**Nits (unfixed at review time):** (1) the list container's timeout is hard-coded `timeoutSeconds=300` at manager.py:1582, unlike install/update which honor `install-container.timeout-seconds` + caller override (manager.py:1005-1007, 1191-1193); (2) `TestUpdateRuntimeLibraries` has no analog of `testInstallRemoveFailureDoesNotFailInstall` (test_manager.py:510-536) pinning best-effort `removeContainer`-failure tolerance on the update path (manager.py:1222-1225), so a regression there would go uncaught.

**Verified correct:** update keeps a failed update container and reports its `containerId` (manager.py:1226-1235); failed list containers are always removed and tmp stdout/stderr files unlinked on both refresh paths (manager.py:1618-1623); named-but-empty request returns success with `metadataRefreshed=False` before the lock (manager.py:1102-1111); empty-pool `--all` early return fires inside the lock without backend call (manager.py:1151-1160).

title: CORRECTION: Path.resolve() raises RuntimeError on symlink loops on Python ≤3.12, both strict modes
content:
Corrects item 3 of memory 6a9d3f95 ("pathlib gotchas"), which wrongly claims "Python ≥3.12 non-strict Path.resolve() does NOT raise on symlink loops — older RuntimeError-on-loop behavior is unreachable on supported versions."

Verified 2026-09-04 via CPython gh-109187 (opened by barneygale, fixed in 3.13) + docs.python.org 3.13 pathlib changelog:

- On Python ≤ 3.12, `Path.resolve()` raises **RuntimeError** on symlink loops in BOTH strict modes — strict=False included. gh-109187: "resolve(strict=True) raises RuntimeError rather than OSError" (backwards-compat quirk since bpo-#25264 made pathlib delegate to os.path.realpath), and "resolve(strict=False) suppresses every kind of OS error EXCEPT symlink loop errors".
- Changed in 3.13: strict mode raises OSError(ELOOP); non-strict mode raises NOTHING — it silently returns a partially-resolved (loop-terminated) path.

Consequence for the repo's jail idiom (`except (OSError, ValueError)` around resolve(), e.g. `_resolveJailed` in lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/pool_update_packages.py:270 and `resolveWorkspacePath` in lib/sandbox/storage.py:100-109): a planted symlink loop on a candidate path LEAKS RuntimeError on the repo's target py312, escaping the jail helper. Fix pattern: `except (OSError, ValueError, RuntimeError)` — harmless on 3.13+ where the loop is either OSError (strict) or already silent (non-strict).

The prior memory's claim was probably tested on a 3.13+ interpreter mislabeled as 3.12. Safety note: on 3.13+ non-strict the silently-partially-resolved path is still passed through the relative_to() jail check, so containment holds on all versions — only the abort-vs-continue behavior differs.

title: pool_update_packages.py security review: 2 minors + 4 nits (unfixed at review time); prior NEEDS-FIXES items confirmed fixed
content:
Read-only security review 2026-09-04 (code-analyst role) of lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/pool_update_packages.py + tests/lib/sandbox/runtimes/test_pool_update_packages.py as uncommitted Phase-1 working-tree code. Findings were reported but NOT fixed in-session — re-verify current state before relying.

MINOR 1 — pool_update_packages.py:270: `_resolveJailed` except tuple `(OSError, ValueError)` misses RuntimeError. On py≤3.12 (repo target) `Path.resolve()` raises RuntimeError on symlink loops (see correction memory on pathlib). Static planted content — `pool/l → pool/l` self-link plus old RECORD entry `l/x.py`, or a looped dist-info dir at :311 — aborts the ENTIRE dedup pass: no per-dir catch in dedupPool's loop (:378-379); only main's catch-all (:473) contains it, fail-closed, pip exit code preserved. Fix: add RuntimeError to the tuple.

MINOR 2 — :440-466: `--all` with zero names surviving `isValidCanonicalName` (the all-hostile-pool case the filter exists for) still invokes pip (:466) → pip fails "You must give at least one requirement", non-zero exit, container marked failed/kept. Host-side empty-pool early return (`any(libsDir.glob("*.dist-info"))`, docs/plans/sandbox-update-v1.md ~:211/:248) only covers zero-dist-info pools, not all-hostile-name pools. Fix: `if not specs: return EXIT_SUCCESS` after the filter (warnings already on stderr).

NIT 3 — :289-321 TOCTOU at deletion: jail is check-then-use — `_resolveJailed` validates a resolved snapshot, then deletion re-traverses the original path (candidate.unlink :302, resolved.unlink :310, distInfoDir.unlink/rmtree :318-321). A concurrent in-pool component swap could redirect deletion outside the jail (shutil.rmtree fails closed on a swapped symlink dir; unlink does not). No concurrent writer exists in the one-shot-container threat model and static planted content IS fully handled by resolve+relative_to, so defense-in-depth only. Fix: re-verify the parent still resolves inside the pool immediately before each unlink, or delete via a jailed dirfd.

NIT 4 — :343: new/old discrimination by PATH identity (`entry.path not in set(oldDirs)`) misclassifies a dist-info dir pip re-created at the same path (same-version reinstall) as OLD → would delete its fresh files + rmtree its fresh metadata (when another package also gained a new dist-info; with only the rewritten dir, newDirs is empty and dedup skips safely). NOT reachable with the helper's current argv (no --force-reinstall; --upgrade skips already-satisfied reqs; a genuinely newer version always yields a different dist-info dir name) — latent against pip behavior drift, which is real (dedup exists because pip's --target behavior changed before). Also hoist `set(oldDirs)` out of the comprehension (rebuilt per iteration).

NIT 5 — :378-379: OSError from unlink/rmtree inside `_removeOldDistInfo` is not contained per-package — one failing dir aborts dedup for all remaining snapshot entries (only RECORD *reads* are contained per-package at :356/:368). Fix: per-dir try/except OSError around the call.

NIT 6 — tests: no coverage for findings 1 (symlink-loop RuntimeError), 2 (all-names-hostile / --all empty-specs exit code), 5 (deletion-error containment). TestJail ~:297, TestAllModeNameValidation :789.

VERIFIED CLEAN (focus areas): jail traversal/absolute paths (pathlib absolute-RHS join replacement → `/abs` caught by relative_to; `../..`, `//x` rejected; `.`/trailing-slash RECORD entries hit the refuse-directory warning); symlink handling (in-pool old-only symlinks unlinked AS LINKS, targets preserved, matches testOldOnlySymlinkDeletedNotItsTarget; escaped symlinks and symlinked dist-info dirs skipped, never followed); RECORD parsing/normalization (normpath equivalence, blank/comma-only lines skipped, unreadable RECORD → whole-package skip, §4.1 set-subtraction correct); pip argv (flags → `--target` inserted after `install` → `--` before specs; `--all` names provably reduce to `[a-z0-9-]` because canonicalizeName collapses every [-_.]+ run).

CROSS-REF — the earlier NEEDS-FIXES review (memory 0130e853, baseline 1cebcba9) findings appear ALREADY FIXED in this working tree; do not re-flag: its major 1 (METADATA-name pip injection — now isValidCanonicalName + `--` separator exist), minor 4 (RECORD symlink deleted via resolved target — symlink branch now unlinks the unresolved candidate), minor 5 (RECORD subtraction raw-string compare — normpath now applied in readRecordPaths).

DESIGN NOTE (documented §4.1 contract, not a defect): a readable planted old RECORD can name arbitrary in-pool relative paths for deletion (subtraction only protects same-name new installs); inherent to RECORD-based dedup and mirrors pip's own uninstall RECORD trust; the jail prevents any escape from the pool.

CAVEAT: severity of findings 1 and 4 depends on the gromozeka-sandbox-python:install image's Python/pip versions — image not inspectable from the review session.

title: Pool dedup Major: symlink-alias RECORD paths bypass subtraction and delete newly installed files
content:
Post-fix-round review 2026-09-04 (code-reviewer session, review-only, NO code changed) of uncommitted Phase-1 sandbox pool-update code found a NEW Major in lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/pool_update_packages.py dedup deletion (~:290-310, subtraction at :379). Unfixed at review time — re-verify before relying.

TRACE (verified step-by-step): old RECORD entry `alias/mod.py` where in-pool symlink `alias → pkg`, new install owns `pkg/mod.py`. (1) readRecordPaths normalizes only lexically (posixpath.normpath :248) — cannot know the alias → `oldPaths − newPaths` keeps `alias/mod.py`. (2) Jail passes: `_resolveJailed` (:268-269) follows the INTERMEDIATE symlink → pool/pkg/mod.py is in-pool → relative_to succeeds. (3) `candidate.is_symlink()` (:298) lstats only the final component (mod.py is a regular file) → symlink branch skipped. (4) `resolved.unlink()` (:310) deletes pool/pkg/mod.py — the file the NEW RECORD claims. New install corrupted; helper still exits pip's code. Aggravator: a planted RECORD naming `pkg/mod.py` DIRECTLY would be protected by subtraction; the `alias/` route launders the path past exactly that protection. Benign trigger too: wheels may contain symlinks, so an honest old package with a symlinked top-level dir upgraded to a version shipping the real dir hits this without malice.

CRITICAL INSIGHT — the tempting fix fails: swapping :310 to `candidate.unlink()` does NOT help; unlinking `pool/alias/mod.py` removes the same directory entry (mod.py in the dir alias points to) as unlinking pool/pkg/mod.py.

INVERSE CASE (also confirmed, unguarded): new RECORD ships symlink `pkg/alias.py → pkg/real.py` (installed by new wheel), old RECORD lists `pkg/real.py` → old-only lexically, candidate is a regular file, resolved == lexical → :310 deletes the target and the new install's symlink dangles.

FIX STRATEGY (preserves intended stale-link deletion; order matters):
1. In dedupPool, alongside lexical newPaths, build `newRealPaths: set[Path] = {(poolRootResolved / p).resolve() for p in newPaths}` and pass to _removeOldDistInfo.
2. In the regular-file branch (:304-310), before unlinking: skip+warn if `resolved in newRealPaths` (physical file claimed by new install — fixes inverse case); skip+warn if `resolved != lexically-normalized absolute candidate` (intermediate component is a symlink → RECORD's lexical path doesn't name the physical file → "never delete what we cannot account for", module docstring :22 — fixes main trace).
3. KEEP the final-component-symlink branch (:298-303, candidate.is_symlink → candidate.unlink) first and unchanged — it is intended behavior pinned by testOldOnlySymlinkDeletedNotItsTarget (tests .../test_pool_update_packages.py:599-644).
4. Do NOT resolve the old side during subtraction — folding resolved identities into oldPaths would exclude old final-symlinks from pathsToRemove entirely and leave stale links uncleaned, breaking that test's contract.
Per repo regression-test rule: two failing-first tests in TestSubtraction (assert pkg/mod.py survives the alias trace; assert pkg/real.py survives / new link not dangling in the inverse).

title: parseListCommandOutput returns [] on malformed output → packages.json silently wiped with metadataRefreshed=True
content:
Post-fix-round review 2026-09-04 (review-only, findings unfixed at review time) found a Major metadata-loss path in the /sandbox update refresh chain. Re-verify current state before relying.

ROOT CAUSE: lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/runtime.py parseListCommandOutput fails NON-atomically — :200-202 catches only json.JSONDecodeError and returns []; :192-194 returns [] for valid-JSON non-list output; :196-198 silently skips non-dict elements (partial wipe). Meanwhile lib/sandbox/manager.py:1628-1629 runs `savePackagesInfo(...)` UNCONDITIONALLY on the refreshOk path (only container exitCode/signal/oomKilled are gated).

IMPACT: a list container that exits 0 with malformed stdout (pip notice printed to stdout, truncated redirect, wrong interpreter emitting a banner) overwrites packages.json with [] (or a partial list) and updateRuntimeLibraries returns metadataRefreshed=True — SILENT. This reopens the exact "every package looks vanished" failure mode the refreshOk guard (manager.py:1603-1626) was added to prevent, via the parse path. Downstream: runCode's required-package gate (manager.py:557-562) raises MissingDependenciesError for everything, and the next update's diff reports every package as old=X → new=None. Contradicts _refreshPackageList's own contract (manager.py:1540-1543: "in failure cases the existing packages.json metadata is preserved untouched").

FIX: make parseListCommandOutput RAISE on JSON-decode failure / non-list output (and consider rejecting non-dict elements) so the existing exception paths (manager.py:1241-1246 for update → metadataRefreshed=False; 1608-1626 → return False preserving packages.json) do their job; _refreshPackageList then never saves on parse failure.

Verification status at review time: make lint clean, 64 targeted sandbox tests + full suite green (4486 passed, 11 skipped — Docker integration among skipped, so the real pip-in-container path was NOT exercised; parser regression tests should run with a malformed-stdout fixture, not a real container).

title: Install image Alpine 3.23 = Python 3.12.14: pathlib RuntimeError-on-symlink-loop confirmed reachable; venv runs 3.14
content:
Confirmed 2026-09-04 via Alpine package index: the sandbox install/update image (lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/Dockerfile.install, `FROM alpine:3.23`, apk python3) ships Python **3.12.14-r0**. This closes the "image not inspectable" caveat from the earlier pool_update_packages review (memory 36e4ddb9): its RuntimeError symlink-loop finding IS reachable in the container.

Why it matters — host/container divergence: the local venv runs Python 3.14.6, where `Path.resolve()` on a symlink loop raises the silent `OSError`; on the image's 3.12 it raises `RuntimeError` REGARDLESS of strict= (behavior changed only in 3.13). So helper code catching only `(OSError, ValueError)` in `_resolveJailed` (pool_update_packages.py ~:270) works on the host and in host-run tests but breaks in the real container on planted symlink loops — test-green-on-3.14 does NOT prove container behavior for pathlib/exception-type edge cases. Fix (still unfixed as of the 2026-09-04 post-fix-round review): add RuntimeError to the catch tuple + a symlink-loop regression test.

General rule for lib/sandbox container-side helpers: anything whose behavior differs across 3.12/3.13/3.14 (pathlib symlink handling, exception types) must be validated against the IMAGE's Python (3.12.x), not the venv's.

title: Residual sandbox-update review findings: test-function imports, hard-coded list timeout, missing update-path removeContainer twin test, stale diff on failed update
content:

2. lib/sandbox/manager.py:1582 — the list container's timeout is hard-coded `timeoutSeconds=300`, unlike install/update which source `installContainerConfig.timeoutSeconds` with caller override (manager.py:1005-1007, 1191-1193). Fix: use the config value (or keep 300 but document why).

3. Test gap: no update-path twin of `testInstallRemoveFailureDoesNotFailInstall` (tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py:510-536). updateRuntimeLibraries mirrors install's best-effort removeContainer (manager.py:1222-1225, keeps failed container + reports containerId :1226-1235), but a regression making removal failure fail the UPDATE would go uncaught. Fix: add the twin test in TestUpdateRuntimeLibraries.

4. On FAILED update, after-snapshot + diff are still computed (manager.py:1251) from stale metadata: _refreshPackageList was skipped so afterVersions == beforeVersions, and the result reports updated=[] + unchanged=[entire pool] with success=False — while a killed pip may have partially mutated the pool. LibraryUpdateResult.metadataRefreshed's doc (types.py:407-409) covers only the success case, inviting callers to read `unchanged` as fact. Fix: skip after-snapshot/diff when not success (return empty lists), or document the diff is meaningful only when success=True.

title: canonicalizeName preserves / and spaces; use .fullmatch for PEP 508 name grammar
content:
In `lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/pool_update_packages.py`, `canonicalizeName` (PEP 503) collapses runs of `[-_.]+` to a single `-` but PRESERVES `/` and whitespace: `"../escape"` → `"-/escape"`, `"/tmp/evil"` unchanged, `"-r"` unchanged, `"-r requirements.txt"` unchanged. Hostile METADATA `Name:` headers therefore canonicalize to unexpected spellings, and tests asserting on hostile names must use the CANONICALIZED form (a fix-round test initially asserted `"../escape"` in stderr output and failed until corrected to `"-/escape"`).

Validity checking against the full PEP 508 name grammar (`^[A-Za-z0-9]([A-Za-z0-9._-]*[A-Za-z0-9])?$`, `CANONICAL_NAME_PATTERN`) must use `.fullmatch()`, NOT `.match()` with `$` anchors: `$` also matches before a trailing newline, so `"foo\n"` would wrongly pass `.match`; `.fullmatch` requires whole-string consumption. Legitimate canonicalization outputs can still be invalid (e.g. METADATA name `foo.` → canonical `foo-`, trailing separator → grammar rejects) — that is intended "warn on stderr, skip" behavior.

Related defense-in-depth fact: the `--` separator before positional specs in `buildPipCommand` stops pip option parsing but does NOT block absolute/local-path requirements — name validation AND `--` are both required.

title: _removeOldDistInfo deletion ordering is load-bearing: jail-resolve BEFORE is_symlink branch
content:
The dedup deletion order in `_removeOldDistInfo` (`lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/pool_update_packages.py`) is: (1) `_resolveJailed()` — resolved path is used ONLY for jail validation, skip+warn if target escapes the pool; (2) if `candidate.is_symlink()` → unlink the CANDIDATE (the link itself, target survives); (3) non-symlink directory → refuse; (4) unlink resolved file.

The resolve-first ordering is load-bearing and must not be "simplified": if the `candidate.is_symlink()` branch ran before the jail resolve, a RECORD path with lexically-escaping `../` components whose final component is a symlink would delete a symlink living OUTSIDE the pool. Also remember: `candidate.is_symlink()` lstats only the FINAL component — intermediate directory symlinks are only caught by the resolve step, and `resolved.is_symlink()` is always False on a fully resolved path (see memory 6a9d3f95). The still-unguarded intermediate-symlink alias vector (old RECORD `alias/mod.py` where `alias → pkg`) is documented with a full fix strategy in memory 5e3b82e4 — do not confuse the guarded final-symlink case (pinned by testOldOnlySymlinkDeletedNotItsTarget) with that unguarded one.

title: Sandbox pool test patterns: poolLock monkeypatch wrapper for concurrency, test_enums.py = re-export surface home
content:
Three test conventions/patterns for lib/sandbox pool work (from the Gate-1 fix round, 2026-09-04):

1. **Concurrency simulation via poolLock monkeypatch**: `lib/sandbox/manager.py` calls `locks.poolLock(...)` through the module attribute, so `monkeypatch.setattr(lib.sandbox.locks, "poolLock", fake)` intercepts the manager's lock acquisition. Pattern: an `@asynccontextmanager` wrapper that (a) writes metadata (simulated concurrent install completing) BEFORE delegating to the real lock, (b) yields inside `async with realPoolLock(rt, dir)`, (c) writes metadata again (simulated concurrent update) AFTER release. Capture `realPoolLock = sandboxLocks.poolLock` BEFORE monkeypatching. This proves lock-scoped before/after snapshots (`testConcurrentOperationBetweenSnapshotPointsDoesNotCorruptDiff`): old out-of-lock flow reports pillow as wrongly changed; fixed in-lock flow shows it unchanged.

2. **Public-surface test home**: `tests/lib/sandbox/test_enums.py` holds the package-level re-export surface tests for `lib/sandbox/__init__.py` — `testPackageReExport` (enums) and `testPackageResultTypesReExport` (`PackageUpdate`, `LibraryUpdateResult`, added in the fix round). There is no dedicated `__all__` test file for lib.sandbox; extend test_enums.py for new exports. Keep such imports at module top per repo rule.

3. **Failure-outcome fixtures**: `ContainerOutcome.signal` is `str | None` (not int). `tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py::_makeContainerOutcome` accepts `exitCode`, `containerId`, plus `signal`/`oomKilled` kwargs for failed-list-container fixtures; feed multiple outcomes via `AsyncMock(side_effect=[outcome1, outcome2])` (update container first, list container second).

title: Mutation-testing version-divergent code: shim the stdlib call to simulate old-interpreter behavior
content:
The dev venv is Python 3.14.6, where non-strict `Path.resolve()` no longer raises on symlink loops (3.13+ returns a loop-terminated path) — but the sandbox helper runs on the Alpine container image's Python 3.12, where it raises `RuntimeError` (see memory 59cade95). Consequence: a regression test relying on a REAL symlink loop is green-under-mutation on the dev venv, so it cannot verify the `except (OSError, ValueError, RuntimeError)` guard in `_resolveJailed`.

Deterministic technique (used by `testSymlinkLoopEntrySkippedWithoutAbortingPass`): monkeypatch `Path.resolve` with a shim that raises `RuntimeError` for a specific filename (e.g. `loop.py`) and delegates to the real resolve otherwise — reproducing ≤3.12 behavior on any interpreter; revert the guard and the test goes red with the propagated RuntimeError. General rule: when a code path's behavior depends on the interpreter version (dev venv vs container runtime), mutation-verify via a shim reproducing the old-version behavior instead of trusting the local interpreter.

title: Gate-1 fix round landed (7/7 mutation-verified); 3 review findings deferred as follow-ups
content:
All 7 Gate-1 review findings for `/sandbox update` Phase 1 were fixed and mutation-verified on 2026-09-04 (each guard temporarily reverted → target test red → restored): (1) `--all` snapshot names validated against full PEP 508 grammar (warn+skip invalid) + `--` inserted before positional pip specs in `buildPipCommand`; (2) `_refreshPackageList` requires exitCode==0 / no signal / not oomKilled, preserves packages.json and returns False on failure — install path stays best-effort (`testInstallSucceedsEvenWhenListRefreshFails` stays green); (3) before/after version snapshots moved inside `locks.poolLock`, after-snapshot captured before release, diff computed outside from captured dicts, `InvalidPackageSpec`/`ConfigError` raises stay pre-lock; (4) symlink candidates unlinked as links (target preserved); (5) RECORD paths normalized symmetrically via `posixpath.normpath`; (6) `PackageUpdate`/`LibraryUpdateResult` exported from `lib.sandbox`; (7) safety-branch tests added (dist-info dir symlink escape, unreadable new RECORD). Plus `RuntimeError` added to `_resolveJailed`'s except (per memory 59cade95). Gates: `make format lint` clean; `make test` 4486 passed / 11 skipped.

Any future session touching pool dedup or metadata refresh should check these three first.

title: _resolveJailed except clause requires RuntimeError — symlink loops raise it (Python ≤ 3.12)
content:
In `lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/pool_update_packages.py` (`_resolveJailed`, ~line 271), the except clause MUST be `except (OSError, ValueError, RuntimeError): return None` — do not drop `RuntimeError`. Rationale: symlink loops raise `RuntimeError` on Python ≤ 3.12, so a crafted symlink loop in a package RECORD entry would crash pool package updates instead of being treated as a jail escape (`return None`). A mutation test had removed `RuntimeError` and left the marker comment `# MUTATION: RuntimeError removed` in the working tree; it was restored (2026-09-04) to the exact committed HEAD state.

Distinct from the separate unlink-target gotcha (memory 953605cc): this is about the except-clause breadth of the jail check itself, not about which path gets unlinked.

title: MUTATION-marker leftovers: interrupted rounds leave sabotaged code in working tree; grep sweep + restore-to-HEAD
content:
Mutation sanity checks in Gromozeka (see also memory 207e5b6c for the sabotage→FAIL/revert→PASS convention) temporarily edit production code and tag the change with a `# MUTATION: <what was removed>` comment. If a session is interrupted mid-check, the mutated line + marker can be left behind in the working tree.

Recovery pattern (used 2026-09-04):
1. Sweep: `grep -rn "MUTATION" lib/ tests/ internal/` — must return NOTHING.
2. Restore per the surrounding code's intent; the committed HEAD is ground truth — mutation edits are working-tree-only, so a correct restore makes the file vanish from `git diff` entirely (that disappearance IS the confirmation the restore landed).
3. `make format` can also normalize a dirty test file back to its committed HEAD state as a side effect (black reformatting non-formatted leftovers).

Never invent changes beyond restoring the mutated line; no changelog/doc updates are needed since restoring returns existing committed behavior.

title: CRITICAL: pip --target --upgrade into live sandbox pool destroys shared-namespace packages — /sandbox update Phase 1 NEEDS-FIXES
content:
Found 2026-09-04 during delta re-review of /sandbox update Phase 1 (uncommitted tree on top of 1cebcba9; all 7 earlier findings verified fixed — see separate memory — but this blocks merge).

Root cause: `pool_update_packages.py` `buildPipCommand()` (~:398-403) points pip's `--target` at the LIVE shared pool (rw bind mount, `manager.py` ~:1172-1177). pip semantics (verified against pip 25.3 source): `--target` implies `--ignore-installed`; under `--upgrade`, pip's `_handle_target_dir` does `shutil.rmtree` on any colliding top-level directory in the target before moving the staged one in. So updating package A whose files live under a shared namespace dir (e.g. `google/protobuf/…`) wholesale-replaces `pool/google/`, destroying package B's subtree (`google/auth/…`).

Why it is SILENT: B gains no new dist-info → `dedupPool`'s `if not newDirs: continue` branch (`pool_update_packages.py` ~:342-352) skips it; `_refreshPackageList`/`pip list --path` still reports B installed → `savePackagesInfo` writes it; `runCode` requiredPackages precheck (`manager.py` ~:556-562) checks metadata names, not importability → corruption surfaces only as later ImportError in run containers. Diff classifies B "unchanged"; pip exits 0. RECORD post-dedup cannot repair: subtraction is per-name old-vs-new dist-info only, deletion-only (never restores files), and the loss happens before dedup runs.

Pre-existing vs new: the same pip hazard exists in `installCommand(upgrade=True)` (`manager.py` ~:990) but NO production caller passed upgrade=True (bot handler omits it; only `scripts/sandbox_bootstrap.py` exposes it) — plan §1 line 21 documents this. The update subcommand makes it the routine owner-facing path: that is the new defect. Selected (named) updates are unconditionally exposed; `--all` topology depends on pip staging granularity (needs a container test to pin).

Remediation options (review recommendation: A+B together):
- A (root-cause): stage-then-merge — pip `--target` into a FRESH staging dir inside the same mount (empty target → nothing to collide), then merge union(new RECORDs) into the pool copy-only (create dirs, never rmtree existing parents); keep existing old−union(new) RECORD deletion; remove staging last. Amends plan §4.1 — do while Phase 2 is unmerged.
- B (detection, keep even after A): final helper step verifies every current dist-info RECORD path exists under the pool; any missing → name victims on stderr, exit non-zero (amends step-4 contract at plan :23-24/:477-478). Manager failure mapping then does the right thing untouched (success=False, container kept, metadata preserved). Repair = `/sandbox install <victim>`. Caveat: pools with pre-existing drift flag on first run.
- C (stopgap): do not ship the update subcommand; document hazard in plan §15 + docs/llm/sandbox.md.

Testing strategy (regression-first per AGENTS.md): fake-pip test `testSharedNamespaceDirSurvivesSelectedUpdate` (must FAIL before fix); parametrized two-sharer ordering test; real-pip `slow` container test with two tiny local wheels sharing `google/` via `--find-links file://` (only test that pins actual pip behavior vs upstream drift — log pip version); doc correction of plan :68/:252; manager-level test triggering helper non-zero via post-verify asserting the failure mapping.

title: pip --target ⟹ --ignore-installed CONFIRMED (pip 25.3) — plan's "already satisfied, zero download" claim is false
content:
Supersedes the earlier "unverified — check in Phase 2" note (deleted). Confirmed 2026-09-04 by reading pip 25.3 source: `pip install --target DIR` forces `ignore_installed=True` — the target dir is never consulted for satisfaction, so "Requirement already satisfied" can NEVER fire for pool content.

Consequences for /sandbox update: every bare-name `--all` run resolves against the index and re-downloads/reinstalls the LATEST version of every pool package even when identical. The plan's perf claims are FALSE and need doc correction: docs/plans/sandbox-update-v1.md:68 (§4.1) and the §9 row at :252 (plus the §1 rationale sentence objecting to pre-remove re-downloads — the ratified mechanism re-downloads too).

Related facts pinned in the same investigation:
- `--upgrade-strategy only-if-needed` is irrelevant here: it governs dependency upgrades within the resolve set, not whether the requirement itself reinstalls.
- A same-version in-place overwrite still produces no NEW dist-info path, so dedup no-ops; the existing `testAlreadySatisfiedNoOp` (tests/lib/sandbox/runtimes/test_pool_update_packages.py:1068-1094) remains valid — it pins the deletion no-op only and, using a mocked pip, cannot observe downloads.
- This also widens the critical `--target --upgrade` shared-namespace corruption exposure (separate memory): the collision-rmtree runs on EVERY update-all, not only on version bumps.
