title: EMPIRICAL pip 26.2.1: --target pool corruption + no satisfied-skip + staging/PYTHONPATH failures — all measured
content:
Empirical verification (2026-09-04, throwaway mktemp experiment, real PyPI downloads with --no-cache-dir, repo venv pip 26.2.1 / Python 3.14.6). Converts two prior knowledge items from claimed/source-read to measured: (a) the pip-25.3 source-read finding (memory 41c3adcb) that `--target` forces ignore_installed=True — holds empirically on 26.2.1; (b) the review claim (memory 735a8518) that `--target --upgrade` into the live pool destroys shared-namespace packages — CONFIRMED with hard numbers, and the damage is WORSE than claimed: the no-flag path is ALSO corrupting.

E1 — shared namespace corruption, both paths unsafe (repro: pool with googleapis-common-protos 1.63.0, which pulls protobuf 4.25.9; NOTE PyPI has no `163.0.0` spelling — `==163.0.0` fails to resolve, use `==1.63.0`):
- `pip install --target <pool> --upgrade protobuf==5.29.0` (5.29.0 is yanked — WARNING only, installs fine): exit 0, NO "Attempting uninstall" lines (zero RECORD-based cleanup). Deleted 197 files, 196 of them listed in googleapis_common_protos-1.63.0.dist-info/RECORD (google/api 99, google/cloud 6, google/gapic 3, google/logging 6, google/longrunning 13, google/rpc 18, google/type 51); `google/` left containing only protobuf's `_upb` + `protobuf`; stale protobuf-4.25.9.dist-info AND orphaned gcp dist-info both left behind (duplicate dist-infos never cleaned).
- Mechanism: the unit of a --target install is the TOP-LEVEL DIRECTORY. Without --upgrade pip skips existing top-level dirs entirely: `WARNING: Target directory .../google already exists. Specify --upgrade to force replacement.` — yet STILL writes the new dist-info → pool left in a LYING state (metadata says 5.29.0, code is 4.25.9).

E2 — "Requirement already satisfied" NEVER fires under --target (26.2.1): unpinned no-flag (target had six 1.16.0 → downloaded + "Successfully installed six-1.17.0" while `WARNING: Target directory .../six.py already exists` left six.py at 1.16.0 → lying metadata); exact-pin with --upgrade (six==1.16.0 re-downloaded + force-replaced); unpinned --upgrade; idna==3.6 → --upgrade → 3.19 (idna-3.6.dist-info left beside idna-3.19.dist-info). Every invocation re-downloads; duplicate dist-infos accumulate and are never cleaned. pip also compiles __pycache__ into the target.

D — staging + PYTHONPATH does NOT preserve satisfied-skipping: `PYTHONPATH=<pool with six> pip install --target <empty staging> six` fully downloads + installs into staging (same with --upgrade; same for the venv-absent wcwidth control). pip ignores PYTHONPATH entirely for --target resolution → a stage-then-merge redesign cannot keep the zero-download-when-current property.

E3 — `--dry-run --report <file>`: the report's `install` array lists the package anyway even when it is present in the PYTHONPATH pool → NOT an is-satisfied oracle; usable only as a DIY outdated-check (compare the report's resolved version against pool dist-info versions). Dry-run is non-mutating (target stayed empty).

Side findings: pip DOES scan the running venv for dependency-conflict WARNINGS (e.g. `yandexcloud 0.403.0 requires six<2,>=1.17.0, but you have six 1.16.0`) but never aborts on them (exit 0) and never uses env content for satisfaction. Venv contents (six/idna/protobuf/gcp all present in repo venv) are irrelevant to --target installs.

Design implication (experiment conclusion): never mutate the live pip pool in place — rebuild atomically into a fresh dir + rename swap; do outdated checks in our own code by comparing dist-info versions (or --dry-run --report resolved versions) against the pool.

title: opencode Bash tool: shell env vars do NOT persist across tool calls
content: Despite being described as a persistent shell session, the Bash tool does NOT carry variables between calls: during the 2026-09-04 pip --target experiment, `XP=$(mktemp -d)` set in one call was EMPTY in the next, so `mkdir -p $XP/pool1` ran as `mkdir /pool1` → "Read-only file system", and every follow-up path in that call broke. Right way: in the creating call, echo the path; then hardcode the literal path (e.g. /var/folders/.../tmp.XXXX) at the start of every subsequent command instead of relying on the variable.

title: opencode-go provider and x-opencode-session session plumbing
content:
OpenCode Go requires the `x-opencode-session` header on every request from 2026-09-06 (prompt-cache affinity; they also flagged the broad "Python OpenAI client" UA). Implemented 2026-09-04:

1. **Session identity = chat + thread root**, user's explicit choice ("bot builds context differently for different conversations inside a chat"): format `gromozeka-<chatId>-<rootMessageId>`, built by `BaseBotHandler.getLLMRequestSessionId` (internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py, one DB lookup via getChatMessageByMessageId; falls back to the message's own id when no thread root; stable across restarts).
2. **Transport = task-local ContextVar** `_requestSessionIdVar` + `getCurrentRequestSessionId()` in lib/ai/abstract.py. All four public AbstractModel wrappers (generateText/generateStructured/generateImage/generateEmbeddings) take `sessionId: Optional[str] = None` and set/reset the var around the whole body (try/finally, including the `_runWithFallback` lambdas which also pass it explicitly). This avoided changing any `_generate*` provider signatures. Do NOT set the var only when non-None — always set + reset, otherwise stale sessions leak between sequential calls in one task.
3. **`OpencodeGoProvider`/`OpencodeGoModel`** (lib/ai/providers/opencode_go_provider.py), provider type `opencode-go` registered in manager.py. `_getExtraParams()` merges `extra_headers = {"x-opencode-session": ...}` at the HEADER level with user customParams.extra_headers (user wins per header). Resolution: ContextVar (stripped) → provider config `session_fallback` → DEFAULT_SESSION_ID "gromozeka" — header is ALWAYS present. base_url check happens BEFORE super().__init__ (unlike CustomOpenAIProvider, which raises KeyError from _initClient).
4. **Threading**: LLMService.generateTextViaLLM/generateText/generateStructured/generateImage/generateEmbedding all take sessionId and pass it down, including the condensing call inside condenseContext (same conversation → same session). Wired in llm_messages.py at both generateTextViaLLM call sites (main chat path + llm_test_command). Other handlers (summary/media/search/divination) don't pass sessionId yet → they use the provider fallback; fine for now.
5. **Global UA**: `DEFAULT_USER_AGENT = "GromozekaBot/1.0.0 (+https://notacompany.org/products/gromozeka)"` in basic_openai_provider.py, applied in `_initClient` via default_headers with setdefault (subclass-provided headers win). Version must be kept in sync with pyproject [project].version manually.
6. configs/common/01-opencode-go.toml (gitignored overlay) switched `type = "custom-openai"` → `"opencode-go"`. Tests: tests/lib/ai/providers/test_opencode_go_provider.py (14 tests incl. ContextVar reset/isolation + LLMManager e2e). Docs: docs/llm/libraries.md §1 (sessionId block), docs/llm/configuration.md provider types.

title: Sandbox pool update revision 2 ratified: staged install + atomic swap (supersedes live-pool pip variants)
content:
Ratified 2026-09-04, recorded in docs/plans/sandbox-update-v1.md revision 2 (397 lines). SUPERSEDES both earlier pip-writes-into-live-pool variants: the pre-remove D1 design AND the post-remove upgrade+dedup mechanism (supersedes the design in the memory "D1 superseded by post-remove mechanism"), and it is the ratified fix path for the Phase-1 "pip --target --upgrade destroys shared-namespace packages" NEEDS-FIXES finding.

Core invariant: pip NEVER writes into the live pool (<root>/runtimes/python/libs). Flow: (1) outdated pre-filter — one dry-run report container (read-only, BEFORE taking the lock; delivers the D2 zero-download skip property in our code); (2) poolLock held for the whole mutation phase; (3) host-side copy pool → <root>/tmp/<runId>/newpool (same FS, ~2× pool disk headroom); (4) one container run: pip install --target staging/delta (live pool NOT mounted); (5) host-side merge on the private copy: delete old dist-info files per its FULL RECORD (plain deletion, NO set-subtraction — new version lives in a separate tree, killing the same-path-overwrite hazard), then copy staged files in; (6) atomic rename swap libs→oldpool, newpool→libs (any failure before swap leaves the live pool untouched — no holes by construction); (7) post-swap refresh + diff. Any failure leaves pool 100% intact.

Sub-decisions: helper renamed to pool_pip_runner.py with two modes --report <file> / --install-into <dir> (`--` before specs, exit code = pip's); ALL deletion/merge/swap logic moves host-side into new pool_staging.py (unit-testable without containers; RECORD-jail/symlink/normpath checks carried over from the old helper); update-all name source = host-side dist-info enumeration (METADATA Name: parser, avoids hyphen-splitting) ∪ packages.json canonical names (self-heal union, grammar-validated); installRuntimeLibraries unified through the same staged core (no pre-filter; upgrade param kept as documented no-op for sandbox_bootstrap.py compat; installing an already-present package becomes a clean re-install — fixes the corruption bug); Runtime ABC: installCommand DELETED, replaced by reportCommand + stageInstallCommand; LibraryUpdateResult gains upToDate: list[str]; diff baseline switched from packages.json to host-side enumerations; zero new config keys (staging under <root>/tmp/<runId>/ is derived); cross-filesystem staging rejected via pre-swap st_dev guard raising ConfigError. D3 upgraded: Linux bind-mount inode semantics mean containers that mounted the pool keep seeing the OLD contents after the swap — in-flight mixed-version hazard largely eliminated (one-sentence residual caveat only). Phases re-cut: 1R (host core + helper rewrite), 1I (install unification — must stay separate from 1R so the install-bug regression test fails-before/passes-after), 2 (handler), 3 (docs sync incl. Added + Fixed CHANGELOG entries).

title: /sandbox install already-present package corruption: root cause is pip --target writing dist-info while skipping code
content:
Root cause of the ratified /sandbox install corruption bug (pip 26.2.1 spike, 2026-09-04): `pip install --target <dir>` WITHOUT `--upgrade` onto an existing top-level package dir warns "Target directory … already exists. Specify --upgrade to force replacement", SKIPS code replacement but STILL writes the new dist-info → lying metadata + duplicate dist-info dirs + stale code. Combined with the confirmed fact that pip --target forces ignore_installed (no satisfaction check — "Requirement already satisfied" NEVER appears, re-verified empirically on 26.2.1 after the pip-25.3 source reading), every `/sandbox install <already-present-package>` corrupts the pool today.

Additional spike mechanics worth keeping: (a) pip's unit of installation under --target is the TOP-LEVEL DIRECTORY, wholesale-replaced with --upgrade — installing protobuf==5.29.0 into a pool containing googleapis-common-protos==1.63.0 deleted 197 files/added 20, removed google/api/ entirely (196 deleted files belonged to googleapis-common-protos per its RECORD), orphaned its dist-info, and left stale protobuf-4.25.9 dist-info next to 5.29.0, with no "Attempting uninstall" line; (b) PYTHONPATH is ignored for --target resolution (staging+PYTHONPATH cannot restore satisfied-skips); (c) `pip install --dry-run --report <file> --target <scratch>` is NON-MUTATING (dry-run targets stay empty) and its install[] array carries resolved versions + wheel URLs — usable as a DIY outdated-package oracle.

Fix (revision 2, ratified): installRuntimeLibraries routes through the staged install + atomic-swap core — container pip --target staging/delta, host-side merge deletes old dist-info per full RECORD then copies staged files, atomic rename swap.

title: flock file must live outside rename-swapped directories — pool.lock already compliant (sibling of libs/)
content:
General gotcha for atomic-swap directory designs: a flock file INSIDE a directory replaced via rename(2) breaks mutual exclusion — a waiter blocked on the OLD inode's lock can acquire it while the next process locks the NEW file at the same path. The lock file must live outside the swapped tree.

Gromozeka specifics: this is already satisfied — locks.py:294 derives lockPath = poolDir/"pool.lock" where poolDir = <root>/runtimes/python (manager.py:949/1098), i.e. pool.lock is a SIBLING of the swapped libs/ dir, never inside it. Revision 2 pins this as a load-bearing invariant (regression test asserting the lock path is not inside libs/) and forbids any future "swap the whole runtime dir" refactor. No relocation code change was needed.

Meta-lesson (agent correction): the task brief asserted "the flock file must move OUTSIDE the swapped dir" assuming relocation was required; verifying against code showed the premise already held. Always check the code before designing around stated premises — the right design move was pinning an invariant + test, not specifying a no-op move.

title: Phase 1R part (a) implemented: pool_pip_runner.py + pool_staging.py + new Runtime builders exist; part (b) still pending
content:
Implemented 2026-09-04 (uncommitted working tree on top of commit 1cebcba9), per docs/plans/sandbox-update-v1.md rev 2 Phase 1R part (a). Now in the tree:

- `lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/pool_pip_runner.py` (NEW, ~135 lines): stdlib-only thin pip runner. Two mutually exclusive argparse modes (required group, argparse exits 2 on zero/both modes): `--report <file>` → `pip install --dry-run --report <file> --target /tmp/pip-dryrun-scratch --no-cache-dir --no-input -- <specs>`; `--install-into <dir>` → `pip install --target <dir> ... -- <specs>`. Runs via subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", ...]) argv (no shell); exit code = pip's; mandatory `--` before specs; argv builders `buildReportCommand`/`buildInstallCommand` are separate pinned functions; constant DRY_RUN_SCRATCH_TARGET.
- `lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/pool_staging.py` (NEW, ~429 lines): host-importable, stdlib-only. Moved from pool_update_packages.py: canonicalizeName, extractSpecName, isValidCanonicalName + grammar regex, DistInfoEntry/enumerateDistInfos + _parseDistInfoDir (METADATA Name-first, dir-stem fallback), readRecordPaths (normpath), _resolveJailed. Simplified full-RECORD deletion in _removeOldDistInfo (symlink entries unlink the link never the target; jail resolve()+relative_to on every target incl. dist-info dirs before rmtree; directory RECORD entries refused). NEW: mergeStagedDelta(poolCopy, deltaDir) — full-RECORD deletion of all old dist-infos of staged names then shutil.copytree(deltaDir, poolCopy, dirs_exist_ok=True); swapPools(pool, newPool, oldPoolParking) — os.stat().st_dev same-FS guard raising ConfigError, two renames, inline rollback; parsePipReport(reportPath) -> dict[str,str] | None — fail-safe install[].metadata extraction (None on missing/bad JSON/malformed structure → callers treat all specs as outdated; per-entry garbage skipped).
- `lib/sandbox/runtimes/base.py`: Runtime ABC gained abstract reportCommand(specs) and stageInstallCommand(specs); updateCommand KEPT (deprecated, removed in part (b) when manager stops calling it); installCommand untouched (removed in Phase 1I).
- `lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/runtime.py`: UPDATE_HELPER_CONTAINER_PATH re-pointed to "/sandbox/pool_pip_runner.py"; NEW class constant PythonRuntime.STAGING_CONTAINER_PATH = "/sandbox/staging" (mount target; report at <staging>/report.json, delta at <staging>/delta); updateHelperHostPath → Path(installDockerfile).parent / "pool_pip_runner.py"; reportCommand/stageInstallCommand emit ["python", UPDATE_HELPER_CONTAINER_PATH, <mode flag>, <path>, "--", *specs].
- `lib/sandbox/types.py`: LibraryUpdateResult gained upToDate: list[str] after unchanged.
- Tests: NEW tests/lib/sandbox/runtimes/test_pool_pip_runner.py, test_pool_staging.py; test_locks.py extended with §4.4 pool-lock placement invariant (lock is sibling of libs, exclusion survives a live libs swap); test_python_runtime.py extended + two literal constant pins updated.

Still present until part (b): pool_update_packages.py + tests/lib/sandbox/runtimes/test_pool_update_packages.py (old helper and its tests NOT deleted). STILL PENDING: Phase 1R part (b) (manager rewrite: stop calling updateCommand, populate upToDate, wire report→pre-filter→stage→merge→swap) and Phase 1I (install unification, deletes installCommand). Verified: make format lint clean, make test 4550 passed / 11 skipped, mutation spot-checks on jail / st_dev guard / `--` separator all red-before-restore.

title: LibraryUpdateResult.upToDate needed field defaults because manager.py was untouchable in part (a)
content: Gotcha/decision from Phase 1R part (a): §5.2 spec shows `upToDate: list[str]` without a default, but all 3 `LibraryUpdateResult(...)` constructor sites live in `lib/sandbox/manager.py`, which the dispatch forbade touching. Python dataclass rules make this non-trivial: a field WITH a default cannot precede fields without one. Solution: `upToDate: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)` placed after `unchanged` as ordered, which then FORCED defaults on the trailing fields too (`failedSpecs: list[tuple[str,str]] = field(default_factory=list)`, `containerId: str | None = None`, `metadataRefreshed: bool = False`). Field order preserved; manager keeps passing everything as kwargs so nothing breaks. Deliberate deviation from the literal spec snippet — part (b) may drop the defaults when it populates upToDate and rewrites the constructors. General lesson: when adding a field to a dataclass constructed in files frozen by a phased dispatch, defaults are the only way to keep both mandated field order and a green tree.

title: Intermediate inconsistency after part (a): manager still calls updateCommand against the pool_pip_runner mount
content: Known-deli berate intermediate state after Phase 1R part (a), acceptable per the dispatch ordering adjustments: manager.py still calls runtimeImpl.updateCommand(...), which emits the OLD helper's `--pool-dir` CLI, while UPDATE_HELPER_CONTAINER_PATH and updateHelperHostPath() now point at pool_pip_runner.py — a helper that does not understand `--pool-dir`. A real update-container run before part (b) would fail with the helper's usage error. Functionally inert for CI/tests because manager tests mock the backend and reference the helper path symbolically (PythonRuntime.UPDATE_HELPER_CONTAINER_PATH), so they stay green. Part (b) resolves this by removing updateCommand entirely and wiring report→pre-filter→stage→merge→swap. Do not "fix" updateCommand to match the new helper — it gets deleted, not repaired.

title: pytest monkeypatch patterns for testing atomic swap (Path.rename counter, os.stat st_dev fake)
content:
Reusable test techniques proven in tests/lib/sandbox/runtimes/test_pool_staging.py::TestSwapPools:
1. Second-rename failure / rollback: swapPools uses `.rename()` methods, so monkeypatch `Path.rename` at class level with a counting wrapper that delegates to the captured original but raises OSError on call #2. All three renames (pool→parking, newPool→pool, rollback) are intercepted; assert pool restored with original content, parking gone, newPool untouched at its original path, original OSError propagates.
2. Same-FS guard: monkeypatch the os module's stat (pool_staging.os is the shared os module; pytest.MonkeyPatch restores it automatically) with a fake returning SimpleNamespace(st_dev=...) keyed on the path (pool→1, newPool→2) → ConfigError raised, and assert NO renames happened (all three dirs still in place).
Mutation-check discipline used: for each load-bearing guard (jail relative_to check, st_dev guard, `--` separator in builders): mutate → targeted tests red → restore → green → grep to confirm zero mutation leftovers.

title: Grep tests for literal constant pins before re-pointing a class constant
content: Gotcha hit in Phase 1R part (a): re-pointing PythonRuntime.UPDATE_HELPER_CONTAINER_PATH from "/sandbox/pool_update_packages.py" to "/sandbox/pool_pip_runner.py" (and updateHelperHostPath to pool_pip_runner.py) silently broke two EXISTING tests that pinned the literal old value: test_python_runtime.py::TestUpdateCommand::testContainerPathConstant asserted the exact string, and TestUpdateHelperHostPath::testDerivedFromInstallDockerfileParent asserted `.name == "pool_update_packages.py"`. Tests using the symbolic constant (e.g. test_manager.py uses PythonRuntime.UPDATE_HELPER_CONTAINER_PATH) stayed green automatically. Rule: when renaming/moving a constant or helper file, grep tests/ for the old literal value and update those pins in the same change.

title: Unreadable-RECORD skip semantics + host-logging vs container-stderr split
content:
Two related conventions confirmed while writing pool_staging.py / pool_pip_runner.py:
1. Deletion safety semantic ("never delete what you cannot account for"): mergeStagedDelta reads ALL old RECORDs of a staged canonical name BEFORE deleting anything — one unreadable RECORD (OSError/UnicodeDecodeError/csv.Error) skips that name's entire deletion (old dist-info dirs and their files stay), while the staged copy still lands beside it. Multiple old dist-infos of one name are all removed (heals duplicate installs); namespace dirs shared with other packages survive because only RECORD-listed files are deleted, never directories.
2. Warning channel: host-side sandbox modules (pool_staging.py) log via logging.getLogger(__name__) + logger.warning; in-container helper scripts (pool_pip_runner.py, pool_update_packages.py) print to stderr because containers run without logging config. Keep the split when adding code to either side.

title: Phase 1R-b staged-install implementation decisions + Phase 1I reuse contract
content:
Phase 1R part (b) of docs/plans/sandbox-update-v1.md (rev 2) implemented — updateRuntimeLibraries now runs copy → stage → merge → swap; rev-1 live-target machinery removed. Implementation decisions with rationale (code is in lib/sandbox/, this records the WHY and the Phase 1I contract):

- Shared staged core signature (Phase 1I install unification MUST reuse it, passing purpose="install"; update passes "update"): `SandboxManager._runStagedInstall(runtime, runtimeImpl, specs, timeoutSeconds, *, purpose) -> tuple[bool, str | None]`. The `purpose` kwarg feeds both the `sandbox.purpose` container label and the container-name prefix `sandbox-{purpose}-<runId>` — that is the ONLY divergence between update and install staging.
- The pre-filter (report) container runs BEFORE the pool lock and is a read-only probe that is ALWAYS removed, even on failure — the keep-container-on-failure contract applies only to the stage container. Consequence for tests: a LibraryPoolLocked scenario involves exactly 1 backend call (the pre-filter) before the lock raises; the old "zero backend calls" assertion is wrong under the rev-2 flow.
- Staging GC reaps (`GarbageCollector.collectStagingArtifacts`, reaps <root>/tmp/* dirs+files older than orphanWorkspaceRetentionMinutes) are folded into `GcResult.removedOrphans` instead of adding a new public field — deliberately avoids public-type churn; documented in collectAll's docstring.
- recover() crash-window case 2 (oldpool restore) ALSO deletes the emptied run dir; the spec (§4.5) only mandates run-dir deletion in case 1. Judgment call: symmetric hygiene, nothing valuable remains after the rename.
- Annotation-only `STAGING_CONTAINER_PATH: str` added to the Runtime ABC in runtimes/base.py (same ratified annotation-only pattern as UPDATE_HELPER_CONTAINER_PATH) so the manager builds staging mounts runtime-agnostically without importing PythonRuntime.
- Revision-1 test `testConcurrentOperationBetweenSnapshotPointsDoesNotCorruptDiff` was dropped, not ported: its mechanism (metadata version snapshots taken inside the lock) no longer exists — the diff baseline is now host-side dist-info enumeration re-read under the lock per §5.1.

title: AsyncMock side_effect LIST elements are values, never invoked as callables
content:
Gotcha hit in tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py (Phase 1R-b, 2026-09-04): `AsyncMock(side_effect=[fnA, fnB, value])` returns list elements AS-IS per call — a function element is NEVER invoked; the awaited result is the function object itself, surfacing downstream as e.g. `AttributeError: 'function' object has no attribute 'containerId'`. Only when side_effect is a SINGLE callable does AsyncMock call it and await a coroutine result.

Fix pattern (reference impl: `_oneshotSequence(*steps)` in tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py): dispatch through one callable that pops steps in call order — awaits callable steps with the mock's call kwargs (e.g. `spec=`), returns plain ContainerOutcome values verbatim, and raises AssertionError on over-call (do NOT let bare StopIteration propagate inside the async dispatcher — PEP 479 converts it to RuntimeError).

Plain-value list side_effects (e.g. [outcome1, outcome2]) remain fine and are used by the install tests. Note AsyncMock semantics differ here from what one might assume from sync MagicMock docs examples.

title: manager._gc keeps the ORIGINAL real DockerBackend when tests rewire manager._backend
content:
Complements memory 2b091e4d (GC receives backend via __init__). SandboxManager.__init__ (lib/sandbox/manager.py) constructs GarbageCollector passing the freshly created REAL DockerBackend. When a test replaces `manager._backend` with a MagicMock AFTER construction (the standard _makeManager pattern), `manager._gc` still holds the original real backend.

Consequences seen in Phase 1R-b recover() tests (2026-09-04):
- Green runs: recover() → collectGarbage() → _gc.collectAll() hits real Docker; `DockerUnavailable` is raised inside a GC pass but collectAll catches per-pass exceptions into its `errors` list, so the failure is swallowed (only logged) and the test passes.
- Red runs (e.g. under mutation testing): the traceback SHOWS `DockerUnavailable: Docker daemon unreachable at unix:///var/run/docker.sock` — this is teardown noise from _gc's real backend, NOT the failure signal. Look past it for the real AssertionError (e.g. "the complete newpool must be adopted").
- If deterministic silence is needed, also patch the backend reference held by `manager._gc` (or build the manager with gc disabled) instead of only `manager._backend`.

title: Fake-pip container test patterns for sandbox staged update (spec-driven side effects)
content:
Patterns established in tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py + test_gc.py for the rev-2 staged-update flow (mocked backend, real merge/swap exercised end-to-end):

- Fake pip containers are side-effect callables receiving the call's `spec: ContainerSpec`; they locate the host staging dir by scanning `spec.mounts` for `containerPath == STAGING_CONTAINER_PATH`, then write artifacts there: `report.json` (dict → `{"install":[{"metadata":{"name","version"}}]}`; str → raw garbage to exercise the fail-safe path; None → file omitted, also fail-safe) or a fake `delta/` populated via `_makeDistInfo` (METADATA + RECORD + payload files). This drives the REAL mergeStagedDelta/swapPools host-side machinery.
- Cross-FS staging test: monkeypatch `lib.sandbox.runtimes.python.pool_staging.os.stat` (pool_staging's `os` IS the global os module — patch is global but monkeypatch-reverted) with a delegating fake that overrides st_dev for paths ending in "newpool". Do NOT use `os.stat_result._replace`; construct from the 10-field tuple: `os.stat_result(tuple(fields))` with `fields[2]` replaced. shutil during copytree/rmtree is unaffected (it never branches on st_dev).
- The "vanished" diff transition (newVersion=None) is UNREACHABLE through the real flow — mergeStagedDelta only deletes names whose dist-infos are staged in the delta. Classify all four transitions by unit-testing module-level `_diffPoolVersions` directly; integration tests cover upgrade/fresh/unchanged.
- Byte-identical pool verification on stage failure: hash `libsDir` ONLY, not the runtime pool dir — acquiring the pool lock creates `pool.lock` as a SIBLING of libs/ during the call, which would false-positive a tree-hash diff.
- Update-all name-set test: plant a grammar-invalid dist-info (METADATA `Name: -r`) and a phantom packages.json entry; assert both pre-filter and stage commands carry exactly enumeration ∪ packages.json sorted, minus invalid names (visible in caplog as warnings).

title: Stale __pycache__ of deleted modules is a known test-failure suspect — clear caches before diagnosing
content:
Known failure suspect when running `make test` after a refactor that DELETED or renamed Python modules (notably in `lib/` and `tests/`): stale `__pycache__` directories of the deleted modules can cause confusing collection/import failures that look like real breakage. Clear them mechanically before diagnosing:

`find lib tests -name __pycache__ -type d -exec rm -rf {} +`

Only after clearing caches and re-running should a failure be treated as a real logic problem. Stated by the user (2026-09-04) as "a known suspect" — i.e., this has bitten before. title: Staged-update security-model facts verified by review: stale pool symlinks inert, pip emits no symlinks into --target, `--` layering, dual canonicalizers
content:
Non-obvious facts established while reviewing the staged-install + atomic-swap implementation (lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/pool_staging.py / pool_pip_runner.py, 2026-09-04):

1. STALE SYMLINKS IN THE POOL ARE INERT, NOT A HOLE. The pool is bind-mounted READ-ONLY into run containers at /sandbox/libs, and symlink resolution happens in the container's filesystem (container paths), never on the host — bind mounts do not chase symlinks across the mount. So a symlink planted in the pool pointing at a host file resolves to a nonexistent container path; skipping (not deleting) symlink-out RECORD entries per design §9 leaves only inert stale links. The deletion path (§11) unlinks the link and uses the resolved path solely for jail validation; broken symlinks and symlink loops are covered by _resolveJailed catching OSError/ValueError/RuntimeError.

2. EMPIRICAL PREMISE (unguarded in code): pip's wheel unpacker never reproduces symlinks into a `--target` tree — wheel zip entries with symlink mode bits are materialized as regular files. This is why the merge overlay has no symlink defense and why symlinks=False vs True in the overlay is theoretical. Pinned by the plan's spike (pip 26.2.1); no code guard exists if a future pip changes this.

3. `--` INJECTION-DEFENSE LAYERING in the pip runner: the real defense is the `--` that buildReportCommand/buildInstallCommand insert into PIP's argv (before specs), which blocks pip-option injection via pool-derived package names; the helper's OWN CLI `--` separator is cosmetic/advisory only (argparse with nargs="*" accepts specs with or without it). Host-side grammar gating (§6) is a separate layer.

4. DUAL CANONICALIZERS: manager.py:1656 uses packaging.utils canonicalize_name (snake_case, from the packaging lib) while pool_staging.py has its own canonicalizeName — both implement PEP 503 and agree; flagged for the author to confirm intentional rather than drift.

5. pip report JSON shape relied upon: install[].metadata.name/version (strings). Drift is mitigated by parsePipReport's fail-safe (None → every spec treated as outdated; wrong skip leaves packages outdated, full stage merely re-installs). {"install": []} correctly yields {} (not None) — both directions still fail safe downstream because a name absent from {} compares as outdated.

6. Empty-directory leftovers after a package's files are all deleted are an accepted, design-ratified consequence (file-only deletion protects namespace dirs; same as pip's own --target behavior; empty dirs shadow nothing because they become namespace-package portions).

title: Sandbox Phase 1R manager.py review: 3 open LOW findings + 2 informational (unfixed)
content:
Read-only review 2026-09-04 (working tree vs HEAD 3d4d9880, Phase 1R artifact) of updateRuntimeLibraries/_runStagedInstall/_recoverRuntimePool in lib/sandbox/manager.py vs docs/plans/sandbox-update-v1.md rev 2. Open low-severity findings, all UNFIXED at review time:

1. LOW latent — `_recoverRuntimePool` (scan manager.py:1525-1533, per-runtime loop 1475-1479) adopts ANY `tmp/<runId>/newpool|oldpool` from the SHARED tmp root with no runtime marker. With 2+ registered runtimes a python leftover would be adopted as e.g. the typescript pool. Unreachable today (only PYTHON registered, manager.py:264-266) but recovery code never gets re-read. Fix: stamp runDir with a `.runtime` marker file in `_runStagedInstall` (~manager.py:1838) and filter in recovery.

2. LOW — adoption/restore rename failure cascade: if `newPoolDir.rename(libsDir)` (manager.py:1541) or oldpool restore (1555) raises (documented scenario: operator symlinks layout across mounts — same case swapPools' st_dev guard defends against), the exception is logged and recovery continues; step 4 (manager.py:1482-1490) then runs prepareRuntime which creates an EMPTY libs/ (manager.py:331) and _refreshPackageList writes an EMPTY packages.json, while the complete real pool sits in tmp/<runId>/ until GC reaps it after 60 min (gc.py:226-246) → permanent pool loss with metadata claiming nothing installed. Fix: on case-1 rename failure fall through to the oldpool candidate, or in recover() step 4 skip the refresh for a runtime whose libs/ was missing before prepareRuntime when reconciliation failed.

3. LOW — `unchanged` ∩ `upToDate` overlap in LibraryUpdateResult (manager.py:1302+1308; types.py:402-404, field upToDate at 417): a pre-filter-skipped spec is never staged, survives the swap at the same version, and _diffPoolVersions therefore also classifies it as `unchanged` — one package legitimately appears in BOTH lists. Plan §5.2 doesn't forbid it; a Phase 2 renderer printing both double-reports (e.g. "numpy 1.0 → 1.0" AND "Already up to date, skipped: numpy"). Fix: exclude upToDate names from unchanged when building the result, or document the overlap on the type so _handleUpdateCommand filters.

Informational (not defects): (a) `_runPrefilterContainer` never inspects outcome.exitCode/signal/oomKilled (manager.py:1748-1773) — ratified fail-safe direction (plan §4.2), a timeout/OOM collapses into full stage; one warning log would help ops. (b) Host staging I/O blocks the event loop: copytree manager.py:1843, mergeStagedDelta 1891, swapPools 1896, old-pool rmtree 1901, recovery renames/rmtree 1541-1562 run sync on the asyncio loop — largest blocking burst in the manager; wrap in asyncio.to_thread if loop stalls surface. Consistent with existing repo sync-fs-on-loop patterns.

Related context: pip --target dry-run has no satisfaction check (see pip --target gotcha memory), so update-all BARE names rarely yield upToDate entries; the zero-download skip only fires for pinned specs already at the requested version or pools already at PyPI-latest.

title: Sandbox GC review Phase 1R: 3 pending defects (expired-session run leak, live-container kill, unvalidated rmtree)
content:
Read-only review 2026-09-04 of lib/sandbox/gc.py + tests (working tree vs HEAD 3d4d9880, Phase 1R) found 3 defects NOT yet fixed (complements memory 5aad0554: the runId cross-reference exists but only covers run containers):

F1 (MEDIUM — metadata leak): collectExpiredSessions (gc.py:68-82) deletes the session via deleteSession (gc.py:78) but never deletes that session's run records. collectExpiredRuns enumerates via loadAllSessions() (gc.py:140-141), so once the session record is gone its meta/runs/*.json are unreachable and leak forever. deleteSession has NO cascade (metadata/filesystem.py:168-179). manager's dropSession DOES cascade runs-then-session (manager.py:522-532, 1445-1453) — only the GC path leaks. test_fullCycle (test_gc.py:653-710) gives the expired session no runs, hiding the bug. Fix: before deleteSession, `for run in await self._metadata.listRunsForSession(session.sessionId): await self._metadata.deleteRun(run.runId)` (or add MetadataStore.loadAllRuns() and iterate that). Regression test: expired session with an old finished run → loadRun() is None after collectAll().

F2 (MEDIUM — GC can kill live install/update container): collectOrphanContainers protection keys on the `sandbox.runId` label (gc.py:188) but ONLY run containers carry it (manager.py:723-724). Install (manager.py:1090), pre-filter (1761-65), stage (1860-64), list (1994-98) containers carry only sandbox.managed/purpose/runtime → runId None → survive purely by age vs orphanContainerRetentionMinutes (default 10, config.py:235). Default install/stage budget 600s + 60s grace (config.py:267, manager.py:1684) ≈ 11 min > 10 min retention, and GC runs every 30 min from the bot cron (internal/bot/common/handlers/sandbox.py:223-230) → a tick in the last ~minute of a maxed-out install/stage kills the container mid-operation (age check is strict `>`). Fix: skip containers whose status=="running" in the reap loop (exited containers incl. kept-for-post-mortem failed stage containers still age out), or add sandbox.runId labels to install/update/list specs.

F3 (LOW-MEDIUM — unvalidated rmtree): collectExpiredSessions rmtree's workspacePath.parent (gc.py:73-76) with no check it really is sessions/<hash>. A parsed-but-wrong/legacy record (workspacePath = <root>/sessions itself, or outside root) makes GC delete the wrong tree. Fix: guard parentDir.parent == self._rootDir/"sessions" AND parentDir.name == session.sessionHash before rmtree; else log-and-skip.

title: Sandbox GC review Phase 1R: symlink handling + staging-age race findings
content:
Read-only review 2026-09-04 of lib/sandbox/gc.py found robustness gaps (unfixed as of then):

F4 (LOW): collectStagingArtifacts age check uses entry.stat() (gc.py:231, follows symlinks) → broken symlinks under tmp/ raise OSError → continue → NEVER reaped; symlink-to-fresh inherits target mtime and lingers. The removal branch IS symlink-safe (`not entry.is_symlink()` guard gc.py:238 → unlink the link, never the target). Fix: use entry.lstat() for the age read + stat.S_ISDIR / entry.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False) (fine on py312).

F5 (LOW): collectOrphanWorkspaces (gc.py:108-124) LACKS that guard: entry.is_dir() (gc.py:109) and stat() (gc.py:117) follow symlinks; a directory symlink under sessions/ not in knownHashes with aged target reaches shutil.rmtree(entry) (gc.py:124), which raises OSError on a symlink arg — uncaught inside the loop → aborts the whole pass (only collectAll's wrapper catches, gc.py:281-284), leaving remaining orphans unprocessed. Fix: unlink symlinks after the age check, mirroring the staging pass. Likely pre-existing; only host-side/operator action can place such a link.

F6 (LOW, residual risk config-dependent): staging run-dir mtime freezes once staging begins (child writes don't touch parent). Stage >60 min (only if operator raises install-container.timeout-seconds ≳3600 vs default 600s) would expose tmp/<runId> to GC; worst interleaving is rmtree between swapPools' two renames (manager.py:1896) — oldpool already inside runDir, newpool rename then fails → pool lost. Unreachable at defaults (plan §4.6 "in-flight runs are minutes at most" holds). Fix options: os.utime(runDir) before swapPools + after merge, or GC skips the staging pass when the pool lock can't be acquired.

title: Sandbox GC operational facts: trigger cadence, no deleteSession cascade, tmp litter sources
content:
Cross-file facts established during the 2026-09-04 Phase 1R review (not obvious from any single file):

- GC trigger points: bot cron every 30 MINUTES (internal/bot/common/handlers/sandbox.py:223-230) + once at startup inside recover()/reconcile (manager.py:1493, runs AFTER _recoverRuntimePool so newpool adoption precedes GC reaping — plan §4.5 backstop ordering). - Only RUN containers get the `sandbox.runId` label (manager.py:723-724); install/pre-filter/stage/list containers get only sandbox.managed/purpose/runtime labels → collectOrphanContainers' activeRunIds protection never applies to them.
- Kept-for-post-mortem failed stage containers (manager.py:1869-1878 returns (False, containerId)) are intentionally reaped by GC after orphanContainerRetentionMinutes (default 10).
- MetadataStore.deleteSession (filesystem.py:168-179) has NO cascade to run records; any caller wanting cascade must delete runs first (manager dropSession does; GC does not — see F1).
- atomicWriteJson writes `.tmp-*` temp files DIRECTLY into <root>/tmp (storage.py:145-148); _refreshPackageList litter writes <uuid>.stdout/.stderr into tmp/ (manager.py:2002-2027, unlinked even on failure) — both are reaped by collectStagingArtifacts by age (orphanWorkspaceRetentionMinutes default 60, config.py:236); this interaction is intended and documented in gc.py docstrings.
- libUtils.now() returns tz-aware UTC (lib/utils/utils.py:404-406) → no naive-datetime skew in GC age math; all metadata datetimes written aware.
- Stage-failure path cleans the run dir in finally but keeps the container for docker logs; pool untouched (manager.py:1869-1901).

title: Phase 1R BLOCKERS: symlink deref in mergeStagedDelta, empty-libs recovery suppression, rollback-failure rmtree
content:
Three BLOCKER-class defects found in the uncommitted Phase 1R staged-update code (all UNFIXED at 2026-09-05 review; root causes + fixes):

**1. pool_staging.py:343 `mergeStagedDelta` — host dereferences container-controlled symlinks.** `shutil.copytree(deltaDir, poolCopy, dirs_exist_ok=True)` uses default `symlinks=False`, so the HOST bot process dereferences symlinks planted in the delta (written by pip incl. arbitrary PEP 517 build code): `delta/leak -> /proc/self/environ` gets its target content copied into poolCopy; swapPools lands it in the live pool mounted read-only into every run container → sandbox code reads host secrets (bot token). Partial exfil works (copytree collects errors only after copying). Compounding retarget attack: if the container replaces `newpool` with a symlink, `poolCopy.resolve()` → the LIVE pool → merge mutates it non-atomically AND swapPools renames the symlink into `libs` with success=True (pool destroyed; the deletion jail itself is NOT escaped — the protected root is silently swapped). Fix: `symlinks=True` in the overlay (hostile link lands as a link; run containers resolve it in-container where host paths don't exist); reject symlinked/non-dir delta root; defense-in-depth: refuse `poolCopy.is_symlink()` before merge/swap. Special files safe already (copy2 raises SpecialFileError → pre-swap abort). Tests: staged absolute/dir/dangling symlink → host target content must NOT appear in merged copy (red under current code); symlinked poolCopy → merge/swap refuse.

**2. manager.py:1517-1518 `_recoverRuntimePool` — empty libs/ suppresses crash recovery → permanent pool loss.** `if libsDir.exists(): return` treats EMPTY libs as "pool present". Combined with: (a) recovery is ONE-SHOT — only caller `SandboxHandler._dtCronJob` gated by `self._recoveryDone` flipped True BEFORE the call, no retry ever; (b) `prepareRuntime` does `libsDir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` BEFORE the prep lock (manager.py:329-331), reachable pre-tick via the `run_python` LLM tool (NOT owner-gated), `/sandbox run`, `/sandbox install`; (c) GC reaps tmp/<runId> after 60 min. Chain: crash between the two renames → restart → any request creates empty libs → tick-1 recovery returns early → refresh blesses empty pool + wipes packages.json → GC deletes complete newpool/oldpool. Fix (one line, ordering-independent): `if libsDir.exists() and any(libsDir.iterdir()): return` — POSIX rename(dir, existing_empty_dir) SUCCEEDS so adoption still lands; also consider invoking recover() at application startup. Test: leftover tmp/<runId>/newpool + EMPTY libsDir → adoption must occur (fails under current code); pin that rename onto an existing empty dir succeeds.

**3. pool_staging.py:375-381 + manager.py:1898-1901 — failed rollback made unrecoverable.** If the second rename (newPool→pool) fails AND the rollback rename (parking→pool) also fails, both complete copies sit in tmp/<runId>/ but `_runStagedInstall`'s unconditional `finally: shutil.rmtree(runDir, ignore_errors=True)` deletes BOTH — libs missing, nothing to adopt, "no holes ever" violated. st_dev guard rules out EXDEV; remaining causes exotic (EBUSY/ESTALE/NFS, target non-empty) but low-probability × catastrophic × one-line fix. Fix: `finally: if libsDir.exists(): shutil.rmtree(runDir, ignore_errors=True)` — every other path (copy/stage/guard failure, success) has libs present; failed-rollback state leaves complete newpool for recover() case-1 adoption. Also wrap rollback in try/except OSError re-raising the ORIGINAL error (currently rollback OSError masks root cause). Test: patch rename to fail on calls 2 AND 3 → error propagates AND tmp/<runId>/{newpool,oldpool} survive with libs missing → recover() adopts (extend flakyRename pattern from test_pool_staging.py:940-988).

title: Phase 1R MAJORS + minors: runDir over-mounted rw incl. newpool, recovery fail-open, GC kills update containers
content:
Major/minor findings from the 2026-09-05 consolidated Phase 1R review (all UNFIXED):

**MAJOR 1 — manager.py:1703-1714 `_stagingMounts` binds the ENTIRE runDir rw at /sandbox/staging, and newpool already exists inside it** (copytree'd at manager.py:1842-1843 BEFORE the stage container runs at 1847; container user 1000:1000 = same uid as staging files in typical deployment). Build code can rewrite/delete newpool or symlink-retarget it (see blocker on poolCopy resolve → live pool). Note BOTH update containers are exposed: pip `--dry-run` (pre-filter, manager.py:1753) still executes PEP 517 build backends for sdists → arbitrary package code runs in the "read-only" pre-filter too. Root-cause fix: mount only an isolated io subtree (runDir/delta or runDir/io holding delta/ + report.json) — create delta host-side BEFORE runOneshot (currently manager.py:1889-1890, after); keep newpool/oldpool outside EVERY container mount (apply to both containers); report.json outside delta/ so the overlay can't copy it into the pool. Test per plan §12: stage AND report ContainerSpecs must mount no hostPath containing newpool's path.

**MAJOR 2 — manager.py:1475-1493 recovery fails open.** Adoption/restore rename exceptions are logged-and-ignored; step 4 then runs prepareRuntime (creates empty libs at manager.py:331), refreshes metadata (empty packages.json), step 5 runs staging GC → transient rename/perm/stat failure converts a recoverable crash artifact into a blessed empty pool, possibly deleted in the same recover() call if beyond retention. Fix: track per-runtime success; on reconciliation failure skip prepare/refresh/GC for that runtime and leave retryable; on case-1 newpool adoption rename failure fall through to case-2 oldpool candidate.

**MAJOR 3 — gc.py:186-203 container GC can kill an ACTIVE update container at defaults.** Reap protection keys on the `sandbox.runId` label, but only RUN containers carry it (manager.py:723-724); install/pre-filter/stage/list containers are unlabeled → survival is purely age vs `orphan-container-retention-minutes=10` (configs/00-defaults/sandbox.toml:41), while the install/stage budget is timeout 600s + 60s grace ≈ 11 min > 10 min; GC every 30 min from bot cron (internal/bot/common/handlers/sandbox.py:223-230); boundary comparison `createdTs > cutoff → continue` proceeds to kill at exactly the boundary. Fix (minimal): skip containers with `status == "running"` (ManagedContainerInfo.status, types.py:588); exited containers (incl. kept failed stage containers) still age out. Alternative: label update containers with the staging runId and treat a live tmp/<runId> as active.

**MINORS:** (a) recovery adoption + step-4 refresh run OUTSIDE poolLock — in-process torn swap refuted (rename pair is synchronous under the lock holder), residual: cross-process race with scripts/sandbox_bootstrap.py live-pool installs (until Phase 1I) and lockless refresh racing a lock-holding updateRuntimeLibraries; fix: wrap steps 3+4 per runtime in a NON-BLOCKING poolLock (skip+log if held). (b) manager.py:1617-1619 `_enumeratePoolVersions` picks the FIRST dist-info of duplicate canonical names from unordered enumeration → pre-filter can classify the name up-to-date and never run the merge that removes all duplicates; fix: force multi-dist-info names into the outdated set + regression. (c) types.py LibraryUpdateResult doc drift: oldVersion is derived from pool enumeration (not packages.json); `unchanged` and `upToDate` can legitimately overlap (pre-filter-skipped spec appears in both — a Phase 2 renderer would double-report); document the overlap or exclude upToDate names from unchanged; `success` should acknowledge no-op/all-current results. (d) NIT: tests/lib/sandbox/test_gc.py:608 function-local `import shutil` violates AGENTS.md imports-at-top (also :409, :89, :124 pre-existing in helpers).

title: Sandbox update gotchas: dry-run executes build backends, rename-onto-empty-dir, one-shot recovery, GC lstat
content:
Mechanistic facts confirmed during the 2026-09-05 Phase 1R review (load-bearing for the sandbox staged-update design and future fixes):

1. **pip `--dry-run` still executes PEP 517 build backends for sdists** (pip builds to obtain metadata) → arbitrary package code runs in the pre-filter container. The "read-only" pre-filter is NOT code-safe; BOTH update containers are attack surface. Owner-only gating (isBotOwner) limits likelihood, not relevance — PyPI packages are the designated attack surface (plan §11).
2. **POSIX rename(dir, existing_empty_dir) SUCCEEDS** — recovery adoption (newpool → libs) works even when libs/ exists but is empty; the proposed `any(libsDir.iterdir())` guard in _recoverRuntimePool is safe to add.
3. **Relative symlink targets need no host-path knowledge to escape a mount**: `../../runtimes/python/libs` planted under a rw-mounted staging dir resolves host-side; `env={}` on the container does not mitigate (symlinks are pure strings).
4. **shutil.copytree(symlinks=False) dereferences in the HOST process**, recursing into symlinked dirs; errors are COLLECTED and raised only after copying → partial copies land before shutil.Error. Always use symlinks=True when copying untrusted trees.
5. **Recovery is one-shot by design-as-implemented**: `SandboxHandler._recoveryDone` is flipped True BEFORE recover() on the first cron tick; any suppression (e.g. empty libs early-return) is never retried. First CRON_JOB fires immediately at scheduler start (rescheduled +60 s; scheduler task created before polling starts) and races inbound messages on the same loop; scheduler start includes DB task restores.
6. **GC tmp reaping is by mtime; a run-dir's mtime FREEZES once staging begins** (child writes don't touch the parent) — an in-flight tmp/<runId> ages out only if the stage exceeds orphan-workspace-retention-minutes (default 60 min vs 600 s budget: unreachable at defaults, reachable if operator raises install timeout to ≳3600 s). Mitigation if needed: os.utime(runDir) before swapPools, or GC skips the staging pass when the pool lock is held.
7. **Path.stat()/entry.stat() follow symlinks** — for age-based reaping use lstat()/stat.S_ISDIR (or is_dir(follow_symlinks=False), fine on py312); broken symlinks raise OSError on stat and are otherwise NEVER reaped.
8. **`{"install": []}` pip report parses to `{}` (not None) and is still fail-safe**: a name absent from {} compares as outdated downstream. parsePipReport returns None only on missing file/bad JSON/non-dict root/missing install[] — that None must degrade to "stage all specs".

title: Code-review process: sequential-baseline hazard, verdict supersession discipline, subagent shell limits
content:
Review-process lessons from the 2026-09-05 Phase 1R consolidated review:

1. **Sequential-baseline hazard**: when a working tree accumulates multiple diff layers (superseded revision, fix rounds, current revision), review the CURRENT tree state as the artifact — never flag remnants already deleted from the tree, and never demand rollback of absorbed layers as "diff noise". The Phase 1R review prompt explicitly sanctioned this (3 layers atop 1cebcba9; rev-1 live-target flow deleted from tree; `pool_update_packages.py` gone except doc/memory greps; `installCommand` intentionally kept until Phase 1I; `installRuntimeLibraries` still live-pool = NOT a finding).
2. **Baseline discrepancies**: user-cited baseline 1cebcba9 vs actual HEAD 3d4d9880 — check `git log` first; if intervening commits don't touch the reviewed subtree, state the equivalence and proceed.
3. **Verdict supersession discipline**: per-scope subagent verdicts (PASS / no-blocker-major) can be invalidated by CROSS-COMPONENT threat analysis (stage-container mount scope × merge symlink handling × swap trust). The consolidated reviewer must re-grade severity across components and explicitly record the supersession in memory, so future sessions don't act on stale PASS verdicts (db4c2c8c, fb3f0b5e are superseded by the NEEDS-FIXES verdict).
4. **Subagent capabilities**: code-analyst task subagents in this setup had NO shell (no git diff, no lint/test runs) — they review the working tree as-is; the coordinating agent must run verification itself. Verified for Phase 1R: make lint clean; ./venv/bin/pytest tests/lib/sandbox -q → 301 passed/10 skipped; ./venv/bin/python scripts/check_docs.py → 0 broken links.
5. **Uncommitted-but-ratified plan doc** (docs/plans/sandbox-update-v1.md rev 2, itself modified in the working tree) was treated as the authoritative spec per the review prompt's instruction.
6. `.opencode/memory.jsonl` (modified in git status) is excluded from review scope per repo rules.

title: Sandbox GC supplement: orphan-workspace symlink aborts sweep + stale container-GC "stub" claims
content:
Supplement to memory 174e820c (GC review F1-F3) — remaining GC findings from the 2026-09-05 Phase 1R consolidated review, UNFIXED:

- **collectOrphanWorkspaces lacks the symlink guard its staging sibling has** (gc.py:108-124): `entry.is_dir()` and `stat()` follow symlinks; a directory symlink under sessions/ not in knownHashes with an aged target reaches `shutil.rmtree(entry)` which RAISES OSError on a symlink argument — uncaught inside the loop, aborting the whole pass (only collectAll's wrapper swallows it), leaving remaining orphans unprocessed that sweep. title: Phase 1R fix round A applied: io/ mount scope, links-as-links merge, PoolSwapRollbackFailed
content:
Fix round A (Gate-1 review) applied to the uncommitted Phase 1R tree in lib/sandbox/. This SUPERSEDES the "unfixed-at-review" status of the blocker memory (557c5759) for: its #1 (mergeStagedDelta symlink deref), its #3 (failed-rollback rmtree), plus the major finding (stage container could modify the future live pool) and the nit (function-local import in test_gc.py). STILL OPEN, deliberately deferred to round B: #2 `_recoverRuntimePool` empty-libs suppression (one-line fix `if libsDir.exists() and any(libsDir.iterdir()): return` proposed there) and other recovery/GC findings. `installRuntimeLibraries` untouched — Phase 1I must reuse the shared `_runStagedInstall(runtime, runtimeImpl, specs, timeoutSeconds, *, purpose)` core unchanged.

**New staging run-dir layout (mount-scope fix):** `<tmpDir>/<runId>/{io/, newpool/, oldpool/}`. ONLY `io/` (holding report.json + delta/) is container-mounted rw at STAGING_CONTAINER_PATH; newpool/oldpool live OUTSIDE every mount, so stage-container build code can no longer delete/rewrite/symlink the future live pool. `STAGING_IO_DIRNAME = "io"` constant in manager.py; `_stagingMounts` mounts runDir/io; `_runPrefilterContainer` + `_runStagedInstall` pre-create io/ (Docker would auto-create binds, but we create explicitly). Container-side paths unchanged (/sandbox/staging/report.json, /sandbox/staging/delta) → reportCommand/stageInstallCommand/pool_pip_runner.py needed NO changes. recover()/GC deliberately unchanged: `_recoverRuntimePool` expects entry/"newpool" + entry/"oldpool" at run-dir ROOT (io/ siblings), and GC reaps whole run dirs by mtime (layout-agnostic).

**Symlink policy = links-as-links** (documented in mergeStagedDelta docstring): `copytree(..., dirs_exist_ok=True, symlinks=True)`; guards raise `LibraryInstallFailed` for a symlinked poolCopy, symlinked or non-directory deltaDir; `enumerateDistInfos` skips symlinked *.dist-info entries (is_symlink() checked BEFORE is_dir()). Safety rationale: an absolute hostile link landing in the pool resolves INSIDE run containers (mount namespace → container's own files), never on the host — the load-bearing invariant is "the HOST process never dereferences container-controlled symlinks". The enumeration skip extends the "never delete what you cannot account for" convention.

**Rollback-failure design:** new `PoolSwapRollbackFailed(LibraryError)` in errors.py — attrs pool, oldPoolParking, swapError, rollbackError; swap error chained as __cause__; both errors in the message; re-exported from lib/sandbox/__init__.py. swapPools semantics: rename#2 (newpool→libs) fails + rollback rename#3 succeeds → plain OSError, run dir still cleaned (existing contract intact); BOTH fail → PoolSwapRollbackFailed (old pool stays parked, libs absent, both complete copies survive in run dir). `_runStagedInstall` catches it, logs, sets rollbackFailed, `finally` skips shutil.rmtree → run dir preserved; recover() case-1 then adopts newpool ("no holes, ever", plan §4.5); GC is the age-based backstop. Note PoolSwapRollbackFailed is NOT an OSError, so existing `pytest.raises(OSError)` tests pin the ordinary-failure vs rollback-failure distinction automatically.

**Tests added:** tests/lib/sandbox/runtimes/test_pool_staging.py — TestStagedSymlinkPolicy (7 tests: absolute/dir/dangling staged links copied as links with host targets unread, symlinked delta root rejected, non-dir delta root rejected, symlinked poolCopy rejected, symlinked dist-info in delta skipped by enumeration) + TestSwapPools::testRollbackFailureRaisesPoolSwapRollbackFailed. tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py — io/ mount-scope assertions + `_scopeCheckingStage` wrapper in testReportAndStageContainerSpecs; testRollbackFailurePreservesRunDirForRecovery (renames #2+#3 fail → run dir survives → recover() adopts newpool).

**Verification at session end:** `make format lint` clean; targeted suites green (test_pool_staging + test_gc: 64 passed; test_manager: 37 passed); all 4 mutation spot-checks red→restored with no leftovers (drop symlinks=True; unconditional rmtree; mount whole runDir; remove root guards). The FULL `make test` was the one mandatory gate NOT yet run when steps ran out.

Review-fix-round conventions honored: strict scope (no internal/, docs/, CHANGELOG.md, TODO.md), tests written against the FINAL io/ layout, contradictions reported not improvised.

title: Path.is_dir()/is_file() follow symlinks — check is_symlink() first on container-controlled trees
content:
Generalizable Python pitfall behind the sandbox staging symlink blocker: `Path.is_dir()`, `.is_file()`, `.exists()` all FOLLOW symlinks. A planted `*.dist-info -> /outside/dir` entry passes `is_dir()` enumeration checks, so host-side validation reads METADATA through the link; if the stolen name matches a staged package, the host then DELETES the real old dist-info — all without the host "intending" to dereference anything. Rule for this repo: when validating any tree a container could have written, test `entry.is_symlink()` BEFORE `is_dir()`/`is_file()`, and skip symlinked entries ("never delete/read what you cannot account for").

Related shutil.copytree behavior (why the default is dangerous here): `symlinks=False` (default) dereferences — absolute and directory symlinks copy their TARGET content into the host-side destination, and a DANGLING symlink makes copytree raise OSError mid-copy (it collects errors only after copying). With `symlinks=True`, links are copied verbatim (absolute stays absolute) and dangling links copy fine as links.

Pre-fix red-test design pattern for this class of bug: assert the OLD behavior's observable — the merged entry `is_symlink()` (was a regular file with target content pre-fix); the legitimate old dist-info survives (was deleted pre-fix when enumeration followed the link); the outside target file/dir is never materialized under the pool copy.

title: Monkeypatching Path.rename for pool-swap failure tests — global patch, name-based dispatch
content:
Technique + gotchas for testing rename-swap failure paths (sandbox staged update, tests/lib/sandbox/):

- A `Path.rename` monkeypatch is GLOBAL — manager and pool_staging use the same pathlib.Path class. Dispatch on (path.name, target.name), e.g. fail only `path.name in {"newpool", "oldpool"} and target.name == "libs"` to kill exactly swap rename#2 + rollback rename#3; never count call order (metadata/other code may rename in between).
- Call `monkeypatch.undo()` before any later phase that legitimately renames — notably `manager.recover()` (adopts via `newPoolDir.rename(libsDir)`), else recovery fails under the still-active patch.
- The rename patch is safe across the rest of the update flow: metadata `atomicWriteJson` (lib/sandbox/storage.py) uses `os.replace`, and locks use flock — neither touches Path.rename.
- test_manager.py helper `_oneshotSequence` raises AssertionError when runOneshot gets MORE calls than scripted steps. If the same test then calls `recover()`, re-wire `backend.runOneshot = AsyncMock(return_value=_makeContainerOutcome(exitCode=0))` for the recovery-phase containers (prepare/refresh) before undoing the rename patch.
- Mount-scope regression technique: wrap the delta side effect to assert DURING the container window that the staging mount's hostPath basename == "io" and that newpool is a SIBLING of it (not inside) — fails immediately if `_stagingMounts` ever reverts to mounting the whole run dir. Existing helpers: _makeMockBackend, _makeContainerOutcome, _stagingHostDir, _reportSideEffect, _deltaSideEffect in tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py.
- Test naming is mixed across the sandbox tests: test_pool_staging.py and test_manager.py use camelCase test names; test_gc.py uses snake_case — follow the host file's convention when adding tests.
- During review-fix rounds the tree is uncommitted, so mutation spot-checks (remove guard → red → restore) must restore edits by hand; grep for mutation markers afterwards to prove no leftovers.

title: Phase 1R fix round B applied: fail-closed pool recovery, GC staging-run-dir liveness, duplicate force-outdated
content:
Fix round B (Gate-1 review, 2026-09-05) applied to the uncommitted Phase 1R tree in lib/sandbox/. Baseline before changes: `make test` green at 4541 passed / 11 skipped. Supersedes the "unfixed-at-review" status of memories 557c5759 (empty-libs recovery suppression) and aab0cca1 (recovery fail-open, GC kills update containers) for the findings below.

Design decisions (all on the round-A `io/` staging layout):

1. Empty-libs no longer suppresses recovery (blocker). `_recoverRuntimePool` collects leftover candidates FIRST; a non-empty `libs` still wins, but an existing EMPTY libs dir is `rmdir()`ed before adoption when crash leftovers exist. Pre-op wiring: `updateRuntimeLibraries` calls `await self._reconcileRuntimePool(runtime, refreshMetadata=False)` at method start (otherwise update-all would short-circuit to "Nothing installed" over an unrecovered pool), AND a second `self._recoverRuntimePool(runtime)` inside the mutation-phase pool lock before baseline enumeration (closes the defer-then-proceed race where `_runStagedInstall`'s `libsDir.mkdir` would bless an empty pool). `installRuntimeLibraries` calls `_recoverRuntimePool` INSIDE the already-held lock before its mkdir — deliberately NOT a nested lock acquisition, because flock is per open-file-description and re-acquiring on a second fd in the same process deadlocks/EBUSY (extends known gotcha 6e735f79).

2. Fail-closed recovery (blocker). New `_reconcileRuntimePool(runtime, *, refreshMetadata) -> bool`: non-blocking `poolLock` acquisition; `LibraryPoolLocked` → defer (False, leftovers untouched, startup never blocks); any exception → False. `recover()` steps 3–5 track per-runtime success: failed runtimes skip `prepareRuntime`/refresh, and staging GC is skipped entirely via a new `includeStaging: bool = True` kwarg threaded `collectGarbage` → `GarbageCollector.collectAll` when ANY runtime failed (run dirs carry no runtime marker, so per-runtime staging-GC filtering is impossible — skip-all is the minimal safe semantics). `_recoverRuntimePool` falls back newpool → SIBLING oldpool within the same run dir and raises the last OSError when every rename fails. Root cause found mid-session: the original `elif`-based candidate collector registered a run dir holding BOTH newpool and oldpool as newpool-only, making the oldpool fallback dead code — collector restructured to carry `(mtime, kind, newPoolDir, oldPoolDir, runDir)` per run dir, sorted kind-asc (newpool-bearing first) then mtime-desc.

3. GC staging liveness (major). Pre-filter (`_runPrefilterContainer`) and stage (`_runStagedInstall`) ContainerSpecs now carry label `sandbox.stagingRunId=<runId>`; `collectOrphanContainers` treats a labeled container as active while `<root>/tmp/<runId>/` exists. Residual out-of-scope risk flagged: install/list containers still have no liveness marker and share the same retention-vs-runtime exposure.

4. Recovery under poolLock (minor) — covered by `_reconcileRuntimePool` above (adoption + refresh inside the lock).

5. Duplicate dist-infos (minor). `_splitOutdatedSpecs(specs, baselineVersions, report, duplicateNames)` forces names with MULTIPLE dist-info entries into the outdated set; new `_collectDuplicatePoolNames` helper; threaded through `_runPrefilterContainer`.

6. types.py docstring corrections: `PackageUpdate.oldVersion` derives from pool enumeration (not packages.json); `LibraryUpdateResult.success` also covers no-op/all-current results; `metadataRefreshed` failure does NOT under-report the diff (diff uses before/after enumerations).

Test-contract change to flag in review: `testEmptyOutdatedEarlyReturnsWithoutLockOrStage` now asserts exactly ONE pool-lock acquisition (the mandated opportunistic recovery) instead of zero.

title: APFS iterdir order nondeterministic — first-entry pool-version pick made the duplicate-dist-info mutation check vacuous
content: In `lib/sandbox/manager.py`, `_enumeratePoolVersions` resolves a canonical name to the FIRST entry of an unordered `iterdir()` over dist-infos. On macOS/APFS directory order is NOT creation order: in one run `foo-2.0.dist-info` was enumerated before `foo-1.0.dist-info` even though 1.0 was created first. Consequence observed: a test hardcoding the pip report version to the "first created" dist-info (`_reportSideEffect({"foo": "1.0"})`) passed VACUOUSLY with the duplicate-force-outdated guard mutated away, because the baseline enumerated foo=2.0, mismatched the report, and classified the spec outdated via the ordinary path. Correct test pattern: derive the report version from the production enumeration itself — `reportVersion = manager._enumeratePoolVersions(libsDir)["foo"]` — and build the report from that, so ONLY the `duplicateNames` guard can classify the spec as outdated. General rule: never assume directory-entry order in tests, and treat any logic picking `entries[0]` as nondeterministic (this nondeterminism is exactly why finding 5 forces duplicated names into the outdated set).

title: Staging-GC tests must age the RUN DIR entry, not a subdir, or GC-skip mutation checks pass vacuously
content: `GarbageCollector.collectStagingArtifacts` iterates `<root>/tmp` and stats each run-dir ENTRY's mtime directly — it never looks at mtimes nested inside the run dir. Fix-round-B tests initially aged only `<runDir>/newpool` via `_ageDirByMtime(runDir / "newpool", minutes=120)`, so a mutation forcing the staging pass to run (`allReconciled = True`, i.e. removing the `includeStaging=False` skip) still reaped nothing and the fail-closed test passed vacuously. Correct pattern: `_ageDirByMtime(runDir, minutes=120)` on the run dir itself (default retention 60 min per `orphanWorkspaceRetentionMinutes`). Aging the run dir is safe for recovery tests: `_recoverRuntimePool` uses the NEWPOOL subdir's mtime only for candidate sort order, and tests with a single run dir are unaffected. Applies to any future test of staging-artifact aging or GC-skip behaviour.

title: Sandbox duplicate-guard fix round COMPLETED (2026-09-05): guard restored, test deterministic, mutation verified RED→GREEN
content: 2026-09-05 completion of the interrupted fix-round-B (previously tracked by a now-deleted stale memory): in `lib/sandbox/manager.py` `_splitOutdatedSpecs` the duplicate-force-outdated guard `if canonicalName in duplicateNames: outdated.append(spec); continue` is restored verbatim, and `tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py::testDuplicateDistInfoNameForcedOutdatedAndHealed` is fixed to be order-deterministic per the APFS iterdir gotcha — manager constructed BEFORE backend side effects, then `reportVersion = manager._enumeratePoolVersions(libsDir)["foo"]` and `_reportSideEffect({"foo": reportVersion})` so report == baseline and ONLY the duplicateNames guard can classify the spec outdated. Test-infra note: `_makeManager` wires `manager._backend = backend`, so `backend.runOneshot` may be assigned after manager creation (same mock object). Mutation verification is now empirically confirmed: guard removed → test RED with exactly the right failure (`result.upToDate == ['foo']` vs `[]`, i.e. "duplicated name classified up-to-date"); guard restored → GREEN. `make format lint` clean; `make test` 4552 passed / 11 skipped. No changelog entry (restore of committed behavior + test-only change are both exempt). Durable process lesson (from the interrupted round this completed): finish each mutation spot-check (sabotage → RED → restore → final sweep) BEFORE session steps run low, never defer it to "after everything else".

title: MUTATION marker sweep must be case-SENSITIVE; `rg -i MUTATION` can never return empty on this repo
content: When sweeping for leftover `# MUTATION:` sabotage markers, the sweep MUST be case-sensitive: `rg "MUTATION" lib/ tests/` (or `grep -rn "MUTATION" lib/ tests/ internal/`). The `-i` variant (which appeared in a handoff and in the old fix-round-B checklist as `rg -i MUTATION lib/ tests/` — "must return NOTHING") is UNSATISFIABLE on this repo: pre-existing lowercase "mutation" domain prose exists across lib/ and tests/ — e.g. "dict mutation" regression tests in `tests/services/stats/test_service.py` (testDictMutationRaceDuringIteration, aggregateWithMutation), docstrings in `lib/ai/providers/yc_sdk_provider.py` and `lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/pool_staging.py`, and "mutation phase" feature docstrings. Purging those violates scope and would damage legitimate domain vocabulary (snapshot→mutation→after-snapshot is the staged-update terminology). Corollary: even a case-sensitive sweep is tripped by uppercase PROSE tokens — `tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py` `testEmptyOutdatedEarlyReturnsWithoutLockOrStage` docstring said "the MUTATION phase never runs" (domain vocabulary, not a marker) and had to be reworded to "the staging phase never runs" to keep the sweep clean; write domain prose with a lowercase "mutation" or a synonym. When a handoff verification item as literally written conflicts with its own scope constraint, resolve by INTENT (marker sweep, per the marker convention), apply only the minimal in-scope edit, and report the literal-command deviation with evidence.

title: Phase 1R one-lock contract RESOLVED: testEmptyOutdatedEarlyReturns ==1 lock is correct and mutation-sensitive
content:
Read-only test-quality review (2026-09-05, code-analyst) of the uncommitted Phase 1R sandbox tree RESOLVES the round-B "flag for review" item from memory 6351faa5: the new expectation in `testEmptyOutdatedEarlyReturnsWithoutLockOrStage` (tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py:1280-1334) that the empty-outdated early return performs EXACTLY ONE pool-lock acquisition is CORRECT and MEANINGFUL, not a weakening.

Why it's genuine:
- Production contract: `updateRuntimeLibraries` runs the opportunistic `_reconcileRuntimePool` at manager.py:1219 (acquires `locks.poolLock` non-blockingly at manager.py:1729) BEFORE the empty-outdated early return at manager.py:1302-1314; the mutation-phase lock at manager.py:1316 is never reached → exactly 1 acquisition.
- Correct patch seam: the test patches `sandboxLocks.poolLock` (test_manager.py:1320); manager imports the module (`from . import locks`, manager.py:23) and resolves `locks.poolLock` at call time, so both acquisition sites are intercepted. The recording wrapper appends then DELEGATES TO THE REAL FLOCK (test_manager.py:1316-1318) — the counter reflects real lock behavior, not a mock tally.
- Mutation-sensitive in both directions: reconciliation removed → 0 calls → red; empty-outdated short-circuit regressed (mutation phase runs) → 2 calls → red. `backend.runOneshot.await_count == 1` (:1333) additionally pins "no stage container".

Gotcha for future test edits on this seam:
- Patching `lib.sandbox.locks.poolLock` works ONLY because manager does `from . import locks` (module-attribute lookup at call time). Any refactor to `from .locks import poolLock` would silently bypass the patch.

Drift to fix (LOW, test-file-only):
- Test NAME "WithoutLockOrStage" now contradicts its own one-lock assertion; module docstring test_manager.py:18-19 still claims "empty-outdated early success (no lock, no stage container)". Both are stale vs the documented round-B design (one opportunistic non-blocking acquisition). Risk: a future reader "corrects" the assertion back to zero.
- Minor semantic note: the wrapper records calls before entering the real lock, so under contention it counts failed attempts too (irrelevant in this uncontended test).

title: Sandbox recovery locking model: all _recoverRuntimePool sites locked; _reconcileRuntimePool defers; no nested poolLock in production
content:
From the 2026-09-05 Phase 1R re-review (findings 7-10 focus, HEAD 3d4d9880): the recovery locking model in lib/sandbox/manager.py is now fully locked and deadlock-free.

- `_recoverRuntimePool` (the ONLY live-pool recovery mutations: rmdir empty libs, newpool→libs rename, oldpool→libs rename, rmtree runDir) has exactly THREE call sites, every one under `async with locks.poolLock(...)`: installRuntimeLibraries (manager.py:1078, lock :1069), updateRuntimeLibraries in-lock second recovery (:1323, lock :1316), and `_reconcileRuntimePool` (:1730, lock :1729). Verified by repo-wide grep — no other callers.
- `_reconcileRuntimePool` (:1699-1739) is the non-blocking opportunistic wrapper: it catches LibraryPoolLocked AND generic Exception and returns False (defer) — it can never abort a caller or leak the lock. Callers: updateRuntimeLibraries :1219 (refreshMetadata=False) and recover() step 3 :1541 (refreshMetadata=True). recover() is fail-closed: a failed reconciliation skips prepareRuntime and staging GC for that runtime (:1550-1566).
- updateRuntimeLibraries lifecycle: the :1219 opportunistic pass is SEQUENTIAL before the mutation-phase lock (:1316), not nested. The in-lock recovery at :1323 calls `_recoverRuntimePool` DIRECTLY (plain sync method, never touches the lock) — critically it does NOT route through `_reconcileRuntimePool`, which would attempt a second flock on a fresh fd and spuriously fail (flock binds to the open file description; see memory 6e735f79). PRODUCTION COROLLARY: never nest locks.poolLock acquisitions in the same process; when already holding the lock, call _recoverRuntimePool directly.
- Pre-filter container runs WITHOUT the pool lock by design (read-only: mounts only the run-dir io/ subtree rw + helper ro, never the pool; writes confined to <root>/tmp/<runId>, removed in finally).
- Release ordering: stage-failure early return exits the async-with (lock released); `_refreshPackageList` runs inside the lock; the updated/unchanged diff is computed AFTER release from captured before/after enumeration snapshots.
- Recovery failure is fail-closed: `_recoverRuntimePool` re-raises the last OSError when all adoption renames fail → propagates out of the async-with → lock released → operation aborts, crash leftovers stay retryable.
- Tests pinning these invariants: testEmptyOutdatedEarlyReturnsWithoutLockOrStage (tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py:1280-1334, exactly one lock acquisition on the no-mutation path), testRecoveryDefersWhenPoolLockHeld (:2063-2105), test_locks.py:635-691 (lock file must be a sibling of libs, not inside it — mutual exclusion must survive the staged swap).

title: Sandbox pool recovery must run BEFORE libsDir.mkdir (empty libs suppresses adoption)
content: From the 2026-09-05 Phase 1R re-review. Ordering invariant in installRuntimeLibraries: `_recoverRuntimePool` runs BEFORE `libsDir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` (manager.py:1078 before :1081-1082, inside the pool lock). Rationale: an empty libs directory created by mkdir-first would suppress crash adoption (recovery's libs-missing check). Recovery also independently removes an empty libs before adopting (manager.py:1634-1641), so the hole is closed twice — this is also what makes prepareRuntime's outside-lock libsDir mkdir safe. Same discipline for any future pool-mutating entry point: recover first, then mkdir. Failure semantics: adoption OSError re-raised (manager.py:1697) → propagates out of the async-with → lock released → install fails closed, crash leftovers intact and retryable; LibraryPoolLocked propagates from the non-blocking lock acquire itself (nothing is mutated before the lock — spec validation only).
