Finding-1 symlink residuals: (a) RECORD/METADATA files inside an ACCEPTED (non-symlink) dist-info dir are opened without per-file link checks (pool_staging.py ~L154, ~L227) — a planted link causes a bounded in-process host read-through (derived data only drives jailed deletions/name matching, so info-leak is minimal); (b) a RECORD path whose INTERMEDIATE component is an in-pool symlink deletes the RESOLVED target file rather than the literal path (~L292-95) — could delete another package's file in the pool copy, but requires an already container-corrupted pool; confined to the copy pre-swap.

title: updateRuntimeLibraries ignores _reconcileRuntimePool boolean — update-all path (b) returns false success over stranded crash leftovers
content:
2026-09-05 REVIEW-ONLY finding (unfixed-at-review) in lib/sandbox/manager.py `updateRuntimeLibraries`: the boolean from the opportunistic reconciliation pass `await self._reconcileRuntimePool(runtime, refreshMetadata=False)` at manager.py:1219 is DISCARDED (unlike recover(), which consumes it fail-closed at :1539-1548). Consequence: when the pass returns False, the method can return success=True through the update-all "Nothing installed" early exit (manager.py:1269-1281, via read-only `_collectUpdateAllNames` :1829-1868) WITHOUT reaching the in-lock `_recoverRuntimePool` retry at :1323 — re-opening the exact bug window that fix-round-B item #1 (memory 6351faa5) added the :1219 pass to close. The happy path is covered by testUpdateAllAdoptsCrashLeftoverBeforeCollectingNames (tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py:1706-1744), but the pass-failure branch has zero coverage (no test references `_reconcileRuntimePool` anywhere in tests/).

Path triage (why only update-all is exposed):
- (a) empty named list (:1222-1232): benign by ratified contract (test :1436-1453; "A named-but-empty request updates nothing; only None means 'all'" :1221) — no container, no mkdir, no mutation.
- (b) update-all + empty name set: THE GAP. Returns success while a complete newpool/oldpool sits unadopted in staging.
- (c) all-up-to-date (:1304-1314): structurally SAFE — `_splitOutdatedSpecs` (manager.py:85, esp. :122-127) forces every spec outdated when baselineVersions is empty, so empty-outdated implies a non-empty live pool, and `_recoverRuntimePool` treats a non-empty pool as the winner with leftovers as GC debris (:1634-1637) — the skipped retry would have been a no-op.

Cause conflation blocks a clean fix: `_reconcileRuntimePool` converts BOTH LibraryPoolLocked (:1734-1736, non-blocking flock from locks.py:300-302/321) AND any other exception including the adoption-failure OSError (:1737-1739) into a single False. Lock-busy is transient/self-healing (the holder completes its swap); adoption-failure is persistent and is the harmful case — the docstring's promise "OSError: If crash-recovery adoption failed under the pool lock (fail closed)" (manager.py:1194-1201) never materializes via path (b). The in-method comment at :1216-1218 ("the mutation phase re-attempts recovery under the lock") is false for (b) — there is no mutation phase on that exit.

Mitigating fact (verified): none of the three early-success exits creates libsDir, so the empty-libs-suppresses-adoption hazard is NOT triggered; damage is a misleading success + eventual leftover reaping (see recovery-lifecycle memory).

Fix shape that does NOT conflict with ratified semantics: propagate failure only when `reconcileOk is False AND libsDir absent-or-empty` at the :1271 check. Preserves: empty-named-list success (:1436-1453), all-current-no-lock (:1280-1334), and genuinely-empty-RECONCILED-pool "Nothing installed" success (testEmptyPoolNoArgEarlyReturnsWithoutBackendCall :1414-1434 covers only the reconciled case). title: Sandbox recovery lifecycle: recover() is single-shot per process; periodic GC not gated on reconciliation reaps stranded leftovers after ~60 min
content:
Two non-obvious lifecycle facts (2026-09-05 review of internal/bot/common/handlers/sandbox.py + lib/sandbox/manager.py + gc.py) that undermine the "leftovers stay retryable, a later tick adopts them" reasoning used in several sandbox-recovery code comments:

1. recover() is SINGLE-SHOT per process, not a recurring cron. The sandbox handler runs it once on the first cron tick guarded by a `_recoveryDone` flag (internal/bot/common/handlers/sandbox.py:213-217; consistent with manager.py:1211 "the cron recover() normally handles this on its first tick"). So any comment/deferral logic assuming "a later recovery tick will retry" is wrong in steady state — deferral really defers to the NEXT MUTATION REQUEST (install/update reaching the pool lock) or an APP RESTART, nothing automatic.

2. The PERIODIC GC is not reconciliation-gated. The same handler runs collectGarbage() every 30 minutes with the default includeStaging=True (sandbox.py:225-229), unlike recover()'s gated call `collectGarbage(includeStaging=allReconciled)` (manager.py:1565-1566, where any failed runtime skips the staging pass because run dirs carry no runtime marker). collectStagingArtifacts (gc.py:223+) reaps staging run dirs by mtime older than orphanWorkspaceRetentionMinutes — default 60 min (gc.py:241, configs/00-defaults/sandbox.toml:42). Net effect: crash leftovers stranded by a failed/deferred opportunistic pass are destroyed ~60 minutes later by the periodic GC; subsequent recovery finds no candidates (manager.py:1629-1632) and treats the absent pool as fresh — the only recoverable pool copy is permanently lost until packages are reinstalled. (The fix-round-B container-label liveness protection covers only labeled prefilter/stage containers, not stranded leftovers while no container is running.)

These two facts are what elevate a "misleading success" return in updateRuntimeLibraries (ignored `_reconcileRuntimePool` boolean, see companion memory) from cosmetic to potential data loss. Any future fix reviewing deferral semantics in the sandbox pool-recovery code must account for: no automatic retry tick + un-gated staging GC on a 60-minute fuse.

title: Verification: staged-symlink fix NOT fully resolved — file-level METADATA/RECORD opens unguarded
content:
2026-09-05 REVIEW-ONLY verification of the fix for prior Phase-1R blocker 1 (see memory 557c5759). VERDICT: NOT fully resolved — the fix closes only the directory-level case; a file-level gap remains.

RESOLVED part: symlinked `.dist-info` DIRECTORY is skipped — pool_staging.py:194 (`entry.is_symlink() or not entry.is_dir(): continue`), tested by testSymlinkedDistInfoInDeltaSkippedNotFollowed (tests/lib/sandbox/runtimes/test_pool_staging.py:1072). copytree now `symlinks=True` (:370), delta/poolCopy roots guarded (:338-341).

RESIDUAL GAP A — `_parseDistInfoDir` pool_staging.py:152-154 opens `<real dist-info>/METADATA` with no symlink check (no O_NOFOLLOW anywhere). Reachable on the FIRST update, no planted state needed: `enumerateDistInfos(deltaDir)` :343 parses every real dist-info in the fresh container-controlled delta (io/ mounted rw at manager.py:2075-2090); also `enumerateDistInfos(poolCopy)` :344 and live-pool enumerations manager.py:1799/1823/1848 (live pool is container-written from day one: legacy install binds libsDir rw at libMountPath, manager.py:1095-1102, `pip install --target` runtime.py:119-131). Planting needs no symlink: a plain FIFO as METADATA works. A symlink inside the container resolves in the HOST namespace when the host opens it.

RESIDUAL GAP B — `readRecordPaths` pool_staging.py:225-227 opens RECORD with no symlink check; only production call site mergeStagedDelta:355 on pool-copy dist-infos. The dir is guaranteed real (line 194 skipped link-dirs) but RECORD inside can be a planted link propagated by copytree(symlinks=True) :370 → swap → live → next update's copy manager.py:2081.

IMPACT (availability-dominant, Medium):
- FIFO as METADATA or RECORD → blocking open() → PERMANENT EVENT-LOOP HANG: mergeStagedDelta runs synchronously inside `async def _runStagedInstall` (manager.py:1999 → call :2135, no to_thread; only to_thread in lib/sandbox is locks.py:305). Whole-bot freeze; persistent — re-fires every update touching that name once planted in live pool.
- Symlink → /dev/zero-style stream → OOM: `\x00` is not whitespace so `line.strip()` (:156) stays truthy, readline never finds `\n` → unbounded line buffer.
- Binary METADATA → UnicodeDecodeError NOT caught: :161 has `except OSError` only (UnicodeDecodeError is a ValueError subclass); contradicts the documented per-entry-skip contract (:183-186) and crashes the staging run (before deletions — pool untouched, but update pipeline dies). RECORD site DOES catch UnicodeDecodeError at :356, but a blocking FIFO open raises nothing so the catch never fires.
- Host-file read through planted link = invariant violation ("the HOST process never reads through a planted link" :319-325, module docstring :13-15); no direct exfil channel back to the container observed; weak timing/existence oracle (dangling → instant OSError fallback; FIFO → hang).
- NOT at risk: deletion amplification — jail `_resolveJailed` :254-259 holds, symlinked candidates link-only-unlinked :285-291, dirs refused :292-294; `Path.resolve()` never opens targets (FIFOs don't block it); parsed `Name:` adds nothing (dir stem already gives full name control). Swap is pure rename.
- Same class, third instance: parsePipReport pool_staging.py:447 opens container-written report.json (manager.py:1994).

TEST COVERAGE GAP: TestStagedSymlinkPolicy (test_pool_staging.py:872-1114) covers only root-level delta links (:882/:918/:952), root guards (:980/:1017/:1034), and symlinked dist-info DIR (:1072). NO test plants symlink/FIFO/binary METADATA or RECORD inside a REAL dist-info dir (delta or pool copy); no "second update" test re-enumerating a pool copy with previously merged planted links.

FIX SHAPE (not applied — review-only): file-level lstat/is_symlink gate or O_NOFOLLOW open on METADATA + RECORD (and report.json); add `except UnicodeDecodeError` to _parseDistInfoDir to honor its skip contract; run merge/report parsing off the event loop (to_thread).

title: Why adopting a surviving newpool is safe: libs-missing ⇒ post-merge invariant
content:
Crash-recovery completeness invariant for the sandbox library pool (verified 2026-09-05 delta re-review of lib/sandbox/manager.py + runtimes/python/pool_staging.py) — non-obvious, prevents future reviewers from re-flagging "partial newpool adoption" as a bug:

A surviving `newpool` in a staging run dir is guaranteed COMPLETE whenever adoption fires, because adoption only triggers when `libs` is missing-or-empty (`_recoverRuntimePool` rmdirs an empty libs first, manager.py:1634-1641), and `libs` is removed ONLY by swapPools' first rename `pool → oldpool` (pool_staging.py:411), which runs only AFTER the stage merge completed. Consequences:
- Crash during copytree/stage/merge leaves `libs` NON-empty → live pool wins and the leftover run dir is GC debris (manager.py:1636-1637). No partial-newpool adoption is possible.
- The only empty-libs-with-partial-newpool corner implies the pre-update pool was itself empty (first-ever update on an empty pool), where a partial copy of nothing is harmless.
- The libs-missing crash windows are exactly: between rename1/rename2 (complete newpool + oldpool both present → adopt newpool, :1643 kind-0 first), and after rollback failure (both preserved in the run dir → recover() adopts; testRollbackFailurePreservesRunDirForRecovery :1529).

Candidate selection details (manager.py:1614-1697): candidates are `(mtime, kind, newPoolDir, oldPoolDir, runDir)`; newpool-bearing kinds sort before oldpool-only REGARDLESS of age (documented rationale :1611-1613: a surviving merged copy always wins); newest mtime first within a kind. A failed newpool rename falls back to the SIBLING oldpool in the SAME run dir (:1670-1692); both failing raises the last error fail-closed (:1693-1697), leaving leftovers intact for retry. Only candidates[0] is processed per pass; other run dirs remain staging-GC debris by design (docstring :1591-1592).

title: flock binds per open-file-description + pool-lock assertion test technique
content:
Two verified facts about the sandbox pool lock (2026-09-05 delta re-review), useful for reasoning and writing tests:

1. fcntl.flock locks bind to the OPEN FILE DESCRIPTION, not the process: two separate `open()` calls on the same lock file within one process DO conflict — a second `LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB` flock fails fast with EWOULDBLOCK → `LibraryPoolLocked` (lib/sandbox/locks.py:299-302). Only dup'd FDs share a lock. Therefore: sequential acquire/release in one process is fine (updateRuntimeLibraries' opportunistic reconcile at manager.py:1219 releases the lock before the mutation-phase acquire at :1316); accidental nesting can NEVER deadlock — it fails fast, and inside `_reconcileRuntimePool` it converts to a deferral (returns False). Lock acquisition itself runs in `asyncio.to_thread` (locks.py:~305) and `acquirePoolLock` mkdirs poolDir (locks.py:293) — creating poolDir is benign for recovery since `_recoverRuntimePool` only inspects `libs` and `<root>/tmp/*`.

2. Test technique for asserting lock behavior: wrap the REAL `poolLock` with a recording decorator (append path to `lockCalls`, delegate to the captured real lock) and monkeypatch it onto the locks module — this works because manager.py does attribute lookup `locks.poolLock(...)` at call time on the shared module object. The pattern (testEmptyOutdatedEarlyReturnsWithoutLockOrStage, tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py:1280-1334, asserts `len(lockCalls) == 1` + `runOneshot.await_count == 1`) catches: nested double-acquire (LibraryPoolLocked raised through the REAL flock → test errors) and a mutation-phase acquisition (count == 2). Fixture note: pool fixtures create `runtimes/python/` via mkdir(parents=True), so a bare `open(poolDir/"pool.lock", "a")` works when a pool exists (test :913-942); crash-scenario tests with NO pool must `poolDir.mkdir(parents=True)` explicitly before holding the flock (test :2087).

title: Fake-container runtime scope-check pattern: verify mount containment during execution, not just spec shape
content:
Testing pattern from the Phase 1R sandbox review (test_manager.py): for container-mount isolation guarantees, pair structural spec assertions with a RUNTIME scope check inside the fake container.

- Structural: `testReportAndStageContainerSpecs` (tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py:819-834) asserts `len(spec.mounts) == 2`, no `libMountPath` mount, staging hostPath endswith `/io`, and no `newpool`/`oldpool` substring in any hostPath.
- Runtime: the fake stage container itself (`_scopeCheckingStage`, test_manager.py:841-873) re-verifies at execution time that `newpool` is a SIBLING of the mounted directory and does not exist inside it.

Why both: a future regression that silently widens the mount to the whole run dir can still pass shape assertions (e.g. if the spec grows a third legitimate mount and the count assertion gets loosened), but the runtime check fails the test mid-flow while the fake container actually runs — catching the real exploitation path, not just the spec shape. Generalizes to any security boundary expressed via mounts/paths: assert the spec AND have the fake consumer verify containment at the moment it "uses" the resource.

title: Leaf-file no-follow guard `_isRegularLeaf` in pool_staging (fix round C) — per-site rejection semantics
content:
2026-09-05 fix round C CLOSED the file-level gap from memory cec90061: all container-controlled leaf-file opens in lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/pool_staging.py are now guarded BEFORE any open by a new `_isRegularLeaf()` helper — `Path.is_symlink()` OR-fail, then `stat.S_ISREG(path.lstat().st_mode)`, `except OSError: return False`. NO-FOLLOW semantics; never `Path.is_file()` (follows links). Rationale: planted symlink crosses the container/host trust boundary, FIFO blocks the host event loop indefinitely on open, device-like streams can exhaust memory, non-UTF-8 METADATA must not crash enumeration.

Per-site rejection mapping (deliberate, test-locked):
- METADATA (`_parseDistInfoDir`): PRESENT-but-non-regular (symlink/FIFO/device, incl. dangling links: `exists() or is_symlink()`) → warn + return None (entry skipped by caller's generic "leaving it alone" path). `UnicodeDecodeError` on read → warn + return None (previously escaped enumeration). ABSENT METADATA and plain `OSError` mid-read → existing dir-stem fallback PRESERVED (required by `testStemFallbackWithoutMetadata` — do not make FileNotFoundError skip the entry).
- RECORD (`readRecordPaths`): non-regular/missing → raise `OSError` (same shape as missing/unreadable) so `mergeStagedDelta`'s documented per-package skip applies: warn, skip that package's deletions, staged copy still lands beside the untouched old dist-info.
- pip report (`parsePipReport`): non-regular → warn + return None (fail-safe: every spec treated as outdated). UnicodeDecodeError/OSError catches already existed at this site.

Invariant across all new tests (TestContainerControlledLeafFiles in tests/lib/sandbox/runtimes/test_pool_staging.py): sibling packages must still process, and host-side link targets must remain untouched/unread.

title: updateRuntimeLibraries false-success guard: empty update-all find + failed/deferred recovery must fail closed
content:
2026-09-05 fix round C (lib/sandbox/manager.py): `updateRuntimeLibraries` previously discarded `_reconcileRuntimePool`'s bool; if the opportunistic recovery deferred (lock busy) or failed AND update-all found no names, it returned a false "Nothing installed" success while complete crash leftovers sat stranded under `<root>/tmp/` — later destroyable by periodic staging GC.

Fix: capture `reconciliationOk = await self._reconcileRuntimePool(...)`. In the empty update-all branch: `if not updateAllNames and not reconciliationOk and self._hasPoolCrashLeftovers():` → retry recovery under `locks.poolLock` (new `_hasPoolCrashLeftovers()` helper = cheap read-only mirror of `_recoverRuntimePool`'s candidate scan: any `<root>/tmp/<runDir>/` carrying `newpool/` or `oldpool/`), then re-collect names; a still-empty set (leftovers were GC debris beside a live pool) returns the now-honest empty success. A recovery that still fails PROPAGATES — `LibraryPoolLocked` (lock still busy; documented raise, acceptable per "either recovers after lock release or propagates") or `OSError` (failed adoption renames; leftovers preserved for retry).

Deviations worth remembering: (1) `locks.poolLock` has NO blocking mode (non-blocking flock only, raises LibraryPoolLocked — see memory 4fd873aa); the retry reuses it instead of adding one — a still-busy lock fails closed rather than blocking the caller. (2) Docstrings updated: `installRuntimeLibraries` Raises += recovery OSError; `updateRuntimeLibraries` Raises += `PoolSwapRollbackFailed` (exactly what `_runStagedInstall` raises) with clarified LibraryPoolLocked/OSError sources.

title: Monkeypatching pool_staging os.stat is PROCESS-WIDE — fake must forward kwargs and accept str|Path
content: Extends memory 460158b9 with a trap hit in fix round C: patching `"lib.sandbox.runtimes.python.pool_staging.os.stat"` replaces the attribute on the SHARED `os` module, so every `os.stat` call in the process hits the fake — not just swapPools. Consequences: (1) callers pass both `Path` objects (pool_staging) and plain `str` (e.g. `shutil.copystat` internals), so match paths with `str(path).endswith("newpool")`, never `path.name` (AttributeError on str → testCrossFsStagingRaisesConfigError broke). (2) `shutil.copystat` calls `os.stat(src, follow_symlinks=...)` during copytree, so a single-arg fake raises TypeError — forward kwargs. Pyright-clean typed signature with no type-ignore: `def fakeStat(path: str, **kwargs: bool) -> os.stat_result:` forwarding to `realStat(path, **kwargs)` (`dir_fd` is never used in this flow, so `kwargs: bool` suffices for `follow_symlinks`). Also: mutating/rebuilding st_dev uses `fields = list(result); fields[2] = 999999; os.stat_result(tuple(fields))`.

title: Mutation-testing FIFO/no-open guards: guard removal makes the test BLOCK — run under timeout, exit 124 is the red signal
content: Technique from fix round C verification of the `_isRegularLeaf` no-open guard: when the guard on a FIFO leaf (`os.mkfifo` RECORD in tests) is removed/mutated away, the production code's `open()` on the FIFO blocks forever — the test doesn't fail, it HANGS. Run the mutated test under `timeout 30 ./venv/bin/pytest ...` and treat exit 124 (kill) as the mutation being caught; this is precisely the proof that the guard rejects BEFORE any open (correct code returns instantly, no writer ever needed). For follow-semantics mutations, replacing the guard body with `return path.is_file()` kills the three symlink tests (symlinked METADATA/RECORD/report.json) without hanging, but the FIFO test stays green under that mutation (is_file() on a FIFO is False) — hence the second `return True` + timeout mutation is needed for full FIFO coverage. The suite-level `timeout 5m` wrapper would mask this as a whole-suite kill, so always demo FIFO mutations with an explicit per-command timeout.

title: Accepted-by-design races in sandbox staging: leaf TOCTOU + leftover-check vs second-process GC
content:
Two races in the Phase 1R sandbox staging/recovery flow are ACCEPTED BY DESIGN — flagged informational in the 2026-09-05 round-C review and NOT previously recorded; do not "fix" either without revisiting the plan ratification (docs/plans/sandbox-update-v1.md):

1. Leaf-file check-then-open TOCTOU (pool_staging.py): `_isRegularLeaf()` guard followed by `.open()` is not atomic — a writer swapping the leaf between guard and open could win the race. Safe operationally because the container FINISHES STAGING before the host parses/merges, so no concurrent writer exists in the normal flow. Full hardening would be `os.open(..., O_NOFOLLOW)` + `fstat` on the fd; explicitly not required by the review criteria.

2. Leftover-check-vs-GC race (manager.py updateRuntimeLibraries guard): between `_hasPoolCrashLeftovers()` and the guard's non-blocking `poolLock` acquisition, a SECOND PROCESS's staging GC could in principle reap the leftovers, making the empty "Nothing installed" return honest-but-late. In-process this cannot happen: recover() skips staging GC when reconciliation failed (manager.py ~:1588). Leftovers are also retention-aged.

Related latent issue RECONFIRMED in the same review (already tracked as aca20874 finding 1, still unfixed-by-design): `_recoverRuntimePool`/`_hasPoolCrashLeftovers` scan the shared `<root>/tmp/` without qualifying candidates by runtime (run dirs are `tmp/<uuid4hex>`, runtime only in the container label). Harmless while RuntimeName has a single member (PYTHON); a second pooled runtime could get the wrong runtime's pool adopted — stamp/filter before adding one.

title: Phase 1I: installRuntimeLibraries unified onto staged core; upgrade is a documented no-op
content:
Implemented 2026-09-05 per docs/plans/sandbox-update-v1.md §5.5/§5.6 (uncommitted at the time). Facts not obvious from a glance at the code:

- `installRuntimeLibraries(packages, *, runtime, upgrade=False, timeoutSeconds=None) -> bool` now calls `self._runStagedInstall(runtime, runtimeImpl, validated, timeoutSeconds, purpose="install")` INSIDE the existing `poolLock` hold; the in-lock `_recoverRuntimePool` call is preserved immediately before the core. Signature unchanged (bootstrap + handler compatibility). Success → best-effort `_refreshPackageList` (wrapped in try/except, never fails the install); stage failure → returns False, stage container kept, pool untouched.
- `upgrade` is now a DOCUMENTED NO-OP: pip `--target` has no satisfaction check, so a staged install always resolves fresh into the empty delta — nothing for `--upgrade` to do. The param is retained solely for `scripts/sandbox_bootstrap.py` call compatibility (bootstrap passes `upgrade=args.upgrade`; `tests/scripts/test_sandbox_bootstrap.py` passes unchanged). This SUPERSEDES earlier memory 259913f7: the old "upgrade plumbing exists end-to-end" is gone — `upgrade` no longer reaches any command.
- `Runtime.installCommand` deleted from `lib/sandbox/runtimes/base.py` (ABC) and `lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/runtime.py`; grep-verified the sole caller was the replaced manager call site (manager.py:1097). Its 4 argv tests (incl. `--upgrade` expectations) removed from `tests/lib/sandbox/runtimes/test_python_runtime.py`.
- Install container contract, pinned by `TestInstallRuntimeLibrariesStagedCore.testInstallContainerSpecStagesIntoIoSubtree` in tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py: container name `sandbox-install-<runId>`; argv == `runtimeImpl.stageInstallCommand(specs)`; labels `sandbox.purpose="install"` + `sandbox.managed` + `sandbox.runtime` + `sandbox.stagingRunId`; EXACTLY 2 mounts — staging `io/` subtree rw + helper ro; NEVER the live pool (no `libMountPath`, no newpool/oldpool in any hostPath).
- Raises docstring corrected: `installRuntimeLibraries` returns False on stage failure and NEVER raises `LibraryInstallFailed` (the old docstring wrongly listed it). Actual raises: `InvalidPackageSpec` (all specs invalid), `LibraryPoolLocked`, `UnknownRuntime`, `ConfigError` (helper missing / staging cross-FS), `OSError` (crash-recovery adoption), `PoolSwapRollbackFailed`.

title: Sandbox staged-core test kit: _deltaSideEffect staging-mount guard + install-vs-update lock divergence
content:
Test-infrastructure facts for the staged install/update core in tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py:

- The fake-backend helper `_deltaSideEffect({name: version})` writes a fake staged delta into the ContainerSpec's staging `io/` mount and RAISES AssertionError ("ContainerSpec has no staging mount") when the spec has none. This is the mechanism that makes the install-path tests red on ANY non-staged implementation — the pre-fix code mounted the pool at `libMountPath` instead of a staging dir, so the regression needs no pip simulation.
- Companion helpers: `_makeDistInfo(poolDir, "numpy-1.0.dist-info", name=, version=, payloadFiles=[...])` builds a REAL dist-info (METADATA + RECORD + payload files with content `body of <relPath> @ <version>`); `_makePool`; `_oneshotSequence` (ordered side_effect list); `_makeContainerOutcome(exitCode=, containerId=)`.
- Ratified-bug regression `testReinstallingPresentPackageReplacesOldDistInfo`: real pool with old dist-info + RECORD + files, fake staged 2.0 delta; asserts the pool ends with EXACTLY ONE dist-info for the name, shared paths recreated with the NEW version's content, old-only files gone (deleted per the old RECORD by `mergeStagedDelta`), and truthful metadata. `testFreshInstallIntoEmptyPool` covers copy-of-empty → merge → swap.
- Mutation sensitivity is dual by construction because install and update share the staging helpers (`_stagingMounts` / `_stagingLimits` in manager.py): removing the per-RECORD old-dist-info deletion in `pool_staging.mergeStagedDelta` (e.g. `stagedNames.clear()`) breaks BOTH the install reinstall regression AND the update duplicate-heal test; adding a pool mount inside `_stagingMounts` breaks BOTH the install mount-assertion test AND the update container-spec test. When mutating the shared core, expect both suites to go red — don't "fix" one and think the other is collateral.
- `LibraryPoolLocked` divergence: update runs its pre-filter report container BEFORE the pool lock (so a locked pool still shows 1 backend call before the raise); install has NO pre-filter — a held lock raises with ZERO backend calls, so `runOneshot.assert_not_awaited()` is the correct assertion in the install lock test.

title: Phase 1I install-path unification audit verdict (2026-09-05) — conformant, no High/Medium
content:
Read-only audit (2026-09-05) of the Phase 1I delta in lib/sandbox/manager.py::installRuntimeLibraries against docs/plans/sandbox-update-v1.md §§5.5/5.6/9-12/14-Phase-1I. VERDICT: fully conformant; zero correctness findings. Complements the existing Phase 1R-b memory (2ea1c6dd) which recorded the implementation contract; this records the verified outcome.

Clean checks (all traced at then-current line numbers, will drift):
- No live-pool container install remains: sole mutation call is `_runStagedInstall(..., purpose="install")` (~manager.py:1108-1110); stage container mounts come from `_stagingMounts` — only run-dir `io/` subtree rw + helper ro; live pool/newpool/oldpool outside every mount. No pre-filter on install (§5.5 "installing is intentional") — `_runPrefilterContainer` is called only from updateRuntimeLibraries.
- ONE `async with locks.poolLock(runtime, poolDir)` (~manager.py:1093) spans in-lock `_recoverRuntimePool` (~:1103) + copy/stage/merge/swap (~:1108) + best-effort refresh (~:1116-1124); flock released via context-manager finally even when exceptions propagate (locks.py:335-338).
- Stage failure returns False, container kept, pool untouched (`_runStagedInstall` returns `(False, outcome.containerId)` without removing container); success refresh is try/except best-effort and cannot flip the bool result.
- All-invalid specs raise aggregated InvalidPackageSpec BEFORE any container starts; partial failures logged+skipped (only valid specs reach the container).
- LibraryPoolLocked (locks.py:296-305), OSError from `_recoverRuntimePool` total-rename-failure, ConfigError (helper missing / cross-FS st_dev guard in pool_staging.swapPools), PoolSwapRollbackFailed (run dir deliberately preserved for startup recovery) all propagate and are documented in the docstring.
- `upgrade` param kept but documented no-op; pinned by testUpgradeFlagAcceptedAndIgnored (no --upgrade in argv).
- Signature `installRuntimeLibraries(packages, *, runtime, upgrade=False, timeoutSeconds=None) -> bool` unchanged; both production callers pass unchanged: scripts/sandbox_bootstrap.py (~:177-181, `upgrade=args.upgrade`) and internal/bot/common/handlers/sandbox.py (~:1194).
- Runtime.installCommand deleted from runtimes/base.py and runtimes/python/runtime.py; ZERO dangling references to `installCommand`/`install_command`/`INSTALL_COMMAND`/`installCmd` in lib/, tests/, scripts/ (also zero for sibling §5.6 deletions buildPipCommand, PIP_INSTALL_ARGS, dedupPool, pool_update_packages).
- In-lock recovery wired for install and pinned by testInstallRecoversLeftoversWithEmptyLibsPreCreated (adoption runs before _runStagedInstall's libsDir.mkdir can bless an empty pool over crash copies) — matches the existing recovery-before-mkdir gotcha memory (ccaa2c36).
- Acceptance test class: TestInstallRuntimeLibrariesStagedCore in tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py (~:763+) covers staging-mount isolation, already-present reinstall regression, fresh install, stage-failure pool-untouched, all-invalid raise, partial proceed, LibraryPoolLocked propagation, upgrade no-op.

Audit was read-only (tests read, not executed); closing the loop requires `./venv/bin/pytest tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py::TestInstallRuntimeLibrariesStagedCore -v` + `make format lint && make test`.

title: Sandbox install path residuals: §11 refresh-mount deviation, no dedicated LibraryPoolLocked catch, all-or-nothing install, discarded kept container id
content:
Plan-accepted residual risks in the sandbox INSTALL path surfaced by the 2026-09-05 Phase 1I audit — none are defects, but all can surprise future work:

1. `_refreshPackageList` mounts the LIVE pool rw into a networked (`network="bridge"`) container (manager.py ~:2234-2256), against the letter of plan §11 ("the live pool is never mounted into a networked container"). Phase-1R behavior kept per §5.6; `pip list` performs no fetches. Phase 1I added a second caller (install success path) — install and update both refresh inside the pool lock.
2. The `/sandbox install` handler (internal/bot/common/handlers/sandbox.py ~:1194-1222) catches only InvalidPackageSpec + generic Exception — a lock-busy install renders via the generic catch as "Error: Library pool for runtime python is locked by another process" rather than the §8 dedicated lock-busy copy. Propagation itself is correct and test-pinned; the dedicated LibraryPoolLocked import arrives with the Phase 2 update handler per plan §7.
3. Install is now ALL-OR-NOTHING per invocation: if pip fails on any one spec in a mixed batch, no package lands (pool untouched) — ratified §5.5/§9 semantic, but a user-visible change vs the old live-pool path where pip may have partially populated the pool.
4. The kept stage-failure container id is DISCARDED for install callers (`success, _keptContainerId = self._runStagedInstall(...)` — install returns plain bool per §5.5 "Return type stays bool; handler contract unchanged"), so the failure reply is the generic "Failed to install packages. Check logs for details."; the container id is discoverable only via docker ps/logs/GC labels. Intentional asymmetry with updateRuntimeLibraries, which returns LibraryUpdateResult.containerId (§8).

title: Dead code: installRuntimeLibraries all-invalid tail `return False` unreachable
pool_pip_runner.buildInstallCommand is the helper's --install-into mode, NOT a dangling Runtime.installCommand reference
content: When auditing for deleted `Runtime.installCommand` references (Phase 1I / §5.6 deletions), do NOT flag `lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/pool_pip_runner.py::buildInstallCommand(targetDir, specs)` (~line 74) — it is the in-container helper's `--install-into` staged-install entry point, which plan §5.6 explicitly KEEPS. The Runtime protocol after the deletion exposes only: runCommand, reportCommand, stageInstallCommand, listCommand, parseListCommandOutput, updateHelperHostPath, validatePackageSpec, getScriptName (lib/sandbox/runtimes/base.py + runtimes/python/runtime.py). Sibling §5.6 deletions verified fully gone as of 2026-09-05: buildPipCommand, PIP_INSTALL_ARGS, dedupPool, pool_update_packages — zero *.py references.

title: Phase 1I: installRuntimeLibraries unified onto staged core; installCommand removed
content: Phase 1I "install-path unification" (docs/plans/sandbox-update-v1.md §5.5 at line 255, Phase 1I section at line 369) is implemented: `SandboxManager.installRuntimeLibraries` (lib/sandbox/manager.py:1004-1011, signature `(packages, *, runtime, upgrade=False, timeoutSeconds=None)`) routes through the SAME `_runStagedInstall` staged copy/stage/merge/swap core as `updateRuntimeLibraries`. Install has NO pre-filter (intentional): installing an already-present package is a clean re-install — `mergeStagedDelta` deletes the old dist-info per its RECORD and copies the staged one, fixing the ratified pip --target corruption. `upgrade=` is a documented no-op kept only for bootstrap-script compat (never forwarded). Production `Runtime.installCommand` (live-pool pip --target builder) was REMOVED — protocol now has `stageInstallCommand` (lib/sandbox/runtimes/base.py:117; python/runtime.py:126). `TestInstallCommand` was deleted from tests/lib/sandbox/runtimes/test_python_runtime.py (no dangling references); coverage moved to manager-level `TestInstallRuntimeLibrariesStagedCore` (8 tests, tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py:762-1084) plus retained argv-shape tests (TestStageInstallCommand, test_python_runtime.py:157-173). Callers: bot handler calls `installRuntimeLibraries(packages=packages, runtime=RuntimeName.PYTHON)` (internal/bot/common/handlers/sandbox.py:1194, no upgrade/timeoutSeconds); scripts/sandbox_bootstrap.py:177-181 passes positionally with `runtime=runtime, upgrade=args.upgrade`. NOTE: a stale note in the repo's .opencode/memory.jsonl (line 1852) still claims TestInstallCommand exists at test_python_runtime.py:114-148 — outdated, could mislead future agent sessions.

title: StagedCore test architecture: _oneshotSequence dispatcher + fake delta side effects
content: `TestInstallRuntimeLibrariesStagedCore` (tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py:762-1084) tests the host-side staged-install core with a mocked backend; the reusable patterns: (1) `_oneshotSequence` (:224-262) is a fail-loud dispatcher for `backend.runOneshot` — raises AssertionError on extra/missing calls; use it instead of plain list `side_effect` when steps would be callables (AsyncMock returns list elements as-is, never invoking them). (2) `_deltaSideEffect` simulates the container: it discovers the staging mount via `_stagingHostDir` (:277, raises AssertionError "ContainerSpec has no staging mount" if the spec lacks the STAGING_CONTAINER_PATH mount) and writes the pip delta under `<staging>/delta`; this makes install tests fail mechanically if production regresses to mounting the live pool. (3) `_makeDistInfo` (:156-193) builds dist-info fixtures matching exactly what production consumes: METADATA Name:/Version: headers (parsed by `enumerateDistInfos`, lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/pool_staging.py:193-199), RECORD as pool-root-relative CSV paths + `<dir>/RECORD,,` self-entry (consumed by `readRecordPaths`, pool_staging.py:284-292; deletion by `mergeStagedDelta`, pool_staging.py:363-427), payload files with version-tagged bodies. The 8 tests pin: container spec (mounts io/ rw + helper ro, never the pool; labels purpose=install + stagingRunId; name prefix sandbox-install-), reinstall regression, fresh install into empty pool, stage-failure keeps pool byte-identical (full-tree sha256), all-invalid specs raise InvalidPackageSpec pre-container, partial-invalid proceeds with valid specs, LibraryPoolLocked propagation (raised before libsDir.mkdir), upgrade= no-op.

title: Reinstall regression test power + RECORD fixtures: hashes/sizes fake but inert
content: `testReinstallingPresentPackageReplacesOldDistInfo` (tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py:854-909) genuinely distinguishes the old live-pool pip --target behavior via three assertions mapping 1:1 to the corruption symptoms: (1) exactly one dist-info survives — `[p.name for p in libsDir.glob("numpy-*.dist-info")] == ["numpy-2.0.dist-info"]` (:897-898) catches skipped RECORD-based deletion; (2) payload `numpy/__init__.py` content embeds the new version (:903) — the load-bearing check for stale code/lying metadata; (3) old-only file `numpy/old_extra.py` gone (:905) — proves deletion is driven by the OLD dist-info's RECORD, not the delta's file set. On the pre-fix path the test fails mechanically (no staging mount → `_stagingHostDir` AssertionError → success False). Fixture realism limit worth remembering: `_makeDistInfo` RECORD hash column is 8 zeros (not 64-hex sha256) and recorded sizes (`11 + len(path)`, :186) omit the version-suffix length — numerically fake but INERT because `readRecordPaths` reads only the path column and nothing validates hashes/sizes today. Delta omits INSTALLER/WHEEL/REQUESTED files pip emits — irrelevant to the code under test. If RECORD hash validation is ever added, these fixtures break loudly (acceptable).

title: Bot /sandbox install test mock under-pinned: only packages kwarg asserted
content: tests/bot/test_sandbox.py:618,623-625: the /sandbox install handler test uses a bare `AsyncMock(return_value=True)` for `installRuntimeLibraries` and asserts only `callArgs[1]["packages"]`. Because AsyncMock accepts any call shape, a handler regression dropping `runtime=RuntimeName.PYTHON` (a TypeError against the real keyword-only signature at manager.py:1004-1011) would PASS the test and break in production. Contrast: tests/scripts/test_sandbox_bootstrap.py:196-198 pins the exact bootstrap call `(["numpy","pandas"], runtime=RuntimeName.PYTHON, upgrade=True)` matching scripts/sandbox_bootstrap.py:177-181. Related path fact: the pool lock file is `poolDir / "pool.lock"` where poolDir = `<rootDir>/runtimes/<runtime>` (lib/sandbox/locks.py:294; acquired at manager.py:1067/1093) — tests hold fcntl flock on exactly that path to trigger LibraryPoolLocked.

title: Staged install/update tests require CWD = repo root (helper pre-check)
content: `_runStagedInstall` (lib/sandbox/manager.py:2065-2069) pre-checks the pip helper at the repo-relative path `lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/pool_pip_runner.py` (derived from `updateHelperHostPath()` = install-Dockerfile directory) and raises ConfigError if the file is missing. Consequence: ALL staged install/update tests (TestInstallRuntimeLibrariesStagedCore and update-side classes) implicitly require pytest to run from the repo root — running from any other directory turns the whole suite into ConfigError failures. Consistent with the project's "run everything from repo root" rule, but a latent fragility when debugging tests from an IDE with a different working directory.

title: Known weak spots in Phase 1I staged-install tests (review findings)
content: Findings from the 2026-09 Phase 1I test audit (all low severity, none blocking): (1) Manager-level command assertions `stageSpec.command == runtimeImpl.stageInstallCommand([...])` (test_manager.py:835, 1016, 1080) are self-referential — a break INSIDE `stageInstallCommand` (e.g., losing the `--` separator) passes at manager level; argv shape is only pinned by the separate TestStageInstallCommand.testArgvShape (test_python_runtime.py:157-173). (2) The StagedCore class never asserts the stage container is REMOVED on success (only keep-on-failure at :969-970); success-path removal is covered by TestInstallRuntimeLibrariesContainerCleanup.testInstallRemovesInstallContainerOnSuccess (test_manager.py:679-708). (3) `testStageFailureKeepsContainerAndPoolUntouched` calls `TestUpdateRuntimeLibraries._hashTree` (:960, :972) defined ~300 lines later (:1283) — forward cross-class reference, works at call time but couples classes. (4) Container-side pip behavior is entirely mocked: the only real-Docker coverage is the DOCKER_AVAILABLE-gated bootstrap integration test (tests/scripts/test_sandbox_bootstrap.py:381-449) which installs `six` once into a fresh workspace and would NOT catch a reinstall corruption; the original pip --target bug therefore has no fast-suite exercise of pip itself — the tests pin the host-side architecture that makes it structurally impossible.

title: Phase 1I code review verdict: PASS on executed checks; dead branch at manager.py:1090; buildInstallCommand is NOT a dangling reference
content:
Second-pass code review of the Phase 1I delta (install-path unification, uncommitted, /sandbox update arc), 2026-09-05. Complements memory e64b7bcd (implementation facts) and 9da61eb7 (residual risks) from the earlier read-only audits — this pass EXECUTED the gates, closing the "read-only, not run" caveat those audits carried.

VERDICT: PASS, no blocking/actionable findings. Executed: `make lint` clean (flake8, isort, circular-import check, pyright 0 errors/0 warnings); focused pytest `tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py tests/scripts/test_sandbox_bootstrap.py tests/bot/test_sandbox.py` = 142 passed / 1 skipped. Review confirmed conformance to plan §§5.5, 5.6, 9, 10, 12, 14-Phase-1I: single poolLock spans recovery+stage+merge+swap+refresh; no live-pool install path remains; InvalidPackageSpec only when ALL specs fail; LibraryPoolLocked propagates pre-container; callers (scripts/sandbox_bootstrap.py:177-181, handler sandbox.py:1194) compatible with the unchanged signature.

Code observations recorded for later cleanup (Low, no fix required for 1I):
1. DEAD BRANCH at lib/sandbox/manager.py:1090: `if not validated: ... return False` is unreachable — every loop iteration appends to exactly one of validated/failedPackages, and packages is non-empty (early return ~:1060), so empty validated always implies non-empty failedPackages → the raise fires. Behavior correct; branch is dead code.
2. `buildInstallCommand(targetDir, specs)` in lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/pool_pip_runner.py:74 is NOT a dangling leftover of the deleted install path — it is the pool_pip_runner helper's `--install-into` staged mode, which plan §5.6 explicitly KEEPS. Do not flag it (or delete it) when auditing for installCommand remnants; likewise zero legit references to buildPipCommand/PIP_INSTALL_ARGS/dedupPool remain (grep-verified).

title: Sandbox staged-core test-quality observations: under-pinned bot install mock, self-referential command assertions, CWD dependence, reinstall-regression failure mechanics
content:
Test-quality findings from the 2026-09-05 Phase 1I review of tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py::TestInstallRuntimeLibrariesStagedCore (8 tests, all verified present, honest, and asserting real on-disk state). None blocking; useful when extending this class:

1. UNDER-PINNED BOT MOCK (worth strengthening): tests/bot/test_sandbox.py:618-625 installs a bare `AsyncMock(return_value=True)` for installRuntimeLibraries and asserts only the `packages` kwarg. A handler regression dropping `runtime=RuntimeName.PYTHON` would pass the mock but TypeError against the real signature (manager.py:1004, runtime is keyword-only required). Contrast: tests/scripts/test_sandbox_bootstrap.py:196-198 pins the FULL call. If touching the bot test, pin runtime= too.
2. SELF-REFERENTIAL COMMAND ASSERTIONS: `stageSpec.command == runtimeImpl.stageInstallCommand([...])` (test_manager.py:835, :1016, :1080) compares production output against the SAME production builder, so a break inside stageInstallCommand itself (e.g. losing `--`) passes manager-level tests. Mitigated by independent argv-shape tests in tests/lib/sandbox/runtimes/test_python_runtime.py (TestStageInstallCommand). Keep both layers if refactoring.
3. STAGED-CORE CLASS NEVER ASSERTS STAGE-CONTAINER REMOVAL ON SUCCESS — it pins only keep-on-failure (:969-970). Success-path removal is covered indirectly by TestInstallRuntimeLibrariesContainerCleanup.testInstallRemovesInstallContainerOnSuccess (test_manager.py:679-708). Note the asymmetry if extending StagedCore.
4. CWD DEPENDENCE: _runStagedInstall pre-checks the helper at the repo-relative path lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/pool_pip_runner.py (manager.py:2065-2069). Running pytest from outside the repo root turns every StagedCore test into a ConfigError failure. Consistent with the project's run-from-root convention but latent.
5. REINSTALL REGRESSION HONESTY (confirmed): testReinstallingPresentPackageReplacesOldDistInfo (:854) pins all three corruption symptoms on independent axes — exactly one dist-info after reinstall, version-tagged payload body (only real delete-per-RECORD + delta overlay yields new bytes), old-only files gone (proves deletion is driven by OLD RECORD, not the delta file set). It mechanically fails on the pre-fix live-pool path: old code mounted the live pool instead of a staging io/ subtree, so the _stagingHostDir side effect raises AssertionError("ContainerSpec has no staging mount") and `assert success is True` fails. Fake delta fixtures are structurally exactly what enumerateDistInfos/readRecordPaths/mergeStagedDelta consume (METADATA Name:/Version: headers; pool-root-relative RECORD CSV + `<dir>/RECORD,,` self-entry; version-tagged bodies); RECORD hash/size columns are inert placeholders (harmless — nothing validates them today).
6. STRENGTH WORTH REUSING: the `_oneshotSequence` mock-backend helper (test_manager.py:224-262) fails loudly on extra/missing backend calls instead of silently misaligning — prefer it over a plain list side_effect with callable steps for container-call sequences.

title: commandHandlerV2 attaches metadata at _commandHandlerInfoV2 for help-text tests
content:
The @commandHandlerV2 decorator (internal/bot/models/command_handlers.py) attaches a CommandHandlerInfoV2 object to the decorated function via the module constant `_HANDLER_METADATA_ATTR_v2 = "_commandHandlerInfoV2"` (command_handlers.py:24). The metadata object exposes `.commands`, `.shortDescription`, and `.helpMessage`.

This is how to write regression tests for help-text drift WITHOUT dispatching a command:
```python
metadata = getattr(SandboxHandler.sandbox_command, "_commandHandlerInfoV2")
helpMessage: str = metadata.helpMessage
for subcommand in ("files", "read", "status", "packages", "install", "update"):
    assert subcommand in helpMessage
```
Use getattr (not direct attribute access) so pyright does not flag the setattr-attached attribute. Discovered 2026-09-05 while adding /sandbox update (Phase 2 of sandbox-update-v1); the decorator helpMessage had silently omitted `packages` until a regression test locked all six sandbox subcommands.

title: MessageCategory imports from internal.database.models, not internal.bot.models
content:
`MessageCategory` is NOT re-exported from the `internal.bot.models` package — it lives in `internal.database.models` (same module as MessageCategory.toRole). Handlers already import it as `from internal.database.models import MessageCategory`; tests must do the same. Adding `MessageCategory` to a `from internal.bot.models import (...)` block fails with pyright/LSP error "MessageCategory is unknown import symbol" at edit time.

This parallels the existing gotcha that HandlerResultStatus comes from internal.bot.common.handlers.base, not internal.bot.models. Both bot-models-adjacent enums live elsewhere; check the handler's own imports before guessing a location. Encountered 2026-09-05 while writing tests/bot/test_sandbox.py section 6b (/sandbox update).

title: test_sandbox.py mock routing: fixture mock is live, _makeHandler's internal mock is inert
content:
In tests/bot/test_sandbox.py there are TWO SandboxManager mocks and only one is live:

- The `mockSandboxManager` fixture patches `lib.sandbox.SandboxManager.getInstance`, so during a test every manager call made by the handler (via getInstance) goes to the FIXTURE's AsyncMock.
- `_makeHandler()` also creates an internal AsyncMock manager, but it is dead weight unless explicitly passed — configure methods and assertions on the fixture mock: `mockSandboxManager.updateRuntimeLibraries = AsyncMock(return_value=...)`, then `mockSandboxManager.updateRuntimeLibraries.assert_called_once()`. AsyncMock auto-creates missing method attributes, but their default return_value is a Mock, so always set return_value explicitly for dataclass results.

Second, regression-test-design nuance for adding a new subcommand branch: dispatcher-level gating tests (sandbox not configured / allow-sandbox false) PASS even before the subcommand branch exists, because `_checkSandboxAccess` runs at the top of `sandbox_command` before the elif chain. They are coverage tests, not regression tests — the tests that actually fail pre-change are the dispatch/owner/reply ones and any usage/helpText regressions (the else branch replies "Unknown subcommand"). Verified 2026-09-05 with /sandbox update: 2 gating tests green pre-change, other 12 red.

title: /sandbox update bot-layer reply decisions (category, note gating, capping)
content:
Bot-layer reply decisions made while wiring /sandbox update (sandbox-update-v1 Phase 2, 2026-09-05) that plan §8 did NOT pin — they follow SandboxHandler/install precedents and are now locked by tests:

- Failure reply category: `result.success == False` renders through the normal reply path but is sent with `messageCategory=MessageCategory.BOT_ERROR` (mirrors install's failure branch); successful renders use BOT_COMMAND_REPLY. Exception replies (InvalidPackageSpec / LibraryPoolLocked / generic) are also BOT_ERROR.
- In-flight note line ("sandbox runs started before this update keep seeing their previous pool...") is emitted ONLY when `result.updated` is non-empty (a swap actually happened); all-current and empty-pool replies omit it. The all-current line counts N = len(upToDate) + len(unchanged).
- Empty-pool detection: manager short-circuits a no-arg update on an empty pool to an all-empty success result; the handler infers "Nothing installed..." from success + updated/unchanged/upToDate all empty (no dedicated flag on LibraryUpdateResult).
- Reply length capped via accumulator at MAX_UPDATE_REPLY_LENGTH = 3000 with "...and more lines omitted" marker, mirroring run_command's maxLength=3000 pattern.
- LibraryUpdateResult/PackageUpdate/InvalidPackageSpec/LibraryPoolLocked are all re-exported from the `lib.sandbox` package root (handlers import from there, not from .errors/.types).
- Manager call shape: `manager.updateRuntimeLibraries(packages=packages or None, runtime=RuntimeName.PYTHON)`; ack messages "Updating all packages..." / "Updating packages..." sent inside the try, before the call.

title: Phase 2 /sandbox update handler review: NEEDS-FIXES — 3 rendering bugs (cap, newVersion=None, swap-note gating)
content:
Outcome of the 2026-09-05 review-only session on the sandbox-update-v1 **Phase 2** delta (`internal/bot/common/handlers/sandbox.py` +184/−2, `tests/bot/test_sandbox.py` +288; uncommitted at review time) against `docs/plans/sandbox-update-v1.md` §3/§7/§8/§12. Verdict: **NEEDS-FIXES** — no CRITICAL, 3 IMPORTANT (all rendering), 3 RECOMMEND (tests). Verified: `make lint` clean, `git diff --check` clean, `./venv/bin/pytest tests/bot/test_sandbox.py -q` → 65 passed. All findings UNFIXED at review time — re-verify current state before acting. This memory CORRECTS decision memory 6b188b81 (bot-layer reply decisions) on two points.

IMPORTANT findings:
1. ~sandbox.py:1353-1404 — reply-length cap incomplete. Failure replies return BEFORE the truncation step, so a large `failedSpecs` list can exceed MAX_UPDATE_REPLY_LENGTH=3000; on success, truncation can drop the "...and more lines omitted" marker when preceding lines leave no room. Fix: build every reply variant first, then apply ONE common cap that reserves marker space (`reply[:MAX-len(marker)] + marker`). Add boundary tests for long diff/skipped/unchanged/failedSpecs lists asserting both cap and marker.
2. ~sandbox.py:1322-1324 — `newVersion=None` renders as literal "None" ("scipy 1.0 → None"). Only `oldVersion is None` is handled, but the contract permits `newVersion=None` (package absent after update). Fix: explicit branch, e.g. "scipy 1.0 → absent after update"; test both nullable sides.
3. ~sandbox.py:1369-1385 — in-flight note keyed to version changes, not swap occurrence: emitted only when `result.updated` non-empty, but a successful staged swap CAN produce only `unchanged` entries (fail-safe prefilter or same-version reinstall) → users not warned about old-pool visibility. Fix: predicate = `bool(result.updated or result.unchanged)`; normal prefilter "all current" and empty-pool results leave BOTH lists empty so still omit the note. Add `updated=[]` + `unchanged=[...]` regression test.

RECOMMEND (tests/bot/test_sandbox.py): usage/help regression tests (~918-936) use substring checks that cannot fail ("install" matches inside "installed"; "packages" in help prose) — assert the complete helpMessage/usage text or parse command tokens; deterministic-reply tests (~793-936) tolerate ordering/extra text — prefer exact equality plus MessageCategory assertions (BOT_COMMAND_REPLY success / BOT_ERROR failure) and cover failure-without-containerId; new tests (~713-923) perpetuate `cast(Any, handler)` against the no-Any rule — cast to a concrete callable instead.

Confirmed clean (do not re-flag): owner gate before any manager call; `packages or None` (whitespace-only arg → None → update-all, correct per §3); exception ordering `InvalidPackageSpec` → `LibraryPoolLocked` → generic `Exception`; `result.containerId` used only when present; gating tests exercise the dispatcher path; camelCase/docstrings/type hints/≤120 cols pass the toolchain.

title: LibraryUpdateResult contract: swap can complete with updated=[] (key off updated OR unchanged); PackageUpdate versions nullable on both sides
content:
Contract semantics of `LibraryUpdateResult` / `PackageUpdate` (lib/sandbox/types.py, returned by `SandboxManager.updateRuntimeLibraries`, lib/sandbox/manager.py:1128) that consumer code must respect — discovered while reviewing Phase 2 handler rendering:

- **A successful atomic pool swap does NOT imply `updated` is non-empty.** The fail-safe prefilter (`_partitionSpecsByCurrentState` in manager.py forces already-current/duplicate specs into processing) and same-version reinstalls yield `unchanged` entries with no version change — so `updated=[]` + `unchanged` non-empty can still mean a real swap happened. Correct "swap occurred" predicate for user-facing old-pool-visibility warnings: `bool(updated or unchanged)`. Gating only on `updated` under-warns. (Normal prefilter "all current" and manager's empty-pool short-circuit leave `updated`/`unchanged`/`upToDate` ALL empty.)
- **`PackageUpdate.oldVersion` and `newVersion` are each `str | None`.** `newVersion=None` = package absent after the update (e.g. removed by dependency resolution) — rendering must branch explicitly, never f-string it (literal "None" leaks). `oldVersion` is also nullable, so rendering must handle None on either side.
- No dedicated "empty pool" flag exists on the result; consumers infer it from `success` + all of `updated`/`unchanged`/`upToDate` empty.
- `failedSpecs` carries (spec, error) tuples; `containerId` is populated only on the failure result.

title: Bot-handler test gotchas: substring checks can't pin command lists; cast(Any, handler) pattern vs no-Any rule
content:
Two testing gotchas for Gromozeka bot-handler tests, surfaced by the 2026-09-05 Phase 2 /sandbox update review:

1. **Substring assertions cannot pin command lists.** Usage/help regression tests that check `"install" in text` / `"packages" in text` pass even when the subcommand entry is missing, because "install" matches inside "installed" and "packages"/"files" appear in help prose. For regression tests meant to pin the exact set of subcommands in helpMessage/usage text, assert the COMPLETE expected string or parse and compare the command tokens/lines. (Sibling of the vacuous-disjunct gotcha in test_stats.py, but a different failure mode: false-pass via accidental containment, not always-true disjuncts.)

2. **`cast(Any, handler)` in handler tests vs the no-Any rule.** The `commandHandlerV2` decorator (internal/bot/models/command_handlers.py) types decorated handlers as `CommandHandlerFuncUnbound` (unbound callables), so tests cannot invoke methods like `sandbox_command`/`run_command` on the handler instance with clean typing; the established pattern in tests/bot/test_sandbox.py is `await cast(Any, handler).sandbox_command(...)`. This technically conflicts with the repo's "No Any" hard rule. Review recommendation for NEW tests: cast to a concrete callable type (or call the underlying method via a typed accessor) rather than `Any`. Pre-existing occurrences were not flagged as must-fix.

title: Sandbox update reply: single-cap-with-marker pattern (Gate-1 fix)
content:
In `internal/bot/common/handlers/sandbox.py`, `_renderUpdateReply` must build EVERY reply variant in full (failure, empty-pool, all-current, diff) with NO early returns, then apply ONE common cap `_capUpdateReply`. Root cause (Gate-1 finding 1, fixed 2026-09-05): the failure branch previously returned before truncation, so a long `failedSpecs` list could exceed `MAX_UPDATE_REPLY_LENGTH` (3000); on success, line-based truncation could omit the marker entirely.

`_capUpdateReply` arithmetic: slice to `MAX_UPDATE_REPLY_LENGTH - len(marker) - 1`, trim back to the last `\n` (whole-line granularity, preserving the old line-dropping behavior), then append `"\n" + UPDATE_REPLY_TRUNCATION_MARKER` (`"...and more lines omitted"`). This guarantees len ≤ 3000 AND the marker is always present when truncated. The `-1` reserves room for the newline before the marker.

GOTCHA for future edits: any new reply variant or section added to this handler MUST flow through `_capUpdateReply` — never early-return a variant. Accepted micro-deviation from the pre-fix behavior: the `Skipped invalid specs:` suffix is now appended uniformly after ALL variants (including empty-pool, which previously skipped it) — unreachable in practice because the empty-pool no-op only arises from update-all (`packages=None`), which produces no rejected specs.

Regression tests added (tests/bot/test_sandbox.py): long diff list (~500 entries), long skip/unchanged lists (exercises a single line LONGER than the cap), long failure failedSpecs (~300 specs, fails against old early-return code) — each asserts `len(msgText) <= MAX_UPDATE_REPLY_LENGTH` AND `msgText.endswith(UPDATE_REPLY_TRUNCATION_MARKER)` AND first section intact.

title: Handler test call sites: direct typed invocation + cast mock args to concrete param types
content:
Pattern from fixing Gate-1 finding 6 (tests/bot/test_sandbox.py Phase 2 update-test block): replace `await cast(Any, handler).sandbox_command(...)` with direct typed invocation `await handler.sandbox_command(em, ...)` — the real method signature type-checks fine under pyright. The only blocker is mock ARGUMENTS: build them via a helper that returns the concrete parameter type, e.g.

```python
def _makeUpdateObject() -> UpdateObjectType:
    return cast(UpdateObjectType, Mock(spec=Update))
```

where `UpdateObjectType = Union[telegram.Update | maxModels.Update]` is importable from `internal.bot.common.models`. Cast to the CONCRETE parameter type, never `Any`. `Mock(spec=...)` alone does not satisfy pyright — the cast is still required.

Distinction from the existing assignment-site convention (direct attribute assignment + `# type: ignore[method-assign]` for monkey-patching handler methods): this pattern covers call-site mock arguments passed TO a typed method.

Known follow-up: pre-existing tests in tests/bot/test_sandbox.py (older run/files/read/status/install blocks and the `_makeHandler` stubs at ~lines 285/288) still use `cast(Any, handler)` — deliberately left untouched during the Phase 2 fix round because the finding scope was limited to the new update-test block. They are migration targets for both patterns.

title: InvalidPackageSpec str form enables exact-equality reply assertions
content:
`InvalidPackageSpec(spec, reason)` (lib/sandbox) stringifies as `invalid package spec 'spec': reason` — set via `super().__init__(f"invalid package spec {spec!r}: {reason}")` in its `__init__`. So the handler's reply `f"Invalid package spec: {e}"` is fully deterministic, e.g. `Invalid package spec: invalid package spec 'numpy!': Invalid package name`, and can be exact-asserted (with `MessageCategory.BOT_ERROR`) rather than substring-checked.

Same fix round applied the anti-vacuity convention to deterministic bot replies: composite success, empty-pool, failure (with/without containerId), lock-busy, all-current, invalid-specs suffix, usage text, and `helpMessage` are all pinned by COMPLETE exact-equality strings (variable parts like container id are templated into the expected string) plus a `messageCategory` assert. Substring checks proved too weak — the old usage/help assertions passed on prose words like "installed"/"files" without actually pinning the subcommand lists.

content:

title: updateRuntimeLibraries(packages=None) skips named-spec validation — failedSpecs always empty on update-all
content:
In `lib/sandbox/manager.py`, `updateRuntimeLibraries` (manager.py:1128) validation flow: when `packages=None` (update-all), named-spec validation is skipped entirely, so `failedSpecs=[]` (manager.py:1203-1223); the empty-pool early return for update-all (manager.py:1245-1264) therefore cannot carry failed specs. Only explicitly named specs get the shell-metacharacter/flag validation, so `failedSpecs` is populated only when `packages` is a concrete list.

Consequence (code-verified 2026-09-05, upgrading the prior assumption in memory 6b218373 to confirmed fact): the SandboxHandler's uniform invalid-specs suffix on empty-pool replies is a micro-deviation that is UNREACHABLE via the real update-all flow — an empty-pool reply can never show "Skipped invalid specs:". This holds because an empty pool can only reach the handler via update-all (`packages=None`).

title: Bash pipes denied when piped-to command is not allowlisted (corrects 'pipes pass')
content: Correction to memory 68abed20 ("pipes pass"), observed 2026-09-05 (docs-writer, /sandbox update Phase 3 docs sync): pipe segments are evaluated against the allowlist INDIVIDUALLY. `rg -n "..." <file> | head -60` was DENIED even though the agent config allows `rg*` and `grep*` — the piped-to command `head` is not allowlisted, and that breaks the match. The earlier "pipes pass" example (`git diff … | grep '^+'`) only worked because `grep` was itself allowlisted, not because pipes are transparent. Practical rules for docs-writer-style agents: (a) never pipe to non-allowlisted commands (`head`, `tail`, `wc` only if explicitly allowed — note `wc*` was allowlisted in this config); (b) prefer the structured Grep tool over bash rg/grep for content search; (c) keep bash calls to single unpiped commands matching allowlisted prefixes (make lint*, make check-docs*, git status/diff/log/show*, ls*). Related: d07a80d9 (`&&` chaining also denied), eefc752f (patterns exact-match without trailing `*`).

title: Gate-2 sandbox audit: 3 new low findings (jail divergence, undocumented merge raise, empty-pool mid-merge adoption)
content:
Gate-2 integration audit (2026-09-05, read-only, working tree vs HEAD of the /sandbox update arc) surfaced three cross-component defects NOT previously recorded (all LOW severity — no Medium/High found anywhere in the audit):

1. **Divergent jail idioms — storage.resolveWorkspacePath lacks the RuntimeError guard its self-declared mirror has.** `lib/sandbox/storage.py:100-109`: both `.resolve()` calls sit OUTSIDE any try, and only `ValueError` is caught around `relative_to`. The new `lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/pool_staging.py:311-316` `_resolveJailed` — whose docstring claims it "Mirrors the resolveWorkspacePath idiom" — catches `(OSError, ValueError, RuntimeError)`. On Python ≤3.12 `Path.resolve()` raises RuntimeError on symlink loops (see memory 59cade95); the workspace is container-written (rw /workspace), so a planted loop + `/sandbox files|read <loop>` leaks raw RuntimeError out of manager.listFiles/readFile → generic handler "Error: …" instead of the documented PathOutsideWorkspace "Access denied". Fail-closed, no escape. Fix: wrap both resolves in `try/except (OSError, RuntimeError)` → raise PathOutsideWorkspace; regression-test via a Path.resolve shim (dev venv may run 3.13+/3.14 where resolve no longer raises).

2. **mergeStagedDelta's LibraryInstallFailed bypasses the LibraryUpdateResult failure contract and is undocumented.** `pool_staging.py:395-398` raises LibraryInstallFailed when poolCopy/delta is a symlink or delta non-dir; `_runStagedInstall` calls it unguarded (`manager.py:2143`). The stage container has rw on the whole io/ subtree (`manager.py:1922-1927`), so PEP 517 build code can plant `io/delta` as a symlink after pip exits 0. The exception then propagates out of installRuntimeLibraries/updateRuntimeLibraries — neither Raises list mentions it (`manager.py:1048-1058`, `1156-1169`) — so the caller gets a raw exception instead of the structured `(success=False, containerId)` every other stage failure yields. Pool stays safe (finally removes runDir, rollbackFailed=False). Fix: catch around the merge → return `(False, outcome.containerId)`, or minimally add to both Raises sections.

3. **Recovery invariant "a surviving newpool is a complete pool" has one unguarded corner: mid-merge crash on a previously-EMPTY pool.** `manager.py:1558-1560` + plan `docs/plans/sandbox-update-v1.md:134` justify adoption by "renames start only after merge completed". Sound for non-empty pools (crash mid-merge leaves libs present+non-empty → "non-empty live pool wins" rule at manager.py:1617-1620 refuses adoption). But if the pool was empty at copy time (`manager.py:2089`), a hard kill during mergeStagedDelta's interruptible copytree overlay (`pool_staging.py:427`) leaves libs empty → rmdir'd (`manager.py:1621-1624`) → the PARTIAL newpool is adopted. Bounded consequences: no pre-existing pool lost, request never reported success, retry re-stages over the partial state, packages.json only refreshed post-swap. Optional fix: write a `merge.done` marker after mergeStagedDelta and require it before newpool adoption.

Note: the earlier round-2 review claim "empty pool suppresses crash recovery" is the INVERSE of finding 3 — recovery does fire on empty pools; the risk is it adopts a partially-merged copy.

title: Read-only analyst role: no bash/git — audit via cross-references, never read .git/status
content: The code-analyst / read-only review role in this project has NO bash/exec tooling, so `git status` / `git diff` cannot be run to enumerate uncommitted changes. A `read` of `.git/status` fails (git status is a command, not a file; .git holds no status artifact). Working pattern that succeeded across the 2026-09-04/05 sandbox-update Gate reviews: (1) take the audited file set from the user's task description; (2) take the baseline HEAD from prior review memories (e.g. 3d4d9880 for the sandbox-update arc) instead of git; (3) do the audit as cross-file consistency verification (production constants ↔ test pins ↔ plan doc) rather than diff inspection; (4) state the limitation explicitly in the report and hand the `git status --porcelain` checklist item to an agent with exec. title: Gate-2 NEEDS-FIXES: partial-newpool adoption after mid-merge crash on first install
content: Gate-2 whole-work integration review (2026-09-05, uncommitted /sandbox update arc) verdict: NEEDS-FIXES, one major finding. THE FLIP-SIDE of Phase 1R blocker #2: `_recoverRuntimePool` (lib/sandbox/manager.py ~1604, 1617-1635) treats ANY surviving `newpool` as a complete pool and adopts it (empty live libs gets rmdir'd — enabled by the earlier empty-libs-adoption fix). But `oldpool` only exists once `swapPools` performed its FIRST rename. So on a FIRST install (live `libs` empty), a hard crash during `mergeStagedDelta`'s interruptible copytree leaves empty libs → rmdir → the PARTIALLY OVERLAID `newpool` (copied at pool_staging.py ~427) is adopted as the live pool, contradicting the documented "crash before swap leaves live pool untouched" invariant. Consequences bounded (request never reported success; no pre-existing pool lost; retry re-stages), but invariant violated. Fix direction: only prefer `newpool` when sibling `oldpool` ALSO exists (newpool-only run = uncommitted staging garbage, since the first swap rename creates oldpool), or write a durable swap-phase / `merge.done` marker required before adoption. Regression test: empty libs + partial newpool + NO oldpool must NOT be adopted; the existing both-present adoption case must keep passing. TENSION to preserve: empty-libs adoption itself is REQUIRED (Phase 1R blocker #2 showed empty-libs suppression caused permanent pool loss) — it just needs swap-began proof.

title: resolveWorkspacePath lacks RuntimeError symlink-loop guard — jail idiom divergence
content: Jail-idiom divergence found by Gate-2: `resolveWorkspacePath` (lib/sandbox/storage.py ~100-109) calls `.resolve()` twice OUTSIDE any try and catches only ValueError around `relative_to`, while its self-declared mirror `_resolveJailed` (pool_staging.py ~298-316) catches `(OSError, ValueError, RuntimeError)`. The RuntimeError arm is required on Python ≤ 3.12 (repo floor): `Path.resolve()` raises RuntimeError on symlink loops. Workspace content is container-written (rw /workspace), so a planted symlink loop + `/sandbox files <loop>` or `/sandbox read <loop>` leaks raw RuntimeError out of manager.listFiles/readFile → handler generic arm renders "Error: …" instead of PathOutsideWorkspace "Access denied". Fail-closed (no escape, no corruption) — it is a consistency/error-shape defect. Fix: wrap both resolves in try/except (OSError, RuntimeError) → raise PathOutsideWorkspace. Regression-test note: the dev venv runs Python 3.14.6 where loop behavior differs, so tests must shim/patch Path.resolve instead of relying on a real loop. (Existing memory 078cbbb9 covers the _resolveJailed-side rule; this records that the canonical storage.py helper is the one currently missing the guard.)

title: mergeStagedDelta LibraryInstallFailed bypasses LibraryUpdateResult failure contract
content: Error-contract seam (Gate-2): `mergeStagedDelta` (pool_staging.py ~390-398) raises `LibraryInstallFailed` when the staged delta is a symlink or non-directory (reachable because the stage container has rw on io/ and PEP 517 build code can exit pip 0 leaving io/delta malicious), and `_runStagedInstall` calls it UNGUARDED (manager.py ~2141-2143). The raw exception propagates out of installRuntimeLibraries/updateRuntimeLibraries: (a) it bypasses the structured `LibraryUpdateResult(success=False, containerId)` contract every other stage failure produces; (b) neither method docstring's Raises section lists it (~1048-1058, ~1156-1169). Handler renders generic "Error: Staged delta … refusing to merge" via the generic arm. Safety holds (pool untouched, finally still cleans run dir, rollbackFailed False) — it is a contract/documentation seam, not a hole. Fix: catch around the merge and return the failure result (decide containerId deliberately: the container is already removed on this path, so pass None or keep contract consistent), or at minimum add LibraryInstallFailed to both Raises sections.

title: Fixed: pool recovery adopts newpool only with oldpool sibling (both-present guard)
content:
Gate-2 MAJOR (memory 855dd910) FIXED in `_recoverRuntimePool` (lib/sandbox/manager.py, /sandbox update arc, 2026-09-05). Root cause was: recovery treated ANY surviving `newpool` as a complete pool; on a first install (empty libs) a hard crash during `mergeStagedDelta()`/`copytree()` left an empty live pool + partial newpool, and recovery promoted the partial tree.

New invariant: a staging run dir's `newpool` is an adoption candidate ONLY when the sibling `oldpool` also exists — both-present proves `swapPools()` rename #1 (libs→oldpool) happened, which by the ordering guarantee happens strictly AFTER the merge completed. Newpool-only run dirs = uncommitted staging garbage (crash before/during merge) → deliberately NOT candidates, left for staging GC.

Implementation details worth knowing:
- Empty-libs handling REORDERED: non-empty libs wins first (return); `libsDir.rmdir()` of an empty libs happens only when an actionable candidate exists — garbage newpool-only leftovers can no longer cause adoption away from a live (even empty) libs dir.
- Oldpool-only candidates now pass `newPoolDir=None` (previously a guaranteed-failing `newPoolDir.rename()` ran before oldpool restoration, relying on the OSError fallback). Restore goes straight to oldpool now.
- Note: the oldpool-only crash window is theoretically unreachable via swapPools (rename #1 libs→oldpool, #2 newpool→libs; a crash between them leaves BOTH), the elif is defensive.
- Candidate sort: both-present (kind 0) before oldpool-only (kind 1), newest mtime first within a kind.
- `_hasPoolCrashLeftovers()` intentionally left counting newpool-only dirs — conservative: triggers the under-lock recovery re-attempt; after the retry the empty result is honest.
- Regression test `testNewpoolOnlyLeftoverIsGarbageEmptyLibsStays` (tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py, TestRecoverCrashWindowAdoption); mutation-verified: guard removed → test RED (partial newpool adopted away from empty libs) → restored → 11/11 recovery tests green.

title: Sandbox crash-leftover test seeds must be both-present (newpool+oldpool)
content:
Gotcha introduced by the both-present recovery adoption guard (lib/sandbox/manager.py `_recoverRuntimePool`): tests modeling ADOPTABLE crash leftovers must seed BOTH `newpool` AND `oldpool` in the staging run dir. A newpool-only seed now models non-adoptable garbage — the test silently degrades to "no adoption" and fails or, worse, pins wrong behavior.

Four tests in tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py were converted from newpool-only to both-pool seeding (2026-09-05): `testAdoptsNewestNewpool`, `testUpdateAllAdoptsCrashLeftoverBeforeCollectingNames`, `testBusyLockAndLeftoversPropagateInsteadOfFalseSuccess`, `testRecoveryDefersWhenPoolLockHeld`. Their old seeds modeled a crash "between the swap renames" incorrectly — a crash between rename #1 (libs→oldpool) and #2 (newpool→libs) always leaves BOTH pools.

Related assertion updates from the same round: three no-op-path tests changed `result.metadataRefreshed is False` → `is None` (stage-failure, all-current early return, empty-pool no-arg paths — refresh never attempted under the tri-state contract).

title: metadataRefreshed is now bool | None tri-state (supersedes False-conflation notes)
content:
`LibraryUpdateResult.metadataRefreshed` (lib/sandbox/types.py) changed from `bool` to `bool | None` (2026-09-05, Gate-2 fix round).
