title: Sandbox update audit verdict: runtime-owned staging mounts proposal (replaces ABC path constants)
content:
2026-09-05 REVIEW-ONLY audit of /sandbox update (HEAD 3e81c113) — verdict on the owner's proposal to stop exposing STAGING_CONTAINER_PATH / UPDATE_HELPER_CONTAINER_PATH from the Runtime ABC.

VERDICT: Owner's instinct correct. The ugliness is that container-side layout is split three ways: constant values on PythonRuntime (runtime.py:41,44), annotation-only ABC declarations (base.py:32-48, UNENFORCEABLE — a subclass that forgets them fails only at first use with AttributeError inside manager._stagingMounts; abstractmethods are enforced at instantiation + flagged by pyright), and mount ASSEMBLY in the manager (manager.py:1943-1954) while argv builders join the same constants on the runtime (runtime.py:119-146).

RECOMMENDED minimal shape: `stagingMounts(self, hostStagingIoDir: Path) -> list[dict[str, str]]` on the ABC (abstract). Pass ONLY hostStagingIoDir (runDir/"io", manager-owned); do NOT pass helperHostPath back in — circular, the manager got it from runtime.updateHelperHostPath(). ContainerSpec.mounts is already list[dict[str,str]] (types.py:559), so zero translation.

CRITICAL constraint: the constants must REMAIN PUBLIC on PythonRuntime (drop from ABC, keep as class attrs) — tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py:275,845-847,1165-1167 discover the staging mount via symbolic `PythonRuntime.STAGING_CONTAINER_PATH`, so keeping them public leaves the whole manager test suite green without edits (consistent with memory 3cea411d literal-pin gotcha).

MAX-COHESION "staging plan" variant: `StagingRun(command, mounts)` frozen dataclass; `reportRun(hostIoDir, specs) -> StagingRun` / `stageRun(...)`. Folds reportCommand + stageInstallCommand + _stagingMounts into the runtime; manager keeps only policy (limits/labels/lifecycle/host run-dir layout). ABC stays 3 abstract methods, minus 2 annotations, plus one dataclass. Cost: argv tests (test_python_runtime.py:131-173) change shape to assert .command. Lean recommendation: StagingRun if willing to touch runtime tests; stagingMounts-only otherwise (~90% of benefit, zero argv-test churn).

REJECTED middle-ground: `containerPaths() -> dict[str, str]` — stringly-typed dict keys just relocate the annotation problem; assembly stays in manager.

The constants are NOT removed from the codebase by either variant (argv joins still need them) — they leave the CONTRACT (ABC) and become class-internal. That is encapsulation, not hiding; inlining literals into runtime methods is possible but worse for tests.

Blast radius: base.py:32-48 (delete annotations, add abstract method); runtime.py:41-53 (implement, docstrings shrink); manager.py:1923-1954 _stagingMounts becomes delegation or deleted; call sites manager.py:2000 and :2120. Docs: no docs/llm/* file references the constants (grep-verified); docs/plans/sandbox-update-v1.md §4.2/§5.3 describes old shape but is a frozen design record. EFFORT: M (half-day incl. make format lint + make test).

title: Sandbox helper pre-check duplication: two copies, fix is MOVE into _runPrefilterContainer not delete
content:
2026-09-05 audit finding (HEAD 3e81c113), corrects the prior suspicion of THREE copies of the update-helper pre-check: there are exactly TWO — manager.py:1234-1238 (updateRuntimeLibraries step 2) and manager.py:2085-2091 (_runStagedInstall). _runPrefilterContainer (manager.py:1956-2026) has NO check — it goes mkdir → runOneshot directly.

Consequence: the outer check is NOT redundant — it is the ONLY guard for the pre-filter container's file-bind. Deleting it outright would turn a missing helper into: Docker silently creates a directory at the bind path → `python /sandbox/pool_pip_runner.py` fails ("is a directory") → non-zero exit → report missing → fail-safe ALL-OUTDATED → wasted pre-filter container run + confusing failure before _runStagedInstall finally raises ConfigError.

The actual smell is ASYMMETRY: one container-runner self-checks, the other relies on its caller. Correct fix: MOVE the check into _runPrefilterContainer (before runOneshot), delete the outer block at :1231-1238. Pattern becomes uniform "every container-runner verifies its own file-binds". Behavior delta: ConfigError fires slightly later — after the update-all empty-pool short-circuit (:1260-1270) and empty-outdated short-circuit (:1293) — which is MORE correct (no container run → helper not needed).

Test safety: tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py:1793-1811 stubs updateHelperHostPath and asserts ConfigError + backend.runOneshot.assert_not_awaited() — still passes after the move because the check precedes runOneshot inside the helper. VERDICT: simplify, EFFORT: S, RISK: low.

title: Sandbox update audit: keep-as-is justifications and ratified out-of-scope boundaries
content:
2026-09-05 REVIEW-ONLY audit (HEAD 3e81c113) — candidates that LOOK like over-engineering but are justified; do not re-litigate in future audits.

1. metadataRefreshed: bool | None tri-state (LibraryUpdateResult, types.py:413-419) — VERIFIED it has NO production consumer: the handler render cluster (sandbox.py:1319-1428) never reads result.metadataRefreshed (touches only success/containerId/updated/unchanged/upToDate/failedSpecs/runtime). Only consumers: manager internals (manager.py:1339-1342,1355; None sites :1206,:1269,:1302,:1333) + 8 manager-test assertions (test_manager.py:1329,1367,1398,1464,1498,1534,1667,1771) + one bot-test constructor (test_sandbox.py:215). KEEP: collapsing to bool would make a no-op path report False ("refresh failed") — a lie; breaks 8 tests for ~5 lines saved. Extends memory 286800a4.

2. readRecordPaths (pool_staging.py, used by mergeStagedDelta :412) — manager doesn't import it, but tests call it directly (test_pool_staging.py:247,279,295,1571) and the module docstring lists it as a capability (:16,:32). No __all__ exists, so "exported" is moot. KEEP public.

3. Module-level single-caller helpers _splitOutdatedSpecs / _diffPoolVersions / _collectDuplicatePoolNames — _diffPoolVersions is unit-tested DIRECTLY (test_manager.py:70 import; :1409-1414 pins all four old/new transitions incl. the flow-unreachable `vanished` case). They are module-level precisely for instance-free testing. KEEP.

4. Retry-under-lock double _collectUpdateAllNames (manager.py:1252/:1259) — the fail-closed empty-find guard (plan §4.5; comment :1240-1250). Runs only when update-all ∧ empty ∧ reconciliation deferred/failed ∧ crash leftovers. Flattening reintroduces false "Nothing installed" on stranded swap copies. RATIFIED — out of audit scope.

5. pool_staging.py (537 lines) — no single-caller indirection wrappers (every public symbol has a manager caller and/or direct test; every private helper ≥1 internal caller: _isRegularLeaf ×3 :184/:279/:504, _parseDistInfoDir :244, _resolveJailed :338/:353, _removeOldDistInfo :424). Apparent duplication with manager is actually TWO TRUST BOUNDARIES: _validatePackageSpec (manager.py:2192-2215) gates caller-supplied specs; isValidCanonicalName in _collectUpdateAllNames (manager.py:1878-1896) gates CONTAINER-CONTROLLED pool metadata. Neither subsumes the other. pool_pip_runner.py:126-129 unreachable else = documented pyright-exhaustiveness fallback. KEEP ALL.

6. Handler render cluster (_formatPackageUpdate :1319, _formatFailedSpecs :1340, _capUpdateReply :1352, _renderUpdateReply :1376) — _handleInstallCommand has NO render utilities (two fixed strings, :1211/:1218), so nothing to share; the cluster is new and self-contained. The cap-with-marker pattern is itself the FIX for a prior review finding, test-pinned (test_sandbox.py:1085-1131).

7. sessionId dead param — unused in BOTH _handleUpdateCommand (:1245) and _handleInstallCommand; it is the uniform subcommand-dispatch signature convention. KEEP.

8. stagingRunId liveness labels present on update containers (manager.py:2012-2015,:2132-2137), absent on install/list — logged deferral, GC honors the skip. Do not relitigate.

OUT OF SCOPE BY RATIFICATION (spike-verified, pip --target corruption): the rev-2 staged-swap core, recovery/reconcile cluster (_recoverRuntimePool :1561, _hasPoolCrashLeftovers :1703, _reconcileRuntimePool :1728, opportunistic pass :1194, in-lock re-recovery :1312), and the pip-never-touches-live-pool invariant.

SEQUENCING for the actionable items (from memories 0e1b1682/2fafc812/3590e661): staging-mounts refactor, pre-check move, upgrade removal, and enumerate-once merge are mutually independent (one commit each); #1 and #2 both edit manager.py's staging cluster — separate commits within one PR for reviewability. Symbolic-constant test architecture means the mounts refactor should leave manager tests green without edits — if not, a mount-dict key drifted, which is exactly what those tests exist to catch.

title: Correction: .opencode/memory.jsonl IS staged when user's commit file list includes it
content: Memory 0361a10d ("agents should NOT read, edit, stage, or touch .opencode/memory.jsonl") is wrong on the staging point for commit workflows. Clarified 2026-09-05 (commit f1b083b0, "Add sandbox update simplification plan document"): when the user provides an explicit staging file list that includes `.opencode/memory.jsonl`, it MUST be staged and committed as a ride-along — hands-off, meaning: include whatever modification `git status`/`git diff --stat` shows, never inspect/parse its contents, never mention its contents in the report or commit message. Just `git add` it as-is. The "don't touch" rule applies to reading/editing its contents and to cases where the user explicitly says to exclude it — not to staging when requested. This matches established repo practice: the file is git-tracked and routinely committed (e.g., 5ea9cbcd, 65c29049, f1b083b0). Related: 981fabf2, dcd918fe, ada19995, b46ac701.

title: Sandbox update simplification ratified 2026-09-05: 4-item plan doc, frozen design record + keep-as-is register
content:
Post-landing audit of 3e81c113 ("/sandbox update": staged install + atomic pool swap) found accidental complexity AROUND the ratified core; the owner ratified specific simplifications on 2026-09-05. Execution plan written to docs/plans/sandbox-update-simplification-v1.md (created 2026-09-05; docs-only; make lint + make check-docs green). Companion design record docs/plans/sandbox-update-v1.md documents the preserved mechanism (§4.2/§5).

Ratified decisions:
- D1 (variant B): runtime-owned StagingRun — frozen-slots dataclass {command: list[str], mounts: list[dict[str,str]]} added to the Runtime ABC; abstract reportCommand/stageInstallCommand replaced by reportRun(hostStagingIoDir, specs) / stageRun(...); manager's _stagingMounts deleted; PythonRuntime keeps STAGING_CONTAINER_PATH / UPDATE_HELPER_CONTAINER_PATH as public class attrs used only by its own methods (tests reference them symbolically; tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py expected UNTOUCHED — symbolic-constant insulation). Rejected alternatives: minimal stagingMounts() method (fallback consideration); dict of named container paths (stringly-typed).
- D2: scripts/sandbox_bootstrap.py + tests/scripts/test_sandbox_bootstrap.py deleted; upgrade: bool no-op param removed from SandboxManager.installRuntimeLibraries (method itself STAYS — /sandbox install handler calls it at internal/bot/common/handlers/sandbox.py:1206).
- D3: four independent self-verifying commits (make format lint + make test), each ticking its checkbox in the plan doc.

Load-bearing constraints future agents must NOT violate:
- docs/plans/sandbox-update-v1.md is a FROZEN design record — never edit it during simplification implementation.
- Work items 1 and 2 both edit the manager.py staging cluster — never land them in the same commit.
- §7 keep-as-is register (audited 2026-09-05) forbids "simplifying": metadataRefreshed bool|None tri-state in LibraryUpdateResult; single-caller pure helpers (_splitOutdatedSpecs, _diffPoolVersions, _collectDuplicatePoolNames — module-level for direct unit testability); _collectUpdateAllNames retry-under-lock (ratified fail-closed guard); pool_staging.py defensive surface (test-pinned responses to verified threat classes); handler render/cap cluster; dead sessionId dispatch params (uniform dispatcher signature convention).
- Accepted behavior delta (item 2): updateHelperHostPath().is_file() → ConfigError pre-check moves into _runPrefilterContainer, so ConfigError now fires only when a container will actually run (after empty-pool/nothing-outdated short-circuits). Cross-reference: existing memory a57632fd notes python-sandboxing-v1.md (~line 959) still documents the removed installCommand ABC and that the ABC "now has reportCommand / stageInstallCommand / updateHelperHostPath" — work item 1 of this plan renames those to reportRun/stageRun, so any pending docs-drift fix in python-sandboxing-v1.md must align with item 1's final shape, not the current one.

title: StagingRun plan object implemented: runtime owns staging container command+mounts
content:
Work item 1 of docs/plans/sandbox-update-simplification-v1.md IMPLEMENTED in working tree (2026-09-05, uncommitted; supersedes the "not-yet-implemented" status of the audit-verdict memory). Design as built:
- lib/sandbox/runtimes/base.py: module-level @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True) `StagingRun` with `command: list[str]` and `mounts: list[dict[str, str]]` — mounts typed EXACTLY as ContainerSpec.mounts in lib/sandbox/types.py (a LIST of dicts with keys hostPath/containerPath/mode, NOT a flat dict). The ABC's annotation-only UPDATE_HELPER_CONTAINER_PATH / STAGING_CONTAINER_PATH declarations were deleted; abstract `reportRun(hostStagingIoDir: Path, specs: Sequence[str]) -> StagingRun` and `stageRun(...)` replace reportCommand/stageInstallCommand; updateHelperHostPath() kept (manager pre-check uses it).
- lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/runtime.py: the two path constants kept as PUBLIC class attributes (tests reference them symbolically); reportRun/stageRun implemented; mount-dict construction moved VERBATIM from the manager into private `_buildStagingMounts(hostStagingIoDir)` (io bind rw at STAGING_CONTAINER_PATH, helper bind ro at UPDATE_HELPER_CONTAINER_PATH); old argv-builder methods deleted.
- lib/sandbox/manager.py: `_stagingMounts` deleted; _runPrefilterContainer hoists `ioDir = runDir / STAGING_IO_DIRNAME` and builds the ContainerSpec from `runtimeImpl.reportRun(ioDir, list(specs))` (.command/.mounts); _runStagedInstall uses `stageRun(ioDir, list(specs))`; report parse reads ioDir/"report.json"; no imports became dead.
- tests/lib/sandbox/runtimes/test_python_runtime.py: TestReportRun/TestStageRun assert .command (exact argv, pins unchanged) AND .mounts (exact two-mount list via symbolic constants, correct rw/ro). 22/22 green.
Rationale: the runtime owns its container-side layout; the manager consumes .command/.mounts verbatim into ContainerSpec and never assembles mounts itself.

content: From the StagingRun refactor (work item 1, 2026-09-05): when a task defines acceptance via a mechanical `rg` pattern (e.g. `_stagingMounts` must show zero hits), name NEW private helpers to avoid colliding with the scanned pattern — the runtime-side mount builder was deliberately named `_buildStagingMounts` instead of `_stagingMounts` so the acceptance scan for the deleted SandboxManager method returns zero hits unambiguously. title: StagingRun test amendment applied: self-referential assertions were the breakage; hostStagingIoDir is a mount-only arg
content: Root cause of the 5 test_manager.py failures during the StagingRun refactor: assertions computed expected argv by calling the production builders themselves (self-referential expected values), so deleting reportCommand/stageInstallCommand broke them via AttributeError — the symbolic-constant insulation held (every mount assertion referencing PythonRuntime.STAGING_CONTAINER_PATH etc. passed unchanged). Fixed 2026-09-05 by the authorized mechanical swap to plan methods: `runtimeImpl.stageRun(Path("io"), ["x"]).command` / `.reportRun(Path("io"), ["x"]).command` at :835, :1016, :1080, :1154-1155, :1590 plus docstrings :17/:773; amendment note recorded in docs/plans/sandbox-update-simplification-v1.md. Gates after fix: pyright 0 errors; 4590 passed / 11 skipped. Testability contract worth remembering: reportRun/stageRun's first arg hostStagingIoDir ONLY feeds the mount hostPath (via str(hostStagingIoDir.absolute())); it never appears in .command, so any Path literal is a valid dummy for command-only comparisons. LESSON: before trusting a plan's "tests stay untouched via symbolic-constant insulation" claim, grep the test files for direct references to the symbols being removed — self-referential command assertions bypass that insulation.

title: replaceAll over identical lines consumes targets needed by later paired edits — order multi-edit batches accordingly
content: During the test_manager.py amendment (2026-09-05), three identical lines (`assert stageSpec.command == runtimeImpl.stageInstallCommand(["numpy"])` at :1016/:1080/:1155) were handled with a replaceAll edit, while a later batch item planned a paired :1154–1155 edit whose oldString included :1155 unchanged. The replaceAll executed first and rewrote :1155, so the paired edit's oldString no longer matched and :1154 had to be fixed in a separate follow-up edit. Rule: when a multi-edit batch mixes replaceAll over duplicated strings with region/paired edits that include any of those duplicates, apply the paired/region edits FIRST, or re-read the file and re-derive oldStrings after each edit. No impact this time — final content matched spec exactly.

title: updateRuntimeLibraries flow ordering + _enumeratePoolVersions tolerates missing pool dir
content:
Gromozeka lib/sandbox/manager.py, after sandbox-update-simplification-v1 work item 2 (2026-09-05):

- Flow order in `updateRuntimeLibraries`: Step 1 validate named specs → Step 2 build pre-filter spec set (empty-pool short-circuit applies ONLY when `packages is None`) → Step 3 baseline enumeration (`_enumeratePoolVersions` + `_collectDuplicatePoolNames`) → Step 4 `_runPrefilterContainer`. The helper-existence ConfigError now fires ONLY inside the container runners (`_runPrefilterContainer` after run/io dir setup before `reportRun`/`runOneshot`; `_runStagedInstall` before `stageRun`) — zero inline copies in the public flow.
- CRITICAL non-obvious behavior: `_enumeratePoolVersions(libsDir)` returns `{}` (and `_collectDuplicatePoolNames` returns empty set) for a MISSING/non-dir libsDir — it does NOT raise. The plan doc had claimed it "propagates"; code shows fault-tolerance. This is load-bearing: `testMissingHelperRaisesConfigError` (tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py) calls `updateRuntimeLibraries(["numpy"])` with NO pool set up and passes unchanged because (a) named-specs requests never hit the short-circuits and (b) enumeration tolerates the missing dir, so the flow reaches `_runPrefilterContainer` which raises ConfigError before `runOneshot` (asserted not-awaited via stubbed `updateHelperHostPath`).
- Gotcha for future reordering (esp. work item 4, single pool walk): any change that makes an earlier step raise on a missing pool dir, or moves a container run before the spec-set step, will silently change when/whether this pinned ConfigError fires. Ratified behavior delta: missing-helper ConfigError on the update path fires only when a container will actually run (after empty-pool and nothing-outdated short-circuits).

title: StagingPurpose StrEnum landed (work item 2); audit memory 3590e661 partially superseded
content:
2026-09-05: sandbox-update-simplification-v1 work item 2 implemented (uncommitted at session time; work item 1 StagingRun landed in a3fee9ae):

title: Load-bearing check-before-mkdir ordering in _runStagedInstall
content:
Verified 2026-09-05 during the work-item-2 review of sandbox-update-simplification-v1 (working tree, items 3-4 still pending; line numbers drift after item 4):

In `lib/sandbox/manager.py` `_runStagedInstall`, the `updateHelperHostPath().is_file()` → ConfigError pre-check MUST stay BEFORE `libsDir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)`. If reordered, a missing-helper ConfigError would create an empty live-pool directory — which suppresses crash-leftover adoption in pool recovery (the failure mode documented in the installRuntimeLibraries docstring). Current code has the correct order (check ~:2056-2060, mkdir ~:2062-2064).

Related non-gaps confirmed so nobody re-flags them:
- `if not specs: return (True, None)` early return precedes the check — harmless: no container runs, and both callers guarantee non-empty specs (installRuntimeLibraries validates/raises; updateRuntimeLibraries short-circuits empty-outdated before staging).
- In `_runPrefilterContainer`, runDir/ioDir are created before the check but the `finally: shutil.rmtree(runDir)` cleans them — no leak, no live-pool side effect.

title: ConfigError test relies on missing-dir tolerance of pool enumerators
content:
Verified 2026-09-05 (work-item-2 review; line numbers as of that tree):

`tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py::testMissingHelperRaisesConfigError` (~:1793-1811) creates NO pool (via `_makeManager`, no `_makePool`), stubs `updateHelperHostPath` to a missing file, and calls `updateRuntimeLibraries(["numpy"])` (named spec). After work item 2 moved the ConfigError into `_runPrefilterContainer`, the Step-3 baseline enumeration (`_enumeratePoolVersions` + `_collectDuplicatePoolNames` in updateRuntimeLibraries) now runs BEFORE the ConfigError site — the test passes only because both enumerators tolerate a missing pool dir: `_enumeratePoolVersions` returns `{}` when `libsDir.is_dir()` is False (~manager.py:1816-1817) and `_collectDuplicatePoolNames` returns `set()` (~:1840-1841), no filesystem walk, no raise.

Consequence: if either missing-dir guard is ever removed, this test breaks with OSError/FileNotFoundError instead of the expected ConfigError. This reliance was introduced by item 2 (pre-move, the outer check fired before Step 3). No other test couples missing-helper with the short-circuits.

title: Update-path short-circuit ordering vs pre-filter; plan wording imprecise
content:
Verified 2026-09-05 exact ordering in `updateRuntimeLibraries` (lib/sandbox/manager.py, working tree with item 2 applied; line refs drift after item 4):

UnknownRuntime check → opportunistic `_reconcileRuntimePool` (non-raising; converts lock-busy/errors to False) → SC-0 named-but-empty packages → success noop → spec validation (all-fail raises) → SC-1 empty update-all name set → "Nothing installed" success (~:1251-1261, BEFORE pre-filter; named specs skip it entirely) → baseline `_enumeratePoolVersions` + `_collectDuplicatePoolNames` (~:1271-1272) → `_runPrefilterContainer` (~:1278, FIRST container; ConfigError site) → SC-2 empty-outdated → success noop (~:1284-1294, necessarily AFTER pre-filter: the pre-filter produces the outdated/upToDate split) → poolLock/recover/re-enumerate → `_runStagedInstall(purpose=StagingPurpose.UPDATE)`.

Missing-helper behavior: update-all on an empty pool returns success without touching a container; the "All up to date" (SC-2) reply is UNREACHABLE with a missing helper — ConfigError fires first because the pre-filter must run to compute the split.

DOC DRIFT: docs/plans/sandbox-update-simplification-v1.md (~:96-98) says ConfigError "now fires after the empty-pool and nothing-outdated short-circuits" — half imprecise. True for empty-pool only; for nothing-outdated the causal arrow is inverted (ConfigError necessarily precedes SC-2). docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md echoes the loose phrasing. Wording nit, not a code defect — worth fixing if the plan doc is touched again.

title: Four runOneshot sites; pre-filter/refresh purpose literals by design; GC ignores purpose values
content:
From the 2026-09-05 work-item-2 guard-gap sweep (lib/sandbox):

1. `lib/` has exactly FOUR `backend.runOneshot` call sites: `runCode` (~manager.py:726, mounts workspace rw + libPool ro — no helper), `_runPrefilterContainer` (~:1965, helper ro via `reportRun`), `_runStagedInstall` (~:2085, helper ro via `stageRun`), `_refreshPackageList` (~:2218, libsDir rw + tmp rw — no helper). Only the middle two mount `updateHelperHostPath`, and each self-checks. Handlers (internal/bot/common/handlers/sandbox.py) only call manager methods — never construct containers.

2. Residual free-form purpose literals are BY DESIGN and test-pinned: the pre-filter container hardcodes name prefix `sandbox-update-{runId}` (~:1967) and label `"sandbox.purpose": "update"` (~:1980); `_refreshPackageList` uses `"list"` (~:2255). Plan item 2 deliberately scoped `StagingPurpose` to `_runStagedInstall` only (see memory 4c15d239); a future pass could reuse `StagingPurpose.UPDATE` in the pre-filter but that was outside the ratified scope. Tests assert these literals (test_manager.py ~:836-837, ~:1158).

3. GC does NOT key on purpose-string values or container-name prefixes: gc.py (~:186-203) matches only `sandbox.runId` and `sandbox.stagingRunId` liveness; `listManagedContainers` filters `sandbox.managed=true` (backends/docker.py ~:440). So changing StagingPurpose values would break only external ops tooling (docker ps filters), not in-repo GC — value stability is still required and pinned by tests/lib/sandbox/test_enums.py.

title: Plan doc + teamlead memory misstate ConfigError vs nothing-outdated ordering (work item 2)
content:
Review finding (2026-09-05, work item 2 of sandbox-update-simplification-v1, Important / focus-4 FAIL): the ratified behavior-delta sentence in `docs/plans/sandbox-update-simplification-v1.md:96-98` — "ConfigError on the update path now fires only when a container will actually run... after the empty-pool AND nothing-outdated short-circuits" — is HALF WRONG, and `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md:47` echoes the same wrong claim.

Only the empty-pool (SC-1) half is true. The nothing-outdated short-circuit (SC-2, manager.py:1284-1294) is computed FROM the pre-filter container's report, and the missing-helper ConfigError fires inside `_runPrefilterContainer` (:1959-1963) BEFORE that container runs. So with a missing helper the "all up to date" success reply is UNREACHABLE — ConfigError always fires first. (This was equally true pre-move — the old outer check also preceded the pre-filter — so it is plan-wording drift, not a regression introduced by item 2.)

Precise `updateRuntimeLibraries` order (manager.py, pre item-4 renumber): :1177 UnknownRuntime → :1194 opportunistic _reconcileRuntimePool (non-raising) → SC-0 :1197 named-but-empty noop → :1213-1229 validate specs / all-fail InvalidPackageSpec → SC-1 :1251-1261 update-all empty pool "Nothing installed" (BEFORE pre-filter) → :1271-1272 baseline enumeration → :1278 _runPrefilterContainer (ConfigError site) → SC-2 :1284-1294 empty outdated noop (necessarily AFTER pre-filter) → :1312 _runStagedInstall(UPDATE).

Fix direction: reword the plan (and teamlead-memory) to say the check fires after the update-all empty-pool short-circuit but before the pre-filter container; the all-current path still requires a valid helper. Related same-cluster drift this review flagged (Recommend): plan :109-113/:147-170 and teamlead-memory.md:49 keep the old "Step 4" name for the baseline-enumeration block that code comments now call Step 3 (:1266) — recommendation is to RENAME the references rather than keep the interpretive "Step 4 now means..." amendment wording; teamlead-memory.md:47-50 overall still describes the pre-item-2 state (no runner check, StagingPurpose pending) and needs marking item 2 implemented.

content:

title: Work-item-4 review verdict: implementation PASS on 5/6, tests FAIL — two concrete test-strength fixes outstanding
content:
2026-09-05 code review of the uncommitted sandbox-update-simplification-v1 work-item-4 diff (vs HEAD 8c2d1b8c; 4 files +90/−24; implementation background in memory 5c42e5a6). Review-only session — fixes NOT applied; they remain outstanding for a future session.

Verdicts by focus point: (1) walk count PASS, (2) semantic equivalence PASS (`entries[0].version` first-entry rule, `len(entries) > 1` duplicate rule, missing/non-dir → `({}, set())` all preserved), (3) OSError reasoning PASS (old order versions-first; `_collectDuplicatePoolNames` had 1 production caller, 0 direct test callers), (4) tests FAIL, (5) docs PASS, (6) AGENTS.md compliance PASS. Gates re-verified: make lint clean (pyright 0), targeted test_manager.py 57 passed, make check-docs 3046 links 0 broken, zero `_collectDuplicatePoolNames` refs.

Outstanding finding 1 — healing-test vacuity (tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py ~:2015-2038, `testDuplicateDistInfoNameForcedOutdatedAndHealed`): the test derives `reportVersion` from one `_enumeratePoolWithDuplicates()` call, but `updateRuntimeLibraries()` performs ANOTHER unordered `enumerateDistInfos` walk. On a filesystem returning different iterdir orders across the two scans, the ordinary version-mismatch path forces the update and the test stays green even if the `duplicateNames` guard is disconnected. Recommended fix: give both duplicate dist-info dirs the SAME parsed version but different directory names (e.g. `foo-1.0.dist-info` + `foo-legacy-1.0.dist-info`, both `Name: foo`, version 1.0) and hard-code reportVersion — then only the duplicate guard can trigger staging.

Outstanding finding 2 — direct unit test underpowered (test_manager.py ~:2043-2077, `testEnumeratePoolWithDuplicatesVersionsAndDuplicateNames`): despite its "one walk" docstring it only checks returned values — it would pass if the helper called `enumerateDistInfos` twice, and `versions["foo"] in {"1.0", "2.0"}` cannot distinguish first-entry from last-entry selection. Recommended fix: monkeypatch/spy `enumerateDistInfos` (a controlled mock seam IS feasible — this refines the implementer-session claim in memory 5c42e5a6 that "no call-count seam exists") with a deterministic inventory; assert exactly ONE call, the first entry's version, and `{"foo"}` duplicates; keep the real-filesystem missing-dir assertion separate.

Nit + residual risk: helper docstring's "zero behavior change" is too absolute given the acknowledged TOCTOU race (suggest "equivalent for a stable pool; sole-enumeration errors propagate"); OSError propagation posture is verified statically only — no direct regression test raises OSError mid-walk.

Scope clarifications confirmed during review: update-all keeps its own separate Step 2 `_collectUpdateAllNames()` enumeration — outside the ratified Step-3 single-walk scope; the empty-pool short-circuit precedes the pre-filter container, so the helper pre-check inside `_runPrefilterContainer` never fires on that path (pinned by the regression test at test_manager.py ~:1740).

title: Deterministic duplicate-heal test pattern: identical parsed versions + hard-coded report version
content:
Review fix (2026-09-05, work-item-4 re-review) for `tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py::TestUpdateRuntimeLibraries::testDuplicateDistInfoNameForcedOutdatedAndHealed`:

GOTCHA: production `updateRuntimeLibraries` runs a SECOND independent `enumerateDistInfos` walk over the pool after the pip report; if a test derives its expected report version from its OWN `_enumeratePoolWithDuplicates()` walk, unordered scans can disagree and the test passes via the ordinary version-mismatch path even with the duplicate-name guard broken (complements the known APFS iterdir nondeterminism — here the failure mode is test-vs-production walk divergence, not first-entry pick alone).

Fix pattern: make BOTH duplicate dist-info directories parse to the SAME version but keep different directory names — `foo-1.0.dist-info` + `foo-legacy-1.0.dist-info`, both `Name: foo`, version "1.0" — then HARD-CODE the expected report version ("1.0"). With identical parsed versions the version comparison always says up-to-date, so ONLY the duplicate-name guard can force the outdated/staged-heal path — deterministic regardless of scan order. The helper call remains only to pin `duplicateNames == {"foo"}` (order-independent).

Key parsing detail that makes this work: `_parseDistInfoDir` (`lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/pool_staging.py`) reads `Name:` from METADATA headers and derives the version from the directory stem's LAST `-` segment (`stem.rpartition("-")[2]`), so `foo-legacy-1.0.dist-info` parses to `("foo", "1.0")` — a legacy-named dir can carry the same parsed version as the canonical one. Healing assertions unchanged: after merge `foo-3.0.dist-info` present, both old dirs gone.

title: Spying on enumerateDistInfos in SandboxManager tests: patch target + is_dir guard ordering
content:
Technique proven 2026-09-05 in `tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py::testEnumeratePoolWithDuplicatesVersionsAndDuplicateNames` for pinning `_enumeratePoolWithDuplicates` invariants:

1. Patch target: `lib/sandbox/manager.py` binds `enumerateDistInfos` via a top-level `from .runtimes.python.pool_staging import enumerateDistInfos` (~line 47), so the monkeypatch target is the string `"lib.sandbox.manager.enumerateDistInfos"` (module-namespace reference, NOT the source module).
2. ORDERING GOTCHA: `_enumeratePoolWithDuplicates` checks `libsDir.is_dir()` and returns `({}, set())` BEFORE calling `enumerateDistInfos` — a spy test must `libsDir.mkdir(parents=True)` even though the spy bypasses real filesystem scanning, or the spy is never reached.
3. Spy inventory type: `dict[str, list[DistInfoEntry]]`; `DistInfoEntry` is a NamedTuple `(path: Path, version: str)` in pool_staging.py — construct synthetic entries without touching disk.
4. The three invariants the spy pins (impossible to pin via real filesystem, whose iterdir order is nondeterministic on APFS): (a) spy called EXACTLY ONCE per helper call (`spyPoolRoots == [libsDir]`), (b) FIRST-entry version selection via full-dict equality `versions == {"foo": "1.0", "bar": "0.9"}` with a two-entry "foo" inventory, (c) `duplicateNames == {"foo"}`.
5. Convention: real-filesystem behaviors (e.g. missing-dir → `({}, set())`) stay in their own separate test method — don't merge with spy tests. The real enumeration path remains covered end-to-end by the update-flow tests that create real dist-infos.

title: Docstring wording rule: no absolute "zero behavior change" claims for behavior-preserving refactors
content:
Decision from the 2026-09-05 work-item-4 re-review (NIT finding): docstrings/comments must NOT claim absolute "zero behavior change" for a refactor that merged two enumeration walks. Reviewer-approved wording, now in `lib/sandbox/manager.py::_enumeratePoolWithDuplicates` docstring: "for a stable pool this single walk is equivalent to the former call pair; OSErrors from the sole enumeration propagate; the removed second walk was the only location that swallowed OSError. A missing or non-directory pool is NOT an error: empty results are returned."

Rationale: behavior equivalence holds only for a stable pool; under concurrency/errors the postures genuinely differ (the deleted second walk `_collectDuplicatePoolNames` swallowed OSError, the surviving walk propagates), so an unqualified "zero behavior change" claim is false and misleads future readers.

Also verified: `docs/plans/sandbox-update-simplification-v1.md` amendment (~lines 188-197) already uses accurate non-absolute wording (propagate posture resolved; swallow was reachable only in a becomes-unreadable-between-calls TOCTOU race; no test pinned it) — deliberately left unchanged. Note the phrase "zero behavior change" DOES appear legitimately elsewhere in the repo for genuinely inert defaults (e.g. NullStatsStorage in test_message_stats.py / stats docs) — context matters; the rule targets refactors with error-path posture changes.

title: _enumeratePoolWithDuplicates fail-loud OSError contract, pinned by regression test
content:
Contract (sandbox simplification arc, close-out 2026-09-05): `lib/sandbox/manager.py::_enumeratePoolWithDuplicates` deliberately propagates `OSError` from `enumerateDistInfos` — only the missing-directory case is tolerated (yields empty results). The deleted `_collectDuplicatePoolNames` second walk was the only OSError swallower on the update path; propagation is intentional fail-loud so an unreadable pool aborts the update rather than silently passing the duplicates check. Do NOT reintroduce swallowing (e.g. broad try/except around the walk).

Pinned by `tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py::TestUpdateRuntimeLibraries::testEnumeratePoolWithDuplicatesPropagatesOSError`: monkeypatches the string target `"lib.sandbox.manager.enumerateDistInfos"` with a signature-faithful raiser, builds an existing libsDir via the class `_libsDir` helper, calls `manager._enumeratePoolWithDuplicates(libsDir)`, asserts `pytest.raises(OSError)`.

Testing conventions confirmed: the `_enumeratePoolWithDuplicates` tests are sync `def` (the helper is sync, no await); the spy/raiser uses the string-target monkeypatch pattern from `testEnumeratePoolWithDuplicatesVersionsAndDuplicateNames`; black may join the test signature to one line (within 120-char limit).

title: docs/plans/ close-out conventions: status line phasing + keep-as-is register pruning
content:
Two conventions from the sandbox-update-simplification-v1 close-out (2026-09-05):

1. **Status line**: companion plan docs under `docs/plans/` use a single-line phase+date list (`Status: **approved 2026-09-05, implementation in progress.**`). Related status-line conventions already recorded for docs/design/ multi-arc docs and ADRs are separate formats — docs/plans/ companion plans use this simpler phase-list style.

title: Dead-config deletion workflow: sweep surface, stop condition, full edit surface, exempt locations
content:
Proven recipe from the image-pull-policy removal (2026-09-06, follow-up (b) of sandbox-update-simplification-v1):

1. SWEEP: search all spellings (`kebab-case|snake_case|camelCase`) across lib/ internal/ scripts/ tests/ configs/ main.py AND a broader fragment sweep (`pullPolicy|pull_policy|pull-policy`) to catch docstring mentions and hypothetical dynamic `getattr` strings. Zero fragment hits outside definition sites = conclusive no-reader proof.
2. STOP CONDITION: if any production path actually CONSULTS the value, stop and report the reader. Parse/store-in-config-with-zero-consumers still counts as dead.
3. FULL EDIT SURFACE (wider than the obvious four): TOML key; dataclass field + its docstring entry + its `data.get(...)` line (keep surrounding parse structure); docs/llm/configuration.md table row; STALE DOCSTRING MENTIONS IN CONSUMING CLASSES — `DockerBackend.__init__` Args docstring listed `imagePullPolicy` even though it only stored the config; check these; NEWLY-UNUSED IMPORTS — removing the `Literal[...]`-typed field orphaned the `Literal` import (flake8 catches it at lint, fix proactively); test pins (there were none here).
4. ACCEPTANCE-SWEEP EXEMPT LOCATIONS: after deletion, `rg` legitimately still hits docs/plans/ (historical plan docs, including the ticked checkbox line itself), docs/archive/plans/, docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md, plus the sanctioned CHANGELOG Removed entry. Do not scrub these.
5. GOTCHA — transient LSP diagnostics: removing a field and its parse line as two sequential edits fires an LSP error ("No parameter named X") between the edits that self-resolves once the paired edit lands. Confirm with `make lint` (pyright) rather than reacting mid-edit.
6. No regression test is required for dead-config removal with zero behavior change when no test referenced the field — note this explicitly in the handoff.
7. Deliverable format the user expects: hit-classification table (hit → classification → action), per-file change summary, gate results with exact counts.

Caveat: before deleting, also check docs/llm/tasks.md — its bad-example rows cite REAL config keys and can go stale (see separate memory on that trap; tasks.md did not cite image-pull-policy).

title: Kept-for-post-mortem stage container 409s image deletion — cleanup must sweep containers first
content:
Gotcha hit while bringing up `tests/lib/sandbox/test_install_integration.py`: `SandboxManager._runStagedInstall()` deliberately KEEPS the stage container when the pip install fails (for post-mortem), by design. That container holds the image, so `backend.removeImage()` fails with HTTP 409 Conflict until it's gone. Test cleanup that only removes images will therefore fail (and if cleanup raises in a `finally`, `pytest.fail` MASKS the original test failure).

Correct cleanup order for Docker-gated sandbox tests:
1. `manager.listManagedContainers()` (filter label `sandbox.managed=true`), `inspectContainer()` each and match `Config.Image` against the test's unique image tags — `ManagedContainerInfo` has NO image field, so inspecting is required; matching on unique test-scoped tags gives precise ownership.
2. `removeContainer(force=True)` on matches (also cleans the kept-for-post-mortem container).
3. THEN `removeImage()` × 2, each wrapped so failures don't mask a body failure; guard any cleanup `pytest.fail` with `sys.exc_info()[0] is None` so it only fires when the test body itself passed.

title: Errno 13 on staging delta from unshared bind path — looks like uid perms, root cause is Colima mount scope
content:
Refines two existing memories (1d8c717d "/tmp & /var/folders not shared", 997ce065 "$HOME binds work across uids"): when the staging io-dir bind source lives under pytest `tmp_path` (`/var/folders/...`), Colima doesn't share it, Docker silently materializes an EMPTY directory inside the VM owned by root, and the uid-1000 container then fails `ensure_dir(/sandbox/staging/delta)` with `PermissionError: Errno 13` — a symptom that masquerades as a bind-ownership problem when the real cause is the unshared host path. pip had already downloaded fine (network OK), which adds to the misdirection.

Implication: per the prior observation that bind mounts from `$HOME` DO work across uids on this Colima setup, the `SecurityConfig(user="0:0")` now baked into `test_install_integration.py` is likely unnecessary belt-and-suspenders (it was added alongside the home-dir fix while debugging). Don't cargo-cult root-user containers for home-dir binds; if revisiting the test, root could probably be dropped — but the hardening contract is covered by production config + unit tests either way.

Also learned: pre-existing empty `~/.gromozeka-tests/test-<nanosecond-timestamp>/` dirs (dated May) are junk from some older run whose creator is no longer greppable — not from any current sandbox test; don't blame new tests for them during leak checks.

title: DockerBackend swallows DockerError in removeImage/removeContainer; close() never raises
content:
DockerBackend (lib/sandbox/backends/docker.py) deliberately defangs Docker-API-level failures, which callers must not rely on exceptions to detect:

- `removeImage` (lines 176-191): catches `aiodocker.DockerError` and only logs a warning (lines 189-190). Removal failures — e.g. 409 conflict when a container (even stopped) still uses the image — never propagate.
- `removeContainer` (lines ~380-397): same pattern — `aiodocker.DockerError` swallowed (lines 396-397).
- `close()` (lines 463-484): internally guards every step (connector close → try/except-log; client.close → try/except-pass; no-op when `_client is None`), so close can never raise in practice.
- Only non-DockerError exceptions propagate — chiefly `DockerUnavailable` raised lazily from `_getClient` (lines 54-102).

Consequence for tests/callers: wrapping these calls in try/except gives an illusion of verified cleanup. To actually verify removal, post-delete `images.inspect`/`containers.inspect` and expect a 404. Discovered 2026-09-06 while reviewing tests/lib/sandbox/test_install_integration.py whose `cleanupErrors` mechanism silently misses every DockerError-based removal failure, so its "nothing leaks" contract could pass vacuously. Related: the existing memory that `removeImage` has zero production callers (it exists for this kind of test cleanup).

title: ensureImage skips build when tag exists; _buildImage success check is weak; DOCKER_HOST preferred over config
content:
Non-obvious behaviors in sandbox image management (lib/sandbox/backends/docker.py, lib/sandbox/manager.py):

- `ensureImage` skips the build entirely when `client.images.inspect(imageTag)` succeeds (docker.py:167-172). An assertion like `prepareRuntime(...) is True` with fixed image tags therefore proves images EXIST, not that they were built — a stale image with the same tag (leaked from an aborted prior run, or a concurrent run) is silently reused and indistinguishable from a fresh build. To make a build deterministic in a test, pre-delete the tags before prepareRuntime.
- `_buildImage` success detection is weak: `if ret and "error" in ret[-1]` (docker.py:235) — an empty build-message stream short-circuits to success. Builds also run with `pull=True` (network dependency).
- `_getClient` prefers the `DOCKER_HOST` env var over the configured `DockerBackendConfig.baseUrl` (docker.py:95). The client connects lazily — `DockerBackend.__init__` only stores config (`self._client = None`, docker.py:45-52) — so importing/constructing the manager has NO daemon access; safe at pytest collection time.
- `Runtime.isPrepared()` starts False for fresh runtimes (lib/sandbox/runtimes/base.py:63,79); on `ImageBuildFailed`, `prepareRuntime` returns `isPrepared()` (i.e. False), so `prepared is True` does require both ensureImage calls to succeed. But `DockerUnavailable` is NOT an `ImageBuildFailed` — it propagates out of prepareRuntime uncaught (manager.py ~357-384), so a wrong DOCKER_HOST makes prepareRuntime raise rather than return False.
- Production default image tags: `gromozeka-sandbox-python:run` / `:install` (lib/sandbox/config.py:321-322). Default baseUrl is `unix:///var/run/docker.sock`.
- GarbageCollector does NOT start a background loop in __init__ — collectGarbage/recover run only when explicitly called, so manager construction has no async side effects.

title: Staged-install failure semantics: swap errors raise, refresh is best-effort, pool never mounted by stage container
content:
Failure/reporting semantics of the sandbox staged-install pipeline (verified 2026-09-06 while reviewing tests/lib/sandbox/test_install_integration.py):

- pip's exit code propagates through the in-container runner (lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/pool_pip_runner.py:130-131) and `stageOk = exitCode == 0 and no signal and not oom` (manager.py:2113), so `installRuntimeLibraries()` returning False genuinely means the stage container/pip failed.
- BUT swap-stage failures do NOT return False — they raise: `swapPools` raises `ConfigError`/`PoolSwapRollbackFailed` (lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/pool_staging.py:458-482, re-raised at manager.py:2142-2152); pool-lock contention raises `LibraryPoolLocked` (lib/sandbox/locks.py:299-302). Callers/tests must expect exceptions, not a False sentinel, for swap/lock errors.
- `_refreshPackageList` is best-effort: its failure is swallowed with logger.exception (manager.py:1105-1113) and install still returns True. The only way to detect a failed refresh is `listRuntimeLibraries()` — `loadPackagesInfo` returns `[]` (not an error) when packages.json is missing (lib/sandbox/metadata/filesystem.py:295-297), and in the install flow `_refreshPackageList` is the sole writer of `meta/runtimes/<runtime>/packages.json` (manager.py:2292-2294). `atomicWriteJson` mkdirs parents (lib/sandbox/storage.py:136), so no pre-created subdirs needed.
- Proof of merge/swap: the stage container never mounts the live pool — its mounts are only the `io/` subtree plus the read-only helper script (lib/sandbox/runtimes/python/runtime.py:114-125); `newpool`/`oldpool` sit outside every mount (manager.py:2072-2081). Therefore a dist-info appearing in the live libsDir can only be explained by the host-side merge (manager.py:2134-2136) + atomic swap (manager.py:2143).
- `enumerateDistInfos` only creates a per-name key when appending an entry (pool_staging.py:249), so entries are non-empty by construction — asserting `inventory[name]` non-empty is tautological.
- `prepareRuntime` mkdirs libsDir (manager.py:350-352) BEFORE image ensure, so `libsDir.is_dir()` alone doesn't prove image prep.

title: Review findings on test_install_integration.py: vacuous cleanup paths, over-broad rmtree(parent), image-identity ownership
content:
Read-only review verdict (2026-09-06) on the then-uncommitted tests/lib/sandbox/test_install_integration.py against production code. Core assertions proved non-vacuous: `installed is True` (pip exit propagates), dist-info glob (pool starts empty, stage container can't write pool — merge+swap is the only path), `listRuntimeLibraries` (loadPackagesInfo returns [] on missing file, sole writer is the refresh). Concrete gaps found, relevant if a fix session picks this up:

1. Vacuous "nothing leaks" cleanup: backend removeImage/removeContainer swallow DockerError internally (see memory 38ac5922), so the test's `cleanupErrors` except-handlers only ever see non-DockerError raises; per-container inspect failure → `containerImage = ""` → container silently skipped → subsequent image delete hits 409 → swallowed → test passes with leaked container+image. Fix direction: verify via post-delete inspect expecting 404.
2. `shutil.rmtree(storageRoot.parent, ignore_errors=True)` (test:225) removes `~/.gromozeka-tests/test-install-integration/` — the PARENT — deleting sibling run dirs of concurrent runs mid-flight. Should rmtree `storageRoot` (the uuid dir) instead. `ignore_errors=True` also silently leaks root-owned files on native Linux (test containers run as `0:0`).
3. Fixed tags guarantee no collision with production defaults (`gromozeka-sandbox-python:run|:install`, config.py:321-322) but do NOT guarantee a build happens (ensureImage skips on existing tag, docker.py:167-172); a leftover image survives swallowed cleanup failures and gets silently reused. Pre-deleting the tags before prepareRuntime would make the build deterministic.
4. Concurrency: ownership is keyed solely by `Config.Image` equality (test:204-214) — two concurrent runs share the fixed tags and force-remove each other's in-flight stage/list containers. `listManagedContainers` is daemon-wide, filtered only by `sandbox.managed=true` label (docker.py:440-441); production containers carry the same label (manager.py:744), so the scan inspects every managed container on a shared daemon (safe — image gate — but O(daemon)). Per-run storage roots mean per-run pool.lock files, so no cross-run lock serialization.
5. `listManagedContainers()` itself raising (DockerUnavailable from lazy _getClient, docker.py:54-102) at test:204 is uncaught: skips container AND image removal, propagates through the inner finally, and the `if cleanupErrors:` block (test:226-230) never runs — cleanup exception can mask the original body assertion error.
6. Dead branches: the `RUN_IMAGE_TAG` container-removal branch never fires (no runCode in this test); the `close()` except (test:223-224) is unreachable (close never raises).
7. No collection-time Docker access anywhere (lazy client; env reads only) — confirmed safe; autouse singleton-reset fixture touches class attributes only.

title: ensureImage() skips build when tag already exists — fixed test tags allow stale-image reuse
content:
`DockerBackend.ensureImage()` (lib/sandbox/backends/docker.py ~:167-172) first tries `client.images.inspect(imageTag)` and **skips the build entirely if a tag already exists locally**. Consequences verified 2026-09-06 while reviewing tests/lib/sandbox/test_install_integration.py:

1. Fixed test image tags (`gromozeka-sandbox-test-install:run`/`:install`) make any "image was built" claim vacuous: an image left by an aborted prior run is silently reused, so Dockerfile regressions can hide. No assertion in the test proves a build occurred.
2. Concurrent runs sharing fixed tags are mutually destructive: ownership is identified solely by `Config.Image` matching the tag, so run A's cleanup force-removes run B's in-flight stage/list containers, then deletes the shared image. Per-storage-root pool locks (lib/sandbox/locks.py:293-294) give NO cross-run serialization, and a failed run-B removeImage hits a swallowed Docker 409 (see backend error-swallowing memory) so cleanup still reports success.
3. Fix direction (review recommendation): derive BOTH tags from one per-run `uuid4().hex` (`gromozeka-sandbox-test-install-<id>:run`/`:install`), pass into `_makeIntegrationConfig()`, and use the same locals in cleanup. Unique-per-run tags are preferable to `rebuildImage=True` alone because they simultaneously guarantee the build, give unambiguous cleanup ownership, and make concurrent runs safe. Test tags cannot collide with production defaults (`gromozeka-sandbox-python:run`/`:install`, lib/sandbox/config.py:321-322), but static names can never guarantee zero collision with developer artifacts.

Related backend facts found in the same trace: `_buildImage`'s success check is `if ret and "error" in ret[-1]` (docker.py:235) — an empty build-message stream short-circuits to success; `listManagedContainers()` is daemon-wide filtered only by the `sandbox.managed=true` label (docker.py:440-441), which production containers also carry (manager.py:744), so test-cleanup ownership scans inspect every managed container on a shared daemon (safe but O(daemon)).

title: test_install_integration.py review 2026-09-06: CHANGES REQUESTED — open defects and docs recommendation
content:
Code-reviewer verdict 2026-09-06 on the then-uncommitted follow-up-C test `tests/lib/sandbox/test_install_integration.py` (vs HEAD b88ad569): **CHANGES REQUESTED**. Focus verdicts: gating (1), deviations+docs (4), conventions (5), plan §9 edit (6), repo hygiene (7) PASS; isolation+cleanup (2) and assertion quality (3) FAIL. Verified: `make lint` green, targeted pytest without env gate → `1 skipped`, `make check-docs` 0 broken links.

Open Important findings (all UNFIXED at review time):
1. **Fixed image tags** (test:79-83) → stale-image reuse + cross-run interference; fix = per-run UUID-derived tags (see the ensureImage skip-on-existing memory).
2. **Cleanup deletes `storageRoot.parent`** (test:225, `shutil.rmtree(..., ignore_errors=True)`): removes the shared `~/.gromozeka-tests/test-install-integration/` dir, i.e. sibling concurrent runs' pools/meta/tmp vanish mid-flight. Must rmtree `storageRoot` (the uuid-scoped dir) only; optionally non-recursive `rmdir()` the parent when empty. `ignore_errors=True` also hides root-owned-file failures on native-Linux daemons (fine on Colima/Docker Desktop where root maps to host user).
3. **Cleanup error observability**: uncaught `listManagedContainers()` raise (test:204, e.g. DockerUnavailable from a dropped/wrong DOCKER_HOST) skips image removal, never reaches the `cleanupErrors`→`pytest.fail`/`warnings.warn` reporting, and REPLACES the original body failure when the body also failed (masking). Per-container inspect failure → `containerImage=""` → silent skip, then removeImage's swallowed 409 keeps `cleanupErrors` empty → test passes with leaks. Fix: wrap enumeration in try/except appending to `cleanupErrors`, and verify removals post-delete via inspect-expecting-404 (backend swallows DockerError — see related memory).

Recommend-level: add payload assertion `assert (libsDir / "six.py").is_file()` — all current assertions are metadata-only (dist-info glob, `enumerateDistInfos()`, `listRuntimeLibraries()`); a merge bug copying dist-info without the module payload would pass every one. Nit: `assert poolInventory[INSTALL_PACKAGE]` (test:187) is tautological (see staged-install semantics memory).

Docs recommendation (answer: YES): restore a short note in docs/llm/sandbox.md testing section naming this test and explaining the `~/.gromozeka-tests/` workspace + `0:0` container-user deviations — the previous bullet was deleted in 8c2d1b8c along with the dead bootstrap test, but a live user exists again. After fixes land, rerun one real-Docker execution because the resource-ownership path changes.

title: Gate-1 redesign of test_install_integration.py: per-run UUID image tags + daemon-verified, workspace-scoped cleanup
content:
Gate-1 code review findings applied 2026-09-06 to `tests/lib/sandbox/test_install_integration.py` (uncommitted at the time). SUPERSEDES two details in memory 22e96606: the constant test-scoped image tags and the unscoped storage rmtree.

1. PER-RUN IMAGE TAGS (was `gromozeka-sandbox-test-install:run`/`:install` constants): both tags now derive from the same per-run UUID as the workspace — `gromozeka-sandbox-test-install-<uuid4hex>:run` / `:install` (module constant `TEST_IMAGE_PREFIX` + run id) — and are passed as required params into `_makeIntegrationConfig(rootDir, runImageTag, installImageTag)`. Rationale: `DockerBackend.ensureImage()` skips building when a tag already exists, so process-global tags made the build assertion vacuous after any aborted run and made concurrent runs interfere. Tags stay clearly distinct from production defaults (`gromozeka-sandbox-python:run`/`:install`).

2. WORKSPACE DELETION SCOPE (was "rmtree'd in finally" of a broader path): cleanup now removes ONLY the per-run UUID dir (`shutil.rmtree(storageRoot)`, OSError → cleanupErrors). The shared `~/.gromozeka-tests/test-install-integration/` parent is removed only via a guarded non-recursive `rmdir()` (silently kept when non-empty) — concurrent runs can no longer delete each other's workspaces. Observed: after a single run the guarded rmdir removes the now-empty parent too.

3. DAEMON-VERIFIED CLEANUP: because `DockerBackend.removeContainer()`/`removeImage()` swallow `DockerError` (see memory 38ac5922), cleanup re-verifies postconditions against the daemon: re-lists managed containers (flagging any whose inspect `Config.Image` matches a per-run tag) and image-inspects both per-run tags via `backend._getClient()` — `aiodocker.DockerError` status 404 = removed = success; any other error or still-present artifact appends to `cleanupErrors`, and non-empty `cleanupErrors` fails the test. `listManagedContainers()` and per-container inspect failures during enumeration are recorded (no longer silently skipped). Postconditions run BEFORE `backend.close()`.

title: Pyright: manager._backend typed as abstract SandboxBackend — isinstance-narrow to DockerBackend for _getClient()
content: `SandboxManager._backend` is declared as the abstract `SandboxBackend` (lib/sandbox/manager.py ~line 282: `self._backend: SandboxBackend = DockerBackend(dockerConfig)`), so pyright blocks access to DockerBackend-specific members — e.g. `_getClient()` — with "Cannot access attribute for class SandboxBackend". Fix pattern used in tests/lib/sandbox/test_install_integration.py: narrow explicitly with `assert isinstance(backend, DockerBackend)` right after grabbing `manager._backend` (import `DockerBackend` from `lib.sandbox.backends.docker`). This both satisfies pyright basic mode and makes a future backend swap fail loudly in a test that is Docker-only by contract. Related: `aiodocker.DockerError` carries a `.status` attribute — check `exc.status == 404` to treat not-found as success in postcondition/hasImage-style checks (isinstance check needed since it subclasses Exception).

title: Re-review output contract: per-finding resolution table + grouped findings + PASS/FAIL verdict

title: ResourceWarnings in test_manager.py root-caused and fixed via _swapBackend helper
content:
Root-caused and FIXED (2026-09-06, HEAD 48700d77) the ~21 `ResourceWarning` (unclosed aiohttp UnixConnector / socket raddr=…/docker.sock / transport) warnings from tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py. Supersedes the old "noise, don't chase it" observation (deleted memory b3dfdeab). Complements memory 149e323e (manager._gc keeps real backend) — that gotcha is now actually mitigated in the test file.

ROOT CAUSE (classification: (a) test-hygiene, NOT a production leak): `SandboxManager.__init__` captures the real `DockerBackend` at TWO sites — `self._backend` (manager.py:282) and `GarbageCollector(backend=self._backend)` (manager.py:295-300). Tests swapped only `manager._backend` with a mock, leaving `_gc` on the real backend. `recover()` Step 5 (manager.py:1534) → `collectGarbage()` → `_gc.collectAll()` → real `listManagedContainers()` (gc.py:171) → `DockerBackend._getClient()` (docker.py:99) opens a real aiodocker client. Production is sound: nothing in prod reassigns `manager._backend`, and `shutdown()` (manager.py:1414) closes `self._backend`, which IS the GC's object.

KEY MECHANICS (non-obvious):
- Env-dependence: warnings reproduce ONLY when a Docker daemon is reachable (e.g. `DOCKER_HOST=unix:///Users/vgoshev/.colima/default/docker.sock` for Colima). Unreachable daemon → `_getClient()` except-branch (docker.py:104-121) closes the client properly → zero warnings. That's why default/CI runs looked clean.
- Attribution is misleading: ResourceWarnings fire at Python-GC time and pytest blames whichever test is running; the producing tests are the recover()-callers (TestRecoverCrashWindowAdoption etc.). Warning count varies run-to-run (21 vs 27 observed).
- `PYTHONTRACEMALLOC=10` pinned every allocation to aiodocker/docker.py:426 inside `version()` — the `_getClient()` healthcheck. `-W error::ResourceWarning` is the strict acceptance check.
- Aggravating hazard (not just cosmetic): the GC pass could kill/remove REAL sandbox-labeled containers (gc.py:215-216) on the developer's daemon.

FIX (test-only, tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py): added module-level `_swapBackend(manager, backend)` helper that sets BOTH `manager._backend` and `manager._gc._backend`; converted all 11 swap sites (the 4 class-local `_makeManager` helpers + direct test swaps). No client is ever constructed → nothing to close, and no real Docker I/O mid-test (this is why fixture-teardown-close, the test_gc.py pattern, was rejected — it silences the warning but leaves the real I/O). Verified: 0 warnings with DOCKER_HOST + PYTHONTRACEMALLOC=10, `-W error::ResourceWarning` passes, full tests/lib/sandbox real-Docker run 355 passed with 0 warnings, `make format lint` clean, `make test` 4580 passed / 11 skipped.

title: Extracting a mock assignment into a helper breaks pyright narrowing at await_args_list sites
content:
When refactoring Gromozeka tests to move an inline mock assignment (e.g. `manager._backend = _makeMockBackend(...)`) into a helper function, pyright loses the type narrowing the inline reassignment provided. Hit 2026-09-06 in tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py: tests doing `manager._backend.runOneshot.await_args_list[0].kwargs["spec"]` started failing with `Cannot access attribute "await_args_list" for class "MethodType"` because `manager._backend` now stayed typed as `SandboxBackend` (the assignment moved inside `_swapBackend`).

RIGHT WAY: capture the mock in a local variable in the test (`backend = _makeMockBackend(...); _swapBackend(manager, backend)`) and assert against `backend.runOneshot.await_args_list...`. Do NOT use `cast()` — the local-capture pattern is the established, cleaner fix.

General lesson: the repo's pyright (basic mode, tests ARE type-checked) narrows attribute types from preceding assignments in the same scope; extracting assignments into helpers silently breaks downstream attribute-access assertions. Check for attribute assertions on the reassigned attribute before/after such a refactor and run pyright, not just pytest.

title: Latent real-Docker I/O hazards in test_gc.py manager tests + repo-wide warning policy follow-ups
content:
Follow-up findings from the 2026-09-06 ResourceWarning root-cause session (deliberately NOT acted on — out of scope; fix only covered tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py):

1. tests/lib/sandbox/test_gc.py `TestSandboxManagerCollectGarbage` builds REAL managers WITHOUT swapping the backend and calls `manager.collectGarbage()` with gc.enabled=True (default). Whenever DOCKER_HOST resolves, those tests perform REAL Docker I/O (listManagedContainers; collectOrphanContainers can kill/remove real sandbox-labeled containers past retention). They are warning-free ONLY because the `_resetSingleton` fixture does `await instance._backend.close()` in teardown. Same hazard class as the test_manager.py bug, latent.

2. test_gc.py's `_resetSingleton` closes `instance._backend` but NOT `instance._gc._backend` — currently safe only because those tests never swap `_backend`. If someone adds a backend swap there without rewiring the GC, the leak/hazard returns. The two-capture-points trap (manager.py:282 and 295-300) applies everywhere.

3. Policy suggestion: add `error::ResourceWarning` to pyproject.toml `filterwarnings` to turn this leak class into a hard CI failure (today `always::ResourceWarning` only reports). Repo-wide decision, needs owner buy-in.

If touching test_gc.py's manager tests later, apply the same `_swapBackend`-style pattern (swap BOTH `manager._backend` and `manager._gc._backend`) or disable gc in the test config.

title: _swapBackend fix review verdict: correctness PASS, 2 open items (regression pin + tree scope)
content:
Code-review verdict (2026-09-06, review-only session vs HEAD 48700d77) on the uncommitted `_swapBackend` ResourceWarning fix in tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py — complements memory a66533ba (the fix itself).

VERDICT: fix correctness PASS (7/7 focus points analyzed: 1,2,3,4,7 PASS; 5,6 FAIL on non-code grounds). No Critical findings.

VERIFIED HAZARD CLOSURE (trace facts, useful for future sandbox test reviews):
- `recover()` uses `self._backend` directly; `collectGarbage()` delegates to `self._gc.collectAll()` (manager.py:1777). GarbageCollector's ONLY backend reference is the constructor-stored `self._backend` (gc.py:54) — no lazy attributes, no secondary captures; runtimes and metadata stores retain no backend. Swapping both sites therefore severs every path to the real DockerBackend.
- The discarded real DockerBackend sits with `_client = None` until first use (lazy aiodocker client init) — this is why the old leak only materialized when DOCKER_HOST resolved to a live daemon.
- Swap coverage audited: 11 `SandboxManager.getInstance()` sites ↔ 11 `_swapBackend()` calls; the only remaining direct `_backend =` assignments are the helper's two intentional lines (test_manager.py:178-179). `_gc` is the real manager attribute (created manager.py:295), not a test-set shadow.
- TestInstallRuntimeLibrariesTimeout conversions (~lines 601-674): local `backend` var is the exact object installed via the helper; `await_args_list` semantics unchanged — no assertion weakened (local capture was for pyright narrowing).

TWO IMPORTANT OPEN FINDINGS (action items for the next session on this file):
1. Missing deterministic regression pin: no test directly asserts that after `_swapBackend()`, BOTH `manager._backend` and `manager._gc._backend` are the same mock object. With Docker unavailable, a regression deleting the `_gc._backend` assignment (test_manager.py:179) would stay green — the GC swallows backend connection failures. Add a small identity-assertion test; this is what AGENTS.md's regression-test rule requires for test-code bug fixes.
2. Working tree is NOT test-file-only: `.markdown-mcp.toml`, `.opencode/memory.jsonl`, `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md` are also modified vs 48700d77. No production files touched, and the test diff itself (42+/14−) is clean (no debug leftovers, no assertion changes) — but unrelated changes must be separated/removed before committing the fix.

Verification run in review: `make lint` clean; `./venv/bin/pytest tests/lib/sandbox/test_manager.py -q` → 59 passed; `-W error::ResourceWarning` (no DOCKER_HOST prefix) → 59 passed, zero warnings; `make check-docs` clean.

content:
In review-mode opencode sessions on this repo, the user's bash permission config ALLOWS only: plain `./venv/bin/pytest *`, `make lint` / `make test` / `make check-docs`, git read-only ops (status/diff/log/blame/show/rev-parse/ls-files/grep), ls/grep/rg/head/tail/wc/cat/awk/sed -n/diff/sort/uniq/echo/pwd, and `arc` read ops. content:
Where shared test helpers go in Gromozeka (established 2026-09-06 when moving `swapBackend`):

- `tests/scripts/_lib/` is NOT a shared-test-helper convention — it mirrors the production `scripts/_lib/` package and holds tests FOR `scripts._lib.bootstrap`. Creating a new `tests/lib/sandbox/_lib/` would have invented a convention, not followed one.
- The actual in-repo convention for a helper shared by test modules in the SAME directory: that directory's `conftest.py`, imported explicitly as a plain module. Precedents: `from tests.lib.rate_limiter.conftest import installFakeClock`, `from tests.lib.cache.conftest import fakeClockContext`. Works because `tests/` is a real package (`__init__.py` at every level), so pytest imports conftest as `tests.lib.sandbox.conftest` — no double-import under default importmode=prepend.
- Cross-DIRECTORY helpers use a shared non-fixture module: `tests/lib/aurumentation/test_helpers.py` (`baseGoldenDataProvider`, imported by five golden test dirs). Note `test_helpers.py` matches pytest's `test_*.py` glob and gets collected harmlessly (no tests inside).
- Importing helpers from `test_*.py` modules has no precedent and couples collection — avoid.
- Naming: cross-module helpers are PUBLIC (no leading underscore): `swapBackend`, `installFakeClock`, `createAsyncMock`.
- isort detail: `known_first_party = ["internal", "lib"]`, so `tests.*` imports sort into LOCALFOLDER — the LAST import section, after the `lib.*` block, separated by one blank line.

title: DockerBackend client is lazy; GC swallows connection errors (why sandbox hazards stay latent)
content:
Two lib/sandbox facts that explain why real-Docker test hazards are latent (confirmed 2026-09-06 while converting test_gc.py):

1. `DockerBackend.__init__` only stores config — the aiodocker client is created lazily on the FIRST backend call. So constructing a real `SandboxManager` via `getInstance()` is daemon-free; the first backend METHOD call is the I/O point. Test isolation therefore only needs to swap the backend, not avoid construction.

2. `GarbageCollector.collectOrphanContainers()` (lib/sandbox/gc.py) wraps `listManagedContainers()` in try/except and returns 0 on exception. Consequences:
   - On daemon-less CI, GC tests pass "green" while silently swallowing connection failures — a real-I/O hazard is invisible in CI results.
   - On a live daemon (e.g. Colima at `unix:///Users/vgoshev/.colima/default/docker.sock`), the same tests do REAL list/kill/remove of `sandbox.managed` containers older than `orphanContainerRetentionMinutes` (default 10 min) — they could reap real user containers.
   - To reproduce CI semantics deterministically in mocks: `listManagedContainers = AsyncMock(return_value=[])` (empty result, NOT an exception side_effect). Add `close = AsyncMock()` so best-effort singleton-reset cleanup awaits cleanly.
   - Proof that GC never touches the daemon: after `swapBackend`, assert `backend.listManagedContainers.await_count == 1` (exactly one `collectAll` pass) + kill/remove not awaited; `await_count == 0` would mean the swap missed a reference and the real backend did the I/O.

title: Pre-existing dirty files: .markdown-mcp.toml and .opencode/memory.jsonl are NOT yours
content:
In this workspace, `git status` routinely shows two modified files that agents did NOT touch and must leave alone (flagged by a 2026-09-06 task as "Do NOT touch .markdown-mcp.toml"):

- `.markdown-mcp.toml` — the user's local markdown-MCP tooling config (local additions like `exclude = ["archive/"]`, `writable`, `rescan_interval`). Pre-existing local modification; do not revert, do not include in diffs/reports.
- `.opencode/memory.jsonl` — auto-written by the opencode harness itself.

Before reporting a "final diff", sanity-check `git status` and attribute these; don't mistake them for accidental edits by you, and don't stage or revert them.

title: collectOrphanContainers: exception → EARLY RETURN vs [] → metadata scan (mock-fidelity refinement of beb86749)
content:
Branch-level semantics of `collectOrphanContainers()` in lib/sandbox/gc.py (found 2026-09-06 review of the fix-1 test_gc.py conversion, vs HEAD 2eb1d414):

- An EXCEPTION from `listManagedContainers()` is caught at gc.py ~lines 170-174 and causes an IMMEDIATE EARLY RETURN. An EMPTY LIST result instead CONTINUES execution into the active-run metadata scan (gc.py ~lines 176-180).
- `GcResult` is IDENTICAL either way — the swallowed exception is NOT added to `errors` — so GcResult-level assertions cannot distinguish which branch ran. A regression in swallowed-backend-failure handling could pass unnoticed with an empty-list mock.
- This REFINES memory beb86749 (which advised `listManagedContainers = AsyncMock(return_value=[])` and explicitly "NOT an exception side_effect") and memory f89816df (claiming "[] reproduces exactly the CI semantics"): [] is equivalent at GcResult level but exercises a DIFFERENT branch than CI's daemon-unreachable path (which hit the early return).
- Review recommendation to restore branch fidelity: `backend.listManagedContainers = AsyncMock(side_effect=ConnectionError("Docker daemon unavailable"))`. Keep `await_count == 1` (single collectAll pass through the swapped backend) and kill/remove `assert_not_awaited()` — both hold on the early-return path.
- Related mock-realism fact: `DockerBackend.killContainer` swallows `aiodocker.DockerError` and only logs a warning (lib/sandbox/backends/docker.py ~410-416) — backend kill/remove failures don't propagate either. On the GC empty/exception paths no other backend method is called, so no other mock default return can change which GC branch runs.

title: Disabled-GC short-circuit: assert_not_awaited on the disabled path proves short-circuit, NOT swap wiring
content:
Testing gotcha (found 2026-09-06 review of tests/lib/sandbox/test_gc.py::TestSandboxManagerCollectGarbage disabled test):

When GC is disabled, `SandboxManager.collectGarbage()` SHORT-CIRCUITS before consulting `manager._gc`. Therefore `backend.listManagedContainers.assert_not_awaited()` in a disabled-GC test passes even if `swapBackend()` were omitted or regressed — nothing reaches the GC's (possibly stale real) backend during collectGarbage anyway.

- The disabled-path assertion is a valid GC-disabled-short-circuit proof, but NOT proof of the two-reference backend swap.
- For an explicit wiring proof, assert identity before invoking GC: `assert manager._backend is backend` and `assert manager._gc._backend is backend`.
- Contrast: on the ENABLED path, `listManagedContainers.await_count == 1` IS load-bearing — it fails if the swap missed a capture and the real backend performed the I/O (consistent with memory beb86749's await-count proof, which applies to the enabled path only).

content:
On 2026-09-06 the two Gate-1 findings on the GC-test isolation fix (uncommitted working tree on top of HEAD 2eb1d414; conftest.py swapBackend + converted test_gc.py/test_manager.py) were applied to tests/lib/sandbox/test_gc.py only:

title: ResourceWarnings are hard test failures repo-wide
content: Since 2026-09-06, pyproject.toml [tool.pytest.ini_options] filterwarnings = ["error::ResourceWarning"] (upgraded from the display-only "always::ResourceWarning"). content: Supersedes the census technique in memory 82f2ddfb (2026-09-01): pyproject.toml filterwarnings is now ["error::ResourceWarning"] (since 2026-09-06, see memory de443c11), which makes every ResourceWarning a hard test failure.
