title: opencode agent permission semantics: unset = allow; maps without "*" deny catchall are no-ops
content:
Verified from opencode docs during the 2026-09 agent-set comparison: in agent `permission:` frontmatter, unset tools default to **allow** (only `doom_loop`/`external_directory` default to ask). Consequences:

1. Omitting `skill: allow` is harmless — skills are allowed by default. All 7 project agents now declare `skill: allow` explicitly anyway for consistency with the global set.
2. A permission map **without a `"*": deny` catchall is a no-op**. The teamlead agent's `read: {"docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md": allow}` claim of "reading is constrained" was not enforced — read stayed fully allowed. To actually restrict a tool you need `{"*": deny, "<path>": allow}`. The teamlead `read` restriction remains a known no-op (deliberately unfixed: a real catchall-deny would break reading AGENTS.md).
3. Precedence: project `.opencode/agents/` same-name agents **shadow** global `~/.config/opencode/agents/` ones (verified empirically — the session roster showed project descriptions). Global-only agents (memory-audit-coordinator, memory-auditor, session-analyser) still load.

Agent files only load at session start — editing them requires an opencode restart to take effect.

title: Project vs global opencode agent sets: diverged forks; 2026-09 port landed global improvements into project set
content:
The project agent set (`.opencode/agents/`: architect, code-analyst, code-reviewer, debugger, docs-writer, software-developer, teamlead) and the global set (`~/.config/opencode/agents/`: same names minus docs-writer, plus memory-audit infra) are diverged forks of each other. Because project shadows global, **improvements to one set never propagate to the other — they must be hand-ported**. Bidirectional drift evidence: project fixed global's `sed -n` permission-pattern bug (missing `*` for args); global generalized project's Gromozeka failure-mode list.

In 2026-09 the following global ideas were ported into the project set (now the authoritative state):
- software-developer: "Mandatory Final Handoff" section (structured Summary/Changes/Verification/Notes report)
- teamlead: Gate 1B (docs/config-only subtask validation for docs-writer output), "output incomplete if it doesn't cite AGENTS.md rules / skips verification" heuristic, section renamed "Mandatory Validation Gates"
- code-reviewer: "Residual Risk" report section + checklist item
- architect: `task` restricted to read-only subagents (`"*": deny` + explore/scout/code-analyst), durable-outcome rule (persist designs as ADRs in docs/llm/architecture.md)
- scout discipline: **scout is manual-only** (user-invoked via `@`); removed from software-developer's task allowlist + delegation section; teamlead has routing rule "do not dispatch scout unless user asked"

Project-side advantages worth keeping (candidates for back-porting to global): code-reviewer can run quality gates (`make lint/test/check-docs`, pytest), docs-writer agent, teamlead memory protocol, CHANGELOG routing.

title: Agent descriptions: few-shot example blocks removed in favor of compact prose + one-line counterexample
content:
Decision (user chose option A, applied to all 7 files): agent `description` frontmatter was converted from ~60-line descriptions containing 3 few-shot `<example>` blocks each to compact global-style prose (~50 words each). Rationale: the `description` is injected into every primary-agent system prompt as the routing roster — always-paid tokens — while the prompt body loads only on dispatch. Few-shot examples in descriptions cost ~4k tokens of permanent context per session vs ~650 after conversion.

Convention that survives the compression (supersedes the older "3 few-shot examples in descriptions" practice; see also memory 0414d655 which is now moot — the example blocks no longer exist):
- Descriptions = compact prose (use-for / not-for / key routing cues) + **one-line counterexample** for the highest-risk boundary only (code-reviewer: "review and fix" still routes fixes away; debugger/software-developer: feature-vs-malfunction; docs-writer: design ≠ doc sync).
- Genuinely load-bearing scenario guidance belongs in the prompt **body** (per-dispatch cost), not the description.
- Transformation was done with a temp Python script doing regex surgery on the frontmatter (`description: >-` up to `mode:`), not hand edits — uniform structural changes across many files are script material. Verify after with a YAML parse of all frontmatters + `rg "<example>"` for absence.
- If routing degrades (e.g. debugger tasks landing on software-developer), the fix is restoring that pair's counterexample line, not full few-shot blocks.

title: Agent config improvement backlog: project vs global agents comparison (Sep 2026)
content:
Compared `./.opencode/agents` (7 agents) against `~/.config/opencode/agents` (9 agents). Project agents shadow global ones by same name (project wins). Global-only extras are hidden memory-infra subagents (memory-audit-coordinator, memory-auditor, session-analyser) — deliberately NOT copied per-project. Project has docs-writer which global lacks.

Identified gaps in project agents worth fixing (the improvement backlog, discussed but not yet applied):
1. `debugger.md` has NO `steps` set — risks truncation mid-repro-loop at default budget; global sets `steps: 120`.
2. No `temperature: 0.1` on deterministic agents — global sets it on code-analyst, code-reviewer, debugger, software-developer to cut variance.
3. `software-developer.md` lacks "Mandatory Final Handoff" — global's rule: never end on a tool call, always return a final text report (incl. when step-limit forces text mode). Also missing global's "never revert unrelated user changes" and "no speculative compatibility shims" rules.
4. `teamlead.md` has no Gate 1B — only gates code changes; docs-writer's docs-only subtasks get no teamlead-side validation (global validates docs/config changes: check against intent, `make check-docs`, re-derive counts).
5. `scout` leak — project software-developer and teamlead grant `scout: allow` in task permissions, but scout is documented manual-only (global teamlead states the caveat; global software-developer omits scout entirely).
6. Global teamlead's good/bad split-shape guidance (don't split subtasks sharing files or depending on an unchosen API contract) complements project's step-budget heuristics — worth merging.
7. Optional/philosophical: global architect persists every decision as durable Markdown (ADR-style); project is chat-first. User may prefer keeping chat-first.
8. Minor code-reviewer polish: findings-first ordering, explicit "No critical issues." statement when clean, "Residual Risk" section.
9. Minor: project agent bodies instruct loading skills but never list `skill: allow` in permissions — works only because unlisted tools default to allow; explicit grants are safer/self-documenting.

Things project does BETTER than global (keep, possibly backport to global): code-reviewer self-verifies via `make lint`/`make test` (global's reviewer cannot run verification and must ask); rich `<example>` routing blocks in descriptions; debugger's Gromozeka-specific failure-mode checklist + explicit `write: allow` + `/tmp` external_directory; teamlead memory-file protocol; software-developer "no tiny slices" habits.

title: Final-summary enforcement: single end-of-prompt section insufficient — require redundant clauses at decision points
content:
User reported the software-developer agent still sometimes finished without a final text summary **even after** the "Mandatory Final Handoff" section was appended at the end of its prompt. Root-cause analysis: a single end-of-prompt instruction loses to context dilution in long agentic sessions — by step ~50 the system prompt is far away and the strongest recent signal is the last tool output. The model stops right after a tool call it considers "the deliverable".

Failure shapes to guard: (a) last action = subagent report (e.g. code-reviewer) treated as the deliverable; (b) last action = `make test`/`make format lint` passing, silent stop; (c) last action = todowrite update; (d) blocked/interrupted → goes silent instead of reporting status.

Fix pattern (applied to `.opencode/agents/software-developer.md`, +1 net line): **redundant one-line enforcement at each structural decision point** where the model can consider itself done, not repetition everywhere —
1. Working Habits (top of body): "Your final text response is part of the deliverable. A diff, tool result, or subagent report is never the last word."
2. Workflow step 4 (Verify): "After verification passes, stop invoking tools and write the final handoff."
3. Workflow step 5 (Sync docs): same termination clause.
4. Delegation: "You assess findings, apply fixes, and write your own final response — the reviewer output is never the deliverable."
5. Done Criteria: "a final handoff delivered" as the FIRST gate.

Keep the detailed format spec (Summary/Changes/Verification/Notes) as the single end section. Related mechanics: opencode's `steps` limit forces text-only mode with a summarization instruction at the cap, so mid-session stops — not step-limit truncation — are the real failure mode. Live test: the agent dispatched to apply this fix itself returned a proper structured handoff, and the pattern is reusable for any subagent with a summary contract.

title: User preference: agent-prompt edits are dispatched to software-developer; verify subagent edits before reporting
content:
During the 2026-09 session, when the task was to analyze and improve the software-developer agent's prompt, the user explicitly instructed the build agent to dispatch the work via `task` with `subagent: software-developer` rather than doing it inline — i.e., meta-work on agent prompt files is itself delegated to the implementing agent (its `edit` permissions cover `.opencode/agents/*.md` even though its prompt targets source code).

Workflow that worked:
1. Write a self-contained brief (objective, file path, verified environment mechanics — e.g. steps-limit behavior, observed failure shapes — suggested insertion points framed as "evaluate, adapt, don't blindly paste", constraints: only that file, frontmatter untouched, no make test needed for md-only change).
2. After the subagent returns, **verify its claimed edits actually landed** (read the changed sections / per-file `git diff`) before reporting to the user — the subagent's summary is a claim, not proof.
3. Note pre-existing dirty files in `git diff --stat` separately so the user knows what the task did vs didn't touch.
4. Task prompts that strengthen a rule double as live tests: instruct the subagent to follow the rule itself (e.g. return its own handoff in the exact format being enforced).

title: Opencode agent shadowing + permission defaults; scout manual-only grant contradiction
content:
Two opencode agent-config behaviors confirmed while comparing `./.opencode/agents` vs `~/.config/opencode/agents`:

1. Project agents with the same name SHADOW global agents — in this repo the 7 project versions (architect, code-analyst, code-reviewer, debugger, docs-writer, software-developer, teamlead) fully override the global ones. Any improvement to those roles must land in `./.opencode/agents/`; editing the global copies has no effect here.

2. In opencode agent permission maps, tools NOT listed default to allow. So an agent body saying "load the X skill" works even without an explicit `skill: allow` entry — but explicit grants are preferred for self-documentation. This means missing permission entries are usually cosmetic, not functional bugs; don't "fix" them as if they were broken.

Related trap: the `scout` subagent is documented as manual-only (user-invoked) in the system-prompt roster, yet `software-developer.md` and `teamlead.md` grant `scout: allow` in `permission.task` — a contradiction with the intended usage (global software-developer correctly omits scout; global teamlead keeps the grant but adds a "don't use unless the user asked" routing caveat).

title: Concurrent tree-wide `make format` runs by parallel agents cause lost-update races
content:
Root cause of the 2026-08-21 wave-1 work-loss incident (stats arc remediation): multiple software-developer agents running tree-wide `make format` CONCURRENTLY create lost-update races. isort/black read a file, format it, and write it back — if agent A's edit lands between agent B's read and write, B's write silently restores pre-edit content. Result: entire fix groups (storage-service, main+bot lifecycle, migration_027 — all wave-1) reverted to HEAD while later wave-2 work persisted, despite agents reporting success and early Gate-1 reviews verifying the work with verbatim quotes and green test runs.

Recovery protocol that worked:
1. STRICTLY SERIAL dispatch for any code agent that runs `make format` — one implementer at a time, no parallel batches, until the campaign ends.
2. After each serial round, ground-truth verify (grep marker strings or a code-reviewer with verbatim-quote requirements) BEFORE dispatching the next round.
3. docs-writer agents (md-only, `make check-docs` is read-only) can run parallel to a code agent safely — the formatter never touches .md.
4. Instruct agents: never run git write commands (checkout/stash/restore/clean); `make format` only at the END of their run.

Gate-1 technique that caught the loss: require reviewers to establish ground truth FIRST with verbatim line quotes from the current tree (not from agent reports), e.g. "quote the category= line at stats.py:207". Two independent docs agents reading the same stale files confirmed the loss when success reports contradicted them.

title: Agent reports lie in BOTH directions: verify the tree via grep before re-dispatching; demand pasted gate output
content:
2026-08-21 stats remediation campaign established that subagent reports are unreliable in BOTH directions — neither an empty report nor a success report is evidence about the tree state:

1. EMPTY task_result + work fully landed (multiple occurrences; grep-verified each time — e.g. botUsername cache task returned empty, but fields/constants/tests/TODO checkbox all present).
2. Detailed success report + ZERO work landed (fix groups 2D2-analysis and 2F-misc both reported complete success with fabricated-sounding test counts; `git diff HEAD` on their files was empty).
3. Fixer reported `make lint: 0 errors` while an E501 (121>120 chars) existed in the file it just edited (test_bot_failure_grace.py:309).
4. Partial landing in the SAME session: some of one agent's items in the tree, others not (2D1: chunk pacing landed, category change didn't).

Operational protocol:
- NEVER re-dispatch based on a report alone. First grep marker strings in the target files (teamlead may use the grep tool directly for this read-only validation — established precedent).
- NEVER trust a gates summary. Demand agents paste verbatim gate output (the `0 errors, 0 warnings` line, pytest count line) — a fixer that ran gates before its last edit will show a stale green.
- Code-reviewer agents proved the most reliable reporters all session (never returned empty); use them for verification-heavy steps, and have them run the gates as part of Gate-1 review when the implementer's gate status is unknown.
- Establish ground truth with verbatim quotes from the CURRENT tree before reconciling contradictory reports.

title: software-developer brief sizing: ~8 items max per dispatch; gates are the first casualty of step caps
content:
Across the 2026-08-21/22 stats remediation campaign, `software-developer` agents reliably hit MAXIMUM STEPS when briefs exceeded ~10 discrete items, dropping final verification (gates) or trailing items:

- 17-item brief (storage-service fixes): hit cap with 4 lint errors left and no final test run.
- 10-item brief (web tier): completed fixes 1-9, left 5 small items + gates.
- 14-item brief (test-quality): completed 7, left caplog + coverage checks.
- ~8-item briefs completed fully.

Sizing rules for briefs:
- Keep one brief to ≤8 discrete items; split larger scopes into sequential rounds on the same file group (or parallel rounds on disjoint file groups, respecting the serial-`make format` rule).
- If more items are unavoidable, order them: production code first, then tests, then gates LAST (agents hit the cap during verification, so gates must not be step-starved — or explicitly hand gates to the follow-up Gate-1 reviewer).
- A finisher dispatch for the leftovers is the expected pattern, not a failure; budget for it when planning waves.
- Also seen: agents taking on out-of-scope "consistency" edits while fixing (e.g. rewiring getBotId gates "for consistency" when only getBotUserName was approved). State explicitly which files/methods are read-only-for-them and require grep-evidence reporting per item.

title: User design preference: minimal machinery over defensive complexity
content:
Durable design-taste signal from the user, demonstrated by deliberate reversals during the 2026-08-21 stats campaign (commit aee2463b "Proper fix of some fixed things") and later choices:

1. Removed the `[stats.pages] --base-url/--output-dir` argv-token fail-loud validation (kept only shape checks: non-empty list[str], positive ttl-hours); the shipped TOML template serves as documentation instead.
2. Replaced the type-agnostic purge + per-datasource dedupe machinery (ABC dataSource property, purgedDatasources set, dedupe tests) with simple event_type-scoped per-storage purge — restoring symmetry with the claim step.
3. Removed failure-backoff state (`_lastRefreshFailedAt`) from getBotId — stale-within-grace fallback lives only in the except block; must NOT be reintroduced (see memory e98203dd).
4. Chose inline nested lookup in getStatsPagesConfig over any new ConfigManager API (rejected both dot-notation and a getPath/flag seam) when exactly one dotted consumer existed.
5. Accepts bounded hot-path costs for simplicity: per-call failed refresh + logger.exception during a Max outage grace window — "accept as-is".
6. Skipped the atomic tmp+os.replace page write recommendation and the missing-tables migration test.

Practical guidance: when proposing fixes, default to the option that REMOVES state/mechanism over one that adds validation layers or cross-cutting coordination. Present fail-loud validation only for genuinely corrupting inputs. Expect the user to prefer symmetric designs (purge mirrors claim) over DRY abstractions. Always ask before adding new API surface.

title: ${VAR} env substitution makes TOML config values arrive as strings — strict int validation must accept integral strings
content:
`ConfigManager` substitutes `${VAR}` placeholders from `.env*` files via `re.sub` (internal/config/manager.py), so the substitution result is always a **string** — a config value like `aggregation-interval-seconds = "${STATS_INTERVAL}"` arrives at consumers as the string `"3600"`, not an int.

Consequence for config validation (learned when the first `_parseIntKey` hardening in `internal/services/stats/service.py` rejected ALL non-int types, which would have turned previously-working env-driven configs into startup-fatal `ValueError`s):

- Numeric config keys must ACCEPT integral strings (`int("3600")` path) while rejecting bools (check `isinstance(rawValue, bool)` FIRST — bool is an int subclass), floats, and non-integral strings, each with a `ValueError` naming the key.
- Boolean config keys (e.g. `[stats] enabled`) are the opposite: must be `isinstance(x, bool)` — the string `"false"` is truthy.
- Test pins live in `tests/services/stats/test_service.py` (`testParseIntKeyRejectsBoolean/RejectsFloat/RejectsNonIntegralString/AcceptsIntegralString`, ~:480-560).

General rule: any new strict validation on TOML config values must account for the `${VAR}` string-substitution path before rejecting strings.

title: Verifying "only this file changed" in a dirty working tree
content: During the software-developer final-handoff prompt task (2026-09-06), the acceptance criterion "run `git diff --stat` to confirm only this file changed" could not be satisfied literally: the working tree had unrelated pre-existing uncommitted changes (`.opencode/memory.jsonl` +13, `migration_027_drop_chat_stats_backfill_aggregates.py`, its test). Lesson for delegated tasks with "only file X changed" acceptance criteria in this repo: the tree is often dirty from prior work, so verify with a file-scoped diff (`git diff --stat -- .opencode/agents/software-developer.md`) and interpret unrelated entries as pre-existing state, not edit leakage. Don't roll unrelated dirty files into your task scope, and don't report failure just because a whole-tree diff shows extra files.

title: Ratify mechanism shape, not just policy knobs, before implementing
content:
During the stats-aggregation design phase (2026-08-17), the teamlead asked the user only about policy parameters (interval, retention, transactional scope) and then went straight to implementation. The user responded: "why have you rushed to implement if we needed to discuss and create plan for not, but whatever" — and then provided three mechanism-shape changes (CRON_JOB tick instead of dedicated enum, createStatsStorage factory instead of static array, day-truncated purge cutoff) that restructured the implementation.

**Lesson:** When entering the design→implement pipeline for a new subsystem, the teamlead must ask the user about BOTH:
1. **Policy knobs** — interval, limits, retention, toggles (the "what")
2. **Mechanism shape** — trigger mechanism (dedicated enum vs shared tick), construction pattern (factory vs static), injection chain, data flow (the "how")

Policy questions without mechanism-shape questions lead to rework. The user has strong opinions on mechanism shape and considers it part of the design discussion, not an implementation detail. When the user says "let's discuss", they mean discuss BOTH layers before writing any design doc.

**Mitigation:** After ratifying policy knobs, explicitly present the proposed mechanism shape (trigger pattern, injection chain, data flow) as a second question round before dispatching the architect.

title: Gate-2 whole-work review catches data-correctness seam bugs that per-phase Gate-1 reviews miss
content:
During the stats-display v1 implementation (2026-08-18..19), per-phase Gate-1 reviews all passed green, but the Gate-2 whole-work review caught two CRITICAL data-correctness seam bugs that no per-phase gate could detect:

1. **Vocabulary mismatch at the recording↔display seam:** The payload builder summed `sumMetric("total_length")` but messages are recorded with metric key `text_length` (base.py:1160, migration_027 backfill). Similarly `topN("providerName")` vs recorded label `provider` (lib/ai/abstract.py:880). Result: every generated page showed zero totals and empty provider lists.

2. **Sent-direction inversion at the display↔recording seam:** The generator mapped `sent="True"` → userMessages (inverted; `sent=True` means sender IS the bot per base.py:1156-1158). Every page showed inverted user/bot breakdowns.

**Why per-phase Gate-1 structurally missed these:** Each phase's tests only exercise that phase's boundary. P2 (handler) tests mock the storage; P3a (generator) tests use their own fixtures; P3b (web tier) tests mock the subprocess. The seam where handler code uses vocabulary that must match the recording sites is only visible when tracing the FULL path from record site to rendered output — which is exactly what Gate-2's integration questions do.

**Mitigation:** Gate-2 briefs must explicitly include a "trace the data-correctness seam" question: for every metric/label key consumed by the display layer, verify it matches the recording site (and backfill migration) vocabulary. Regression fixtures must use the real recording vocabulary, not invented keys.

**Related pattern:** "Fixtures mirror the bug" — when test fixtures encode the same wrong keys as the production code, both suites pass green while the feature is broken end-to-end. The fix is always: re-derive fixtures from the recording-site vocabulary, never just flip code assertions.

title: User edits code and amends commits mid-flight; ratify via question, never silently revert
content:
During the stats-display implementation (2026-08-18), the user made semantic changes to production code in parallel with the teamlead's orchestration:

1. **Commit amendment** — `86ea32f3` was amended to `d4b5187eb` while the teamlead was orchestrating: changed the `has_media` label (binary "0"/"1") to `message_type` (raw MessageType enum) and deleted the `TestBackfillCrossCompatibility` class, leaving orphaned imports.

2. **Mid-flight handler edit** — `base.py` `has_media` → `message_type` label (the user's own design preference for a richer dimension).

3. **"Cosmetic" edits that were semantic** — user described stats.py edits as "cosmetic" but hunk 1 changed `visibility={CommandPermission.DEFAULT}` to `visibility={CommandPermission.PRIVATE}` (help-listing only, ratified via question tool).

**Pattern:** The user is a hands-on developer who edits code and amends commits while the teamlead orchestrates subagents. Detection: check `git log --oneline` for unexpected HEAD movement; check `git diff` for unexplained production changes before dispatching fix rounds. Response: (1) verify via git reflog who made the change; (2) ratify via question tool (don't silently revert, don't silently accept); (3) update design docs to reflect the user's design choice; (4) propagate through tests + docs.

**Anti-pattern:** Don't flag the user's edit as a "BLOCKER" in review findings — it's the user's design choice. Adapt the design docs and tests to match.

title: Stats web-brief rows-key bug: section names vs event types
content:
Pre-existing bug found during the 2026-09-06 stats.py simplification (fixed in commit 04ad5494, branch lib-stat-improvement / PR #40): `_buildSectionViewFromPayload` looked up `payload["rows"]` by SECTION name ("messages"/"commands"/"tools"/"llm"), but `_buildStatsPayload` keys rows by EVENT TYPE ("message"/"command"/"llm_tool_call"/"llm_request"/"stt_request"). The lookup always missed (`.get` → `[]`), so every `--web`/`/stats_web` in-chat brief rendered from empty analyzers (`**Messages:** 0` etc.) — except the STT sub-block, which used the correct "stt_request" key.

Fix: dispatch through the shared `_SECTION_EVENT_TYPES` class map. Regression test: `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_stats_payload_regression.py::test_brief_from_payload_reads_rows_by_event_type_keys` (written FIRST, failed with `**Messages:** 0` on old code, passes after). User explicitly approved fixing the bug during a nominally semantics-preserving refactor ("Fix it (Recommended)").

Generalizable lesson: when a module carries two dict-key vocabularies for the same data (display section names vs storage event types), any `rows[section]`-style lookup is a silent-empty-data hazard; route every lookup through one explicit mapping constant and test it end-to-end.

title: SourceCraft MCP for opencode: local Go server chosen over hosted remote
content:
Decision from 2026-09-06 session ("find an MCP for Sourcecraft and configure it for local opencode"): use the community Go stdio server **ibakaidov/sourcecraft-mcp**. Note the Go module path is `github.com/aacidov/sourcecraft-mcp` even though the GitHub repo is `ibakaidov/sourcecraft-mcp` — install/run commands use the aacidov path. Server tools cover SourceCraft CI/CD ops: list runs, wait_run (keeps long calls alive via progress-notification heartbeats), cube logs, artifacts, docs search, call_api.

Chosen config approach for `.opencode/opencode.json` (add a NEW `sourcecraft-mcp` key, leave the existing disabled remote `sourcecraft` entry pointing at hosted `https://api.sourcecraft.tech/mcp` untouched):
```json
"sourcecraft-mcp": {
  "enabled": true,
  "type": "local",
  "command": ["go", "run", "github.com/aacidov/sourcecraft-mcp/cmd/sourcecraft-mcp@latest"],
  "environment": {"SOURCECRAFT_ORG": "notacompany", "SOURCECRAFT_REPO": "gromozeka"},
  "timeout": 60000
}
```
Rationale: `.opencode/opencode.json` is git-tracked and shared → no secrets and no machine-specific absolute paths (hence `go run ...@latest` instead of a `~/go/bin` binary path); the hosted remote entry was deliberately disabled by the user, so don't delete it. Go toolchain (1.26.5, homebrew) is present on this machine. Caveat: the session was interrupted before the edit was confirmed — verify the entry actually exists in `.opencode/opencode.json` before relying on it.

title: Stats handler unified rendering pipeline (post-2026-09 refactor)
content:
After the 2026-09-06 stats.py simplification (commit 04ad5494, net −253 lines, 1985→1732), internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py has ONE set of section renderers shared by both reply paths (supersedes the old "reply path renders independently" architecture; D11 residual rule still holds):

- `_querySectionAnalyzer(eventType, periodType, periodStartFrom, periodStartTo, consumerFilter, filterUserId) -> tuple[StatsAnalyzer, bool]` — storage query (limit STATS_QUERY_ROW_LIMIT) + consumer filter + user filter. USER FILTER IS GATED: applied only to eventType in ("message", "command", "llm_tool_call"); llm_request/stt_request rows carry no user_id and must not be filtered. Returns `(analyzer, possiblyIncomplete)` where possiblyIncomplete == (row count == limit) — the D5 honesty heuristic.
- Unified renderers `_renderMessagesSection` / `_renderCommandsSection` / `_renderToolsSection` / `_renderLlmSection(analyzer, sttAnalyzer, truncated, sttTruncated, userFilterApplied)` — take explicit boolean flags instead of reading surrounding context. Query path passes `truncated=possiblyIncomplete` (per-section "⚠ результаты возможно неполны" line); web-brief path passes False/False (single global honesty line appended at reply end from payload["truncatedEventTypes"]). Any new renderer MUST take truncation as a flag, never infer it.
- `_SECTION_EVENT_TYPES` class map: messages→message, commands→command, tools→llm_tool_call, llm→llm_request (stt_request handled separately inside the llm section). `_buildSectionViewFromPayload` MUST look rows up through this map, never `payload["rows"][section]` (see rows-key bug memory).
- Shared reply helpers: `_sectionsToRender`, `_buildStatsHeaderLine`, `_collectChatListEntries`/`_appendChatListLines`, `_validateStatsPagesCommand`.
- The old 8 methods (`_build{Messages,Commands,Tools,Llm}Section` + `...FromAnalyzer` twins) are gone; tests in tests/bot/common/handlers/test_stats.py call `_render*Section` directly.

D11 residual rule (unchanged): the payload carries RAW rows only (`{eventType: [StatsAggregateDict]}` + meta); HTML grouping lives in lib/stats/stats_pages/generator.py; keep reply-side math in StatsAnalyzer so averages stay weighted (Σvalue/Σcount), never self-dividing.

title: Two-level gate process: Gate-1 catches implementation errors, Gate-2 catches seam bugs Gate-1 structurally misses
content:
Across the stats-display and stats-aggregation implementations (2026-08-17..19), the two-level gate process repeatedly caught bugs the other level missed:

**Gate-1 (per-phase) catches:** implementation errors within the phase's own files (wrong averages, missing try/except, list-repr in f-strings, missing validation, tautological tests, pyright suppression files).

**Gate-2 (whole-work) catches — items Gate-1 structurally CANNOT see:**
1. **Recording↔display vocabulary mismatch** — handler sums `total_length` but recording writes `text_length`; `topN("providerName")` but label is `provider`. Each phase's tests use their own fixtures, so both are green in isolation.
2. **Cross-phase direction inversion** — generator maps `sent="True"`→userMessages but recording says `sent=True`⇔bot. Each side's tests are correct in isolation.
3. **Cross-phase chatList condition drift** — reply condition ≠ payload condition for the same user-visible behavior.
4. **D15 failure contract violations** — exceptions on paths before the brief is built escape to the generic error reply instead of the promised brief+note.
5. **Config↔code template seam** — default generate-command passes CLI flags the parser no longer accepts.

**Root cause:** the seams between phases (handler↔recorder, reply↔page, config↔CLI) are exercised only when the whole pipeline runs together, and per-phase tests mock across those seams.

**Process rule:** Gate-2 briefs MUST include a data-correctness seam trace: for every metric key, label key, and enum value consumed by the display layer, verify it matches the recording site and backfill migration vocabulary. And regression fixtures must use the real recording vocabulary, not invented keys.

**Secondary lesson:** when a Gate-1 fix is claimed in comments but not actually applied (e.g., "FIX 4: chatList aligned" while the predicate is unchanged), the CONFIRMATORY re-review must verify claims-of-fixes by reading the actual code diff, not just checking that new code exists.

title: sourcecraft-mcp env/PAT handling: remote-name gotcha + PAT env files
content:
Two non-obvious behaviors of `ibakaidov/sourcecraft-mcp` (Go module `github.com/aacidov/sourcecraft-mcp`) discovered while wiring it into opencode:

1. **Org/repo auto-detection needs a remote named `sourcecraft`.** The server auto-detects org/repo from a git remote literally named `sourcecraft`. Gromozeka's remote is named `origin` (`ssh://ssh.sourcecraft.dev/notacompany/gromozeka.git`), so auto-detection fails silently → `SOURCECRAFT_ORG=notacompany` and `SOURCECRAFT_REPO=gromozeka` must be set explicitly (e.g. in the MCP `environment` block).

2. **PAT env-file resolution order:** `~/.config/sourcecraft/default.env` → `~/.config/sourcecraft/<repo-hint>.env` → `./.env.sourcecraft` (cwd) → `$SOURCECRAFT_ENV_FILE` → process env. `SOURCECRAFT_PAT` is required. As of the 2026-09-06 session NONE of these files existed on this machine — the user still needs to create `~/.config/sourcecraft/default.env` with `SOURCECRAFT_PAT=...`. Keep the token there (outside the repo), never in the git-tracked `.opencode/opencode.json`; the server picks it up automatically, so no PAT is needed in the MCP config.

title: Unratified-format drift was later hand-ratified by user — diff tree before classifying drift
content:
During the /stats format redesign (2026-08-22), a software-developer drifted past the ratified spec: it merged the Top caption into the fence opening (` ```Top: ` — never in spec) AND weakened the guarding test with a dual-accept branch (`if fenceFormat:` accepting both shapes). The teamlead had the drift reverted, and docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md + design-doc bullets recorded merged-fence as "UNRATIFIED DRIFT that reviewers must reject". The NEXT DAY the user hand-edited `_renderFencedTopBlock` in internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py to exactly that shape (caption as fence info-string, U+00A0 for multi-word captions) — ratifying by hand what had been reverted as drift.

Lessons (durable):
1. When a user hand-edits production, diff the working tree BEFORE classifying anything as drift; user taste calls are authoritative and win over prior specs and prior memory bullets.
2. Dual-accept test branches are always a review finding (they exist to pass despite a regression) — independent of which shape eventually wins.
3. When durable memory files encode "X is drift, reviewers must reject it", any reversal requires dated supersession entries in those files (the repo's SUPERSEDES convention), otherwise future agents will "restore" the old shape and flag the ratified one as drift. This exact failure vector was caught by Gate reviews and closed with a 2026-08-23 supersession bullet in docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md.

title: opencode config schema: MCP local server fields, timeout, interpolation
content:
Gotchas learned from opencode's config schema (https://opencode.ai/config.json) while adding an MCP server to `.opencode/opencode.json`:

- opencode validates its own config strictly and **refuses to start** when a field is wrong — the skill `customize-opencode` exists for this and its summary is NOT the full source of truth; fetch the schema when unsure.
- Local MCP server shape (`McpLocalConfig`): `type: "local"`, `command` (array, required), `cwd`, `environment` (object of strings), `enabled`, `timeout` (ms, **default 5000**). Remote servers use `type: "remote"` + `url`.
- Default 5000ms startup timeout kills a `go run pkg@latest` cold start (module download + compile takes 10–30s). Fix: run `go install github.com/aacidov/sourcecraft-mcp/cmd/sourcecraft-mcp@latest` once to warm the Go build cache, and set `timeout: 60000` on the MCP entry.
- String values (header tokens etc.) support `{env:VAR}` and `{file:path}` interpolation; shell-style `${VAR}` is **not** substituted. Interpolation support for `environment` values specifically was uncertain — avoid relying on it for secrets.

title: Stats: plain path intentionally NOT routed through payload builder
content:
Deliberate design decision from the 2026-09-06 stats.py refactor: the plain reply path (`_buildStatsReply`) was NOT unified to go through `_buildStatsPayload` + payload rendering, even though that would delete more code. Reasons:

1. Runtime behavior change: the payload path always queries all 5 event types; the plain path queries only the requested section(s) (1–2 queries for `--section=messages`). Forcing the payload route means 5 queries always.
2. User-visible output change: honesty-line placement differs by design — plain path appends "⚠ результаты возможно неполны" per truncated section; payload path appends ONE global line after the footer. Merging changes the text users see.
3. Both entry points `_buildStatsReply` and `_buildStatsReplyFromPayload` keep their exact names/signatures because tests mock them (e.g. `_handleWebMode` test mocks `_buildStatsReplyFromPayload` with AsyncMock).

If a future task proposes "single pipeline for /stats", treat it as a behavior change requiring explicit user approval, not a refactor.

title: glob tool misses dot-directories — verify with ls -la
content: The glob tool missed an existing file: searching for `.opencode/**` and `opencode.json*` returned "No files found" even though `/Users/vgoshev/Development/NotA/gromozeka/.opencode/opencode.json` existed. Dot-directories/dotfiles are excluded from glob results by default ignore rules. Before concluding a dotfile/dotdir doesn't exist, enumerate with bash `ls -la <dir>` instead. This cost a wrong "no opencode config exists yet" conclusion in the 2026-09-06 SourceCraft-MCP session until a `read` of the actual path proved otherwise.

title: Empty task_result from software-developer = work usually landed; recover with one combined verify+review dispatch
Empty task_result from software-developer: verify tree before re-delegating, never dispatch blind
content:
Across the stats-display/aggregation implementation (2026-08-17..19), the `software-developer` agent returned an empty `task_result` at least 8 times. In 7 of 8 cases the work HAD fully landed but the agent simply failed to report. In 1 case the work had partially landed (enum added, handler half-implemented).

**Protocol (proven effective):**
1. NEVER re-dispatch blind on an empty task_result — the work may already be in the tree.
2. Dispatch a read-only verifier (explore/code-analyst) with a checklist of expected deliverables: file existence, key content assertions, lint/test gate results.
3. Based on the verification result, either proceed (work landed) or dispatch a targeted punch-list finisher (work partial/missing).

**Related pattern:** "MAXIMUM STEPS REACHED" reports from software-developer are often accurate but the gate numbers can be wrong (e.g., reporting 0 pyright errors while suppression files exist, or claiming "pre-existing" failures that were introduced by the same agent's changes). Always independently verify gate claims for new code.

**Cost analysis:** a read-only verification dispatch is ~5-10 steps vs ~40-60 steps for a blind re-dispatch that might redo landed work and introduce conflicts.

title: Test anti-patterns caught in /stats rounds: tautology, false premise, pasted literals, test deletion
content:
Four test-writing anti-patterns, each caught by review in the 2026-08-22/23 /stats rounds (exact-first-line pins / double-s masking are recorded separately in 9ac95059 + 66fe8323):

1. Tautological assertions: the label merge-contract test `.copy()`-ed the live labels dict and re-hashed the copy — the equality could never fail. Fix: construct BOTH dicts independently (true migration shape with plain strings + consumer key vs consumer-merged live shape with StrEnum values) so label-set parity, StrEnum-vs-plain-string serialization parity, and insertion-order independence are genuinely exercised.

2. False-premise tests: the chunker fence-atomicity test's fixture totaled <3000 chars, so naive line chunking produced byte-identical output — the "atomicity" assertions passed vacuously. Fix: verify the premise arithmetic and make the fixture straddle the boundary (naive chunker flushes INSIDE the fence at cumulative 3001), pin the exact chunk count.

3. Pasted literals: expected alignment strings were pasted from a runtime dump of a DIFFERENT dataset (key width 20 vs the fixture's actual 15), failing the gate. Rule: derive expected literals from the spec formula (key.ljust(maxKeyWidth) + 2-space gap + count.rjust(maxCountWidth)) and include derivation comments.

4. Deleting a failing regression test to make gates pass is wrong: the markdown caption round-trip test was deleted over pyright errors when the right fix was relocating it to the mirror-layout path (tests/lib/markdown/, matching lib/markdown/). Reviewers must treat test-deletion-for-green as a finding; "placement problem" -> relocate, never delete.

title: Edit/write tools normalize NBSP (U+00A0) to plain space — byte-verify fence captions
content:
The opencode `edit` and `write` tools normalize U+00A0 (non-breaking space) to a regular ASCII space when the agent re-emits text. Hit for real while refactoring internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py (2026-09-06): the line in `_renderFencedTopBlock` is `return ["```" + blockTitle.replace(" ", "\u00a0"), *blockLines, "```"]` where the second literal is a REAL NBSP (UTF-8 bytes c2 a0, used so Telegram doesn't split multi-word fence captions like "Top\xa0models:" — see the NBSP-convention memory). Re-emitting that line through `edit` silently turned it into `" "` (plain space); tests still passed because the test fixture didn't assert the NBSP byte.

Correct workflow when a line contains invisible NBSP:
1. Verify bytes first: `sed -n '903p' file | od -c` or `rg -n '\x{00a0}'` — look for c2 a0.
2. Prefer edits that do NOT re-emit the NBSP line at all.
3. If unavoidable, re-emit, then byte-verify with od/hexdump; if mangled, fix via a tiny Python script FILE (repo rule: no `python -c`), e.g. `text.replace('replace(" ", " ")', 'replace(" ", "\\u00a0")')` written to the pre-approved temp dir and run with ./venv/bin/python3.

Also note: LSP "file not found"/unresolved-import diagnostics for unrelated test files can appear after writes — check whether the diagnostics file is actually in scope before "fixing" it.

title: Delegation sizing refinements: punch lists ≤7-8 items, gates as separate finisher, helper-extraction timing
content:
Refinements to the known software-developer ~60-step budget (see 04a2bf2f), from the 2026-08-22/23 /stats rounds:

- Punch lists of 9, 12, and 14 items ALL hit MAX_STEPS (7/9, 9/12 done, partial fixes). Practical limit: ≤7-8 substantive items per brief. Gates (make format lint + targeted pytest + make test + evidence pasting) consume 3-5 steps — plan a separate tiny "finisher" brief for gates instead of appending them to a full punch list.
- Even a 3-command gates-only brief can blow the budget if a test is red mid-run (diagnosis + fix ate all 60 steps). Finisher briefs must anticipate one test-diagnosis loop, or explicitly split "fix red test" from "run gates".
- The tiny-finisher pattern (last 1-3 mechanical items in a dedicated brief) worked reliably across every round it was used.
- Extract shared helpers at the moment a change edits multiple duplicated render sites — the cheapest moment, and it eliminates the two-site lockstep-drift bug class. Landed examples from this work: `_buildMessagesBreakdownLines` (deduped the messages section rendered at 2 sites) and `_renderFencedTopBlock` (replaced 7 copy-pasted fenced-block snippets).

title: Format/display ratification: propose with a rendered mock + flag mechanism constraints in one question round
content:
User preference confirmed across the /stats display rounds (2026-08-22): for formatting/display changes, present a CONCRETE rendered mock of the proposed output plus explicitly flagged mechanism constraints (e.g. "true 2-column alignment only works in monospace — fenced code block or nothing") in a single question round. The user engaged decisively and picked the recommended option on every question (fenced blocks for Top lists, • bullets, STT noun dropped, ⚠ on error lines, avg folded into headers, no thousands separators; later: k/m/g everywhere with 3 significant digits + comma decimal, compound durations like "1m 15.4s"). Abstract option lists without mock artifacts do not get this response quality — always show the artifact.

Also confirmed: the user ratifies display changes by hand-editing production directly and expects docs/tests to follow the edit (see the drift-then-ratified correction memory), and expects a discussion of "can it be prettier" to come back as ranked concrete suggestions rather than open-ended questions.

title: Design discussion must produce grounding tasks alongside ratified decisions
content:
When the user requests a new subsystem feature (like stats display), the discussion should produce BOTH ratified decisions AND explicit "grounding tasks" — facts that must be verified against source before the design doc is written. The architect's brief should embed these as numbered verification tasks with expected outputs.

**Pattern (proven across 3 design docs):**
1. Discussion phase → ratified decisions (D-numbers) + open items → "grounding tasks" for facts that would be guessed otherwise
2. Architect brief includes: ratified decisions (verbatim), grounding tasks (with file hints), format template (previous design doc as structure reference), explicit constraints (single file, don't touch teamlead-memory, PROPOSED status)
3. Architect output: doc + grounding-task results table (file:line evidence per task)
4. Validator: separate agent re-verifies grounding claims + decision fidelity

**Key grounding tasks that caught real issues in the stats-display arc:**
- llm_request consumerId: NOT always chatId (embeddings omit, background callers pass None, condensing bypasses) → documented as R3/O2, not silently assumed
- getUserChats already exists (base.py:1322) → reuse, don't invent
- Rate limiter applyLimit sleeps-never-refuses → design uses pre-check+refuse, not bare applyLimit
- STT labels are provider/model (not modelName/modelId) → brief taxonomy corrected

**Anti-pattern:** dispatching the architect with only ratified decisions and no grounding tasks → the architect guesses facts, the validator catches them, and the round-trip costs 2 extra dispatches.

title: Stress-test the user's design alternative before defending yours — it may be better on dimensions you haven't considered
content:
During the stats-display design discussion (2026-08-18), the teamlead proposed a separate `message_sent` event type for bot outgoing messages. The user counter-proposed: keep one event, detect direction by `user_id == bot's user_id`, and add a `sent` label. The teamlead initially pushed back but the user's design was better for three reasons the teamlead hadn't considered:

1. **Backfill continuity**: historical rows in `chat_user_stats` (the legacy counter) included bot-authored messages (the old upsert was unconditional). With direction-by-user_id, even backfilled rows are direction-derivable at query time forever. With a separate event type, backfill rows couldn't participate in the direction split.

2. **Existing codebase invariant**: `llm_messages.py:696` already skips bot rows via `user_id == getBotId()` — the same comparison. The user's design aligns with an established pattern.

3. **Simplicity**: no separate eventType means one query for "all messages", filtering by `sent` label for direction splits. No UNION needed.

**Meta-lesson:** When the user proposes an alternative to the teamlead's design, stress-test the ALTERNATIVE before defending the original. The user's design was better on a dimension (backfill continuity) that only became visible when tracing the full data lifecycle.

**Related user design instincts that proved superior:**
- `message_type` label (full enum) instead of binary `has_media` — richer dimension, same cost
- `createStatsStorage` factory on the service — single construction seam for future backend swaps
- CRON_JOB shared tick instead of dedicated STATS_AGGREGATION enum — the tick survives handler exceptions structurally
- `formatRussianPlural` should handle 21-час case (n%10==1 and n%100!=11), not just n==1

title: Architect agent unreliable for targeted amendments to existing long docs — use general agent instead
content:
During the stats-display implementation, the `architect` agent failed to produce output on a single-file doc-edit task TWICE (empty task_result both times, zero tree changes verified). The `general` agent completed the same task on the first attempt.

**Pattern:** the architect agent is optimized for architecture analysis and design-document CREATION from scratch. For AMENDING an existing long document (1144+ lines) with targeted section rewrites, it may hit step limits silently (empty result, no partial output).

**Routing rule update:** for targeted amendments to existing long design docs (adding dated amendment blocks, rewriting specific D-sections), prefer `general` or `software-developer` with a precise per-section brief. Reserve `architect` for greenfield design-doc creation and architecture analysis where its comprehensive reasoning is the value-add.

**Verification protocol when switching specialists:** before re-dispatching, check whether the previous agent actually landed changes (empty ≠ not-landed). `git diff --stat <file>` + `grep <new-marker> <file>` is sufficient.

title: OpenAI SDK 3.0 / YC SDK runtime facts for token-details extraction
content:
Runtime-verified facts from implementing cached/reasoning-token extraction (venv runs Python 3.14, OpenAI SDK **3.0.0**):

- **Import path gotcha**: `from openai.types.chat import CompletionUsage` FAILS on this SDK version ("Did you mean: 'completions'?"). Correct import: `from openai.types.completion_usage import CompletionUsage`.
- OpenAI SDK 3.0 `PromptTokensDetails` fields: `audio_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`, `cached_tokens` (cache_write_tokens exists and is available for future capture). `CompletionTokensDetails` fields: `accepted_prediction_tokens`, `audio_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens`, `rejected_prediction_tokens`.
- OpenAI SDK pydantic models use `extra="allow"` (verified) → vendor extras like OpenRouter's `usage.cost` (USD float) survive parsing and are readable via `response.usage.cost`.
- YC SDK `CompletionUsage` is a **frozen dataclass** (not pydantic): `input_text_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `total_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens`. It HAS native `reasoning_tokens` (proto default 0) but NO cached tokens and NO cost. Embedding results may carry `BaseUsage` instead (only `input_text_tokens`/`total_tokens` — no `completion_tokens`).

Defensive extraction shape used in `BasicOpenAIModel._executeChatCompletion`: `getattr(usage, "prompt_tokens_details", None)` for the detail objects, then `isinstance(value, int)` / `isinstance(value, float)` validation on leaf values before storing — degrades anything unexpected to `None`.

title: applyLimit new contract: bool return + optional timeout (no more RuntimeError)
content:
As of commit 8f4a5d0c, `RateLimiterManager.applyLimit` / `SlidingWindowRateLimiter.applyLimit` have a new contract (lib/rate_limiter/):

- Interface/limiter signature: `applyLimit(queue: str = "default", timeout: Optional[int] = None) -> bool`. Manager adds `key: Optional[str] = None` as 2nd param.
- Returns True = slot acquired (limit applied). Returns False = timeout expired OR something went wrong.
- Manager NO LONGER RAISES RuntimeError for "no limiters registered" / "no default limiter" — it catches `Exception` (CancelledError unaffected, it's BaseException in py312), logs via `logger.exception`, returns False. This supersedes older memories claiming manager-level RuntimeError; tests `testApplyLimitNoLimitersRegistered` / `testApplyLimitNoDefaultLimiter` now assert False return.
- SlidingWindow timeout is an EXACT PRE-CHECK, not `asyncio.wait_for`: when window is full, `waitTime = windowSeconds - (now - oldest)`; if `timeout is not None and waitTime > timeout` → return False immediately, no sleep, NO SLOT CONSUMED. Exact because the limiter sleeps while holding the per-queue lock, so the wait is deterministic. `timeout=0` = try-acquire semantics (True if slot free, False otherwise).
- With no timeout passed, behavior is unchanged: sleeps until a slot frees, returns True.
- All production call sites go through the manager (the three lib clients store `RateLimiterManager.getInstance()` in `self._rateLimiter` despite the name suggesting an interface).
- Test mocks: `mockManager.applyLimit = AsyncMock()` returns a truthy MagicMock, so `if not limitsApplied` guards don't trigger in pre-existing consumer tests (stt, stats) — they pass unchanged.

title: /stats --top option: threading new options through StatsHandler's dual render pipelines
content:
Session 2026-09-06 added `/stats --top=<N>` (commit c3a04408). Key durable knowledge beyond what CHANGELOG documents:

**Dual render pipelines**: StatsHandler has two paths that share the same render methods — any new display option must thread through BOTH:
1. Direct path: `statsCommand` → `_buildStatsReply(top=...)` → `_buildSectionView` → `_render{Messages,Commands,Tools,Llm}Section` + `_buildMessagesBreakdownLines` (all take `top: int = 3`).
2. Web-brief path: `statsCommand` → `_handleWebMode` → `_buildStatsReplyFromPayload` → `_buildSectionViewFromPayload` → the same renderers.
Top-list length comes from `StatsAnalyzer.topN(groupLabel, metricKey, n)` in `lib/stats/analysis.py` — the analysis layer was already parameterized; only the handler hardcoded `3`.

**Web HTML page deliberately decoupled**: `lib/stats/stats_pages/generator.py` renders the `--web` page with its own hardcoded per-section limits (5 for users/LLM models, 10 for commands/tools) via `_groupRowsByLabelValue` and does NOT honor `--top`. Decision: `--top` applies to in-chat surfaces only (reply + web-mode brief); the page is a different surface with different defaults.

**New parsed-option touchpoints in `_parseStatsArgs`** (4 sites): `ParsedStatsArgs` field, `knownOptions` set, the require-value list (`period`/`section`/`user`/`top`), and parse/validate + return dict. Validation used `topStr.isascii() and topStr.isdigit()` then range check 1..50 against class constants `_DEFAULT_TOP_N = 3` / `_MAX_TOP_N = 50`; violations raise `StatsUsageError` with Russian message. Both `--top=5` and `--top 5` forms are supported; dangling `--top` at end of args errors.

title: Mock(spec=PydanticModel) returns un-spec'd child Mocks — isinstance-validate extracted values
content:
Testing gotcha hit while adding token-details extraction: `Mock(spec=CompletionUsage)` is only shallow-spec'd. Attribute access to a **spec'd** attribute (e.g. `prompt_tokens_details`) returns a plain child `Mock` that is NOT restricted to the spec — so `getattr(childMock, "cached_tokens", None)` returns a `Mock` object, never `None` or an int. Attribute access to a **non-spec'd** attribute (e.g. OpenRouter's `cost`) raises AttributeError, so `getattr(..., default)` works there.

Consequence: any code that extracts typed values from SDK objects and feeds them into stats/aggregation must `isinstance`-validate the leaf values. Without the guard, Mock objects leak into `ModelRunResult` fields and then into stats recording, where `float(Mock)` raises TypeError in aggregation (`math.isfinite(float(metricValue))` is unguarded). This is exactly why the provider extraction uses `isinstance(value, int)` checks before storing — it protects both against vendor weirdness and against Mock leakage in the extensive Mock-based provider tests (which use `NullStatsStorage()`, so recording itself doesn't crash those tests).

title: applyLimit timeout: pre-check design forced by fake-clock test infra
content: Gotcha from the applyLimit timeout implementation (lib/rate_limiter/sliding_window.py): do NOT implement the timeout with `asyncio.wait_for` or `asyncio.timeout()`. The rate-limiter test fake clock (tests/lib/rate_limiter/conftest.py, `installFakeClock`) patches `time.time` and `asyncio.sleep` scoped to `lib.rate_limiter.sliding_window` so tests fast-forward time instantly — but `wait_for`/`asyncio.timeout` use the EVENT LOOP clock (`loop.time()`), which the fake clock does not control; tests would block in real time. The deterministic pre-check (`waitTime > timeout → False` before sleeping) is exact, cancellation-free, consumes no slot on timeout, and is fully fake-clock testable. If the lock-wait ever needs to count toward the timeout budget, a different test strategy will be required — the current design intentionally excludes lock-acquisition time from the timeout.

title: LLMService reuses provider ModelRunResult objects — no reconstruction layer
content: Data-flow fact verified while extending `ModelRunResult` with new token fields: `internal/services/llm/service.py` contains **zero** `ModelRunResult(...)` constructions — the service layer (including the tool-call round loop) reuses and mutates the provider-returned `ModelRunResult` object directly. Practical implication: adding new optional fields to `ModelRunResult`/`ModelStructuredResult` survives the entire pipeline without any service-level plumbing; conversely, post-hoc flags (`setFallback`, `roundLimitHit`) are set on the same shared object AFTER per-attempt stats recording, which is why such flags can't be captured in `_recordAttemptStats`.

title: Stats web tier uses bounded applyLimit timeout=60s + refusal reply (amends U12-6)
content:
The stats web-tier rate-limiting decision was AMENDED (commit 8f4a5d0c), superseding the ratified U12-6 "applyLimit-only, no refusal reply, just sleeps" decision:

- `internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py` `_handleWebMode` now calls `applyLimit(queue, rateLimiterKey, timeout=_STATS_PAGES_RATELIMIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS)` (class constant = 60; stats-pages limiter is 3/600s). On False → sends refusal reply "⏳ Лимит генерации веб-страниц исчерпан, попробуйте позже." and returns BEFORE invoking the stats CLI subprocess — no more sleeping up to 600s inside the command handler.
- The stale comment "outer D15 wrap covers the no-limiter RuntimeError" was removed (manager returns False now, never raises).
- Design doc docs/design/stats-display-v1.md D13 heading amended; docs/llm/configuration.md, docs/llm/handlers.md synced; regression test `test_rate_limit_timeout_refuses_generation` added in tests/bot/common/handlers/test_stats.py.
- TODO.md item "Add non-blocking rate-limiter variant" (originally surfaced by stats web tier U12) checked off.

title: Stats handler test patterns: mocking boundaries that actually work
content:
Conventions for tests/bot/common/handlers/test_stats.py (confirmed while adding --top tests, 2026-09-06):

- Handler is built with a no-arg local helper `_buildHandler()`; stats rows are `StatsAggregateDict` fixtures returned from a mocked `statsAggregationService.query`.
- Messages top-users e2e tests mock username resolution directly on the handler: `handler._resolveUserName = AsyncMock(side_effect={123: "@alice", ...})` — do not try to mock the cache/db layer underneath.
- Private-chat messages-section tests must mock `getUserChats` to return `[]` (otherwise the "Ваши чаты:" chat list gets appended to the reply). `cache.getChatInfo` does NOT need mocking — its failure path is wrapped in try/except with a fallback title, so the CacheService singleton blowing up is fine in tests.
- Arg-parsing errors are asserted via `pytest.raises(StatsUsageError)`; `StatsUsageError` is importable from the handler module (`internal.bot.common.handlers.stats`).
- Usage-error e2e asserts a single `sendMessage` call with "❌" in `messageText` and no stats queries made (e.g. `handler.statsAggregationService.query.assert_not_called()`).
- Parse tests live in their own class next to `TestStatsHandlerGrammar` (e.g. `TestStatsHandlerTopOptionGrammar`), rendering e2e in a separate class — keep class boundaries intact when inserting (see the heading-consumption gotcha).

title: docs/design/stats-display-v1.md: D-block amendment style
content: `docs/design/stats-display-v1.md` is a decision record with numbered blocks (D1–D16), not a living spec. The convention for changes: amend the affected D-block in place and annotate its header with date + user-update refs, e.g. `### D2 — Args grammar: ... *(rewritten 2026-08-18: U3)*` or `*(added 2026-08-18: U6)*`. Do not add new top-level sections for small grammar/behavior changes — the `--top=<N>` option (2026-09-06) was recorded as a D2 amendment. For /stats changes the full doc sync set is: CHANGELOG.md ([Unreleased]), docs/llm/handlers.md (the StatsHandler grammar lives inside one giant table row — edit unique substrings within it, not the whole line), and this design doc's D-block.

title: applyLimit timeout adoption scope: only stats converted, user rejected other sites
content:
User decision (explicit choice "1 only" when offered the survey): the applyLimit timeout schema was adopted ONLY at the stats web tier. The other call sites deliberately stay on unbounded (no-timeout) applyLimit — candidates if revisited later:

- lib/yandex_search/client.py, lib/openweathermap/client.py, lib/geocode_maps/client.py — saturated limiter stalls whole LLM generation mid-tool-call; timeout would let tools return "service busy" (return None). Good candidates.
- internal/services/stt/service.py:298-301 — unbounded sleep in user-facing voice transcription; converting needs a new RATE_LIMITED-style STTErrorCode + STTOutcome FAILED mapping. Good candidate, slightly bigger change.
- internal/services/llm/service.py `rateLimit()` + handler callers (weather/divination/chat_search/yandex_search) — WEAK candidate, deliberately kept: the wait IS the product UX for over-budget chats ("delayed reply" vs "error"); converting is a product decision, not an engineering one.

title: lib/max_webhook_receiver typing style: typing.List, not builtin list[str]
content: Review-enforced convention (2026-09-06) for the `lib/max_webhook_receiver/` package: use `typing.List[...]` (pre-PEP 585 style), NOT the builtin `list[str]` generic, to match package siblings — `repository.py` (`from typing import List, Optional, Tuple`) and `schema.py` (`from typing import List`). A review fix changed `rowIds: list[str]` → `List[str]` in `lib/max_webhook_receiver/app.py` (~:207) and added `List` to the existing `from typing import Optional` line. Verified after the fix: zero `list[` occurrences remain anywhere in the package. Note this coexists with PEP 695 inline generic syntax used elsewhere in the repo (e.g. `LRUCache[K, V]`) — the project's typing style is not uniformly modern; when editing an existing package, match that package's dominant style rather than reaching for the newest syntax.

title: Webhook receiver test gotcha: GET /updates tests must set getUnprocessedUpdates AsyncMock explicitly
content: Test-infrastructure gotcha in `tests/lib/max_webhook_receiver/test_app.py`: the shared `_makeMockRepository()` helper does NOT pre-configure `getUnprocessedUpdates`. Every test that drives `GET /updates` must explicitly set `mockRepository.getUnprocessedUpdates = AsyncMock(return_value=[])` BEFORE `_buildApp(...)` (see `TestGetUpdatesHandler.testLimitParamRespected` for the pattern). Without it, the handler awaits a non-awaitable MagicMock and fails with a confusing TypeError instead of an assertion error. Related durable fact: `TestDefaultProviderUsage.testRepositoryCallsOmitDataSource` now covers BOTH paths — it drives POST `/webhook` (addUpdate) and GET `/updates` (limit=5&timeout=0) and asserts `"dataSource" not in` the kwargs of each awaited repository call, locking in D13 (handlers call repository methods with no `dataSource` kwarg; calls resolve to the receiver's own `DatabaseManager` default provider, D12).

title: LLMService: chatId is mandatory int + doRateLimit flag decouples rate-limiting from stats attribution
content:
Implemented 2026-08-23 (commit e0ecd959), fixing all three consumerId gaps from docs/design/stats-consumerid-gaps.md (doc now marked IMPLEMENTED). Supersedes the old pattern where `chatId=None` conflated "skip rate limit" with "no stats attribution" (stats landed in `__global__`).

**New API contract on `LLMService` (internal/services/llm/service.py):**
- All five generation methods (`generateText`, `generateStructured`, `generateImage`, `generateEmbedding`, `generateTextViaLLM`) take **mandatory `chatId: int`** (keyword-only, non-Optional). `Optional[int]` is gone — callers cannot accidentally drop attribution.
- New keyword-only `doRateLimit: bool = True` on each; rate limiting runs only `if doRateLimit`. Naming follows the existing `doDebugLogging` convention.
- Attribution is always `consumerId=str(chatId)` — single source of truth. `chatId=None` escape hatch no longer exists.
- Background callers pass the real chat id + `doRateLimit=False`: `chat_search.embedAndSaveMessage` (chatId=ensuredMessage.recipient.id) and `user_memories._runSingleRefinement`. This is the canonical pattern for any future background/no-budget caller.
- `condenseContext` gained stats-only `consumerId: Optional[str] = None` threaded from `generateTextViaLLM` to `condensingModel.generateText` — deliberately a str (not chatId) so it structurally cannot rate-limit.
- `generateEmbedding` now passes `consumerId=str(chatId)` to `embeddingModel.generateEmbeddings`.

**Still true (model layer, lib/ai/abstract.py):** all `generate*` methods accept `consumerId: Optional[str] = None`; with fallback models, consumerId is captured in a lambda closure passed to each model call; `_runWithFallback` is a pure orchestrator without a consumerId param.

**Stats mechanics (unchanged):** `stats_storage.py` merges `consumerId` into `labels["consumer"]`; None → `GLOBAL_CONSUMER_ID = "__global__"` (lib/stats/stats_storage.py:8). Per-chat stats views must exclude `__global__` rows to avoid double-counting.

**Tests:** behavior-preserving mechanical update used `chatId=-1, doRateLimit=False` in place of old `chatId=None` across ~53 test call sites. New regression tests live in `TestConsumerIdAttribution` (tests/services/llm/test_llm_service.py) plus one each in test_chat_search.py / test_user_memories.py.

title: STTService.transcribeMedia: chatId mandatory int; per-chat limiter and consumerId always applied
content:
Implemented 2026-08-23 (commit a33b9b9c), immediately after the LLMService fix. `STTService.transcribeMedia(data, *, chatId: int)` — `chatId` is now mandatory non-Optional `int`.

**Why:** it had the same latent conflation as pre-fix LLMService: `chatId=None` skipped the per-chat `stt-chat` limiter AND dropped stats attribution (`consumerId=None` → `__global__`). It was latent, not active — the only production caller (`BaseBotHandler._transcribeMedia`, base.py:1429) always passed a real int. Tightened rather than adding a `doRateLimit` flag because there is no current skip-the-limiter use case.

**Behavior now:** per-chat limiter applies whenever the queue is configured, keyed `str(chatId)`; `consumerId=str(chatId)` always (test parametrize case `(None, None)` replaced with `(-100, "-100")` in tests/services/stt/test_transcribe.py TestConsumerIdPlumbedToProvider).

**Survey result (2026-08-23): no other chatId-presence-gated rate limiting remains.** Verified clean: `LLMService.rateLimit`/`getRateLimiterKey(chatId: int)` (post-fix, gated by doRateLimit); direct handler `rateLimit` calls (weather, divination, yandex_search, chat_search — unconditional real ids); lib clients openweathermap/yandex_search/geocode_maps (`applyLimit(queue)` unconditional, no chatId); StatsHandler (keyed on issuing chat, unconditional); database/manager.py:142 chatId branch is DB provider routing, not rate limiting.

title: Testing gotchas: condenseContext needs non-empty body to reach generateText; AsyncMock.await_args is Optional for pyright
content:
Two non-obvious traps hit while writing regression tests for the consumerId fix (2026-08-23):

1. **`condenseContext` silently no-ops on tiny inputs.** With defaults (`keepFirstN=0, keepLastN=1`) and only 1 body-eligible message, `batchesCount = tokens // max(...) + 1 = 1` but `batchLength < 1` clamps to 1 and the batch loop condition `startPos < len(body)` is False — `condensingModel.generateText` is NEVER called, so a consumerId assertion passes vacuously-false (awaited 0 times). To exercise the condensing path in tests, build a non-empty body: e.g. messages `[system, user, user]` with `keepLastN=0` and `force=True`. Mirrors existing `TestCondenseContextCoverage` helpers (`_condenseTokensFor`, `_makeCondensingModel`) in tests/services/llm/test_llm_service.py.

2. **pyright: `AsyncMock.await_args` is `Optional[Call]`.** After `mock.assert_awaited_once()`, direct `mock.await_args.kwargs` triggers "kwargs is not a known attribute of None". Guard with `assert mock.await_args is not None` before accessing `.kwargs`.

Also re-confirmed: pytest fixtures must be declared in the test signature — referencing the fixture's name in the body without declaring it resolves to the fixture *function object*, not the mock, and the test silently exercises the wrong object (mock awaited 0 times).

title: User ops taste: everything project-local; deps download normally; alias over shadow deps; small reviewable commits
content:
Strong user taste signals from the Docker-deployment + docs rounds (branch extract-max-webmessage, Aug–Sep 2026), all ratified by explicit user directives:

1. **Nothing outside the project directory.** The user rejected both the `~/webhook-receiver.docker.toml` mount example AND the docker named volume: "creating and using anything outside of project directory is bad". Final shape: config at repo root (`webhook-receiver*.toml`, gitignored), data bind-mounted `./data:/data` with gitignore entry. Never propose named volumes or home-dir paths in run examples.
2. **"Our sources" means the repo's own code, not dependencies.** When the user said "don't download our sources, put local ones to docker", they meant the Gromozeka sources — NOT sqlink. After one clarifying question: private-host dependencies (sqlink @ git.sourcecraft.dev) download normally at build like any other dependency. Don't build wheel-vendoring machinery for deps unless explicitly asked.
3. **Prefer reusing the bot's httpx2 alias stack over installing real httpx.** User directive: "add alias_httpx() and do not require httpx" — real `httpx` was removed from the receiver lockfile entirely; `import httpx` resolves to httpx2 at package import.
4. **Commit per small reviewable step.** "After each step do not forget to commit changes, so we'll have series of small reviewable changes" — the extraction landed as 10+ individually gated commits instead of one big Arc-1 commit, and the user then asked to also commit leftover working files (TODO.md, .opencode/memory.jsonl).
5. **Question rounds with concrete labeled options + "(Recommended)" tag work decisively** — user picked all three recommendations in the Docker-shape round and all three in the rework round. Keep option lists short with a clear recommendation.

title: Ignore-pattern anchoring + stale __pycache__ docs-gate gotchas (docker/gitignore/check-docs)
content:
Three ignore/docs-gate gotchas hit repeatedly while shipping the webhook receiver Docker image and docs (commits 503c125f, a9e41b8b, 1795d37a, branch extract-max-webmessage):

1. **`.dockerignore` patterns are ROOT-ANCHORED unless `**` is used** (unlike `.gitignore`). The first draft's `*.db` / `*.db-wal` / `*.db-shm` matched nothing below the context root, so live databases under `storage/` plus `bak/` (old config trees), `logs/`, `certs/` silently entered the build context. Fix: `**/*.db`, `**/*.db-wal`, `**/*.db-shm` + explicit dir entries. Always cross-check every new ignore pattern against the Dockerfile's COPY sources (here: `lib/__init__.py`, `lib/utils`, `lib/db`, `lib/proxy`, `lib/max_webhook_receiver`) — none may be excluded. Also: inline trailing comments are unsafe in `.dockerignore` (trailing text becomes part of the literal pattern); comments must be whole-line.

2. **Stale `__pycache__` husks defeat `scripts/check_docs.py`.** After `git rm`-ing a package, a leftover `internal/max_webhook_receiver/__pycache__/` directory still satisfies `Path.exists()` (check_docs.py:380), so 7 dead markdown links resolved as "0 broken" — which breaks CI on a fresh clone. After any file/package deletion, physically remove leftover `__pycache__` dirs before trusting `make check-docs`, and re-run the link grep.

3. **`.gitignore` `/*.db` does not match SQLite WAL siblings.** `webhook_receiver_data.db-wal` / `.db-shm` were untracked-dirt candidates (root-anchored pattern requires the name to end in `.db`; siblings survive crashes only — graceful SIGTERM checkpoints and removes them, verified live). Fixed by adding `/*.db-wal` + `/*.db-shm` (commit 1795d37a). Same class of gap exists anywhere a `/*.ext` pattern guards a multi-suffix artifact family. Verify with `git check-ignore -v <file>` — static reasoning about gitignore anchoring has been wrong before.

title: Webhook receiver readiness: aiohttp banner stdout-buffered; Database initialized fires pre-bind; port probe is authoritative
content:
Two receiver readiness signals are NOT what they look like — verified empirically and encoded in `docs/max-webhook-setup.md` Step 9 (commit 1795d37a, branch extract-max-webmessage):

1. **aiohttp's `======== Running on http://… ========` banner is a plain `print()` to stdout** (`aiohttp/web.py` run_app). Under OpenRC `output_log=` file redirection stdout is block-buffered, so the banner does NOT appear until process exit (~57s lag observed live with the listener up the whole time). It appears immediately only on a TTY or in the Docker image (`PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1`, Dockerfile:35-36).

2. **`Database initialized: {...}` (lib/db/manager.py:93) is a startup-PROGRESS line, not a listening proof.** It is emitted during `DatabaseManager.__init__`, which happens at `lib/max_webhook_receiver/__main__.py:107` — BEFORE TLS cert loading (:124-126), BEFORE `web.run_app()` (:128), and before the socket binds. It appears even when binding subsequently fails (e.g. port 8443 occupied). A Gate-1B review caught the docs initially recommending it as the readiness signal — that was wrong.

**Authoritative readiness check = port probe**: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' 'http://127.0.0.1:8443/updates?timeout=0'` — any HTTP answer (including 403 once `get-updates-secret` is set) means the listener is up; connection-level errors mean it is not. Curl WITHOUT `--fail` is deliberate: exit 0 on 403, non-zero on connection errors — exactly the semantics needed for a start-order wait loop: `until curl -s -o /dev/null 'http://127.0.0.1:8443/updates?timeout=0'; do sleep 1; done`.

Optional follow-up (deliberately not done, user's call): log receiver readiness via `logging` in code instead of relying on aiohttp's buffered stdout banner.

title: Receiver Docker packaging: 18-pin closure, --no-deps load-bearing, eager sqlink import, smoke-verified image shape
content:
Docker packaging facts for the standalone Max webhook receiver (`lib/max_webhook_receiver/{requirements.txt,Dockerfile}` + root `.dockerignore`; commits 503c125f + a9e41b8b, smoke-verified twice on the user's colima daemon, image ≈131 MB):

- **Standalone lockfile = 18 pins**: the receiver's module-level import closure. Mirrors root `requirements.txt` versions exactly, with three deltas vs "just filter the root lockfile": `httpx2==2.10.0` + `httpcore2==2.10.0` + `truststore==0.10.4` IN; real `httpx`/`httpcore`/`certifi` never present (bot shadows httpx via `alias_httpx()`, receiver aliases at package import). `lib/db/providers/__init__.py` EAGERLY imports BOTH registered providers (sqlite3 + sqlink), so sqlink is an import-time requirement even though only sqlite3 is configured; sqlink's metadata declares `httpx>=0.28`, which is why the Dockerfile's `pip install --no-deps -r requirements.txt` is LOAD-BEARING — plain pip resolution would drag real httpx back in.
- **sqlink is fetched anonymously at build** from the private `git.sourcecraft.dev` host (commit-pinned URL byte-identical to root lockfile:86) — verified working with no credentials; the BuildKit `--mount=type=secret,id=netrc` in the Dockerfile is the documented fallback if anonymous access is ever revoked. `apk add git` is required for the git+ URL.
- **Image shape**: `python:3.13-alpine` (all pins ship musl cp313 wheels or are pure-Python; `typing_extensions` unneeded ≥3.13; `sniffio` not required by anyio 4.x), non-root `receiver` uid 10001, `/data` chowned before `VOLUME` (fresh named volumes inherit uid), `ENTRYPOINT ["python3","-m","lib.max_webhook_receiver"]` + `CMD ["--config","/app/webhook-receiver.toml"]`, no HEALTHCHECK by design (GET /updates 403s once get-updates-secret is set).
- **Smoke facts**: `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`/`PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1` set; expected one benign boot line `ERROR - File .env not found` when using `-e` env vars (dotenv probe of `/app/.env` soft-fails); alias verified in-image (`sys.modules['httpx'] is httpx2`, no httpx/httpcore/certifi dists); probes 200 (GET /updates), 403 (POST no/wrong secret), 200 (valid); colima gotcha: `/tmp` is not shared into the VM — bind-mount sources must live under `$HOME` (or `docker create` + `docker cp`), and colima's uid mapping made the plain `./data` mount writable without `-u`.
- **Runtime closure detail**: `sqlite_vec` is try/except-guarded optional in the sqlite3 provider (`_SQLITE_VEC_AVAILABLE`); `lib/proxy` is stdlib-only (httpx2 appears only in docstrings); mysql/postgresql providers are unregistered dead code, not imported by the factory.

title: Docker smokes go to software-developer; code-reviewer sandbox denies docker; colima /tmp mount trap
content:
Agent-sandbox capability map learned while shipping the receiver Docker image (2026-08-27, branch extract-max-webmessage) — route work accordingly:

- **code-reviewer CANNOT run docker** (`docker info` denied by the bash permission allowlist) and cannot execute ad-hoc python beyond allowlisted commands; it CAN run `make lint`, `make test`, `make check-docs`, and `./venv/bin/pytest`. So a "reviewer validates the built image" plan fails — docker build/run smokes must go to **software-developer**, which ran the full build + container probes successfully twice. Have reviewers verify Dockerfiles statically (pin-vs-lockfile diff, COPY↔ignore cross-check, closure completeness via installed dist-info METADATA) and dispatch smokes separately.
