title: fusion-agent model-catalog generation system: reference implementation for gromozeka tooling
content:
Full read-only survey of /Users/vgoshev/Development/NotA/fusion-agent (2026-09-14), done as the reference implementation for gromozeka's planned "generate model catalogs from models.dev + filter globs + disabled-by-default" tooling. Replicate without re-reading fusion-agent.

**Layout:** three standalone catalog TOMLs at repo root, each = one `[providers.<name>]` section + flat `[models."<provider>/<model_id>"]` entries; user's `fusion.toml` pulls them in via `[include] files = [...]` with recursive deep merge (later file wins per key; including file wins last). Catalogs are COMMITTED to git; personal fusion.toml + .env are gitignored.

**Files:**
- `scripts/catalog_common.py` — stdlib-only shared helpers: `fetch_json(url)` (urllib, timeout=60, custom User-Agent `fusion-agent-catalog/0.1` — default python-urllib UA gets 403 from models.dev; NO retry/cache/offline), `toml_key()` (bare key iff `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$`, else double-quoted — dotted/slashed ids force quoted headers like `[models."opencode-go/glm-5.3"]`), `fmt_price()` (`%.6f` with trailing zeros stripped; negative raises), `model_block()`/`provider_block()` emitters, `write_catalog()` (FULL OVERWRITE, never merges).
- `scripts/fetch_opencode_models.py` — `uv run python scripts/fetch_opencode_models.py [output.toml]`, default out `opencode-go.toml` (36 models). Source: https://models.dev/api.json, provider key "opencode-go". api_key_env `OPENCODE_API_KEY`.
- `scripts/fetch_openrouter_models.py` — same CLI shape, default out `openrouter.toml` (445 models). Source: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models (public, no auth).
- `docs/model-catalogs.md` — the how-to doc: include/merge rules + alias-prefix rationale + per-provider update procedures (YC manual, others regenerate).
- Runtime engine: `fusion_agent/config.py` (include tree, deep merge, `${ENV}` expansion, validation) + `fusion_agent/backends/manager.py`.
- Guard test: `tests/test_config.py::test_shipped_example_config_loads` — loads real fusion.example.toml + all three catalogs with fake env keys, asserts provider set and `len(cfg.models) == 11 + 36 + 445 + 3` (a cross-catalog alias collision would shrink the union). This drift-guard count assertion is the pattern to copy.

**KEY NEGATIVE FINDING:** fusion-agent has NO blacklist/whitelist, NO glob patterns, NO per-provider filter config file anywhere. Its only in-code filters: opencode script skips models whose `modalities.input` lacks "text"; openrouter script emits everything. "Disable" is a runtime mechanism: re-declare the alias in your own fusion.toml with `enabled = false` — deep merge overlays the flag, `BackendManager` skips it, and fusion references to it are rejected. Gromozeka's requested whitelist/blacklist-globs feature must be designed fresh; fusion-agent only offers the disabled-by-default-ish `enabled = false` overlay pattern.

**Conventions worth copying:** aliases are prefixed `<provider-name>/<model_id>` (commit 11e044d) so deep-merged catalogs can never silently rebind colliding vendor ids; generated files carry a GENERATED-marker header with source URL + fetch date + regenerate command ("edit-free"); models sorted by id; prices emitted only as input/output pair with optional `price_cached` between; `support_structured_output = true` only when strictly true. Scripts have no try/except: any failure → traceback → exit 1; success prints `wrote <path>: N models (...), B bytes` → exit 0. Scripts are stdlib-only, import catalog_common via `sys.path.insert(0, Path(__file__).parent)`, and are NOT covered by lint (ruff runs on `fusion_agent tests` only). No direct script tests exist.

**fusion-agent runtime model-entry schema (reference):** required `provider` + `model_id`; optional `context_size` (default 32768; legacy `context` fallback), `model_version` ("latest"), `price_input`+`price_output` (MUST be set together; `price_cached` defaults to price_input; local table only prices calls when backend reports none — reported cost wins), `support_structured_output`, `custom_params` (dict; deprecated camelCase `customParams` accepted with warning), `enabled` (default true). Provider types: `openrouter`, `yc-openai` (+folder_id), `custom-openai` (+base_url), `opencode-go`; all support `proxy` and `${ENV}` expansion.

**YC AI Studio has no machine-readable price API** — its catalog (11 models) is hand-maintained per docs/model-catalogs.md: authoritative ids via `curl -s https://ai.api.cloud.yandex.net/v1/models -H "Authorization: Bearer $YC_API_KEY"` (take `gpt://<folder>/<id>/latest`, skip `emb://` and `speech-realtime*`), context sizes from the Model Gallery page, prices from the USD ex-VAT pricing column ×1000 (per-1K→per-1M), RUB kept in entry comments, `support_structured_output = true` on all entries, deprecation deadlines recorded in comments.

Git history shape: catalogs landed as separate commits (YC manual → opencode from models.dev → openrouter from public API → alias-prefix commit → doc commits).

title: models.dev + OpenRouter API shapes and pricing-mapping gotchas for catalog generators
content:
Field-level API shapes and mapping rules extracted from fusion-agent's generator scripts (scripts/fetch_opencode_models.py, scripts/fetch_openrouter_models.py), for building gromozeka's equivalent generators.

**models.dev** (https://models.dev/api.json): top-level dict keyed by provider id → take `catalog["opencode-go"]` (the catalog OpenCode publishes for its subscription gateway; matches the provider's base_url). Provider object: `.get("doc")` → docs URL for the header comment; `["models"]` → dict of model-id → model object. Per model: `modalities.input` list — SKIP if `"text"` not in it (only filter); `limit.context` → context_size; `cost.input` / `cost.output` → price_input/price_output (ALREADY USD per 1M tokens — no conversion); `cost.cache_read` → price_cached; `cost.cache_write` deliberately IGNORED (not expressible in per-call accounting); `structured_output` bool → support_structured_output; `name` → TOML comment line; `id` → model_id (falls back to dict key). GOTCHA: send a real User-Agent header (fusion-agent uses `fusion-agent-catalog/0.1`) — python-urllib's default UA gets 403 from models.dev. timeout=60, no retry/cache.

**OpenRouter** (https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models, public no-auth): response is OpenAI-style — `catalog["data"]` is a LIST of model objects. Per model: `id` → model_id (contains vendor slashes); `name` → comment; `context_length` → context_size; `pricing.prompt` / `pricing.completion` / `pricing.input_cache_read` — USD PER TOKEN as strings → multiply ×1_000_000 for per-1M values. CONVENTION: negative price means "variable/unknown pricing" (e.g. auto-routers like `openrouter/fusion`) → emit the entry WITHOUT any price keys. `supported_parameters` list containing `"structured_outputs"` → support_structured_output = true. No filtering at all — every model emitted, sorted by id.

**Price formatting rule** (catalog_common.fmt_price): negative → ValueError; `f"{n:.6f}"` then rstrip("0").rstrip(".") → compact per-1M values (0.15, 3, 0.003). Prices written only when BOTH input and output exist; price_cached optional between them.

**TOML key quoting rule** (catalog_common.toml_key): bare key iff matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$`, else double-quote and escape `\` and `"`. Model ids with dots or slashes (nearly all) require quoted table headers: `[models."provider/model.id"]`.

**YC AI Studio** (manual): no price API. Ids: `GET https://ai.api.cloud.yandex.net/v1/models` with Bearer $YC_API_KEY → take `gpt://<folder>/<model-id>/latest`, skip `emb://` and `speech-realtime*`. Prices: yandex.cloud pricing page, sync-mode USD ex-VAT column ×1000 (per-1K → per-1M); "cached tokens" column → price_cached; "tool tokens" rate = cached rate. All YC AI Studio models support structured output (verified live) → support_structured_output = true on every entry.

title: markdown-mcp fitness audit results (2026-09-14): verdicts + 6-item fix list
doc_search behavioral gotchas: duplicate window chunks, mid-cell snippet truncation, canonical-doc ranking losses
content:
New doc_search behavioral gotchas observed 2026-09-14 during the fitness audit (complements memory c6037516, which already records weak search-score separation and doc_outline cost from the A/B benchmark — score separation was re-confirmed here, not new):

1. NEW — Duplicate window chunks: overlapping window chunks of the SAME section routinely occupy 2 of 3 top-k slots, halving result diversity. Observed on llm/testing.md §7 template (Q4 "test fixtures conftest mockBot singleton reset"), llm/tasks.md §3.1 (Q9 MessageId), sql-portability-guide.md upsert section (Q10). Root cause is server/index-level window chunking without per-section dedup; doc content edits cannot fix it. Report to markdown-mcp maintainers.
2. NEW — Mid-cell snippet truncation on dense gotcha tables: for llm/tasks.md §3.1 (MessageId row, getChatSettings row) the search snippet cuts off mid-table-cell exactly where the answer begins ("`Dict[Ch…", "`.asSt…"). The section content itself is complete — doc_read(section_slug="3-1-data-shapes-settings-keys-and-platform-quirks") returns the full 21-row table. NEVER conclude content is missing from a truncated snippet; follow up with a targeted doc_read.
3. NEW — Canonical llm/ docs can lose to human-facing docs on near-identical queries: llm/handlers.md §2 lost "how do I add a new handler" to guides/handlers.md (2 slots); llm/database.md §9 lost "update both schema docs" to database-README.md. When a search misses, check whether the canonical agent doc exists and was merely outranked before assuming the answer lives elsewhere. Search rewards phrasing/vocabulary, not authoritativeness.
4. NEW — file_glob filtering works reliably for memories discovery: file_glob="llm/memories/*.md" returned the right memory file in top-3 for 3/3 realistic queries (user memories relevance score; sandbox docker tests recipe; vector search sqlite-vec). Safe to rely on for teamlead memory discovery.
5. Practical search recipe implied by all of the above: trust doc_outline + section-addressed doc_read for answers; treat doc_search as a locator whose top-3 is diversity-impaired and whose scores are noise (0.88–0.92 band regardless of relevance — see memory c6037516).

title: Design: model-catalog generation from models.dev (fetch_models.py + models-filters.toml) — locked decisions
content:
Design (2026-09-14, architect pass; implementation pending) for scripts/fetch_models.py — generates configs/00-defaults/{openrouter-models,opencode-go-models}.toml from https://models.dev/api.json.

LOCKED decisions:
- Two files: scripts/fetch_models.py (CLI entry: network via httpx2 sync + custom User-Agent, --provider/--all/--dry-run/--filters/--output-dir) + scripts/models_catalog.py (PURE logic: filters/mapping/TOML emission, zero network, imported by tests). Per-glob `name` override exists because openrouter/qwen3.5-flash ← model_id qwen/qwen3.5-flash-02-23 (suffix must be dropped to keep overlay-referenced name stable). Name collisions → hard error.
- openrouter/free auto-router NOT guaranteed in models.dev → hand-defined via [[providers.X.extraModels]] (emitted verbatim, bypass filters). Bot-defaults selectors require names: openrouter/free, openrouter/gemini-2.5-flash-image (+ yc names out of scope).
- Tier values MUST be ChatTier strings: free/paid/friend/bot-owner (HYPHEN — chat_settings.py:60; fromStr returns None for "bot_owner" underscore → model unusable in picker per base.py:321-322). Existing configs/common/01-opencode-go.toml uses "bot_owner" — latent bug, flag for manual fix. lib/ai/abstract.py:827 default "bot_owner" also inconsistent (latent, unaffected by generator since tier always emitted).
- models.dev schema VERIFIED (github.com/anomalyco/models.dev README): per-provider models have tool_call, structured_output (optional), temperature (optional bool — false ⇒ suppress customParams.temperature), status (alpha/beta/deprecated), limit.context, modalities.input/output, name, cost.* (DROPPED — gromozeka has no price fields).
- providers.toml opencode-go block stays COMMENTED-OUT: substituteEnvVars (lib/utils/utils.py:32, os.getenv(key, match.group(0))) passes missing ${VAR} through literally → a live block would register a provider with garbage api_key in every default install (init is non-fatal, manager.py:142-143; failures only at request time).

Initial whitelist = the 9 current ids (claude-haiku-4.5 disabled-by-default, tier bot-owner; google/*-image* tier friend + supportText=false override; rest tier paid). opencode-go: NO whitelist (include all), disabledByDefault=["*"] (all enabled=false → zero runtime change; models skipped at manager.py:172-174 BEFORE provider lookup, so no warnings without provider).
- Exact-id whitelist entry matching nothing → HARD ERROR exit 1 (drift guard); wildcard unmatched → warning only. Always emit enabled explicitly. Sort by final name; GENERATED header with source URL + UTC date + regenerate command + overlay how-to comment.
- Tests: tests/scripts/test_fetch_models.py + fixture tests/scripts/fixtures/models_dev_api.json, offline, import scripts.models_catalog directly; includes drift-guard integration test (tomllib-read tracked configs, assert bot-defaults selector names exist).

title: markdown-mcp has NO dedup/diversity config knob — result crowding is a contracted upstream design (v1.8.0)
content:
Verdict of a 2026-09-14 read-only investigation, triggered by a doc_search result-quality issue: for one query, two overlapping WINDOW chunks of the SAME section (lines 413-478 and 446-477) occupied 2 of 3 top-k slots.

(a) NO config or CLI knob exists for chunk dedup, per-section result diversity, window overlap, or chunking. The complete recognized config schema (verified in markdown-mcp src/markdown_mcp/config.py:432-534) is: [docs] root/exclude/writable/rescan_interval/create_root_if_missing; [index] location/model; [search] min_score (the ONLY search key); [read] section_read_cap/disk_read_cap; [embeddings] provider/api_key/base_url/query_model/passage_model/dimensions/prefixes/timeout_seconds/recovery_command/recovery_cooldown_seconds/max_input_chars. CLI: `serve` has zero options; `index` only --force/--verbose; `search` only --top-k (1-50, default 8)/--tag/--category/--glob/--json. So a config-fix for crowding is impossible — don't retry that path.

Root cause is CONTRACTED design, not misconfiguration: window constants are hard-coded `Final` in src/markdown_mcp/constants.py:104-111 (WINDOW_CHAR_THRESHOLD=1200, WINDOW_MIN_CHARS=200, WINDOW_OVERLAP_MAX_CHARS=200) under an explicit "zero new config keys" design commitment. The section-KNN + window-KNN merge (commands.py:259) is "No dedup, no score aggregation (contracted, v1.1-backlog.md §5)"; storage-indexing.md (~955-958): each KNN yields ≤top_k rows, merged pool ≤2×top_k, plain descending-score sort, trim to top_k; min_score applies per-KNN before the merge. The 200-char paragraph overlap legitimately creates distinct near-duplicate window rows, and the no-dedup merge lets them share top-k slots — exactly the observed Q4 symptom.

(b) Upstream is aware and evidence-gated: markdown-mcp's docs/design/v1.1-backlog.md §5 ("deduplication needs measured examples") and §6 (reranking); docs/dogfood-log.md already has reranking evidence-gate rows, incl. a 2026-09-06 golden-set crowding case (quickstart section crowded out of top-18 by ~23 window hits). The gromozeka Q4 observation is exactly the "measured example" their gate wants — the recommended path is filing it upstream (query + two line ranges + scores) rather than any local config change.

(c) Other search-relevant knobs: [search] min_score (float, default 0.8281339991975838) — raising it prunes weak hits but CANNOT dedup near-identical windows (they score almost the same); top_k is per-call only; [index] model (default e5-small); [read] caps affect the read path, not ranking; SNIPPET_LENGTH=200 chars is a constant. Mitigations available today: raise top_k and skim, or narrow with file_glob.

title: markdown-mcp binary is a shim to a local editable checkout — source directly browsable; `config show` dumps resolved config
content:
Discovered 2026-09-14 during a markdown-mcp config investigation:

- `~/bin/markdown-mcp` is an 88-byte sh shim: `exec /Users/vgoshev/Development/NotA/markdown-mcp/.venv/bin/markdown-mcp "$@"` — the tool (v1.8.0 as of 2026-09-14) is an EDITABLE install of a local source checkout at `~/Development/NotA/markdown-mcp`. content:

title: Post-fix validation of doc-fitness pass: prose callouts moved doc_search rankings; links/intro sentences did not (2026-09-14)
content:
Post-fix validation of the markdown-mcp fitness fix pass, 2026-09-14 (code-analyst; read-only re-run of the SAME 10 doc_search queries, top_k=3, from the baseline audit in memory 07e21ab3, compared against that recorded baseline). All content fixes verified landed via doc_read before measuring: `llm/tasks.md` two new H4 prose callouts ("MessageId platform IDs", "Chat-settings return shapes by layer"); `llm/handlers.md` §2 intro sentence; `llm/database.md` §4 See-also → §9; +description/tags on three files.

## Measured effect
Clean 1-call wins 4→5; misses 3→2; no regressions.
- POSITIVE: the two new H4 prose callouts in `llm/tasks.md` took the #1 and #2 scores of the entire run (0.917 "Chat-settings return shapes by layer", 0.916 "MessageId platform IDs" — highest of all 30 returned chunks). Q7 (getChatSettings shape) flipped partial→WIN with fully legible prose (Dict[ChatSettingsKey, ChatSettingsValue] + .toBool()/.toStr() visible). Q9 (MessageId) improved to improved-PARTIAL (platform mapping legible, but snippet truncation still cuts exactly at the accessor names — known truncation gotcha, memory 54600de4). Q4 (conftest fixtures) miss→PARTIAL: canonical `llm/testing.md` now surfaces 2/3 slots, though via §7 (duplicate windows), not the intended §2 "Available Fixtures".
- NEGATIVE (fix verified present in indexed content, ZERO ranking movement): (a) intro sentence inside the large `llm/handlers.md` §2 body — Q1 still a MISS, §2 absent, guides/handlers.md still takes 2 slots; (b) See-also cross-link in `llm/database.md` §4 → §9 — Q5 still a MISS on the canonical-target criterion (database-README.md still substitutes, though its snippet self-answers by naming both schema docs).
- Duplicate-window crowding persisted post-fix (Q4: testing.md §7 twice; Q10: ExcludedValue slug twice) — confirms memory 54600de4; chunking limitation, not addressable by content edits.

## Load-bearing lesson (validated, not hypothesized)
markdown-mcp search ranking follows section content volume + title match — NOT inbound links, NOT thin intro prose inside large sections. The lever that demonstrably moves a query from miss/partial to win is promoting the key content into a dedicated SHORT, self-contained H2/H3 prose section with a keyword-rich title. When a canonical doc must surface for a question, add a prose callout section; do not rely on cross-links or one-line intros.

title: Phase A models_catalog.py implemented — brief deviations locked in as decisions
content:
Phase A of the model-catalog generation feature implemented 2026-09-14 (files in repo: `scripts/models_catalog.py` pure-logic module, `scripts/models-filters.toml`, `tests/scripts/fixtures/models_dev_api.json`). Public API exactly per the locked design (see design memory 12f6b5c7): CatalogError; dataclasses ModelOverride/FilterConfig/ModelSpec/CatalogStats; functions loadFiltersConfig/parseFilterConfig/extractProviderSection/buildModelName/applyFilters/emitCatalog/tomlKey/formatTomlValue; stdlib-only imports. Verified: make format lint clean (pyright 0 errors, lint's import-main circular check passes), make test 4582 passed/11 skipped, throwaway smoke run (temp dir, not committed) round-trips via tomllib.

Deviations from the implementation brief — behavior NOT obvious from code, treat as locked decisions:
1. Drift guard: exact (no `* ? [`) WHITELIST miss -> CatalogError. Exact misses in blacklist/disabled-by-default -> warning appended to stats.unmatchedWildcardGlobs (brief was silent; routed to the warning channel). Wildcard misses from any filter list -> same warning list.
2. Drift matching is a pre-pass over ALL upstream ids independent of the pipeline: an id that exists upstream but is skipped (deprecated / audio-only) still counts as matched, so no false drift error.
3. Extra-vs-extra duplicate names also raise CatalogError (brief listed only derived-vs-derived and derived-vs-extra collisions).
4. parseFilterConfig requires each [[extra-models]] entry to carry a non-empty "name" (it becomes the table header); the remainder of the entry is stored/emitted verbatim.
5. Extra-model-only override fields (input-image-format, image-generation-api) validate and are stored in ModelOverride.fields but are no-ops on upstream-derived ModelSpecs.
6. `enabled = ...` is always emitted only for upstream-derived tables; extra-models are verbatim, so `openrouter/free` has no enabled line (runtime default true).
7. stats.enabledByDefault/disabledByDefault are computed from the FINAL emitted enabled flags (an override can flip a disabled-by-default match back to true); they sum to included.
8. An override's custom-params REPLACES the whole customParams dict (last-match-wins per field; dicts wholesale, not merged).

Emission facts: header exactly per design; entries sorted by plain ASCII name sort ('-' < '.', so qwen3-vl sorts before qwen3.5; gemini models land mid-list, unlike today's hand-written file); canonical field order enabled -> provider -> model_id -> model_version("latest") -> context -> support_* -> tier -> customParams.* flattened dotted; tomlKey double-quotes any key not matching [A-Za-z0-9_-]+.

Phase B still pending (separate session): scripts/fetch_models.py CLI entry + pytest tests + CHANGELOG entry + docs sync (docs/llm/model-catalogs.md per the design memory). Deferred because nothing is user-visible until the CLI exists.

4. ALL-OR-NOTHING: main processes every provider before writing any file; on any CatalogError/fetch error -> "error: ..." to stderr, exit 1, nothing written. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 filters/fetch/filtering error, 2 argparse error.
5. `fetchCatalog()` accepts `file://` URL (scheme stripped) or plain filesystem path -> local read, else `httpx2.Client(timeout=60, follow_redirects=True, headers={"User-Agent": "gromozeka-catalog-fetch/1.0"})` + raise_for_status (models.dev 403s default python UAs).

content:

title: Agent mistakes corrected during Phase B implementation
content:
Agent mistakes made and self-corrected during Phase B implementation (scripts/fetch_models.py + tests/scripts/test_fetch_models.py, 2026-09-14) — right ways to do it:

1. Pytest fixture params must keep framework names: naming the fixture param `tmpPath` caused `fixture 'tmpPath' not found` — pytest registers `tmp_path` (snake_case). Fix: test methods take `tmp_path` (also `capsys`, `monkeypatch` as-is); only internal test-local helper functions keep camelCase params (house camelCase rule does not override framework-registered names).
2. Inline TOML section constants: forgetting a top-level key (`disabled-by-default = [...]`) silently produced wrong test results (enabled=True instead of False). In TOML strings, ALL top-level keys must appear BEFORE any sub-table header like `[defaults]` — after the header, keys belong to that table.
3. Leftover drafting placeholders: a half-written line sliced a section string to `""` and passed it to `parseFilterConfig` (would raise CatalogError on empty provider-key). Lesson: remove scratch lines before running; read the full written file before executing.
4. Black reformats wrapped signatures — oldString-based edits on freshly formatted files fail unless the exact reformatted text is read first. Read the file (or the region) before targeted edits after `make format`.
5. Sketched-signature conflict resolution pattern: the task sketch's `processProvider -> Tuple[int, Path]` could not support all-or-nothing writes (main needs the rendered text) — when a sketch conflicts with a functional requirement (all-or-nothing), the functional requirement wins and the deviation gets documented in the handoff, not silently worked around.

title: httpx2 boundary rule: plain import OK for leaf scripts, alias_httpx only for transitive-httpx importers
content:
When the `alias_httpx()` dance is (and is not) required for scripts under `scripts/` — boundary rule confirmed 2026-09-14 while writing scripts/fetch_models.py:

- Plain `import httpx2` + `httpx2.Client` is CORRECT for a standalone script that imports only the stdlib and other leaf modules (e.g. `scripts.models_catalog`) — no `internal.*`/`lib.*` import that transitively does `import httpx`. The alias dance (mandatory ordering before any transitive httpx import, per the httpx2 migration memories) exists solely to redirect `import httpx` performed by third-party/project code; a script that never triggers one needs no alias.
- Enforcement is allowlist-based, not global: `tests/scripts/test_httpx_alias_import.py` checks only an explicit list of scripts that DO import project code; a new leaf script like fetch_models.py is not auto-added and passes with a plain import. A short code comment in the script should note WHY plain import is safe, so future readers don't "fix" it into the alias pattern.
- Contrast: `scripts/list_models.py`/`scripts/prune_unknown_chat_settings.py` import `internal.*`/`lib.*` and therefore DO need the alias — do not copy their import block into leaf scripts verbatim.
- httpx2.Client accepts `timeout=`, `follow_redirects=True`, `headers=` (verified against installed httpx2 2.10.0).

title: Catalog regeneration verification gotchas: git-diff alignment, generator data precedence, cosmetic diffs
content:
Gotchas learned while verifying the live catalog regeneration (Phase C, 2026-09-14) — applicable to any future `scripts/fetch_models.py` re-run diff review:

1. **`git diff` alignment is MISLEADING for regenerated TOML model catalogs.** Git matches common lines (`provider =`, `context =`, `tier =`) across DIFFERENT model blocks, so hunks look like one model "became" another (e.g. the qwen3-235b-a22b block appeared to morph into openrouter/free). To enumerate per-name deltas precisely, READ the new file directly and compare against the old content — don't trust hunk alignment. (`git diff --stat` is still fine for "which files changed".)

2. **Generator data precedence (confirmed against real data):** upstream models.dev capability fields win when present; `scripts/models-filters.toml` defaults apply only when upstream lacks the data; filters-file policy fields (support-text overrides, tier-rules, extra-models) are always enforced. Consequences seen: `qwen3-235b-a22b` `support_structured_output` true→false (models.dev has no structured-output data for it → generator default false); both gemini image models flipped `support_tools` true→false AND `support_structured_output` false→true (models.dev capability data) while `support_text = false` and `tier = "friend"` stayed policy-enforced. Context values: NO drift at all — every hand-written context already matched models.dev.

3. **Cosmetic diffs to expect on every regeneration** (not regressions): explicit `enabled = true` added to all previously-implicit-enabled models; hand-written inline comments dropped (policy now lives solely in models-filters.toml — re-adding comments to a GENERATED file is pointless, they get overwritten); upstream display-name comments replace hand-written ones; an extra-model entry defined without `enabled` in filters gets NO explicit `enabled` line (absent = enabled at runtime, same semantics as the old hand-written files).

4. **Commented provider blocks survive config merge:** a fully-commented `[models.providers.X]` block in providers.toml produces zero provider registration in the merged config — unset `${VAR}` pass-through only becomes a hazard if someone uncomments without the env var (silent bogus-key provider). Verify with `--print-config | grep`: provider name should appear only inside per-model `"provider"` values, never as a providers-section key.

title: Review findings: test_fetch_models.py gaps — url-template untested, fixture↔shipped drift, name-only drift guard
content:
Read-only review (2026-09-14) of tests/scripts/test_fetch_models.py + fixture + models-filters.toml found NO functional bugs, but four test gaps:

1. **`model-url-template` is 0% covered.** scripts/models-filters.toml:25 declares it; shipped openrouter-models.toml carries the resulting `# https://openrouter.ai/...` comment lines. But no test sets the key: `_openrouterSection` (test:104-109), `_opencodeSection` (:125-130), `_CLI_FILTERS_TOML` (:179-238) all omit it → FilterConfig.modelUrlTemplate parsing (models_catalog.py:602), substitution (:767) and emission (:943-945) are untested; a regression (e.g. bad `{model_id}` handling) surfaces only at next live regeneration. Related nit: test comment :133-135 claims `_FULL_OPENROUTER_SECTION` is "byte-for-byte the same rule set" — it isn't (omits model-url-template).

2. **Fixture has drifted from the shipped catalogs** (fixture is a hand-maintained stand-in, not a live snapshot):
   - `qwen3-235b-a22b`: fixture structured_output=true (fixture:84) vs shipped `support_structured_output = false` (openrouter-models.toml:112) — live models.dev lacks the field so generator default won.
   - `glm-5.3-flash` context: fixture 200000 vs shipped 1000000 (opencode-go-models.toml:111); `deepseek-v4-flash`: fixture 1048576 vs shipped 1000000 (:20).
   Consequence: a "regenerate == shipped file (modulo `# Fetched:` line)" equivalence test IS feasible for openrouter (fixture covers exactly the 9 whitelisted ids + openrouter/free extra) but would currently fail on qwen3-235b-a22b until the fixture is updated. Until then, shipped tiers/contexts/support values are drift-guarded only by NAME (the 5 bot-defaults selectors, test:864-889) — hand-edits or bad regenerations of values pass CI.

3. **Real filters' tier-only override shape (override with `tier`, no `name`, models-filters.toml:90-96) never runs through `main()`** — `_CLI_FILTERS_TOML` drops those two overrides; test:469-491 covers tier-in-override only together with a name replacement.

4. **Offline-safety footnote**: `fetchCatalog` checks file:// and existing local paths BEFORE any HTTP (fetch_models.py:200-204), so tests are offline — but a typo'd/missing fixture path in a FUTURE test would silently fall through to a real HTTP GET of that string (fails fast with httpx error, but is a network attempt). Nothing current hits this.

Verified good: offline (all fixture paths absolute+existing), cwd-independent (both script and test anchor to repo root via `__file__`; CLI tests use absolute tmp_path args; main() mkdirs output dir), roundtrip assertions solid (tomllib re-parse, exact extra-model dict, all-or-nothing empty-dir-on-failure), tiers all valid hyphenated ChatTier values with underscore rejection asserted (test:308-309).

title: Code review of models.dev catalog feature (Phases A+B+C): 6 findings, no functional bug; gates green
content:
Full code-review pass (2026-09-14, code-reviewer, read-only; Phases A+B+C uncommitted in working tree) over the 9 scoped files: scripts/models_catalog.py, scripts/fetch_models.py, scripts/models-filters.toml, tests/scripts/test_fetch_models.py, tests/scripts/fixtures/models_dev_api.json, both regenerated catalogs, providers.toml append, openrouter-models-free.toml deletion. Verdict: NO functional bug in the scoped files; shipped catalogs runtime-valid. Six findings to address (severity-ordered):

1. MAJOR — Extra models bypass runtime-schema validation (models_catalog.py:592–595, 1015–1021). Extra-model parsing validates only `name`; emission writes remaining fields verbatim → an extra model with tier="bot_owner" (underscore → ChatTier.fromStr → None → invisible in picker), missing provider/model_id, or non-int context would be accepted. openrouter/free itself is valid; the generator's guarantee is not. Fix: validate extras independently of filtering (require nonempty provider+model_id, run tier through _validateTier, enforce runtime field types, reject bool context). "Bypass filtering" must not mean "bypass schema validation". Add negative tests per invalid shape.

2. MAJOR — String escaping + comment emission can produce invalid TOML (models_catalog.py:258–267, 924–945). _escapeTomlString handles backslash+quote but leaves \n / \r / control chars literal in values and quoted keys; upstream display names / URL-template / header values are interpolated into comments without line-break handling → a multiline upstream name can inject an uncommented line into the generated doc; the CLI never parses rendered TOML before writing. Floats verified OK (Python repr incl. inf/nan spelling is TOML-compatible). Fix: escape all TOML-sensitive control chars, normalize comments to one line or # prefix every line, tomllib.loads each finished document before enqueueing the write; roundtrip tests for \n \r \t control chars quotes backslashes.

3. MAJOR — Drift-failure CLI test passes for the wrong reason (tests/scripts/test_fetch_models.py:778–808). test_whitelistMissFailsWritingNothing writes filter fields at the TOML doc root WITHOUT [providers.openrouter], so loadFiltersConfig rejects the file BEFORE the whitelist/drift-guard logic runs; assertions (exit 1, "error:", empty dir) pass vacuously w.r.t. the test's name. Also single-provider → cannot prove an earlier successfully-rendered provider stays unwritten when a later one fails. Fix: supply a valid provider table and assert the specific drift-guard diagnostic; add an --all test (first provider renders, second fails); pre-seed output files and assert bytes unchanged.

4. MINOR — Malformed filter/upstream shapes escape the promised CatalogError diagnostic path (models_catalog.py:560, 574, 593, 735–761; fetch_models.py:309–311): tier-rules=1 / overrides=false / scalar extra-models → raw TypeError during enumeration; empty string/table silently accepted as empty rule collections; null upstream model → AttributeError; modalities.input=null → TypeError; string modalities use SUBSTRING membership rather than list membership; non-object JSON root reaches catalog.get unvalidated. Processing-before-writes still holds, so nothing is corrupted. Fix: validate rule collections as lists of tables, JSON root + model entries as mappings, modalities as lists of strings, all → CatalogError. (Missing limit/cost already harmless; non-string whitelist elements and non-table defaults.custom-params already correctly rejected.)

5. MINOR — Override fields `input-image-format` and `image-generation-api` are accepted + type-validated (models_catalog.py:55–56) but applyFilters deliberately discards them (:783–806); since extras bypass overrides, these fields have NO effective target anywhere. Fix: carry both through ModelSpec + emission, or reject them in overrides and document as extra-model-only; add a test proving every accepted override field affects emitted output.

6. MINOR — Explicit `Any` annotations (models_catalog.py:24, 135, 185–186; fetch_models.py:52, 167–183) violate the project's no-`Any` hard rule; pyright basic passing does not establish compliance (socially enforced). Fix: recursive JSON/TOML value types, `object` at unvalidated boundaries, TypedDicts/narrowed types after validation.

Test gaps + stale-link findings already recorded separately (memories 52a9e250, 90fe1130): model-url-template 0% coverage, fixture↔shipped-catalog drift (name-only drift guard), tier-only override never through main(), stale docs/archive link to the deleted openrouter-models-free.toml.

Spec conformance verdict (6 points): all conform at shipped-catalog level. Nuances: all-or-nothing holds for provider-processing failures but is NOT filesystem-transactional (mid-write I/O failure can leave earlier files changed); AGENTS.md conventions partial due to `Any` (finding 6). Gates: `./venv/bin/pytest tests/scripts/test_fetch_models.py -v` 31/31 passed (1.09s); `make lint` clean (pyright 0 errors/0 warnings); the suggested tomllib round-trip one-liner was permission-blocked (see opencode-permissions memory) — the tracked-catalog test independently tomllib-parses all configs/00-defaults TOMLs instead.

title: Catalog ↔ runtime interplay: enabled=false skips before provider lookup; missing enabled=true; openrouter/free standalone entry
content:
Verified (2026-09-14 catalog review) facts about how generated configs/00-defaults/*-models.toml catalogs interact with the runtime (lib/ai/manager.py::_initModels, lines 145–204):

- **Check ordering is load-bearing**: models with `enabled = false` are skipped BEFORE the provider-availability check (manager.py:172–184). Consequence: the 27 enabled=false opencode-go entries + the fully-commented-out providers.toml opencode-go block coexist with ZERO "Provider opencode-go not available" startup warnings. The disabled-by-default catalog and the commented provider block depend on each other — don't change one without the other.
- A model entry WITHOUT `enabled` resolves to True (manager.py:172). This is why the absorbed `openrouter/free` extra-model entry (openrouter-models.toml:59–69, carrying its own provider+model_id since it no longer merges with a tracked base entry) stays live and bot-defaults chat-model="openrouter/free" keeps working after the openrouter-models-free.toml deletion.
- Emitted keys map exactly to runtime readers: provider/model_id/model_version/context/customParams ← manager.py:176–180; support_* flags ← extraConfig (manager.py:194 → lib/ai/abstract.py:816–829, getInfo at 822–827). Tier gating sites: internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py:321, configure.py:545/723.
- Tier trap re-confirmed: _MODEL_TIERS (models_catalog.py:38) is exactly the hyphenated model-appropriate subset of ChatTier (internal/bot/models/chat_settings.py:50–61); ChatTier.fromStr (:145–157) returns None for underscore variants (bot_owner → model silently invisible in the picker). The generator validates tiers and the underscore trap is asserted (test:308–309).

title: Gate-1 review fixes: validation stance + emitter hardening decisions (model-catalog)
content:
Implementation decisions formed for the Gate-1 6-finding fix session on the model-catalog feature (scripts/models_catalog.py + scripts/fetch_models.py, uncommitted at the time):

1. **Lenient-null / strict-wrong-type validation stance** (Finding 3): upstream `limit: null` and `modalities: null` are treated as ABSENT (default context 32768 / model skipped as non-text) rather than CatalogError — chosen deliberately so regeneration of live models.dev data can keep the mandated date-only git diff (a live model with null limit would otherwise break `--all`). Non-dict non-null shapes (`limit: "big"`, `modalities: "text"`, `modalities.input: null`) raise CatalogError naming provider+model. modalities.input/output null IS a CatalogError (finding explicitly required it).
2. **Phase A verified behavior** (Finding 3 "verify what Phase A did"): absent `modalities.input` was already treated as `[]` → model SKIPPED as non-text — NOT `["text"]` as the finding's parenthetical guessed. Kept as-is. String modalities previously used substring membership (`"text" in "text,image"`) — now a type error.
3. **Unknown [[extra-models]] keys are NOT rejected** (Finding 1): extra models are emitted verbatim by design ("bypass filtering"), so only known fields are schema-validated: name/provider/model_id required non-empty str; tier via _validateTier; context int with EXPLICIT bool rejection (bool subclasses int); enabled/support_tools/support_text/support_images/support_structured_output bool; model_version str; customParams table of scalars or lists of scalars (None rejected — formatTomlValue cannot emit it); input_image_format list[str]; image_generation_api non-empty str. Errors name the model: `[[extra-models]] '<name>': '<field>' must be …`.
4. **tomllib validity gate placement** (Finding 2): in `fetch_models.processProvider` immediately after `emitCatalog`, raising `CatalogError("Provider '<name>': rendered catalog is not valid TOML: …")` so the error names the provider AND propagates through main()'s CatalogError catch, preserving all-or-nothing writes.
5. **Finding 5 decision: CARRY THROUGH** input_image_format / image_generation_api into ModelSpec (optional fields, None = omit from emission); emitted after `support_structured_output`, before `tier`. `_CANONICAL_MODEL_KEYS` left untouched (extra-model emission keeps alphabetical append — no change to current data).
6. **`_validateTier` signature changed to return str** so `tierRules: List[Tuple[str, str]]` needs no cast after validation.
7. **model-url-template parse-time validation** (extra item): `string.Formatter().parse` must yield exactly `["model_id"]` field names (duplicates, `{}`, `{0}`, `{name}`, literal-only all rejected; `{model_id!r}`/format-specs pass — field-name check only); malformed template ValueError → CatalogError "not a valid format string". Errors name the provider.
8. **Test-suite hygiene rule from Finding 4**: the fixed drift test must assert the SPECIFIC diagnostic ("drift guard" phrase), not just exit code 1 — a config-rejection can exit 1 for the wrong reason. Drift-guard stderr text: "Whitelist entries match no upstream model id (drift guard): ".

title: Gotchas: _TomlValue pyright invariance, sorted() provider order, TOML control chars, wrong-reason test passes
content:
Non-obvious gotchas hit while planning the Gate-1 fixes for scripts/models_catalog.py / scripts/fetch_models.py:

1. **Pyright List/Dict invariance vs the recursive `_TomlValue` alias**: with `_TomlValue = Union[None, bool, int, float, str, List["_TomlValue"], Dict[str, "_TomlValue"]]` (replaces Any per project hard rule), `List[str]` is NOT assignable to `List[_TomlValue]` (invariance), so every isinstance-validated string list needs `cast(List[str], value)` — in `_stringList`, `_modalityList`, `_stringListValue`; `_requireRuleList` needs `cast(List[Dict[str, _TomlValue]], value)`; `extractProviderSection` needs a cast for the models dict. Test calls like `formatTomlValue(["a", "b"])` may also trip this (annotate the list as `List[_TomlValue]` if pyright flags it) — verify empirically with `make lint`. Plain `Union` + string forward refs works at runtime (typing stores ForwardRef lazily); no datetime needed in the alias.
2. **No-Any narrowing pattern for parse-validated override fields**: generic helper `def _fieldValue(fields: Dict[str, _TomlValue], key: str, expectedType: type[_T]) -> _T` (TypeVar; isinstance check raising CatalogError) + `_stringListValue(fields, key) -> List[str]` (cast inside). Caveat: `isinstance(True, int)` is True — the bool rejection for `context` must stay explicit at parse time; the generic int helper would accept bools.
3. **`fetch_models --all` iterates sorted(provider names)**: "opencode-go" < "openrouter" ('c' < 'r'). To test "earlier successfully rendered provider stays unwritten when a later provider fails", name the providers alpha (valid) / zulu (drift-guard failure) — with the real provider names the failing one could sort FIRST and prove nothing.
4. **TOML basic strings prohibit U+0000–0008, U+000A–001F, U+007F**: escape `\t` `\n` `\r` with named escapes, all other control chars as `\uXXXX` (lowercase hex fine; TOML ABNF allows either case). Replace backslash/quote first, then `str.translate(_TOML_ESCAPE_MAP)` (translate only maps listed codepoints, so introduced backslashes are safe).
5. **Comment normalization order matters**: replace `"\r\n"` → `" "` BEFORE lone `"\n"`/`"\r"`. Normalize not just model displayName/url but ALSO header comment interpolations (sourceUrl, providerKey, regenerateCmd) — TOML basic strings in the filters file can legally contain `\n` escapes that would inject an uncommented line.
6. **False-positive test trap (Finding 4 root cause)**: the original `test_whitelistMissFailsWritingNothing` wrote filter fields at the document root with no `[providers.openrouter]` table, so `loadFiltersConfig` rejected the file for a missing `[providers]` table BEFORE the whitelist logic ran — exit 1 for the wrong reason. Always assert the specific error phrase, not just exit code.
7. **Existing test `test_extraModelsBypassFilters` must be updated**: its inline extra model has only name+tier; the new schema validation requires provider/model_id. Tests file already uses `Any` liberally (established convention there) and Finding 6 scopes the no-Any cleanup to the two scripts only. `badRoot: Any = [...]` style is the accepted way to feed wrong-typed input into an API whose declared type is a dict.

title: kw_only dataclass field trick: defaulted field required mid-dataclass before non-default fields
content:
Dataclass rule "non-default argument follows default argument" blocks placing a defaulted Optional field mid-dataclass before non-default fields. Hit when the Gate-1 brief required ModelSpec.inputImageFormat/imageGenerationApi (default None) BETWEEN supportStructuredOutput and tier (both non-default) in scripts/models_catalog.py.

Solution: `field(default=None, kw_only=True)` (Python 3.10+, repo targets 3.12+) — kw_only fields are exempt from the ordering rule and excluded from positional binding entirely. Import `field` from dataclasses.

Safety precondition: tests never construct ModelSpec directly (specs come from the applyFilters pipeline), so changing __init__ positional arity is risk-free HERE — but any future direct construction must pass these fields as keywords. Check for direct positional constructions before applying the same trick elsewhere.

title: _TomlValue recursive alias: four pyright cast sites when eliminating Any
content:
Replacing `Any` with a recursive value alias (`_TomlValue = Union[None, bool, int, float, str, List["_TomlValue"], Dict[str, "_TomlValue"]]`, models_catalog.py:31) under pyright basic hits four error patterns, all needing `cast`:

1. Assigning `_TomlValue` dict values to narrowed locals (int/bool/str) — pyright infers the local's type from first assignment and flags later incompatible assignments. Fix: `cast(int, fields["context"])`, `cast(bool, ...)`, etc. at the applyFilters override-application loop (~11 casts). Justification: `_validateOverrideValue` already type-validated at parse time, so casts restate validated types.
2. List invariance: `List[_TomlValue]` is NOT assignable to `List[str]` even after `isinstance(raw, list) and all(isinstance(item, str) ...)` narrowing — pyright narrows to `List[_TomlValue]` only. Fix: `cast(List[str], raw)` after the validation check (in `_stringList`, `_modalitiesList`).
3. `dict()` overloads reject the `_TomlValue` union argument — cast the INNER value first: `dict(cast(Dict[str, _TomlValue], fields["customParams"]))`, not `cast(Dict[str, _TomlValue], dict(x))`.
4. Reverse invariance: `List[str]` is not assignable to `_TomlValue` (List[str] vs List[_TomlValue] member) at emission — `formatTomlValue(cast(List[_TomlValue], spec.inputImageFormat))`.

The recursive alias itself is fine: string forward-refs inside `Union[...]` at module level become lazy ForwardRefs (no runtime resolution needed), and pyright supports recursion through List/Dict type arguments. `from __future__ import annotations` is irrelevant to the runtime Union expression but harmless.

title: TOML comments: newline-normalized only; exotic control chars caught by pre-write gate, not sanitized
content:
Deliberate scope decision from the Gate-1 fix round (brief-prescriptive): generated-TOML comment lines (`# {displayName}` / `# {url}` in emitCatalog) get ONLY newline normalization (`\r\n`/`\n`/`\r` → single space via `_singleLine`). Other control chars (e.g. `\x0b`, `\x1b`) in upstream display names are NOT stripped and would make the output invalid TOML (tomllib rejects control chars in comments other than tab).

Design backstop: the pre-write `tomllib.loads` gate in fetch_models.main catches this → clean `error: <provider>: generated TOML invalid: <msg>`, exit 1, nothing written — rather than silently sanitizing. String VALUES are fully safe either way (`_escapeTomlString` escapes all control chars as \uXXXX).

If upstream data ever actually contains exotic control chars in names, the decision point is: extend `_singleLine` to strip/replace them, or keep relying on the gate's fail-fast. Discovered via smoke test that initially (incorrectly for the value path) put \x0b in displayName; the gate caught it exactly as designed.

title: test_whitelistMissFailsWritingNothing was broken-by-luck: generic "error:" assert masked a wrong-reason pass
content:
Discovered 2026-09-14 while strengthening the weak assertion in `tests/scripts/test_fetch_models.py::TestFetchModelsCli::test_whitelistMissFailsWritingNothing` (Gate-1 fix loop): the test was passing for the WRONG reason. Its filters fixture lacked the `[providers]` wrapper table (top-level keys only), so `main()` exited 1 on "Filters file ... has no [providers] table" — and the old generic `assert "error:" in captured.err` passed without the drift guard ever executing. The review memory 52a9e250 had listed this test's "all-or-nothing empty-dir-on-failure" as verified-good; that verdict was partly illusory.

Fix: fixture rewritten to use `[providers.openrouter]` (correct shape), so the drift guard genuinely fires; assertions now check the exact diagnostic `"match no upstream model id (drift guard)"` plus the offending id `no/such-model`.

Lessons (generalizable):
1. Generic error-marker assertions (`"error:"` in stderr) can mask tests that fail for an unintended reason — strengthen them to assert the SPECIFIC diagnostic substring; strengthening is what exposed this.
2. Task/bug briefs paraphrase error strings ("matched no models") — the real message at `scripts/models_catalog.py:907` is `"Whitelist entries match no upstream model id (drift guard): "`. Always read the source for exact wording before asserting substrings.

title: test_fetch_models.py authoring patterns: json.loads for pyright invariance, kw_only ModelSpec, patch emitCatalog at lookup site, sorted --all order
content:
Patterns established/confirmed 2026-09-14 while adding 16 tests to `tests/scripts/test_fetch_models.py` (all pyright-clean under `make lint`):

1. **Hand-built catalog/model dicts must go through `json.loads(...)`.** `applyFilters`/`extractProviderSection` take `Dict[str, _TomlValue]` (invariant value type); a Python literal like `{"bad": {"name": "B"}}` infers `Dict[str, Dict[str, str]]` and pyright (basic, enforced by make lint) rejects it. `json.loads` returns `Any`, which short-circuits invariance. Same trick for `ModelSpec(customParams=...)`: annotate the local as `Dict[str, Any]`. (Consistent with the golden-suite `Dict[str, Any]` convention in memory 6025799f.)

2. **Construct `ModelSpec` all-keyword.** `inputImageFormat`/`imageGenerationApi` are `kw_only=True` dataclass fields, and `tier`/`customParams` sit after them in field order, so positional construction past `supportStructuredOutput` is impossible in practice.

3. **Patch `emitCatalog` at its lookup site via monkeypatch's string-target form**: `monkeypatch.setattr("scripts.fetch_models.emitCatalog", lambda *args, **kwargs: "[unterminated")`. `scripts/fetch_models.py` imports the function directly into its namespace (`from scripts.models_catalog import ... emitCatalog`), so patching `scripts.models_catalog.emitCatalog` would NOT affect the CLI path. The pre-write `tomllib.loads` gate then rejects invalid rendered text before any write.

4. **Provider processing order in `--all` mode is `sorted(filtersRaw)` by section key.** For CLI all-or-nothing tests, name the healthy provider's key so it sorts FIRST (e.g. `openrouter` < `zdrift`), making the failure occur after a successful render but before any write — a stronger proof than failing-first. Prove byte-preservation by pre-seeding output files with sentinel bytes (`b"sentinel-A"`) and re-reading after `main()` returns 1.

5. **`_parseSection(_openrouterSection(""))` yields a minimal real FilterConfig** suitable for direct `emitCatalog([spec], config, ...)` calls with hand-built specs (escaping round-trip tests etc.). Fixtures-config-level malformed shapes are tested by appending scalar keys (`tier-rules = 1`, `overrides = false`, `extra-models = "x"`) to a valid section text.

Accepted-but-broken templates that pass parseFilterConfig then raise at `.format()` (:957) with a NON-CatalogError: `{model_id:{slug}}` → KeyError, `{model_id!q}` → ValueError (unsupported conversion), `{model_id:d}` → ValueError. fetch_models.py:319 catches only CatalogError, so the CLI emits a traceback instead of the promised config diagnostic; the pre-write tomllib gate cannot help (render never completes); existing output files stay untouched. title: doc_section_edit CAS rule: expected_text = COMPLETE section flat body; blank-line damage confirmed on 4/4 edits
content:
2026-09-14 docs-writer session (model-catalogs.md creation) confirmed two operational rules for markdown-mcp `doc_section_edit`:

1. **CAS semantics: `expected_text` must be the section's COMPLETE flat body exactly as `doc_read` serves it — not just the fragment being changed.** Two consecutive `expected_text mismatch` failures occurred when passing only the lines to be altered; the edit only succeeded once the full body (everything between the anchor heading and the next sibling heading, verbatim) was supplied as `expected_text` with the full replacement in `new_text` (op=replace). title: string.Formatter().parse() semantics: validate the full 4-tuple, not just field names
content:
Validating a str.format template by checking only field names from `string.Formatter().parse()` is insufficient — templates with format specs or conversions pass such validation but crash later at `.format()` time with KeyError/ValueError (NOT the app's CatalogError), producing a traceback instead of a config diagnostic.

`Formatter().parse(template)` yields 4-tuples `(literal_text, field_name, format_spec, conversion)`:
- Bare field `{model_id}` → format_spec is `""` (empty string), so truthiness (`if formatSpec`) correctly detects specs.
- Numeric spec `{model_id:d}` → format_spec = `"d"` (ValueError at format time on strings).
- Nested spec `{model_id:{slug}}` → format_spec = `"{slug}"` (KeyError 'slug' at format time).
- Conversion `{model_id!q}` → conversion = `"q"`. CRITICAL: parse() does NOT validate the conversion character — any single char after `!` is accepted at parse time; the ValueError only surfaces at `.format()` time.
- Literal `{{` braces → field_name is None (skip in validation loops).

Correct validation shape: iterate all four components; raise when `fieldName != "model_id" or formatSpec or conversion is not None`; track a `sawModelId` flag for the at-least-one requirement. Implemented in `_validateUrlTemplate` in scripts/models_catalog.py.

title: tomllib temporal types break _TomlValue; _validateTomlValue guard must take `object`, not the alias
content:
In scripts/models_catalog.py, the `_TomlValue` alias (`Union[None, bool, int, float, str, List["_TomlValue"], Dict[str, "_TomlValue"]]`) accurately describes json.loads output, but **tomllib additionally produces datetime.date / datetime.time / datetime.datetime for TOML temporal literals** — e.g. `custom-params = { when = 1979-05-27 }` parses to `datetime.date`. These temporal values flow through validation untouched and crash the TOML emitter with a raw TypeError. Free-form customParams values are therefore guarded by a recursive validator `_validateTomlValue(value, where)` applied at all three parse-time boundaries (`[defaults] custom-params`, `[[overrides]] custom-params`, `[[extra-models]] customParams`): only None/bool/int/float/str/list/str-keyed-dict allowed, recursing into list items and dict values, raising CatalogError naming `where`.

Typing decision: the `value` parameter is declared **`object`, NOT `_TomlValue`**. Declaring `_TomlValue` would let pyright narrow the union exhaustively through the isinstance cascade, making the final `raise` provably unreachable — risking reportUnnecessaryIsInstance / unreachable-code diagnostics (strict-mode landmines even though the project runs pyright basic). `object` accepts any runtime value, keeps every isinstance check legitimate, and honestly signals "validating an unknown-shape parsed value". Reuse this pattern for any future parse-time value validators in this module.

title: Pathspec-scoped commit required when concurrent workstream has pre-staged index changes
content:
Trap hit 2026-09-14 during a mechanical commit arc in the shared Gromozeka working tree: a concurrent model-catalogs workstream had in-flight changes, and `git status --porcelain` showed `D  configs/00-defaults/openrouter-models-free.toml` — the deletion was ALREADY STAGED in the index (first-column `D`) by the other workstream.

Trap: after `git add`-ing only your own paths, a plain `git commit` commits the ENTIRE index, silently sweeping the foreign staged deletion into your commit — violating "commit ONLY the named paths" and mutating the other workstream's staging state.

Fix: pathspec-scoped commit — `git commit -m "..." -- <your paths>`. This commits only the named paths (taking their working-tree content) via temporary-index machinery and leaves ALL other staged entries staged and untouched. Verified post-commit: `git status --porcelain` still showed `D ` for the foreign file, intact.

Extension of commit-scope validation (cf. memory 7520ce60): when validating scope before a commit in a shared tree, read the INDEX first column for every path, not just your own file list. Any first-column status code on a path you didn't touch means foreign staged content will ride into a plain commit. Unstaging the foreign change is NOT an option (it mutates workstream state) — the pathspec commit is the correct tool.

title: Gotcha: customParams nested dicts/lists pass validation but crash the TOML emitter
content:
Gate-2 finding 1 (IMPORTANT, 2026-09-14, still open) in scripts/models_catalog.py: validation and emission disagree on nested customParams shapes.

- `_validateTomlValue()` ACCEPTS nested dicts and lists containing dicts. Both `custom-params = { tools = [{ name = "t", args = ["a", 1, true] }] }` and `custom-params = { reasoning = { effort = "low" } }` pass parse-time validation; the nested-list shape is even enshrined in `test_customParamsNestedTablesAndListsValid` (tests/scripts/test_fetch_models.py:401).
- But `_customParamsLines()` flattens only the OUTER dict, and `formatTomlValue()` raises `TypeError("Unsupported TOML value type: dict")` for any dict it encounters — including dicts inside lists. Emission runs BEFORE the tomllib round-trip gate, and the CLI's per-catalog error handler catches only `CatalogError` → the user gets a raw traceback instead of a configuration diagnostic.
- Root-cause class: a config the tooling explicitly validates as valid can crash generation — same lesson as the finding-7 URL-template case (memory d3b27d67): validation must cover everything the emitter will subsequently do with the value.
- Fix options: (a) extend `formatTomlValue()` to serialize string-keyed dicts as recursive TOML inline tables while keeping the dotted `customParams.*` outer keys, or (b) reject unsupported nesting in `_validateTomlValue()` and document the restriction.
- Test gap to close with the fix: the existing nested-shape test stops after parsing — the regression must run applyFilters → emitCatalog → tomllib.loads and assert exact nested-value preservation.

title: test_fetch_models.py pyright pattern 3: cast for deliberately-unassignable invalid values
content:
Extends memory 013dfb86's `tests/scripts/test_fetch_models.py` pyright patterns (found 2026-09-14, Gate-2 final correction round). Third pattern: to unit-test that a runtime value which validation forbids (e.g. a `datetime.date` sneaking past `_validateTomlValue`) raises `CatalogError`, the bare literal fails pyright — `"date" is not assignable to "_TomlValue"` — because the alias deliberately excludes temporal types. Do NOT use `# pyright: ignore`; wrap with `cast(_TomlValue, datetime.date(...))` (import `cast` from typing; `Any` is banned repo-wide). Working example in `TestFormatTomlValue.test_formatTomlValueScalarsListsAndInlineTables`:

```python
with pytest.raises(CatalogError, match="Unsupported TOML value type: date"):
    formatTomlValue(cast(_TomlValue, datetime.date(1979, 5, 27)))
```

Rationale: `cast` expresses "type-unsafe value that should have been caught at validation" without weakening the type alias or reaching for `Any`. Related: memory 65d728c2 (why temporal types are excluded from `_TomlValue`).

title: markdown-mcp doc_search: top_k no longer guaranteed count; snippets shorter-not-longer — benchmark harness implications
content:
Two behavior changes in markdown-mcp post-v1.8.0 (landed 2026-09-15, unreleased) that any doc_search/search consumer — especially the search-quality benchmark harness — must account for:

1. **top_k is no longer a guaranteed result count.** After the (file_path, slug) merge dedup, "lists may come back shorter than top_k when distinct keys are exhausted" (their playbook/skill docs were corrected in commits 21722b6/e2b9d7f "correct top-K guarantee after dedup"). A `doc_search top_k=3` may legitimately return 2 results; harnesses must tolerate shorter lists instead of treating them as failure.

2. **Snippets are cut at boundaries, never longer.** From the 200-char cut the snippet backtracks to the last sentence/line boundary within 50 chars, else last whitespace, else hard cut; 150-char floor when a boundary is taken; results can only get SHORTER than v1.8.0. Mid-answer 200-char cuts should disappear, but rank-1 snippets will NOT get longer.

Benchmark re-run expectations: the slot-crowding issue (same slug filling all k slots) should be fixed; raw scores unchanged (same flat 0.88–0.92 band, ~0.006 margins — score separation was explicitly parked as "not actionable by calibration", see decision memory on post-v1.8.0 changes).

title: Native-edit junction repair leaves MCP index line-map off-by-one until next reindex
content:
Refinement of the doc_section_edit junction-blank repair workflow (memories 7d3ebbe8, dd4ec8b0): the in-call reindex fired by doc_section_edit captures the PRE-repair bytes. A subsequent native `edit` repair of the eaten junction blank changes disk bytes WITHOUT reindexing, so the MCP index's line map for that file goes stale by the number of inserted lines — off-by-one for a single blank-line repair (e.g. doc_outline/doc_read report the appended section at lines 131-157 while the file actually has it at 132-158).

Impact is bounded: content, section boundaries, and embeddings are unaffected; doc_lint returns [] and does not flag the disk/index sha drift. Accept as a known cost of the batch-then-repair path; it resolves on the next indexing pass. Do NOT re-run doc_section_edit just to refresh line numbers — that re-eats the junction blank.

title: Missing/invalid model tier → owner-only via new ChatTier.resolveModelTier (silent-invisibility bug fixed)
content:
Implemented 2026-09-19 (developer session). Models whose `tier` config value is missing or invalid (e.g. `"bot_owner"` with underscore, which `ChatTier.fromStr` rejects) are NO LONGER silently invisible everywhere — they resolve to `bot-owner` (owner-only visibility), with a logged warning for invalid values. This resolves the latent-bug consequence described in memory 12b5e92e and the pending "abstract.py default" flag; `fromStr` itself is UNCHANGED (still returns None for underscore variants) — only consumers changed.

**Single resolver:** new classmethod `ChatTier.resolveModelTier(modelName: str, tierStr: str) -> ChatTier` in `internal/bot/models/chat_settings.py` (~160-188). Contract: empty/whitespace tier → `BOT_OWNER` silently (documented default, NO warning); valid → parsed normally; invalid non-empty → `logger.warning("Model 'X' has invalid tier 'Y'; treating as 'bot-owner'")` + `BOT_OWNER`. Never returns None (that's why consumer `modelTier is None` branches were deleted). Coerces via `str(tierStr or "").strip()` so non-str/None config values don't crash.

**Four consumer sites routed through the resolver (3 known + 1 discovered):**
1. `internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py:~321` — `getChatSettings` MODEL/IMAGE_MODEL gate.
2. `internal/bot/common/handlers/configure.py:~545` — ConfigureKey picker filter.
3. `internal/bot/common/handlers/configure.py:~723` — `chatConfiguration_SetValue` selection validation (revert only when chat tier < resolved model tier now).
4. **Discovered during implementation:** `ConfigureCommandHandler.__init__` selectable-models filter used `modelInfo.get("tier", None)` TRUTHINESS — it dropped tier-less models from `selectableModels` entirely, which would have silently defeated desired behavior #1 (missing tier = owner-visible) even after fixing sites 1-3. Now also calls the resolver; tier-less models stay selectable (gated at display time), invalid tiers warn at startup.

**`lib/ai/abstract.py`:** `getInfo()` tier default fixed `"bot_owner"` → `"bot-owner"` (line 827; docstring spots ~796 and ~812) — tier-less models now parse cleanly end-to-end.

**Deliberately NOT routed through the resolver (different semantics — chat-tier strings, not model tiers):** `base.py:286/377/380` (`BASE_TIER`/`PAID_TIER` from chat settings), `scripts/check_condensing.py:250/255/260`. Unrelated enums: `MessageCategory.fromStr`, `MarkupType.fromStr`. `scripts/models_catalog.py` only documents the gotcha in a comment (its `_MODEL_TIERS` set is catalog-generation validation, no runtime parse) — no change.

**pyright note:** return type is `-> "ChatTier"`, NOT `-> Self` — pyright rejects `return cls.BOT_OWNER` as `Self` (`Literal[ChatTier.BOT_OWNER]` not assignable to `Self@ChatTier`); `fromStr`'s `Optional[Self]` only works because it returns the `cls(...)` result directly.

**Tests (written FIRST, all failed on unfixed code — 6 × AttributeError resolveModelTier, 8 × visibility/warning assertions; 3 characterization guards passed):** `TestResolveModelTier` in `tests/bot/models/test_chat_settings.py` (6 cases); NEW `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_configure.py` (picker visibility + SetValue revert/accept); `TestGetChatSettingsModelTierFilterRegression` appended to `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_base.py` (getChatSettings keeps/drops model settings). Suite: 4649 passed / 11 skipped (= 4632 baseline + 17 new). Docs synced: CHANGELOG.md Fixed entry; `docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md:203` durable-gotcha bullet rewritten to the resolved state.

title: ConfigureCommandHandler test-construction pattern: patch 4 getInstance singletons, return Mocks alongside typed handler
content:
Established 2026-09-19 in the new `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_configure.py` (no prior configure-handler test file existed). Pattern for constructing `ConfigureCommandHandler` with all service deps mocked, satisfying pyright basic mode:

1. **Patch all four singleton `getInstance` classmethods** — `patch.object(CacheService, "getInstance", return_value=cacheMock)`, same for `QueueService`, `StorageService`, `LLMService` (llmServiceMock with `getLLMManager = Mock(return_value=llmManagerMock)`). Keeping the Mock references lets you configure methods later WITHOUT reassigning typed handler attributes (`handler.cache`/`handler.llmService` are inferred as the real service types; assigning Mocks to them trips pyright).
2. **Helpers return the Mock collaborators explicitly** — e.g. `-> Tuple[ConfigureCommandHandler, Mock, AsyncMock]` returning `(handler, cache, editMessageMock)`. pyright REJECTS `return handler` where `Mock` is declared, and rejects inspecting `.await_args`/`.await_args_list` through real method attributes — so pass the captured AsyncMock/returned cache Mock directly to assertion helpers. (`Mock`'s class is not assignable to/from the handler class in either direction.)
3. **`# type: ignore[method-assign]`** when overriding real handler methods post-construction: `handler.editMessage = AsyncMock(return_value=True)`, `handler.getChatSettings = AsyncMock(...)`, `handler.getChatInfo`, `handler.getChatTitle` (established pattern, also in test_llm_messages.py — see memory 1b4fa968).
4. **Production `await`s cache.setChatSetting** → the cache Mock needs `cache.setChatSetting = AsyncMock(return_value=None)`, a plain auto-Mock raises `TypeError: 'Mock' object can't be awaited`. Assert reverted/accepted values via `cache.setChatSetting.await_args.args[2].value` (positional: chatId, key, ChatSettingsValue).
5. **"No warning" assertions need a clean model catalog:** `ConfigureCommandHandler.__init__` now calls `ChatTier.resolveModelTier` while building `selectableModels`, so constructing a handler whose catalog contains an invalid-tier model emits the startup warning into `caplog` BEFORE the test body runs. title: Tier-rescue review verdict: FAIL — resolveModelTier silently normalizes whitespace-padded valid tiers
content:
2026-09-19 read-only code review (code-reviewer agent) of the tier-rescue fix (the fix documented in memory e02bd612) returned **FAIL** — one IMPORTANT open finding supersedes the "verified" status of that fix for one behavior.

**Bug:** `ChatTier.resolveModelTier(modelName, tierStr)` (`internal/bot/models/chat_settings.py` ~lines 178-183) applies `.strip()` to `tierStr` and parses the STRIPPED value. Result: a whitespace-padded but otherwise valid tier string — `" free "`, `"paid\n"` — silently resolves to FREE/PAID with NO warning. But `ChatTier.fromStr(" free ")` (unstripped) returns None, and the spec says every present-but-invalid string (including padded) must fall back to BOT_OWNER with a `logger.warning` naming the model and the raw value. Impact: a malformed tier intended to be owner-only becomes visible to free chats.

**Correct fix shape:** strip ONLY for emptiness detection, parse the ORIGINAL string:
```python
if tierStr is None or not tierStr.strip():
    return cls.BOT_OWNER
tier = cls.fromStr(tierStr)
```
keeping the existing invalid → BOT_OWNER + warning fallback. If None is an intentional input, annotate the parameter accordingly.

**Why gates didn't catch it:** targeted suite green (49 tests pass), `make lint` clean, `make check-docs` clean (148 files / 2937 links / 0 broken) — but there is no padded-input coverage. Add resolver test cases for `" free "`, `"paid\n"`, whitespace-only, and None before re-approval.

title: Tier-rescue review gotchas: tests bypass constructor filter, None→\"None\" at configure.py:102, new Any annotations
content:
Secondary findings from the 2026-09-19 tier-rescue review (main FAIL finding recorded separately):

1. **Regression-test gap — tests bypass the constructor filter.** Tests in `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_configure.py` (~185-187 picker, ~311-313 set-value) overwrite `handler.selectableModels` AFTER constructing the handler. Consequence: reverting the `__init__` selectable-models filter to the old `.get("tier")` truthiness gate would NOT fail these tests. Fix: add an integration-style test that uses the constructor-generated `selectableModels`. Also, constructor warnings stay in caplog during later assertions — for consumer-warning tests, clear captured logs after construction and assert the warning came from the specific consumer path.

2. **None-tier inconsistency at `configure.py` ~102.** The `__init__` filter stringifies a None tier to `"None"` before calling the resolver → emits a startup warning, while direct resolver calls with None take the silent missing-tier path (`tierStr or ""`). Inconsistent defensive handling; pass the raw value through. Low priority: TOML has no native null.

3. **No-`Any` rule applies to tests too.** The new test helpers introduced `Dict[str, Any]` annotations (`test_configure.py` ~14 and ~44; `test_base.py` ~23 and ~1657), violating the project convention. Use a small TypedDict payload with optional `tier` + capability fields, or concrete types. Existing production `Any` annotations need not be refactored in the same change.

**Confirmed clean in the same review (verified facts):** all four consumer sites (configure.py __init__ ~96-103, picker ~549-553, set-value ~726-731, base.py ~321-325) correctly route through the resolver with `isBetterOrEqualThan`, `isSetByBotOwner` bypass, and configure owner-elevation intact; free/paid visibility unchanged. No runtime consumer depends on the old `"bot_owner"` default literal in `lib/ai/abstract.py` `getInfo()` (remaining underscore hits are tests/diagnostics/docs only). 17 new test instances confirmed (6 resolver, 7 configure, 4 base) and they assert real visibility + caplog warning content, not just no-crash. title: Handler-test patterns: constructor-state testing, caplog phase attribution, never str() a possibly-None .get()
content:
Reusable lessons distilled from the Gate-1 review of the tier-rescue fix (2026-09-19; fix record = memory ea58c950) — applicable to any future handler test in this repo:

1. **Post-construction attribute replacement hides constructor regressions.** If a test helper does `_makeHandler(...)` and then replaces an attribute the constructor built (e.g. `handler.selectableModels = [...]`), no test can detect a regression in `__init__`'s own logic (e.g. reverting the selectable-models filter to the old truthiness-only gate). Every handler whose constructor filters/derives state needs at least ONE integration-style test that uses the constructor-generated state with mocked deps and never replaces the attribute post-construction. Site: `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_configure.py::test_constructorSelectableModels_includeMissingAndInvalidTierModels`.

2. **Attribution of duplicate warnings via `caplog.clear()`.** Handlers can log the same warning at two phases — constructor (startup validation) and consumer paths (picker/set-value). A consumer-warning test that only does `caplog.at_level(...)` may pass off the constructor's warning instead of the path under test. Call `caplog.clear()` after handler construction/mocking, right before the `with caplog.at_level(...)` act block. Applied in `_collectButtonTexts` and `_selectModel` helpers of test_configure.py.

3. **Never wrap a possibly-None `.get()` result in `str(...)` at a call site.** `str(modelInfo.get("tier", ""))` turns a `None` tier into the literal string `"None"`, defeating any downstream Optional-aware handling and producing spurious warnings ("has invalid tier 'None'"). Pass the raw value and widen the callee signature to `Optional[str]` when it must treat None as missing — this is exactly what `ChatTier.resolveModelTier(modelName, tierStr: Optional[str])` now does. The other call sites (configure.py picker ~552, set-value ~731, base.py ~321) already passed raw `.get("tier", "")` values.

title: Model-catalog price comments landed: cost→# Price comment rules + regeneration report
content:
Price-comments extension to the model-catalog generation feature implemented 2026-09-19 (developer session, uncommitted, docs/CHANGELOG deliberately deferred to a separate phase, no commits). Extends the lineage of memories 1aa2be13/bf8097ea/Gate-2.

**Feature**: generated catalogs carry an informational `# Price: $X in / $Y out per 1M tokens [(cache read: $Z)]` comment per model when models.dev provides usable `cost` data. Prices are COMMENTS ONLY — the runtime `[models.models]` TOML schema is untouched (no price fields).

**Landed in `scripts/models_catalog.py`:**
- `ModelSpec.priceComment: Optional[str] = field(default=None, kw_only=True)` — placed between `imageGenerationApi` and `tier` (same kw_only-Optional pattern as the other optional fields).
- `_formatCompactNumber`: `f"{value:.6f}".rstrip("0").rstrip(".")` with `"0"` fallback → 0.150000→`0.15`, 3→`3`, 0→`0`.
- `_buildPriceComment` suppression rules (informational, never raises — deliberately unlike `limit` which raises on malformed):
  - `cost` must be a dict; missing/non-dict → no comment (silent).
  - Both `cost.input` AND `cost.output` required: numeric (int/float, bool excluded) and >= 0. Negative side → treated as absent (variable-pricing convention) → no comment. Partial (one side only) → no comment.
  - `cache_read` appended as ` (cache read: $…)` only when present, numeric, and > 0.
  - Zero-cost ($0/$0) DOES emit a comment (accurate: free).
- `emitCatalog` emits `# {priceComment}` routed through `_singleLine()` AFTER displayName/url comment lines, immediately above the table header. Extra-models are emitted verbatim and never get price comments.

**Live regeneration 2026-09-19** (`./venv/bin/python3 scripts/fetch_models.py --all`): openrouter-models.toml 22/22 and opencode-go-models.toml 27/27 models got Price comments — NO whitelist/opencode-go model lacked cost upstream. `openrouter/free` → `$0 in / $0 out`. Verified diff vs pre-regeneration snapshot: only `# Fetched:` timestamps + `# Price:` lines. Gates: `make format lint` clean; `make test` 4659 passed / 11 skipped (baseline 4653 + 6 new).

title: Regeneration diff verification: snapshot working tree first — git diff vs HEAD has pre-existing drift
content:
Gotcha for verifying `./venv/bin/python3 scripts/fetch_models.py --all` regeneration output (learned 2026-09-19 during price-comments work): `git diff` on configs/00-defaults/*-models.toml vs HEAD is USELESS for proving "only date + expected lines changed" because the catalog files are routinely already modified (MM) in the working tree relative to HEAD — upstream models.dev data drifts between HEAD and the last regeneration, so the HEAD diff contains large unrelated churn (added/removed models, changed tiers, etc.) that predates the current session.

Correct technique: BEFORE regenerating, snapshot the working-tree catalogs (`cp configs/00-defaults/{openrouter,opencode-go}-models.toml /tmp/...`), run the regeneration, then plain `diff` against the snapshot. That isolates exactly what THIS regeneration changed. Diff exit code 1 is expected (differences exist); inspect hunks: date-only regeneration shows a `5c5` hunk on the `# Fetched:` line; feature additions show only `NNaMM` hunks of added `# Price:` lines.

To map comments→models afterwards, extract `(following-table-header, price-line)` pairs from the regenerated files rather than parsing diff line numbers.

**ANOMALY RESOLVED — openrouter/free**: the implementer report listed `openrouter/free → $0 in / $0 out`, which seemed to contradict "extras are emitted verbatim, no derived comments". Finding: `openrouter/free` is NO LONGER an extra-model — it is a whitelisted upstream model in the CURRENT scripts/models-filters.toml (whitelist entry at ~L31, `free` tier at ~L66–68), and the old `[[extra-models]]` block (~L71–81) is entirely commented out.
