A stale explanatory comment inside the commented-out extras block (~L70) predates the delta.

**Finding 1 (IMPORTANT, blocking)** — scripts/models_catalog.py ~L723–734 + ~L686: `_buildPriceComment` accepts ANY non-bool int/float. Consequences: NaN passes the `>= 0` checks → `$nan`; +inf → `$inf` (incl. cache suffix); oversized int like `10**400` passes validation but `f"{v:.6f}"` raises OverflowError → aborts catalog generation, violating the "malformed cost → silently absent, never raises" contract. All reachable via legit `json.loads` input (NaN literal, `1e400`, 401-digit ints). Suggested fix: after the existing bool/type check, `try: if not math.isfinite(raw): return None / except OverflowError: return None`; keep invalid-input/output (whole-comment suppression) and invalid-cache (suffix omission) as separate outcomes; regression tests for NaN, inf, exponent overflow, oversized ints in both required and cache fields. NOT observed in shipped data — upstream robustness issue only.

**Finding 2 (RECOMMEND, non-blocking)** — tests/scripts/test_fetch_models.py ~L903–916: the malformed-cost test's `assert all(spec.priceComment is None for spec in specs)` is vacuous-pass-prone (also passes if filtering returns zero models). Fix: assert the six expected model names first; extend cache edge coverage (0, negative, bool, string, null) and malformed output values.

**Judged clean / non-blocking**: bool-exclusion precedes numeric acceptance; negative input/output → whole comment suppressed; missing/partial/string/null/non-dict cost → suppressed; zero cost valid; cache ≤ 0 → suffix omitted. Emission (~L1288–1294) places comment after displayName/url, before table header, via `_singleLine()`, emits nothing on None; extras unchanged; tomllib round-trip unaffected; all 6 new tests assert exact strings; no existing assertion changed. Conventions clean (camelCase, type hints, Args:/Returns: docstrings, no new Any/emojis). Catalog diff: all 49 price comments (22 openrouter + 27 opencode-go) adjacent to their model headers, no orphans; opencode-go diff vs index = Fetched date + comments only; openrouter diff also contains the acknowledged out-of-scope membership drift — implementer's "only comments + dates" snapshot comparison accepted as reported evidence, not independently reproduced (pre-regen snapshot unavailable).

**Small-price rounding (accepted, monitor)**: `_formatCompactNumber` collapses 1e-7 → "0" and rounds 0.0000015 → "0.000002" — lossy but non-blocking since prices are USD per 1M tokens and no real catalog price approaches sub-micro-dollar. Revisit only if such prices appear (keep scientific notation or more decimals below 1e-6).

title: Gotcha: json.loads admits NaN/inf/oversized ints — type+sign checks alone can't make cost formatting never-raise (`.6f` OverflowError)
content:
Root-cause analysis behind review finding 1 on `_buildPriceComment` (scripts/models_catalog.py ~L723–734, formatting at ~L686) — applies to ANY code path validating numeric fields parsed from JSON before formatting them.

Mechanics:
1. **`json.loads` accepts NaN/Infinity/−Infinity literals** by default (Python's json decoder is non-strict here), and `1e400` parses to `float('inf')`. So "malformed" upstream cost data can legally be non-finite floats even though the JSON spec forbids them.
2. **Type-only validation is insufficient**: a plain `isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not isinstance(v, bool)` check plus `v >= 0` lets NaN through (`nan >= 0` is False, but the negative-check pattern `v < 0 → reject` doesn't catch NaN if written as `not (v >= 0)`... in this codebase the check was `>= 0` gating, and NaN comparisons are all False, so it slipped through) and lets +inf through (inf >= 0 is True).
3. **Huge ints break fixed-point formatting**: `f"{10**400:.6f}"` raises `OverflowError` because float-formatting an int converts it to float first (max ~1.8e308). A 401-digit integer is VALID JSON, so an unvalidated `int` cost field can crash generation with a traceback instead of the intended silent suppression.

Contract violated: "malformed/missing cost → comment silently absent, never raises" — an exception here aborts the whole catalog generation.

Fix pattern (apply at the validation boundary, once for each of input/output/cache fields):
```python
try:
    if not math.isfinite(raw):
        return None  # or omit suffix for cache field
except OverflowError:
    return None
```
placed AFTER the `isinstance(v, bool)` exclusion and int/float acceptance, BEFORE negative checks. Keep the two suppression outcomes separate: invalid input/output → suppress entire comment; invalid cache_read → omit only the ` (cache read: $…)` suffix.

Regression coverage needed: NaN, +inf, `1e400`, and ~10**400 int in each of input, output, and cache_read positions. Related hardening precedent in this repo: memory d3b27d67 (validate full format-spec tuples, not just field names) — same theme: validate at the boundary against everything `.format`/f-string evaluation can raise.

title: doc_section_edit CAS valid across sibling-section edits; blank-eating 3/3 again
content:
2026-09-19 docs-writer session (3 section edits, extends memories 1b836dfd + dd4ec8b0):

1. **Blank-eating reconfirmed on 3/3 boundaries**: `doc_section_edit` op=replace consumed the blank line between the edited section body and the NEXT heading every time (model-catalogs.md §2.2→`### 2.3`, §3 trailing `---`→`## 4.`, teamlead-memory bullet→next `##` heading). Detection: outline line-ranges shift but only NATIVE reads reveal the missing blank. Repair: plain native `edit` inserting the blank works and survives (never repair via doc_section_edit — its normalization re-eats it, per a9a57832).

2. **NEW: section-body CAS stays valid across edits to OTHER sections in the same file.** `expected_text` anchors on the section's flat body text, not the file sha256 — a CAS fetched from `doc_read` before an earlier `doc_section_edit` can be reused for a second, untouched section of the same file (used successfully for §3 of model-catalogs.md after §2.2 was replaced). The per-file `sha256` in doc_read responses DOES change after each edit; only the body-CAS is stable for untouched sections. Parallel edits to different files are safe; serialize edits within one file to keep anchor resolution predictable.

3. Untracked-file caveat held: `git diff -U0` shows nothing for newly created files (model-catalogs.md was untracked), so native reads are the only verification channel for boundaries.

title: test_fetch_models.py: inline filter sections insulate the suite from real-filters/fixture drift; collision detection covers only included specs
content:
Why adding fixture models doesn't break tests (verified 2026-09-19: 57/57 passed with zero adjustments after adding `openrouter/free` to the fixture):

1. The suite never runs the REAL `scripts/models-filters.toml` against the fixture. It uses inline sections — `_FULL_OPENROUTER_SECTION` and `_CLI_FILTERS_TOML` — that deliberately whitelist only ids present in the fixture and model `openrouter/free` as an `[[extra-models]]` verbatim entry (no cost → no price comment) instead of a whitelisted upstream model. So fixture additions that only the real filters whitelist perturb no assertion, and `test_noCostModelsGetNoPriceComment`'s exact price-comments dict is unaffected.
2. Collision detection scope (models_catalog.py): `[[extra-models]]` name collisions are checked against `nameToModelId`, which maps final names of INCLUDED (whitelisted) upstream specs only, plus upstream-vs-upstream collisions among included specs. A non-whitelisted upstream id sharing an extra-model's name does NOT collide. This is why fixture `openrouter/free` + inline extra-model `openrouter/free` coexist peacefully.
3. Confusion trap: `anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5` is whitelisted ONLY in the test's inline section, NOT in the real filters — so the real dry-run legitimately omits claude-haiku (9 models), and its absence from dry-run output is correct, not a bug.
4. Stale comment: the inline-section comment "the real file's whitelist matches the fixture, so this is byte-for-byte the same rule set" (~line 134-136) stopped being true once the real filters gained `openrouter/free` + wildcard entries; it's comment-only drift, unfixed under the minimal-touch mandate.

title: fetch_models.py drift guard: exact-id miss = hard error, glob miss = stderr warning; *:free blacklist does not match openrouter/free
content:
Drift-guard severity asymmetry in `scripts/models_catalog.py` applyFilters (confirmed 2026-09-19 by the offline dry-run): only EXACT (wildcard-free) whitelist ids that match no upstream model id hard-error ("Whitelist entries match no upstream model id", exit 1, nothing written). Whitelist/blacklist GLOB entries with zero matches merely print stderr warnings — e.g. the offline fixture run warns about `qwen/qwen3.8-*`, `*:free`, and `deepseek/deepseek-*-pro*` — expected and non-fatal.

fnmatch nuance: blacklist glob `*:free` does NOT match upstream id `openrouter/free` — fnmatch requires the literal `:` before "free", and the router id uses `/` — which is precisely why the free-router id survives the per-model `:free` blacklist while genuine `vendor/model:free` variants are excluded. The `tier = "free"` in the generated catalog comes from the `[[providers.openrouter.overrides]] match = "openrouter/free"` override in `scripts/models-filters.toml`, not from any fixture field.

title: Verifying regenerated model catalogs with no committed baseline: snapshot-diff technique
content:
2026-09-19 (tier-rules removal session): The model-catalog feature files (scripts/fetch_models.py, scripts/models_catalog.py, scripts/models-filters.toml, and the generated configs/00-defaults/{openrouter-models,opencode-go-models}.toml) sit uncommitted in the working tree for long stretches (git status was a mix of `A`/`MM`/`AM`). Two consequences worth remembering:

1. **Regeneration proof needs a snapshot, not git diff.** `git diff` cannot establish a "before" state for regenerated catalogs — there is no committed baseline. Technique: BEFORE running `./venv/bin/python3 scripts/fetch_models.py --all`, copy the generated TOMLs to a temp dir; after regeneration, `diff` snapshot vs regenerated. For a filter-pipeline-only change the expected drift is ONLY the `# Fetched:` timestamp line per file, with byte sizes identical (9619 / 9921 at the time). Any other diff means the pipeline change altered catalog content — investigate before claiming "date-only".

2. **Git-diff hunk attribution gotcha.** A plain `git diff scripts/models-filters.toml` shows staged-vs-worktree hunks that may contain PRE-EXISTING uncommitted work from earlier sessions (e.g. the extra-models comment rewrite visible in the tier-rules session diff). Don't attribute such hunks to the current session's change when writing handoffs, reviews, or changelog entries — check which hunks the session actually produced.

Related: offline pipeline exercise without network — `./venv/bin/python3 scripts/fetch_models.py --provider openrouter --api-url tests/scripts/fixtures/models_dev_api.json --dry-run` (exit 0 expected). Distinct from memory 71e750f7 (dirty-tree "only this file changed" acceptance) — that one concerns file-attribution via git diff; this one concerns content-diff of generated artifacts.

title: Config-driven script recipe (flavor 2): argparse + bootstrapProxy + Database init + _load_env.sh mechanics
content:
Consolidated, verified 2026-09-19 recipe for a NEW script that must read the merged TOML config (ConfigManager) and/or the DB via the config-driven path — i.e. flavor 2 from memory 91d23ab9. (Flavor 1 maintenance scripts: positional `dbPath` + raw sqlite3; do not mix.) Audited from `check_structured_output.py`, `run_llm_debug_query.py`, `reproduce_llm_dialog.py`, `check_condensing.py`.

## Argparse convention
- Module constant `_DEFAULT_CONFIG_DIRS = ["configs/00-defaults", "configs/local"]`; main() falls back via `args.configDirs or _DEFAULT_CONFIG_DIRS`.
- `--config-dir`: `action="append", dest="configDirs", metavar="DIR"` (repeatable).
- `--dotenv-file`: `default=".env"`.
- Extract `buildParser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser` as a module-level function so tests exercise the parser without sys.argv. `RawDescriptionHelpFormatter` + exit-code epilog. camelCase `dest`s.

## Canonical header order (run_llm_debug_query.py)
shebang → docstring (Usage/Exit codes) → stdlib imports → repo-root sys.path shim (`_REPO_ROOT = str(Path(__file__).parent.parent.resolve())`) → logging silencing → `import httpx2; httpx2.alias_httpx()` → project imports (`# noqa: E402`) → `from scripts._lib.bootstrap import bootstrapProxy`.
The `alias_httpx()` call MUST be made by the script itself, directly before its first project import — importing `scripts._lib.bootstrap` is too late because isort sorts `scripts._lib` after `internal.*`/`lib.*` (see memory c186ed64).

## Exact init sequence (`async def main() -> int`, tail `sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))`)
```python
configManager = ConfigManager(
    configPath="config.toml",  # may not exist; dirs take precedence
    configDirs=configDirs,
    dotEnvFile=args.dotenv_file,
)
bootstrapProxy(configManager)  # REQUIRED before any proxy-consuming service (LLMManager, Database w/ sqlink, httpx clients)

db = Database(
    configManager.getDatabaseConfig(),  # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType] — returns raw [database] TOML dict, not DatabaseManagerConfig
)
cache = CacheService.getInstance()
await cache.injectDatabase(db)
```
`ConfigManager.__init__` signature: `(configPath="config.toml", configDirs: Optional[List[str]] = None, dotEnvFile=".env")`.

## Negative facts (prevent wrong assumptions)
- There is NO `database.path` config key — the SQLite path lives at `[database.providers.default.parameters] dbPath = "bot_data.db"`.
- No script under `scripts/` uses StorageService.

## Shell side
- `scripts/_load_env.sh` (sourced by every `run-*.sh` after `cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."`): consumes `--env=NAME` out of the caller's `$@` via `shift` (so `--env=foo` never reaches the python script), sources `.env.NAME` (default `.env`) under `set +x`, defaults `CONFIGS="local"`, exports `ENV_FILE` and `CONFIG_DIRS` (built as `--config-dir ./configs/<v>` flags). Never pass arguments to the `.` command — the loader mutates the caller's `$@` directly.
- Canonical wrapper body: `./venv/bin/python scripts/<name>.py --dotenv-file "$ENV_FILE" --config-dir ./configs/00-defaults $CONFIG_DIRS $@` — defaults always included, user args appended last, `$@` UNQUOTED (current wrappers as of Sep 2026; older memory cbab12f4 showed `"$@"` quoted).
- New wrapper = byte-for-byte copy of an existing `run-*.sh` with the script name swapped (e.g. `scripts/run-migrate-models.sh`).

Cross-refs: cbab12f4 (shebang/shim/wrapper basics), 91d23ab9 (two flavors), 66eabbf8 (bootstrapProxy call sites), c186ed64 (alias-ordering follow-up idea).

title: Model-holding ChatSettingsKey members: 11 MODEL/IMAGE_MODEL keys + EMBEDDING_MODEL is STRING (skips validation)
content:
Mapped 2026-09-19 (read-only research for a model-id maintenance script). All config keys that hold model ids:

**11 catalog-model settings keys** (all on `ChatSettingsPage.LLM_MODELS`, typed `ChatSettingsType.MODEL` or `IMAGE_MODEL`), string values: `chat-model`, `fallback-model`, `summary-model`, `summary-fallback-model`, `image-parsing-model`, `image-parsing-fallback-model`, `image-generation-model`, `image-generation-fallback-model`, `condensing-model`, `memory-refine-model`, `memory-refine-fallback-model`. Defaults in `configs/00-defaults/bot-defaults.toml:173-183` (`[bot.defaults]`); the real deployment values live in the overlay `configs/common/01-bot-defaults.toml` (`[bot.defaults]` :3-54, `[bot.tier-defaults.{banned,free,free-personal,paid,friend}]` :78-151 — 00-defaults' own `[bot.tier-defaults.free]` is empty). Never hardcode TOML paths — read the merged view via `ConfigManager.getBotConfig()` (defaults / `<type>-defaults` / `tier-defaults`), mirroring `HandlersManager.__init__` (internal/bot/common/handlers/manager.py:459-489).

**GOTCHA: `ChatSettingsKey.EMBEDDING_MODEL` (`embedding-model`) is typed `ChatSettingsType.STRING` (chat_settings.py:1177-1182), NOT MODEL/IMAGE_MODEL** — so it does NOT get the model-availability validation in `BaseBotHandler.getChatSettings` (base.py:316 filters on MODEL/IMAGE_MODEL types only). Maintenance scripts that enumerate "model settings" must handle it separately. (Page assignment of embedding settings already covered by memory 1689f7bc.)

**Out of scope:** `[stt] model = "general"` (configs/00-defaults/stt.toml:15) is a Yandex SpeechKit model name, not a `[models.models]` catalog id — exclude from model-id migration.

Enumerate model-typed keys programmatically: filter `getChatSettingsInfo()` (internal/bot/models/chat_settings.py:1224-1235) by `meta["type"] in (ChatSettingsType.MODEL, ChatSettingsType.IMAGE_MODEL)`.

title: Runtime model availability = getModelInfo(name) is not None; reusable API surface with signatures
content:
Surveyed 2026-09-19. **A model id is "available at runtime" iff `name ∈ llmManager.modelRegistry`, equivalent to `llmManager.getModelInfo(name) is not None`.** There is NO `getAvailableModels()`/`isModelAvailable()` helper — tier gating is done ad hoc at each call site.

Registration rules (`LLMManager._initProviders` lib/ai/manager.py:99-143, `_initModels` :145-204, registry write :200): a model is registered only if (1) `enabled != false` in the merged `[models.models]` table, (2) its `provider` names an initialized provider (known `type` + constructor succeeded — missing API key ⇒ whole provider skipped), (3) `provider.addModel()` doesn't raise. All failure causes are indistinguishable via the public API (all → `None`) — exactly what an availability checker wants to flag.

**Reusable surface:**
- `LLMManager.listModels() -> List[str]` (lib/ai/manager.py:206-212); `getModel(name) -> Optional[AbstractModel]` (:214-231); `getModelInfo(name) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]` (:233-244)
- `AbstractModel.getInfo() -> Dict[str, Any]` (lib/ai/abstract.py:777-829) returns: `provider` (CLASS name, e.g. "OpenrouterProvider"), `model_id` (UPSTREAM id, not the app key), `model_version`, `customParams`, `context_size`, `support_tools/text/images/structured_output/embeddings`, `tier` (raw config string, default "bot-owner"), `extra`
- `LLMService.getLLMManager()` (internal/services/llm/service.py:1622-1630); `LLMService.resolveModel(modelKey, *, chatSettings, defaultKey)` (:1632-1661; three resolution paths already in memory 099ffb0d)
- `ChatSettingsValue.toModel()` (chat_settings.py:624-641) **raises ValueError** on unknown model
- Construction chain: `ConfigManager.getModelsConfig()` (internal/config/manager.py:334-348) → `LLMManager(modelsConfig, statsStorage=...)` at main.py:121-125 → `LLMService.getInstance().injectLLMManager(...)`

**Tier gating:** `ChatTier.resolveModelTier(modelName, tierStr) -> ChatTier` (chat_settings.py:160-191) — `None`/blank/invalid tier string silently → `BOT_OWNER`; compare with `chatTier.isBetterOrEqualThan(modelTier)` (:115-124). ChatTier order: BANNED < FREE < FREE_PERSONAL < PAID < FRIEND < BOT_OWNER; catalog tier strings restricted to `{free, paid, friend, bot-owner}` (scripts/models_catalog.py:50).

**Capability filtering in the /configure picker** (ConfigureCommandHandler, internal/bot/common/handlers/configure.py): selectable universe built once at init (:92-106); per-key filter requires `support_text` for MODEL keys, `support_images` for IMAGE_MODEL keys, plus tier check (:533-571); set-time validation re-checks tier and value must be an index into `selectableModels` (:717-738). There is no free-text /model command — the picker is the only write path, so DB rows with out-of-picker ids come from older catalogs.

Per-chat validation point: `BaseBotHandler.getChatSettings` base.py:316-325 — `getModelInfo(...)` is `None` ⇒ per-chat value silently dropped, falls back to default (merge layering itself already covered by memories 07499b18/4e9a7503).

title: DB surfaces holding model ids: chat_settings, models (embedding provenance), stat_events label mismatch
content:
For model-id migration/usage-count scripts (complements existing chat_settings rename gotchas in memories a30cda8c/05f48544/12cdbec3):

**1. `chat_settings` table** — `(chat_id, key, value, updated_by, updated_at, created_at)`, PK `(chat_id, key)` (upsert: internal/database/repositories/chat_settings.py:44-82). Usage counts: `SELECT key, value, COUNT(*) FROM chat_settings WHERE key IN (<11 MODEL/IMAGE_MODEL keys + embedding-model>) GROUP BY key, value`. Precedent maintenance script: `scripts/prune_unknown_chat_settings.py` (direct sqlite3, stop-the-bot/TOCTOU discipline, `--dry-run`, transactional update).

**2. `models` embedding-provenance table (migration_025)** — `(model_id INTEGER PK, model TEXT, dimensions INT, created_at)`, `UNIQUE(model, dimensions)`; repo internal/database/repositories/embedding_models.py:79-165 (`getOrCreateModelId` is the allocation point). Referenced by `user_memories.model_id` and `chat_messages.model_id` — renaming an embedding model id must update `models.model` AND account for `dimensions` (a rename that changes dimensions changes embedding-provenance lookups).

**3. BIG GOTCHA — stat_events labels do NOT carry app-level model keys:** `llm_request` stat rows record `modelName`/`modelId` labels BOTH set to the **upstream `model_id`** (e.g. `"deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1"`, not the catalog key `"openrouter/deepseek-chat-v3.1"`), and the `provider` label holds the provider **class name** (e.g. `"OpenrouterProvider"`), not the config provider name (lib/ai/abstract.py:949-959; `_recordEmbeddingStats` :986-1007). Per-model usage counts from stats therefore require joining through the catalog mapping `[models.models."key"].model_id → key`, not string equality with config keys.

title: Model-ID storage map in DB: chat_settings + models + stat tables
content:
Complete map of where model IDs live in the SQLite DB (researched 2026-09-19 for a model-migration maintenance script):

**Primary store — `chat_settings`** (migration_001; `updated_by INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` added in migration_010): columns chat_id INTEGER, key TEXT, value TEXT, updated_by, created_at/updated_at (app-set); PK (chat_id, key). Repo `internal/database/repositories/chat_settings.py` ChatSettingsRepository: `setChatSetting(chatId, key, value, *, updatedBy)` via `provider.upsert(conflictColumns=["chat_id","key"])`, `getChatSettings(chatId) -> Dict[str, tuple[str, int]]` (key → (value, updated_by)), `getChatSetting`, `unsetChatSetting`, `clearChatSettings`.

**12 model-holding ChatSettingsKey values** (enum `internal/bot/models/chat_settings.py`, cross-checked against `_chatSettingsInfo` types): chat-model, fallback-model, summary-model, summary-fallback-model, image-parsing-model, image-parsing-fallback-model (type MODEL); image-generation-model, image-generation-fallback-model (type IMAGE_MODEL); condensing-model, memory-refine-model, memory-refine-fallback-model, embedding-model.

**Other locations:**
- `models` lookup table (migration_025): model_id INTEGER PK (app-generated, NOT AUTOINCREMENT), model TEXT, dimensions INTEGER, UNIQUE(model, dimensions). Embedding-provenance registry. Repo `internal/database/repositories/embedding_models.py`: `getOrCreateModelId(model, dimensions, *, dataSource)`, `getModelById`, `listModels`.
- `chat_messages.model_id` + `user_memories.model_id` — nullable INTEGER FKs to models.model_id (post-025), not the string.
- `stat_events.labels` JSON: modelName/modelId labels for event_type='llm_request' (written by `lib/ai/abstract.py` _recordAttemptStats ~:949-959 and _recordEmbeddingStats ~:988-994, both from `getInfo()["model_id"]`); STT events carry a "model" label (Yandex STT model name, from `lib/stt/providers/yandex_speechkit.py:351`).
- `stat_aggregates.labels` JSON + labels_hash; PK (event_type, period_start, period_type, labels_hash, metric_key); metric_key values include request_count, input_tokens, output_tokens, total_tokens, generation_text.

**Verified NOT to contain model ids:** `cache` table (only USERS + CHAT_PERSISTENT namespaces persist; CHAT_PERSISTENT holds spam warnings only; the CHATS namespace containing settings is MEMORY_ONLY, never persisted), chat_users.metadata, divinations, media_attachments, delayed_tasks.kwargs, spam/ham_messages, settings (migration tracking only). **Dropped tables — do not target:** user_data (022), chat_stats/chat_user_stats (027), message_embeddings (025). vec0 virtual tables partition by integer model_id — irrelevant for string-id renames.

title: chat_settings.value is plain TEXT — exact-match UPDATE for model migration
content:
`chat_settings.value` stores the model-id string as plain TEXT — no JSON, no wrapper (verified 2026-09-19 via write chain: BaseBotHandler.setChatSetting at internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py:334 → CacheService.setChatSetting at internal/services/cache/service.py:543 calls `value.toStr()` → repo upsert; ChatSettingsValue.__init__ normalizes with `str(value).strip()` at internal/bot/models/chat_settings.py:553; convertToSQLite in lib/db/providers/utils.py passes str through).

**Consequence for model-id migration scripts:** exact-match UPDATE is correct — `UPDATE chat_settings SET value = :newModel, updated_at = :now WHERE key IN (...) AND value = :oldModel` — no substring matching or JSON rewriting needed. `.strip()` in the writer guarantees no surrounding whitespace in stored values.

**Exception — JSON columns:** `stat_events.labels` / `stat_aggregates.labels` are `libUtils.jsonDumps`-encoded dicts (params converted via convertToSQLite). If model ids must be rewritten there, do read–parse–rewrite in Python (project convention), never SQL string REPLACE or JSON1 functions (non-portable, forbidden by AGENTS.md). Label values equal the id string exactly (modelName/modelId keys), so a JSON-aware Python rewrite is safe.

title: Per-model usage counts: stat_aggregates + Python JSON parsing, never SQL JSON
content:
How to compute per-model usage counts (researched 2026-09-19 for the model-maintenance script):

**Project convention:** zero JSON filtering in SQL — `lib/stats/analysis.py` module docstring: "All analysis happens in pure Python — no SQL label filtering" (json_extract is SQLite JSON1 → non-portable, forbidden).

**LLM usage per model** (same path as /stats command): query `stat_aggregates` with plain WHERE, parse labels JSON in Python:
```sql
SELECT labels, metric_value FROM stat_aggregates
WHERE event_type = :eventType    -- 'llm_request'
  AND metric_key  = :metricKey   -- 'request_count' (also input_tokens, total_tokens, generation_text)
  AND period_type = :periodType  -- 'total' = all-time bucket
```
then group by `json.loads(labels)["modelName"]`. In-code precedent: `internal/bot/common/handlers/stats.py:1208` — `analyzer.topN("modelName", "request_count", top)`; row loader precedent `lib/stats/sql_storage.py:434-445`. Raw-events variant: `SELECT labels FROM stat_events WHERE event_type = :eventType` and count in Python.

**Embedding-model usage — fully portable plain SQL:**
```sql
SELECT m.model, COUNT(*) AS usageCount
FROM chat_messages cm JOIN models m ON m.model_id = cm.model_id
GROUP BY m.model
```
(same shape for user_memories).

**Per-model chat_settings usage:** `SELECT key, value, COUNT(*) FROM chat_settings WHERE key IN (:k0, ...) GROUP BY key, value` over the 12 model keys.

**Caveats:** stats recording is best-effort and gated by `[stats] enabled` config; processed stat_events rows are subject to retention cleanup — stat_aggregates 'total' buckets survive. **"is-available" is NOT in the DB** — it comes from the models TOML catalog via LLMManager (`lib/ai/manager.py`, `enabled` key, `listModels()` / `getModelInfo(name)` from `configManager.getModelsConfig()`). Related known gotchas (existing memories): labels_hash is unusable for partial label filtering; must exclude labels["consumer"]=="__global__" rollup rows to avoid double-counting.

title: Standalone script DB access: raw sqlite3 vs Database() provider stack + migration hook
content:
Two established DB-handle patterns for standalone scripts (full map researched 2026-09-19; the raw-sqlite3-is-sanctioned decision itself was already recorded earlier — this adds the full-staff alternative and the migration-hook gotcha):

**Pattern A — raw sqlite3** (all chat_settings maintenance scripts): `scripts/prune_unknown_chat_settings.py` is canonical — `sqlite3.connect(str(dbPath), isolation_level=None)`, sqlite_master existence guard, manual BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK, `--dry-run` flag, TOCTOU "stop the bot first" warning in module docstring. Also `scripts/clear_memory_embeddings.py:246`, `scripts/delete_stopwords.py`. Tests call `processDatabase(dbPath, dryRun=...)` on a temp DB (tests/scripts/test_prune_unknown_chat_settings.py).

**Pattern B — full provider stack** (when repositories needed), precedent `scripts/check_condensing.py:434-447`:
```python
configManager = ConfigManager(configPath=..., configDirs=..., dotEnvFile=...)
bootstrapProxy(configManager)                      # scripts/_lib/bootstrap.py — ProxyHelper singleton MUST init first
db = Database(configManager.getDatabaseConfig())   # use as async ctx manager
```
Test-exact sequence (tests/conftest.py:98-133):
```python
config: DatabaseManagerConfig = {"default": "default", "chatMapping": {},
    "providers": {"default": {"provider": "sqlite3", "parameters": {"dbPath": <path>}}}}
db = Database(config); ... ; await db.manager.closeAll()
```

**Config keys:** `[database] default = "default"`; `[database.providers.default] provider = "sqlite3"`; `[database.providers.default.parameters] dbPath = "bot_data.db"` (configs/00-defaults/00-config.toml:41-52). `ConfigManager.getDatabaseConfig()` (internal/config/manager.py:270) returns the DatabaseManagerConfig TypedDict (lib/db/manager.py:28).

**Gotcha:** `Database.__init__` registers `migrateDatabase` as a provider-init hook — the first `getProvider()` runs pending migrations. If the script must not mutate schema, use Pattern A.

**StorageService is unrelated** — it is media file storage (filesystem/s3/null backends under internal/services/storage/backends/), NOT the SQL database. Never needed for DB scripts.

title: Renaming embedding-model id in chat_settings alone orphans embedding provenance
content:
When migrating/renaming the `embedding-model` chat setting value, renaming only `chat_settings.value` is NOT enough to keep the system consistent (identified 2026-09-19 during model-migration research):

EMBEDDING_MODEL ids are materialized as `models` table rows (`model` TEXT + integer `model_id` PK, created lazily by `EmbeddingModelsRepository.getOrCreateModelId`). The integer `model_id` is referenced by `chat_messages.model_id`, `user_memories.model_id`, and vec0 virtual-table partitioning.

**Consequence:** if a migration renames the id in `chat_settings` alone, the next `getOrCreateModelId(oldModel, dims)` call under the new id allocates a fresh `models` row and ALL affected chats re-embed from scratch. Decide explicitly:
1. Also rename `models.model` (UPDATE models SET model = :new WHERE model = :old) → provenance counts stay continuous; or
2. Leave `models` alone → accept full re-embedding cost.

Either way, the string model id appears in TWO table families (chat_settings + models) plus the JSON labels in stat_events/stat_aggregates — a complete rename must address all three, or explicitly document why not.

title: migrate_models.py tool: invariants, exit codes, and Phase-2 test seam
content:
Created 2026-09-19: `scripts/migrate_models.py` (model report + model-id migration tool) and `scripts/run-migrate-models.sh` (755 wrapper, byte-for-byte run-check-structured-output.sh pattern). CHANGELOG entry added under [Unreleased] (new standalone scripts = feature, fetch_models.py precedent).

User-approved design decisions (scope-limiting; do not "improve" later):
- Availability is BINARY via `LLMManager.getModelInfo()` only — never diagnose unknown/disabled/provider-failed causes, never inspect the [models.models] catalog or TOML files for status.
- Config-reference scan uses MERGED config layers only (bot.defaults, bot.<type>-defaults, bot.tier-defaults.<tier> via getBotConfig()); never scan or name physical TOML files.
- `--migrate OLD NEW` is DRY-RUN by DEFAULT; `--apply` does ONE transaction: re-select preview → UPDATE value+updated_at → verify rowcount == preview (mismatch → ROLLBACK + exit 2) → COMMIT. `updated_by` never touched. OLD unavailable is fine (informational note); NEW unavailable → refuse (exit 1).
- Scope: only MODEL/IMAGE_MODEL chat settings (keys derived from getChatSettingsInfo() type filter — exactly 11 keys); `chat_settings` is the only table ever written; embedding models explicitly out of scope.

Exit-code contract: 0 ok; 1 validation/usage error; 2 apply count-mismatch rollback. `MigrationCountMismatchError` (module-level exception) carries the exit-2 path, caught in main.

Phase-2 test seam (tests pending in `tests/scripts/test_migrate_models.py`): pure importable helpers — `collectModelKeys()`, `collectLayerEntries(botConfig, modelKeys) -> List[Tuple[layerName, key, value]]`, `modelStatus(llmManager, value)`, `previewMigration(conn, old, modelKeys)`, `applyMigration(conn, old, new, modelKeys, nowStr)`, `findConfigReferences(botConfig, modelKeys, old)`, `collectDbUsage(conn, modelKeys)`, `resolveDbPath(dbConfig)`, module-level `buildParser()`. No ConfigManager/LLMManager construction at import time.

title: Verifying config-driven scripts: dbPath misdirection + connection-local TEMP TRIGGER
content:
Two verification traps hit 2026-09-19 while end-to-end testing `scripts/migrate_models.py` (both were tester errors, the script was correct):

1. **Config-driven dbPath misdirection**: the test config override dir still pointed `dbPath` at the original synthetic DB while I inspected a second (`race.db`) — two runs "behaved oddly" but were actually correctly operating on the first DB. Rule: when a script resolves file paths from config layers, confirm WHICH file the config actually resolved to before interpreting results; use a dedicated override dir per target DB.

2. **SQLite TEMP TRIGGER is connection-local**: `CREATE TEMP TRIGGER` exists only on the connection that created it. A race simulation built on the "preparing" connection was invisible to the script's own connection, so the trigger never fired and the run silently "passed" normally. To simulate a concurrent-write race for ANOTHER connection, use a PERSISTENT trigger in the DB file. Deterministic recipe: persistent `AFTER UPDATE ON chat_settings` trigger that DELETEs a row matching the migration filter before the UPDATE scan reaches it → in-transaction preview (N) ≠ UPDATE rowcount (N-1) → exercises the rollback + exit-2 path. Verify the DB is byte-identical after the rollback.

Useful companion technique: build a synthetic test env in temp — seeded sqlite DB with the real `chat_settings` shape + a temp config dir overriding only `[database.providers.default.parameters] dbPath` (and optionally a `[bot.tier-defaults.free]` layer to exercise config-reference output), then run the script with `--config-dir configs/00-defaults --config-dir <temp-override>`. No network calls occur (getModelInfo is a local registry lookup).

title: Raw-sqlite3 scripts must write timestamps as getCurrentTimestamp().isoformat()
content:
Complements the provider-layer timestamp memories (pass datetime objects to BaseSQLProvider; never isoformat INTO the provider). The inverse applies to RAW sqlite3 scripts (maintenance tools bypassing the provider, e.g. scripts/migrate_models.py, prune_unknown_chat_settings.py): there is no convertToSQLite in the path, so the script must pre-format the string itself.

Production `updated_at`/`created_at` values in the DB are what `convertToSQLite` produces: `getCurrentTimestamp().isoformat()` → tz-aware ISO-8601 like `2026-09-19T19:36:56.980926+00:00` (`getCurrentTimestamp` = `lib/db/utils.py:377`, returns `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`; repos also import it as `dbUtils`). Raw-SQL UPDATEs must write `getCurrentTimestamp().isoformat()` to match byte-for-byte — verified in the migrate_models --apply test.

title: ConfigManager sys.exit(1) bypasses except Exception; construct before relative dbPath resolution
content:
Two ConfigManager gotchas confirmed 2026-09-19 during the migrate_models.py review (extends the known os.chdir(rootDir) gotcha):

1. **`sys.exit(1)` bypasses `except Exception` guards.** `ConfigManager` calls `sys.exit(1)` directly on a missing bot token or TOML parse failure (`internal/config/manager.py:224-233`). `SystemExit` derives from `BaseException`, so a script's `except Exception` init guard does NOT intercept it — the process exits 1 with ConfigManager's own `logger.error` ("Bot token not found in configuration!") rather than the script's formatted init-failure message. Matters when smoke-testing standalone scripts without a populated `.env`.

2. **Ordering: construct ConfigManager BEFORE resolving a relative dbPath.** Because `ConfigManager.__init__` does `os.chdir(rootDir)` (root-dir = "storage"), a script that resolves `database.providers.default.parameters.dbPath` (= relative `bot_data.db`) must construct `ConfigManager` FIRST, then `Path(dbPath).exists()` / `sqlite3.connect()` — otherwise it checks/opens `./bot_data.db` instead of `storage/bot_data.db` (the file the bot actually uses). `migrate_models.py` does this correctly (init at ~785-789 before resolve/open at ~720-728).

title: channel-defaults: registered for all ChatType but resolution coerces non-private to GROUP
content:
Cross-file asymmetry in chat-settings channel defaults (confirmed 2026-09-19 while verifying migrate_models.py layer iteration):

- **Registration/defaults-loading** iterates ALL `ChatType` (`internal/bot/common/handlers/manager.py:470-478`), so a `bot.channel-defaults` TOML layer is real and appears in per-layer config reports (migrate_models.py Section A mirrors registration; its docstring is accurate).
- **Resolution-time behavior differs**: `internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py:267-271` coerces non-private chats to GROUP ("no full support for Channels defaults"), with separate channel-default copying in `updateChatInfo` (`base.py:1034-1044`).

Consequence: a `channel-defaults` entry shown in a config-layer report may reach chats through a different path than private/group-default entries — do not assume layer parity between a static report and runtime resolution. Also confirmed safe: `tierDefaults.get(chatTierEnumMember)` dict lookups work against plain-string TOML keys because `ChatTier` is a `StrEnum` (same pattern production uses at manager.py:486).

title: Standalone script init chain + raw-sqlite3 conventions (bootstrapProxy failure mode, timestamp equivalence)
content:
Confirmed 2026-09-19 during the migrate_models.py review:

- **`bootstrapProxy(configManager)` is load-bearing before `LLMManager(modelsConfig)`** in standalone scripts: without it, `ProxyConfig.getCombined()` raises inside each provider's `_initClient()`, so EVERY provider fails and `LLMManager` silently ends up with 0 models (looks like an empty catalog, not an error). Correct order: `ConfigManager` → `bootstrapProxy` → `LLMManager` (helper in `scripts/_lib/bootstrap.py`).
- **`LLMManager.getModelInfo(name)` returns None** for unknown models, disabled models (skipped at registration, manager.py:142-143), and provider-init-failures (logged-and-continued) — so a binary ok/unavailable report mark is exactly faithful to that single check; no cause distinction is possible without extra catalog/TOML inspection.
- **Raw-sqlite3 scripts must write `updated_at` as `getCurrentTimestamp().isoformat()`** — byte-identical to what the provider stores: repositories pass datetime objects and `convertToSQLite` serializes with `data.isoformat()` (`lib/db/providers/utils.py:64-65`); `getCurrentTimestamp()` = `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` (`lib/db/utils.py:377`).
- **SQL NULL semantics help migrations**: NULL `value` rows never match `value = :old`, so they are naturally excluded from both reporting and migration predicates — no special NULL handling needed.
- Raw sqlite3 (not the `Database` class) is the correct choice for maintenance scripts because `Database` runs pending migrations as a side effect.

title: migrate_models.py: report-mode DB problems nonfatal by design; Phase-2 tests exist

Final documented contract: 0 = success incl. partial report with DB section skipped with a note; 1 = validation/usage errors (OLD==NEW, NEW model unavailable, --apply without --migrate, missing/unusable DB in MIGRATION mode, init failure, unexpected runtime errors); 2 = apply aborted + rolled back (preview/update count mismatch). Lesson: when a CLI treats the same condition as fatal in one mode and nonfatal in another, per-mode exit-code docs must say so explicitly. title: In-process SQLite mid-UPDATE trigger race test: isolation_level=None required
content: Unit-test variant (pytest) of the persistent-trigger race recipe for `applyMigration` rollback verification (see earlier e2e recipe memory). Used in `tests/scripts/test_migrate_models.py` `TestApplyMigration.testCountMismatchRaceRollsBack`. Non-obvious requirements discovered 2026-09-19: (1) the temp-DB connection MUST be opened with `sqlite3.connect(path, isolation_level=None)` — the script issues manual BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK statements, which are silently ignored under Python's default deferred isolation and the rollback path can't be exercised; (2) create the PERSISTENT `AFTER UPDATE ON chat_settings` trigger on the SAME connection BEFORE calling applyMigration — created in autocommit, it survives the migration's ROLLBACK; (3) SQLite permits a trigger to DELETE from the same table being UPDATEd mid-scan, and the in-flight UPDATE skips rows deleted under it → rowcount (1) ≠ preview (2) deterministically → `MigrationCountMismatchError` → ROLLBACK restores both rows to the old value (assert with a post-failure re-preview). Trigger shape: `AFTER UPDATE` → `DELETE FROM chat_settings WHERE key = NEW.key AND value = '<OLD>' AND chat_id <> NEW.chat_id` (triggers take no parameters — embed the constant via f-string). Scratch-verify such trigger mechanics with a throwaway script via ./venv/bin/python3 BEFORE embedding in a test. Full SQL lives in the test file.

title: Deterministic DB race test: AFTER UPDATE trigger for count mismatch + assert rollback before connection close
content:
Deterministic race-testing pattern validated 2026-09-19 in `tests/scripts/test_migrate_models.py` (applyMigration count-mismatch test) — reusable for any DB invariant that depends on row counts under concurrency:

1. **Simulate the race with a SQLite `AFTER UPDATE` trigger, not timing/threads.** The trigger deletes the OTHER still-matching row on the first update, so the count mismatch fires regardless of which row the code under test visits first. Fully deterministic — no sleeps, no flaky scheduling. (Caveat: this tests race *semantics*, not real multi-connection contention — acceptable when the invariant is count-based.)
2. **Verify rollback on the SAME connection BEFORE closing it.** If rollback is only checked after `close()`, an implicit rollback-on-close can mask a missing explicit rollback in the code under test — the test would pass vacuously. Assert restored state while the connection is still open.
3. Require the specific exception (here `MigrationCountMismatchError`) explicitly, and separately assert the pre/post row state to prove the rollback restored everything.

Also from the same review: preview-selection tests should insert rows in scrambled order and assert an exact ordered tuple (not subset/loose checks), and apply-semantics tests should assert exact per-key counts plus preserved attribution columns (`updated_by`, `created_at`) and untouched out-of-scope rows read back via a fresh connection.

title: SQLite composite PK does not imply NOT NULL — fixture DDL must mirror production constraints exactly
content:
In SQLite, a single-column `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` (rowid alias) implies NOT NULL, but a **composite `PRIMARY KEY (a, b)` on an ordinary table does NOT** — PK columns stay nullable unless explicitly declared `NOT NULL` (only `WITHOUT ROWID` tables differ). Bitten 2026-09-19: the `chat_settings` fixture in `tests/scripts/test_migrate_models.py` (`_makeChatSettingsTable`) declared the composite PK without NOT NULL while production (migration_001 / migration_013 lineage) declares `chat_id INTEGER NOT NULL` + `key TEXT NOT NULL`.

Convention when writing test-fixture DDL that mirrors production migrations: **copy the production constraints verbatim** (NOT NULL, defaults), don't reconstruct from memory — a loose fixture silently accepts inserts production would reject, and a fixture tightened blindly can break tests. Before adding NOT NULL to a fixture, confirm every test insert supplies the constrained columns explicitly (here: all `_insertSetting` calls pass both PK columns, so the change was safe and no test needed edits).

title: doc_section_edit mechanics for inserting/renumbering sections with TOC

Practical mechanics learned inserting model-catalogs.md §4 (2026-09-19), complementing docs/docs-playbook/mcp-docs-workflow.md:

- Section bodies parsed by markdown-mcp include the trailing `---` horizontal-rule separator. `insert_after` places new_text right after the target section's body; the inserted text must start with its own `## N. Heading` and END with its own `---` to keep the separator cadence.
- After inserting, the MCP outline response shows the newly assigned slug immediately — check it against any TOC link you wrote BEFORE trusting the anchor (slugger gotchas: see the underscore/dot divergence memory).
- Renumbering existing sections: rename bottom-up (6→7, then 5→6, then 4→5) via `rename` op with `expected_title` taken from a fresh `doc_outline`; full-title slugs never collide at intermediate steps.
- Front-matter (`description:`) is NOT covered by section ops — `doc_write` overwrite replaces content after the front matter; edit the description line with the plain `edit` tool.
- Cosmetic whitespace (e.g. restoring the blank line after a `---` that an insert consumed) is also a plain-`edit` job — don't contort section ops for it.
- Large-section edits: `replace` requires the complete flat body exactly as served by `doc_read` (CAS). For a one-paragraph change to a long section, reproduce the served body verbatim with only the target paragraph modified.

title: Root cause of 4x 'Failed to initialize model unknown: provider' — stale enable-toggles in configs/common/10-openrouter.toml
content:
Diagnosed 2026-09-20 (research-only explore session, triggered by 4 identical `ERROR:lib.ai.manager:Failed to initialize model unknown: 'provider'` lines during `./scripts/run-migrate-models.sh --env=local-telegram`).

**Root cause — override-without-base drift.** `configs/common/10-openrouter.toml` contains bare enable-toggle entries (`[models.models."…"]` with ONLY `enabled = true`) whose base entries don't exist in the generated `configs/00-defaults/openrouter-models.toml` catalog (generated by `scripts/fetch_models.py` per `scripts/models-filters.toml`). The four `enabled = true` culprits:
- `openrouter/deepseek-chat-v3.1` (10-openrouter.toml:9-11) — no base anywhere in the 4 loaded dirs
- `openrouter/qwen3.5-flash` (:21-23) — no base
- `openrouter/qwen3.6-plus` (:29-31) — no base
- `openrouter/gemini-3-pro-image-preview` (:40-42) — DRIFTED KEY: base `openrouter/gemini-3-pro-image` exists at 00-defaults/openrouter-models.toml:122 under a different (renamed) id, so the toggle silently misses it

Three sibling toggles in the same file (`openrouter/claude-haiku-4.5`, `openrouter/qwen3-235b-a22b`, `openrouter/qwen3-vl-235b-a22b-instruct`, all `enabled = false`) are silently absorbed — the enabled-check (manager.py:172-174) runs BEFORE the `providerName: str = modelConfig["provider"]` dict access (manager.py:176), so disabled provider-less entries never error. That's why exactly 4 lines, not 7. Live-verified via `ConfigManager(configPath='config.toml', configDirs=['configs/00-defaults','configs/common','configs/local','configs/local-telegram'], dotEnvFile='.env.local-telegram')`: merged `[models.models]` = 56 entries, 7 lacking `provider`.

**Mechanism:** a merged entry lacking `provider` hits `modelConfig["provider"]` (manager.py:176) → `KeyError('provider')`; `str(KeyError('provider'))` is `'provider'` (repr of the key) → the message suffix. RULE: bare `[models.models."…"]` toggles with only `enabled` are safe ONLY when a base entry carrying `provider` exists in an earlier-loaded config dir; after any catalog regeneration/rename, manual toggles can silently drift into standalone broken entries.

**Bot parity:** pre-existing behavior, NOT script-introduced — `main.py:121-124` constructs `LLMManager(self.configManager.getModelsConfig(), statsStorage=statsStorageMap["llm_request"])`, same `getModelsConfig()` input (only delta is the statsStorage kwarg, irrelevant to `_initModels`), so the bot logs the same 4 ERROR lines at startup in this env.

**Why visible in scripts:** the "silence noisy libraries" header uses `logging.basicConfig(level=WARNING)` (migrate_models.py:81; identical pattern in check_structured_output.py:60, run_llm_debug_query.py:45) — ERROR passes to console while the manager's per-model INFO lines are suppressed.

**Fix candidates:** refresh the 4 stale ids in 10-openrouter.toml against the current generated catalog, and/or fix the manager.py:204 logging bug (see companion memory). General schema context: memory ae53b572; skip-ordering facts: memory 8702b7e8.

title: LLMManager failure log always renders 'unknown' — manager.py:204 logs wrong variable
content:
Latent logging bug in `lib/ai/manager.py::_initModels()` except-block (line 204):

```python
except Exception as e:
    logger.error(f"Failed to initialize model {modelConfig.get('name', 'unknown')}: {e}")
```

It logs `modelConfig.get('name', 'unknown')` — the raw config dict — instead of the loop variable `modelName`. Model config entries NEVER carry a `name` field (identity is the TOML table key `modelName`; the API id is `model_id`), so the `'unknown'` fallback fires for EVERY model failing in this try-block. Consequence: all failure lines are byte-identical (`ERROR:lib.ai.manager:Failed to initialize model unknown: <e>`) and unattributable — you cannot tell WHICH model config broke without re-running the merge yourself (done 2026-09-20: it was 4 stale enable-toggles in configs/common/10-openrouter.toml, see companion memory).

Correct fix when touched: log `modelName` (the dict key from `for modelName, modelConfig in modelsConfig.items():` at line 170). Discovered 2026-09-20 while root-causing the recurring identical-error output; not yet fixed as of that date.

title: ModelImageMessage multimodal payload: text part uses "text" key
content: ModelImageMessage.toDict() (lib/ai/models.py, ~line 883) emits OpenAI multimodal content; the text part MUST be {"type": "text", "text": "..."} — historically it wrongly used a "content" key (since ai/abstract.py Sep 2025), causing strict upstreams (e.g. opencode-go gateway) to reject with 400 'text content parts must carry a string "text" (got undefined)'. Fixed 2026-09-20; regression tests in tests/lib/ai/test_models.py::TestModelImageMessageTextPart. Production image-parsing paths (base.py ~2066, media.py ~528) deliberately send content="" (prompt lives in the system message) — that's why the bug went unnoticed; the stale comment at base.py:2068-2072 blaming "Openrouter LLMs does not support adding text to message with image" likely documents this same bug. Also note: providers without their own proxy section INHERIT the global socks5 proxy (lib/proxy getCombined rule 2).

title: /configure model-picker UI: single render site at configure.py:556, callback-by-index safe for label changes
content:
Research findings (2026-09-20) for planning a vision-marker (👁) suffix on image-capable models in the /configure model picker:

**Single render site.** The model button label is constructed in exactly one place: `chatConfiguration_ConfigureKey` in `internal/bot/common/handlers/configure.py`, line 556: `buttonText = f"{modelTier.emoji()} {modelName}"`, plus `" (*)"` appended at line 558 for the currently-selected model. These two decorations (tier emoji prefix, `(*)` selection suffix) are the ONLY existing label decorations — no price/free/enabled markers exist. The `MODEL`/`IMAGE_MODEL` branch starts at line 533; filtering skips non-`support_text` models for MODEL (line 541) and non-`support_images` for IMAGE_MODEL (lines 543-544).

**Callback safety for label changes.** The callback payload stores `modelIdx` (index into `self.selectableModels`), never the label text; `chatConfiguration_SetValue` (configure.py lines 624+, validation 721-732) resolves models by index. So appending an emoji suffix to labels requires no callback-handling changes.

**support_images flag already available.** Inside the line-535 loop, `getModelInfo(modelName)` already exposes `"support_images"` (default False) and `"support_text"` (default True) — set in `lib/ai/abstract.py` base provider lines 823-824 from provider `_config`. No AI-catalog changes are needed to compute the vision marker.

**Platform-agnostic.** `ConfigureCommandHandler(BaseBotHandler)` (configure.py line 54) lives in `internal/bot/common/handlers/`, instantiated once in `manager.py` line 513 with `botProvider=botProvider`, uses neutral `CallbackButton`. No Telegram/Max variants exist — one edit covers both platforms.

**Display asymmetry gotcha.** The setting-detail text (configure.py line 500) echoes the current model value as a bare string in a code fence; a button-label marker will NOT propagate there. `/models` owner command (dev_commands.py, loop lines 186-201) already lists `support_images` as a labeled field, so a vision emoji there would be redundant. `BaseBotHandler.getChatSettings` (base.py lines 316-325) uses `getModelInfo` for tier gating only, no rendering.

title: Emoji-in-code convention: constants.py typed-constant block is canonical; ChatTier.emoji() inline literals is the enum-method variant
content:
Two established precedents for emoji in bot UI code (found while planning a vision 👁 marker):

**Canonical: module-level typed constants with docstrings** in `internal/bot/constants.py` (lines 81-92, under a `# Emoji constants` comment): `DUNNO_EMOJI: str = "🤷‍♂️"`, `ROBOT_EMOJI: str = "🤖"`, `CHAT_ICON: str = "👥"`, `PRIVATE_ICON: str = "👤"`. Pattern: UPPER_SNAKE, `: str` annotation, docstring per constant. Note two naming suffixes coexist (`*_EMOJI` and `*_ICON`). A new constant (e.g. `VISION_EMOJI: str = "👁"`) should join this block.

**Fallback: inline literals in an enum method** — `ChatTier.emoji()` at `internal/bot/models/chat_settings.py` lines 63-84 returns inline literals via `match`: `"⛔️"` BANNED, `"🆓"` FREE, `"✅"` FREE_PERSONAL, `"⭐️"` PAID, `"🌟"` FRIEND, `"😎"` BOT_OWNER, `"🚫"` fallback. Used as the tier-emoji prefix in /configure model buttons.

Handler-local inline emoji also exists (user_memories.py line 1947 `➕` button label, common.py line 268 `👋`, stats.py repeated inline `📊`/`❌`/`⚠`) but is the weak precedent — prefer the constants.py block for shared markers. Unrelated: docs-tree emoji has its own stricter policy (see existing docs-emoji-normalization memories) — that policy governs markdown, not Python string constants.

title: Per-model LLM config is a raw dict — no schema class; exact capability-flag list with defaults
content:
Re-verified 2026-09-20 (explore pass); SUPERSEDES memory 380cb6b4 (extraConfig flow, 2026-06-10) whose step 1 was outdated: it claimed per-model TOML lives under `[models.<name>]` and that a `modelConfig["extraConfig"]` wrapper key is extracted — neither is true today.

There is NO dataclass/TypedDict/parse site for per-model LLM config — it is a raw dict passed through untouched:
- `lib/ai/manager.py` `_initModels()` (l.145–204) reads `config["models"]` (per-model tables under `[models.models."name"]`), extracts only `provider`, `model_id`, `model_version` (default "latest"), `customParams` (default {}), `context` (default 32768), skips `enabled=false` — then passes the ENTIRE raw TOML dict as `extraConfig=modelConfig` to `provider.addModel(...)` (l.187–195).
- `AbstractModel.__init__` (`lib/ai/abstract.py:143`): `self._config: Dict[str, Any] = extraConfig or {}`. Provider chain addModel → _createModelInstance → model __init__ threads extraConfig through unchanged (re-confirmed).

All capability flags are read lazily via `self._config.get(...)` — TOML key = Python lookup key VERBATIM (snake_case in both; sole exception `customParams`, camelCase on both sides):
- `support_tools` → default False (abstract.py:822; cached as `self._supportTools` in basic_openai_provider.py:244)
- `support_text` → default True (abstract.py:823; yc_sdk_provider.py:215)
- `support_images` → default False (abstract.py:824; yc_sdk_provider.py:216) — GENERATION only
- `support_structured_output` → default False (abstract.py:458, 825)
- `support_embeddings` → default False (abstract.py:534, 826)
- `tier` → default "bot-owner" (abstract.py:827)
- `input_image_format` → list of MIME types (basic_openai_provider.py:536/644/772)
- `image_generation_api` (str), `embedding_dimensions` (int) — override/extra-models keys only

Emitter canonical key order `_CANONICAL_MODEL_KEYS` (scripts/models_catalog.py:107–118): enabled, provider, model_id, model_version, context, support_tools, support_text, support_images, support_structured_output, tier.

title: Vision-input flag design inputs: api.json modalities.input parsed-then-discarded by catalog generator; fixture already has image-input models
content:
New facts for designing a per-model vision-INPUT flag (extends memory d5fafc54 which already establishes support_images = generation-only):

1. **models.dev api.json already carries input-modality data**: per-model `modalities: {input: [...], output: [...]}` with string values "text"/"image"/"audio" (fixture `tests/scripts/fixtures/models_dev_api.json`). Input-vision examples present in the fixture: anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5 (l.62), qwen/qwen3-vl-235b-a22b-instruct (l.100), anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5 (l.157), google/gemini-2.5-flash-image (l.123 — output ["image","text"], both directions). So a new flag needs NO upstream-format change — just read `modalities.input`.

2. **The catalog generator parses `modalities.input` then DISCARDS it** (the key gap): in `applyFilters` (`scripts/models_catalog.py:950–1164`) `inputModalities` is used ONLY for the structural include/skip decision (`"text" not in inputModalities` → skip, l.1030–1039; missing/null modalities counts as ["text"] and is INCLUDED) and is never persisted to TOML. `support_images` derives from `"image" in modalities.output` (l.1061–1065). A vision-input flag slots in exactly alongside l.1064–1065.

3. **Runtime confirmation (2026-09-20 line refs)**: every `support_images` gate is generation-only — basic_openai_provider.py:768/875 (`raise NotImplementedError("Image generation isn't supported…")`), yc_openai_provider.py:178 (`_getImageModelId`, `art://` URI), yc_sdk_provider.py:216/528 plus exactly-one-of support_text/support_images validation (l.218–221 — YC-SDK-only constraint, NOT a general rule), configure.py:540–548 model picker (IMAGE_MODEL rows filtered by support_images, MODEL rows by support_text), dev_commands.py:199 label «Поддержка генерации изображений».

4. **Sending image INPUT is gated by NO model flag**: the only input-related key, `input_image_format`, merely triggers lossless re-encoding via `convertImageIfNeeded` (`lib/ai/models.py:78–151`) threaded through `message.toDict(..., supportedImageFormats=...)` — converts, never gates.

title: Adding a new emitted field to generated model catalogs — coordinated code sites + exact test-breakage list
content:
Checklist from the 2026-09-20 explore pass (extends review memory 52a9e250). Adding a new capability field to the generated `configs/00-defaults/*-models.toml` requires touching ALL of:

**Code (scripts/models_catalog.py):**
1. `_ALLOWED_OVERRIDE_KEYS` kebab→snake map (l.57–69) + `_BOOLEAN_OVERRIDE_KEYS` (l.72–78) if boolean — `parseFilterConfig` raises `CatalogError` on ANY unknown override key in models-filters.toml, so skipping this hard-breaks overrides; add to `_ALLOWED_DEFAULTS_KEYS` too if provider-level defaults should set it.
2. `applyFilters` mapping from the api.json field (l.950–1164; note pattern: explicit `false` in api.json beats provider defaults for tool_call/structured_output, l.1066–1069).
3. `_CANONICAL_MODEL_KEYS` emission order (l.107–118).
4. `emitCatalog` emission (l.1224–1304). Precedent for optional keys (`test_imageFieldsAbsentWithoutOverride`, l.1196–1204): emit ONLY when set — `input_image_format`/`image_generation_api` are emitted just before `tier` (l.1289–1292). models-filters.toml override keys are kebab-case (`support-tools`, `input-image-format`).

**Tests that break (tests/scripts/test_fetch_models.py):**
- `test_enabledAlwaysEmittedAndExtraModelsVerbatim` (l.1148–1159) HARD-BREAKS on any new always-emitted key — it asserts exact whole-dict equality on an extra-models entry (incl. `support_images: False`).
- `test_roundTripTomllibFieldsMatch` (l.1116–1135) — per-field pins on `openrouter/deepseek-v4-flash`; additive fields need an added assert, removal/rename breaks it.
- `test_imageOverrideFieldsCarriedThroughAndOrdered` (l.1161–1194) — pins key ORDER via `tableText.index(...)` between `support_structured_output` and `tier`.
- Inline fixtures `_FULL_OPENROUTER_SECTION`/`_CLI_FILTERS_TOML` (l.137–237) hard-code `support_images = false` lines.
- Generated catalogs are validated by tomllib parse-back, NOT byte-diffed against fixture; `test_dryRunAllProvidersPrintsCatalogs` (l.1330) only greps stdout headers.

**Drift guards (unaffected by field addition):** (1) exact wildcard-free whitelist ids matching no upstream fixture id → CatalogError (applyFilters l.999–1022); (2) `TestTrackedCatalogDriftGuard.test_botDefaultModelSelectorsResolve` (l.1570–1598) — every `[bot.defaults]` `*-model` selector must resolve to a real `[models.models]` key (name-based, regeneration-safe).

**For a modality-derived flag specifically:** `test_supportModalitiesFromOutput` (l.701–713) pins the output-modality mapping — write a sibling test for input modalities using existing fixture ids (claude-haiku-4.5 → input-vision true, deepseek-v4-flash → false).

title: support_image_input flag implemented end-to-end in catalog pipeline + getInfo()
content:
Implementation LANDED 2026-09-19 (developer session, uncommitted at handoff) — implements the design from memory 7be52a07 and resolves the "no such flag exists" gap noted in memory d5fafc54.

**Naming disambiguation (user-mandated, do not revisit):** `support_image_input` = image INPUT (vision / "can see"); `support_images` = image GENERATION (output). Orthogonal flags — never rename or merge.

**Decision — extra-models stay verbatim:** hand-defined extra-model entries accept `support_image_input` as an optional bool (`_validateExtraModel`) but are emitted verbatim with NO defaulting at emission, exactly like `support_images`. The brief's "defaults to False when absent" is satisfied only at the runtime layer: `lib/ai/abstract.py` `getInfo()` returns `self._config.get("support_image_input", False)`. Inline test fixtures set the key explicitly so exact-dict pins gain it.

**Pipeline facts:** emission order in `_CANONICAL_MODEL_KEYS`/emitCatalog is `support_images` → `support_image_input` → `support_structured_output` (always emitted, True and False). Derivation: `"image" in inputModalities`; missing/null `modalities` → input defaults to `["text"]` → False. Override kebab key `support-image-input` in both `_ALLOWED_OVERRIDE_KEYS` and `_BOOLEAN_OVERRIDE_KEYS` (last-match-wins); NOT in `_ALLOWED_DEFAULTS_KEYS` — `[[overrides]]` is the escape hatch for bad upstream data. `scripts/fetch_models.py` needed ZERO changes (delegates to models_catalog.applyFilters).

**Live regen baseline (2026-09-19) + accepted upstream deltas:** openrouter-models.toml 15 models (11 true / 4 false); opencode-go-models.toml 17 models (10 true / 7 false). title: markdown-mcp server: doc_section_edit CAS false-mismatch + no reindex after plain edits
content:
Gotchas found 2026-09-19 while syncing two docs tables (complements memory 8258c3d7, which covers the CLI index counter quirk; this is the MCP-server side):

1. **doc_section_edit CAS can mismatch byte-identical text.** Editing `docs/llm/model-catalogs.md` §2.2 (the-filters-file) failed twice with "expected_text mismatch … body changed since it was read" — including on an immediate retry after a fresh doc_read that returned the IDENTICAL sha (0e8d008f…). Text was reproduced exactly from the served body_text; disk verification showed no invisible Unicode (no NBSP/narrow-space; em-dashes/§/¹/→ all copied). Never root-caused. Suspects: the tool's "flat body" may include a trailing newline the served body_text doesn't show, or subtle transcription normalization of a ~90-line body. The same copy-approach succeeded on a smaller section (configuration.md §models-model-configuration-keys) minutes earlier. Practical guidance: for small sections doc_section_edit works; for large bodies, don't burn attempts — fall back to plain `edit` (sanctioned by the AGENTS.md fallback policy), then verify with `git diff` that exactly the intended lines changed.

2. **An MCP write to one file may invalidate CAS reads of another.** The first CAS failure came right after a successful doc_section_edit on a different file. First move on CAS failure: re-read the section and retry immediately. If the retry with an identical-sha fresh read still fails, switch to plain edit rather than iterating.

3. **The top-level `sha256` in doc_read / doc_section_edit responses is the whole-FILE hash** (verified via shasum), not a hash of the section body_text. Usable as `expected_sha256` for a `doc_write` overwrite if a whole-file MCP write is ever needed.

4. **Plain filesystem edits do NOT reindex the MCP server's index** — after plain `edit`, doc_read/doc_search keep serving the stale content with the unchanged file sha until the next MCP write touches that file. Verify disk truth with git diff/read, not doc_read. Server-side manifestation of the same class of issue as memory 8258c3d7 (CLI incremental index reporting indexed=0 after out-of-band edits).

title: Additive model-catalog fields are downstream-safe: consumer audit facts
content:
Findings from the 2026-09-20 downstream-compatibility audit performed during the support_image_input review. Reusable rationale for why ANY additive capability field on `[models.models]` catalog tables is safe to introduce (complements the coordinated-sites checklist in memory 8a4ec1b4, which covers the producer side):

- **scripts/migrate_models.py is field-agnostic.** Its "drift guard" `collectModelKeys()` (l.163-175) derives chat-setting keys from `getChatSettingsInfo()`, never enumerates catalog fields. All availability checks are pure None/non-None tests on `LLMManager.getModelInfo()`; the returned dict's keys are never inspected. Migration SQL touches only `chat_settings.value` strings.
- **Config → model plumbing has no whitelist:** `LLMManager._initModels` passes the whole `modelConfig` dict as `extraConfig` unfiltered (lib/ai/manager.py:194) → `AbstractModel._config = extraConfig or {}`. New keys flow through verbatim and appear in getInfo() both directly and via the `"extra": self._config.copy()` entry (additive only).
- **No payload-leak path:** every provider read of `self._config` is a specific-key `.get()` (support_images/support_text/support_tools/input_image_format/image_generation_api/embedding_dimensions in basic_openai_provider.py, yc_sdk_provider.py); nothing iterates `_config` into an API request — request params come from the separate `_customParams` dict. So a new config key cannot leak into provider payloads.
- **All other getInfo() consumers use keyed access**, never strict dict-shape comparison: internal/services/llm/service.py (`.get("support_structured_output", False)`), base.py (`.get("tier", "")`), configure.py picker gating on support_text/support_images (semantically correct: MODEL=text, IMAGE_MODEL=image generation — deliberately orthogonal to the input flag), scripts/check_*.py print/inspect only.
- **Unknown keys render leniently in dev UI:** internal/bot/common/handlers/dev_commands.py:191-200 `modelKeyI18n` map lacks entries for support_image_input (and pre-existing for support_structured_output/tier/support_embeddings) → falls back to raw key name via `.get(k, k)`. Established lenient pattern, not a defect.
- **Catalog generation scope:** fetch-generated catalogs are ONLY `openrouter` and `opencode-go` (scripts/models-filters.toml). Hand-maintained `yc-sdk`/`yc-openai`/`fastembed` catalogs legitimately omit optional fields and resolve to runtime defaults (False) per getInfo() default. The fetch_models.py drift guard compares model IDs, not fields.
- **Expected regeneration drift convention:** a live re-fetch of the generated catalogs produces only `# Fetched:` timestamp churn plus occasional upstream price-comment updates; any OTHER diff is unexpected drift and worth flagging in review.

title: models_catalog semantics pinned: per-field last-match-wins overrides; extra-models emit verbatim (omitted key stays absent)
content:
models_catalog.py emission/override semantics for `support_image_input`, verified by reading the code then pinned by tests (2026-09-20) in `tests/scripts/test_fetch_models.py`:

1. **Overrides: last-match-wins PER FIELD.** A later matching override beats an earlier one on the fields it sets; an override touching only an unrelated field (e.g. tier) does NOT reset previously-set fields. Pinned by `TestApplyFilters::test_supportImageInputOverridePrecedence_lastMatchWinsPerField` — chain broad `anthropic/*`=true → exact=false → later tier-only override; final asserted `False` + `tier == "friend"` (the tier assertion proves the unrelated override matched, so a reset would have been caught).

2. **Extra-models emit VERBATIM.** `_extraModelLines` emits dict keys in canonical order "where present"; `_validateExtraModel` type-checks a field ONLY when present. So a `[[extra-models]]` entry omitting `support_image_input` keeps the key ABSENT from the emitted TOML → runtime `getInfo()` defaults to False. Pinned by `TestEmitCatalog::test_extraModelOmittingSupportImageInput_staysAbsentFromEmission` (includes upstream-model contrast assertion so the test can't pass vacuously).

3. **Non-bool value rejected.** Extra-model with e.g. `support_image_input = "yes"` → `_validateExtraModel` raises `CatalogError` matching `'support_image_input' must be a boolean`. Pinned by `TestExtraModelValidation::test_supportImageInputNonBooleanRejected`.

title: Keyboard button labels are display-only: verbatim passthrough both adapters, never parsed
content:
Verified end-to-end during Phase2 support_image_input review (2026-09-20): inline-keyboard button TEXT is display-only on both platforms — nothing in the codebase ever parses, compares, truncates, or string-ops button labels. All interaction logic flows through the packed payload instead.

**Adapter trace (text passes verbatim):**
- `CallbackButton.toTelegram()` → `telegram.InlineKeyboardButton(text=self.text, callback_data=utils.packDict(payload))` (internal/bot/common/models/keyboard_button.py:28-34) → `_keyboardToTelegram` builds `InlineKeyboardMarkup` (internal/bot/common/bot.py:401-410) → `reply_markup` (bot.py:454/466/527). Callback returns via `unpackDict(query.data)` (internal/bot/telegram/application.py:186).
- `CallbackButton.toMax()` → `maxModels.CallbackButton(text=self.text, ...)` (keyboard_button.py:36-42; text stored unmodified lib/max_bot/models/keyboard.py:53,101; serialized verbatim by `Keyboard.to_dict` keyboard.py:446-460) → `InlineKeyboardAttachmentRequest` (bot.py:412-423) → API client appends attachment as-is (lib/max_bot/client.py:927-928, 998-1000). Callback returns via `unpackDict(update.callback.payload)` (internal/bot/max/application.py:250).

**Escaping: not applicable.** Markdown parsing applies only to message TEXT, never labels: Telegram parse_mode/`markdownToMarkdownV2` touch `text` only (bot.py:457-460); Max `format=TextFormat.MARKDOWN` likewise (bot.py:476). Model names with markdown metacharacters are safe in labels; in message bodies they go through `markdownToMarkdownV2` (configure.py:609).

**Length: non-issue for the eye marker.** Telegram's hard 64-BYTE limit applies to `callback_data` (the packed payload), NOT button text — decorative label additions don't change payload size. Labels are a display-truncation-only concern.

**VS16 emoji in labels is safe** (e.g. EYE_EMOJI "👁️" = U+1F441+U+FE0F): consumed only by platform UI renderers; tests compare against the identical constant so no normalization mismatch is possible.

**configure.py model picker value resolution is payload-index-driven** (labels never parsed): payload `{a: set-value, c: chatId, k: keyId, v: modelIdx}` (ButtonDataKey enum internal/bot/models/enums.py:43-96, Value="v" at :94). Render enumerates the FULL `self.selectableModels` (configure.py:536) — skipped models (538-540 missing info, 541-549 capability filter, 551-555 tier filter) produce no button but don't shift later indices. Resolution (configure.py:720-738) accepts int/float/digit-string (`unpackDict` coerces "3"→int, "0"→int 0 via len==1 exemption, lib/utils/utils.py:249-264), bounds-checks against `len(selectableModels)-1` (:727, safe when list empty), re-validates tier with a None-guard for removed models (:731-734). Review verdict: no bugs in the eye-marker addition (ordering eye-before-"(*)" pinned by tests/bot/common/handlers/test_configure.py:440-454; shared render site correctly marks IMAGE_MODEL picker too, :456-472).
