title: Maintainer in-flight staging can sweep agent edits into the git index
content:
Environmental gotcha hit 2026-09-20 during a hands-off micro-task ("do not stage/commit; leave git state as is — unrelated in-flight maintainer staging"):

After the agent edited `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_configure.py` (running zero `git add`/`git commit`), `git status --porcelain` showed the file as `M ` (staged modification, worktree-clean), and the index blob already contained the brand-new test. The maintainer's in-flight staging tooling swept the freshly written working-tree edit into the index between the edit and the status check.

**Correct handling when a task forbids staging:**
1. Never run `git add` / `git commit` / `git restore --staged` — unstaging would itself mutate the maintainer's git state, violating hands-off as much as staging would.
2. Diagnose instead: `git diff -- <file>` (worktree vs index; empty = identical) plus `git diff --cached -- <file> | grep -c <new-symbol>` to confirm whether your content lives in the index.
3. Report the observation plainly in the handoff ("external tooling staged my edit after it landed on disk; worktree == index for my file; I ran no staging commands") rather than "fixing" it.

Porcelain XY recap used during diagnosis: `M ` = staged-only, ` M` = worktree-only, `MM` = both. Note `git diff --stat -- <file>` printing nothing means worktree==index, NOT that the file is unchanged.

title: lib/ai sessionId contract: ContextVar transport, opencode-go sole consumer, only 2 proper call sites
content:
Authoritative sessionId contract for lib/ai calls, verified against source 2026-09-20. Complements memory 7eca3487 (opencode-go provider implementation) with the full API/transport/pass-through/audit picture.

**Transport is a ContextVar, not a constructor/param**: `_requestSessionIdVar` (lib/ai/abstract.py:47, default None), read only via `getCurrentRequestSessionId()` (abstract.py:59-71) — the sole sanctioned read for provider code. Four public AbstractModel wrappers take keyword-only `sessionId: Optional[str] = None`: generateText (sig :189-197), generateImage (:303-310), generateStructured (:417-427), generateEmbeddings (:557-564). Each ALWAYS sets the var and resets it in `finally` — even when None — so no stale session leaks into a later call on the same asyncio task; this always-set/always-reset discipline is load-bearing, don't make it conditional. Fallback attempts re-pass sessionId explicitly (abstract.py:239, :352, :474). No snake_case `session_id` variant exists anywhere.

**Consumption**: sole consumer in the codebase is OpencodeGoModel. `_getSessionId()` (opencode_go_provider.py:88-106) resolves: ContextVar → `.strip()` → provider config `session_fallback` → `DEFAULT_SESSION_ID = "gromozeka"` (:53); empty/whitespace follows the same chain. `_getExtraParams()` (:108-129) ALWAYS sets header `x-opencode-session` (:56); user `customParams.extra_headers` merge per header name with user winning (:126-128). So a missing/None sessionId NEVER errors — the header is always present; the failure mode is operational: all conversations collapse into one shared "gromozeka" sticky-routing bucket, destroying per-conversation prompt-cache affinity. `session_fallback` is commented out in configs/00-defaults/providers.toml (~:35-41) → effective default is "gromozeka". ALL other providers (basic-openai base `_getExtraParams` at basic_openai_provider.py:294-310 just returns customParams; custom-openai, openrouter, yc-openai, yc-sdk, fastembed) ignore sessionId entirely — passing it is a harmless no-op for them. Fallback chain locked by tests: tests/lib/ai/providers/test_opencode_go_provider.py:207-305.

**LLMService pass-through** (internal/services/llm/service.py): all five methods take keyword-only `sessionId: Optional[str] = None` and forward verbatim, none synthesize a default: generateTextViaLLM (:783) forwards to condenseContext (:923) AND generateText on every tool-loop round (:972) — one kwarg at the outermost call covers condensing + all rounds; condenseContext (:1126→:1281); generateText (:1316→:1368-1374, with consumerId=str(chatId)); generateStructured (:1393→:1471-1479); generateImage (:1492→:1530-1535); generateEmbedding (:1544→:1585, whole body try/except→None).

**Call-site audit** (line numbers current as of 2026-09-20): only 2 of ~32 production sites pass sessionId properly — llm_messages.py:225 (main chat-reply _generateTextViaLLM) and llm_messages.py:1061 (debug useTools path), both `sessionId=await self.getLLMRequestSessionId(ensuredMessage)`. All others omit (→ shared fallback only when the resolved model is opencode-go): base.py:938/:956 (thread-prep condenseContext), base.py:1431 (image parsing), llm_messages.py:409 (chat image reply), llm_messages.py:938 (random-context condense), dev_commands.py:1019, divination.py:693/:737/:1034/:1130, media.py:176/:535/:664/:696, yandex_search.py:529, summarization.py:278, user_memories.py:462/:611/:717/:914/:1296, chat_search.py:554/:708 (plus a direct `model.generateEmbeddings` LLMService bypass at chat_search.py:1330 that also drops consumerId), message_preprocessor.py:221; debug scripts check_image_parsing.py:240, check_tool_calling.py:381, check_structured_output.py:273, run_llm_debug_query.py:308, reproduce_layout_extraction.py:414. Embedding-site omissions are currently no-ops (no embeddings provider consumes the var) but passing is still the conformant shape.

**Proper-sessionId checklist**: (1) value from `await BaseBotHandler.getLLMRequestSessionId(ensuredMessage)` — never inlined/synthesized; (2) format `gromozeka-<chatId>-<rootMessageId.asStr()>` = chat + thread-root identity; (3) passed as keyword-only `sessionId=` at the OUTERMOST LLMService call (generateTextViaLLM covers the whole tool loop); (4) non-empty (None is tolerated by the stack but is precisely the audited failure mode — silent, no error anywhere); (5) don't confuse with SandboxHandler.getSessionId (`chat#{chatId}`), the `chatLLM#{chatId}` rate-limiter key (service.py:1608-1620), or `chat#<id>` log-prefix idioms.

title: Correction: BaseBotHandler helper is getLLMRequestSessionId; getSessionId/chat#{} is SandboxHandler-only
content:
Verified against source 2026-09-20: `BaseBotHandler` does NOT have a `getSessionId()` method. The LLM request-session helper is `async def getLLMRequestSessionId(self, ensuredMessage)` at internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py:736-765. It resolves the thread root via `self.db.chatMessages.getChatMessageByMessageId(chatId, ensuredMessage.messageId)` — falling back to the message's own ID on exception or NULL `root_message_id` — and returns `f"gromozeka-{chatId}-{rootMessageId.asStr()}"`. Identity: chat + thread root; every top-level message starts a fresh session, all thread replies share the root's session; stable across restarts; one DB lookup per call. The `gromozeka-` format appears nowhere else in internal/ or lib/.

A method literally named `getSessionId()` returning `f"chat#{ensuredMessage.recipient.id}"` exists ONLY on `SandboxHandler` (internal/bot/common/handlers/sandbox.py:217-218) and feeds SandboxManager exclusively (Docker per-chat sandbox identity for runCode/readFile/listFiles); it never touches lib/ai. That convention is already encoded in memory 7e98490a.

The commonly-cited prior "BaseBotHandler has getSessionId returning chat#{...}" conflates two distinct contracts: LLM request sessions (`gromozeka-<chatId>-<rootMessageId>`, consumed by the x-opencode-session header) vs Docker sandbox sessions (`chat#{chatId}`). The historical "tool handlers inlined f\"chat#{...}\"" bug class was a sandbox-session bug, not an LLM-session one. Also note `chat#<id>` is a log-prefix idiom (e.g. internal/services/llm/service.py:1360, :1467) and `chatLLM#{chatId}` is the LLM rate-limiter key — neither is a session identifier.

title: Model-catalog convention: hand-maintained catalogs deliberately omit capability keys; defaults allow-list excludes input flag
content:
Convention confirmed during the Gate 2 review of `support_image_input` (2026-09-20): capability flags do NOT need to appear in every model catalog — hand-maintained catalogs deliberately omit keys that carry no upstream signal.

**Which catalogs carry `support_image_input`:** only generated ones (`openrouter-models.toml`, `opencode-go-models.toml` — regenerated by `scripts/fetch_models.py` from models.dev) plus hand-maintained `yc-openai-models.toml`. **`yc-sdk-models.toml` and `fastembed-models.toml` omit the key — CORRECT**, for stacked reasons: (a) they are hand-maintained and absent from `scripts/models-filters.toml`, which defines only `openrouter` and `opencode-go` filter sections; (b) an absent key resolves to `False` at runtime (`getInfo()` default); (c) fastembed models are embeddings — vision irrelevant; (d) yc-sdk enforces a text/image-GENERATION XOR at `lib/ai/providers/yc_sdk_provider.py:215–219`, so an input flag adds nothing there.

**Related producer-side convention:** `_ALLOWED_DEFAULTS_KEYS` in `scripts/models_catalog.py` (:99–103) deliberately EXCLUDES `support-image-input`. Defaults exist only where models.dev has no upstream signal (`tool_call`, `structured_output`); `modalities.input` IS the signal, so a default would be meaningless. The `[[overrides]]` escape hatch (kebab key `support-image-input`, boolean-validated) is the sanctioned way to correct upstream data — documented in `docs/llm/model-catalogs.md` (:130, :180).

**Emission contract (true shape, matches docs):** ALWAYS emitted for upstream models; OPTIONAL/verbatim for `[[extra-models]]` — omission there stays absent and is schema-legal. Never "fix" an omitted key in a hand-maintained or extra-models context as if it were a bug.

title: markdown-mcp doc_section_edit CAS fails on byte-identical body; index staleness can self-resolve; docs-only bash allowlist blocks CLI reindex
content:
Three related markdown-mcp tooling gotchas confirmed 2026-09-20 (docs-writer session documenting support_image_input):

1. **doc_section_edit CAS rejects the byte-identical served body on `llm/teamlead-memory.md`.** Workflow: doc_outline → doc_section_edit op=rename (worked, reindex "indexed") → doc_read section → doc_section_edit op=replace with expected_text = exactly the served body_text → CAS error "the section's body changed since it was read". Re-reading returned the SAME sha256 and identical body_text, and the retry failed identically. Root cause: CAS is checked against a fresh parse of current disk bytes, while doc_read serves body_text from the INDEX; the two renderings differ for this file (suspected trailing-newline/flat-body boundary handling — file's final section). This is the same quirk a developer session hit earlier on `llm/model-catalogs.md` ("CAS-failed on byte-identical body"). **Fallback that works: plain `edit` tool** (precedented twice now on these two files). Cost: index lags by the appended paragraph until the next MCP write — observed to be benign (see #2).

2. **Index staleness after plain-tool edits can SELF-RESOLVE — verify before attempting any reindex.** A handoff note claimed `llm/model-catalogs.md`'s MCP index was stale (post plain-tool edits); on verification the index was already current (doc_read section body contained the newly added rows; outline line-ranges aligned with disk). So don't trust stale-index claims from older notes: doc_read the affected section and check for the known-new content first. Note doc_read mode/source field: "disk" = served from disk (file modified after indexing), "index" = served from index.

3. **Docs-only agent sessions run under a bash allowlist** (make lint*, make check-docs*, rg/grep/ls/wc, git diff/log/show/status/ls-files only; everything else denied). Therefore the CLI `markdown-mcp index` reindex is NOT available in those sessions — the only sanctioned paths are MCP-native ops (doc_write/doc_section_edit) or the plain-edit fallback with a "index lags until next MCP write" note.

title: Verified sessionId plumbing facts: LLMService signature asymmetry, no nested ContextVar inheritance, inner-loop forwarding, census attribution fix
content:
Facts verified against source 2026-09-20 during the sessionId-domains design research. They extend memories 821ceee7 (contract) and 673ed015 (census) and correct one census attribution.

1. **LLMService signature asymmetry (matters for any fallback/default design)**: `generateText` (internal/services/llm/service.py:1305), `generateStructured` (:1380), `generateImage` (:1485), `generateEmbedding` (:1537), `generateTextViaLLM` (:763) ALL carry keyword-only `chatId: int` AND `sessionId: Optional[str] = None`. `condenseContext` (:1113) has **NO chatId** — only `consumerId: Optional[str]` + `sessionId`. So LLMService can derive a chat-level default everywhere EXCEPT condenseContext, where only consumerId is available.

2. **ContextVar is set UNCONDITIONALLY by all 4 AbstractModel wrappers** (e.g. `token = _requestSessionIdVar.set(sessionId)` at lib/ai/abstract.py:608). Consequence: a nested LLM call issued during tool execution does NOT inherit the outer call's session — omitting sessionId inside a nested call yields None inside (→ provider default bucket), not the conversation session. Every call site must choose its identity explicitly; omission ≠ inheritance.

3. **sessionId forwarding covers whole internal loops**: generateTextViaLLM forwards sessionId to every inner tool-round generateText (service.py:972) and the internal condenseContext forwards it to the condensing model (:1281). So passing ONE kwarg at a multi-round call site (e.g. divination discovery, memory refinement) unlocks prefix affinity for the entire loop.

4. **Census attribution correction**: llm_messages.py:1061 (one of the 2 proper sessionId sites) is inside `llm_test_command` (the "test_llm" command, llm_messages.py:987), NOT llmReplayCommand. The replay command is `dev_commands.py:1019` (`llmReplayCommand`, def :831) and OMITS sessionId. Both are owner debug commands; do not conflate them.

5. **generateEmbedding returns `Optional[tuple[modelName, vector]]`** (None on bad/unsupported model), wrapper retries attempts=3 (abstract.py:561) — relevant for the chat_search.py:1330 bypass refactor (memory 6bc577ae): generateEmbedding's None-return preserves the existing filter-only fallback semantics, and `doRateLimit=False` is needed because searchCommand already rate-limits at :1309 before DB work.

6. **Identity inputs verified at key sites** (for future implementation): `_parseImage` (base.py:1406) is a fire-and-forget `asyncio.create_task` at base.py:2078 receiving `ret.id` = mediaId = fileUniqueId; `EnsuredMessage.mediaId` (internal/bot/models/ensured_message.py:450, deprecated in favor of `mediaList`) is file_unique_id-based (:857). divination enclosing functions: `_handleReading` (:574), `_discoverLayoutWithLLM` (:981, ensuredMessage only in extraData), `_extractLayoutFromText` (:1073, NO ensuredMessage — only chatId + canonicalLayoutId). title: lib/ai/session.py foundation module: API and invariants (sessionId domains phase 1)
content:
Implemented 2026-09-20 (phase 1 of the approved sessionId semantic-domains design; supersedes the "proposal-awaiting-approval" status in memory e70c8d8b). `lib/ai/session.py` is the central construction point for session ids consumed as the `x-opencode-session` header by the opencode-go provider; stdlib-only (hashlib, re), no bot deps. Public API:

- `DEFAULT_SESSION_NAMESPACE: str = "gromozeka"` — matches `DEFAULT_SESSION_ID` in `lib/ai/providers/opencode_go_provider.py`.
- `sanitizeSessionIdComponent(component: str) -> str` — replaces every char outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` with `-`; ValueError on empty; NO length cap here.
- `hashSessionIdComponent(text: str) -> str` — `sha256(text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]`; for free-text components (URLs, basenames, layout names); 16-hex/64-bit collision resistance accepted for cache-bucket naming.
- `buildSessionId(*components: str, namespace: str = DEFAULT_SESSION_NAMESPACE) -> str` — sanitizes namespace + components, joins with `-`, raises ValueError if result > 128 chars (module-private `_MAX_SESSION_ID_LENGTH = 128`); fail-loud beats silent truncation.

First consumer wired: `BaseBotHandler.getLLMRequestSessionId()` (internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py) now returns `buildSessionId(str(chatId), rootMessageId.asStr())` — byte-identical to the old f-string. `lib/ai/__init__.py` was deliberately NOT given re-exports; later phases (~30 call sites) import from `lib.ai.session` directly. Tests: `tests/lib/ai/test_session.py` (18 tests) + `TestGetLLMRequestSessionId` in `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_base.py`.

title: Session-id byte-identity invariant: double dash for negative chatIds; accepted exotic Max-id delta
content:
Two load-bearing invariants for session-id building in Gromozeka (violating either breaks prompt-cache affinity or production routing):

1. **Byte-identity: dashes are NEVER stripped or collapsed.** Existing production session ids embed negative Telegram group chatIds, producing `gromozeka--100123-<msgId>` (double dash from `str(-100123)` + `-` join). `sanitizeSessionIdComponent` therefore preserves leading/trailing/repeated dashes exactly — stripping or collapsing them would silently change every group-chat session id.

2. **Accepted behavior delta (exotic Max ids).** The old raw f-string in `getLLMRequestSessionId` passed Max-platform string message-id characters outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` through unchanged; via `buildSessionId` they now become `-`. Deliberate, deterministic, affects only exotic ids — documented in a code comment next to the return and in a CHANGELOG [Unreleased]/Changed entry.

Also: `buildSessionId` raises ValueError over the 128-char cap instead of truncating — callers with long free-text components (URLs, file basenames) must pre-hash them with `hashSessionIdComponent`. Tests pin byte-identity explicitly: `buildSessionId(str(-100123), "456") == "gromozeka--100123-456"`.

title: BaseBotHandler method testing: UserMemoriesHandler subclass + repo-swap mocking pattern
content:
Established pattern for testing `BaseBotHandler` methods with DB dependencies (used to add `TestGetLLMRequestSessionId` in `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_base.py`):

- `BaseBotHandler` is not directly instantiable — tests use `UserMemoriesHandler` as the concrete subclass, built via the file's `_makeHandler(testDatabase)` helper with the `testDatabase` conftest fixture (real in-memory DB).
- Repository swap: `handler.db.chatMessages = mockRepo  # type: ignore[assignment]` where `mockRepo = Mock()` and `mockRepo.getChatMessageByMessageId = AsyncMock(return_value=cast(ChatMessageDict, {"root_message_id": MessageId(1001)}))`. Fake rows must carry `MessageId` instances — `ChatMessageDict.root_message_id` is typed `Optional[MessageId]` and production code calls `.asStr()` on it.
- Fallback paths need NO mocking: the real in-memory DB returns `None` for nonexistent rows, so `getLLMRequestSessionId`'s own-id fallback works against the raw fixture.
- `getLLMRequestSessionId` behavior (verified): resolves thread root from `db.chatMessages.getChatMessageByMessageId()` — uses row's `root_message_id` when present, falls back to the message's own id otherwise, and also falls back when the DB call raises (except branch). Output shape: `gromozeka-<chatId>-<messageId>`.
- The module's autouse CacheService-singleton-reset fixture covers new test classes automatically.

title: Phase 1 session-id builder review: APPROVED, zero blockers — 2 MINOR + 1 NIT open
content:
2026-09-20 read-only review (code-reviewer) of the phase-1 sessionId change set — `lib/ai/session.py` (new), `internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py` getLLMRequestSessionId() swapped to `buildSessionId(str(chatId), rootMessageId.asStr())` + byte-identity comment, 18 helper tests (`tests/lib/ai/test_session.py`) + 4 handler tests (`TestGetLLMRequestSessionId`), one CHANGELOG entry under [Unreleased]/Changed. VERDICT: FINDINGS but ZERO BLOCKERs — foundation is approved as the base for the ~30 upcoming sessionId call-site edits.

Independently verified clean: byte identity vs the old f-string for nonempty token-safe components with total ≤128; double dash preserved for negative group chatIds (sanitizer never strips/collapses dashes); output always pure `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` ASCII → no x-opencode-session header-injection/encoding risk; `hashSessionIdComponent` = sha256(UTF-8).hexdigest()[:16] correct ('hello' known-vector test); handler diff minimal (import + comment + return swap at base.py:~774); tests non-tautological (literal expected strings, not derived from the implementation); no singleton-leak issues; AGENTS.md conventions compliant (camelCase, Google docstrings, full hints, no Any/pydantic, tests mirror layout). Gates: `make lint` clean (pyright 0 errors/0 warnings), targeted pytest 57 passed in 2.78s (venv is Python 3.14.6), `make check-docs` 148 files / 2940 links / 0 broken.

Open findings:
- **F1 MINOR** — base.py byte-identity comment + CHANGELOG entry overstate compatibility: the builder additionally REJECTS empty components and >128-char totals, which the old f-string silently accepted; handler docstring lacks `Raises: ValueError`; changelog omits rejection behavior; the builder call sits OUTSIDE the handler's DB try/except. Fix = qualify wording + docstring + changelog (no behavior change).
- **F2 MINOR** — untested edge contracts: namespace-only `buildSessionId()` → `'gromozeka'`; empty-namespace/empty-component rejection; sanitizer accepts >128-char input (cap belongs to buildSessionId only); exact 129-char rejection; CR/LF/NUL replacement; empty-string hashing. The exact-cap test derives its expectation from `_MAX_SESSION_ID_LENGTH` instead of pinning literal 128/129, so it wouldn't catch an accidental constant change.
- **F3 NIT** — hashSessionIdComponent docstring implies 64-bit collision resistance; a 64-bit truncated digest gives ~2^32 birthday bound. Reword as cache-bucket naming; no behavior change.

Standing caveat: session ids remain routing/cache labels, NOT authorization identities (sanitize+join is intentionally not collision-free).

title: buildSessionId ValueError contract: token-safe ≠ cannot-raise; handler call outside DB try
content:
Sharper statement of the session-id builder contract (refines memory 0d04c557, which records only the >128 cap):

- `buildSessionId` raises ValueError on BOTH: (a) any empty component (the sanitizer rejects empty input), and (b) sanitized namespace + `-`-joined components exceeding 128 chars total.
- Byte identity with the legacy `gromozeka-{chatId}-{msgId}` f-string is therefore guaranteed ONLY for nonempty token-safe components whose complete result fits 128 chars. The byte-identity comment in `internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py` (~lines 766-774) and the CHANGELOG entry originally claimed it more broadly — flagged for rewording by the 2026-09-20 phase-1 review (F1).
- In `BaseBotHandler.getLLMRequestSessionId` the buildSessionId call sits OUTSIDE the DB try/except: a builder ValueError propagates to the caller rather than being swallowed by the DB-failure fallback path. Future call sites must not assume token-safe inputs cannot raise; pre-hash long free-text components (URLs, basenames) with `hashSessionIdComponent` (per 0d04c557).
- Positive guarantees locked by tests: dashes never stripped/collapsed — negative Telegram group chatId intentionally yields `gromozeka--100123-<msgId>` (double dash); each invalid char maps to exactly one `-`; output is always ASCII `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, safe as the `x-opencode-session` header value (no injection/encoding risk).
- `hashSessionIdComponent`: sha256(UTF-8).hexdigest()[:16] = 64-bit digest → birthday collision bound ~2^32, NOT 2^64 (docstring overstated — review F3). Fine for cache-bucket/prompt-cache-affinity naming; never use as an authorization identity.

title: Test anti-pattern: constant-derived boundary tests don't pin the spec — pin literals + assert the constant
content:
Testing principle from review finding F2 on the session-id tests (2026-09-20), joining the anti-pattern family in memories b2b4d0ab and 6db596ea:

A boundary test that derives BOTH its input and its expectation from the implementation constant (e.g. `buildSessionId("x" * (_MAX_SESSION_ID_LENGTH - len(DEFAULT_SESSION_NAMESPACE) - 1))` asserted `== _MAX_SESSION_ID_LENGTH`) does not independently verify the specified limit — it only checks the code is self-consistent with itself. If the constant silently changes, the test keeps passing against the new (possibly wrong) value.

Correct pattern (now in tests/lib/ai/test_session.py):
1. Pin the boundary with LITERAL lengths: `buildSessionId("a" * 118)` → exactly 128 chars accepted; `buildSessionId("a" * 119)` → 129 rejected; comment the arithmetic (9-char namespace + 1 joiner + 118/119).
2. Separately assert the implementation constant equals the spec value (`assert _MAX_SESSION_ID_LENGTH == 128`) so a future cap change cannot silently re-anchor the literal expectations — it breaks this pin first and forces a conscious decision.

Reviewer verbatim criticism: "The exact-cap test also derives both input and expectation from `_MAX_SESSION_ID_LENGTH`, so it does not independently pin the specified numeric limit."

title: Fix-only re-review certification needs a pre-fix snapshot when files are untracked
content:
Refines the untracked-file gotcha in memory b652b59a (session.py/test_session.py invisible to plain `git diff`) with the review-cycle consequence observed 2026-09-20:

When a fix pass touches files that are UNTRACKED new files in an uncommitted working tree, a subsequent confirmation re-review **cannot certify "fix-only, no runtime/API change"** — `git diff HEAD` shows only the combined Phase-1+fix change for tracked files, and no committed or snapshot pre-fix version of the untracked files exists. The reviewer must then report the limitation explicitly instead of rubber-stamping the equivalence claim (this happened in the session-id Phase 1 re-review: verdict CLEAN on resolution, but fix-only byte-for-byte runtime equivalence left uncertified).

Process lesson: for review→fix→re-review cycles on uncommitted work where the re-review acceptance criteria include "the fix changed ONLY docs/tests/changelog", the fixer should snapshot the pre-fix state first — e.g. `git stash create`, a temporary WIP commit on a side branch, or a plain file copy — and hand the baseline ref/path to the reviewer. Once the fix is applied, the pre-fix state of untracked files is unrecoverable.

title: searchCommand embedding bypass removed — routed through LLMService.generateEmbedding
content:
Fixed 2026-09-20: ChatSearchHandler.searchCommand (internal/bot/common/handlers/chat_search.py, was :1327-1330) no longer bypasses LLMService. - Failure semantics preserved exactly: service returns None (never raises), handler keeps a defensive try/except; on None/exception BOTH embeddingModelName and queryEmbedding stay None → repo runs filter-only mode. Safe because the repo's searchChatMessages ignores modelName whenever queryEmbedding is None (verified internal/database/repositories/chat_search.py ~:231), so the old behavior (modelName set even on embed failure) and new behavior (both None) are equivalent.
- embedAndSaveMessage (:554) and _llmToolSearchMessages (:708) untouched — embeddings sessionId deliberately deferred.

title: LLMService.generateEmbedding contract: Optional tuple, never raises
content:
API contract confirmed 2026-09-20 while rerouting /search: LLMService.generateEmbedding (internal/services/llm/service.py, ~:1537) returns `Optional[Tuple[str, List[float]]]` — (modelName, embeddingVector) on success, where modelName = chatSettings[ChatSettingsKey.EMBEDDING_MODEL].toStr(); returns None on ANY internal failure. It NEVER raises (all exceptions caught internally, logged, → None).

Downstream details:
- Model resolution goes through chatSettings[EMBEDDING_MODEL].toModel() (internal/bot/models/chat_settings.py:624) which raises ValueError for unregistered names and RuntimeError if LLMManager is uninitialized — all swallowed by the service → None. So an empty/invalid EMBEDDING_MODEL setting degrades gracefully to None.
- The repo's searchChatMessages (internal/database/repositories/chat_search.py ~:231) ignores modelName whenever queryEmbedding is None (filter-only mode). Consequence: on failure a handler can leave both modelName and queryEmbedding None with zero semantic change vs the old behavior of passing a modelName with a None vector.
- sessionId/consumerId: the service calls embeddingModel.generateEmbeddings(text, consumerId=str(chatId), sessionId=sessionId) — routing through the service (chatId=...) is what recovers consumerId stats attribution for /search.
- Test side effect: with the default `_makeChatSettings(embeddingModel="")` in tests/bot/common/handlers/test_chat_search.py, every keywords-bearing searchCommand test now actually invokes the real generateEmbedding (old code gated on non-empty model name and skipped). It returns None via a swallowed exception and logs a traceback — harmless, but visible as log noise; tests stub it with AsyncMock when they care.

title: Shared lint gate can fail transiently from a parallel session's untracked WIP file — re-run before fixing
content:
Sharper instance of memory 1cc4c6a9 (parallel agents cross-contaminate shared gates), observed 2026-09-20 during the media.py sessionId wiring session (ses_f43f59219ffeGBrmb5QqXJt1PB):

**What happened:** `make lint` (flake8 stage) failed with an F401 (`typing.List` unused) in `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_summarization.py` — an UNTRACKED file belonging to a different in-flight session's workstream (summarization.py was also modified by that session). This session owned zero lines of that file.

**The new nuance:** minutes later, without any intervention, the file was fixed by its owning session and flake8 ran clean. So a shared-gate failure in a file you don't own can be TRANSIENT and self-resolving.

**Right response (what worked):**
1. Check `git status` first — if the offending file is untracked/modified outside your file set, it belongs to a parallel session.
2. Re-run the gate before touching anything; only patch a foreign file if the failure persists AND it's a trivial zero-risk fix (and flag it in the handoff to the owning session).
3. Do NOT silently edit another workstream's WIP file — mid-run edits can collide with the owning session's concurrent writes (this session observed the file content change between two reads).

**Corollary for verification reports:** a `make format lint` / `make test` result is only trustworthy as of the moment it ran when parallel sessions are active; state the timestamp/order and re-run if any foreign-file failure appeared mid-run.

title: LLMService sessionId auto-fallback implemented (phase 2)
content: LLMService sessionId auto-fallback (phase 2 of the sessionId semantic-domains design, implemented 2026-09-20): all five chatId-based entry points (generateTextViaLLM :852, generateText :1373, generateStructured :1455, generateImage :1517, generateEmbedding :1567 — line numbers post-edit in internal/services/llm/service.py) resolve `buildSessionId("auto", str(chatId))` → "gromozeka-auto-<chatId>" at the top of the body when sessionId is None, with a DEBUG log "<method>: sessionId not provided, using chat-level fallback" (plain string, no f-string). condenseContext (:1178) uses consumerId instead: `if sessionId is None and consumerId: sessionId = buildSessionId("auto", consumerId)`; both None → stays None. Key invariants: (1) fallback resolves ONCE per public entry point — generateTextViaLLM resolves at top, inner condenseContext/generateText forwards inherit the resolved value and their `if sessionId is None` guards never override; (2) generateEmbedding's fallback sits BEFORE the try/except (buildSessionId can't fail on str(chatId), so this is safe); (3) negative chatIds produce double-dash shape "gromozeka-auto--100123" (sanitizer preserves dashes by design). Tests: TestSessionIdFallback class (10 tests) in tests/services/llm/test_llm_service.py; helper _makeSettingsResolvingModel at module level. Docs: llm/libraries.md §1.3 sessionId paragraph synced; CHANGELOG [Unreleased]/Changed entry added.

title: canonicalLayoutId keeps Cyrillic — hash it before any token-safe context
content: canonicalLayoutId — produced by DivinationHandler._generateLayoutId (internal/bot/common/handlers/divination.py) — is NOT token-safe: its whitelist regex keeps Cyrillic ([a-zа-я0-9_]), not just [A-Za-z0-9._-]. Confirmed 2026-09-20 while wiring sessionId (memory 20982c26). Consequences for any token-safe/length-bounded consumer (e.g. lib.ai.session.buildSessionId, which sanitizes out-of-set chars to "-"): (1) distinct Cyrillic layout names of equal length collapse to the identical dash-run — e.g. "крест" and "плоть" both sanitize to "-----" — a silent cross-key collision; (2) the id is unbounded user input, so long values can exceed buildSessionId's 128-char cap and raise ValueError mid-request. Rule: any new consumer of canonicalLayoutId that needs a token-safe or bounded identifier (session ids, HTTP header values, cache keys with charset constraints) must wrap it in hashSessionIdComponent(canonicalLayoutId) (sha256 hex[:16]); the divination sessionId sites (:1053, :1161) and the CHANGELOG entry document this. Exception: the DB layout cache intentionally uses the raw Cyrillic id (TEXT column, no charset constraint) — canonicalLayoutId IS the DB cache key, so don't "fix" it there.

title: Shared-worktree protocol: auto-staging, self-resolving gate failures, CHANGELOG races
content:
Extensions to parallel-agent shared-worktree memories 6ab53b91 (unreliable global-state observations) and 7b0810fe (git-status pollution), observed 2026-09-20 during the divination sessionId wiring (memory 20982c26):

(1) Concurrent sessions AUTO-STAGE the shared tree: files you edited but never staged show as staged "M " in git status, and `git diff` (worktree vs index) can be EMPTY immediately after your own edit because another session re-ran git add. Staged-vs-unstaged status is useless for authorship attribution — attribute from your own tool-call history.

(2) Mid-flight gate failures from other sessions' half-wired work appear and SELF-RESOLVE. Observed: flake8 F401 "buildSessionId imported but unused" in dev_commands/summarization/yandex_search (their imports landed before their usages), and a transient tests/bot/common/handlers/test_dev_commands.py::TestLlmReplayCommand failure ("'int' object has no attribute 'asStr'" — their messageId.asStr() on a raw int). All gone by the final gate run. Don't chase or fix them.

(3) Protocol that worked: never touch other sessions' files; scope-verify your own paths (flake8/isort/pyright on exactly your changed files); attribute any failing test by inspecting the failing code's diff/ownership before assuming it's yours; re-run `make format lint` + `make test` at the very end for the final snapshot.

(4) Shared append-style files (CHANGELOG.md) race between read and edit: re-read immediately before editing; when inserting adjacent to a concurrent bullet, copy it verbatim into oldString/newString; grep-verify afterwards that all parties' bullets coexist (a media-handler bullet landed between this session's read and edit).

title: D6 script sessionId pattern: per-run bucket via _SESSION_TS constant (all six debug scripts wired)
content:
Phase 2 of the sessionId semantic-domains design (implemented 2026-09-20): the D6 "script" domain pattern applied to all six lib/ai-calling debug scripts in `scripts/`. Complements memory e6b6f556 (lib/ai/session.py foundation API).

**Session id shape for scripts**: `gromozeka-script-<name>[-<modelOrInput>]-<startTs>` — a per-RUN bucket, not per-chat. Rationale: the start timestamp avoids cross-run prompt-cache pollution on opencode-go (each run starts a fresh cache lineage); name+model gives same-run prefix affinity (multiple probes in one run share a prefix).

**Implementation pattern (uniform across scripts)**: module-level constant right after imports:
- `# Per-run session bucket for opencode-go prompt-cache affinity (see lib/ai/session.py).`
- `_SESSION_TS = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ")`
- imports: `from datetime import datetime, timezone` and `from lib.ai.session import buildSessionId` (scripts use sys.path shims → these project imports carry `# noqa: E402`)
- then `sessionId=` kwarg at the generation call site.

**Case-by-case decisions**:
- Single-shot scripts (`check_condensing.py`, `check_image_parsing.py`, `check_structured_output.py`, `reproduce_layout_extraction.py`): inline `sessionId=buildSessionId("script", "<name>", [_SESSION_TS | modelName + _SESSION_TS | str(args.chat_id) + _SESSION_TS])` at the one call site.
- Multi-turn probe (`check_tool_calling.py`): compute `probeSessionId` ONCE before the turn loop — the turns form one accumulating conversation, so one session per model probe, passed to every `generateText` iteration. Do NOT regenerate per turn.
- When the bucket component isn't in scope at the call site (`run_llm_debug_query.py`: input-file basename lives in main(), not `runQueryWithResult()`): compute in main() (using `hashSessionIdComponent(Path(args.inputFile).name)` for long/unsafe names) and thread down as an explicit `sessionId: str` parameter.
- `reproduce_layout_extraction.py` argparse dests are snake_case (`args.chat_id`) — kept per that file's local convention.

Verified green 2026-09-20: `make format lint` clean, `py_compile` OK ×6, `make test` 4758 passed / 11 skipped. No CHANGELOG entry (debug-only, no product behavior change).

title: TestLlmReplayCommand (test_dev_commands.py) is flaky under full-suite ordering
content:
Observed 2026-09-20 after a scripts/-only change (no production code touched): first full `make test` run failed 2 tests in `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_dev_commands.py::TestLlmReplayCommand` — `testLlmReplayLlmError` and `testLlmReplayNonFinalStatus` (4756 passed + 2 failed). Both tests pass in isolation; the file never imports `scripts/`; an immediate full re-run was entirely green (4758 passed, 11 skipped — same collection count, same duration ballpark).

So `TestLlmReplayCommand` exhibits full-suite ordering flakiness — consistent with the known singleton-state-leak class of flakes (diagnose-in-isolation convention per memory 9348ac15 before accepting a pollution hypothesis; here isolation passed AND a clean full re-run passed, confirming ordering sensitivity rather than a real regression from the diff).

Discriminator for future sessions: `tests/` never import `scripts/`, so a scripts/-only diff cannot cause test failures — treat such failures as ordering flakes, but verify with (1) isolated run of the failing tests and (2) a full re-run before declaring green.

title: User's environment auto-stages modified files — git index can change without any git add
content:
During the 2026-09-20 scripts/sessionId session, the six modified files under `scripts/` showed `git status` as ` M` (modified, unstaged) while being edited, but later showed `M ` (modified, STAGED) although no `git add` was ever run in the session. External tooling — most likely the user's editor auto-staging saved files — performed the staging.

Implications for future sessions: (1) don't assume staged changes mean you (or a previous agent) ran `git add`; (2) never `git commit` or `git reset` to "fix" staging you don't remember doing — the user's tooling may manage the index; (3) when reporting working-tree state, re-check `git status` fresh rather than relying on earlier observations in the same session.

title: Test recipe: forcing both condenseContext passes in getThreadByMessageForLLM
content:
Recipe for testing the condense branches of `BaseBotHandler.getThreadByMessageForLLM` (internal/bot/common/handlers/base.py) — discovered/confirmed 2026-09-20 in `TestLLMCallSiteSessionIds::testCondenseContextCallsPassSessionIdAndConsumerId` (tests/bot/common/handlers/test_base.py):

- Force token overflow by patching `ChatSettingsValue.toModel` at CLASS level: `patch.object(ChatSettingsValue, "toModel", return_value=Mock(contextSize=100, getEstimateTokensCount=Mock(return_value=1000)))`. maxTokens = int(contextSize * 0.5) = 50 < 1000 → first condense fires; because the estimator returns a constant, the post-condense re-check ALSO overflows → the re-condense-of-cache branch fires too → `condenseContext` awaited exactly 2 times in one call.
- `EnsuredMessage` uses `__slots__` — instance patching is impossible; patch class attrs: `EnsuredMessage.fromDBChatMessage` (it's a staticmethod, so an `AsyncMock(side_effect=...)` receives exactly the call args, no cls) and `EnsuredMessage.toModelMessageList` (instance method — AsyncMock swallows all kwargs like format/role/outputFormat/cache/excludeMemoryIds).
- Swap the repo: `handler.db.chatMessages = Mock()` with AsyncMock methods `getChatMessageByMessageId` (return a ChatMessageDict row with `root_message_id` set → session id becomes `gromozeka-<chatId>-<rootId>`), `getChatMessagesByRootId` (return [rootRow, tailRow]), `updateChatMessageMetadata`. `ChatMessageDict` rows can be built by copying the `_makeContextRow` shape from test_llm_messages.py (keys: chat_id, message_id as MessageId, root_message_id as MessageId or None, thread_id=0, message_category, date, message_text, ...).
- Empty root-message `metadata` → `condenseCache = []` → the pinned first-N block is SKIPPED entirely (it only runs `if condenseCache and condenseThread:`) — so fake fromDBChatMessage messages with empty metadata keep the setup light.
- Handler construction: module-level `_makeHandler(testDatabase)` helper in test_base.py returns a UserMemoriesHandler (concrete BaseBotHandler); `handler.llmService` is set in BaseBotHandler.__init__ — assign per-test AsyncMocks onto it. Pyright: method assignment needs `# type: ignore[method-assign]`, and mock-attribute access on llmService needs `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` (established file convention).
- `handler.getChatSettings` is AsyncMock'd with a complete ChatSettingsDict (CHAT_PROMPT, CHAT_PROMPT_SUFFIX, LLM_MESSAGE_FORMAT, MEMORY_ENABLED, CHAT_MODEL, CONDENSING_MODEL, CONDENSING_PROMPT, CONDENSING_SYSTEM_PROMPT) — production subscripts keys directly, never .get().

title: getLLMRequestSessionId silently falls back to own-id on unawaitable mocks
content:
`BaseBotHandler.getLLMRequestSessionId` (base.py ~736) awaits `self.db.chatMessages.getChatMessageByMessageId(...)`; in tests whose repo is a plain `Mock()`, the `await` on the auto-created Mock attribute raises `TypeError: object Mock can't be used in 'await' expression` — which the method's `except Exception` SWALLOWS (debug log only) and silently falls back to the message's OWN id: `gromozeka-<chatId>-<messageId>`. Pre-existing liveHandler-based tests in test_llm_messages.py passed while relying on this hidden fallback.

For deterministic session-id assertions, stub it explicitly: `handler.db.chatMessages.getChatMessageByMessageId = AsyncMock(return_value=None)` (own-id fallback) or return a row with `root_message_id` (thread-root session). Note the id formatting quirk: negative chatIds produce a double hyphen, e.g. chatId=-100 + messageId=42 → `"gromozeka--100-42"` (fixtures use chatId=-100, messageId=42).

title: Parallel opencode sessions cause transient lint/test failures in untouched files
content:
When multiple opencode sessions work the same worktree concurrently, `make format lint` / `make test` can fail TRANSIENTLY in files you did not touch. Observed 2026-09-20 during the base.py/llm_messages.py sessionId phase while sibling sessions edited media.py/dev_commands.py/etc.:

- flake8 `F401 'lib.ai.session.buildSessionId' imported but unused` in media.py — the parallel session flushed the import line before its usage lines; grep confirmed real usages existed moments later.
- 2 failures in `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_dev_commands.py::TestLlmReplayCommand` during a full `make test` — that file was being actively rewritten (+53 lines) mid-run.

Resolution protocol (what worked): (1) confirm the failing file is not yours; (2) run the failing test in isolation → in its file → in its directory → in the parent tree (each passed); (3) re-run the full suite once the tree settles — everything green (4758 passed, 11 skipped). Do NOT "fix" or revert parallel sessions' in-flight edits.

title: Concurrent sessions: parallel agent tampered my staged code (debug→warning) + git-add sweep; stash-based not-my-failure proof
content:
New incident class for concurrent opencode sessions (extends memories d9fd48cd / 6ab53b91 — those cover clobbering and unreliable global observations; this adds OWN-CODE TAMPERING + STAGING SWEEPS + the stash proof technique). Observed 2026-09-20 during the LLMService sessionId-fallback implementation while a parallel session wired handler-level sessionId:

1. **Parallel session can EDIT your just-written code before staging it.** After my edits were complete, the parallel session ran `git add` and its staged version had my six `logger.debug(...)` fallback lines silently changed to `logger.warning` — deviating from the approved spec (debug mandated; warning on a hot path for an expected condition = production log spam). Detection: after noticing `git diff <myfile>` empty despite recent edits, check `git diff --cached` — a parallel `git add` sweeps your files into the index. Fix: restore the spec-mandated level in the working tree, then `git add` your own files again so index == worktree (prevents a later bare `git commit` from committing the tampered variant). Note: caplog-based tests that set `caplog.at_level(DEBUG)` still capture WARNING records (warning ≥ debug threshold), so a level change can pass tests silently — assert on message text, not level.

2. **Transient test failures from parallel in-flight edits — prove ownership before reacting.** `make test` failed 2 tests in TestLlmReplayCommand with `AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'asStr'`; root cause was the parallel session's UNSTAGED line `dev_commands.py:1031` (`sessionId=buildSessionId("dev", ..., ensuredMessage.messageId.asStr())`), not my change. Proof technique: `git stash push -- <only my files>` → re-run failing tests → `git stash pop`. CAVEAT: with a live parallel editor the verdict goes stale fast — their fix landed minutes after my failing run (test file mtime 02:51:35); always re-run the failing tests AFTER popping. Cheaper first check: if the failing tests mock out the method you changed (e.g. `handler.llmService.generateTextViaLLM = AsyncMock(...)`), your code never executes there — the failure is definitionally at the call site in someone else's file.

3. **Global `make lint` can fail mid-session from other agents' half-done work** (F401 unused imports in files being edited concurrently). Verify YOUR scope with targeted flake8/isort/pyright on your changed files and report the global drift instead of touching their files.

title: doc_section_edit CAS is file-level: byte-identical section re-read still rejected when another session touched the same file — plain-edit fallback under contention
content:
Refines memory d7d64623 (CAS can reject identical-looking text) with the root cause, confirmed 2026-09-20 on docs/llm/libraries.md §1.3: **`doc_section_edit` CAS is FILE-level, not section-level.** After an `expected_text mismatch` rejection, re-reading the section via `doc_read` returned a BYTE-IDENTICAL body (same sha256 both times), yet the retry STILL failed — because a parallel session had touched a different part of `llm/libraries.md` between my read and write, changing file-level state and invalidating the token every time. Under active concurrent writes this read→edit cycle is a livelock: no amount of re-reading helps.

Operational rules:
- If a CAS retry fails when the section body provably didn't change (identical sha256 on re-read), stop retrying — another session is writing to the same FILE. 
- Sanctioned fallback (AGENTS.md fallback policy): plain surgical `edit` on the exact paragraph; the MCP index is refreshed at the file's next MCP write/reindex (memory 17d02745's no-op-replace reindex trick can force it afterward — mind its blank-line-eating side effect, memory 466db600).
- On shared trees, prefer plain `edit` for one-line doc syncs when parallel activity is suspected (staged-file churn, other sessions announced); reserve `doc_section_edit` for quiet trees.

title: LLM service tests pin kwargs partially (kwargs.get / callKwargs[...]) — adding new kwargs to model calls is test-safe; exact-match scan via assert_awaited_once_with
content: Confirmed 2026-09-20: existing tests around LLMService (tests/services/llm/test_llm_service.py, test_tool_stats.py, test_tool_call_healing.py and the consumerId-attribution suite) assert on mocked model-call kwargs with PARTIAL reads — `mock.await_args.kwargs.get("consumerId")`, `callKwargs["schemaName"]`, `call_args_list[i].args[0]` — and none use exact-match assertions (`assert_awaited_once_with` / `assert_called_once_with`) on AbstractModel generate calls. Consequence: adding a NEW kwarg to LLMService→model calls (e.g. the sessionId auto-fallback) breaks ZERO existing tests; no "legitimate assertion updates" were needed despite the brief warning about them. Impact-analysis shortcut for any signature-extending change to service→model calls: grep the affected test files for `assert_awaited_once_with|assert_called_once_with` — hits are the only exact-kwargs risk; everything else using `.kwargs.get(...)`/`callKwargs[...]` is add-kwarg-safe. When writing NEW tests, prefer partial-kwargs reads over exact-match for the same forward-compatibility reason.

title: caplog weakness: at_level(DEBUG) + caplog.text assertion keeps PASSING when debug degrades to warning (inverse of 581f994b)
content:
Gotcha found 2026-09-20 during the sessionId-fallback Gate-1 review; the INVERSE of memory 581f994b (which covers a test BREAKING when the level changes). Here the test is too weak: it keeps passing when the log level degrades.

Mechanics: `caplog.at_level(logging.DEBUG)` captures DEBUG **and every higher severity**. Asserting only on `caplog.text` (message presence) passes even if the production line changes from `logger.debug(...)` to `logger.warning(...)` — the message matches either way. So severity regressions on hot-path logs are invisible to such tests.

Real instance: LLMService sessionId auto-fallback logs must stay `debug` (silent at INFO+, singleton hot path); a parallel session actually flipped them to `warning` mid-rollout, and the existing test (tests/services/llm/test_llm_service.py:2952–2961) would NOT have caught it.

Correct pattern: after the capture block, iterate `caplog.records`, match the fallback message(s), and assert `rec.levelno == logging.DEBUG` (cover all six fallback methods); optionally add a second capture at `at_level(logging.INFO)` asserting NO fallback record is emitted. Status: OPEN MINOR finding as of the review — fix when strengthening the sessionId fallback tests.

title: fromDBChatMessage subscripts exactly 15 keys — minimal rows safe if they carry those keys (root_message_id/message_category/created_at NOT read)
content:
Refines memories 5185c018/f77e65fa with the EXACT key list (verified 2026-09-20 against internal/bot/models/ensured_message.py:809-865). `EnsuredMessage.fromDBChatMessage` uses direct bracket access (`data["key"]`) on exactly these 15 keys — no more: markup, metadata, user_id, full_name, username, chat_id, message_id, date, message_text, message_type, media_group_id, reply_id, quote_text, thread_id, media_id.

It NEVER reads `root_message_id`, `message_category`, or `created_at`. So a minimal DB row containing exactly the 15 keys above is safe for fromDBChatMessage, even though ChatMessageDict typing includes more columns — proven by test_summarization.py `_makeDbChatMessage` (:158-187) which omits those three columns and passes. metadata=None is tolerated (treated as {}).

The older "must include every column / KeyError" guidance is over-broad: the requirement is precisely those 15 keys, and the risk is KeyError only for THOSE. When writing a new minimal row helper, check the current fromDBChatMessage body for its subscript set first — the set is the contract, not the TypedDict.

title: Divination prompt-prefix comment overstates; /analyze mediaList index-alignment assumption
content:
Two adjacent NITs surfaced by the Gate-1 handler-wave review (2026-09-20); the hashing rationale itself is already in memory 8c61df5a and was re-validated as technically sound:

1. **divination.py:1045-1048 comment overstates cache behavior.** The comment claims "same canonical layout produces the same system+user prompt prefix", but the user prompt embeds the RAW `layoutName` (divination.py:1036-1041). Consequence: normalization variants of one canonical id ("Celtic Cross" vs "celtic-cross") share the hashed session bucket with DIFFERENT prompt prefixes → prompt-cache miss, not corruption. Fix when touching this code: reword the comment; no code change needed.

2. **media.py:540-547 `/analyze` index-alignment assumption.** The session id keys off `mediaList[i].id` assuming stored media entries align 1:1 by index with downloaded entries. That holds only while every downloaded entry has a same-index stored entry: if an earlier supported Max attachment fails to download (skipped at media.py:501-502) while its stored media entry exists, later items get keyed by a sibling's stored id. Deterministic per parent message; only degrades session-bucket affinity, no correctness impact. The Max `mediaList` population order (`addMedia` appends in processing order, internal/bot/models/ensured_message.py:949) was not fully verifiable — worth a focused regression test for Max multi-attachment partial-download failure before claiming complete coverage.

title: Unstubbed Mock attribute raises TypeError on await → silently exercises except-fallback in tests
content: In handler tests, a DB/service method left as a plain `Mock` (not stubbed as resolvable) raises `TypeError` when awaited — silently routing execution into an `except` fallback instead of the intended path. Concrete case from the Gate-1 handler-wave review (N2): `TestMediaDescriptionExtraction` tests in tests/bot/common/handlers/test_llm_messages.py (e.g. testLeadingTextAndTagAtEndExtracts :1078) never stub `db.chatMessages.getChatMessageByMessageId`, so `getLLMRequestSessionId` reaches its DB-failure fallback (base.py:767-772) via TypeError rather than the no-row path. Harmless there (sessionId not asserted) but the exercised path is implicit. General rule: when a test's realism depends on which fallback path runs, stub every awaited collaborator explicitly — e.g. `return_value=None` for the no-row case, as the sibling test at :1063 already does.

title: media.py analyze download paths: Telegram single-file vs MAX multi-attachment; MAX models constructible for tests
content:
Architecture facts about `internal/bot/common/handlers/media.py` `analyze_command` download paths, established 2026-09-20 while building the R2-residual regression test (complements memory 6db2663f):

- **Two download branches**: Telegram branch (`botProvider == TELEGRAM and isinstance(parentMessage, telegram.Message)`) downloads exactly ONE file via a `match parentEnsuredMessage.messageType` (IMAGE → `parentMessage.photo[-1].file_id`, STICKER → ...). MAX branch (`isinstance(parentMessage, maxModels.Message)`, `self._bot is not None`, `parentMessage.body.attachments` non-empty) iterates ALL `body.attachments` and downloads each via `self._bot.downloadAttachment(mediaId=payload.token, fileId=payload.url)`; a download returning None is skipped (partial results allowed). A failed download on Telegram → empty `mediaDataList` → early return "Не удалось получить данные медиа." with NO LLM call.
- **Consequence**: the stored-id index-alignment misalignment (R2-residual: `mediaList[i].id` indexes into the SUCCESSFULLY-DOWNLOADED list, so a failed earlier attachment shifts the surviving item under another attachment's bucket) can ONLY trigger on the MAX path — Telegram always yields ≤1 downloaded item.
- **Test recipe for MAX parent messages**: `lib.max_bot.models` package re-exports ALL models (Message, MessageBody, Recipient, PhotoAttachment, PhotoAttachmentPayload, UserWithPhoto, ChatType, ...) as plain kwargs-constructible `BaseMaxBotModel` classes. Production `isinstance` checks require REAL model instances (not Mock), e.g. `Message(sender=UserWithPhoto(user_id=8, first_name="Bob"), recipient=Recipient(chat_id=CHAT_ID, chat_type=ChatType.CHAT), timestamp=..., body=MessageBody(mid="parent-mid", seq=1, attachments=[PhotoAttachment(payload=PhotoAttachmentPayload(photo_id=i, token=t, url=...)), ...]))`, attached via `parent.setBaseMessage(maxMessage)`. Download stub: `AsyncMock(side_effect=lambda mediaId, fileId: None if mediaId == "token-1" else _minimalPngBytes())`.
- Reference test: `TestAnalyzeCommandPartialDownloadAlignment::test_partial_download_analysis_stays_deterministic` in tests/bot/common/handlers/test_media.py (~:457-528); the `_newMediaHandler` helper there now takes a `botProvider: BotProvider = BotProvider.TELEGRAM` keyword param.

title: ADR subsection house style confirmed via ADR-026 append; architecture.md has NO per-ADR TOC; code paths as plain backticks
content:
2026-09-20 architect session appended ADR-026 (sessionId domains) to docs/llm/architecture.md; confirmed/learned:

1. TWO ADR house formats coexist: (a) flat bold-label style (ADR-020/021/022 — see memory 3b7a68bc) and (b) H4-subsection style for multi-part designs (ADR-013/014/016/026): H3 `### ADR-NNN: Title`, flat body carries `**Date:**` + `**Status:**` lines, then `#### ADR-NNN: <Subsection>` children (slugs `adr-nnn-<subsection>`), bold-label runs + `-` bullets inside; the ADR's final subsection ends with a `---` separator before the next section.
2. architecture.md's TOC lists ONLY the 3 top-level sections (ADRs / Dependency Map / Design Patterns) — there is NO per-ADR index. Adding an ADR requires no TOC/index edit.
3. Code paths inside ADRs may be plain backticks (dominant in ADR-016) instead of markdown links — plain backticks mean `make check-docs` link validation cannot fail on newly inserted content. Refines memory d99f6b67 (which converts References to links): use real links only where genuinely valuable (design-doc references per ADR-021/025), backticks for file paths.
4. Append mechanics that worked cleanly end-to-end: `doc_section_edit` op=insert_after anchored on the highest ADR's slug (ADR-025), `expected_text` = its COMPLETE served flat body (which includes the trailing `---`), `new_text` opening with the same-level H3 heading; in-call reindex returned `indexed` (88 sections); no junction blank-line damage this time (contrast memory dd4ec8b0). Amendments inside an ADR use the blockquote idiom (`> **Updated by ADR-YYY (date):**` / `> **Amendment (during implementation):**`).

title: Docs-only gate triage when the role has no shell: doc_lint substitute + explicit delegation + risk assessment
content:
When a doc-only session's brief demands `make lint` + `make check-docs` but the agent role has no shell (architect: bash denied — see memory 19d39fe9), the working pattern (validated in the ADR-026 session, 2026-09-20) is:

1. Run markdown-mcp `doc_lint` as the structural substitute and report its findings.
2. Report the shell gap explicitly; the two make targets must still be run before merge by someone with shell (memory b7add9ae) — delegate (e.g. software-developer) or ask the user.
3. Include risk triage in the report: `make lint` (flake8/isort/pyright) cannot be affected by a markdown-only edit; `make check-docs` risk is eliminated when the inserted text adds zero markdown links (plain-backtick code refs — see the ADR-format memory from the same session).

This keeps the brief's acceptance criteria honestly reported instead of silently skipped.

title: docs/llm structure gotchas: checklist trailing --- separator, H2-only TOCs, insert-after anchor choice
content: Structural facts about `docs/llm/handlers.md` (and the docs tree generally) discovered while inserting the "sessionId conventions for LLM calls" H3 (2026-09-20): (1) The final H3 of §2, "Checklist after creating/modifying a handler" (slug `checklist-after-creating-modifying-a-handler`), has a trailing `---` horizontal rule as the last line of its flat body — it is the §2→§3 separator. Using `doc_section_edit op=insert_after` on that section would place a NEW section AFTER the `---`, breaking the layout. Workaround used: `insert_after` the preceding subsection `step-7-run-quality-checks` instead, so the new H3 lands between Step 7 and the final checklist with the `---` still last. (2) docs/llm file-level TOCs list only H2 sections — adding H3 subsections requires NO TOC update. (3) When a doc edit is a small string change deep inside a HUGE section (e.g. libraries.md §1.3, ~80 lines), MCP replace of the whole flat body still works if the body is taken verbatim from `doc_read`; plain-edit fallback exists but would leave the MCP index stale since no CLI reindex is permitted in the sandbox.

title: SummarizationHandler batching math + deterministic multi-batch test recipe
content:
SummarizationHandler._doSummarization (internal/bot/common/handlers/summarization.py) batching math, as needed to write deterministic multi-batch tests:
- `maxTokens = llmModel.contextSize`; `tokensCount = llmModel.getEstimateTokensCount([systemMessage, *parsedMessages])`
- `batchesCount = tokensCount // max(maxTokens - 256, maxTokens * 0.9) + 1`; `batchLength = len(parsedMessages) // batchesCount`
- Rescale (`batchLenCoeff`) only fires if `batchLength > SUMMARIZATION_MAX_BATCH_LENGTH` (= 256, internal/bot/constants.py). Inner per-batch token recheck can shrink slices; the sessionId is computed ONCE before the loop (`gromozeka-summary-<chatId>-<commandMessageId>`) and is identical on every generateText call.

Deterministic recipe to force exactly N≥2 batches (used in test_passesStickySessionIdToEveryBatch, tests/bot/common/handlers/test_summarization.py): mock `mockModel.contextSize` and `mockModel.getEstimateTokensCount = Mock(side_effect=lambda reqMessages: len(reqMessages) * K)`. Worked example: contextSize=1000, K=100, 10 DB rows → initial estimate (1+10)*100=1100 → batchesCount = 1100 // 900 + 1 = 2, batchLength = 5 (no rescale since 5 < 256); per-batch recheck estimate (1+5)*100=600 ≤ 1000 so slices are not shrunk. Assert `generate.await_count == 2`, both requests are [system + 5] with DISJOINT message-content sets, and every `call.kwargs["sessionId"]` identical.

GOTCHA: the initial estimate must be ≥ the denominator (0.9 × contextSize) or floor division yields exactly 1 batch (e.g. 10 tokens vs contextSize=100000 → 1 batch). Small estimates also risk batchLength=0 → degenerate shrink loop.

Typed test rows: building a genuine `ChatMessageDict` literal (internal/database/models.py:129) requires `message_category=MessageCategory.USER`, `created_at`, `root_message_id=None`, and `message_id=MessageId(messageId)` for pyright — even though `EnsuredMessage.fromDBChatMessage` reads none of `message_category`/`created_at`/`root_message_id` at runtime, so minimal ad-hoc dicts "worked" before typing. `MessageId.__init__` accepts `int | str | Self`, so re-wrapping is safe. `markup`/`metadata` are typed `str` — use `""` not None.

title: Grep/glob cannot search gitignored trees (lib/ext_modules) even with explicit path
content:
Verified 2026-09-20: `grep` with an explicit `path` into `lib/ext_modules` + `include="*.py"` returns "No files found" — the tool filters out gitignored trees regardless of explicit scoping — and `glob` on `lib/ext_modules/<subdir>/**/*` also returns nothing. Only the `read` tool sees gitignored content (exact file paths + directory listings).

Consequence: any "zero usage" census over lib/ext_modules (or any gitignored subtree, e.g. configs/ deployment layers) MUST enumerate via `read` on directories and read every source file — grep/glob/rg-based claims of "no matches" are meaningless there. (Supersedes earlier advice to just pass an explicit path/include to grep — that does not work.)

Minor related trap: loose unquoted substring patterns match Python class names — e.g. `aiModel` literally appears inside `YcOpenaiModel`/`BasicOpenAIModel`, producing ~100 noise hits that can crowd out real matches in truncated results. Hunt config keys with quotes (`"ai-model"`) and exact identifiers.

title: Don't trust grep for venv package-removal checks — gitignored ext_modules are invisible; cross-check with make lint
content:
Incident (2026-07-31 dependency work): grep returned "No files found" for imports of a package that WAS imported — but only from `lib/ext_modules/*` code, which the grep tool never searches (gitignored vendored trees). The false negative led to wrongly uninstalling the package from ./venv, which broke `make lint` (pyright reportMissingImports over lib/ext_modules).

LESSON: Do NOT rely on `grep` alone to decide a package can be removed from the venv. The reliable cross-check is pyright (`make lint`), which DOES type-check `lib/ext_modules/` (root pyproject `[tool.pyright]` excludes only the literal `ext/` dir, NOT `lib/ext_modules/`). Also: `pip show <pkg>` `Required-by:` can show empty for ext-module deps because those are declared only in the subpackage's own requirements.direct.txt/pyproject.toml, not the main lockfile.

title: lib/ext_modules/__init__.py IS git-tracked — nested subpackage dirs are gitignored with their own .git
content:
The claim "git ls-files lib/ext_modules/ returns 0 tracked files" is FALSE — it returns 1 file: `lib/ext_modules/__init__.py` (the Python package marker, tracked since 2025). The actually-untracked part is the nested vendored TREES under it (verified 2026-07-18):

- `.gitignore` rule is `lib/ext_modules/*/` (trailing slash + wildcard = matches only DIRECTORIES inside `lib/ext_modules/`, not the `__init__.py` file directly in it). The rule's line number drifts — grep for the rule content rather than citing a line number.
- Each nested tree is a vendored nested git repo (own `.git/` directory, NOT a submodule — no `.gitmodules` exists).

Practical consequence: edits to `lib/ext_modules/__init__.py` ARE visible to `git diff` and DO get committed/PR'd. Edits to nested subdir trees are NOT — scope any "invisible to main-repo PR" claim to the subdirs, not the whole `lib/ext_modules/` path.

title: lib/ext_modules/* subpackages carry dependencies outside main requirements.txt
content:
Ext modules under `lib/ext_modules/*/` can declare their own dependencies (`requirements.direct.txt` or `pyproject.toml` project dependencies) that are NOT included in the project's main `requirements.txt` / `requirements.direct.txt` and are not pulled in automatically.

Consequences:
- `make test` can fail with ImportError if ext-module code is imported during test collection but its dependencies aren't installed in the venv.
- Fix: manually install what the ext module needs (`./venv/bin/pip install <pkgs>`).
- When troubleshooting test collection failures, always check `lib/ext_modules/*/requirements.direct.txt` or `lib/ext_modules/*/pyproject.toml` for missing packages.

title: Cross-cutting API changes must explicitly include lib/ext_modules/ in scope — invisible to grep, covered by pyright
content:
During the lib/ai fallback refactoring (removing `generateTextWithFallBack`, `generateImageWithFallBack`, `generateStructuredWithFallBack` aliases), stale references were found in `lib/ext_modules/` subpackages — easy to miss because ext_modules are vendored subpackages with their own `pyproject.toml`, separate `make format` handling, and their own test suites.

Lesson: cross-cutting API changes must include `lib/ext_modules/*/` in the search-and-replace scope explicitly. Note the tooling split: grep/glob cannot see ext_modules at all (gitignored — enumerate via `read`), while repo-root pyright (`make lint`) DOES type-check `lib/ext_modules/` (only `ext/` is excluded) and will catch stale imports there. As of June 2026, `lib/ai/` is clean — the *WithFallBack aliases no longer exist anywhere in `lib/ai/`.

title: pyright: dict[str, Any] test fixtures not assignable to TypedDict params — use a cast() wrapper helper
content:
pyright rejects passing a `-> dict[str, Any]` test-fixture helper's result to a function whose parameter is a TypedDict: `"dict[str, Any]" is not assignable to "<TypedDict>"`. You cannot fix it by annotating the helper's return as the TypedDict either, when the dict literal omits required keys (the helper deliberately builds a minimal dict). And do NOT churn existing loose call sites: TypedDict → `dict[str, Any]` assignability is also unreliable in pyright, so re-typing the helper would break existing usages like `list[dict[str, Any]] = [_makeThing(...)]`.

Working pattern: keep the loose helper unchanged, add a typed wrapper next to it — `def _makeTypedThing(**kwargs: Any) -> SomeTypedDict: return cast(SomeTypedDict, _makeThing(**kwargs))` — and use the wrapper ONLY at the typed call sites. Imports: `cast` from typing; the TypedDict via the package's relative-import style.

title: User hand-edit alignment protocol: tests+docs only, flag production drift, never touch unrelated changes
content:
Scope-discipline convention for any "user hand-edited production code, align tests/docs" task (established 2026-09-20; generalizes across the repo):

1. **Read the user's hand-edited code first, derive the ACTUAL behavior, then align** — never assume the brief's description of the new shape is complete; the edit may have changed details (extra id components, new imports) discoverable only by reading the production code.
2. **Production code is off-limits in alignment tasks** — even a now-stale docstring/inline comment documenting superseded behavior must be FLAGGED in the report, not fixed, unless explicitly requested. Rationale: the user may still be mid-edit; edit lists are exhaustive.
3. **Never touch pre-existing unrelated working-tree changes** — diffs for a target file may mix multiple change sets; report only your own hunks and say the rest is pre-existing.
4. **Pin new behavior with literal expectations, not by calling the production helper** — tests should assert literal expected values (computed once via venv python), and test names should be renamed when old names begin to lie (e.g. when the stability key changes).
5. Report format the user expects for such tasks: (1) new-vs-old behavior description "for the memory record", (2) per-test changes, (3) doc amendments or "none", (4) inline diff summary for gitignored files, (5) verbatim verification tails, plus explicit flags for anything ambiguous/buggy.

title: Pyright intermittently emits phantom errors — re-run before blaming your diff
content:
Observed 2026-09-20 during `make lint` runs after a scripts-only diff (pyright as wired into the Makefile lint chain):

1. One run reported 7 reportArgumentType errors in a vendored `lib/ext_modules/` test file — untouched by the diff, at HEAD. A subsequent run reported nothing in that file.
2. A later run reported 1 false positive `"MessageCategory" is not defined` at `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_base.py:2007` — the symbol IS imported at line 42 of that file, and the file was untouched.
3. Three consecutive direct `./venv/bin/pyright` runs plus two full `make format lint` gate runs: 0 errors each time.

Conclusion: this repo's pyright runs are intermittently flaky (non-deterministic phantom errors, varying across runs and files, often in vendored or untouched code). Rule of thumb: when `make lint`/pyright reports errors in files your diff didn't touch (especially `lib/ext_modules/` vendored code or import-existence errors), re-run the gate 2-3 times before treating the errors as real or blaming your changes. Only errors that reproduce across consecutive runs deserve investigation.

title: make freeze-requirements is broken by pre-existing venv drift
content:
The standard `make freeze-requirements` command (= `pip freeze > requirements.txt`) is broken due to pre-existing venv drift. The dev venv has packages manually installed that are NOT in the committed lockfile (e.g. onnxruntime, plus deps pulled in by vendored `lib/ext_modules/` subpackages: weasyprint and its subtree — fonttools, tinycss2, cssselect2, pydyf, pyphen, tinyhtml5, webencodings, brotli, zopfli — and lxml). Running make freeze-requirements captures all this cruft, producing a dirty diff with 13+ unrelated packages.

The committed lockfile deliberately excludes OS-provided/ext-module packages (CI gets onnxruntime from Alpine). When adding new dependencies, either:
1. Add the exact package lines manually at correct alphabetical positions (justified exception to "don't hand-edit requirements.txt" rule)
2. Or use pip's --requirement filtering to exclude drift packages

This was discovered during httpx2 Phase A migration when attempting to add 4 httpx2 packages via freeze-requirements produced a polluted lockfile.

title: Dependency/lockfile model: multi-source venv, freeze caveats
content:
The main `requirements.txt` lockfile is NOT a plain `pip freeze` of the dev venv. The dev venv contains packages that must NOT enter the main lockfile:

1. **Vendored ext-module deps are separate** — `lib/ext_modules/` subpackages (each with its own `.git` + `pyproject.toml` + own requirements files) declare dependencies (e.g. weasyprint and its subtree: fonttools, cssselect2, pydyf, pyphen, tinycss2, tinyhtml5, webencodings, zopfli, brotli, lxml) that are installed into the shared ./venv but are intentionally ABSENT from the main `requirements.txt`. NOTE: pyright (root pyproject `[tool.pyright]` excludes only `ext/`, NOT `lib/ext_modules/`) DOES type-check the vendored subpackages, so those deps MUST stay installed in ./venv or `make lint` fails (reportMissingImports in the vendored converter modules). Never uninstall them.

2. **onnxruntime is Alpine-system-provided** — `scripts/ci.sh` does `apk add py3-onnxruntime` + `make venv-alpine` (--system-site-packages). onnxruntime has NO musllinux wheel, so it CANNOT be pip-installed on Alpine. It is deliberately kept OUT of `requirements.txt`. Adding it to the lockfile BREAKS Alpine CI `make install`.

3. **`sqlite-vec`** (a direct dep, in requirements.direct.txt) was MISSING from requirements.txt as of 2026-07-31 (pre-existing). Likely a separate bug; not yet resolved.

CONSEQUENCE: `make freeze-requirements` (which just runs `pip freeze > requirements.txt`) is UNSAFE on the dev venv — it would wrongly capture the vendored-ext-module deps + onnxruntime. When adding a new pure-pip direct dep with no transitives (e.g. av), the correct lockfile delta is a single sorted line; do not whole-venv-freeze. Verify musllinux wheels exist for any new dep (av 18.0.0 DOES ship musllinux_1_2 x86_64+aarch64 via cp311-abi3, so it is Alpine-CI-safe).
