title: Gotcha: lockfile contamination from dirty venv when using make freeze-requirements
content:
`make freeze-requirements` runs `pip freeze > requirements.txt` (Makefile:43-45), which captures ALL packages installed in the current `./venv`, not just those declared in `requirements.direct.txt`. This causes lockfile drift: the `requirements.txt` diff for a single dependency addition may include unrelated packages that happened to be installed in the developer's venv.

Common sources of contamination:
- Dependencies from `lib/ext_modules/*/` subpackages (e.g., weasyprint and its transitive tree, lxml — declared only in the ext-modules' own requirements files) manually installed for development but not declared in root `requirements.direct.txt`.
- Transitive dependencies from prior `pip install` commands outside of `requirements.direct.txt`.
- Testing/tooling packages installed ad-hoc.

**Fix**: Before running `make freeze-requirements` for a clean lockfile update:
1. Recreate `./venv` from scratch.
2. Run `make install-direct` (installs from `requirements.direct.txt` only — Makefile:35-37). NOTE: `make install` (Makefile:31-33) installs from the FROZEN `requirements.txt`, NOT from `requirements.direct.txt`, so it is the WRONG target for producing a clean re-freeze.
3. Then run `make freeze-requirements` — the resulting `requirements.txt` diff will only contain the new package and its genuine transitive dependencies.

**Concrete example**: Adding `sqlite-vec==0.1.9` (which has `requires_dist: null` — no transitive deps) produced a diff adding 12 unrelated packages (brotli, cssselect2, fonttools, lxml, onnxruntime, pydyf, pyphen, tinycss2, tinyhtml5, weasyprint, webencodings, zopfli) because the venv contained packages from ext_modules development and prior manual installs.

**Lighter alternative** (when requirements.txt is already clean but venv is dirty): `pip uninstall` only the leaked packages, then re-freeze — avoids reinstalling heavy deps (torch, onnxruntime, numpy). See memory 0978ac64.

title: Dirty-venv cleanup: uninstall specific packages rather than recreating venv
content:
When `requirements.txt` is already clean (restored from git or never contaminated) but the venv still has leaked packages, the lighter-weight fix is:

1. `pip uninstall` only the leaked packages from the venv (not recreating the whole venv)
2. Then run `make freeze-requirements` to regenerate `requirements.txt`

This avoids the cost of reinstalling all heavy dependencies (torch, onnxruntime, numpy, etc.) from scratch. It's the better first-line fix compared to the "recreate venv" approach in the existing lockfile contamination gotcha (memory e5844e56).

**Concrete case**: 12 packages from weasyprint's transitive tree (brotli, cssselect2, fonttools, lxml, onnxruntime, pydyf, pyphen, tinycss2, tinyhtml5, weasyprint, webencodings, zopfli) were in the venv but never in `requirements.direct.txt`. Uninstalling them and re-freezing produced a clean diff with only the intended `+sqlite-vec==0.1.9`.

**Caveat**: Removing leaked packages from the venv can surface pre-existing pyright errors in `lib/ext_modules/` that were previously masked. Ext-module code imports `lxml` and `weasyprint` (declared only in the ext-modules' own `lib/ext_modules/*/requirements.direct.txt`, not in root requirements). These ext_module pyright errors are pre-existing on any clean root install and are unrelated to the lockfile change. They are not a reason to keep leaked packages in the venv.

title: Repo-wide dedoodization completed (90 files, 1231 tokens removed)
content:
A comprehensive "dedoodization" pass was performed (2026-07-04): the stylistic "dood" suffix/marker (Prinny style from Disgaea, per `lib/bayes_filter/__init__.py` `__author__`) was removed from all internal/developer-facing source across the entire repo. This SUPERSEDES earlier partial cleanups (e.g. divination.py docstring cleanup, lib/ai/ pass). 1231 of 1294 occurrences removed across 90 .py files.

**Classification convention (the keep/remove rule):**
- REMOVE "dood" from: docstrings, inline comments (#), log messages (logger.*), exception/error messages (raise ValueError/RuntimeError/NotImplementedError/TypeError), assert *failure messages*.
- KEEP "dood" in: user-facing bot messages (messageText=, helpMessage=), argparse description=/help=, print() calls, __author__ metadata, test fixture data (mock LLM prompts, assert *comparands* that represent expected output containing "dood").

After this pass, ~53 remaining "dood" occurrences are all verified legitimate user-facing/fixture contexts. `make format lint` clean; `make test` 2802 passed (1 pre-existing failure in test_forwardOriginAuthorMatching[originUser-matchByUsername] which was unrelated and since fixed).

NOTE: .md/.toml documentation files and Makefile echo statements were NOT touched (those are user-facing docs). The gitignored lib/ext_modules/* ext_module trees WERE also cleaned.

title: Third-party library test coverage: real-vs-mocked map and gap list
content:
Map of which third-party libraries have REAL behavioral test coverage (lib called without mocking) vs which are always mocked/untested, as of 2026-07. This identifies where a dependency-version bump could silently break the app.

== LIBS WITH REAL COVERAGE (exercised through production code, not mocked) ==
- openai SDK deserialization: golden tests via OpenAIReplayerPatcher (see separate memory). Also `openai.BadRequestError` real in test_basic_openai_provider.py.

- python-magic (MIME detection): tests/bot/test_sandbox.py::test_sandbox_send_file_mime_detection — handler NOT patched for magic, real PNG bytes → magic.from_buffer → asserts image/png.

title: make ci tar excludes miss host-side cache artifacts — minor CI fidelity gap
content:
The `make ci` target (Makefile, `ci:` at line 123; staging `tar` at line 131) copies the repo into the container via `tar -C /src -cf - --exclude=./venv --exclude=./.git --exclude="./.env*" --exclude="*/__pycache__" --exclude="./lib/ext_modules/*" . | tar -C /app -xf -`. The exclude list was extended after the original 2026-07-16 review: it now covers FIVE entries (`./venv`, `./.git`, `./.env*`, `*/__pycache__`, `./lib/ext_modules/*`) — the `.env*` entry keeps secrets out of the container, and `lib/ext_modules/*` keeps the gitignored vendored code out, matching what a clean sourcecraft checkout would contain.

Still missing from excludes (residual nit, status open): `.pytest_cache/`, `htmlcov/`, `.coverage`, `.mypy_cache/`, `*.egg-info`, `build/`. These host-side stale artifacts get copied into the container's `/app`, slightly overstating the clean-checkout fidelity (the Makefile comment at lines 114-122 promises a run that "mirrors sourcecraft's clean-container run").

Practical impact remains negligible: `make test` runs the full suite (not `--last-failed`), so `.pytest_cache/` reuse doesn't change results; pyright/coverage don't read these caches. For strict CI fidelity, extend the excludes or note the caveat in the comment. Note also that the recipe between staging and `sh scripts/ci.sh` now includes `rm -rf /app/venv`, `apk add --no-cache git`, `git init .`, and `git config --global --add safe.directory /app` (Makefile lines 129-135).

title: Zero-transitive-dep packages: hand-editing requirements.txt is byte-safe but still violates AGENTS.md
content:
Verified during av==18.0.0 (PyAV) lockfile addition (2026-07-31):

Hand-editing `requirements.txt` directly (instead of running `make freeze-requirements`) produces a **byte-correct result ONLY when the new package has zero transitive dependencies** — because the complete delta is exactly one line (`pkg==version`), which can be placed alphabetically by hand without error. This was confirmed for av==18.0.0: its `dist-info/METADATA` has zero `Requires-Dist:` lines (PyAV bundles FFmpeg libs in a self-contained wheel), so the lockfile delta is genuinely `+av==18.0.0` (one line) and nothing more.

**For any package WITH transitive dependencies, hand-editing is fragile and must not be done** — you'd have to manually compute, pin, and sort the full transitive closure. The clean-venv freeze is mandatory in that case.

**Even for zero-dep packages, the hand-edit still technically violates AGENTS.md** ("requirements.txt is regenerated from requirements.direct.txt via freeze-requirements; do not edit it by hand"). The correct workflow that satisfies both the rule AND produces clean output:
1. Clean the venv of leaked packages (`pip uninstall` the ext-module/onnxruntime/etc. contaminants, OR recreate via `rm -rf venv && make install-direct`)
2. `pip install <new-package>`
3. `make freeze-requirements`

This produces the same single-line delta without the AGENTS.md violation.

**av==18.0.0 specific facts** (verified from METADATA, no python -c used):
- Zero `Requires-Dist:` lines — no Python-level runtime deps
- `Requires-Python: >=3.11` (satisfied by project's 3.12 target)
- Ships musllinux wheels — safe on Alpine CI, no system-FFmpeg dependency needed
- Bundles FFmpeg shared libraries in the wheel

**Format note**: requirements.txt uses bare `==` pins throughout (no `--hash` annotations anywhere), and `make install` is just `pip install -r requirements.txt` with no `--require-hashes` flag. So missing hashes never break install — the hash-pinning concern is moot for this project.

title: Phase A httpx2 migration completed with alias_httpx()
content:
Phase A of the httpx→httpx2 migration was successfully implemented using httpx2.alias_httpx() process-wide alias. Key implementation details:

1. **Lockfile fix**: Added exactly 4 packages to requirements.txt at correct alphabetical positions:
   - httpcore2==2.10.0 (after httpcore==1.0.9)
   - httpx2==2.10.0 (after httpx-sse==0.4.3)
   - socksio==1.0.0 (after sniffio==1.3.1)

title: httpx2 frozen lockfile must keep httpx/httpcore as installed-but-shadowed transitives
content:
Lockfile invariant from the httpx2 migration Phase D correction — SUPERSEDED by the actual repo state (verified 2026-08-20):

**The original argument (2026-08-13):** PTB 22.8 requires httpx<0.29 and openai 2.45.0 required httpx<1 unconditionally; httpx2 does not satisfy those Requires-Dist constraints (different dist names), so a plain `pip install -r requirements.txt` would reinstall httpx (unpinned) — hence httpx/httpcore "must remain" in the frozen lockfile for reproducibility.

**What actually happened:** the lockfile was later regenerated (openai is now 3.0.0 — its httpx requirement status changed with the major bump; yandex-ai-studio-sdk 0.22.1; httpx-sse removed). Current requirements.txt pins **httpcore==1.0.9 but has NO httpx entry**. The migration-time prescription is therefore obsolete as a description of the repo; ADR-021:793 ("httpx and httpcore REMAIN pinned") is stale in the same way.

**Durable guidance going forward:**
- Before any dependency change, recompute the ACTUAL closure (fresh venv install or pip resolution), because the lockfile and ADR-021 disagree with each other on httpx.
- If PTB still requires httpx, a fresh `make install` may pull an unpinned httpx transitively — check whether that matters for the change at hand (the alias shadows it at runtime either way).
- The general freeze-requirements caveats (dirty multi-source venv: ext-module deps, Alpine onnxruntime; hand-edit only provably-zero-transitive single-line deltas) still apply.

title: make ci staging evolved: .env* and lib/ext_modules/* excluded; git init in /app
content:
The `make ci` recipe (Makefile lines 123-137) has evolved since its 2026-07-16 introduction. Verified current staging pipeline inside `docker run --rm -v "$(CURDIR):/src:ro" $(CI_IMAGE) sh -c '...'`:

1. `set -eo pipefail` then `apk add --no-cache git` (git is installed in-container; the base Alpine image alone is not enough for the later git steps).
2. `mkdir -p /app` then tar-copy `/src` → `/app` excluding FIVE patterns: `./venv`, `./.git`, `./.env*`, `*/__pycache__`, `./lib/ext_modules/*`.
   - `./.env*` keeps host secrets out of the container copy (AGENTS.md: .env files contain secrets, never expose them).
   - `./lib/ext_modules/*` keeps the gitignored vendored ext-module code out — a clean sourcecraft checkout wouldn't have it either, so this preserves CI fidelity (vendored ext-module trees exist only on the developer disk; they are gitignored per memory c4d3c2cd).
3. `rm -rf /app/venv` — belt-and-braces venv removal after the copy (the tar exclude already skips `./venv`).
4. `cd /app && git init . && git config --global --add safe.directory /app` — the container-side copy is turned into a fresh git repo (the `.git` dir is excluded from the copy, so a new one is initialized and marked safe; git-dependent tooling in `make check`/`make test` sees a repo root).
5. `sh scripts/ci.sh` — the shared single-source-of-truth CI script.

Editing rule: keep `.env*` and `lib/ext_modules/*` in the exclude list — removing them would either leak secrets into the container or ship untracked vendored code into a 'clean CI' run.

title: Different types of "dotted" mentions in documentation
content:
When grepping for "dotted", "dot notation", or "dot-navigation" in docs to fix drift, be aware that not all mentions refer to ConfigManager key navigation. Different contexts:

1. **ConfigManager.get() navigation** - The now-reverted feature where get("a.b") traversed nested dicts. Docs should reflect that get() is now literal-key-only (as of 2026-08-22).

2. **customParams.* dotted keys** - These are Python parameter path notation (e.g., "customParams.sandbox.bootstrap.starter-packages"), NOT ConfigManager navigation. These are a different concept and should NOT be touched when fixing ConfigManager drift.

3. **Python import dotted paths** - In docs/design/custom-modules-design.md and similar, "dotted" refers to Python module import notation (e.g., "lib.ext_modules.<subpackage>"). These are language-level concepts, unrelated to config access.

4. **Section-name mentions** - References like "[stats.pages]" or "stats-pages" are just table/section names in configs, not claims about access mechanism. These are benign.

5. **Protected historical records** - docs/llm/teamlead-memory.md contains dated historical entries about ConfigManager changes; these are intended as records and should not be updated.

When sweeping for drift, distinguish these contexts. The DO-NOT-TOUCH list from the 2026-08-22 docs pass included: sandbox.md:261,269 (explicitly warns against dotted keys), tasks.md:485, teamlead-memory.md, and any customParams.* mentions.

title: .dockerignore patterns are root-anchored — nested storage/*.db and bak/ enter the build context
content:
Gromozeka root `.dockerignore` (added with the Max webhook receiver Docker artifacts, branch extract-max-webmessage) has a verified intent-vs-effect gap: dockerignore patterns WITHOUT `**/` match only at the build-context ROOT. Consequences found in Gate-1 review (rated Important):

- `*.db`, `*.db-wal`, `*.db-shm` (:19-21) do NOT match the repo's actual databases living nested under `storage/{max,telegram}/bot_data.db(+wal/shm)` and ext-module `storage/*.db` state files — live user/chat SQLite data ships into the build context.
- Also unexcluded: `bak/` (old config trees incl. prod/prod-max copies — most likely place for hand-edited literal tokens), `logs/` (31 profiler dumps), `certs/` (public CA PEMs only — no keys, verified), `htmlcov/`, `.coverage`, `test-video.mp4`, `error.log`, `fail-*.jsonl`, `.vscode`, `.pytest_cache`, `.codeassistant*`.
- Impact scope: context transfer only — NOTHING reaches the image (no COPY touches these paths; COPY list is exactly lib/__init__.py, lib/utils, lib/db, lib/proxy, lib/max_webhook_receiver). Risk materializes with remote buildx builders (context sent off-host) and BuildKit content-store persistence.
- Suggested fix: `**/*.db`, `**/*.db-wal`, `**/*.db-shm`, plus `bak`, `storage`, `logs`, `certs`, `htmlcov`, `webhook-receiver*.toml` (pre-empts Step-4 instruction to create that file at repo root) — none collides with a COPY source. Alternative allowlist form works too: `*` then `!lib/__init__.py !lib/utils !lib/db !lib/proxy !lib/max_webhook_receiver` (last-match-wins negation).
- Contrast that DOES work correctly: `lib/ext_modules` (rooted path), `.env*` (matches all five root .env files), `**/__pycache__` (matches root level too — `**` matches zero directories in BuildKit patternmatcher).

title: Parallel-session lint churn; lib/ext_modules is gitignored
content:
Two repo-workflow gotchas hit 2026-09-20 during the sessionId/embedding-routing session:

1. Parallel-session lint churn: another agent session was actively editing shared files (test_base.py, test_dev_commands.py, test_media.py, test_summarization.py) while this session ran `make lint` repeatedly. Failures (F821 missing import, E501 long line, F401 unused import) appeared and vanished between runs in files this session never touched. Protocol that worked: (a) verify YOUR files are clean individually (flake8/isort/pyright scoped to them); (b) don't chase another session's in-flight edits; (c) fix only persistent (stable across 2+ runs) trivial mechanical blockers that break the shared `make lint` gate, and report the out-of-mandate touch explicitly. This session wrapped two 124-char lines in test_media.py and removed an unused `List` import in test_summarization.py to unblock the gate.

2. lib/ext_modules/*/ is gitignored (.gitignore:56) — vendored subpackages are invisible to git: not in `git status`, absent from a HEAD worktree. Consequences: pyright/flake8 errors inside them CANNOT be verified against HEAD via a throwaway git worktree (files don't exist there); their errors come from local vendored work in progress and may appear/disappear on their own; `make format` formats them via the explicit per-dir loop (why `make format` is required after touching lib/ext_modules, not bare black/isort).

title: Ext-module verification mechanics: root isort skips gitignored ext trees; flake8 does not; scoped lint recipe
content: Derived from Makefile/pyproject behavior observed 2026-09-20 while verifying an ext-modules-only change (not spelled out in AGENTS.md): (1) The ROOT isort pass in `make format`/`make lint` skips the gitignored nested trees entirely ("Skipped 1603 files" — repo isort config ignores gitignored paths), so the explicit per-dir loop in the Makefile `format` target is the ONLY thing that formats `lib/ext_modules/*`; running bare isort/black from root will silently not touch them. (2) flake8 DOES traverse `lib/ext_modules/` (its `ext` exclude entry only matches directories named exactly `ext`, not `ext_modules`) — ext-module code is flake8-checked. (3) `make lint` short-circuits in order flake8 → isort --check → `import main` → pyright; a flake8 failure means the later steps never ran that invocation. (4) When `make lint` is red from unrelated/concurrently-edited main-repo files, verify an ext-module change in scope with targeted commands from repo root: `./venv/bin/flake8 lib/ext_modules/<module>`, `./venv/bin/isort --check-only lib/ext_modules/<module>`, `./venv/bin/black --check lib/ext_modules/<module>`, plus scoped pyright — repo-root venv/pyright resolves internal/lib imports correctly (0 errors) even though the editor LSP cannot (see memory 22bbf218 gotcha 3). (5) An ext-module's tests run via `./venv/bin/pytest lib/ext_modules/<module>/tests/` from repo root: rootdir/configfile resolve to the nested repo's own pyproject.toml (asyncio_mode=auto), relative imports (`from ..<module> import ...`) work.

title: buildSessionId silently accepts None as the literal "None" component — guard Optional values at call sites
content:
Facet of the `buildSessionId` contract NOT covered by the ValueError memory b9d65573 (which records: raises on empty components and >128-char totals): **`buildSessionId` silently accepts `None`**. `str(None)` → `"None"` is a non-empty, token-safe string, so no guard inside the builder fires — a nullable value passed straight through produces a valid-but-wrong stable bucket (e.g. `gromozeka-<module>-None`), silently splitting the prompt-cache affinity bucket. The builder will NOT raise; the caller must.

Rule: any caller whose component comes from an `Optional` source (DB nullable column, config, user input) MUST add an explicit `if value is not None` guard BEFORE calling buildSessionId and pick an explicit fallback component. Confirmed correct in the 2026-09-20 Gate-1 review: ext-module call sites reading nullable DB columns use explicit `is not None` checks with a literal fallback component (shared `…-articles` style bucket), with a dedicated regression test asserting the NULL case using a literal expected string.

title: sessionId semantic domains design (D1–D6): core implemented & review-verified; blueprint for remaining sites
content:
D1–D6 sessionId semantic-domains design for lib/ai calls (delivered 2026-09-20 by architect agent; companion to memories 821ceee7 = sessionId contract, 673ed015 = census). STATUS CORRECTED 2026-09-20 after code-analyst review: NOT "awaiting approval" anymore — phases P0–P2 core sites are IMPLEMENTED and review-verified: lib/ai/session.py exists with the recommended API (sanitizeSessionIdComponent / hashSessionIdComponent sha256[:16] / buildSessionId(*components, namespace="gromozeka"), 128-char cap), media.py wired (memory 14bd3683), divination.py wired (memory 20982c26). This memory remains the BLUEPRINT for the remaining domains (D4–D6).

**Design intent**: sessionId = context-window identity — share a session ⇔ share an evolving prompt prefix; one-shot unique prompts gain nothing from identity but must not pile into the global bucket; only persistent identifiers allowed (never runIds/uuids/timestamps).

**Six-domain taxonomy**:
- D1 Conversation/thread → `getLLMRequestSessionId()` format `gromozeka-<chatId>-<rootMessageId.asStr()>` unchanged; must stay BYTE-IDENTICAL incl. `gromozeka--100…` double-dash for negative group chatIds (compat). Verified at base.py:784 (`buildSessionId(str(chatId), rootMessageId.asStr())`).
- D2 One-shot content item → `gromozeka-media-<fileUniqueId>`; analyze fallback `gromozeka-analyze-<chatId>-<messageId>`; URL condense `gromozeka-url-<sha256(url)[:16]>`; layout extraction `gromozeka-layout-<hash(canonicalLayoutId)[:16]>` (hash added during implementation — memory 8c61df5a).
- D3 Feature-flow invocation → `gromozeka-<feature>-<chatId>-<messageId>` (draw, divination reading shared text+image pair `gromozeka-divination-<chatId>-<messageId>`, summary, dev replay); content-keyed variant for reusable flows: `gromozeka-divination-discovery-<hash(canonicalLayoutId)[:16]>` (multi-round tool loop inherits via forwarded sessionId). LLM-tool path (media.py `_llmToolGenerateAndSendImage`) uses the D1 conversation session.
- D4 User-scoped persistent store → `gromozeka-memory-<chatId>-<userId>-<threadId>`: user_memories.py:1296 (_runSingleRefinement) — strongest non-conversation cache candidate.
- D5 Background maintenance → `gromozeka-task-<name>-<chatId>`: user_memories.py regen, chat_search.py backfill, message_preprocessor.py — all embedding calls, deferred.
- D6 Scripts/probes → `gromozeka-script-<name>[-<modelOrInput>]`: check_*.py, run_llm_debug_query.py (hash of input basename), reproduce_layout_extraction.py.
- Extension modules: `gromozeka-<moduleName>-<flowId>`; never bare D1 format.

**Unimplemented recommendations to check before reusing**: (1) LLMService auto-fallback `gromozeka-auto-<chatId>` defense-in-depth tag (NOT verified implemented in review — grep before assuming); (2) chat_search.py:1327-1330 bypass fix (route through generateEmbedding for consumerId stats); (3) embeddings sessionId skip (7 sites) — revisit only when a session-consuming provider gains embeddings; (4) dev-tag split between llm_test_command and llmReplayCommand.

Status: Accepted (2026-09-20, user-approved; fully implemented and reviewed). Subsections: Context (audit findings, sole opencode-go consumer); Decision — lib/ai/session.py foundation (buildSessionId/sanitizeSessionIdComponent/hashSessionIdComponent, 128-char cap); Decision — semantic domains D1-D6 + extension modules; Defense-in-depth auto-fallback (gromozeka-auto-* floor, /search embedding routing, layout-hash amendment); Consequences (analyze_command index-alignment limitation, byte-identity caveat, ext-module nested-repo note). The ADR is the canonical reference for sessionId construction going forward; cite it instead of the memories.

title: Gate-2 confirmation re-review: CLEAN — sessionId-domains rollout signed off for delivery
content:
2026-09-20 confirmation re-review (code-reviewer, review-only, judged final on-disk state) of the Gate-2 fix pass for the sessionId-domains rollout. Verdict: **CLEAN** — all three Gate-2 findings RESOLVED, zero new findings (0 BLOCKER / 0 MINOR / 0 NIT). This is the final sign-off before user delivery and closes the review chain: findings raised in 670c8583 → fixes applied per c9341fce → confirmed resolved here.

Per-finding resolutions (file:line evidence):
- G2-F1 (typing/conventions in new test code): RESOLVED. `tests/bot/common/handlers/test_media.py` — `Any` dropped from import (:35), `_captureCalls` deleted, direct `handler._bot` assignment (:167, :479), `cast(AsyncMock, …)` + `call_args is not None` narrowing (:366-369, :412-415, :435-438, :546-553), five tests camelCased (:349, :385, :417, :460, :527). `test_summarization.py` — LLMService imported at module scope (:30), annotated fixture args (:83-87), `_makeDbChatMessage()` returns typed `ChatMessageDict` with `message_category`/`created_at`/`root_message_id` and MessageId-wrapped ids (:162-195). Ext-module test files — row-factory helpers concretely typed to their row TypedDict (:86-101), five session-id tests camelCased (:621, :636, :668, :682, :697). Pre-existing ext-module `Any` in older test classes was explicitly out of scope.
- G2-F2 (cross-batch stability coverage): RESOLVED. `test_passesStickySessionIdToEveryBatch` (test_summarization.py:242-291) now drives TWO genuine batches via production batching math (10 rows + system msg, estimator side-effect `len(reqMessages) * 100`, contextSize=1000 → 1100 tokens vs effective budget 900 → batchesCount=2, batchLength=5) and asserts await_count == 2, disjoint 6-message slices, identical `gromozeka-summary-555-42` on every call. Arithmetic verified deterministic — no rescaling (SUMMARIZATION_MAX_BATCH_LENGTH=256), shrink branch never entered (each batch 600 tokens < 1000).
- G2-F3 (docs): RESOLVED. ADR-026 D2 bullet (docs/llm/architecture.md:1120-1124) + docs/llm/handlers.md:283 document the `/analyze` no-stored-id fallback `gromozeka-analyze-<chatId>-<commandMessageId>`, accurately matching internal/bot/common/handlers/media.py:548-558 (note: uses the analyzing command's recipient/message id, NOT the parent message's).

Scope confirmed: fix pass touched test files + two doc one-liners only; no production-logic changes in the parent repo's unstaged diff.

Verification (independently re-run by reviewer): `make lint` PASS (flake8/isort clean, circular-import check ok, pyright 0 errors/0 warnings); targeted pytest on the 3 touched test files → 29 passed in 2.17s; `make check-docs` → 148 files, 2950 links, 0 broken. Full suite NOT re-run per brief; fixer-reported 4762 passed / 11 skipped stands.

Provenance caveat (recurring review gotcha for this repo): gitignored nested ext-module repos under `lib/ext_modules/*/` have an index that does not isolate a specific fix pass — reviews there can only judge final on-disk state; a byte-level "no production changes since Gate-N" claim for them is unprovable without a pre-fix snapshot.
